de.title: Todesfall in Italien (Deutschland): Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei einem Todesfall zwischen Italien und Deutschland: ärztliche Todesbescheinigung, Bestattungsunternehmen, Sterbeurkunde beim Standesamt, Konsulat & Leichenpass (Überführung oder Bestattung vor Ort) sowie Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlass.
de.introHtml: Bitte nehmen Sie unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Verlust Ihres Familienangehörigen entgegen. Wenn ein deutscher Staatsangehöriger in Italien verstirbt, müssen zunächst die ärztliche Todesfeststellung, die standesamtliche Beurkundung und die Ausstellung des Leichenpasses (Passaporto Mortuario) in der italienischen Sterbegemeinde (Comune) abgeschlossen werden, bevor eine Überführung nach Deutschland oder eine Bestattung vor Ort stattfinden kann [1][2].

steps.title: Ärztliche Todesfeststellung und Leichenschauschein in Italien einholen (im Krankenhaus oder außerhalb des Krankenhauses)
steps.html:
Der erste gesetzlich vorgeschriebene Schritt nach der italienischen Bestattungspolizeiverordnung (Regolamento di Polizia Mortuaria, Präsidialdekret D.P.R. 285/1990) richtet sich danach, wo der Tod eingetreten ist [2][3]:

  • Tod im Krankenhaus oder in einer Pflegeeinrichtung: Die ärztliche Krankenhausleitung (direzione sanitaria) veranlasst unmittelbar die klinische Todesfeststellung, füllt den statistischen ISTAT-Meldebogen zur Todesursache (scheda ISTAT) aus, führt die interne Leichenschau durch, überführt den Leichnam in die Prosektur des Krankenhauses und übermittelt die Todesanzeige an das kommunale Standesamt (Ufficio di Stato Civile) [2][3]. Legen Sie unverzüglich den deutschen Reisepass oder Personalausweis der verstorbenen Person vor, damit die Personendaten fehlerfrei erfasst werden [1].
  • Tod außerhalb eines Krankenhauses (Privatwohnung, Hotel, Ferienunterkunft oder öffentlicher Ort): Rufen Sie sofort die einheitliche europäische Notrufnummer 112 (oder 118 für den medizinischen Notruf) bzw. eine Ärztin oder einen Arzt an, damit die erste ärztliche Todesfeststellung (constatazione di decesso) und die Meldung der Todesursache ausgestellt werden [2]. Anschließend muss die Amtsärztin oder der Amtsarzt für Leichenschau (medico necroscopo) der örtlich zuständigen Gesundheitsbehörde (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL) zwischen 15 und 30 Stunden nach Eintritt des Todes die amtliche Leichenschau durchführen und den Leichenschauschein (certificato necroscopico) ausstellen, der für das Verschließen des Sarges sowie die Bestattungs- oder Überführungsgenehmigung zwingend erforderlich ist [2][3].
  • Plötzlicher Tod, Unfalltod oder Tod im öffentlichen Raum unter Einschaltung der Justizbehörden: Tritt der Tod ohne ärztlichen Beistand, plötzlich, infolge eines Unfalls oder unter ungeklärten Umständen ein, werden die Sicherheitsbehörden hinzugezogen und der Leichnam wird der Staatsanwaltschaft (Procura della Repubblica) unterstellt [1][2]. In diesem Fall dürfen Bergung, Einäscherung oder Überführung erst erfolgen, nachdem die zuständige Staatsanwältin oder der zuständige Staatsanwalt die förmliche Freigabe (nulla osta) zur Bestattung oder Überführung erteilt hat [1][2].

steps.title: Reiseversicherungsschutz prüfen und ein Bestattungsunternehmen in Italien und Deutschland beauftragen
steps.html:
Bevor Sie eigenständig Verträge unterzeichnen, prüfen Sie, ob für Ihren Familienangehörigen eine Auslandsreisekrankenversicherung, ein Schutz über eine Kreditkarte oder eine Mitgliedschaft in einem Automobilclub bzw. Assistance-Tarif mit Einschluss des Rücktransports im Todesfall bestand [1]. Ist ein solcher Versicherungsschutz aktiv, beauftragt die Notrufzentrale der Versicherung direkt das internationale Bestattungsunternehmen und übernimmt die tariflich gedeckten Kosten [1].

Besteht kein Versicherungsschutz, beauftragt die Familie ein zugelassenes Bestattungsunternehmen in Italien (impresa funebre) mit der Abwicklung der kommunalen und gesundheitsbehördlichen Formalitäten sowie der Abstimmung mit einem aufnehmenden Bestatter am Zielort in Deutschland [1]:

  • Auswahl eines Bestattungsunternehmens in Italien: Sie können die Orientierungslisten von Bestattungsunternehmen einsehen, die von den deutschen Auslandsvertretungen in Italien veröffentlicht werden - zuständig für Mittel-, Süd- und Inselitalien ist die Deutsche Botschaft in Rom, Ambasciata di Germania a Roma (Telefon: +39 06 492131), und für Norditalien das Deutsche Generalkonsulat in Mailand, Consolato Generale di Germania a Milano (Telefon: +39 02 62311010) [1] - oder sich an den nationalen italienischen Fachverband Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri (FENIOF, Telefon: +39 051 6650285) wenden [4].
  • Auswahl eines aufnehmenden Bestatters in Deutschland: Für die Entgegennahme des Sarges oder der Urne und die Durchführung der Trauerfeier in Deutschland finden Sie qualifizierte Bestattungsunternehmen über das Verzeichnis des Bundesverband Deutscher Bestatter (Telefon: +49 211 1600810; Notfallnummer: +49 211 1600886) [5]. Clarvia nennt berufsständische Verzeichnisse ausschließlich zur Orientierung und gibt keine Empfehlung, Zulassung oder Rangfolge bestimmter Bestattungsunternehmen ab.

steps.title: Sterbefall innerhalb von 24 Stunden beim italienischen Standesamt melden und die mehrsprachige Sterbeurkunde (Formblatt C) anfordern
steps.html:
Die Todesanzeige (dichiarazione di morte) muss innerhalb von 24 Stunden nach dem Tod beim Standesamt (Ufficio di Stato Civile) der italienischen Gemeinde (Comune) eingereicht werden, in der der Tod eingetreten ist (beispielsweise bei den Standesämtern von Roma Capitale oder der Comune di Milano) [2][3]. In der Regel reicht das von der Familie bevollmächtigte italienische Bestattungsunternehmen (oder die ärztliche Krankenhausleitung) die Todesanzeige zusammen mit dem Leichenschauschein und dem ISTAT-Bogen ein [2][3].

Fordern Sie über das Bestattungsunternehmen oder direkt beim kommunalen Standesamt folgende Urkunden an:

  • Vollständige Abschriften oder Bescheinigungen aus dem italienischen Sterberegister (copie integrali / certificati dell'atto di morte): erforderlich für kommunale Überführungs-, Einäscherungs- oder Bestattungsgenehmigungen in Italien [2][3].
  • Mehrsprachiger Auszug aus dem Sterbeeintrag (estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte su modello plurilingue - Formblatt C / Modello C nach dem Wiener CIEC-Übereinkommen vom 8. September 1976): Diese standardisierte internationale Urkunde wird von deutschen Standesämtern, Gerichten und Rentenversicherungsträgern direkt und ohne Apostille oder beglaubigte Übersetzung anerkannt [1][2].

steps.title: Kommunalen Leichenpass (Passaporto Mortuario) einholen und Überführung nach Deutschland oder örtliche Bestattung koordinieren
steps.html:
Da sowohl Italien als auch Deutschland Vertragsstaaten des Internationalen Berliner Abkommens über die Leichenbeförderung vom 10. Februar 1937 sind, erfolgt die grenzüberschreitende Überführung nach einem einheitlichen Verfahren über das Bestattungsunternehmen [1][2][3]:

  • Sargüberführung nach Deutschland (Passaporto Mortuario / Leichenpass): Das italienische Bestattungsunternehmen beantragt den Leichenpass (Passaporto Mortuario) direkt beim Standesamt der italienischen Sterbegemeinde (etwa der Comune di Milano oder Roma Capitale), das ihn mehrsprachig ausstellt, ohne dass eine zusätzliche konsularische Genehmigung einer deutschen Auslandsvertretung erforderlich ist [1][2][3]. Für den internationalen Sargtransport bescheinigt die zuständige örtliche Gesundheitsbehörde (ASL) die konservierende Behandlung sowie den vorgeschriebenen Doppelsarg (hermetisch verlöteter innerer Zinksarg und äußerer Holzsarg) gemäß D.P.R. 285/1990 und dem Berliner Abkommen [2][3].
  • Einäscherung in Italien und Urnenüberführung oder örtliche Bestattung: Wird eine Einäscherung in Italien gewählt, erteilt die Standesbeamtin oder der Standesbeamte (Ufficiale di Stato Civile) die Einäscherungsgenehmigung nach Prüfung des zu Lebzeiten geäußerten Willens der verstorbenen Person oder aufgrund einer Erklärung des überlebenden Ehegatten bzw. der nächsten anspruchsberechtigten Angehörigen (sowie nach Vorliegen des staatsanwaltschaftlichen nulla osta, falls ein Ermittlungsverfahren anhängig war) [2][3]. Die versiegelte Aschenurne wird zusammen mit der kommunalen Auslandsbeförderungsgenehmigung und der Einäscherungsbescheinigung an einen deutschen Friedhof überführt (in Deutschland gilt nach den Bestattungsgesetzen der jeweiligen Bundesländer der Friedhofszwang) [1][5].
  • Konsularische Rolle der deutschen Auslandsvertretungen: Die Ambasciata di Germania a Roma und das Consolato Generale di Germania a Milano unterstützen Angehörige beratend und wirken mit, wenn Verwandte in Deutschland Vollmachten beglaubigen lassen müssen; sie übernehmen jedoch keine Überführungs- oder Bestattungskosten [1].

steps.title: Behördliche Schritte in Deutschland bei Standesamt, Deutsche Rentenversicherung und Nachlassgericht erledigen
steps.html:
Sobald der mehrsprachige Auszug aus dem Sterbeeintrag (Formblatt C / Modello C) vorliegt, können die Angehörigen oder Begünstigten in Deutschland die nationalen Meldungen vornehmen:

  • Nachbeurkundung beim deutschen Standesamt (Nachbeurkundung des Sterbefalls): Obwohl der italienische mehrsprachige Auszug nach Formblatt C in ganz Deutschland unmittelbar gültig ist, können antragsberechtigte Familienangehörige (Ehegatte, eingetragener Lebenspartner, Eltern oder Kinder) beim Standesamt des letzten deutschen Wohnsitzes der verstorbenen Person optional die Nachbeurkundung des Sterbefalls im deutschen Sterberegister beantragen, um deutsche Sterbeurkunden zu erhalten [1][6].
  • Renten und Hinterbliebenenleistungen (Deutsche Rentenversicherung): Informieren Sie unverzüglich den Renten Service der Deutschen Post sowie die Deutsche Rentenversicherung (kostenfreie Servicenummer innerhalb Deutschlands: 0800 1000 4800; aus dem Ausland: +49 800 1000 4800) unter Beifügung der mehrsprachigen Sterbeurkunde [6]. Je nach Verwandtschaftsverhältnis zur verstorbenen Person kann der überlebende Ehegatte oder eingetragene Lebenspartner eine Witwen- oder Witwerrente sowie das Sterbevierteljahr (Auszahlung der Rente in voller Höhe der Versichertenrente für die ersten drei Kalendermonate nach dem Sterbemonat) beantragen, während anspruchsberechtigte Kinder Waisenrente geltend machen können [6].
  • Nachlass, Banken und Versicherungen (Nachlassgericht): Nutzen Sie den mehrsprachigen Auszug (Formblatt C), um die deutsche Krankenkasse, Banken und Lebensversicherungen zu benachrichtigen, und wenden Sie sich an das zuständige Nachlassgericht (beim Amtsgericht des letzten gewöhnlichen Aufenthalts in Deutschland), sofern ein Testament abzuliefern oder ein Erbschein zu beantragen ist [1][6].

de.closingQuestion: Damit wir Ihnen gezielte Angaben zu den zuständigen kommunalen und regionalen Behörden machen können: In welcher italienischen Gemeinde (Comune) ist der Tod eingetreten (im Krankenhaus oder außerhalb des Krankenhauses), und in welcher Stadt bzw. welchem Bundesland in Deutschland hatte Ihr Familienangehöriger seinen Wohnsitz?

title: What to Do When a Brazilian Citizen Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Brazilian Citizen Dies in Portugal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Portugal and Brazil: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a Brazilian citizen dies in Portugal, electronic medical certification, Portuguese civil registration, and Brazilian consular registration follow a strict sequence before the body or ashes can be repatriated to Brazil or buried locally in Portugal [1][3].

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death via SICO (in a Hospital or Outside a Hospital)
steps.html:
In Portugal, medical verification of death is recorded electronically in the Death Certificate Information System (Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito - SICO), managed by the Shared Services of the Ministry of Health (SPMS) and the Directorate-General of Health (Direção-Geral da Saúde - DGS), which transmits the record directly to the civil registry [3][4]. The initial procedure depends on the place and circumstances of death:

  • Death in a hospital or healthcare facility: The attending hospital physician verifies the death, issues the Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Óbito) directly in the SICO platform, and transfers the body to the hospital mortuary [3][4]. Provide the deceased person's Brazilian passport (along with their Portuguese Residence Permit, Título de Residência, or Cartão de Cidadão, if held) so that personal and parentage details are recorded without discrepancies [1][4].
  • Death outside a hospital (private residence, hotel, holiday accommodation, or public place): Call the European emergency number 112 immediately (or the local police authority, PSP or GNR) [1][4]. If the death resulted from a known natural cause and an attending physician or local health officer (delegado de saúde) can certify the cause of death, that physician issues the Medical Certificate of Death in SICO [3][4].
  • Sudden, violent, or unexplained death (Public Prosecutor and INMLCF intervention): If the death occurred without prior medical attendance, suddenly, or under suspicious circumstances, the police report the matter to the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público), which orders the removal of the body to the medico-legal office of the National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences (Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses - INMLCF) for an autopsy or forensic examination [3][4]. Only after release by the Ministério Público and registration in SICO by the forensic pathologist can the funeral agency take charge of the body [3][4].

steps.title: Check Assistance Insurance, Appoint a Funeral Agency, and Grant Power of Attorney if the Family Is in Brazil
steps.html:
Before signing a private funeral contract, check whether your family member held travel insurance, international health insurance, credit card assistance coverage, or life insurance covering funeral repatriation [1]. When an active policy exists, the insurer's assistance centre appoints the international funeral provider directly and covers eligible expenses [1]. Note that the Brazilian State and the Brazilian Consulates General do not have public funds to pay for funerals, cremations, or the repatriation of human remains or ashes [1].

If no insurance coverage applies, the family must appoint a licensed funeral agency in Portugal (registered with the Directorate-General for Economic Activities, Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE) to handle civil registration, preparation, and international transport or local burial [1][2]:

  • Selecting a funeral agency in Portugal: You can consult the consular guidance published by the Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa (Consulate General of Brazil in Lisbon, emergency consular duty phone: +351 962 520 581) [1] or contact the Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (ANEL, National Association of Funeral Enterprises, phone: +351 218 687 978) to identify licensed funeral agencies [2]. Clarvia provides public and trade association references solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific funeral providers.
  • Authorising procedures when the family is in Brazil: If no family member can travel to Portugal, the closest next of kin in Brazil can execute a power of attorney (procuração, either a public deed at a Brazilian notary office, cartório de notas, or a private instrument with notarised signature, apostilled under the Hague Apostille Convention) authorising the contracted Portuguese funeral agency or a local representative in Portugal to claim the body, declare the death, apply for consular registration, and authorise cremation or international repatriation [1].

steps.title: Declare the Death at the Civil Registry Office Within 48 Hours
steps.html:
A death occurring in Portugal must be declared within the statutory 48-hour deadline following the death or following forensic release by the INMLCF [4]:

  • Filing the declaration at the Conservatória do Registo Civil: In practice, the appointed funeral agency files the declaration at any Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil, overseen by the Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado - IRN, Registry Helpline: +351 211 950 500) using the electronic Medical Certificate of Death recorded in SICO and the deceased person's identification documents [3][4].
  • Obtaining the Portuguese death record and medical cause-of-death certificate: The Conservatória do Registo Civil registers the death entry (Assento de Óbito) free of charge and issues the Portuguese death certificate (Certidão de Óbito), which is required for the burial, cremation, or international transit permit (alvará de trasladação) [4]. For Brazilian consular registration and repatriation to Brazil, also ask the funeral agency to obtain the supplementary medical declaration expressly stating the medical cause of death (causa mortis, extracted from SICO/DGS), because the standard Portuguese civil death certificate does not list the cause of death and Brazilian authorities require it [1][5].

steps.title: Complete Brazilian Consular Death Registration and Arrange Repatriation to Brazil or Local Cremation
steps.html:
For the death to have legal effect in Brazil and to allow the entry of human remains or ashes into Brazilian territory, the death must be registered with the Brazilian consular mission holding jurisdiction over the place of death in Portugal (the Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa for Lisbon, Central Portugal, and the Islands; the Consulate General of Brazil in Porto for Northern and parts of Central Portugal; or the Consulate General of Brazil in Faro for the Algarve and Alentejo) [1]:

  • Issuance of the Brazilian Consular Death Certificate (Certidão Consular de Óbito): The application is submitted via the electronic e-Consular platform by the declaring family member or the duly authorised funeral agency representative, presenting the Portuguese Assento de Óbito, the medical document stating the causa mortis, the deceased's Brazilian passport or identity card, and their Brazilian birth or marriage certificate [1].
  • International repatriation of the body to Brazil: Repatriation of a body requires embalming (tanatopraxia / formalin preservation), placement in an impermeable coffin with a hermetically sealed inner zinc liner, an international mortuary transit permit (alvará de trasladação internacional / livre-trânsito mortuário) issued in Portugal, a sanitary certificate confirming the absence of contagious disease, and the Certidão Consular de Óbito [1][5]. At the arrival airport in Brazil, health clearance follows the regulations of the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (ANVISA, Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency, phone in Brazil: 0800 642 9782), and a receiving Brazilian funeral home must clear the coffin at the air cargo terminal [5].
  • Cremation in Portugal and transporting ashes: If the family chooses cremation in Portugal (subject to authorisation by the entitled next of kin and medical/judicial clearance), the ashes are placed in a sealed urn accompanied by the cremation certificate and the Certidão Consular de Óbito, and may be transported by air to Brazil in accordance with airline rules and the requirements of the Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária [1][5].

steps.title: Transcribe the Death Record in Brazil and Notify Segurança Social and INSS
steps.html:
Once consular registration and the funeral or repatriation are complete, civil registry and social security records should be updated in both countries:

  • Transcription of the Consular Death Certificate in Brazil: The Certidão Consular de Óbito issued by the Consulate General in Portugal must be transcribed (trasladada) at the 1st Civil Registry Office (Cartório do 1.º Ofício de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais) of the deceased's last domicile in Brazil (or at the Cartório do 1.º Ofício of the Federal District if the deceased had no prior domicile in Brazil) so that it produces full civil, banking, and probate (inventário) effects in Brazil [1].
  • Portuguese death benefits (Segurança Social): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension in Portugal, report the death to the Segurança Social (Portuguese Social Security, phone: +351 210 545 400 or 300 502 502) to check entitlement to the death grant (subsídio por morte), funeral expense reimbursement, and survivor's pension (pensão de sobrevivência) for an eligible spouse, civil partner (unido de facto), or descendants [6].
  • Brazilian survivor's pension (INSS) and the Brazil-Portugal Social Security Agreement: If the deceased was insured or retired under the Brazilian social security system, report the death to the Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS, National Institute of Social Security, phone in Brazil: 135; Meu INSS portal) to apply for the survivor's pension (pensão por morte) for eligible dependants based on family relationship (spouse, domestic partner, or minor/disabled children) [7]. Under the Bilateral Social Security Agreement between Brazil and Portugal (Acordo Previdenciário Brasil-Portugal), contribution periods completed in both countries can be totalised to establish entitlement to survivor benefits [6][7].

closingQuestion: So that we can confirm the exact consular jurisdiction and local procedures, in which municipality in Portugal did the death occur (in a hospital or outside a hospital), and are the family members currently located in Portugal or in Brazil?

pt.title: O que fazer quando um cidadão brasileiro falece em Portugal: guia oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Passos oficiais após o óbito de um cidadão brasileiro em Portugal: certificado médico de óbito (SICO), agência funerária e seguro, Conservatória do Registo Civil, registo consular no Consulado-Geral do Brasil (Lisboa, Porto ou Faro), traslado para o Brasil (ANVISA) ou sepultamento local, e Segurança Social / INSS.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos os nossos mais sinceros sentimentos pelo falecimento do seu familiar. Quando uma pessoa de nacionalidade brasileira falece em Portugal, a certificação médica eletrónica, o registo civil português e o registo consular brasileiro seguem uma sequência específica antes do traslado do corpo ou das cinzas para o Brasil ou do funeral local [1][3].

steps.title: Obter o Certificado Médico de Óbito através do SICO (no hospital ou fora do hospital)
steps.html:
Em Portugal, a verificação médica do óbito é registada eletronicamente no Sistema de Informação dos Certificados de Óbito (SICO), gerido pelos Serviços Partilhados do Ministério da Saúde e pela Direção-Geral da Saúde, que envia os dados diretamente para o registo civil [3][4]. O procedimento inicial depende do local e das circunstâncias do falecimento:

  • Óbito em hospital ou unidade de saúde: O médico assistente da unidade hospitalar verifica o óbito, emite o Certificado Médico de Óbito diretamente na plataforma SICO e transfere o corpo para a casa mortuária do hospital [3][4]. Entregue o passaporte brasileiro (e o Título de Residência ou Cartão de Cidadão, caso a pessoa falecida o possuísse) para que a identificação e a filiação fiquem registadas sem divergências [1][4].
  • Óbito fora do hospital (domicílio, hotel, alojamento ou via pública): Deve contactar-se de imediato o número europeu de emergência 112 (ou a autoridade policial local, PSP ou GNR) [1][4]. Se a morte tiver causa natural conhecida e houver médico assistente ou delegado de saúde (autoridade de saúde) que possa atestar a causa da morte, este emite o Certificado Médico de Óbito no SICO [3][4].
  • Morte súbita, violenta ou de causa desconhecida (intervenção do Ministério Público e INMLCF): Se o óbito ocorrer sem assistência médica prévia, de forma súbita ou suspeita, a autoridade policial comunica o facto ao Ministério Público, que determina a remoção do corpo para o gabinete médico-legal do Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal e Ciências Forenses (INMLCF) para autópsia ou exame pericial [3][4]. Só após a liberação pelo Ministério Público e o registo no SICO pelo médico legista é que a agência funerária pode assumir o serviço [3][4].

steps.title: Verificar seguros de assistência, contratar uma agência funerária e outorgar procuração se a família estiver no Brasil
steps.html:
Antes de contratar diretamente o serviço funerário, verifique se o seu familiar possuía seguro de viagem, seguro de saúde internacional, plano de assistência associado a cartão de crédito ou seguro de vida com cobertura de repatriação funerária [1]. Quando há apólice ativa, a seguradora aciona diretamente a funerária internacional e assume as despesas cobertas [1]. Note que o Estado brasileiro e os Consulados-Gerais não dispõem de verba para custear funerais, cremações ou traslado de restos mortais ou cinzas [1].

Caso não exista seguro aplicável, a família deve contratar uma agência funerária habilitada em Portugal (registada junto à Direção-Geral das Atividades Económicas - DGAE) para tratar do registo civil, preparação e transporte internacional ou funeral local [1][2]:

  • Escolha da agência funerária em Portugal: Pode consultar as informações de orientação consular do Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa (plantão consular para emergências: +351 962 520 581) [1] ou contactar a Associação Nacional de Empresas Lutuosas (telefone: +351 218 687 978) para identificar agências funerárias habilitadas [2]. A Clarvia fornece referências associativas e públicas apenas para orientação e não recomenda, não endossa nem classifica prestadores funerários específicos.
  • Como autorizar os procedimentos quando a família está no Brasil: Se nenhum familiar puder deslocar-se a Portugal, o familiar mais próximo no Brasil pode outorgar uma procuração (pública em cartório de notas no Brasil ou particular com firma reconhecida, apostilada nos termos da Convenção da Apostila da Haia) conferindo poderes à agência funerária portuguesa contratada ou a um representante em Portugal para retirar o corpo, declarar o óbito, requerer o registo consular e autorizar a cremação ou o traslado internacional [1].

steps.title: Declarar o óbito na Conservatória do Registo Civil no prazo de 48 horas
steps.html:
O óbito ocorrido em território português tem de ser declarado no prazo legal de 48 horas após o falecimento ou após a liberação médico-legal pelo INMLCF [4]. Na prática, a agência funerária contratada realiza a declaração em qualquer Conservatória do Registo Civil (supervisionada pelo Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado - Linha Registos: +351 211 950 500) com base no Certificado Médico de Óbito eletrónico já inserido no SICO e nos documentos de identificação da pessoa falecida [3][4].

A Conservatória do Registo Civil lavra gratuitamente o Assento de Óbito e emite a Certidão de Óbito portuguesa, necessária para o alvará de sepultamento, cremação ou trasladação internacional [4]. Para fins consulares e de traslado para o Brasil, solicite também à agência funerária a declaração médica complementar com a indicação expressa da causa mortis (extraída do SICO/DGS), uma vez que o assento civil português padrão não especifica a causa médica da morte e as autoridades brasileiras a exigem [1][5].

steps.title: Efetuar o Registo Consular de Óbito e organizar o traslado para o Brasil ou a cremação local
steps.html:
Para que o falecimento produza efeitos jurídicos no Brasil e permita a entrada dos restos mortais ou cinzas em território brasileiro, o óbito deve ser registado na repartição consular brasileira com jurisdição sobre o local do falecimento em Portugal (o Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Lisboa para Lisboa, Centro e Ilhas; o Consulado-Geral do Brasil no Porto para o Norte e parte do Centro; ou o Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Faro para o Algarve e Alentejo) [1]:

  • Emissão da Certidão Consular de Óbito: O pedido é submetido na plataforma eletrónica e-Consular pelo familiar declarante ou pelo representante da agência funerária devidamente autorizado, apresentando o Assento de Óbito português, o documento médico com a causa mortis, o passaporte ou documento de identidade brasileiro e a certidão de nascimento ou casamento da pessoa falecida [1].
  • Traslado internacional de corpo para o Brasil: Exige o embalsamamento (tanatopraxia/formolização), acondicionamento em urna funerária impermeável com revestimento interno de zinco hermeticamente fechado, alvará de trasladação internacional / livre-trânsito mortuário emitido em Portugal, atestado sanitário de inexistência de doença infectocontagiosa e a Certidão Consular de Óbito [1][5]. No aeroporto de chegada no Brasil, a liberação sanitária segue as normas da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (telefone no Brasil: 0800 642 9782), devendo uma funerária receptora brasileira receber a urna no terminal de cargas [5].
  • Cremação em Portugal e transporte de cinzas: Caso a família opte pela cremação em Portugal (mediante autorização do familiar legitimado e confirmação médica/judicial), as cinzas são entregues numa urna lacrada acompanhada do certificado de cremação e da Certidão Consular de Óbito, podendo ser transportadas por via aérea para o Brasil conforme as regras da companhia aérea e da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária [1][5].

steps.title: Transcrever o óbito em Cartório no Brasil e comunicar à Segurança Social e ao INSS
steps.html:
Concluídos o registo consular e o funeral ou traslado, devem ser regularizados os registos civis e previdenciários nos dois países:

  • Transcrição da Certidão Consular de Óbito no Brasil: A Certidão Consular de Óbito emitida pelo Consulado-Geral em Portugal deve ser trasladada (transcrita) no Cartório do 1.º Ofício de Registro Civil das Pessoas Naturais do último domicílio da pessoa falecida no Brasil (ou no Cartório do 1.º Ofício do Distrito Federal, se não houver domicílio anterior no Brasil) para que passe a produzir plenos efeitos civis, bancários e sucessórios (inventário) no Brasil [1].
  • Prestações por morte em Portugal e no Brasil (Acordo Previdenciário Brasil-Portugal):
    • Em Portugal: Se a pessoa falecida contribuía ou era pensionista em Portugal, comunique o óbito à Segurança Social (telefone: +351 210 545 400 ou 300 502 502) para verificar o direito ao subsídio por morte, ao reembolso de despesas de funeral e à pensão de sobrevivência para o cônjuge, unido de facto ou descendentes elegíveis [6].
    • No Brasil: Se a pessoa falecida era segurada ou aposentada pelo regime brasileiro, comunique o óbito ao Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (telefone no Brasil: 135; portal Meu INSS) para requerer a pensão por morte para os dependentes habilitados conforme o vínculo familiar (cônjuge, companheiro ou filhos menores ou inválidos) [7]. Ao abrigo do Acordo de Segurança Social entre o Brasil e Portugal, os períodos de contribuição cumpridos em ambos os países podem ser totalizados para abertura do direito às prestações de sobrevivência [6][7].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos detalhar a jurisdição consular e os procedimentos específicos aplicáveis, em qual município de Portugal ocorreu o falecimento (num hospital ou fora do hospital) e os familiares encontram-se atualmente em Portugal ou no Brasil?

title: What to Do When a British Citizen Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a British Citizen Dies in France: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between France and United Kingdom: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a British citizen dies in France, medical verification and civil registration take place first in the French municipality (commune) where the death occurred, while a licensed funeral director coordinates prefectural, consular, and UK authorities for repatriation or local funeral arrangements.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Verification of Death and French Medical Death Certificate
steps.html:
The mandatory first step is to have a physician verify the death and issue the French medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès, on paper form Cerfa or electronically via the CertDc application), which is required to register the death at the town hall (mairie) and authorise any funeral transport or procedure [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or care home (EHPAD): The attending hospital or facility doctor issues the certificat médical de décès directly [1][2]. The deceased person's body can remain in the facility's mortuary suite (chambre mortuaire) pending funeral arrangements.
  • Death outside a healthcare facility (private home, hotel, holiday home, or public place): Call the French emergency medical service (SAMU) on 15 (or the European emergency number 112) immediately so that a doctor attends to certify the death and complete the certificate [1]. Once the medical certificate is signed and provided there is no judicial hold, a licensed funeral operator can transfer the body to a funeral home (chambre funéraire) within 48 hours of death [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or suspicious death (obstacle médico-légal): If the cause of death is unknown, violent, or suspicious, the doctor ticks the medico-legal hold box (obstacle médico-légal) on the medical certificate [1][3]. Law enforcement (National Police or Gendarmerie) and the Public Prosecutor (procureur de la République) then take charge of the investigation (which may include transfer to a forensic institute for an autopsy), and burial, cremation, or repatriation cannot proceed until the prosecutor issues formal judicial burial/removal clearance (permis d'inhumer) [1][3].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage and Appoint a Funeral Director in France and the UK
steps.html:
Do not attempt to handle prefectural permits or international air freight formalities without a licensed funeral operator. Before signing an estimate (devis) with a funeral company, verify any existing assistance coverage [3]:

  • Travel insurance, medical assistance, or bank card coverage: If your family member was visiting France temporarily or held repatriation insurance, contact the insurer's 24-hour emergency assistance centre immediately before making any financial commitment [3]. The insurer typically appoints the funeral directors in France and the UK directly.
  • Appointing a licensed funeral operator: If no insurance applies, the family appoints a licensed funeral company in France (entreprise de pompes funèbres habilitée) or a UK funeral director working with a French international partner [1][3]. In France, you can locate a licensed professional through the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF, phone +33 1 55 43 30 00, email contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] or the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF, phone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. In the United Kingdom, the official directory of the National Association of Funeral Directors (NAFD, phone +44 121 711 1343, email info@nafd.org.uk) allows you to appoint a UK funeral director to receive the coffin or urn [6].
  • Role of British consular assistance: Contact the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and the consular services of the British Embassy Paris (24/7 consular assistance on +33 1 44 51 31 00 from within France or +44 20 7008 5000 from the UK) [3]. The British consular network provides a list of English-speaking funeral directors in France, guides the family on local procedures, and cancels the British passport, though it cannot pay for funeral or repatriation costs [3].

steps.title: Register the Death at the French Town Hall Within 24 Hours and Obtain the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
Under the official rules published on Service-Public.fr, the death must be declared within 24 hours of medical certification (excluding weekends and public holidays) at the civil status office (service de l'état civil) of the town hall (mairie) of the municipality where the death occurred [1][2]:

  • Who files the declaration: If the death occurred in a hospital, the facility may transmit the declaration directly to the mairie; in practice, families usually authorise their appointed French funeral operator to complete this step [1][2]. You must provide the certificat médical de décès together with the deceased person's British passport (and, if available, their birth or marriage certificate) [1][2].
  • Documents to request from the mairie and the doctor: Request several full certified copies of the French death record (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès) as well as multilingual death certificate extracts (extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues - Form C / Formule C under the 1976 Vienna Convention) [1][3]. Because a French civil death record never states the medical cause of death, also ask the hospital doctor or the physician who certified the death for a separate medical certificate (attestation médicale) stating the cause of death, which UK authorities require for repatriation [3].

steps.title: Arrange a Local Funeral in France or Repatriation to the United Kingdom
steps.html:
The person authorised to arrange the funeral (personne ayant qualité pour pourvoir aux funérailles) chooses between a local funeral in France and repatriation to the United Kingdom [1][3]:

  • Option A - Burial or cremation in France: In metropolitan France, burial (inhumation) or cremation (crémation) must take place at least 24 hours and no more than 14 calendar days after death (prefectural extensions may be granted in specific circumstances) [7]. The mayor (maire) of the municipality of death (or cremation) issues the coffin-closing permit (autorisation de fermeture du cercueil) and the burial or cremation permit [7]. If cremation takes place in France followed by transport of the ashes to the UK, the sealed urn travels with the death certificate, the cremation certificate (certificat de crémation), and, where applicable, the prefectural transit permit [3][8].
  • Option B - Repatriating the coffin to the United Kingdom: The French funeral operator applies to the prefecture (préfecture) of the department where the coffin is sealed to obtain the prefectural mortuary transit permit (arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire) [8]. The body undergoes required preservation treatment (soins de conservation) and is placed in a hermetically sealed coffin (with a sealed metal liner and purifying filter) under official supervision prior to air or cross-Channel transport [8].
  • Arrival formalities in the United Kingdom (England and Wales vs Scotland):
    • In England and Wales: Every body repatriated from abroad falls under the jurisdiction of the local Coroner for the district where the funeral will take place [3]. The UK funeral director submits the French death certificate, the medical cause-of-death certificate, and certified translations to the Coroner to obtain the burial or cremation order (Coroner's Order / Form 104 Out-of-England); if the death was violent, unnatural, or unexplained, the Coroner is legally required to open an inquest [3].
    • In Scotland: There is no coroner system. Instead, the Scottish funeral director submits the foreign death certificate and medical documentation to the Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) of Healthcare Improvement Scotland (phone +44 131 623 4300) to obtain authorisation for burial or cremation in Scotland [9], while sudden or suspicious deaths abroad of Scottish residents may be reported to the Procurator Fiscal at the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (phone +44 300 020 3000) [10].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Administrative Steps in the United Kingdom and France
steps.html:
Once the death certificates have been issued, administrative, pension, and estate procedures are divided between the two countries:

  • In the United Kingdom (pensions, tax, and probate): If the deceased was habitually resident in England, Wales, or Scotland and died during a temporary stay in France, the UK government's Tell Us Once service allows you to notify most UK government departments simultaneously (including HMRC, DWP, DVLA, and HM Passport Office) [11]. Conversely, if your relative lived permanently in France, Tell Us Once is not available: you should contact the International Pension Centre of the Department for Work and Pensions directly (phone +44 191 218 7777) regarding the UK State Pension, as well as HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) [11][12]. To administer bank accounts and assets located in the UK, the executor or next of kin applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration in England and Wales) or Confirmation (in Scotland) [11].
  • In France (bank accounts, CPAM, and notarial estate settlement): If your relative lived in France or owned assets there, notify French banks (which freeze individual accounts upon receipt of the death certificate), the local health insurance fund (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM, reachable on 3646 within France or +33 1 84 90 36 46 from abroad), and the French tax authorities [1]. Settling an estate that includes real property in France (or where the deceased had their habitual residence in France) requires a French notary (notaire) to draw up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) and property transfer certificate (attestation immobilière), with inheritance tax declarations generally due within 6 months (or 12 months if the death occurred outside metropolitan France); you can consult the official directory of the Notaires de France (phone +33 1 44 90 30 00) [13].

closingQuestion: So that we can give you exact local details, in which French département or municipality (commune) did the death occur (and was your relative a resident of France or visiting from the UK), and in which part of the United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) will the funeral or estate administration take place?

fr.title: Que faire lorsqu'un citoyen britannique décède en France : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Étapes officielles lors du décès d'un ressortissant britannique en France : certificat médical de décès, déclaration en mairie dans les 24 heures (acte plurilingue Formule C), opérateur funéraire et consulat britannique (FCDO), rapatriement vers le Royaume-Uni (laissez-passer préfectoral et coroner) ou obsèques en France, et démarches DWP / succession.
fr.introHtml: Toutes nos condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne de nationalité britannique décède en France, la constatation médicale et la déclaration d'état civil s'effectuent d'abord dans la commune française du décès, tandis qu'un opérateur funéraire habilité coordonne les autorisations préfectorales, consulaires et britanniques pour le rapatriement ou les obsèques.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et établissement du certificat médical de décès en France
steps.html:
La première étape obligatoire consiste à faire constater le décès par un médecin afin d'obtenir le certificat médical de décès (sur support papier Cerfa ou par voie électronique via l'application CertDc), document indispensable pour déclarer le décès en mairie et autoriser toute opération funéraire [1][2].

  • Décès à l'hôpital, en clinique ou en EHPAD : Le médecin du service établit directement le certificat médical de décès [1][2]. Le corps de la personne décédée peut reposer à la chambre mortuaire de l'établissement dans l'attente du transport funéraire.
  • Décès hors établissement de santé (domicile, hôtel, résidence secondaire ou voie publique) : Appelez immédiatement le SAMU au 15 (ou le numéro d'urgence européen 112) afin qu'un médecin se déplace pour constater le décès et rédiger le certificat [1]. Une fois le certificat signé et en l'absence d'opposition judiciaire, un opérateur funéraire peut transférer le corps vers une chambre funéraire dans un délai de 48 heures suivant le décès [1].
  • Cas de décès soudain, accidentel ou suspect (obstacle médico-légal) : Si la cause du décès est inconnue, violente ou suspecte, le médecin coche la case d'obstacle médico-légal sur le certificat [1][3]. Les forces de l'ordre (police nationale ou gendarmerie) et le procureur de la République prennent alors en charge le dossier (avec transfert éventuel vers un institut médico-légal pour autopsie), et l'inhumation, la crémation ou le rapatriement ne peuvent avoir lieu qu'après délivrance du permis d'inhumer par le parquet [1][3].

steps.title: Vérification de l'assurance et mandat donné à un opérateur funéraire en France et au Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
Ne tentez pas d'effectuer vous-même les démarches techniques auprès des préfectures ou du fret aérien. Avant de signer un devis avec une entreprise de pompes funèbres, vérifiez les garanties d'assistance existantes [3] :

  • Assurance voyage, assistance médicale ou carte bancaire : Si votre proche séjournait temporairement en France ou disposait d'une assurance rapatriement, contactez immédiatement le plateau d'assistance 24h/24 de l'assureur avant tout engagement financier [3]. L'assureur mandate généralement lui-même les opérateurs funéraires en France et au Royaume-Uni.
  • Mandat à un opérateur funéraire habilité : En l'absence d'assurance, la famille mandate une entreprise de pompes funèbres habilitée en France ou un directeur funéraire au Royaume-Uni travaillant avec un correspondant français [1][3]. En France, vous pouvez identifier un professionnel via la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (téléphone +33 1 55 43 30 00, courriel contact@federation-fnf.fr) [4] ou la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (téléphone +33 1 46 60 24 24) [5]. Au Royaume-Uni, l'annuaire officiel de la National Association of Funeral Directors (téléphone +44 121 711 1343, courriel info@nafd.org.uk) permet de désigner l'entreprise funéraire chargée de la réception du cercueil ou de l'urne [6].
  • Rôle de l'assistance consulaire britannique : Contactez le Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office et les services consulaires de la British Embassy Paris (assistance consulaire 24h/24 au +33 1 44 51 31 00 depuis la France ou au +44 20 7008 5000 depuis le Royaume-Uni) [3]. Le réseau consulaire britannique fournit une liste d'opérateurs funéraires anglophones en France, oriente la famille sur les procédures locales et procède à l'annulation du passeport britannique, mais il ne prend jamais en charge les frais d'obsèques ou de rapatriement [3].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès en mairie dans les 24 heures et obtention de l'acte plurilingue (Formule C)
steps.html:
Selon les règles officielles présentées sur Service-Public.fr, le décès doit être déclaré dans les 24 heures suivant sa constatation (hors week-ends et jours fériés) auprès du service de l'état civil de la mairie de la commune où le décès a eu lieu [1][2].

  • Qui effectue la déclaration : Si le décès est survenu à l'hôpital, l'établissement peut transmettre la déclaration directement à la mairie ; dans la pratique, la famille confie le plus souvent cette démarche à l'opérateur funéraire français mandaté [1][2]. Il faut présenter le certificat médical de décès ainsi que le passeport britannique de la personne décédée (et, si possible, son acte de naissance ou de mariage) [1][2].
  • Documents à demander à la mairie et au médecin : Demandez plusieurs copies intégrales de l'acte de décès français ainsi que des extraits d'acte de décès plurilingues (Formule C issue de la Convention de Vienne de 1976) [1][3]. Comme l'acte de décès français ne mentionne jamais la cause médicale du décès, demandez également au médecin hospitalier ou au médecin ayant constaté le décès une attestation médicale séparée précisant la cause du décès (indispensable pour les autorités britanniques lors d'un rapatriement) [3].

steps.title: Organisation des obsèques en France ou du rapatriement vers le Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
La personne ayant qualité pour pourvoir aux funérailles choisit entre des obsèques locales en France et le rapatriement vers le Royaume-Uni [1][3] :

  • Option A - Inhumation ou crémation en France : En France métropolitaine, l'inhumation ou la crémation doit intervenir au moins 24 heures et au plus 14 jours calendaires après le décès (des dérogations préfectorales pouvant être accordées) [7]. Le maire de la commune du décès (ou du lieu de crémation) délivre l'autorisation de fermeture du cercueil et le permis d'inhumer ou l'autorisation de crémation [7]. En cas de crémation en France suivie du transport des cendres vers le Royaume-Uni, l'urne scellée voyage avec l'acte de décès, le certificat de crémation et, le cas échéant, le laissez-passer préfectoral [3][8].
  • Option B - Rapatriement du cercueil vers le Royaume-Uni : L'opérateur funéraire français accomplit les formalités auprès de la préfecture du département où a lieu la fermeture du cercueil pour obtenir l'arrêté préfectoral de laissez-passer mortuaire [8]. Le corps fait l'objet des soins de conservation requis et est placé dans un cercueil hermétique (enveloppe métallique scellée avec filtre épurateur) sous contrôle officiel avant le transport aérien ou transmanche [8].
  • Formalités à l'arrivée au Royaume-Uni (Angleterre/Pays de Galles vs Écosse) :
    • En Angleterre et au Pays de Galles : Tout corps rapatrié de l'étranger relève du contrôle du Coroner local du lieu des funérailles [3]. Le directeur funéraire britannique transmet au Coroner l'acte de décès français, le certificat médical indiquant la cause du décès et leur traduction afin d'obtenir le certificat autorisant l'inhumation ou la crémation (Coroner's Order / Form 104 Out-of-England) ; si le décès est survenu de manière violente, non naturelle ou inexpliquée, le Coroner a l'obligation légale d'ouvrir une enquête (inquest) [3].
    • En Écosse : Il n'existe pas de Coroner. Le directeur funéraire écossais soumet le certificat de décès étranger et les pièces médicales au Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) de Healthcare Improvement Scotland (téléphone +44 131 623 4300) pour obtenir l'autorisation d'inhumer ou de crémer en Écosse [9], tandis que les décès soudains ou suspects à l'étranger concernant un résident écossais peuvent relever du Procurator Fiscal au sein du Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (téléphone +44 300 020 3000) [10].

steps.title: Démarches administratives après le décès au Royaume-Uni et en France
steps.html:
Une fois l'acte de décès obtenu, les démarches administratives et successorales se répartissent entre les deux pays :

  • Au Royaume-Uni (pensions, fiscalité et probate) : Si la personne décédée résidait habituellement en Angleterre, au Pays de Galles ou en Écosse et est décédée lors d'un séjour temporaire en France, le service gouvernemental britannique Tell Us Once permet de notifier simultanément la plupart des administrations (HMRC, DWP, DVLA, bureau des passeports) [11]. En revanche, si votre proche résidait de façon permanente en France, Tell Us Once ne s'applique pas : il convient alors de notifier directement l'International Pension Centre du Department for Work and Pensions (téléphone +44 191 218 7777) pour la retraite d'État britannique (UK State Pension) ainsi que HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) [11][12]. Pour débloquer les comptes et biens situés au Royaume-Uni, l'exécuteur testamentaire ou les proches demandent le Grant of Probate (en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles) ou la Confirmation (en Écosse) [11].
  • En France (comptes bancaires, CPAM et succession notariale) : Si votre proche résidait en France ou y détenait des biens, informez les banques françaises (qui bloquent les comptes individuels dès réception de l'acte de décès), la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM, joignable au 3646 depuis la France ou au +33 1 84 90 36 46 depuis l'étranger) et l'administration fiscale française [1]. Le règlement d'une succession comprenant un bien immobilier en France (ou lorsque la personne décédée avait sa résidence habituelle en France) impose l'intervention d'un notaire français pour établir l'acte de notoriété et l'attestation immobilière dans les 6 mois (ou 12 mois si le décès est hors de France métropolitaine selon le cas) ; vous pouvez consulter l'annuaire officiel des Notaires de France (téléphone +33 1 44 90 30 00) [13].

fr.closingQuestion: Pour nous permettre de vous préciser les démarches locales exactes, dans quel département ou quelle commune de France le décès est-il survenu (et votre proche résidait-il en France ou au Royaume-Uni), et dans quelle nation du Royaume-Uni (Angleterre, Pays de Galles, Écosse ou Irlande du Nord) les obsèques ou les démarches sont-elles prévues ?

title: What to Do When a U.S. Citizen Dies in the Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a U.S. Citizen Dies in the Philippines: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official steps when a U.S. citizen dies in the Philippines: Certificate of Death and Municipal Health Officer / PNP clearance, Local Civil Registrar and PSA registration, Bureau of Quarantine and U.S. Embassy Manila CRDA / Consular Mortuary Certificate, repatriation or local cremation, and SSA / VA survivor claims.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a United States citizen dies in the Philippines, medical certification and civil registration take place first in the Philippine city or municipality of death, while a licensed mortuary coordinates with Philippine health authorities and the U.S. Embassy in Manila (or the U.S. Consular Agency in Cebu) for the Consular Report of Death Abroad and international transport.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death (Municipal Form No. 103) and Health Officer or Police Clearance
steps.html:
Every death in the Philippines must first be documented on the official Certificate of Death (Municipal Form No. 103, prepared in four copies), which records the personal particulars of the deceased and the medical cause of death [1][2]:

  • Death in a hospital or clinic: The attending physician completes and signs the medical certification section of Municipal Form No. 103 directly [1]. Once hospital billing and release formalities are completed, a licensed funeral home can transfer the body to its mortuary facility.
  • Death outside a hospital (residence, hotel, or public place): Report the death immediately to local barangay officials and the Philippine National Police (PNP, emergency hotline 911). When a death occurs without medical attendance, the Municipal Health Officer (MHO) or City Health Officer (CHO) of the local government unit (for example, in Manila, Quezon City, or Cebu City) must examine the deceased and certify the cause of death on Municipal Form No. 103 [1][2]. If the death was sudden, accidental, or under unclear circumstances, PNP Scene of the Crime Operatives (SOCO) or the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) conduct a medico-legal investigation before releasing the body [2][3].
  • 48-hour sanitary rule: Under Chapter XXI (Section 91) of Presidential Decree No. 856 (the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines, enforced by the Department of Health and local health officers), an unembalmed body may not remain unburied or undisposed of for more than 48 hours after death unless held in authorized mortuary cold storage or pending a medico-legal investigation [2][4]. Families planning international repatriation or a viewing should therefore instruct a licensed mortuary promptly.

steps.title: Check Insurance, Appoint Philippine and U.S. Funeral Directors, and Authorize a Representative
steps.html:
Do not attempt to navigate airport cargo, quarantine clearances, or embassy mortuary paperwork alone. Before signing an independent contract with a funeral parlor, verify whether existing coverage applies [3]:

  • Travel or medical-assistance insurance: Check whether your family member held travel medical insurance or medical evacuation/repatriation coverage, and call the insurer's 24-hour assistance center before making independent financial commitments.
  • Appointing Philippine and U.S. funeral homes: To handle local preparation, cremation, or international shipment, the legal next of kin appoints a licensed Philippine funeral home alongside a receiving funeral home in the United States [3][5]. The U.S. Embassy in the Philippines publishes an informational list of funeral homes in Metro Manila, Cebu, Pampanga, and other regions (provided as public-source information for orientation; Clarvia does not endorse, recommend, or rank any provider) [3][6]. In the United States, you can locate a licensed receiving funeral home in the destination state through the National Funeral Directors Association (toll-free 800-228-6332 or +1 262-789-1880) [7].
  • How next of kin in the United States grant authority: If no immediate family member is physically present in the Philippines, the legal next of kin in the United States must execute a notarized Next-of-Kin Affidavit / Letter of Authorization stating the chosen disposition of the remains (repatriation or local cremation/burial) and naming the authorized Philippine funeral home or local representative, and send it to the U.S. Embassy (ACSInfoManila@state.gov) and the appointed mortuary [3][6].

steps.title: Register the Death Within 30 Days with the Local Civil Registrar (LCR) and Request PSA Certificates
steps.html:
Under Philippine civil registration law administered by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA central inquiry line +63 2 8461-0500), the death must be registered at the Local Civil Registry Office (LCRO) of the city or municipality where the death occurred within 30 calendar days of the date of death [1]:

  • Health Officer review and LCR filing: Before the Local Civil Registrar records the death, the Municipal or City Health Officer reviews and signs the medical certification on Municipal Form No. 103 (forwarded within 48 hours of certification) and issues the local burial, cremation, or transfer permit [1][2]. In practice, the appointed Philippine funeral home files Municipal Form No. 103 with the LCRO on the family's behalf [1][3]. (Deaths reported after the 30-day period are treated as delayed registrations requiring additional affidavits and a 10-day municipal posting period [1].)
  • PSA Security Paper (SECPA) Death Certificate: Ask the funeral home and Local Civil Registrar for both certified local copies of the registered Certificate of Death and expedited electronic transmittal to the Philippine Statistics Authority so you can obtain official PSA Death Certificates printed on Security Paper (SECPA) [1].

steps.title: Report the Death to the U.S. Embassy in Manila (or Cebu Consular Agency) for the CRDA and Export Permits
steps.html:
Report the death of the U.S. citizen as soon as possible to the U.S. Embassy in the Philippines in Manila (American Citizens Services telephone +63 2 5301-2000, email ACSInfoManila@state.gov with the subject line "Death of a U.S. Citizen") or, for deaths in the Visayas, to the U.S. Consular Agency in Cebu (telephone +63 32 231-1261) [3][8]:

  • Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060): Provide the certified Philippine Certificate of Death, the deceased's U.S. passport, and proof of the next of kin's identity and relationship [3]. The Embassy cancels the U.S. passport and issues the official electronic Consular Report of Death Abroad (CRDA, Form DS-2060), which U.S. banks, insurers, courts, and federal agencies accept as official English-language proof of death [3]. The U.S. government cannot pay funeral, cremation, or repatriation expenses [3].
  • Repatriating casketed (embalmed) human remains to the United States: Your Philippine funeral director obtains the local Health Officer's Certificate of Non-Contagious Disease and Transfer Permit, a Quarantine Permit from the Philippine Bureau of Quarantine (under the Department of Health, telephone +63 2 5318-7500) [4], and the U.S. Embassy's Consular Mortuary Certificate (which includes the Consular Mortuary Certificate, Affidavit of Foreign Funeral Director, and Certificate of Hermetic Sealing) [3][5]. Under the federal rules of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC, 42 CFR 71.55, telephone 800-232-4636), embalmed human remains placed in a hermetically sealed casket and accompanied by the official death certificate stating the cause of death and the consular mortuary documents may be imported into the United States consigned to a licensed U.S. funeral home without a separate CDC import permit, provided the person did not die of a quarantinable communicable disease [5].
  • Transporting cremated remains (ashes) to the United States: If the family chooses local cremation in the Philippines, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention does not require a CDC import permit for fully cremated remains [5]. The ashes must be placed in a sealed, non-metallic urn that can pass airport X-ray security screening and be accompanied by the certified Philippine Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, the Bureau of Quarantine clearance, and U.S. Customs declaration upon arrival [3][4][5].

steps.title: Coordinate U.S. State Reception and Notify Social Security (SSA / FBU Manila) and Veterans Affairs (VA)
steps.html:
Once the CRDA (Form DS-2060) and Philippine death certificates are issued, complete the U.S. reception and federal benefit notifications:

  • Reception in the destination U.S. state: For casketed repatriation, the receiving U.S. funeral home clears the shipment through U.S. Customs and Border Protection at the arrival airport and obtains the state burial-transit permit in the destination U.S. state [5][7].
  • Social Security Administration (SSA) and FBU Manila: Report the death immediately so monthly retirement or disability payments stop (any benefit paid for the month of death or later must be returned) and to claim the one-time lump-sum death payment and monthly survivor benefits if eligible family members (such as a surviving spouse, eligible divorced spouse, minor or disabled child, or dependent parent) survive the deceased [9][10]. Families in the United States can call the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213 [9]. If the deceased or surviving beneficiaries lived in the Philippines, report the death directly to the U.S. Embassy Manila Federal Benefits Unit (telephone +63 2 5301-6200, email FBU.Manila@ssa.gov with the subject line "Report of Death") [9][10].
  • Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and estate administration: If your family member served in the U.S. Armed Forces, notify the Department of Veterans Affairs (U.S. toll-free 1-800-827-1000, or the VA Regional Benefit Office at the U.S. Embassy in Manila) to check eligibility for burial allowances, a U.S. government headstone or marker, national cemetery interment, or Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) [11]. Use the CRDA (Form DS-2060) and PSA Death Certificate to administer U.S. bank accounts, life insurance, and probate in the U.S. state of domicile, as well as any local Philippine accounts [1][3].

closingQuestion: To help us provide exact local details, in which city or municipality in the Philippines did your family member pass away (and are you planning casketed repatriation or cremation), and in which U.S. state will the remains or estate be handled?

title: What to Do When a Romanian Citizen Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Romanian Citizen Dies in Italy: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step cross-border bereavement checklist between Italy and Romania: medical death certification, licensed international funeral providers, civil death registration and multilingual extracts, consular notification and repatriation or local burial permits, and survivor pensions and estate administration.
introHtml: Please accept our sincere condolences for the loss of your family member. When a Romanian citizen dies in Italy, medical verification, civil death registration, and the issuance of the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) for international transport are handled by the Italian authorities (the local health authority, Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL, and the municipality, Comune, where the death occurred), while transcription of the death into the Romanian civil registry and funeral grant claims involve the Romanian consular network and the social security institutions of both countries.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Pronouncement of Death and Necroscopic Certificate (in a Hospital or Outside a Hospital)
steps.html:
The initial medical procedure depends on where the death occurred, in accordance with the Italian National Mortuary Police Regulations (Regolamento nazionale di polizia mortuaria, Presidential Decree D.P.R. No. 285/1990) [1]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or residential care facility: The facility's medical management (direzione sanitaria) certifies the death, completes the death notice and the ISTAT statistical cause-of-death form (scheda ISTAT), and transmits the paperwork directly to the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the competent municipality [1].
  • Death outside a hospital (private home, temporary accommodation, workplace, or public place): Contact the attending physician or the single European emergency number 112 (or 118) immediately for the initial pronouncement of death (constatazione di decesso) and completion of the cause-of-death report within 24 hours [1]. Subsequently, the public health medical examiner (medico necroscopo) appointed by the territorially competent local health authority (ASL or ATS) performs the mandatory necroscopic examination (normally between 15 and 30 hours after death) and issues the necroscopic certificate (certificato necroscopico) required to seal the coffin and authorise burial or transport [1].
  • Sudden, suspicious, or workplace accident death: If the death occurred at work, in a public place, or from violent or unclear causes, law enforcement intervenes and the body is placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority; in such cases, removal of the body, burial, or repatriation can proceed only after formal judicial clearance (nulla osta della Procura della Repubblica) is issued by the Public Prosecutor's Office [1].

steps.title: Appoint an Authorised Funeral Director and Provide Family Authorisation
steps.html:
Before signing a private funeral contract, check whether the deceased person held an insurance policy (travel, accident, or medical repatriation insurance) providing direct assistance through an emergency operations centre. In the absence of insurance coverage, the family may appoint a licensed funeral company in Italy (impresa di onoranze funebri) experienced in international funeral transport between Italy and Romania [2]. To locate qualified operators in Italy, you can consult the national trade federations: FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri, tel. +39 051 6650285, email info@feniof.it) [4] and FederCoFIt (Federazione Comparto Funerario Italiano, tel. +39 02 33403992, email info@federcofit.it) [5]. Clarvia provides these directory references solely for orientation and does not recommend, endorse, or rank specific funeral companies.

  • What the funeral director handles: Acting on the family's behalf, the appointed funeral company manages the paperwork with the hospital medical management or the ASL, files the death declaration with the municipality (Comune), prepares the regulation double coffin for international transport, and applies for the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) [1][2].
  • Family members residing in Romania: If the closest next of kin are in Romania and cannot travel to Italy, they can issue a formal written authorisation (delega scritta) to the funeral company (accompanied by a copy of the authorising family member's identity document) or execute a notarised power of attorney (procura notarile) in Romania authorising a representative in Italy or the funeral agency to claim the body and request municipal permits [1][2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Status Office and Obtain the Multilingual Extract (Form C)
steps.html:
The declaration of death (dichiarazione di morte) must be filed within 24 hours of the death at the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the Italian municipality (Comune) where the death occurred (for example, at the Civil Status offices of Roma Capitale, the Comune di Milano, or the Comune di Torino) [1][2]. In standard practice, the declaration is submitted by the funeral company authorised by the family or by the hospital medical management [1].

  • Certificates to request immediately in multiple copies: In addition to the burial permit and the domestic Italian death certificate, ask the municipal Civil Status Office to issue several copies of the multilingual death certificate extract (Form C / Modello C, estratto per riassunto dell'atto di morte su modello plurilingue) under the Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976 [2].
  • Exemption from Apostille and translation: Because both Italy and Romania are parties to the 1976 Vienna Convention, the multilingual death extract (Form C / Modello C) is directly valid in Romania and at Romanian Consulates without legalisation (Prefecture Apostille) or certified translation [2]. Conversely, if a domestic-only Italian death certificate is used, it will require an Apostille from the competent Italian Prefecture (Prefettura) and a certified translation into Romanian [2].

steps.title: Obtain the Municipal Mortuary Passport, Coordinate Repatriation to Romania, and Complete Consular Transcription
steps.html:
For the international transport of the body from Italy to Romania (whether by road in an authorised hearse or by air), the funeral company applies to the Civil Status / Mortuary Police Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile / Polizia Mortuaria) of the Italian municipality of death for the Passaporto Mortuario (Mortuary Passport) under the Berlin International Convention of 10 February 1937 and Article 27 of D.P.R. 285/1990 [1][2]:

  • Requirements for transporting the coffin or ashes: For repatriation of a body, Italian public health regulations require a double coffin (an outer wooden casket and a hermetically soldered inner zinc coffin) accompanied by the official coffin-sealing report (verbale di chiusura del feretro) and the ASL sanitary certificate [1][2]. Under the international agreements applied by Romania, no separate Romanian consular mortuary passport is required for repatriation from Italy: the Passaporto Mortuario issued by the Italian municipality together with the death certificate extract is sufficient [2]. If the deceased is cremated in Italy and the cinerary urn is transported to Romania, the sealed urn travels with the death certificate and the ash transport permit (autorizzazione al trasporto delle ceneri) issued by the Italian municipality [2].
  • Consular assistance and transcription into Romanian civil registers: To report the death or obtain emergency consular assistance, you can contact the territorially competent Romanian consular mission in Italy (for example, the Consolato Generale di Romania a Roma - Consulate General of Romania in Rome, emergency phone for deaths and severe emergencies +39 345 147 3935; or the Consulate General of Romania in Milan on emergency phone +39 366 108 1444, as well as the consulates in Turin, Bologna, Bari, Catania, and Trieste) [2][3]. The Italian death record must be transcribed into the Romanian civil status registers (within the standard 6-month timeframe) to obtain a Romanian death certificate (certificat de deces): the application can be submitted at the competent Romanian Consulate in Italy by appointment via the official consular portal (eConsulat.ro), or directly in Romania at the town hall (Primăria / Serviciul Public Comunitar Local de Evidență a Persoanelor - SPCLEP) of the deceased person's last Romanian domicile, enclosing the multilingual Form C extract, the deceased's Romanian identity documents, and their birth and marriage certificates [2].

steps.title: Claim the Romanian Funeral Grant (CNPP), Handle Italian Social Security (INPS and INAIL), and Settle the Estate
steps.html:
Once the death certificate extracts have been obtained, family members can initiate pension, funeral benefit, insurance, and banking procedures in both countries:

  • Funeral grant in Romania (ajutor de deces): If the deceased person was insured or retired under the Romanian public pension system (or held insured status during the 6 months prior to death), or if a dependent family member of a person insured or retired in Romania has died, the person who proves they paid the funeral expenses can claim the funeral grant (ajutor de deces) from the Casa Națională de Pensii Publice (CNPP, National House of Public Pensions, Bucharest headquarters tel. +40 21 318 88 00, email petitii.sesizari@cnpp.ro, through the competent county pension house, Casa Județeană de Pensii) within the 3-year limitation period from the issuance of the death certificate [6]. The application must include the death certificate, the claimant's identity document, civil status records proving family relationship, and original funeral invoices/receipts; payment is normally made within 3 working days of submitting a complete claim [6].
  • INPS and INAIL procedures in Italy: If your family member worked or received a pension/benefit in Italy, the Italian municipality transmits the death notification electronically to INPS (Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale), but eligible survivors (such as a surviving spouse or dependent children) must submit an online claim (or apply free of charge through a Patronato advice centre) for a survivor's pension (pensione ai superstiti - reversibilità or pensione indiretta) or lump-sum benefit [7]. If the death resulted from a workplace accident or occupational disease (infortunio sul lavoro o malattia professionale) in Italy, the employer must file a report within 24 hours with INAIL (Istituto Nazionale per l'Assicurazione contro gli Infortuni sul Lavoro), and surviving family members are entitled to the INAIL survivor's annuity (rendita ai superstiti) and the INAIL funeral grant (assegno funerario) [8].
  • Banks and succession: Present the multilingual death certificate extract to any banks in Italy or Romania where the deceased held accounts. In Italy, an inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) must be filed with the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) within 12 months of the opening of the succession if the deceased was resident in Italy or owned real estate or taxable assets in Italy.

closingQuestion: So that we can give you more specific guidance on territorial jurisdiction, in which Italian municipality (Comune) did the death occur, and have you already decided whether to repatriate your family member to Romania or arrange burial or cremation in Italy?
caseDependentItems: Italian Comune Stato Civile registration and ASL medico necroscopo (or Procura nulla osta if sudden or workplace death)
