title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Italy
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Kingdom & Italy
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Kingdom and Italy: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and holds residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across the United Kingdom and Italy, early planning across both jurisdictions helps protect the person's medical wishes and prevents administrative delays. Because health systems, powers of attorney, and succession rules operate independently under UK common law (or Scots law) and Italian civil law, key legal instruments must be completed while your family member retains full decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
In the United Kingdom, the primary route for symptom management and specialist end-of-life care is a referral from the person's GP or hospital specialist to local National Health Service (NHS) palliative care teams and community hospices supported by networks such as Hospice UK and Marie Curie [1]. If your family member has rapidly deteriorating health needs entering a terminal phase, ask an appropriate clinician (hospital consultant, GP, or community nurse) to complete the NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track Pathway Tool so an urgent, fully NHS-funded care package at home, in a care home, or in a hospice can be put in place without means testing [1].

In Italy, access to specialist palliative care and pain therapy is guaranteed nationwide under Law no. 38/2010 through the Rete Nazionale delle Cure Palliative e Terapia del Dolore, overseen by the Ministero della Salute [2]. Care is activated via the family doctor (medico di medicina generale) or hospital specialist through the local health authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale, or ASL), which coordinates home palliative care units (UCP-DOM) and residential Hospice facilities, with directory support also available through the Società Italiana di Cure Palliative (SICP) [2]. If relocating between the UK and Italy for care, verify UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC), S1 pensioner healthcare registration, or prior planned-treatment authorisation before travel, as routine visitor cover does not fund planned cross-border care relocation or non-emergency medical transport.

steps.title: Written Advance Directives and Living Wills in Both Countries
steps.html:
Because clinical advance directives made in one country are not automatically integrated into the other country's medical registries, separate written directives should be prepared in both jurisdictions while your family member has full capacity.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person can make a written Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment (ADRT, or Living Will) under the Mental Capacity Act 2005 [1]. To refuse life-sustaining treatment (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition and hydration), the ADRT must be written, signed, witnessed, and explicitly state that the refusal applies even if life is at risk [1]. Alongside an ADRT, ask the clinical team to complete a ReSPECT emergency care and treatment summary plan and an Advance Statement of care preferences so ambulance crews and out-of-hours doctors have immediate guidance [1].
  • Italy: Under Law no. 219/2017, an adult with full mental capacity can execute Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT, commonly called a Biotestamento) to express consent or refusal regarding future diagnostic tests and medical treatments (including artificial nutrition and hydration) and to appoint a trusted healthcare representative (fiduciario) [3]. The DAT is filed in person at the Civil Status Office (Ufficio di Stato Civile) of the person's Italian municipality of residence (Comune), executed as a notarial deed before an Italian notary, or lodged at an Italian consulate abroad, and is transmitted to the Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT maintained by the Ministero della Salute [3].

steps.title: Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney
steps.html:
Italian banks, land registries, and notaries do not accept a UK Lasting Power of Attorney directly for property or banking transactions without formal Italian legal recognition, and UK institutions require domestic statutory instruments. Separate powers should be established in both jurisdictions while full legal capacity remains.

  • United Kingdom: In England and Wales, the person should execute and register two separate Lasting Powers of Attorney (LPAs) with the Office of the Public Guardian (phone 0300 456 0300): one LPA for Health and Welfare (which takes effect only when capacity is lost) and one LPA for Property and Financial Affairs (usable once registered, with the person's consent) [4]. If the person lives or holds property in Scotland, prepare a Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland), or an Enduring Power of Attorney in Northern Ireland [4].
  • Italy: For managing bank accounts, property, or tax filings in Italy, the person can sign a general or special notarial power of attorney (procura generale o speciale) before an Italian notary (regulated through the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) or at an Italian consular office in the UK. Because an ordinary Italian mandate can be affected by supervening incapacity, where vulnerability or declining capacity arises, Italian law provides for the court-supervised appointment of a support administrator (Amministrazione di Sostegno under Law no. 6/2004) by petitioning the guardianship judge (Giudice Tutelare) at the competent Italian court (Tribunale), and the person can designate their chosen support administrator in advance by public deed or authenticated private writing.

steps.title: Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both the UK and Italy provide expedited disability assessments, financial allowances, and statutory workplace leave for family caregivers.

  • United Kingdom: Under the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Special Rules for End of Life, if a clinician expects death within 12 months, ask the doctor or specialist nurse to complete an SR1 medical form [5]. This fast-tracks claims for Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance, or Universal Credit without a face-to-face assessment and at enhanced rates [5]. Unpaid caregivers providing at least 35 hours of care per week can claim Carer's Allowance, and employees in Great Britain have a statutory right to up to one week of unpaid Carer's Leave per year [6].
  • Italy: Through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS), a person with a severe, rapidly progressing or oncological illness can request an accelerated disability and severe-handicap assessment (often completed within 15 days under fast-track oncology rules) [7]. Recognition of severe disability under Law no. 104/1992 (art. 3, comma 3) entitles working family caregivers in Italy to 3 days of paid monthly leave (permessi retribuiti Legge 104) and up to 2 years of paid extraordinary caregiver leave (congedo straordinario retribuito) via INPS [7]. Where the person is assessed as 100% invalid and unable to walk independently or perform daily living acts without continuous assistance, INPS also pays the non-means-tested attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento, often referred to as assegno di accompagnamento) [8].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Estate Administration, and Post-Death Deadlines
steps.html:
Aligning wills and beneficiary arrangements in advance prevents conflicts between UK testamentary freedom and Italian forced-heirship rules (quota di legittima).

  • Cross-Border Wills Alignment: Consult a cross-border solicitor or Italian notary (via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, which oversees the Registro Generale dei Testamenti) so that UK and Italian wills complement each other without accidentally revoking earlier wills, and verify whether an explicit choice of national law under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) applies to Italian assets.
  • United Kingdom Post-Death Steps: After a death in the UK is registered, use the Tell Us Once service to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), the Department for Work and Pensions (including the DWP Bereavement Service and International Pension Centre), passport services, and local councils in one step [9]. The executor or administrator applies for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales (or Confirmation in Scotland) to release UK bank accounts and property [10].
  • Italy Post-Death Steps: In Italy, surviving spouses and eligible family members apply to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS) for survivor or reversionary pensions (pensione ai superstiti / pensione di reversibilità) [7]. Heirs and legatees must file the mandatory Italian inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) electronically with the Agenzia delle Entrate within 12 months of the date of death, which also triggers cadastral property transfers (voltura catastale) for any real estate in Italy [11].

closingQuestion: To help tailor this further, in which country is your family member currently receiving care, and what is their nationality and where are their property or bank accounts located?

it.title: Malattia terminale e pianificazione tra Regno Unito e Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi per la gestione medica e legale di una malattia grave tra Regno Unito e Italia: cure palliative, disposizioni anticipate di trattamento (DAT), procure nei due Paesi, congedi per familiari e successione.
it.introHtml: Quando a un vostro familiare viene diagnosticata una malattia grave, progressiva o in fase terminale e sussistono legami di residenza, cittadinanza, famiglia o patrimonio tra il Regno Unito e l'Italia, una pianificazione tempestiva in entrambe le giurisdizioni tutela le volontà terapeutiche della persona e previene blocchi amministrativi. Poiché i sistemi sanitari, le procure e le norme successorie operano in modo indipendente secondo la common law britannica (o il diritto scozzese) e il diritto civile italiano, gli atti giuridici fondamentali devono essere perfezionati mentre il familiare conserva la piena capacità di intendere e di volere.

steps.title: Cure Palliative, Hospice e Coordinamento Sanitario Transfrontaliero
steps.html:
• Regno Unito: Il percorso principale per il controllo dei sintomi e l'assistenza specialistica di fine vita si attiva tramite il medico di base (GP) o lo specialista ospedaliero, che può indirizzare il paziente alle équipe locali di cure palliative del National Health Service (NHS) e agli hospice territoriali supportati da reti nazionali quali Hospice UK e Marie Curie [1]. Se il familiare presenta un rapido peggioramento clinico in fase terminale, un medico o infermiere abilitato (hospital consultant, GP o community nurse) può attivare la procedura d'urgenza NHS Continuing Healthcare Fast Track Pathway Tool, così da predisporre tempestivamente un piano di assistenza interamente finanziato dal NHS a domicilio, in struttura residenziale o in hospice, senza verifica del reddito [1].
  • Italia: L'accesso alle cure palliative specialistiche e alla terapia del dolore è garantito su tutto il territorio nazionale ai sensi della Legge n. 38/2010 attraverso la Rete Nazionale delle Cure Palliative e Terapia del Dolore, coordinata dal Ministero della Salute [2]. La presa in carico viene attivata dal medico di medicina generale o dallo specialista ospedaliero tramite l'Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL) competente, che coordina le Unità di Cure Palliative Domiciliari (UCP-DOM) e le strutture residenziali Hospice, con il supporto informativo della Società Italiana di Cure Palliative (SICP) [2]. Qualora si valuti un trasferimento tra il Regno Unito e l'Italia per proseguire le cure, occorre verificare preventivamente la copertura tramite la tessera UK Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC), il modello S1 per pensionati residenti o l'autorizzazione preventiva per cure programmate all'estero (modello S2), poiché la copertura per soggiorni temporanei non finanzia trasferimenti sanitari pianificati o trasporti medici non urgenti.

steps.title: Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento e *Living Will* in Entrambi i Paesi
steps.html:
Poiché le direttive anticipate redatte in uno Stato non vengono integrate automaticamente nei registri sanitari dell'altro Paese, è opportuno predisporre documenti distinti in entrambe le giurisdizioni mentre il familiare conserva la piena capacità decisionale.

  • Regno Unito: In Inghilterra e Galles, la persona maggiorenne capace può redigere per iscritto una decisione anticipata di rifiuto di trattamento (Advance Decision to Refuse Treatment - ADRT, o Living Will) ai sensi del Mental Capacity Act 2005 [1]. Per rifiutare trattamenti di sostegno vitale (quali rianimazione cardiopolmonare, ventilazione meccanica o nutrizione e idratazione artificiali), l'ADRT deve avere forma scritta, essere firmata dall'interessato in presenza di un testimone che a sua volta sottoscrive, e specificare espressamente che il rifiuto vale anche qualora la vita sia a rischio [1]. Accanto all'ADRT, è consigliabile chiedere all'équipe medica di compilare il piano di emergenza ReSPECT (ReSPECT emergency care and treatment summary) e una dichiarazione di preferenze (Advance Statement), affinché il personale di emergenza e i medici di guardia dispongano di indicazioni immediate [1].
  • Italia: Ai sensi della Legge n. 219/2017, ogni persona maggiorenne capace di intendere e di volere può redigere le Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT, comunemente note come Biotestamento) per esprimere il proprio consenso o rifiuto in merito ad accertamenti diagnostici e trattamenti sanitari futuri (inclusi nutrizione e idratazione artificiali) e nominare un fiduciario incaricato di rappresentarla nelle relazioni con il medico e le strutture sanitarie [3]. Le DAT si depositano personalmente presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune di residenza in Italia, si redigono per atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata davanti a un notaio, oppure si depositano presso gli uffici consolari italiani all'estero, con successiva trasmissione alla Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT istituita presso il Ministero della Salute [3].

steps.title: Procure Finanziarie e Sanitarie Distinte nelle Due Giurisdizioni
steps.html:
Le banche, le conservatorie dei registri immobiliari e i notai italiani non accettano direttamente una Lasting Power of Attorney britannica per operazioni immobiliari o bancarie senza formale riconoscimento legale e traduzione certificata in Italia, e gli enti del Regno Unito richiedono gli strumenti previsti dal diritto interno britannico. Occorre pertanto istituire procure distinte in entrambi i Paesi finché permane la piena capacità di agire.

  • Regno Unito: In Inghilterra e Galles, l'interessato dovrebbe sottoscrivere e registrare due distinte procure continuative (Lasting Powers of Attorney - LPA) presso l'Office of the Public Guardian (telefono 0300 456 0300): una LPA for Health and Welfare (per salute e assistenza personale, efficace solo in caso di perdita della capacità decisionale) e una LPA for Property and Financial Affairs (per patrimonio e affari finanziari, utilizzabile subito dopo la registrazione anche con il consenso dell'interessato) [4]. Se la persona risiede o possiede beni in Scozia, occorre predisporre una Continuing and Welfare Power of Attorney registrata presso l'Office of the Public Guardian (Scotland), oppure una Enduring Power of Attorney in Irlanda del Nord [4].
  • Italia: Per gestire conti correnti, immobili o adempimenti fiscali in Italia, la persona può conferire una procura generale o speciale per atto notarile (tramite un notaio italiano iscritto al Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) oppure presso il consolato italiano nel Regno Unito. Poiché nel diritto italiano il mandato ordinario può estinguersi o subire limitazioni in caso di incapacità sopravvenuta, qualora insorgano fragilità o riduzioni dell'autonomia la Legge n. 6/2004 prevede l'istituto dell'Amministrazione di Sostegno mediante ricorso al Giudice Tutelare presso il Tribunale competente; l'interessato può inoltre designare preventivamente il proprio amministratore di sostegno mediante atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata.

steps.title: Prestazioni Urgenti per Malattia Terminale, Invalidità e Congedi per *Caregiver*
steps.html:
Sia il Regno Unito sia l'Italia prevedono procedure accelerate di accertamento dell'invalidità, indennità economiche e congedi lavorativi retribuiti o tutelati per i familiari che prestano assistenza.

  • Regno Unito: In base alle regole speciali per il fine vita (Special Rules for End of Life) gestite dal Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), quando il medico curante ritiene che l'aspettativa di vita possa essere pari o inferiore a 12 mesi, è possibile richiedere al medico o all'infermiere specialista la compilazione del modulo clinico SR1 [5]. Ciò consente l'erogazione accelerata e all'importo massimo di prestazioni quali Personal Independence Payment (PIP), Attendance Allowance o Universal Credit senza visita medica diretta [5]. I familiari che prestano almeno 35 ore settimanali di assistenza possono richiedere l'indennità Carer's Allowance, mentre i lavoratori dipendenti in Gran Bretagna hanno diritto fino a una settimana all'anno di congedo non retribuito per assistenza (statutory Carer's Leave) [6].
  • Italia: Tramite l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS), la persona affetta da patologia grave o oncologica può richiedere l'accertamento accelerato dell'invalidità civile e dell'handicap in situazione di gravità (con iter prioritario entro 15 giorni per i pazienti oncologici) [7]. Il riconoscimento della disabilità grave ai sensi della Legge n. 104/1992 (art. 3, comma 3) dà diritto ai familiari lavoratori dipendenti in Italia a 3 giorni di permesso mensile retribuito e fino a 2 anni di congedo straordinario retribuito tramite l'INPS [7]. Qualora sia riconosciuta un'invalidità totale (100%) con impossibilità di deambulare senza l'aiuto permanente di un accompagnatore o di compiere gli atti quotidiani della vita, l'INPS eroga inoltre l'indennità di accompagnamento, indipendentemente dal reddito [8].

steps.title: Coordinamento dei Testamenti, Pratiche Successorie e Scadenze Post-Mortem
steps.html:
Allineare preventivamente le disposizioni testamentarie e i beneficiari evita conflitti tra la libertà testamentaria del diritto britannico e le quote di legittima previste dal Codice Civile italiano.

  • Coordinamento dei Testamenti Transfrontalieri: È opportuno consultare un legale esperto in successioni internazionali o un notaio italiano (attraverso il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, che gestisce anche il Registro Generale dei Testamenti) affinché i testamenti nel Regno Unito e in Italia siano coordinati senza revocarsi involontariamente a vicenda, verificando l'eventuale scelta espressa della legge nazionale applicabile (professio iuris) ai sensi del Regolamento (UE) n. 650/2012 per i beni situati in Italia.
  • Adempimenti Post-Mortem nel Regno Unito: Dopo la registrazione del decesso nel Regno Unito, è possibile utilizzare il servizio governativo Tell Us Once per notificare con un'unica comunicazione l'amministrazione fiscale HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), il Department for Work and Pensions (DWP, inclusi il DWP Bereavement Service e l'International Pension Centre), l'ufficio passaporti e le autorità locali [9]. L'esecutore testamentario (executor) o l'amministratore richiede quindi il Grant of Probate (o le Letters of Administration) in Inghilterra e Galles (oppure la Confirmation in Scozia) per svincolare conti bancari e beni nel Regno Unito [10].
  • Adempimenti Post-Mortem in Italia: In Italia, il coniuge superstite e i familiari aventi diritto presentano domanda all'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS) per la pensione ai superstiti (pensione di reversibilità o indiretta) [7]. Gli eredi e i legatari sono tenuti a presentare in via telematica la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione (data del decesso), adempimento che attiva anche la voltura catastale per gli eventuali beni immobili situati in Italia [11].

it.closingQuestion: Per permetterci di adattare queste indicazioni al vostro caso specifico: in quale Paese il vostro familiare riceve attualmente assistenza medica, qual è la sua cittadinanza e dove si trovano i suoi immobili o conti bancari?

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Spain & Germany
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Spain & Germany
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Spain and Germany: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When your family member is diagnosed with a serious, progressive, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Spain and Germany, planning medical, legal, and estate steps in advance across both countries prevents administrative freezes and ensures their wishes are respected. Because healthcare registries, powers of attorney, and succession procedures operate independently in each state, key documents should be formalized while the patient retains full legal capacity.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
• Spain: Palliative care is arranged through the primary care physician or hospital specialist within the National Health System (Sistema Nacional de Salud - SNS), who refers the patient to hospital palliative care units or home palliative support teams (Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria - ESAD) in the relevant autonomous community, supported by the care directory of the Spanish Society for Palliative Care (Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos - SECPAL) and clinical frameworks coordinated by the Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Ministry of Health) [1].
  • Germany: Patients with advanced, incurable illnesses have a statutory right to general outpatient palliative care (Allgemeine Ambulante Palliativversorgung - AAPV) and, where complex symptoms arise, specialized outpatient palliative care (Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung - SAPV under § 37b SGB V), prescribed by the attending physician and funded by statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung), as well as inpatient hospice care (stationäre Hospize) coordinated alongside networks such as the German Hospice and Palliative Association (Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. - DHPV) and overseen by the Bundesministerium für Gesundheit (German Federal Ministry of Health) [2][3]. In palliative situations in Germany, the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse) can also be asked for an expedited care-level assessment (verkürzte Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung under § 18a SGB XI), which must be issued within one week for hospital or hospice patients [2]. If your family member plans to relocate between Spain and Germany for care, verify coverage beforehand via the European Health Insurance Card (temporary stays), portable document S1 (resident pensioners), or prior authorization S2 for scheduled treatment.

steps.title: Executing Advance Directives and Living Wills in Both Countries
steps.html:
While the patient retains full decision-making capacity, separate advance directive documents should be executed for each jurisdiction, as clinical registries are not automatically interconnected across borders.

  • Spain: The patient can execute an Advance Directive Document (Documento de Instrucciones Previas or Voluntades Anticipadas, commonly known as a Living Will or Testamento Vital, governed by Law 41/2002) before a notary, before staff of the regional registry, or before three witnesses depending on the rules of their autonomous community [1]. Once registered in the relevant regional registry (Registro Autonómico), the document is synchronized with the National Registry of Advance Directives (Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas - RNIP) of the Ministerio de Sanidad so that any medical team in Spain can consult it in the patient's clinical record [1].
  • Germany: A written and signed advance medical directive (schriftliche Patientenverfügung under § 1827 of the German Civil Code, BGB) should be drawn up, for instance using the official text modules (Textbausteine) published by the Federal Ministry of Justice (Bundesministerium der Justiz) and provided on the Wege zur Pflege portal [4]. It is advisable to supplement the Patientenverfügung with a palliative emergency sheet (palliativmedizinischer Notfallbogen) signed together with the general practitioner or SAPV team to guide emergency medical services at home [2][4].

steps.title: Preventive Powers of Attorney, Healthcare Proxy, and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
A power of attorney executed in Spain is rarely accepted immediately by German banks or registries without additional apostille and sworn translation formalities (or bank-specific forms), and vice versa. Separate instruments should therefore be formalized in both countries while your family member retains full legal capacity.

  • Spain: It is advisable to execute a public deed before a notary (via the General Council of Notaries, Consejo General del Notariado) granting a Preventive Power of Attorney (Poder Preventivo, or a general power of attorney with an express subsistence clause in the event of future incapacity or support needs), authorizing the representative to manage bank accounts, real estate, tax filings, and personal decisions without having to wait for judicial support proceedings [1].
  • Germany: The patient should execute a precautionary power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht covering financial and healthcare matters) and, as a fallback, a care directive (Betreuungsverfügung), registering both documents with the Central Register of Precautionary Mandates (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister of the Federal Chamber of Notaries, Bundesnotarkammer) so that guardianship courts (Betreuungsgerichte) can locate them immediately [2][4]. To operate accounts at German financial institutions both before and after death, it is particularly useful to sign a transmortal or postmortal bank power of attorney (transmortale Bankvollmacht) directly with the German bank on its own forms [4].

steps.title: Fast-Track Dependency Benefits and Statutory Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both legal systems provide financial support and statutory employment leave when a family member requires end-of-life care.

  • Spain: An urgent dependency assessment (valoración urgente de la situación de dependencia under Law 39/2006, coordinated by IMSERSO and the regional social services) can be requested to access home help services, day centers, or financial allowances for family care. In employment law, the Workers' Statute (Estatuto de los Trabajadores) grants paid leave for serious illness or hospitalization of relatives, as well as the right to reduced working hours (reducción de jornada) or unpaid caregiver leave (excedencia) to care for a dependent relative [5].
  • Germany: Under the Caregiver Time Act (Pflegezeitgesetz), employed relatives in Germany can take short-term absence from work of up to 10 working days with entitlement to the care support allowance (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) paid by the Pflegekasse, as well as full or partial release from work for up to 3 months to accompany a close relative in the final phase of life (Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase) [4][6]. The official Wege zur Pflege portal and the Care Helpline (Pflegetelefon at 030 20179131) of the Federal Ministry for Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth (Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend) provide free guidance on these entitlements and on statutory pension contributions for family caregivers under the Deutsche Rentenversicherung (German Statutory Pension Insurance) [4][6].

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Survivor Pensions, and Post-Death Formalities
steps.html:
Reviewing wills, life insurance policies, and bank accounts in Spain and Germany in advance streamlines estate administration under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012).

  • Testamentary coordination: Where assets exist in both countries, verify with a notary in Spain (Consejo General del Notariado) and in Germany that testamentary dispositions are aligned, assessing whether to include an express choice of national law (professio iuris) and ensuring a later will does not inadvertently revoke provisions intended for the other country [1].
  • Post-death procedures in Spain: Following death, applications are submitted to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) (Spanish National Institute of Social Security) for the death grant (auxilio por defunción) and survivor or orphan pensions (pensiones de viudedad u orfandad) [5][7]. Once 15 working days have elapsed since the death, the Certificate of the General Registry of Last Wills (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad, using Ministry of Justice Modelo 790) is obtained to execute the deed of acceptance and division of inheritance before a notary, and the Inheritance and Gift Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within the general 6-month deadline from death (extendable by a further 6 months if requested within the first 5 months) [5][7].
  • Post-death procedures in Germany: In Germany, the death must be reported to the statutory health insurance fund (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) and survivor or orphan pensions (Witwen-/Witwerrente or Waisenrente) claimed from the Deutsche Rentenversicherung [6]. The surviving spouse can apply through the Renten Service der Deutschen Post for the three-month death quarter advance (Sterbevierteljahr, during which the deceased's full pension rate is paid) within 30 days of the death [6]. To prove heirship before German banks or land registries where a notarized will with opening protocol is insufficient, a German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) or European Certificate of Succession is obtained from the probate court (Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht), which automatically consults the Central Register of Wills (Zentrales Testamentsregister).

closingQuestion: To tailor this information more closely to your case: in which of the two countries is your family member currently receiving medical care (and in which Spanish autonomous community or German federal state), and what is their nationality?

prefillQuestion: We are dealing with a terminal illness involving Spain and Germany. We need guidance tailored to where care takes place (in Spain or Germany), cross-border powers of attorney, and caregiver benefits:

contacts.name: Ministerio de Sanidad
contacts.note: Spanish state health authority responsible for the National Registry of Advance Directives (RNIP) and coordination of the National Health System (SNS).

contacts.name: Bundesministerium für Gesundheit
contacts.note: German Federal Ministry of Health providing official guidance on specialized outpatient palliative care (SAPV), hospices, and end-of-life care.

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y trámites entre España y Alemania: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos ante una enfermedad terminal con vínculos entre España y Alemania: cuidados paliativos, voluntades anticipadas, poderes preventivos en ambos países, permisos laborales y planificación sucesoria.
es.introHtml: Cuando a su familiar se le diagnostica una enfermedad grave, progresiva o en fase terminal y existen vínculos de residencia, nacionalidad, familia o patrimonio entre España y Alemania, anticipar las gestiones médicas, legales y patrimoniales en ambos países evita bloqueos administrativos y garantiza el respeto a su voluntad. Dado que los registros sanitarios, los poderes notariales y los trámites sucesorios funcionan de forma independiente en cada Estado, conviene formalizar los documentos clave mientras la persona enferma conserva plena capacidad de obrar.

steps.title: Organización de los cuidados paliativos y coordinación sanitaria transfronteriza
steps.html:
En España, la atención paliativa se solicita a través del médico de atención primaria o del especialista hospitalario del Sistema Nacional de Salud (SNS), quienes derivan a la persona enferma a las unidades hospitalarias de cuidados paliativos o a los Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria (ESAD) de la comunidad autónoma correspondiente, apoyándose también en el directorio de recursos de la Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos (SECPAL) y en los criterios coordinados por el Ministerio de Sanidad [1].

En Alemania, las personas con enfermedades avanzadas e incurables tienen derecho legal a la atención paliativa ambulatoria general (AAPV) y, cuando existen síntomas complejos, a la atención paliativa ambulatoria especializada (Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung, SAPV, conforme al § 37b SGB V), prescrita por el médico tratante y financiada por la caja del seguro médico legal (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung), así como a cuidados en centros residenciales (stationäre Hospize) coordinados junto con redes como el Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. (DHPV) y supervisados por el Bundesministerium für Gesundheit [2][3]. Asimismo, en situaciones paliativas en Alemania puede solicitarse a la caja de dependencia (Pflegekasse) una valoración urgente del grado de dependencia (verkürzte Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung conforme al § 18a SGB XI), cuyo dictamen en ámbito hospitalario o de hospicio debe emitirse en el plazo de una semana [2]. Si su familiar prevé trasladarse entre España y Alemania para recibir cuidados, verifique previamente la cobertura mediante la Tarjeta Sanitaria Europea (para estancias temporales), el formulario S1 (para pensionistas residentes) o la autorización previa S2 para tratamientos programados.

steps.title: Otorgamiento de Instrucciones Previas y Testamento Vital en ambos países
steps.html:
Mientras la persona enferma conserve plena capacidad de decisión, es fundamental redactar documentos de voluntades anticipadas específicos para cada jurisdicción, ya que los registros clínicos no están interconectados automáticamente a nivel internacional.

  • España: La persona enferma puede otorgar el Documento de Instrucciones Previas o Voluntades Anticipadas (conocido como Testamento Vital, regulado por la Ley 41/2002) ante notario, ante personal del registro autonómico o ante tres testigos según la normativa de su comunidad autónoma [1]. Una vez inscrito en el Registro Autonómico correspondiente, el documento se sincroniza con el Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas (RNIP) del Ministerio de Sanidad para que cualquier equipo médico en España pueda consultarlo en su historia clínica [1].
  • Alemania: Debe redactarse por escrito y firmarse una directiva médica anticipada (schriftliche Patientenverfügung conforme al § 1827 del Código Civil alemán, BGB), utilizando por ejemplo los módulos oficiales de texto (Textbausteine) publicados por el Bundesministerium der Justiz y recogidos en el portal Wege zur Pflege [4]. Conviene complementar la Patientenverfügung con una hoja de urgencias paliativas (palliativmedizinischer Notfallbogen) firmada junto con el médico de cabecera o el equipo SAPV para orientar a los servicios de emergencia en el domicilio [2][4].

steps.title: Poderes preventivos, representación médica y poderes bancarios
steps.html:
Un poder otorgado en España no suele ser aceptado de forma inmediata por los bancos o registros alemanes sin trámites adicionales de apostilla y traducción jurada (o formas específicas bancarias), y viceversa. Por ello, conviene formalizar instrumentos separados en ambos países mientras su familiar mantiene plena capacidad.

  • España: Se aconseja otorgar en escritura pública ante notario (a través del Consejo General del Notariado) un Poder Preventivo (o un poder general con cláusula expresa de subsistencia en caso de incapacidad o necesidad de apoyo futura), facultando al representante para gestionar cuentas bancarias, inmuebles, trámites fiscales y decisiones personales sin necesidad de acudir a un largo procedimiento judicial de provisión de apoyos [1].
  • Alemania: La persona enferma debe otorgar una Vorsorgevollmacht (poder de representación preventiva para asuntos patrimoniales y de salud) y, de forma complementaria, una Betreuungsverfügung (directiva de curatela), inscribiendo ambos documentos en el Registro Central de Previsión (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer) para que los tribunales de tutela (Betreuungsgerichte) los localicen de inmediato [2][4]. Para operar cuentas en entidades financieras alemanas antes y después del fallecimiento, es especialmente útil firmar directamente en el banco alemán un poder bancario transmortal o postmortal (transmortale Bankvollmacht) en los formularios propios de la entidad [4].

steps.title: Prestaciones urgentes por dependencia y permisos laborales para cuidadores
steps.html:
Ambos ordenamientos contemplan ayudas económicas y permisos laborales específicos cuando un familiar requiere cuidados al final de la vida.

  • España: Puede solicitarse por vía de urgencia la valoración de la situación de dependencia (Ley 39/2006, coordinada por el IMSERSO y los servicios sociales de cada comunidad autónoma) para acceder a servicios de ayuda a domicilio, centros de día o prestaciones económicas para cuidados en el entorno familiar. En el ámbito laboral, el Estatuto de los Trabajadores reconoce permisos retribuidos por enfermedad grave o hospitalización de familiares, así como el derecho a la reducción de jornada o excedencia por cuidado de un familiar que no pueda valerse por sí mismo [5].
  • Alemania: Al amparo de la Ley de Tiempo de Cuidado (Pflegezeitgesetz), los familiares trabajadores en Alemania pueden acogerse a una ausencia laboral de corta duración de hasta 10 días laborables con derecho al subsidio de apoyo al cuidado (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) abonado por la Pflegekasse, así como a una exención laboral total o parcial de hasta 3 meses para acompañar a un familiar en la última fase de la vida (Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase) [4][6]. El portal oficial Wege zur Pflege y el Pflegetelefon del Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (teléfono 030 20179131) ofrecen orientación gratuita sobre estos derechos y sobre las cotizaciones de pensión para cuidadores ante la Deutsche Rentenversicherung [4][6].

steps.title: Alineación de testamentos, pensiones y trámites tras el fallecimiento
steps.html:
Revisar con antelación los testamentos, seguros y cuentas bancarias en España y Alemania facilita la futura liquidación sucesoria conforme al Reglamento Europeo de Sucesiones (Reglamento (UE) n.º 650/2012).

  • Coordinación testamentaria: Si existen bienes en ambos países, conviene verificar ante notario en España (Consejo General del Notariado) y en Alemania que los testamentos estén coordinados, valorando si procede incluir una elección expresa de ley nacional (professio iuris) y evitando que un testamento posterior revoque involuntariamente las disposiciones previstas para el otro país.
  • Trámites posteriores en España: Tras el fallecimiento, se solicita ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) el auxilio por defunción y las pensiones de viudedad u orfandad que correspondan [5][7]. Transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la defunción, se obtiene el Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad (mediante el Modelo 790 del Ministerio de Justicia) para acudir a la notaría a tramitar la escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia, debiendo presentarse la autoliquidación del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones en el plazo general de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento (prorrogable por otros 6 meses si se solicita dentro de los primeros 5 meses).
  • Trámites posteriores en Alemania: En Alemania debe notificarse el fallecimiento a la caja de seguro médico (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) y solicitar ante la Deutsche Rentenversicherung la pensión de viudedad o de orfandad (Witwen-/Witwerrente o Waisenrente) [6]. El cónyuge supérstite puede solicitar a través del Renten Service der Deutschen Post el anticipo del trimestre de defunción (Sterbevierteljahr, durante el cual se abona el importe íntegro de la pensión del causante) dentro de los 30 días siguientes al fallecimiento [6]. Para acreditar la condición de heredero ante bancos o registros alemanes cuando no basta un testamento notarial con acta de apertura, se tramita el certificado sucesorio alemán (Erbschein) o el Certificado Sucesorio Europeo ante el tribunal sucesorio (Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht), que consulta de oficio el Registro Central de Testamentos (Zentrales Testamentsregister).

es.closingQuestion: Para adaptar mejor esta información a su caso, ¿en cuál de los dos países recibe actualmente asistencia médica su familiar (y en qué comunidad autónoma o estado federado) y cuál es su nacionalidad?

de.title: Schwere Erkrankung & Vorsorge zwischen Spanien und Deutschland: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei lebensbedrohlicher Erkrankung mit Bezug zu Spanien und Deutschland: Palliativversorgung, Patientenverfügungen in beiden Ländern, Vorsorgevollmachten, Pflegezeit sowie Nachlass- und Rückführungsplanung.
de.introHtml: Wenn bei Ihrem Familienmitglied eine schwere, fortschreitende oder unheilbare Erkrankung diagnostiziert wird und Verbindungen durch Wohnsitz, Staatsangehörigkeit, Familie oder Vermögen zwischen Spanien und Deutschland bestehen, verhindert eine frühzeitige Koordination der medizinischen, rechtlichen und erbrechtlichen Schritte in beiden Staaten bürokratische Blockaden und sichert die Achtung des Patientenwillens. Da Gesundheitsregister, Vorsorgevollmachten und Nachlassverfahren in beiden Ländern unabhängig voneinander geführt werden, sollten die zentralen Dokumente errichtet werden, solange die erkrankte Person voll geschäftsfähig und einwilligungsfähig ist.

steps.title: Organisation der Palliativversorgung und grenzüberschreitende Gesundheitskoordination
steps.html:
• Spanien: Die Palliativversorgung wird über die hausärztliche Versorgung (médico de atención primaria) oder den Krankenhausfacharzt des staatlichen Gesundheitssystems (Sistema Nacional de Salud - SNS) veranlasst; diese überweisen an stationäre Palliativstationen oder an die ambulanten Palliativteams (Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria - ESAD) der jeweiligen Autonomen Gemeinschaft, ergänzt durch das Versorgungsverzeichnis der Spanischen Gesellschaft für Palliativmedizin (Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos - SECPAL) und die vom Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanisches Gesundheitsministerium) koordinierten Leitlinien [1].
  • Deutschland: Versicherte mit einer nicht heilbaren, fortschreitenden und weit fortgeschrittenen Erkrankung haben einen gesetzlichen Anspruch auf allgemeine ambulante Palliativversorgung (AAPV) sowie bei komplexem Symptomgeschehen auf Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung (SAPV nach § 37b SGB V), die ärztlich verordnet und von der gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung (GKV) finanziert wird, ebenso wie auf die Versorgung in stationären Hospizen unter Einbindung von Netzwerken wie dem Deutschen Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. (DHPV) und nach den Vorgaben des Bundesministerium für Gesundheit [2][3]. Zudem kann in palliativen Situationen in Deutschland bei der Pflegekasse eine verkürzte Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung nach § 18a SGB XI beantragt werden, über die bei Krankenhaus- oder Hospizpatienten innerhalb einer Woche entschieden werden muss [2]. Ist eine Verlegung zwischen Spanien und Deutschland geplant, prüfen Sie vorab die Kostenübernahme über die Europäische Krankenversicherungskarte (EHIC bei vorübergehendem Aufenthalt), das Dokument S1 (für im anderen Staat wohnhafte Rentner) oder die Vorabgenehmigung S2 für geplante Behandlungen.

steps.title: Errichtung von Patientenverfügungen in beiden Staaten
steps.html:
Solange die erkrankte Person voll einwilligungsfähig ist, sollten für beide Rechtsordnungen gesonderte Patientenverfügungen erstellt werden, da die klinischen Register international nicht automatisch vernetzt sind.

  • Spanien: Die erkrankte Person kann eine spanische Patientenverfügung (Documento de Instrucciones Previas oder Voluntades Anticipadas, auch Testamento Vital genannt, geregelt durch das Gesetz Ley 41/2002) je nach den Vorschriften ihrer Autonomen Gemeinschaft vor einem Notar, vor dem zuständigen Personal des Regionalregisters oder vor drei Zeugen errichten [1]. Nach der Eintragung im jeweiligen Regionalregister (Registro Autonómico) wird das Dokument mit dem Nationalen Register für Patientenverfügungen (Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas - RNIP) beim Ministerio de Sanidad synchronisiert, sodass jedes Behandlungsteam in Spanien elektronisch darauf zugreifen kann [1].
  • Deutschland: Es sollte eine schriftliche und eigenhändig unterschriebene Patientenverfügung nach § 1827 BGB verfasst werden, beispielsweise mithilfe der amtlichen Textbausteine des Bundesministeriums der Justiz, die über das Portal Wege zur Pflege abrufbar sind [4]. Es empfiehlt sich, die Patientenverfügung durch einen gemeinsam mit dem Hausarzt oder dem SAPV-Team unterzeichneten palliativmedizinischen Notfallbogen (Krisenbogen) zu ergänzen, damit der Rettungsdienst bei häuslichen Notfällen sofortige Handlungsleitlinien hat [2][4].

steps.title: Vorsorgevollmachten, Gesundheitsvertretung und Bankvollmachten
steps.html:
Eine in Spanien beurkundete Vollmacht wird von deutschen Banken oder Grundbuchämtern ohne zusätzliche Haager Apostille und beglaubigte Übersetzung (bzw. bankeigene Formulare) regelmäßig nicht unmittelbar akzeptiert - und umgekehrt. Daher sollten in beiden Ländern getrennte Urkunden errichtet werden, solange volle Geschäftsfähigkeit besteht.

  • Spanien: Es ist ratsam, in öffentlicher Urkunde (escritura pública) vor einem spanischen Notar (über den Consejo General del Notariado) eine Vorsorgevollmacht (Poder Preventivo oder eine Generalvollmacht mit ausdrücklicher Fortgeltungsklausel für den Fall künftiger Geschäftsunfähigkeit oder Unterstützungsbedürftigkeit) zu erteilen, damit die bevollmächtigte Person Bankkonten, Immobilien, Steuerangelegenheiten und persönliche Entscheidungen in Spanien ohne langwieriges gerichtliches Unterstützungsverfahren regeln kann [1].
  • Deutschland: Die erkrankte Person sollte eine Vorsorgevollmacht (für Vermögens- und Gesundheitsangelegenheiten) sowie ergänzend eine Betreuungsverfügung errichten und beide im Zentralen Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer registrieren lassen, damit deutsche Betreuungsgerichte sie im Bedarfsfall sofort einsehen können [2][4]. Um Konten bei deutschen Kreditinstituten sowohl zu Lebzeiten als auch über den Tod hinaus handlungsfähig zu halten, sollte zusätzlich direkt bei der jeweiligen deutschen Bank eine transmortale (oder postmortale) Bankvollmacht auf den bankeigenen Formularen unterzeichnet werden [4].

steps.title: Eilverfahren bei Pflegebedürftigkeit und gesetzliche Pflegezeiten für Angehörige
steps.html:
Beide Rechtsordnungen sehen finanzielle Unterstützungsleistungen und arbeitsrechtliche Freistellungen vor, wenn ein Familienmitglied am Lebensende begleitet wird.

  • Spanien: Es kann im Dringlichkeitsverfahren eine Einstufung der Pflegebedürftigkeit (valoración urgente de la situación de dependencia nach Ley 39/2006, koordiniert durch das IMSERSO und die Sozialdienste der jeweiligen Autonomen Gemeinschaft) beantragt werden, um ambulante Pflegedienste, Tagespflege oder Pflegegeld für die häusliche Pflege zu erhalten. Arbeitsrechtlich gewährt das spanische Arbeitnehmerstatut (Estatuto de los Trabajadores) bezahlte Sonderurlaubstage bei schwerer Erkrankung oder Krankenhausaufenthalt von Angehörigen sowie das Recht auf Arbeitszeitverkürzung (reducción de jornada) oder unbezahlte Freistellung (excedencia) zur Angehörigenpflege [5].
  • Deutschland: Nach dem Pflegezeitgesetz können beschäftigte nahe Angehörige in Deutschland eine kurzzeitige Arbeitsverhinderung von bis zu 10 Arbeitstagen verbunden mit dem von der Pflegekasse gezahlten Pflegeunterstützungsgeld in Anspruch nehmen sowie eine vollständige oder teilweise Freistellung von bis zu 3 Monaten zur Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase beanspruchen [4][6]. Das offizielle Portal Wege zur Pflege und das Pflegetelefon des Bundesministeriums für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (Telefon 030 20179131) beraten kostenfrei zu diesen Ansprüchen sowie zur rentenrechtlichen Absicherung pflegender Angehöriger bei der Deutsche Rentenversicherung [4][6].

steps.title: Abstimmung von Testamenten, Hinterbliebenenrenten und Nachlassabwicklung
steps.html:
Eine frühzeitige Überprüfung von Testamenten, Lebensversicherungen und Bankkonten in Spanien und Deutschland erleichtert die spätere Nachlassabwicklung nach der Europäischen Erbrechtsverordnung (Verordnung (EU) Nr. 650/2012).

  • Testamentarische Koordination: Besteht Vermögen in beiden Staaten, sollte mit einem Notar in Spanien (Consejo General del Notariado) und in Deutschland geprüft werden, ob die letztwilligen Verfügungen aufeinander abgestimmt sind, ob eine ausdrückliche Rechtswahl (professio iuris) zugunsten des Heimatrechts sinnvoll ist und dass ein späteres Testament nicht unbeabsichtigt frühere Verfügungen für das andere Land widerruft [1].
  • Nachlass- und Rentenschritte in Spanien: Nach Eintritt des Todesfalls werden beim Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) das Sterbegeld (auxilio por defunción) sowie etwaige Witwen-/Witwer- oder Waisenrenten (pensiones de viudedad u orfandad) beantragt [5][7]. Nach Ablauf von 15 Werktagen ab dem Todestag wird die Bescheinigung des Zentralen Testamentsregisters (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad über das Formular Modelo 790 des Justizministeriums) eingeholt, um vor dem Notar die Erbschaftsannahme und Erbteilung zu beurkunden; die spanische Erbschaftsteuererklärung (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) ist grundsätzlich innerhalb von 6 Monaten ab dem Todestag einzureichen (mit Verlängerungsmöglichkeit um weitere 6 Monate bei Antragstellung innerhalb der ersten 5 Monate) [5][7].
  • Nachlass- und Rentenschritte in Deutschland: In Deutschland ist der Todesfall der gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung zu melden, und bei der Deutsche Rentenversicherung werden Hinterbliebenenrenten (Witwen-/Witwerrente bzw. Waisenrente) beantragt [6]. Überlebende Ehegatten oder eingetragene Lebenspartner können über den Renten Service der Deutschen Post innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Tod die Vorschusszahlung für das Sterbevierteljahr (in dem die Rente in voller Höhe des Verstorbenen weitergezahlt wird) beantragen [6]. Zum Erbnachweis gegenüber deutschen Banken oder Grundbuchämtern wird - sofern kein notarielles Testament mit Eröffnungsprotokoll ausreicht - beim zuständigen Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht ein deutscher Erbschein oder ein Europäisches Nachlasszeugnis beantragt, wobei das Gericht von Amts wegen das Zentrale Testamentsregister abfragt.

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Spain & France
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: Spain & France
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across Spain and France: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When your family member is diagnosed with a serious, progressive, or terminal illness and has residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both Spain and France, coordinating palliative care, capacity documents, and succession planning in advance across both countries prevents legal and administrative freezes. Because medical registries, powers of attorney, and succession rules operate independently in each jurisdiction, key documents should be formalized while the patient retains full decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Organizing Palliative Care and Cross-Border Healthcare Coordination
steps.html:
• Spain: Access to palliative care is arranged through the primary care physician or hospital specialist within the National Health System (Sistema Nacional de Salud - SNS), who refers the patient to hospital palliative care units or home palliative support teams (Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria - ESAD) in their autonomous community, supported by the care directory of the Spanish Society for Palliative Care (Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos - SECPAL) and the coordination of the Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Ministry of Health) [1].
  • France: Palliative care is delivered through hospital-at-home care (Hospitalisation à domicile - HAD), mobile palliative care teams (équipes mobiles de soins palliatifs - EMSP), and specialized inpatient palliative care units (unités de soins palliatifs - USP), with official guidance and directories maintained by the Centre national des soins palliatifs et de la fin de vie (CNSPFV, National Center for Palliative and End-of-Life Care via its Parlons Fin de Vie portal) and the French Society for Support and Palliative Care (Société Française d'Accompagnement et de Soins Palliatifs - SFAP) [2]. For patients insured under the French system with a serious or progressive illness, the attending physician applies to Assurance Maladie (French National Health Insurance) for exempting long-term illness status (Affection de Longue Durée exonérante - ALD), which covers 100% of medical and palliative costs linked to the condition under French statutory tariffs [3]. If a medical transfer between Spain and France is considered, verify coverage beforehand using the European Health Insurance Card (temporary stays), portable document S1 (resident pensioners), or prior authorization S2 for scheduled care.

steps.title: Executing Advance Directives in Both Countries (*Instrucciones Previas* and *Directives Anticipées*)
steps.html:
While the patient retains full legal capacity, separate advance directive documents should be executed in both countries, as national clinical registries do not cross-reference each other automatically.

  • Spain: Your family member can execute an Advance Directive Document (Documento de Instrucciones Previas or Voluntades Anticipadas, commonly known as a Living Will or Testamento Vital, governed by Law 41/2002) before a notary, before authorized regional registry staff, or before witnesses in accordance with the legislation of their autonomous community [1]. Once registered in the regional registry (Registro Autonómico), the document is integrated into the National Registry of Advance Directives (Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas - RNIP) of the Ministerio de Sanidad so that physicians at any hospital in Spain can consult it [1].
  • France: Under the Claeys-Leonetti Act (loi Claeys-Leonetti), any adult can draft written advance medical directives (directives anticipées regarding the limitation or withdrawal of end-of-life treatments) and designate in writing a trusted person (personne de confiance) to be consulted first by the medical team if the patient can no longer express their wishes [2][4]. These documents can be stored in the French digital health record (Mon espace santé) and provided to the attending physician or hospital in accordance with the guidance on Service-Public.fr (the official French public administration portal) [4].

steps.title: Preventive Powers of Attorney, Bank Mandates, and *Mandat de Protection Future*
steps.html:
A power of attorney granted in Spain generally does not allow direct operation of bank accounts or property sales in France without apostille, sworn translation, or notarial equivalence formalities, and vice versa. Separate instruments should therefore be executed in both states while full legal capacity remains.

  • Spain: It is advisable to execute a public deed before a notary (through the General Council of Notaries, Consejo General del Notariado) granting a Preventive Power of Attorney (Poder Preventivo, or a general power of attorney with an express subsistence clause in the event of future incapacity or support needs), enabling the appointed representative to manage bank accounts, real estate, and tax affairs in Spain without awaiting a court order [1].
  • France: For everyday management of accounts at French banks, a bank power of attorney (procuration bancaire) should be signed directly with each French financial institution. In addition, to prepare for a potential loss of physical or mental capacity, the patient can execute a future protection mandate (Mandat de protection future), either by registered private deed (sous seing privé) or - preferably where real estate or complex assets are involved - by notarial deed before a French notary (Notaires de France), in accordance with the rules detailed on Service-Public.fr [4].

steps.title: Fast-Track Dependency Benefits, Employment Leave, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
Both countries provide fast-track dependency procedures and statutory employment leave for family caregivers.

  • Spain: An urgent dependency assessment (valoración urgente de la situación de dependencia under Law 39/2006, coordinated by IMSERSO and regional social services) can be requested to access home care or care-linked financial benefits. In addition, the Workers' Statute (Estatuto de los Trabajadores) provides paid employment leave for serious illness or hospitalization of family members, as well as the right to reduced working hours (reducción de jornada) or unpaid caregiver leave (excedencia) for direct care of a dependent relative [5].
  • France: Employees in France accompanying a relative in an advanced or terminal phase of a serious, incurable illness are entitled to family solidarity leave (congé de solidarité familiale of up to 3 months, renewable once), as detailed on Service-Public.fr [6]. During this leave or when switching to part-time work, the caregiver can apply to the primary health insurance fund (Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie - CPAM, via Assurance Maladie) for the Daily End-of-Life Accompaniment Allowance (Allocation journalière d'accompagnement d'une personne en fin de vie - AJAP), which pays a daily benefit for up to 21 days (or 42 days when working part-time) [3]. For individuals aged 60 or over in France experiencing a sudden loss of autonomy, the Personalized Autonomy Allowance can also be requested on an emergency basis (Allocation personnalisée d'autonomie - APA en urgence) from the departmental council (Conseil départemental).

steps.title: Aligning Wills, Survivor Pensions, and Post-Death Formalities
steps.html:
Coordinating wills, life insurance policies, and bank accounts in advance between Spain and France avoids conflicts between forced heirship rules in both countries under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012).

  • Testamentary coordination: Review testamentary dispositions with a notary in Spain (Consejo General del Notariado) and a notary in France (Notaires de France), assessing whether to include an express choice of national law governing the succession (professio iuris) and checking beneficiary designations on life insurance policies (assurance-vie in France) [4].
  • Post-death procedures in Spain: Following death, applications are submitted to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) (Spanish National Institute of Social Security) for the death grant (auxilio por defunción) and widowhood or orphan pensions (pensiones de viudedad u orfandad) [5][7]. Once 15 working days have passed since the death, the Certificate of the General Registry of Last Wills (Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad, Ministry of Justice Modelo 790) is requested to execute the inheritance deed before a notary, and the Inheritance and Gift Tax self-assessment (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) is filed within the general 6-month period from death [5][7].
  • Post-death procedures in France: In France, eligible dependents or beneficiaries can claim the lump-sum death benefit (capital décès) from the Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM, via the Ameli.fr portal of Assurance Maladie) if the deceased contributed to the general scheme, as well as survivor pensions (pensions de réversion) from the pension funds (Assurance Retraite / CNAV and the Agirc-Arrco supplementary scheme) [8]. Estate administration in France (including the deed of heirship or acte de notoriété and the French inheritance tax return) is normally handled by a French notary (Notaires de France) [4][8].

closingQuestion: To guide you more precisely: in which of the two countries is your family member currently receiving medical care (and in which Spanish autonomous community or French department), and what is their nationality?

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y trámites entre España y Francia: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos ante una enfermedad terminal con vínculos entre España y Francia: cuidados paliativos, voluntades anticipadas, poderes preventivos en ambos países, permisos laborales y planificación sucesoria.
es.introHtml: Cuando a su familiar se le diagnostica una enfermedad grave, progresiva o en fase terminal y existen vínculos de residencia, nacionalidad, familia o patrimonio entre España y Francia, organizar de forma coordinada la asistencia paliativa, los documentos de capacidad y la planificación sucesoria en ambos países evita bloqueos jurídicos y administrativos. Dado que los registros médicos, los poderes de representación y las reglas sucesorias funcionan de manera independiente en cada jurisdicción, conviene formalizar los documentos clave mientras la persona enferma conserva plena capacidad de decisión.

steps.title: Organización de los cuidados paliativos y coordinación sanitaria transfronteriza
steps.html:
En España, el acceso a los cuidados paliativos se gestiona a través del médico de atención primaria o del especialista hospitalario del Sistema Nacional de Salud (SNS), quienes derivan a la persona enferma a las unidades hospitalarias de cuidados paliativos o a los Equipos de Soporte de Atención Domiciliaria (ESAD) de su comunidad autónoma, contando además con el directorio asistencial de la Sociedad Española de Cuidados Paliativos (SECPAL) y la coordinación del Ministerio de Sanidad [1].

En Francia, la atención paliativa se articula mediante la Hospitalisation à domicile (HAD), los equipos móviles de cuidados paliativos (équipes mobiles de soins palliatifs, EMSP) y las unidades especializadas (unités de soins palliatifs, USP), con información oficial y directorios gestionados por el Centre national des soins palliatifs et de la fin de vie (CNSPFV, a través de su portal Parlons Fin de Vie) y la Société Française d'Accompagnement et de Soins Palliatifs (SFAP) [2]. Para pacientes afiliados al sistema francés con una patología grave o evolutiva, el médico tratante solicita ante la Assurance Maladie el reconocimiento de Affection de Longue Durée (ALD exonérante), que cubre al 100 % los gastos médicos y paliativos vinculados a la enfermedad conforme a las tarifas de la Seguridad Social francesa [3]. Si se valora un traslado asistencial entre España y Francia, verifique previamente la cobertura con la Tarjeta Sanitaria Europea (estancias temporales), el documento portátil S1 (residentes pensionistas) o la autorización previa S2 para atención programada.

steps.title: Otorgamiento de Instrucciones Previas y Directives Anticipées en ambos países
steps.html:
Mientras la persona enferma mantenga plena capacidad de obrar, es recomendable otorgar documentos de voluntades anticipadas específicos en ambos países, ya que los registros clínicos nacionales no se cruzan automáticamente.

  • España: Su familiar puede otorgar el Documento de Instrucciones Previas o Voluntades Anticipadas (Testamento Vital, regulado por la Ley 41/2002) ante notario, ante el personal habilitado del registro autonómico o ante testigos según la legislación de su comunidad autónoma [1]. Una vez inscrito en el Registro Autonómico, el documento queda integrado en el Registro Nacional de Instrucciones Previas (RNIP) del Ministerio de Sanidad para su consulta por los facultativos en cualquier hospital de España [1].
  • Francia: Conforme a la ley Claeys-Leonetti, toda persona mayor de edad puede redactar por escrito sus directivas médicas anticipadas (directives anticipées, sobre la limitación o interrupción de tratamientos al final de la vida) y designar por escrito a una persona de confianza (personne de confiance) que sea consultada prioritariamente por el equipo médico si la persona enferma no puede expresarse [2][4]. Estos documentos pueden guardarse en el expediente médico digital francés (Mon espace santé) y entregarse al médico tratante o al centro hospitalario según las indicaciones de Service-Public.fr [4].

steps.title: Poderes preventivos, procuraciones bancarias y Mandat de Protection Future
steps.html:
Un poder otorgado en España no suele permitir operar directamente cuentas bancarias o vender inmuebles en Francia sin trámites de apostilla, traducción o equivalencia notarial, y viceversa. Conviene formalizar instrumentos separados en ambos Estados mientras se conserve la capacidad legal.

  • España: Es aconsejable otorgar en escritura pública ante notario (a través del Consejo General del Notariado) un Poder Preventivo (o un poder general con cláusula expresa de subsistencia en caso de incapacidad o necesidad de apoyo futura), permitiendo que la persona designada administre cuentas bancarias, bienes inmuebles y gestiones fiscales en España sin tener que esperar a una resolución judicial [1].
  • Francia: Para la gestión cotidiana de cuentas en bancos franceses, conviene firmar una autorización bancaria (procuration bancaire) directamente en la entidad financiera francesa. Además, para prever una eventual pérdida de capacidad física o mental, la persona enferma puede otorgar un Mandat de protection future (mandato de protección futura), ya sea mediante documento privado registrado (sous seing privé) o, preferiblemente cuando existen bienes inmuebles o un patrimonio complejo, mediante escritura pública ante un notario francés (a través de Notaires de France), conforme a las reglas detalladas en Service-Public.fr [4].

steps.title: Prestaciones urgentes por dependencia, permisos laborales y ayudas al cuidador
steps.html:
Ambos países disponen de procedimientos urgentes de apoyo a la dependencia y licencias laborales para familiares cuidadores.

  • España: Puede solicitarse la valoración urgente de la situación de dependencia (Ley 39/2006, coordinada por el IMSERSO y los servicios sociales autonómicos) para acceder a atención domiciliaria o prestaciones vinculadas al cuidado. Asimismo, el Estatuto de los Trabajadores contempla permisos laborales retribuidos por enfermedad grave u hospitalización de familiares, así como el derecho a la reducción de jornada o excedencia para el cuidado directo de un familiar dependiente [5].
  • Francia: Los trabajadores asalariados en Francia que acompañan a un familiar en fase avanzada o terminal de una enfermedad grave e incurable tienen derecho al congé de solidarité familiale (permiso de solidaridad familiar de hasta 3 meses, renovable una vez) regulado en Service-Public.fr [6]. Durante este permiso o en caso de reducción de actividad laboral, el cuidador puede solicitar ante la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM, a través de Assurance Maladie) la Allocation journalière d'accompagnement d'une personne en fin de vie (AJAP), que abona una prestación diaria durante un máximo de 21 días (o 42 días si se reduce la jornada a tiempo parcial) [3]. Para personas mayores de 60 años en Francia con pérdida brusca de autonomía, también puede solicitarse de urgencia la Allocation personnalisée d'autonomie (APA en urgence) ante los servicios del departamento (Conseil départemental).

steps.title: Alineación de testamentos, pensiones y trámites tras el fallecimiento
steps.html:
Coordinar con antelación los testamentos, seguros de vida y cuentas bancarias entre España y Francia evita conflictos entre las normas de legítima de ambos países bajo el Reglamento Europeo de Sucesiones (Reglamento (UE) n.º 650/2012).

  • Coordinación testamentaria: Conviene revisar junto con un notario en España (Consejo General del Notariado) y un notario en Francia (Notaires de France) la redacción de los testamentos, valorando si procede realizar una elección expresa de la ley nacional aplicable a la sucesión (professio iuris) y comprobando las designaciones de beneficiarios en seguros de vida (assurance-vie en Francia).
  • Trámites posteriores en España: Tras el fallecimiento, se tramita ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (INSS) el auxilio por defunción y las pensiones de viudedad u orfandad [5][7]. Pasados 15 días hábiles desde la defunción, se solicita el Certificado del Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad (Modelo 790 del Ministerio de Justicia) para otorgar ante notario la escritura de herencia, y se presenta la autoliquidación del Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones dentro del plazo general de 6 meses desde el fallecimiento.
  • Trámites posteriores en Francia: En Francia, los familiares a cargo o derechohabientes pueden solicitar el capital por fallecimiento (capital décès) ante la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM, portal Ameli.fr de Assurance Maladie) si la persona fallecida cotizaba al régimen general, así como las pensiones de reversión ante las cajas de jubilación (Assurance Retraite / CNAV y el régimen complementario Agirc-Arrco) [8]. La liquidación de la sucesión en Francia (incluyendo el acte de notoriété y la declaración fiscal sucesoria ante la administración tributaria francesa) se tramita habitualmente con la intervención de un notario francés (Notaires de France) [4][8].
