title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Germany
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Germany
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Germany: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and Germany, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coverage (United States and Germany)
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide pain and symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, helpline 1-800-633-4227) once a hospice medical director and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing visits, medical equipment, medications for symptom relief, inpatient respite care, and family bereavement support; state-by-state hospice directories and planning guides are also available through CaringInfo (phone 1-800-658-8898, an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) [2].
  • Germany: If care takes place in Germany or a relocation is planned, patients with an incurable, progressive condition and complex symptoms are entitled to Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung (SAPV nach § 37b SGB V), prescribed by a physician and funded by statutory health insurance (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) [6]. For patients receiving palliative or hospice care, statutory long-term care insurance applies a fast-track assessment deadline of one week for care-level classification (Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung nach § 18a SGB XI) [6]. Regional SAPV teams, inpatient palliative wards, and hospices can be located through Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. [6]. Because US Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States and German statutory health insurance requires prior coordination for cross-border treatment, verify insurance coverage and medical transport fitness before any international transfer.

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives in Both the United States and Germany
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so your family member should execute separate written directives for the United States and Germany while full decision-making capacity remains:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state (for example, in California, New York, or Texas), along with a federal HIPAA release [2][3]. Free federal guides are available from the National Institute on Aging (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. In addition, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST) so emergency medical personnel follow the person's treatment boundaries immediately [2][3].
  • Germany: Prepare a written, personally signed Patientenverfügung nach § 1827 BGB specifying consent or refusal for medical measures in defined end-of-life situations, supplemented by an emergency palliative instruction sheet (palliativmedizinischer Notfallbogen) for emergency services [7]. Official German templates and drafting modules (Textbausteine) are published free of charge by the Bundesministerium der Justiz [7].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
German banks, land registries, and authorities rarely accept a US state Power of Attorney directly, and US financial institutions require state-compliant mandates. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements [2][4]. Plain-language fiduciary guidance for financial agents is provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (phone 1-855-411-2372) [4]. In addition, contact US banks and brokerage firms directly to verify internal POA forms and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations so accounts transfer outside probate.
  • Germany: Execute a written Vorsorgevollmacht and Betreuungsverfügung [7] and register them with the Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer so German guardianship courts (Betreuungsgerichte) and attending physicians can verify the representative's authority immediately [8]. If the mandate covers German real estate or commercial register transactions, it must be notarized or publicly certified (before a German notary or a German embassy or consulate in the US); additionally, set up an explicit post-mortem bank mandate (transmortale Bankvollmacht) directly with each German bank.

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer expedited disability processing and statutory leave for family caregivers:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for fast-track disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which expedite Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for life-limiting diagnoses [5]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administered by the U.S. Department of Labor (phone 1-866-487-9243), alongside state Paid Family Leave programs where applicable [9].
  • Germany: Employees insured in Germany can take up to 10 working days off work in an acute care crisis and claim wage-replacement benefits (Pflegeunterstützungsgeld) from the patient's long-term care fund (Pflegekasse) [10]. Under the Pflegezeitgesetz, caregivers are also entitled to full or partial release from work for up to 3 months to accompany a close relative in the final phase of life (Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase), whether at home or in a hospice [10]. Free advice is available via the Pflegetelefon of the Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (phone 030 20 17 91 31, email info@wege-zur-pflege.de) [10].

steps.title: Align Cross-Border Wills, Pension Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
Coordinate wills covering US and German assets with cross-border estate professionals so that a new will in one country does not inadvertently revoke the other, and consider whether an explicit choice of law is appropriate under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012). Gather civil certificates, Social Security and German pension insurance numbers, property deeds, and written funeral or international repatriation wishes:

  • United States: Following a death, notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US, or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Consulate General in Frankfurt for residents in Germany) regarding survivor benefits and the lump-sum death payment [5], contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if the person served in the US armed forces, file the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and initiate estate administration with the local state Probate Court for assets not held in a trust or POD/TOD designation.
  • Germany: Notify the person's statutory health insurer (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung) and apply to the Deutsche Rentenversicherung for survivor pensions (Witwen-/Witwerrente and Waisenrente) [11]. If the deceased was already receiving a German statutory pension, the surviving spouse or registered partner can apply within 30 days of death to the Renten Service der Deutschen Post for the three-month pension advance (Sterbevierteljahr) [11]. Wills held in official custody are opened by the Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht (linked to the Zentrales Testamentsregister), which also issues the German certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) when required by banks or land registries.

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance to your family member's situation: 1. Which US state and which German federal state (Bundesland) are involved in your family member's medical care, residence, or property? 2. Where is your family member currently residing and receiving medical treatment?

de.title: Schwere Erkrankung & Vorsorge zwischen Vereinigte Staaten und Deutschland: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei lebensbedrohlicher Erkrankung mit Bezug zu Vereinigte Staaten und Deutschland: Palliativversorgung, Patientenverfügungen in beiden Ländern, Vorsorgevollmachten, Pflegezeit sowie Nachlass- und Rückführungsplanung.
de.introHtml:
Wenn bei Ihrem Familienangehörigen eine schwere, lebensverkürzende oder unheilbare Erkrankung diagnostiziert wurde und Verbindungen durch Wohnsitz, Staatsangehörigkeit, Familie oder Vermögenswerte sowohl zu den Vereinigten Staaten als auch zu Deutschland bestehen, schützt die frühzeitige Einrichtung medizinischer, rechtlicher und finanzieller Regelungen in beiden Rechtsordnungen - solange die erkrankte Person voll urteils- und geschäftsfähig ist - deren persönlichen Willen und verhindert grenzüberschreitende Verzögerungen.

Nachfolgend finden Sie die 5 offiziellen Schritte in der empfohlenen Reihenfolge.

steps.title: Palliativ- und Hospizversorgung sowie grenzüberschreitende Krankenversicherung koordinieren (Vereinigte Staaten und Deutschland)
steps.html:
Wenden Sie sich zunächst an das behandelnde Ärzteteam in dem Land, in dem Ihr Familienangehöriger derzeit medizinisch betreut wird, um die Symptomlinderung sowie die ambulante oder stationäre Unterstützung einzurichten:

  • Vereinigte Staaten: Stationäre und ambulante Palliativteams bieten Schmerz- und Symptombehandlung begleitend zur kurativen Therapie an; alternativ kann die erkrankte Person die Medicare Hospice Benefit im Rahmen von Medicare Part A (verwaltet durch die Bundesbehörde Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Helpline 1-800-633-4227) in Anspruch nehmen, sobald die ärztliche Hospizleitung und die behandelnde Ärztin bzw. der behandelnde Arzt eine Lebenserwartung von höchstens 6 Monaten bestätigen [1]. Die Medicare-Hospizleistung umfasst häusliche Pflegebesuche, medizinische Hilfsmittel, Medikamente zur Symptomkontrolle, stationäre Entlastungspflege (Respite Care) sowie Trauerbegleitung für Angehörige; bundesstaatliche Hospizverzeichnisse und Planungshilfen sind zudem über CaringInfo (Telefon 1-800-658-8898, eine Initiative der National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) abrufbar [2].
  • Deutschland: Erfolgt die Versorgung in Deutschland oder ist eine Rückkehr bzw. Verlegung dorthin geplant, haben Versicherte mit einer nicht heilbaren, fortschreitenden Erkrankung und komplexer Symptomatik Anspruch auf Spezialisierte Ambulante Palliativversorgung (SAPV nach § 37b SGB V), die ärztlich verordnet und von der gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung finanziert wird [6]. Für Patientinnen und Patienten in Palliativ- oder Hospizversorgung gilt in der sozialen Pflegeversicherung eine verkürzte Begutachtungsfrist von einer Woche zur Einstufung in einen Pflegegrad (Pflegegrad-Eilbegutachtung nach § 18a SGB XI) [6]. Regionale SAPV-Teams, Palliativstationen und stationäre Hospize lassen sich über den Dachverband Deutscher Hospiz- und PalliativVerband e.V. ermitteln [6]. Da US Medicare grundsätzlich keine Behandlungskosten außerhalb der USA übernimmt und die deutsche gesetzliche Krankenversicherung bei grenzüberschreitenden Leistungen einer vorherigen Abstimmung bedarf, klären Sie Versicherungsschutz und Flug- bzw. Transportfähigkeit vor jeder internationalen Verlegung.

steps.title: Schriftliche Patientenverfügungen in den Vereinigten Staaten und in Deutschland errichten
steps.html:
Medizinische Verfügungen richten sich nach dem Recht des Staates, in dem die Behandlung durchgeführt wird. Ihr Familienangehöriger sollte daher bei voller Entscheidungsfähigkeit getrennte schriftliche Verfügungen für die Vereinigten Staaten und für Deutschland erstellen:

  • Vereinigte Staaten: Erstellen Sie eine bundesstaatsspezifische Advance Directive (Living Will), in der die Wünsche zu lebenserhaltenden Maßnahmen (wie Herz-Lungen-Wiederbelebung, künstlicher Beatmung sowie künstlicher Ernährung und Flüssigkeitszufuhr) gemäß den Zeugen- oder Beurkundungsvorschriften des jeweiligen US-Bundesstaates (beispielsweise in Kalifornien, New York oder Texas) festgehalten werden, ergänzt um eine bundesrechtliche Schweigepflichtentbindung (HIPAA Release) [2][3]. Kostenlose Leitfäden der US-Bundesregierung stellt das National Institute on Aging (Telefon 1-800-222-2225, E-Mail niaic@nia.nih.gov) bereit [3]. Bitten Sie darüber hinaus die behandelnde Ärztin oder den behandelnden Arzt, verbindliche ärztliche Notfallanordnungen (Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment - POLST / MOLST) zu unterzeichnen, damit Rettungsdienste die Behandlungsgrenzen unmittelbar befolgen [2][3].
  • Deutschland: Verfassen Sie eine schriftliche, eigenhändig unterschriebene Patientenverfügung nach § 1827 BGB, die die Einwilligung oder Ablehnung konkreter ärztlicher Maßnahmen in definierten Situationen am Lebensende regelt, ergänzt durch einen palliativmedizinischen Notfallbogen für den Rettungsdienst [7]. Offizielle Muster und Textbausteine veröffentlicht unentgeltlich das Bundesministerium der Justiz [7].

steps.title: Getrennte Finanz- und Gesundheitsvollmachten in beiden Rechtsordnungen ausstellen
steps.html:
Deutsche Banken, Grundbuchämter und Behörden erkennen eine US-amerikanische Vollmacht im Regelfall nicht unmittelbar an, während US-Finanzinstitute bundesstaatskonforme Vollmachten verlangen. Solange volle Geschäftsfähigkeit besteht, sollten in beiden Ländern separate Urkunden errichtet werden:

  • Vereinigte Staaten: Errichten Sie sowohl eine bundesstaatsspezifische Gesundheitsvollmacht (Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care / Health Care Proxy) als auch eine dauerhafte Finanzvollmacht (Durable Financial Power of Attorney), die den gesetzlichen Unterschrifts-, Zeugen- und Notariatsanforderungen des jeweiligen US-Bundesstaates entsprechen [2][4]. Leicht verständliche Leitfäden zu den Treuepflichten finanzieller Bevollmächtigter veröffentlicht das Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (Telefon 1-855-411-2372) [4]. Setzen Sie sich außerdem direkt mit US-Banken und Depotbanken in Verbindung, um bankeigene Vollmachtsformulare zu prüfen und Begünstigtenklauseln für den Todesfall (Payable-on-Death - POD bzw. Transfer-on-Death - TOD) einzutragen, damit Konten außerhalb eines gerichtlichen Nachlassverfahrens (Probate) übergehen.
  • Deutschland: Erstellen Sie eine schriftliche Vorsorgevollmacht und Betreuungsverfügung [7] und lassen Sie diese beim Register (Zentrales Vorsorgeregister der Bundesnotarkammer) eintragen, damit deutsche Betreuungsgerichte und behandelnde Ärztinnen und Ärzte die Vertretungsbefugnis jederzeit sofort einsehen können [8]. Umfasst die Vollmacht Grundstücksgeschäfte oder Handelsregisterangelegenheiten in Deutschland, muss sie notariell beurkundet oder öffentlich beglaubigt werden (vor einem deutschen Notar oder einer deutschen Botschaft bzw. einem deutschen Konsulat in den USA); richten Sie zudem direkt bei jeder deutschen Bank eine ausdrückliche transmortale Bankvollmacht (Vollmacht über den Tod hinaus) ein.

steps.title: Beschleunigte Leistungen bei schwerer Erkrankung, Erwerbsminderungsschutz und Pflegezeit beantragen
steps.html:
Beide Rechtsordnungen bieten beschleunigte Antragsverfahren bei lebensverkürzenden Diagnosen sowie gesetzliche Freistellungsansprüche für pflegende Angehörige:

  • Vereinigte Staaten: Beantragen Sie bei der Social Security Administration (Telefon 1-800-772-1213) die beschleunigte Bearbeitung von Erwerbsminderungsleistungen im Rahmen der Programme Compassionate Allowances (CAL) und Terminal Illness (TERI), die Ansprüche auf Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) und Supplemental Security Income (SSI) bei lebensverkürzenden Diagnosen im Eilverfahren prüfen [5]. Anspruchsberechtigte Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer in den USA, die ein schwer erkranktes nahes Familienmitglied pflegen, können nach dem Bundesgesetz Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) über das U.S. Department of Labor (Telefon 1-866-487-9243) bis zu 12 Arbeitswochen unbezahlten, kündigungsgeschützten Urlaub in Anspruch nehmen, ergänzt durch bundesstaatliche Programme für bezahlten Familienurlaub (Paid Family Leave), sofern im jeweiligen US-Bundesstaat vorhanden [9].
  • Deutschland: In Deutschland beschäftigte nahe Angehörige können in einer akut auftretenden Pflegesituation bis zu 10 Arbeitstage der Arbeit fernbleiben und bei der Pflegekasse der erkrankten Person Pflegeunterstützungsgeld als Lohnersatzleistung beantragen [10]. Nach dem Pflegezeitgesetz besteht zudem Anspruch auf eine vollständige oder teilweise Freistellung von bis zu 3 Monaten zur Begleitung in der letzten Lebensphase (zu Hause oder in einem Hospiz) [10]. Kostenlose Beratung hierzu bietet das Pflegetelefon, das vom Bundesministerium für Familie, Senioren, Frauen und Jugend (Telefon 030 20 17 91 31, E-Mail info@wege-zur-pflege.de) betrieben wird [10].

steps.title: Grenzüberschreitende Testamente, Rentenansprüche, Steuererklärungen und Nachlassabwicklung abstimmen
steps.html:
Stimmen Sie Testamente über Vermögenswerte in den USA und in Deutschland mit auf internationales Erbrecht spezialisierten Fachleuten ab, damit ein neues Testament in einem Land nicht unbeabsichtigt das andere widerruft, und prüfen Sie, ob eine ausdrückliche Rechtswahl nach der EU-Erbrechtsverordnung (Verordnung (EU) Nr. 650/2012) sinnvoll ist. Stellen Sie Personenstandsurkunden, US-Sozialversicherungs- und deutsche Rentenversicherungsnummern, Eigentumsnachweise sowie schriftliche Bestattungs- oder Überführungswünsche zusammen:

  • Vereinigte Staaten: Informieren Sie im Todesfall die Social Security Administration (unter 1-800-772-1213 in den USA oder über die Federal Benefits Unit am US-Generalkonsulat in Frankfurt am Main für Berechtigte in Deutschland) bezüglich Hinterbliebenenrenten und der einmaligen Sterbebeihilfe [5], verständigen Sie das Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), sofern die Person in den US-Streitkräften gedient hat, reichen Sie die abschließende Bundeseinkommensteuererklärung (IRS Form 1040) beim Internal Revenue Service (IRS) ein und leiten Sie für Vermögenswerte, die nicht über einen Trust oder eine POD-/TOD-Begünstigung übertragen werden, das Nachlassverfahren beim örtlichen Probate Court des US-Bundesstaates ein.
  • Deutschland: Informieren Sie die Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung der verstorbenen Person und beantragen Sie Hinterbliebenenrenten (Witwen-/Witwerrente sowie Waisenrente) beim zuständigen Rentenversicherungsträger Deutsche Rentenversicherung [11]. Bezog die verstorbene Person bereits eine gesetzliche Rente, kann der überlebende Ehegatte oder eingetragene Lebenspartner innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach dem Tod beim Renten Service der Deutschen Post die Vorschusszahlung für das Sterbevierteljahr beantragen [11]. Amtlich verwahrte Verfügungen von Todes wegen werden durch das zuständige Nachlassgericht beim Amtsgericht (verknüpft mit dem Zentralen Testamentsregister) eröffnet, das bei Bedarf für Banken oder Grundbuchämter auch den deutschen Erbschein bzw. das Europäische Nachlasszeugnis ausstellt.

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Italy
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Italy
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Italy: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and Italy, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coverage (United States and Italy)
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide pain and symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, helpline 1-800-633-4227) once a hospice medical director and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing visits, medical equipment, medications for symptom relief, inpatient respite care, and family bereavement support; state-by-state hospice directories and planning guides are also available through CaringInfo (phone 1-800-658-8898, an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) [2].
  • Italy: If care takes place in Italy or a relocation is planned, Legge 38/2010 guarantees access to the national palliative care and pain therapy network (Rete Nazionale delle Cure Palliative e Terapia del Dolore) within the Italian National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale), overseen by the Ministero della Salute [6][7]. Through a referral from the general practitioner (Medico di Medicina Generale) or hospital team to the local health authority (Azienda Sanitaria Locale - ASL), patients can access home palliative care units (cure palliative domiciliari UCP-DOM) or residential Hospice facilities; regional network information is published by the Società Italiana di Cure Palliative [6]. Because US Medicare generally does not cover healthcare outside the United States and SSN enrollment in Italy depends on residence or reciprocal coverage, verify health coverage and medical transport arrangements before any cross-border transfer.

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives in Both the United States and Italy
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so your family member should execute separate written directives for the United States and Italy while full decision-making capacity remains:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state (for example, in New York, California, or New Jersey), along with a federal HIPAA release [2][3]. Free federal guides are available from the National Institute on Aging (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. In addition, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST) so emergency medical personnel follow the person's treatment boundaries immediately [2][3].
  • Italy: Under Legge 219/2017, an adult with full mental capacity can execute written Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT / Biotestamento) expressing consent or refusal regarding diagnostic tests, therapeutic choices, and specific medical treatments (including artificial nutrition and hydration) and appointing a trusted healthcare representative (fiduciario) [7][8]. In Italy, DAT are executed as a public deed or authenticated private writing before a notary (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) or delivered in person to the municipal civil registry (Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune of residence) - or via an Italian consulate abroad for Italian citizens residing outside Italy - and transmitted to the Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT maintained by the Ministero della Salute [7][8].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
Italian banks, notaries, and land registries generally require a notarized Italian power of attorney rather than a US state mandate, while US institutions require state-compliant forms. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements [2][4]. Plain-language fiduciary guidance for financial agents is provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (phone 1-855-411-2372) [4]. In addition, contact US banks and brokerage firms directly to verify internal POA forms and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations so accounts transfer outside probate.
  • Italy: For banking, property, tax, and administrative representation in Italy, execute a notarized general or special power of attorney (procura generale o speciale notarile) before an Italian notary (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) or before the consular office of an Italian Embassy or Consulate in the United States (or before a US notary with an Apostille and certified Italian translation) [8]. If the illness later impairs the person's autonomy in Italy without sufficient mandates in place, family members or the beneficiary can petition the guardianship judge (Giudice Tutelare del Tribunale) for the appointment of a support administrator under the Amministrazione di Sostegno procedure (Law 6/2004), as detailed by the Ministero della Giustizia [9].

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions offer expedited disability processing and statutory leave for family caregivers:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for fast-track disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which expedite Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for life-limiting diagnoses [5]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administered by the U.S. Department of Labor (phone 1-866-487-9243), alongside state Paid Family Leave programs where applicable [10].
  • Italy: Through the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, toll-free 803 164 from Italian landlines), patients with oncological or severe life-limiting conditions qualify for an accelerated medical assessment (within 15 days) for severe disability recognition (riconoscimento urgente dell'handicap grave under Legge 104/1992) and the non-means-tested attendance allowance (assegno / indennità di accompagnamento) [11]. Employed family caregivers in Italy are entitled under Legge 104/1992 to 3 days of paid monthly leave and up to 2 years of paid extraordinary caregiver leave (congedo straordinario retribuito) administered by the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale [11].

steps.title: Align Cross-Border Wills, Pension Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
Coordinate wills covering US and Italian assets with cross-border legal professionals so that one will does not inadvertently revoke the other, taking into account Italian forced-heirship rules (quote di legittima) and choice-of-law rules under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) [8]. Gather civil certificates, Social Security and Italian tax codes (codice fiscale), property deeds, and written funeral or international repatriation wishes:

  • United States: Following a death, notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US, or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Mission in Italy) regarding survivor benefits and the lump-sum death payment [5], contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if the person served in the US armed forces, file the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and initiate estate administration with the local state Probate Court for assets not held in a trust or POD/TOD designation.
  • Italy: Apply to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale for Italian survivor pensions (pensione ai superstiti / reversibilità) [11]. If the estate includes Italian real estate or assets, heirs must file the electronic inheritance declaration (dichiarazione di successione) with the Agenzia delle Entrate (toll-free 800 90 96 96 in Italy) within 12 months of the date of death to calculate inheritance/cadastral taxes and unlock Italian bank accounts [12]. Public and formally deposited wills in Italy can be searched through the Registro Generale dei Testamenti via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato and the Ministero della Giustizia [8][9].

Where is your family member currently residing and receiving medical treatment?

it.title: Malattia terminale e pianificazione tra Stati Uniti e Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi per la gestione medica e legale di una malattia grave tra Stati Uniti e Italia: cure palliative, disposizioni anticipate di trattamento (DAT), procure nei due Paesi, congedi per familiari e successione.
it.introHtml:
Quando un vostro familiare riceve una diagnosi di malattia grave, inguaribile o in fase terminale e presenta legami di residenza, cittadinanza, famiglia o patrimonio tra gli Stati Uniti e l'Italia, predisporre tempestivamente gli strumenti clinici, legali e patrimoniali in entrambe le giurisdizioni - mentre la persona conserva la piena capacità di intendere, di volere e di agire - tutela le sue volontà e previene blocchi o ritardi transfrontalieri.

Di seguito sono illustrati i 5 passaggi ufficiali da completare in ordine.

steps.title: Coordinare le cure palliative, l'assistenza in hospice e la copertura sanitaria transfrontaliera (Stati Uniti e Italia)
steps.html:
Rivolgetevi anzitutto all'équipe medica curante nel Paese in cui il vostro familiare riceve attualmente assistenza per impostare il controllo dei sintomi e il supporto domiciliare o residenziale:

  • Stati Uniti: I team ospedalieri e ambulatoriali di cure palliative forniscono terapia del dolore e controllo dei sintomi parallelamente alle cure attive, oppure la persona può attivare la copertura Medicare Hospice Benefit nell'ambito di Medicare Part A (amministrata dai Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, numero verde 1-800-633-4227) una volta che il direttore sanitario dell'hospice e il medico curante certifichino un'aspettativa di vita pari o inferiore a 6 mesi [1]. L'hospice Medicare copre visite infermieristiche domiciliari, presidi medici, farmaci per il sollievo dei sintomi, ricoveri di sollievo (respite care) e supporto al lutto per i familiari; elenchi degli hospice per singolo Stato federato e guide di pianificazione sono inoltre disponibili tramite CaringInfo (telefono 1-800-658-8898, iniziativa della National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) [2].
  • Italia: Se l'assistenza si svolge in Italia o è previsto un trasferimento in Italia, la Legge 38/2010 garantisce l'accesso alla Rete Nazionale delle Cure Palliative e Terapia del Dolore nell'ambito del Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN), sotto la supervisione del Ministero della Salute [6][7]. Tramite impegnativa del Medico di Medicina Generale o del reparto ospedaliero alla competente Azienda Sanitaria Locale (ASL), la persona malata può accedere alle unità di cure palliative domiciliari (UCP-DOM) o alle strutture residenziali di Hospice; i riferimenti delle reti regionali sono pubblicati dalla Società Italiana di Cure Palliative [6]. Poiché il programma statunitense Medicare di norma non copre l'assistenza sanitaria fuori dagli Stati Uniti e l'iscrizione al SSN in Italia dipende dalla residenza o da accordi di reciprocità, verificate la copertura assicurativa e l'idoneità al trasporto medico prima di qualsiasi trasferimento internazionale.

steps.title: Redigere le Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento negli Stati Uniti e in Italia
steps.html:
Le direttive mediche sono disciplinate dalla legge del luogo in cui vengono erogate le cure; è quindi opportuno che il vostro familiare sottoscriva direttive scritte distinte per gli Stati Uniti e per l'Italia finché conserva la piena capacità decisionale:

  • Stati Uniti: Compilate una Advance Directive (Living Will) conforme alla normativa dello Stato federato statunitense interessato (ad esempio New York, California o New Jersey), indicando le preferenze sui trattamenti di sostegno vitale (come rianimazione cardiopolmonare, ventilazione meccanica, nutrizione e idratazione artificiali) nel rispetto delle regole statali su testimoni o autentica notarile, insieme a un'autorizzazione federale alla condivisione dei dati sanitari (HIPAA release) [2][3]. Guide federali gratuite sono messe a disposizione dal National Institute on Aging (telefono 1-800-222-2225, e-mail niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. Chiedete inoltre al medico curante di firmare gli ordini medici operativi Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST), affinché il personale di emergenza rispetti immediatamente i limiti terapeutici stabiliti dalla persona [2][3].
  • Italia: Ai sensi della Legge 219/2017, ogni persona maggiorenne e capace di intendere e di volere può redigere le Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT / Biotestamento) esprimendo il proprio consenso o rifiuto in merito ad accertamenti diagnostici, scelte terapeutiche e singoli trattamenti sanitari (inclusi nutrizione e idratazione artificiali) e nominando un fiduciario incaricato di rappresentarla nelle relazioni con il medico e le strutture sanitarie [7][8]. In Italia le DAT si redigono per atto pubblico o scrittura privata autenticata davanti a un notaio (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) oppure tramite consegna personale presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune di residenza - o presso il Consolato italiano all'estero per i cittadini italiani residenti fuori dall'Italia - e vengono trasmesse alla Banca Dati Nazionale delle DAT istituita presso il Ministero della Salute [7][8].

steps.title: Conferire procure finanziarie e sanitarie separate in entrambe le giurisdizioni
steps.html:
Banche, notai e conservatorie dei registri immobiliari in Italia richiedono di regola una procura notarile italiana anziché un mandato statale statunitense, mentre gli istituti finanziari statunitensi esigono moduli conformi al diritto del singolo Stato USA. Finché il vostro familiare conserva la piena capacità di agire, predisponete atti separati in ciascun Paese:

  • Stati Uniti: Sottoscrivete sia una procura sanitaria permanente (Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care / Health Care Proxy) sia una procura finanziaria permanente (Durable Financial Power of Attorney) conformi ai requisiti di firma, testimoni e autentica notarile dello Stato USA competente [2][4]. Guide pratiche sui doveri fiduciari dei rappresentanti finanziari sono pubblicate dal Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (telefono 1-855-411-2372) [4]. Contattate inoltre direttamente le banche e gli intermediari finanziari statunitensi per verificare i moduli interni di procura e registrare le designazioni di beneficiario in caso di morte (Payable-on-Death - POD o Transfer-on-Death - TOD), così da trasferire i conti al di fuori della procedura giudiziale di probate.
  • Italia: Per la gestione bancaria, immobiliare, fiscale e amministrativa in Italia, conferite una procura generale o speciale notarile davanti a un notaio in Italia (Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato) oppure presso l'ufficio consolare di un'Ambasciata o di un Consolato d'Italia negli Stati Uniti (o davanti a un notaio statunitense munita di Apostille dell'Aia e traduzione giurata in lingua italiana) [8]. Qualora la malattia riduca in seguito l'autonomia della persona in Italia in assenza di mandati sufficienti, i familiari o l'interessato possono presentare ricorso al Giudice Tutelare del Tribunale per la nomina di un amministratore nell'ambito dell'istituto dell'Amministrazione di Sostegno (Legge 6/2004), secondo le indicazioni del Ministero della Giustizia [9].

steps.title: Richiedere prestazioni accelerate per malattia grave, invalidità e congedi per i caregiver familiari
steps.html:
Entrambe le giurisdizioni prevedono corsie preferenziali di accertamento sanitario e tutele lavorative per i familiari che prestano assistenza:

  • Stati Uniti: Presentate domanda alla Social Security Administration (telefono 1-800-772-1213) per la valutazione accelerata dell'invalidità tramite i programmi Compassionate Allowances (CAL) e Terminal Illness (TERI), che velocizzano l'erogazione delle prestazioni Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) e Supplemental Security Income (SSI) in presenza di patologie a prognosi infausta [5]. I lavoratori dipendenti aventi diritto che assistono un familiare stretto affetto da una grave patologia possono usufruire fino a 12 settimane lavorative di congedo non retribuito con conservazione del posto ai sensi del Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) federale gestito dallo U.S. Department of Labor (telefono 1-866-487-9243), oltre ai programmi statali di congedo familiare retribuito (Paid Family Leave) ove previsti [10].
  • Italia: Tramite l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (INPS, numero verde 803 164 da rete fissa in Italia), i pazienti affetti da patologie oncologiche o gravi malattie inguaribili hanno diritto a un iter di accertamento medico accelerato (entro 15 giorni) per il riconoscimento urgente dell'handicap grave ai sensi della Legge 104/1992 e per la concessione dell'assegno / indennità di accompagnamento indipendentemente dal reddito [11]. I lavoratori dipendenti in Italia che assistono il familiare con disabilità grave riconosciuta ai sensi della Legge 104/1992 hanno diritto a 3 giorni di permesso mensile retribuito e fino a 2 anni di congedo straordinario retribuito erogati tramite l'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale [11].

steps.title: Allineare testamenti transfrontalieri, pensioni ai superstiti, adempimenti fiscali e successione
steps.html:
Coordinate i testamenti relativi ai beni situati negli Stati Uniti e in Italia con professionisti esperti di successioni internazionali affinché un testamento non revochi involontariamente l'altro, tenendo conto delle quote di riserva previste dal diritto italiano (quote di legittima) e dei criteri di collegamento e scelta di legge del Regolamento europeo sulle successioni (Regolamento (UE) n. 650/2012) [8]. Raccogliete certificati di stato civile, numeri di Social Security statunitense e codice fiscale italiano, atti di proprietà immobiliare e volontà scritte in merito a esequie o rimpatrio:

  • Stati Uniti: In caso di decesso, informate la Social Security Administration (al numero 1-800-772-1213 negli Stati Uniti, oppure tramite la Federal Benefits Unit presso la Missione diplomatica statunitense in Italia) per le prestazioni ai superstiti e l'assegno funerario una tantum [5], contattate il Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) se la persona ha prestato servizio nelle forze armate statunitensi, presentate la dichiarazione finale dei redditi federali (IRS Form 1040) all'Internal Revenue Service (IRS) e avviate la procedura successoria presso la Probate Court statale competente per i beni non inclusi in un trust o in una designazione POD/TOD.
  • Italia: Presentate domanda all'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale per la liquidazione della pensione ai superstiti / reversibilità [11]. Se l'asse ereditario comprende immobili o attività in Italia, gli eredi devono trasmettere telematicamente la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate (numero verde 800 90 96 96 dall'Italia) entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione per il calcolo delle imposte ipotecarie, catastali e di successione e per lo sblocco dei rapporti bancari italiani [12]. I testamenti pubblici, segreti o olografi formalmente depositati in Italia possono essere ricercati attraverso il Registro Generale dei Testamenti tramite il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato e il Ministero della Giustizia [8][9].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Colombia
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United States & Colombia
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United States and Colombia: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml:
We are sorry that your family is facing this diagnosis. When your family member has a serious, life-limiting or terminal illness and ties across both the United States and Colombia, putting clinical, legal, and financial arrangements in place in both jurisdictions while the person retains full decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents cross-border delays.

Below are the 5 official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Coverage (United States and Colombia)
steps.html:
Start with the treating medical team in the country where your family member currently receives care to establish symptom management and home or inpatient support:

  • United States: Hospital and outpatient palliative care teams provide pain and symptom management alongside curative treatment, or the person can elect the Medicare Hospice Benefit under Medicare Part A (administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, helpline 1-800-633-4227) once a hospice medical director and the attending physician certify a life expectancy of 6 months or less [1]. Medicare hospice covers home nursing visits, medical equipment, medications for symptom relief, inpatient respite care, and family bereavement support; state-by-state hospice directories and planning guides are also available through CaringInfo (phone 1-800-658-8898, an initiative of the National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) [2].
  • Colombia: If care takes place in Colombia or a return to Colombia is planned, Ley 1733 de 2014 (Ley Consuelo Devis Saavedra) guarantees the right of patients with terminal, chronic, degenerative, and irreversible illnesses to receive comprehensive inpatient, outpatient, and home-based palliative care (cuidados paliativos) and pain management [6][7]. Services are coordinated and funded through the person's health promotion entity (Entidad Promotora de Salud - EPS) within the Sistema General de Seguridad Social en Salud, under standards issued by the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social [6][7]. Because US Medicare does not cover healthcare in Colombia and Colombian EPS coverage requires active affiliation, confirm insurance status, opioid medication prescriptions, and medical fit-to-fly clearance before any international relocation.

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives in Both the United States and Colombia
steps.html:
Medical directives are governed by the law of the jurisdiction where care is delivered, so your family member should execute separate written directives for the United States and Colombia while full decision-making capacity remains:

  • United States: Complete a state-specific Advance Directive (Living Will) stating preferences for life-sustaining treatments (such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, and artificial nutrition or hydration) in accordance with the witnessing or notarization rules of the relevant US state (for example, in Florida, New York, Texas, or California), along with a federal HIPAA release [2][3]. Free federal guides are available from the National Institute on Aging (phone 1-800-222-2225, email niaic@nia.nih.gov) [3]. In addition, ask the attending physician or advanced practice clinician to sign actionable Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST / MOLST) so emergency medical personnel follow the person's treatment boundaries immediately [2][3].
  • Colombia: Under Ley 1733 de 2014 and Resolución 2665 de 2018 of the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social, any adult with full mental capacity can sign a written Documento de Voluntad Anticipada (DVA) expressing treatment preferences, refusal of disproportionate interventions, and palliative care wishes [6][7]. Under Resolution 2665 of 2018, a DVA can be formalized through any of three official methods: before the attending physician (médico tratante), in writing before two witnesses (dos testigos), or before a Notary (ante notario), and a copy must be incorporated into the patient's clinical history (historia clínica) [6].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in Both Jurisdictions
steps.html:
Colombian banks, notaries, and land registries do not accept a domestic US state Power of Attorney unless Colombian formalities are met, and US financial institutions require state-compliant mandates. While your family member has full legal capacity, execute separate documents in each country:

  • United States: Execute both a state-specific Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care (Health Care Proxy) and a Durable Financial Power of Attorney complying with state statutory signature, witness, and notary requirements [2][4]. Plain-language fiduciary guidance for financial agents is provided by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (phone 1-855-411-2372) [4]. In addition, contact US banks and brokerage firms directly to verify internal POA forms and register Payable-on-Death (POD) or Transfer-on-Death (TOD) beneficiary designations so accounts transfer outside probate.
  • Colombia: For broad property, banking, and legal representation in Colombia, execute a Poder General por escritura pública (General Power of Attorney by public deed) before a Notary in Colombia (Notaría en Colombia) or before a Colombian Consulate in the United States (Consulado de Colombia en el exterior under the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores), or execute a targeted Poder Especial with authenticated signature (reconocimiento de firma) [8][9]. Notarial deeds and property registrations in Colombia are supervised by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro [9]. If a power of attorney is signed before a US notary public rather than a Colombian consul, it must carry a Hague Apostille and an official Spanish translation.

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Disability Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Both jurisdictions provide disability pathways and workplace protections for family caregivers:

  • United States: Apply to the Social Security Administration (phone 1-800-772-1213) for fast-track disability processing under the Compassionate Allowances (CAL) and Terminal Illness (TERI) programs, which expedite Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) claims for life-limiting diagnoses [5]. Eligible employees caring for an immediate family member with a serious health condition can take up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave under the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administered by the U.S. Department of Labor (phone 1-866-487-9243), alongside state Paid Family Leave programs where applicable [10].
  • Colombia: Under Colombian labor law, employees may request paid workplace leave for serious domestic calamity (licencia por calamidad doméstica) when a close family member suffers a grave health crisis, while medical incapacity benefits are processed through the person's EPS [6]. If the illness results in a certified loss of working capacity of 50% or more (pérdida de capacidad laboral), the insured person can apply for a disability pension (pensión de invalidez) through the public pension administrator Colpensiones (or their private pension fund, AFP) [11].

steps.title: Align Cross-Border Wills, Pension Claims, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration
steps.html:
Coordinate wills covering US and Colombian assets with cross-border legal professionals so that one will does not accidentally revoke the other, taking into account Colombian forced-heirship rules (asignaciones forzosas / legítimas rigurosas). Gather civil certificates, Social Security numbers, Colombian citizenship ID cards (cédula de ciudadanía), property deeds, and written funeral or international repatriation wishes:

  • United States: Following a death, notify the Social Security Administration (at 1-800-772-1213 in the US, or via the Federal Benefits Unit at the U.S. Embassy in Bogotá) regarding survivor benefits and the lump-sum death payment [5], contact the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) if the person served in the US armed forces, file the final federal income tax return (IRS Form 1040) with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and initiate estate administration with the local state Probate Court for assets not held in a trust or POD/TOD designation.
  • Colombia: Apply to Colpensiones (or the relevant private pension fund) for the statutory funeral grant (auxilio funerario, paid to the person who covered funeral expenses, equivalent to between 5 and 10 monthly legal minimum wages - SMLMV) and the survivor pension (pensión de sobrevivientes) for eligible family beneficiaries [11]. To transfer Colombian bank accounts and real estate, heirs may complete a notarial succession procedure (trámite de sucesión ante notaría, when all heirs are in agreement, before a Colombian notary overseen by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro and the Unión Colegiada del Notariado Colombiano) or a judicial succession (sucesión ante juzgado) [9].

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y trámites entre Estados Unidos y Colombia: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos ante una enfermedad terminal con vínculos entre Estados Unidos y Colombia: cuidados paliativos, voluntades anticipadas, poderes preventivos en ambos países, permisos laborales y planificación sucesoria.
es.introHtml:
Cuando un familiar recibe el diagnóstico de una enfermedad grave, limitante para la vida o en fase terminal y mantiene vínculos de residencia, nacionalidad, familia o patrimonio tanto en los Estados Unidos como en Colombia, formalizar a tiempo las disposiciones clínicas, jurídicas y financieras en ambas jurisdicciones - mientras la persona conserva su plena capacidad legal y de decisión - protege su voluntad y evita demoras transfronterizas.

A continuación se presentan los 5 pasos oficiales que deben completarse en orden.

steps.title: Coordinar los cuidados paliativos, el hospicio y la cobertura sanitaria transfronteriza (Estados Unidos y Colombia)
steps.html:
Comience con el equipo médico tratante en el país donde su familiar recibe atención actualmente para organizar el manejo de síntomas y el soporte domiciliario o intrahospitalario:

  • Estados Unidos: Los equipos hospitalarios y ambulatorios de cuidados paliativos brindan control del dolor y de los síntomas junto con el tratamiento curativo, o bien la persona puede acogerse al beneficio Medicare Hospice Benefit bajo la Parte A de Medicare (administrado por los Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, línea de ayuda 1-800-633-4227) una vez que el director médico del hospicio y el médico tratante certifiquen una expectativa de vida de 6 meses o menos [1]. El hospicio de Medicare cubre visitas de enfermería a domicilio, equipo médico, medicamentos para el alivio de síntomas, cuidado de relevo intrahospitalario (respite care) y acompañamiento en duelo para la familia; asimismo, a través de CaringInfo (teléfono 1-800-658-8898, iniciativa de la National Hospice and Palliative Care Organization / National Alliance for Care at Home) se pueden consultar directorios de hospicios por estado y guías de planificación [2].
  • Colombia: Si la atención tiene lugar en Colombia o se planea un traslado al país, la Ley 1733 de 2014 (Ley Consuelo Devis Saavedra) garantiza el derecho de los pacientes con enfermedades en fase terminal, crónicas, degenerativas e irreversibles a recibir atención integral de cuidados paliativos hospitalarios, ambulatorios y domiciliarios y manejo del dolor [6][7]. Los servicios se coordinan y financian por medio de la Entidad Promotora de Salud (EPS) de la persona dentro del Sistema General de Seguridad Social en Salud, conforme a los lineamientos del Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social [6][7]. Dado que el programa Medicare de los Estados Unidos no cubre servicios médicos en Colombia y la cobertura de la EPS colombiana requiere afiliación activa, verifique el estado del aseguramiento, las fórmulas de medicamentos opioides de control especial y la certificación médica de aptitud para viajar antes de cualquier traslado internacional.

steps.title: Otorgar directivas anticipadas por escrito tanto en los Estados Unidos como en Colombia
steps.html:
Las directivas médicas se rigen por la legislación del lugar donde se presta la atención sanitaria, por lo que su familiar debe suscribir documentos separados por escrito para los Estados Unidos y para Colombia mientras conserve plena capacidad de decisión:

  • Estados Unidos: Complete una directiva anticipada específica del estado (Advance Directive / Living Will) en la que consten las preferencias sobre tratamientos de soporte vital (como reanimación cardiopulmonar, ventilación mecánica y nutrición o hidratación artificiales) de acuerdo con los requisitos de testigos o notarización del estado correspondiente de los EE. UU. (por ejemplo, Florida, Nueva York, Texas o California), junto con una autorización federal de divulgación médica (HIPAA release) [2][3]. El National Institute on Aging (teléfono 1-800-222-2225, correo electrónico niaic@nia.nih.gov) publica guías federales gratuitas en lenguaje claro [3]. Además, solicite al médico tratante o profesional clínico autorizado la firma de órdenes médicas de soporte vital (Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment - POLST / MOLST) para que el personal de emergencias respete de inmediato los límites terapéuticos establecidos por el paciente [2][3].
  • Colombia: En virtud de la Ley 1733 de 2014 y la Resolución 2665 de 2018 del Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social, toda persona mayor de edad en pleno uso de sus facultades mentales puede suscribir un Documento de Voluntad Anticipada (DVA) por escrito en el que exprese sus preferencias de tratamiento, el rechazo de intervenciones desproporcionadas y sus deseos de cuidado paliativo [6][7]. Conforme a la Resolución 2665 de 2018, el DVA puede formalizarse mediante cualquiera de las tres vías oficiales: ante el médico tratante, por escrito ante dos testigos o ante notario, y debe incorporarse una copia en la historia clínica del paciente [6].

steps.title: Establecer poderes financieros y de salud separados en ambas jurisdicciones
steps.html:
Los bancos, notarías y oficinas de registro de instrumentos públicos en Colombia no aceptan un poder estatal interno de los EE. UU. a menos que cumpla las solemnidades colombianas, mientras que las entidades financieras estadounidenses exigen mandatos ajustados a la ley de cada estado. Mientras su familiar conserve plena capacidad legal, otorgue instrumentos separados en cada país:

  • Estados Unidos: Otorgue tanto un poder duradero para atención médica (Durable Power of Attorney for Health Care / Health Care Proxy) como un poder financiero duradero (Durable Financial Power of Attorney) que cumplan los requisitos legales de firma, testigos y notario del estado respectivo [2][4]. El Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (teléfono 1-855-411-2372) ofrece guías fiduciarias prácticas para los apoderados financieros [4]. Adicionalmente, comuníquese directamente con los bancos y firmas de corretaje en los EE. UU. para verificar sus formularios internos de poder y registrar beneficiarios directos por causa de muerte (Payable-on-Death - POD o Transfer-on-Death - TOD) a fin de que las cuentas se transfieran sin juicio sucesorio (probate).
  • Colombia: Para la representación amplia sobre bienes inmuebles, cuentas bancarias y trámites jurídicos en Colombia, otorgue un Poder General por escritura pública ante una Notaría en Colombia o ante un Consulado de Colombia en el exterior en los Estados Unidos (adscrito al Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores), o bien suscriba un Poder Especial con reconocimiento de firma y contenido [8][9]. Las escrituras públicas y el registro inmobiliario en Colombia están bajo la vigilancia de la Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro [9]. Si el poder se firma ante un notario público estadounidense (Notary Public) en lugar de un cónsul colombiano, deberá contar con la Apostilla de La Haya expedida por el estado correspondiente de los EE. UU. y traducción oficial al español.

steps.title: Solicitar prestaciones aceleradas por enfermedad terminal, invalidez y licencias para cuidadores
steps.html:
Ambas jurisdicciones contemplan trámites prioritarios por incapacidad o invalidez y licencias laborales para los familiares cuidadores:

  • Estados Unidos: Solicite ante la Social Security Administration (teléfono 1-800-772-1213) el trámite acelerado de discapacidad mediante los programas Compassionate Allowances (CAL) y Terminal Illness (TERI), los cuales agilizan las reclamaciones del Seguro por Incapacidad del Seguro Social (SSDI) y de Seguridad de Ingreso Suplementario (SSI) en diagnósticos que limitan la vida [5]. Los trabajadores elegibles que cuidan a un familiar directo con una condición grave de salud pueden tomar hasta 12 semanas laborales de licencia no remunerada con protección del empleo bajo la ley federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) administrada por el U.S. Department of Labor (teléfono 1-866-487-9243), además de los programas estatales de licencia familiar remunerada (Paid Family Leave) cuando apliquen [10].
  • Colombia: Conforme a la legislación laboral colombiana, los trabajadores pueden solicitar a su empleador licencia por calamidad doméstica remunerada cuando un familiar cercano atraviesa una crisis grave de salud, mientras que las incapacidades médicas del paciente se tramitan por conducto de su EPS [6]. Si la enfermedad ocasiona una pérdida de capacidad laboral calificada del 50 % o más, la persona afiliada puede gestionar el reconocimiento de la pensión de invalidez ante la administradora pública de pensiones Colpensiones (o ante su fondo privado de pensiones - AFP) [11].

steps.title: Alinear testamentos transfronterizos, reclamaciones pensionales, impuestos y sucesión
steps.html:
Coordine los testamentos que abarquen bienes en los Estados Unidos y en Colombia con profesionales en derecho sucesorio internacional para que un testamento no revoque accidentalmente el otro, respetando en Colombia las reglas de asignaciones forzosas y legítimas rigurosas. Reúna registros civiles, números de Seguro Social estadounidense, cédula de ciudadanía colombiana, escrituras de propiedad y las instrucciones escritas sobre exequias o repatriación internacional:

  • Estados Unidos: Tras el fallecimiento, notifique a la Social Security Administration (al 1-800-772-1213 en los EE. UU., o a través de la Unidad de Beneficios Federales - Federal Benefits Unit - de la Embajada de los EE. UU. en Bogotá) para gestionar los beneficios de sobrevivientes y el pago global por defunción [5], comuníquese con el Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) si la persona prestó servicio en las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses, presente la declaración final del impuesto federal sobre la renta (IRS Form 1040) ante el Internal Revenue Service (IRS) e inicie la administración sucesoria ante el tribunal de sucesiones estatal (Probate Court) respecto de los bienes que no estén en un fideicomiso (trust) ni tengan designación POD/TOD.
  • Colombia: Solicite ante Colpensiones (o el fondo privado de pensiones correspondiente) el auxilio funerario legal (pagadero a quien demuestre haber sufragado los gastos de entierro o cremación, equivalente a entre 5 y 10 salarios mínimos mensuales legales vigentes - SMLMV) y la pensión de sobrevivientes o sustitución pensional para los beneficiarios de ley [11]. Para adjudicar cuentas bancarias e inmuebles en Colombia, los herederos pueden adelantar el trámite de sucesión ante notaría (cuando exista mutuo acuerdo entre todos los herederos e interesados, ante una notaría supervisada por la Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro y articulada con la Unión Colegiada del Notariado Colombiano) o un proceso de sucesión ante juzgado [9].

title: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Arab Emirates & India
titleEn: Cross-Border Terminal Illness & Advance Care Checklist: United Arab Emirates & India
cardSummary: Official 5-step guide for terminal illness and advance care planning across United Arab Emirates and India: palliative/hospice care and cross-border healthcare coverage, advance directives in both jurisdictions, separate medical and financial powers of attorney, caregiver leave & disability benefits, and cross-border wills & estate planning.
introHtml: When a family member is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness and holds residence, citizenship, family, or property ties across both the United Arab Emirates and India, early coordination is essential. Because medical decision-making frameworks, powers of attorney, workplace entitlements, and succession laws operate separately in each country, key legal and financial documents must be executed in the appropriate format for each jurisdiction while your family member retains full mental and legal capacity [1][4][5].

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative and Hospice Care and Cross-Border Medical Coverage Between the United Arab Emirates and India
steps.html:
Begin by asking your family member's treating oncology or specialist team to establish a multidisciplinary palliative care and symptom-management plan, and clarify with the health insurer whether care will remain in the United Arab Emirates or involve medical relocation to India [1][2].

  • Palliative and home care in the United Arab Emirates: Under the federal Patient Rights and Responsibilities Charter on the Official Portal of the UAE Government and emirate-level clinical standards issued by the Department of Health - Abu Dhabi (phone: +971 2 449 3333), the Dubai Health Authority (DHA, phone: 800 342), and the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP, phone: 800 11111), patients with life-limiting illnesses are entitled to multidisciplinary pain management and palliative care across licensed tertiary hospitals (such as Tawam Hospital in Abu Dhabi or Dubai Hospital) and licensed home-healthcare providers [1][2]. Before initiating inpatient or home palliative care, have the hospital case manager submit a prior-authorization request to the mandatory health insurer (such as Thiqa or Daman in Abu Dhabi, or an ISAHD-compliant insurer in Dubai) to confirm coverage limits for home nursing and controlled pain medications [1][2].
  • Palliative care networks and care relocation to India: In India, public tertiary hospitals, Regional Cancer Centres, and district hospitals provide pain relief and supportive care under the National Programme for Palliative Care (NPPC, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare), while accredited inpatient hospices and home-care teams across Indian states can be located through the directory of the Indian Association of Palliative Care [3]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers. If your family member plans to travel to India for ongoing care, request a complete English medical summary, pathology reports, and a fit-to-fly certificate (MEDIF clearance for commercial airlines or air ambulance arrangements) from the UAE treating physician, and verify rules for carrying prescribed narcotic analgesics with both UAE authorities and Indian customs in advance [1][3].

steps.title: Execute Written Advance Directives and End-of-Life Care Plans in Both Jurisdictions While Capacity Remains
steps.html:
Advance care preferences and resuscitation rules differ substantially between the United Arab Emirates and India, so written care preferences should be documented separately for whichever country provides clinical care [1][2].

  • Care plans and resuscitation rules in the United Arab Emirates: Under the federal Patient Rights Charter on the Official Portal of the UAE Government, a patient with decision-making capacity has the right to be fully informed of their diagnosis and prognosis and to refuse or discontinue specific medical treatments after being informed of the medical consequences [1]. Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 4 of 2016 on Medical Liability (and its updated federal medical liability framework), Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) orders in cases of incurable terminal illness are strictly regulated clinical orders that must be evaluated and signed by at least three treating consultant/specialist physicians in accordance with Department of Health - Abu Dhabi, DHA, or MOHAP protocols, rather than relying solely on a foreign living will [1][2]. Ask the treating specialist team in the UAE to record your family member's goals of care and designated family spokesperson directly in the hospital electronic medical record (such as Malaffi in Abu Dhabi or Nabidh in Dubai) [1][2].
  • Advance Medical Directive (Living Will) in India: Under the Supreme Court of India's constitutional guidelines (Common Cause v. Union of India, 2018, as simplified by the Supreme Court in January 2023), an adult of sound mind and full capacity can execute a written Advance Medical Directive specifying the withdrawal or withholding of life-sustaining treatment in a terminal or irreversible condition and naming a healthcare proxy/guardian [3]. Under the 2023 guidelines, the directive must be signed by the declarant in the presence of two independent attesting witnesses and attested before a Notary Public or a Gazetted Officer, with copies provided to the appointed guardian, the family physician, and the local municipal or district custodian for inclusion in health records [3].

steps.title: Establish Separate Financial and Healthcare Powers of Attorney in the United Arab Emirates and India
steps.html:
A Power of Attorney (POA) executed in one country is not automatically accepted by banks, land registries, or hospitals in the other without specific notarization, legalization, and local registration [4][5]. Arrange separate instruments while your family member can still appear in person or via video notarization [4][5]:

  • Notarized Power of Attorney in the United Arab Emirates: To manage UAE bank accounts, property, vehicles, residency visa matters, or medical representation, your family member must execute a notarized Power of Attorney (in Arabic or bilingual Arabic-English) before a UAE Notary Public, such as through the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department (phone: +971 2 651 2222) e-Notary portal or the Dubai Courts Notary Public [4]. UAE banks strictly scrutinize general POAs and frequently require explicit clauses authorizing banking transactions or their own internal mandate forms; remember that under UAE civil law, any Power of Attorney automatically expires upon the principal's death [4][6].
  • Power of Attorney and account nominations for India: If your family member is currently in the UAE and needs to appoint an attorney-in-fact for property, banking, or legal matters in India, they can sign a General or Special Power of Attorney before the Consulate General of India, Dubai (phone: +971 4 397 1222; emergency helpline: +971 50 734 7676; email: cons1.dubai@mea.gov.in) or the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi [5]. Once attested by the Indian mission and sent to India, the POA must be adjudicated and stamped before the local Collector of Stamps or Sub-Registrar of Assurances in the relevant Indian state within 3 months of receipt in India to be legally valid for property or banking transactions [5]. Simultaneously, ensure your family member registers or updates statutory nominations (Form DA-1 for bank accounts, demat account nominations, and mutual fund nominations) with all Indian financial institutions [5][9].

steps.title: Claim Fast-Track Terminal Illness Benefits, Medical Advances, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
Check employment contracts, mandatory health insurance policies, and statutory social security schemes in both countries before taking extended leave or paying major out-of-pocket medical bills [1][9]:

  • Sick leave, compassionate leave, and critical illness insurance in the United Arab Emirates: Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 (UAE Labour Law), private-sector employees who have completed probation are entitled to up to 90 days of sick leave per year (the first 15 days at full pay, the next 30 days at half pay, and 45 days unpaid) upon submitting an approved medical report [1][6]. If a family member employed in the UAE is caring for the patient, they should check their employer's HR policy for flexible working arrangements or unpaid compassionate leave, as statutory paid bereavement leave in the UAE private sector (5 days for a spouse; 3 days for a parent, child, sibling, grandchild, or grandparent) applies only after a death occurs [6]. Also review any employer-sponsored group life or critical illness insurance policy, which may pay a lump-sum terminal illness benefit upon diagnosis [1].
  • Medical advances and social security support in India: If your family member has an active or prior account with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (toll-free helpline: 1800 118 005; email: employeefeedback@epfindia.gov.in), they can apply online via the Unified Member Portal for a non-refundable medical advance under Paragraph 68J of the EPF Scheme for hospitalization or treatment of a life-threatening illness (such as cancer or major organ failure) without requiring a minimum service period [9]. Workers covered under the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC, toll-free: 1800 11 2526) may claim Extended Sickness Benefit (up to 2 years at 80% of wages for specified malignant and long-term diseases), while eligible families in India can verify inpatient coverage under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY or private health insurance policies [3][9].

steps.title: Align Wills, Beneficiary Designations, Bank Access, and Repatriation or Funeral Wishes Across Both Countries
steps.html:
Because UAE bank accounts (including joint accounts) are routinely frozen immediately upon the account holder's death until a UAE court succession order is issued, aligning wills and beneficiary records in advance prevents severe financial disruption [6][7][8]:

  • Non-Muslim wills, bank accounts, and workplace entitlements in the United Arab Emirates: Under UAE personal status legislation for non-Muslims (Federal Decree-Law No. 41 of 2022 and Abu Dhabi Law No. 14 of 2021), expatriates can register a formal Will covering UAE bank accounts, real estate, and guardianship so that UAE assets are distributed directly according to their stated wishes [6][7]. Depending on where assets are held, your family member can register a Will with the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department Civil Family Court, the Dubai Courts Notary Public, or the DIFC Courts Wills Service (phone: +971 4 427 3333; email: info@difcwills.ae) [4][6][7]. In addition, an employee in the UAE should confirm in writing with their employer (under MOHRE or the relevant free-zone authority) the designated beneficiary to receive unpaid wages and end-of-service gratuity (which the employer must disburse within 10 days in the event of an employee's death, alongside covering repatriation costs of mortal remains if requested) [6][8].
  • Provident fund, pension nominations, wills, and consular repatriation procedures for India: In India, verify that digital e-Nomination is completed with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation so eligible family members can seamlessly claim the EPF balance, the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) lump-sum assurance benefit, and the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) survivor pension via the online Composite Claim Form [9]. For separate assets in India (real estate, bank accounts, NRE/NRO deposits, and investments), executing a clean Indian Will witnessed by two witnesses (and optionally registered before the local Sub-Registrar in India) avoids lengthy interstate succession disputes or the need for a court Succession Certificate [5][9]. Finally, discuss and record your family member's wishes regarding local burial/cremation in the UAE versus repatriation to India, noting that the Consulate General of India, Dubai (or the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi) issues the mandatory No Objection Certificate (NOC) and passport cancellation for transporting mortal remains or ashes to India [8].

closingQuestion: To help tailor these steps to your situation, which emirate in the United Arab Emirates and which state in India are involved, and is your family member currently receiving care in the UAE or planning to relocate to India?
