title: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of France Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of France dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in France and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with French citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, procedures depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to France or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral arrangements cannot proceed until the cause of death is officially certified or cleared by the competent medical or forensic authority in the United Kingdom [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner system): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which must be independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. The Medical Examiner's office contacts the family or next of kin to explain the cause of death and transmits the countersigned MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (for example, Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), after which the 5-day registration window begins [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be selected for review by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) before registration completes [1]. In Northern Ireland, the doctor issues the MCCD for submission to the district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If your family member died suddenly outside a hospital, call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so the police can attend [1]. Unexplained, violent, or perioperative deaths are referred to the local Coroner in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) in Scotland [1]. If a post-mortem examination or inquest is required, the Coroner or Procurator Fiscal issues interim certificates or direct burial/cremation and transfer authorisations once forensic inquiries conclude [1].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage, Appoint Funeral Coordinators in the United Kingdom and France, and Notify the French Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, bank-card assistance coverage, employer coverage, or a French pre-need funeral or repatriation policy (contrat d'assurance obsèques or assistance rapatriement) [6][7]. If coverage applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance desk immediately, as the insurer normally appoints and pays the international funeral operators directly [6].

If no insurance policy applies, the family can appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom alongside a receiving funeral operator in France to manage the cross-border transfer end-to-end [6][10]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can locate an accredited UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [10].
  • Receiving funeral operator in France: In France, funeral transport and burial/cremation must be carried out by a prefecturally licensed funeral operator (opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture), searchable via municipal directories or national federations such as the Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF) and the Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF) [7]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • French consular notification: Notify the Consulat général de France à Londres (phone: +44 20 7073 1200) or the French Consular Section in Edinburgh (if the death occurred in Scotland), operating under the Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (France Diplomatie) [6]. Consular staff provide procedural guidance, verify documents for mortuary transit into France, and transcribe the UK death record into the French civil registry, though the French state cannot pay funeral or repatriation costs [6].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Transcribe the Death Record for France
steps.html:
The death must first be registered with the civil registry in the UK district where the death occurred before it can be recorded in the French civil registry [1][6]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Once the Register Office confirms receipt of the MCCD or Coroner's notification, register the death within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, or within 8 days at any Registration Office in Scotland (such as Edinburgh City Chambers or Glasgow Registration Office) [1]. Request multiple official certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), as banks, insurers, and French consular authorities require original certificates [1][6].
  • French Consular Transcription vs. Domestic Declaration: Unlike a death occurring inside metropolitan France - which must be declared at the local town hall (mairie du lieu de décès) within 24 hours excluding weekends and public holidays to obtain a French acte de décès intégral or a multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention [7] - a death in the United Kingdom is registered locally first and then submitted to the Consulat général de France à Londres for transcription de l'acte de décès [6]. You can apply by post using the consular transcription form, an original UK Death Certificate, proof of the deceased's French nationality (such as a French passport, national identity card, or French birth certificate), and the livret de famille [6].
  • UK Apostille (when required): While the Consulat général de France à Londres accepts original UK Death Certificates directly for consular transcription [6], French notaries or financial institutions handling estate assets prior to transcription may require a Hague Apostille from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) [3].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to France or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and French funeral directors handle the technical health, coroner, and border clearances depending on whether you select repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6]:

  • Repatriation of the body to France: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director submits notice to the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104), which authorises removal of the body outside England and Wales [1][6]. In Scotland, clearance to move human remains outside Scotland is issued through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. For entry into France under international mortuary transit rules (the Berlin Agreement of 1937 and the Strasbourg Agreement of 1973), the UK funeral director arranges preservation care (soins de conservation / embalming) if required, a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious infection, and a hermetically sealed coffin with a zinc liner (cercueil hermétique), and obtains the consular mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire) via the Consulat général de France à Londres (or prefectural authorisation in France) before air or Eurotunnel transport to the receiving French municipality (such as Paris, Lyon, or Marseille) [6][7].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the crematorium issues an official Certificate of Cremation [6]. Ashes placed in a sealed urn can be transported to France accompanied by the UK Death Certificate, the Certificate of Cremation, and consular or municipal clearance; under French law, cremated ashes may be placed in a cemetery columbarium, sealed onto a family grave monument, or scattered in a designated space after declaration to the local mairie (keeping ashes permanently in a private residence is not permitted in France) [6][7].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation (the "Green Form" in England and Wales, or Form 14 in Scotland) directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Both Countries
steps.html:
After the funeral or repatriation is underway, administrative and estate steps frequently span both jurisdictions [2][4][7]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased lived in England, Scotland, or Wales, the registrar provides a unique reference number for the government's Tell Us Once service, which notifies HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, local councils, and state pension services in one step [2]. You can also contact the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to report the death and check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment or Funeral Expenses Payment [2].
    • If the deceased lived in France but received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) directly [5].
    • If the deceased left property, bank accounts, or investments in the United Kingdom above institution thresholds, the executor or entitled representative must apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration if there is no will) in England and Wales, or apply to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland, after submitting any required Inheritance Tax forms to HMRC [4].
  • French social security, survivor pensions, taxes, and succession:
    • Lump-sum death grant (capital décès): If the deceased was employed or insured under the French general social security system shortly before death, eligible priority dependents can claim the capital décès from the Caisse Primaire d'Assurance Maladie (CPAM via Ameli.fr) within 2 years of the date of death [7][8].
    • Survivor pensions (pension de réversion): An eligible surviving married or formerly married partner can apply for a survivor pension under the French basic scheme through L'Assurance Retraite (phone from abroad: +33 9 71 10 39 60) and for supplementary employee survivor benefits via Agirc-Arrco (using the unified online portal on info-retraite.fr or lassuranceretraite.fr) [7][9].
    • French notary and inheritance tax (déclaration de succession): If the deceased was domiciled in France, held real estate in France, or had French estate assets above the statutory threshold, instruct a notary via Notaires de France (Conseil supérieur du notariat) or the Paris Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires de Paris) [7][11]. The notary checks the central wills registry (Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés - FCDDV), drafts the certificate of heirship (acte de notoriété), and prepares the French inheritance tax return (déclaration de succession) for the French tax authorities (Direction générale des Finances publiques - impôts) [7][11]. When a death occurs outside metropolitan France (including in the United Kingdom), the statutory deadline to file the déclaration de succession with the French tax office is 12 months from the date of death (compared to 6 months when the death occurs inside metropolitan France) [7][11].

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès entre Royaume-Uni et France : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès entre Royaume-Uni et France : certificat médical de décès, opérateur funéraire habilité, déclaration à l'état civil, démarches consulaires et rapatriement ou inhumation locale, et pensions de réversion et succession.
fr.introHtml: Nous vous présentons nos sincères condoléances pour le décès de votre proche. Lorsqu'une personne de nationalité française ou ayant des liens de résidence avec la France décède au Royaume-Uni, les démarches dépendent de la nation constitutive du Royaume-Uni où le décès est survenu (Angleterre et Pays de Galles, Écosse ou Irlande du Nord) et du choix de la famille entre un rapatriement international vers la France et des obsèques locales au Royaume-Uni [1][6].

steps.title: Obtenir le Certificat Médical de Décès et l'Autorisation du Coroner ou du Procurator Fiscal au Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
L'enregistrement à l'état civil et l'organisation des obsèques ne peuvent débuter tant que la cause du décès n'a pas été officiellement certifiée ou validée par l'autorité médicale ou médico-légale compétente au Royaume-Uni [1] :

  • Décès de cause naturelle en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles (système du Medical Examiner) : Le médecin ayant constaté le décès établit le certificat médical de cause de décès (Medical Certificate of Cause of Death - MCCD), qui doit être examiné de manière indépendante et contresigné par un médecin examinateur du NHS (NHS Medical Examiner) [1]. Le bureau du Medical Examiner prend contact avec la famille ou le plus proche parent pour expliquer la cause du décès et transmet électroniquement le MCCD contresigné au bureau local de l'état civil (Register Office, par exemple le Westminster Register Office à Londres ou le Manchester Register Office), ce qui fait courir le délai légal de déclaration de 5 jours [1].
  • Décès de cause naturelle en Écosse et en Irlande du Nord : En Écosse, le médecin établit le certificat médical de cause de décès (Form 11), qui peut faire l'objet d'un contrôle aléatoire par le service d'examen de la certification des décès (Death Certification Review Service - DCRS) de Healthcare Improvement Scotland avant la finalisation de l'enregistrement [1]. En Irlande du Nord, le médecin délivre le MCCD en vue de sa remise au bureau d'enregistrement du district (district Registration Office) [1].
  • Décès soudains, accidentels ou inexpliqués : Si votre proche est décédé subitement hors d'un établissement hospitalier, appelez les services d'urgence au 999 (ou le NHS 111 selon le cas) afin que la police intervienne sur place [1]. Les décès inexpliqués, violents ou périopératoires sont signalés au Coroner local en Angleterre, au Pays de Galles et en Irlande du Nord, ou au Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service) en Écosse [1]. Si une autopsie (post-mortem examination) ou une enquête judiciaire (inquest) est requise, le Coroner ou le Procurator Fiscal délivre un certificat provisoire ou les autorisations directes d'inhumation, de crémation et de transfert dès la clôture des investigations médico-légales [1].

steps.title: Vérifier la Couverture d'Assurance, Mandater les Opérateurs Funéraires au Royaume-Uni et en France et Contacter le Consulat de France
steps.html:
Avant de signer un contrat de prestations funéraires à titre individuel, vérifiez si la personne décédée bénéficiait d'une assurance voyage, d'une assistance liée à une carte bancaire, d'une prévoyance d'entreprise ou d'un contrat d'assurance obsèques ou d'assistance rapatriement souscrit en France [6][7]. Si une garantie s'applique, contactez immédiatement le plateau d'assistance 24h/24 de l'assureur, qui mandate et règle généralement directement les opérateurs funéraires internationaux [6].

En l'absence de prise en charge par une assurance, la famille peut mandater un opérateur funéraire agréé au Royaume-Uni en coordination avec un opérateur funéraire récepteur en France pour organiser le transfert transfrontalier de bout en bout [6][10] :

  • Entreprise de pompes funèbres au Royaume-Uni : Vous pouvez rechercher un opérateur funéraire britannique accrédité et expérimenté en rapatriement international via la National Association of Funeral Directors (téléphone : +44 121 711 1343 ; courriel : info@nafd.org.uk) ou la National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [10].
  • Opérateur funéraire récepteur en France : En France, le transport funéraire ainsi que l'inhumation ou la crémation doivent être assurés par un opérateur funéraire habilité en préfecture, consultable auprès des mairies ou des fédérations professionnelles telles que la Fédération Nationale du Funéraire (FNF) et la Fédération Française des Pompes Funèbres (FFPF) [7]. Nous mentionnons ces répertoires officiels à titre purement informatif et ne recommandons, ne cautionnons ni ne classons aucun prestataire particulier.
  • Notification consulaire française : Informez le Consulat général de France à Londres (téléphone : +44 20 7073 1200) ou la section consulaire française à Édimbourg (si le décès est survenu en Écosse), relevant du Ministère de l'Europe et des Affaires étrangères (France Diplomatie) [6]. Les services consulaires renseignent la famille sur la procédure, vérifient le dossier d'autorisation d'entrée du corps ou des cendres en France et assurent la transcription de l'acte de décès britannique sur les registres de l'état civil français, étant précisé que l'État français ne prend pas en charge les frais d'obsèques ou de rapatriement [6].

steps.title: Déclarer le Décès à l'État Civil au Royaume-Uni et Faire Transcrire l'Acte de Décès pour la France
steps.html:
Le décès doit d'abord être déclaré auprès du bureau de l'état civil du district britannique où il est survenu avant de pouvoir être transcrit à l'état civil français [1][6] :

  • Enregistrement civil au Royaume-Uni (Register Office) : Dès que le Register Office confirme la réception du MCCD ou de la notification du Coroner, déclarez le décès dans un délai de 5 jours en Angleterre, au Pays de Galles et en Irlande du Nord, ou dans un délai de 8 jours auprès de tout bureau d'enregistrement (Registration Office) en Écosse (tel que l'Edinburgh City Chambers ou le Glasgow Registration Office) [1]. Demandez plusieurs copies intégrales certifiées conformes de l'acte de décès britannique (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), les banques, assureurs et autorités consulaires françaises exigeant des exemplaires originaux [1][6].
  • Transcription consulaire française par rapport à une déclaration en France : Contrairement à un décès survenu en France métropolitaine - qui doit être déclaré à la mairie du lieu de décès dans les 24 heures hors week-ends et jours fériés pour obtenir l'acte de décès intégral ou un extrait plurilingue Formule C de la Convention de Vienne de 1976 [7] - un décès survenu au Royaume-Uni est d'abord enregistré localement puis transmis au Consulat général de France à Londres en vue de la transcription de l'acte de décès [6]. La demande s'effectue par voie postale au moyen du formulaire de demande de transcription accompagné d'une copie originale de l'acte de décès britannique (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), d'un justificatif de la nationalité française de la personne décédée (passeport, carte nationale d'identité ou acte de naissance français) et du livret de famille [6].
  • Apostille britannique (le cas échéant) : Bien que le Consulat général de France à Londres accepte directement les originaux d'actes de décès britanniques pour la transcription consulaire [6], les notaires ou établissements financiers français intervenant dans le règlement de la succession avant la transcription peuvent demander l'apposition de l'Apostille de La Haye par le Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (téléphone : +44 3700 00 22 44) [3].

steps.title: Coordonner le Rapatriement International vers la France ou l'Inhumation/Crémation Locale au Royaume-Uni
steps.html:
Les opérateurs funéraires britannique et français que vous avez mandatés prennent en charge les autorisations sanitaires, médico-légales et frontalières selon que vous optez pour le rapatriement du corps, le transfert des cendres après crémation ou des obsèques locales au Royaume-Uni [1][6] :

  • Rapatriement du corps vers la France : En Angleterre et au Pays de Galles, l'opérateur funéraire britannique saisit le Coroner local afin d'obtenir l'Out-of-England Order (Form 104), qui autorise la sortie du corps hors d'Angleterre et du Pays de Galles [1][6]. En Écosse, l'autorisation de sortie du territoire écossais est délivrée par le Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) de Healthcare Improvement Scotland ou par le Procurator Fiscal [1]. Pour l'entrée en France conformément aux accords internationaux de transfert des corps (Arrangement de Berlin de 1937 et Accord de Strasbourg de 1973), l'opérateur britannique organise les soins de conservation (thanatopraxie) lorsque requis, réunit le certificat médical de non-contagion et procède à la mise en bière en cercueil hermétique muni d'une enveloppe métallique zinguée, puis sollicite le laissez-passer mortuaire consulaire auprès du Consulat général de France à Londres (ou l'arrêté préfectoral en France) avant le transport aérien ou via le tunnel sous la Manche vers la commune française de destination (par exemple Paris, Lyon ou Marseille) [6][7].
  • Rapatriement des cendres après crémation : Si la crémation a lieu au Royaume-Uni, le crématorium délivre un certificat officiel de crémation (Certificate of Cremation) [6]. L'urne scellée contenant les cendres peut être transportée vers la France accompagnée de l'acte de décès britannique, du certificat de crémation et de l'autorisation consulaire ou municipale ; en droit français, les cendres peuvent être déposées dans un columbarium, scellées sur un monument funéraire ou dispersées dans un espace aménagé après déclaration à la mairie du lieu de destination (la conservation définitive de l'urne dans une propriété privée n'est pas autorisée en France) [6][7].
  • Inhumation ou crémation locale au Royaume-Uni : Si les obsèques se déroulent au Royaume-Uni, le Register Office (ou le Coroner / Procurator Fiscal) délivre directement à l'opérateur funéraire britannique le certificat d'inhumation ou de crémation (Certificate for Burial or Cremation, appelé « Green Form » en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles, ou Form 14 en Écosse) [1].

steps.title: Accomplir les Notifications Administratives, Demandes de Pensions de Réversion, Déclarations Fiscales et Formalités de Succession dans les Deux Pays
steps.html:
Une fois les obsèques ou le rapatriement engagés, les démarches administratives et successorales concernent fréquemment les deux juridictions [2][4][7] :

  • Notifications, pensions et homologation successorale (Probate) au Royaume-Uni :
    • Si la personne décédée résidait en Angleterre, en Écosse ou au Pays de Galles, l'officier de l'état civil remet un numéro de référence unique permettant d'utiliser le service gouvernemental Tell Us Once, qui informe en une seule démarche HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), HM Passport Office, les services municipaux et les caisses de retraite publiques [2]. Vous pouvez également contacter le Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (téléphone : 0800 151 2012) pour déclarer le décès et vérifier l'éligibilité au Bereavement Support Payment ou au Funeral Expenses Payment [2].
    • Si la personne décédée résidait en France mais percevait une pension de retraite publique britannique (UK State Pension), notifiez directement l'International Pension Centre (téléphone : +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • Si le défunt détenait des biens immobiliers, des comptes bancaires ou des placements au Royaume-Uni dépassant les seuils fixés par les établissements financiers, l'exécuteur testamentaire ou l'ayant droit habilité doit demander un Grant of Probate (ou des Letters of Administration en l'absence de testament) auprès de HM Courts & Tribunals Service en Angleterre et au Pays de Galles, ou une Confirmation auprès du Sheriff Court en Écosse, après avoir déposé les formulaires de droits de succession (Inheritance Tax) requis auprès de HMRC [4].
  • Sécurité sociale française, pensions de réversion, fiscalité et règlement de la succession en France :
    • Capital décès de la Sécurité sociale : Si la personne décédée exerçait une activité salariée ou relevait du régime général français de la Sécurité sociale peu avant son décès, les ayants droit prioritaires peuvent demander le versement du capital décès auprès de la Caisse Primaire d'Assurance Maladie (CPAM via Ameli.fr) dans un délai de 2 ans à compter de la date du décès [7][8].
    • Pensions de réversion : Le conjoint survivant ou l'ex-conjoint éligible peut déposer une demande de pension de réversion au titre du régime de base auprès de L'Assurance Retraite (téléphone depuis l'étranger : +33 9 71 10 39 60) et au titre de la retraite complémentaire des salariés auprès de l'Agirc-Arrco (via le portail unique info-retraite.fr ou lassuranceretraite.fr) [7][9].
    • Notaire français et déclaration de succession : Si la personne décédée était domiciliée en France, possédait des biens immobiliers en France ou laissait un actif successoral imposable en France supérieur au seuil légal, mandatez un notaire via les Notaires de France (Conseil supérieur du notariat) ou la Chambre des Notaires de Paris [7][11]. Le notaire interroge le Fichier central des dispositions de dernières volontés (FCDDV), établit l'acte de notoriété et prépare la déclaration de succession destinée à la Direction générale des Finances publiques (impôts) [7][11]. Lorsque le décès survient hors de France métropolitaine (y compris au Royaume-Uni), le délai légal pour déposer la déclaration de succession auprès de l'administration fiscale française est de 12 mois à compter de la date du décès (contre 6 mois lorsque le décès survient en France métropolitaine) [7][11].

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Spain Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Spain dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Spain and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Spanish citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate steps depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to Spain or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6][7].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral or repatriation arrangements in the United Kingdom begin once the medical cause of death is certified and cleared by the appropriate medical or forensic authority [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner review): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. Once approved, the Medical Examiner's office discusses the cause of death with the next of kin and sends the MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), unlocking the 5-day civil registration window [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, an attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), subject to potential review by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1]. In Northern Ireland, the attending doctor issues the MCCD for registration at the local district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred suddenly outside a hospital, call 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so police and emergency medical services can attend [1]. Unexplained, accidental, or unnatural deaths are referred to the Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scotland), who authorises any required post-mortem examination and issues clearance for burial, cremation, or international transfer once forensic inquiries conclude [1].

steps.title: Check Decesos or Travel Insurance, Appoint Funeral Directors in the United Kingdom and Spain, and Contact the Spanish Consulate
steps.html:
Before entering into an independent funeral contract, check whether your family member held a Spanish funeral and repatriation insurance policy (seguro de decesos), travel insurance, or bank-card assistance coverage [7]. Spanish seguro de decesos policies commonly include a 24-hour international assistance unit that appoints and pays both the UK and Spanish funeral providers directly [7].

If no insurance policy covers the transfer, the family should appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom coordinated with an authorised receiving funeral company in Spain [7][10][11]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can find an accredited UK funeral provider experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Receiving funeral provider in Spain: For reception, airport clearance, and cemetery or crematorium services in Spain (such as in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Seville, or Bilbao), you can locate a licensed Spanish funeral company (empresa funeraria habilitada) via the Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (phone: +34 91 576 31 55; email: info@panasef.com) [10]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Spanish consular assistance: Notify the Consulado General de España en Londres (phone: +44 20 7589 8989; consular emergency phone: +44 7712 764 151; email: cog.londres@maec.es; Civil Registry email: cog.londres.rgc@maec.es), or the Spanish Consulates General in Manchester or Edinburgh depending on the UK region where the death occurred, operating under the Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación (MAEC) [6][7]. The Consulate guides families on consular civil registration and mortuary transit rules, although Spanish state authorities cannot pay funeral or repatriation expenses [7].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Complete Spanish Consular Registration and Legalisation
steps.html:
A death occurring in the United Kingdom must first be registered with the local UK civil registry before being recorded in the Spanish civil registry [1][6]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Register the death at the local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (once notified by the Medical Examiner or Coroner) or within 8 days at a Registration Office in Scotland [1]. Obtain multiple original certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), as original certificates are required for consular registration, legalisation, and estate administration [1][6].
  • Spanish Consular Civil Registry vs. Domestic Spanish Registration: Whereas a death occurring inside Spain is registered within 24 hours at the municipal Registro Civil under the Ministerio de Justicia to obtain the Certificado Literal de Defunción and the multilingual CIEC Form C extract (1976 Vienna Convention) [8], a death of a Spanish citizen in the United Kingdom must be registered at the Consular Civil Registry (Registro Civil Consular) of the Consulado General de España en Londres (or Manchester/Edinburgh) [6]. Submitting the signed declaration sheet, the original UK Death Certificate, the deceased's Spanish DNI or passport, and a Spanish literal birth certificate allows the Consulate to issue the official Spanish Certificado Literal de Defunción and report the death to the Central Civil Registry in Spain [6].
  • UK Apostille (when presenting UK documents directly in Spain): If you need to present the UK Death Certificate or UK probate documents directly to a Spanish notary, bank, or court before Spanish consular registration is completed, obtain a Hague Apostille from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) alongside a sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada) [3][7].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to Spain or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and Spanish funeral directors coordinate the health, forensic, and border permits according to whether you choose repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][7]:

  • Repatriation of the body to Spain: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director notifies the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104) authorising removal of the body from England and Wales [1]. In Scotland, clearance to remove remains outside Scotland is issued through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. For transfer to Spain under international mortuary transit agreements (the Strasbourg Agreement of 1973 and Berlin Agreement of 1937) and Spanish Sanidad Exterior regulations, the UK funeral director completes preservation/embalming, provides a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious diseases, seals the remains in a zinc-lined hermetic coffin (féretro de zinc sellado), and coordinates with the Consulado General de España en Londres and Spanish external border health authorities (Sanidad Exterior) for the mortuary transit permit (salvoconducto mortuorio) [7].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the crematorium issues an official Certificate of Cremation [7]. Cremated ashes can be transported to Spain in a sealed urn accompanied by the UK Death Certificate and the Certificate of Cremation (subject to airline cabin-baggage rules and local Spanish municipal cemetery rules) [7].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Benefits, Wills Registry Checks, and Probate in Spain and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once funeral or repatriation arrangements are in place, administrative and succession procedures typically involve authorities in both countries [2][4][8][9]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased resided in England, Scotland, or Wales, use the Tell Us Once reference provided by the registrar or call the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to notify HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), council services, and state benefit offices, and to check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • If the deceased resided in Spain and received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • If the deceased held UK real estate, bank accounts, or investments requiring formal administration, apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland [4].
  • Spanish social security, Last Wills Registry, notary, and inheritance tax:
    • Death grant and survivor pensions (INSS): If the deceased contributed to or received a pension from the Spanish social security system, eligible beneficiaries can apply to the Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (phone: +34 91 542 11 76) for the funeral expense grant (auxilio por defunción) and survivor benefits (prestaciones de muerte y supervivencia, including pensión de viudedad, pensión de orfandad, or prestaciones en favor de familiares) via the Seguridad Social electronic portal [9].
    • Spanish Registry of Last Wills and Life Insurance (Últimas Voluntades): Once 15 working days (15 días hábiles) have elapsed since the date of death, apply to the Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad of the Ministerio de Justicia (phone: +34 91 837 22 95) using Modelo 790 (code 006) and the death certificate to obtain the Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad (confirming whether the deceased executed a Spanish will before a notary) and the Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [8].
    • Notarial inheritance deed and 6-month tax deadline: If the deceased left assets or habitual residence in Spain, a Spanish notary (Consejo General del Notariado) prepares the deed of acceptance and partition of inheritance (escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia) or declaration of heirs (declaración de herederos abintestato) [8]. Spanish Inheritance Tax (Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones) must be filed within 6 months from the date of death (before the AEAT for non-residents via the Oficina Nacional de Gestión Tributaria, or the competent Autonomous Community tax agency), with the option to request a 6-month extension within the first 5 months [8].

es.title: Qué hacer ante un fallecimiento entre Reino Unido y España: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras un fallecimiento entre Reino Unido y España: certificado médico de defunción, funeraria autorizada, inscripción en el Registro Civil, trámites consulares y repatriación o entierro local, y pensiones de supervivencia y sucesión.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su familiar. Cuando una persona con nacionalidad española o vínculos de residencia en España fallece en el Reino Unido, los pasos inmediatos dependen de la nación constitutiva del Reino Unido donde se haya producido el fallecimiento (Inglaterra y Gales, Escocia o Irlanda del Norte) y de si la familia opta por la repatriación internacional a España o por un funeral local en el Reino Unido [1][6][7].

steps.title: Obtener la Certificación Médica de Defunción y la Autorización del Coroner o Procurator Fiscal en el Reino Unido
steps.html:
La inscripción en el registro civil y las gestiones funerarias o de repatriación en el Reino Unido comienzan una vez que la causa médica de la muerte es certificada y autorizada por la autoridad médica o forense competente [1]:

  • Fallecimientos por causas naturales en Inglaterra y Gales (revisión del Medical Examiner): El médico que atendió al paciente cumplimenta el Certificado Médico de Causa de Defunción (Medical Certificate of Cause of Death - MCCD), el cual es revisado de forma independiente y refrendado por un médico examinador del NHS (NHS Medical Examiner) [1]. Una vez aprobado, la oficina del Medical Examiner se pone en contacto con los familiares para explicar la causa del fallecimiento y remite el MCCD electrónicamente al registro civil local (Register Office, como el Westminster Register Office en Londres o el Manchester Register Office), iniciándose así el plazo legal de 5 días para la inscripción civil [1].
  • Fallecimientos por causas naturales en Escocia e Irlanda del Norte: En Escocia, el médico emite el Certificado Médico de Causa de Defunción (Form 11), sujeto a una posible revisión por el Servicio de Revisión de Certificación de Defunciones (Death Certification Review Service - DCRS) de Healthcare Improvement Scotland [1]. En Irlanda del Norte, el médico expide el MCCD para su inscripción en la oficina de registro del distrito correspondiente (district Registration Office) [1].
  • Fallecimientos repentinos, accidentales o inexplicados: Si el fallecimiento se produjo de forma repentina fuera de un hospital, llame al 999 (o al NHS 111 cuando proceda) para que acudan la policía y los servicios médicos de urgencia [1]. Las muertes inexplicadas, accidentales o no naturales se remiten al juez de instrucción (Coroner en Inglaterra, Gales e Irlanda del Norte) o al fiscal (Procurator Fiscal, del Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service en Escocia), quien autoriza cualquier examen post-mortem necesario y expide la autorización para la inhumación, cremación o traslado internacional una vez concluidas las diligencias forenses [1].

steps.title: Verificar el Seguro de Decesos o de Viaje, Designar Funerarias en el Reino Unido y España, y Contactar con el Consulado de España
steps.html:
Antes de contratar un servicio funerario por cuenta propia, compruebe si su familiar disponía de una póliza española de seguro de decesos, un seguro de viaje o cobertura de asistencia vinculada a una tarjeta bancaria [7]. Las pólizas españolas de seguro de decesos suelen contar con un servicio de asistencia internacional 24 horas que designa y abona directamente tanto a la funeraria británica como a la española [7].

Si no existe ninguna póliza de seguro que cubra el traslado, la familia debe designar una empresa funeraria autorizada en el Reino Unido coordinada con una empresa funeraria receptora habilitada en España [7][10][11]:

  • Director funerario en el Reino Unido: Puede localizar una funeraria británica acreditada y con experiencia en repatriación internacional a través de la National Association of Funeral Directors (teléfono: +44 121 711 1343; correo electrónico: info@nafd.org.uk) o de la National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Empresa funeraria receptora en España: Para la recepción, el despacho aeroportuario y los servicios de cementerio o crematorio en España (por ejemplo, en Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Sevilla o Bilbao), puede localizar una empresa funeraria habilitada a través de la Asociación Nacional de Servicios Funerarios (teléfono: +34 91 576 31 55; correo electrónico: info@panasef.com) [10]. Facilitamos esta información de directorios únicamente a efectos orientativos y no respaldamos, recomendamos ni clasificamos a proveedores concretos.
  • Asistencia consular española: Notifique el fallecimiento al Consulado General de España en Londres (teléfono: +44 20 7589 8989; teléfono de emergencia consular: +44 7712 764 151; correo electrónico: cog.londres@maec.es; correo del Registro Civil: cog.londres.rgc@maec.es), o a los Consulados Generales de España en Mánchester o Edimburgo según la demarcación británica donde haya ocurrido el fallecimiento, dependientes del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Unión Europea y Cooperación (MAEC) [6][7]. El Consulado orienta a las familias sobre la inscripción en el Registro Civil Consular y la normativa de tránsito mortuorio, si bien las autoridades estatales españolas no pueden sufragar gastos funerarios ni de repatriación [7].

steps.title: Inscribir el Fallecimiento en el Reino Unido y Completar el Registro Consular Español y la Legalización
steps.html:
Un fallecimiento ocurrido en el Reino Unido debe inscribirse primero en el registro civil local británico antes de su inscripción en el Registro Civil español [1][6]:

  • Registro civil en el Reino Unido (Register Office): Inscriba la defunción en el Register Office local en el plazo de 5 días en Inglaterra, Gales e Irlanda del Norte (una vez recibida la notificación del Medical Examiner o del Coroner) o en el plazo de 8 días en una oficina de registro (Registration Office) en Escocia [1]. Solicite varias copias certificadas originales del certificado de defunción británico (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death), ya que se exigen ejemplares originales para la inscripción consular, la apostilla y la tramitación de la herencia [1][6].
  • Registro Civil Consular español frente a la inscripción en territorio español: Mientras que un fallecimiento ocurrido en España se inscribe en un plazo de 24 horas ante el Registro Civil municipal dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia para obtener el Certificado Literal de Defunción y el extracto plurilingüe Fórmula C de la CIEC (Convenio de Viena de 1976) [8], el fallecimiento de un ciudadano español en el Reino Unido debe inscribirse en el Registro Civil Consular del Consulado General de España en Londres (o Mánchester/Edimburgo) [6]. Presentando la hoja declaratoria firmada, el certificado original de defunción británico, el DNI o pasaporte español de la persona fallecida y su certificado literal de nacimiento español, el Consulado expide el Certificado Literal de Defunción español oficial y remite el duplicado al Registro Civil Central en España [6].
  • Apostilla del Reino Unido (cuando se presenten documentos británicos directamente en España): Si necesita presentar el certificado de defunción británico o documentos sucesorios británicos (Grant of Probate) directamente ante una notaría, entidad bancaria o juzgado en España antes de que concluya la inscripción consular española, obtenga la Apostilla de La Haya a través de la Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (teléfono: +44 3700 00 22 44) acompañada de una traducción jurada al español [3][7].

steps.title: Coordinar la Repatriación Internacional a España o la Inhumación/Cremación Local en el Reino Unido
steps.html:
Las empresas funerarias designadas en el Reino Unido y en España coordinan los permisos sanitarios, forenses y fronterizos según opten por la repatriación del cuerpo, el traslado de las cenizas o un funeral local en el Reino Unido [1][7]:

  • Repatriación del cuerpo a España: En Inglaterra y Gales, la funeraria británica notifica al Coroner local para obtener la orden de salida del territorio (Out-of-England Order / Form 104) que autoriza el traslado del cuerpo fuera de Inglaterra y Gales [1]. En Escocia, la autorización para trasladar restos mortales fuera de Escocia se tramita a través del Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) de Healthcare Improvement Scotland o del Procurator Fiscal [1]. Para el traslado a España conforme a los acuerdos internacionales de traslado de cadáveres (Acuerdo de Estrasburgo de 1973 y Convenio de Berlín de 1937) y la normativa española de Sanidad Exterior, la funeraria británica realiza las prácticas de conservación o embalsamamiento, aporta el certificado médico que acredita la ausencia de enfermedades infectocontagiosas, introduce el cuerpo en un féretro hermético con caja interior de zinc sellada (féretro de zinc sellado) y gestiona con el Consulado General de España en Londres y las autoridades españolas de Sanidad Exterior la autorización y el salvoconducto mortuorio [7].
  • Repatriación de cenizas tras la cremación: Si la cremación tiene lugar en el Reino Unido, el crematorio emite un certificado oficial de cremación (Certificate of Cremation) [7]. Las cenizas pueden trasladarse a España en una urna sellada acompañada del certificado de defunción británico y del certificado de cremación (con sujeción a las normas de transporte aéreo y a las ordenanzas municipales del cementerio o columbario de destino en España) [7].
  • Inhumación o cremación local en el Reino Unido: Si el funeral se celebra en el Reino Unido, el Register Office (o el Coroner / Procurator Fiscal) entrega directamente a la funeraria británica el certificado de inhumación o cremación (Certificate for Burial or Cremation) [1].

steps.title: Completar las Notificaciones Posteriores, Prestaciones de Supervivencia, Registro de Últimas Voluntades y Sucesión en España y el Reino Unido
steps.html:
Una vez organizadas las exequias o la repatriación, los trámites administrativos y sucesorios suelen involucrar a organismos de ambos países [2][4][8][9]:

  • Notificaciones, pensiones y sucesión (Probate) en el Reino Unido:
    • Si la persona fallecida residía en Inglaterra, Escocia o Gales, utilice el código de referencia del servicio Tell Us Once facilitado por el registro civil o llame al Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (teléfono: 0800 151 2012) para notificar el fallecimiento a HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), a los servicios municipales y a las oficinas de prestaciones públicas, así como para consultar el derecho al Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • Si la persona fallecida residía en España y percibía una pensión estatal británica (UK State Pension), notifíquelo al International Pension Centre (teléfono: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • Si el causante dejó bienes inmuebles, cuentas bancarias o inversiones en el Reino Unido que requieran administración formal, solicite ante HM Courts & Tribunals Service un Grant of Probate (o Letters of Administration si no existe testamento válido) en Inglaterra y Gales, o una Confirmation ante el Sheriff Court en Escocia [4].
  • Seguridad Social española, Registro de Últimas Voluntades, notaría e Impuesto sobre Sucesiones:
    • Auxilio por defunción y pensiones de supervivencia (INSS): Si la persona fallecida cotizaba o percibía una pensión del sistema español de Seguridad Social, los beneficiarios con derecho pueden solicitar ante el Instituto Nacional de la Seguridad Social (teléfono: +34 91 542 11 76) el auxilio por defunción y las prestaciones de muerte y supervivencia (pensión de viudedad, pensión de orfandad o prestaciones en favor de familiares) a través de la Sede Electrónica de la Seguridad Social [9].
    • Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad y Seguros de Vida: Una vez transcurridos 15 días hábiles desde la fecha del fallecimiento, solicite al Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad del Ministerio de Justicia (teléfono: +34 91 837 22 95), mediante el Modelo 790 (código 006) y el certificado de defunción, el Certificado de Actos de Última Voluntad (que acredita si el fallecido otorgó testamento ante notario en España) y el Certificado de Contratos de Seguros de Cobertura de Fallecimiento [8].
    • Escritura notarial de herencia y plazo fiscal de 6 meses: Si el causante dejó bienes o tenía su residencia habitual en España, un notario español (Consejo General del Notariado) autoriza la escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia o el acta de declaración de herederos abintestato [8]. El Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones debe autoliquidarse o presentarse en el plazo de 6 meses desde la fecha del fallecimiento (ante la Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria - Oficina Nacional de Gestión Tributaria para no residentes, o ante la administración tributaria de la Comunidad Autónoma competente), pudiendo solicitarse una prórroga de otros 6 meses dentro de los 5 primeros meses del plazo [8].

es.closingQuestion: Para poder ofrecerle indicaciones más específicas para su caso, ¿en qué nación constitutiva y municipio del Reino Unido se produjo el fallecimiento, y tienen previsto organizar la repatriación a una Comunidad Autónoma concreta en España o celebrar el funeral localmente en el Reino Unido?

title: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When a Citizen of Italy Dies in United Kingdom: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement guide when a citizen or resident of Italy dies in United Kingdom: medical certification and police/coroner clearance in United Kingdom, licensed funeral providers in both countries, civil death registration and legalization, international repatriation vs. local burial/cremation, and survivor pension & probate steps in Italy and United Kingdom.
introHtml: We are very sorry for the loss of your family member. When a person with Italian citizenship or residence ties dies in the United Kingdom, the immediate administrative steps depend on the UK constituent nation where the death occurred (England and Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland) and whether the family chooses international repatriation to Italy or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6][7].

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner or Procurator Fiscal Clearance in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Civil registration and funeral or repatriation arrangements in the United Kingdom require official medical certification or forensic clearance of the cause of death [1]:

  • Natural deaths in England and Wales (Medical Examiner system): An attending doctor completes the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), which is independently reviewed and countersigned by an NHS Medical Examiner [1]. Once approved, the Medical Examiner's office contacts the next of kin to explain the cause of death and transmits the MCCD electronically to the local Register Office (such as Westminster Register Office in London or Manchester Register Office), starting the 5-day civil registration window [1].
  • Natural deaths in Scotland and Northern Ireland: In Scotland, the attending doctor issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 11), which may be reviewed by Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) [1]. In Northern Ireland, the doctor issues the MCCD for registration at the local district Registration Office [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly outside a hospital, call emergency services on 999 (or NHS 111 where appropriate) so police and medical personnel can attend [1]. Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths are referred to the local Coroner (in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland) or to the Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scotland), who conducts any required post-mortem examination or inquest and issues clearance for burial, cremation, or international transfer [1].

steps.title: Check Insurance Coverage, Appoint Funeral Directors in the United Kingdom and Italy, and Contact the Italian Consulate
steps.html:
Before signing an independent funeral contract, check whether the deceased held travel insurance, bank-card assistance coverage, or private repatriation insurance [6]. If a policy applies, contact the insurer's 24-hour assistance centre immediately so it can appoint and fund the international funeral providers directly.

If no insurance policy applies, the family can appoint a licensed funeral director in the United Kingdom coordinated with an authorised receiving funeral company in Italy [6][11]:

  • Funeral director in the United Kingdom: You can locate an accredited UK funeral director experienced in international repatriation through the National Association of Funeral Directors (phone: +44 121 711 1343; email: info@nafd.org.uk) or the National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Receiving funeral company in Italy: For airport clearance, municipal transport, and burial or entombment in Italy (for example in Rome, Milan, Naples, or Turin), coordinate with a licensed Italian funeral operator (impresa funebre autorizzata), such as a member of the national sector federations FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri) or Federcofit [6]. Clarvia provides directory information for orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank specific providers.
  • Italian consular assistance: Notify the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (phone: +44 20 7936 5900; Welfare and Repatriation Office email: sociale.londra@esteri.it), or the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Edimburgo (for Scotland and Northern Ireland) or Consolato d'Italia a Manchester, operating under the Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI) [6][7]. Consular staff process the Italian death transcription and coordinate with the destination Italian municipality (Comune) to issue the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario), though Italian authorities do not pay funeral or repatriation expenses unless specific statutory indigence rules apply [6].

steps.title: Register the Death in the United Kingdom and Complete Italian Consular Transcription and Legalisation
steps.html:
The death must first be registered with the civil registry in the UK district where the death occurred before it can be transcribed into the Italian civil registry [1][7]:

  • UK Civil Registration (Register Office): Register the death at the local Register Office within 5 days in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (once notified by the Medical Examiner or Coroner) or within 8 days at a Registration Office in Scotland [1]. Obtain multiple original certified copies of the UK Death Certificate (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death) [1][7].
  • UK Apostille and Italian Translation: For an Italian citizen who died in the United Kingdom, the original UK Death Certificate must be legalised with a paper Hague Apostille issued directly by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (phone: +44 3700 00 22 44) - apostilles issued by a Notary Public or solicitor are not accepted for civil registry transcription - and accompanied by a typed translation into Italian [3][7].
  • Italian Consular Transcription vs. Domestic Registration: Whereas a death occurring inside Italy is declared within 24 hours at the Ufficio di Stato Civile of the Italian Comune of death to issue the atto di morte, burial permit (permesso di seppellimento), and multilingual CIEC Form C extract under the 1976 Vienna Convention, a death in the United Kingdom is transcribed into the Italian Comune of AIRE registration or last residence by posting the application (Modulo N.5, original apostilled UK Death Certificate, Italian translation, copy of the deceased's passport, and prepaid Special Delivery return envelope) to the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (Ufficio Stato Civile, 83/86 Farringdon Street, London EC4A 4BL) [7].

steps.title: Coordinate International Repatriation to Italy (Passaporto Mortuario) or Local Burial/Cremation in the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Your appointed UK and Italian funeral directors handle the technical permits depending on whether you choose repatriation of the body, transport of cremated ashes, or a local funeral in the United Kingdom [1][6]:

  • Repatriation of the body to Italy: In England and Wales, the UK funeral director notifies the local Coroner to obtain the Out-of-England Order (Form 104) authorising removal of the remains outside England and Wales [1][6]. In Scotland, clearance to remove human remains outside Scotland is obtained through Healthcare Improvement Scotland's Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) or the Procurator Fiscal [1]. Under the 1937 Berlin Convention and Italian mortuary police rules, the UK funeral director submits the repatriation dossier by email to the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (sociale.londra@esteri.it), specifying the receiving Italian Comune, the exact cemetery and grave/niche details, and the entry border/airport in Italy, together with: (1) the original UK Death Certificate legalised with an FCDO Apostille, (2) the Embalming Certificate (certificato di imbalsamazione), (3) the medical certificate confirming the absence of infectious or contagious diseases (corresponding to local health authority / ASL sanitary certification), (4) the Coroner's Out-of-England certificate, and (5) the funeral director's declaration confirming a double coffin with a hermetically soldered zinc/metal inner casket (doppia cassa con cofano metallico saldato) [6]. The Consulate requests entry authorisation (nulla osta) from the Italian Comune and, once granted, issues the Mortuary Passport (Passaporto Mortuario) and seals the coffin for transport [6].
  • Repatriation of cremated ashes: If cremation takes place in the United Kingdom, the funeral director or family submits the apostilled UK Death Certificate, the official Certificate of Cremation, and destination cemetery/Comune details to the Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra to obtain the consular mortuary permit for transporting the sealed urn to Italy [6].
  • Local burial or cremation in the United Kingdom: If the funeral takes place in the United Kingdom, the Register Office (or Coroner/Procurator Fiscal) issues the Certificate for Burial or Cremation directly to the UK funeral director [1].

steps.title: Complete Post-Death Notifications, Survivor Pensions, Tax Filings, and Estate Administration in Italy and the United Kingdom
steps.html:
Once funeral or repatriation arrangements are underway, estate and pension formalities frequently apply in both jurisdictions [2][4][8][9][10]:

  • United Kingdom notifications, pensions, and probate:
    • If the deceased lived in England, Scotland, or Wales, use the Tell Us Once reference provided by the registrar or contact the Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (phone: 0800 151 2012) to report the death across HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), passport, and council records and to check eligibility for Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • If the deceased resided in Italy and received a UK State Pension, notify the International Pension Centre (phone: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • If the deceased held UK real estate, bank accounts, or investments requiring formal authority, apply to HM Courts & Tribunals Service for a Grant of Probate (or Letters of Administration) in England and Wales, or to the Sheriff Court for Confirmation in Scotland [4].
  • Italian survivor pensions, inheritance tax, and wills check:
    • Survivor pensions (pensione ai superstiti - INPS): Eligible surviving family members (such as a surviving married/civil partner or eligible dependent children) can apply to the Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (phone from Italy: 803 164; from abroad or mobile: +39 06 164 164) for the pensione di reversibilità (if the deceased was already a pensioner) or pensione indiretta (if the deceased was an insured worker), as well as any accrued unpaid pension instalments (ratei maturati e non riscossi), online via SPID/CIE or through a Patronato office [8].
    • Italian inheritance tax declaration (dichiarazione di successione within 12 months): Heirs and legatees must file the dichiarazione di successione telematically with the Agenzia delle Entrate (phone from Italy: 800 90 96 96; from abroad: +39 06 97617689) within 12 months from the date of death (unless the estate devolves solely to the surviving partner and straight-line relatives, has a gross value not exceeding EUR 100,000, and includes no real estate or real property rights) [9].
    • Italian wills search and notarial procedures: To verify whether the deceased left a formal or deposited will in Italy, you can request a search of the General Registry of Wills (Registro Generale dei Testamenti, managed by the Ufficio Centrale degli Archivi Notarili of the Ministero della Giustizia) or the voluntary holographic wills registry via the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, and instruct an Italian notary to publish any Italian will and update cadastral land records (voltura catastale) [10].

closingQuestion: To help tailor this guidance, in which UK constituent nation and municipality did the death occur, and are you planning international repatriation to a specific Italian Comune or a local funeral in the United Kingdom?

it.title: Cosa fare in caso di decesso tra Regno Unito e Italia: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso tra Regno Unito e Italia: certificato medico di morte, impresa funebre autorizzata, registrazione allo Stato Civile, pratiche consolari e rimpatrio della salma o delle ceneri, e pensione di reversibilità e successione.
it.introHtml: Esprimiamo le nostre più sentite condoglianze per la perdita del vostro familiare. Quando una persona con cittadinanza italiana o legami di residenza con l'Italia decede nel Regno Unito, gli adempimenti immediati dipendono dalla nazione costitutiva del Regno Unito in cui è avvenuto il decesso (Inghilterra e Galles, Scozia o Irlanda del Nord) e dalla scelta della famiglia tra il rimpatrio internazionale in Italia e lo svolgimento delle esequie localmente nel Regno Unito [1][6][7].

steps.title: Ottenere la Certificazione Medica di Morte e il Nulla Osta del Coroner o del Procurator Fiscal nel Regno Unito
steps.html:
La registrazione dello stato civile e l'organizzazione del funerale o del rimpatrio nel Regno Unito richiedono la certificazione medica ufficiale o il nulla osta medico-legale sulla causa del decesso [1]:

  • Decessi per cause naturali in Inghilterra e Galles (sistema del Medical Examiner): Il medico curante compila il certificato medico di causa di morte (Medical Certificate of Cause of Death - MCCD), che viene esaminato in modo indipendente e controfirmato da un medico esaminatore del servizio sanitario pubblico (NHS Medical Examiner) [1]. Una volta approvato, l'ufficio del Medical Examiner contatta i familiari per illustrare la causa del decesso e trasmette telematicamente il MCCD all'ufficio locale dello stato civile (Register Office, ad esempio il Westminster Register Office a Londra o il Manchester Register Office), facendo decorrere il termine di 5 giorni per la registrazione civile [1].
  • Decessi per cause naturali in Scozia e Irlanda del Nord: In Scozia, il medico curante rilascia il certificato medico di causa di morte (Form 11), che può essere sottoposto a verifica da parte del servizio di revisione della certificazione dei decessi (Death Certification Review Service - DCRS) di Healthcare Improvement Scotland [1]. In Irlanda del Nord, il medico rilascia il MCCD ai fini della registrazione presso l'ufficio di stato civile distrettuale (district Registration Office) [1].
  • Decessi improvvisi, accidentali o per cause non chiare: Se il decesso è avvenuto inaspettatamente al di fuori di una struttura ospedaliera, contattate i servizi di emergenza al 999 (o il servizio NHS 111 ove appropriato) affinché intervengano la polizia e il personale sanitario [1]. I decessi improvvisi, accidentali o non spiegati vengono deferiti al Coroner competente (in Inghilterra, Galles e Irlanda del Nord) o al Procurator Fiscal (Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service in Scozia), il quale dispone eventuali esami autoptici (post-mortem examination) o indagini (inquest) e rilascia il nulla osta per la sepoltura, la cremazione o il trasferimento internazionale [1].

steps.title: Verificare la Copertura Assicurativa, Incaricare le Imprese Funebri nel Regno Unito e in Italia e Contattare il Consolato d'Italia
steps.html:
Prima di sottoscrivere autonomamente un contratto di onoranze funebri, verificate se la persona deceduta disponeva di un'assicurazione di viaggio, di una copertura associata a carta bancaria o di una polizza privata per il rimpatrio sanitario e funebre [6]. Se è attiva una copertura, contattate immediatamente la centrale operativa 24 ore su 24 della compagnia assicurativa, affinché possa incaricare e sostenere direttamente i costi degli operatori funebri internazionali.

In assenza di copertura assicurativa, la famiglia può incaricare un'impresa funebre autorizzata nel Regno Unito coordinata con un'impresa funebre autorizzata ricevente in Italia [6][11]:

  • Impresa funebre nel Regno Unito: È possibile individuare un direttore funebre britannico accreditato ed esperto in rimpatri internazionali tramite la National Association of Funeral Directors (telefono: +44 121 711 1343; e-mail: info@nafd.org.uk) o la National Society of Allied and Independent Funeral Directors (SAIF) [11].
  • Impresa funebre ricevente in Italia: Per lo sdoganamento aeroportuale, il trasporto comunale e la tumulazione, inumazione o cremazione in Italia (ad esempio a Roma, Milano, Napoli o Torino), occorre coordinarsi con un'impresa funebre autorizzata, quale un operatore aderente alle federazioni nazionali di categoria FENIOF (Federazione Nazionale Imprese Onoranze Funebri) o Federcofit [6]. Forniamo i riferimenti di tali elenchi esclusivamente a scopo orientativo e non raccomandiamo, avalliamo né classifichiamo singoli operatori.
  • Assistenza consolare italiana: Informate il Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (telefono: +44 20 7936 5900; e-mail dell'Ufficio Assistenza Sociale e Rimpatri: sociale.londra@esteri.it), oppure il Consolato Generale d'Italia a Edimburgo (per la Scozia e l'Irlanda del Nord) o il Consolato d'Italia a Manchester, operanti sotto il Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI) [6][7]. Gli uffici consolari curano la trascrizione dell'atto di morte in Italia e si coordinano con il Comune italiano di destinazione per il rilascio del Passaporto Mortuario, fermo restando che le autorità italiane non sostengono le spese funebri o di rimpatrio salvo specifici casi di indigenza previsti dalla legge [6].

steps.title: Registrare il Decesso nel Regno Unito e Completare la Legalizzazione e la Trascrizione Consolare Italiana
steps.html:
Il decesso deve essere innanzitutto registrato presso l'ufficio di stato civile del distretto britannico in cui è avvenuto prima di poter essere trascritto nei registri di stato civile italiani [1][7]:

  • Registrazione civile nel Regno Unito (Register Office): Registrate il decesso presso il Register Office locale entro 5 giorni in Inghilterra, Galles e Irlanda del Nord (una volta ricevuta la comunicazione dal Medical Examiner o dal Coroner) o entro 8 giorni presso un Registration Office in Scozia [1]. Richiedete più copie integrali certificate dell'atto di morte britannico (Certified Copy of an Entry of Death) [1][7].
  • Apostille britannica e traduzione in italiano: Per un cittadino italiano deceduto nel Regno Unito, il certificato originale di morte britannico deve essere legalizzato mediante Apostille dell'Aja cartacea rilasciata direttamente dal Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office Legalisation Office (telefono: +44 3700 00 22 44) - non sono accettate per la trascrizione di stato civile le apostille emesse da Notary Public o solicitor - e corredato da una traduzione dattiloscritta in lingua italiana [3][7].
  • Trascrizione consolare italiana rispetto alla dichiarazione in Italia: Mentre per un decesso avvenuto in Italia la dichiarazione viene effettuata entro 24 ore presso l'Ufficio di Stato Civile del Comune italiano di decesso per il rilascio dell'atto di morte, del permesso di seppellimento e dell'estratto di morte plurilingue su Modello C (Convenzione di Vienna del 1976), per un decesso avvenuto nel Regno Unito la trascrizione presso il Comune italiano di iscrizione AIRE o di ultima residenza si richiede inviando per posta l'istanza (Modulo N.5, atto di morte britannico originale munito di Apostille, traduzione in italiano, copia del passaporto del defunto e busta preaffrancata Special Delivery) al Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (Ufficio Stato Civile, 83/86 Farringdon Street, London EC4A 4BL) [7].

steps.title: Coordinare il Rimpatrio Internazionale in Italia (Passaporto Mortuario) o la Sepoltura/Cremazione Locale nel Regno Unito
steps.html:
Le imprese funebri incaricate nel Regno Unito e in Italia gestiscono le autorizzazioni tecniche a seconda che scegliate il rimpatrio della salma, il trasporto delle ceneri o il funerale locale nel Regno Unito [1][6]:

  • Rimpatrio della salma in Italia: In Inghilterra e Galles, l'impresa funebre britannica presenta comunicazione al Coroner locale per ottenere l'Out-of-England Order (Form 104), che autorizza l'uscita della salma dall'Inghilterra e dal Galles [1][6]. In Scozia, il nulla osta al trasferimento fuori dal territorio scozzese viene rilasciato tramite il Death Certification Review Service (DCRS) di Healthcare Improvement Scotland o il Procurator Fiscal [1]. Ai sensi della Convenzione di Berlino del 1937 e del regolamento italiano di polizia mortuaria, l'impresa funebre britannica trasmette via e-mail la documentazione al Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra (sociale.londra@esteri.it), indicando il Comune italiano ricevente, il cimitero e i dati della sepoltura/tumulazione nonché il valico o aeroporto di ingresso in Italia, allegando: (1) l'atto di morte britannico originale munito di Apostille del FCDO, (2) il certificato di imbalsamazione (Embalming Certificate), (3) il certificato medico attestante l'assenza di malattie infettive o contagiose (corrispondente alla certificazione sanitaria ASL), (4) il certificato Out-of-England del Coroner e (5) la dichiarazione dell'impresa funebre attestante il confezionamento in doppia cassa con cofano metallico saldato ermeticamente [6]. Il Consolato richiede l'autorizzazione all'ingresso (nulla osta) al Comune italiano e, una volta ottenuta, rilascia il Passaporto Mortuario e appone i sigilli consolari sul feretro per il trasporto [6].
  • Rimpatrio delle ceneri: Se la cremazione avviene nel Regno Unito, l'impresa funebre o la famiglia presenta al Consolato Generale d'Italia a Londra l'atto di morte britannico apostillato, il certificato ufficiale di cremazione (Certificate of Cremation) e i dati del Comune e del cimitero di destinazione per ottenere il passaporto mortuario per il trasporto dell'urna sigillata in Italia [6].
  • Sepoltura o cremazione locale nel Regno Unito: Se le esequie si svolgono nel Regno Unito, il Register Office (o il Coroner / Procurator Fiscal) rilascia direttamente all'impresa funebre britannica il certificato per la sepoltura o la cremazione (Certificate for Burial or Cremation) [1].

steps.title: Completare le Comunicazioni Post-Decesso, le Domande di Pensione ai Superstiti, la Dichiarazione di Successione e il Probate in Italia e nel Regno Unito
steps.html:
Una volta avviate le pratiche funebri o di rimpatrio, gli adempimenti previdenziali, fiscali e successori riguardano frequentemente entrambe le giurisdizioni [2][4][8][9][10]:

  • Comunicazioni, pensioni e procedura di Probate nel Regno Unito:
    • Se il defunto risiedeva in Inghilterra, Scozia o Galles, utilizzate il codice di riferimento Tell Us Once fornito dall'ufficiale di stato civile o contattate il Department for Work and Pensions Bereavement Service (telefono: 0800 151 2012) per comunicare il decesso a HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), all'ufficio passaporti e alle amministrazioni comunali e per verificare l'eventuale diritto al Bereavement Support Payment [2].
    • Se il defunto risiedeva in Italia e percepiva una pensione statale britannica (UK State Pension), datene comunicazione all'International Pension Centre (telefono: +44 191 218 7777) [5].
    • Se il defunto deteneva immobili, conti bancari o investimenti nel Regno Unito che richiedono un provvedimento formale di legittimazione, occorre presentare domanda a HM Courts & Tribunals Service per ottenere il Grant of Probate (o le Letters of Administration in assenza di testamento) in Inghilterra e Galles, oppure la Confirmation presso la Sheriff Court in Scozia [4].
  • Pensioni ai superstiti, dichiarazione di successione e ricerca testamentaria in Italia:
    • Pensione ai superstiti (INPS): I familiari superstiti aventi diritto (coniuge o parte dell'unione civile superstite, figli a carico o altri familiari aventi titolo) possono presentare domanda all'Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale (telefono dall'Italia: 803 164; dall'estero o da cellulare: +39 06 164 164) per la pensione di reversibilità (se il defunto era già pensionato) o la pensione indiretta (se il defunto era un lavoratore assicurato), nonché per i ratei maturati e non riscossi, online tramite SPID/CIE o attraverso un Patronato [8].
    • Dichiarazione di successione in Italia (entro 12 mesi): Gli eredi e i legatari devono presentare telematicamente la dichiarazione di successione all'Agenzia delle Entrate (telefono dall'Italia: 800 90 96 96; dall'estero: +39 06 97617689) entro 12 mesi dalla data di apertura della successione (salvo il caso di esonero qualora l'eredità sia devoluta al coniuge e ai parenti in linea retta, abbia un attivo lordo non superiore a 100.000 euro e non comprenda beni immobili o diritti reali immobiliari) [9].
    • Ricerca del testamento e adempimenti notarili in Italia: Per verificare se la persona deceduta abbia lasciato un testamento in Italia, è possibile richiedere la consultazione del Registro Generale dei Testamenti (gestito dall'Ufficio Centrale degli Archivi Notarili del Ministero della Giustizia) o del registro volontario dei testamenti olografi tramite il Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, incaricando un notaio italiano per la pubblicazione di eventuali testamenti e per le volture catastali degli immobili [10].
