title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Greece: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Greece: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Greece: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand how demanding it is when a family member in Greece is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness. Taking structured medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity ensures that care preferences are respected, trusted representatives can act without court delays, and statutory support is activated on time [1][3][4]. Below we set out the five key steps in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage (EOPYY / ESY)
steps.html:
Early integration of specialist symptom management and home support helps maintain quality of life and reduces avoidable emergency hospitalizations in Greece [1][2]:

  • Public and accredited palliative care services (Law 5007/2022): Under Greece's institutional framework for palliative care (Law 5007/2022) overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Hellenic Republic, interdisciplinary palliative care (Ανακουφιστική Φροντίδα) is organized through Specialized Palliative Care Structures (Δ.Α.Φ.Α.), hospital pain clinics (Ιατρεία Πόνου και Παρηγορητικής Φροντίδας) within the National Health System (ΕΣΥ), and mobile home-care teams [1][2]. Ask the treating specialist or oncology/internal medicine clinic for a referral to the hospital's Pain and Palliative Care Clinic and request a comprehensive written medical summary (Ιατρική Γνωμάτευση) [1][2].
  • EOPYY coverage and home delivery of high-cost medicines: The National Organization for the Provision of Health Services (EOPYY) covers prescribed medical consumables, oxygen therapy, nutritional support, and zero-copayment or reduced-copayment medications for recognized serious and chronic conditions via the electronic prescription system (ΗΔΙΚΑ) using the patient's AMKA number [1][2]. Patients with serious illnesses can also register online with EOPYY's Home Delivery of High-Cost Medicines (Φάρμακα Υψηλού Κόστους - ΦΥΚ κατ' οίκον) and municipal Help at Home (Βοήθεια στο Σπίτι) nursing programs [2].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
Documenting medical wishes while your family member is able to communicate clearly ensures that treating physicians and relatives have explicit guidance if the patient later becomes unable to consent [1][3]:

  • Informed consent and advance treatment preferences (Law 3418/2005): Under the Greek Code of Medical Ethics (Law 3418/2005, Articles 11 and 12), no medical intervention may be performed without the patient's prior informed consent, and a competent adult has the right to accept or refuse specific medical treatments after full disclosure by the physician [1]. Under Article 12(3) of Law 3418/2005, when a patient can no longer give consent, the physician must take into account any wishes previously expressed by the patient (προγενέστερα εκφρασθείσες επιθυμίες) regarding pain management, intensive care, or life-prolonging interventions [1].
  • Designating a trusted healthcare representative and notarial statement: While your family member has full capacity, they can record their care preferences and name a trusted family member or representative to be consulted by doctors in a written declaration entered into the hospital medical record, and reinforce this through a formal declaration or mandate before a Greek notary (Συμβολαιογράφος) or a digital authorization on gov.gr for accessing medical files (Ατομικός Ηλεκτρονικός Φάκελος Υγείας - ΑΗΦΥ) and hospital records [1][3]. Note that active euthanasia and physician-assisted suicide remain prohibited under Greek criminal law, whereas comprehensive palliative pain relief and the refusal of disproportionate or futile treatment are legally protected [1][2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
In Greece, if a person loses mental capacity without having executed a valid power of attorney, family members cannot manage property or bank accounts without petitioning the Court of First Instance for Judicial Support (Δικαστική Συμπαράσταση under Articles 1666 et seq. of the Greek Civil Code), which takes several months [3][6]:

  • Notarial Power of Attorney (Συμβολαιογραφικό Πληρεξούσιο): For banking transactions, pension collection, tax management (AADE), real estate administration, or representation before healthcare and social security bodies, your family member should execute a General or Special Notarial Power of Attorney (Συμβολαιογραφικό Πληρεξούσιο) before a licensed Greek notary while retaining full legal capacity (Δικαιοπρακτική Ικανότητα) [3][6]. If the ill person cannot travel to a notary's office due to mobility limitations, Greek notaries regularly attend the patient's home or hospital room to execute the deed [3][5].
  • Digital authorizations on gov.gr and Greek bank mandates: For routine administrative errands before public authorities and Citizens' Service Centers (ΚΕΠ), your family member can issue a legally binding Digital Authorization (Έκδοση εξουσιοδότησης) or Solemn Declaration (Υπεύθυνη Δήλωση) online via gov.gr using personal Taxisnet credentials or web banking codes and SMS verification [3]. Simultaneously, check with each Greek commercial bank (such as National Bank of Greece, Eurobank, Alpha Bank, or Piraeus Bank) because banks often require their own specific Notarial Power of Attorney wordings or in-branch co-signatory verification [3][6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Certification (KEPA), Financial Allowances, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
A serious or life-limiting illness often qualifies the patient for disability pensions, care allowances, tax exemptions, and workplace caregiver protections in Greece [4]:

  • Disability evaluation through the Disability Certification Center (KEPA): Submit an electronic application through the National Disability Portal on gov.gr (or call the national social security and labor helpline 1555) for medical assessment by the Disability Certification Center (KEPA) (Κέντρο Πιστοποίησης Αναπηρίας) of e-EFKA [4]. The application can be filed by the patient or by an authorized representative holding a notarial power of attorney or digital authorization, after the treating physician uploads the electronic medical file (Εισηγητικός Φάκελος Παροχών Αναπηρίας) [3][4]. For homebound or hospitalized patients, the physician can request a home assessment (κατ' οίκον εξέταση) or document-based evaluation by the KEPA medical committee [4].
  • Disability benefits (e-EFKA / OPEKA) and statutory caregiver leave: A KEPA disability rating (typically 67% or 80% and above) unlocks e-EFKA disability pensions, the extra-institutional care allowance (Εξωιδρυματικό Επίδομα) or severe disability welfare allowances administered by OPEKA, zero-copayment medication status, and income/property tax reductions with AADE [4][6]. Working family members employed in the private sector in Greece are entitled under Law 4808/2021 (implementing EU Directive 2019/1158) to statutory caregiver leave (Άδεια Φροντιστή) of up to 5 working days per year, as well as the right to request flexible working arrangements or remote work when caring for a close relative with a serious medical need [4].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Records, and Cross-Border Estate Documents
steps.html:
Organizing succession documents and property records in advance prevents administrative disputes and simplifies future estate filings in Greece [5][6]:

  • Executing or reviewing a Greek will: Under the Greek Civil Code, a will must be made personally by the testator while possessing full testamentary capacity - it can never be signed by an agent under a power of attorney [5]. While a Holographic Will (Ιδιόγραφη Διαθήκη) written, dated, and signed entirely in the person's own hand is valid, executing a Public Will (Δημόσια Διαθήκη) before a Greek notary in the presence of three witnesses (or a notary and a second notary) provides maximum legal security against challenges and is registered in the national Register of Wills (Μητρώο Διαθηκών) accessible via gov.gr [5].
  • Organizing property, tax (E9 / ENFIA), and cross-border records: Gather the person's Greek identity card, Family Status Certificate (Πιστοποιητικό Οικογενειακής Κατάστασης) via gov.gr, myAADE / E9 property statements, Hellenic Cadastre (Κτηματολόγιο) sheets, and insurance policies [5][6]. If your family member holds assets in another country or is a foreign citizen residing in Greece, consult a notary regarding the choice of applicable succession law under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) and ensure that any foreign powers of attorney carry a Hague Apostille and official Greek translation [5][6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Argentina: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Argentina: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Argentina: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are deeply sorry for the loss of your family member in the Argentine Republic. When a death occurs in Argentina, families must complete the medical or forensic death certification, civil registration within the statutory deadline, licensed funeral arrangements for burial, cremation, or international repatriation, and social security and judicial probate procedures in sequence [1][3][4]. Below we set out the five official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance
steps.html:
Every civil registration, public health permit, and funeral procedure in Argentina requires the official Medical Certificate of Death (Certificado Médico de Defunción) and Statistical Death Report signed by a licensed physician [1]:

  • Natural death in a hospital, clinic, or sanatorium: When a death occurs under medical care in a public or private healthcare facility (for example, in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires Province, Córdoba, Rosario, or Mendoza), the attending physician verifies the death and issues the Medical Certificate of Death after checking the deceased person's National Identity Document (DNI) or passport [1]. With that certificate, the body remains in the hospital mortuary until collected by an authorized funeral home [1].
  • Expected death at a private residence under regular medical care: If your family member was receiving home hospitalization or documented regular care for a diagnosed illness, the treating physician or home-care doctor who attended the patient may verify the death and sign the Medical Certificate of Death without requiring a judicial autopsy [1].
  • Sudden death, death in a public place, unattended death, or violent or suspicious circumstances: Call the police emergency number 911 and the public emergency medical service (SAME 107 in Buenos Aires City and participating municipalities) immediately [1]. In these cases, the local police precinct and the duty criminal prosecutor or judge intervene and order the transfer of the body to the Judicial Morgue (Morgue Judicial) of the Forensic Medical Corps for a mandatory forensic autopsy before issuing the forensic death certificate and the judicial release and burial order [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry and Obtain the Official Death Certificate
steps.html:
Under the Argentine Civil and Commercial Code and National Civil Registry Law 26.413, every death occurring in Argentina must be declared within 48 business hours of verification [1]:

  • Registration with the Civil Registry (Registro del Estado Civil y Capacidad de las Personas): The death declaration is filed with the Civil Registry office having jurisdiction over the place of death (for example, the Civil Registry of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires or the provincial Civil Registries coordinated with the National Registry of Persons - RENAPER) [1]. In standard practice, the licensed funeral home appointed by the family submits the Medical Certificate of Death and the deceased's DNI to record the death entry and immediately obtain the Burial or Cremation Permit (Licencia de Inhumación o Cremación) [1].
  • Obtaining the Death Certificate (Acta o Partida de Defunción): Once the death is registered, the Civil Registry issues the official Death Certificate (Partida de Defunción) (which in most jurisdictions, including Buenos Aires City and Buenos Aires Province, is issued with a verified digital signature valid for pension, banking, and court filings) [1][3]. If the 48-business-hour statutory deadline expires before registration, a special administrative resolution or prior judicial order is required [1].

steps.title: Appoint a Licensed Funeral Provider, Obtain Sanitary Permits, and Arrange Repatriation or Apostille
steps.html:
The family must appoint a licensed funeral home (cochería or empresa de servicios fúnebres) to coordinate local burial, cremation, or domestic or international transport [1][2]:

  • Selecting a licensed funeral home and burial or cremation permits: Before signing a private contract, verify whether the deceased had funeral coverage through their health fund (obra social, such as PAMI), labor union, mutual association, life insurance, or travel insurance. To locate licensed funeral providers nationwide, families can consult the Federación Argentina de Entidades de Servicio Fúnebre y Afines (FADEDSFYA) [2]. Clarvia provides institutional directory references for informational orientation only and does not endorse, recommend, or rank commercial providers. Using the Civil Registry permit, the funeral home coordinates cemetery interment or cremation (note that whenever police or judicial intervention occurred, cremation requires explicit authorization from the presiding judge or prosecutor) [1].
  • International repatriation and Hague Apostille: If the deceased was a foreign citizen, if the casketed remains or cremated ashes must be transported abroad, or if the Argentine Death Certificate must be used in another country, legalize the certificate with an electronic Hague Apostille via the Distant Procedures platform (Trámites a Distancia - TAD) of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, Comercio Internacional y Culto (Cancillería Argentina) [3]. For international casketed repatriation, the funeral home obtains the transfer permit from the local cemetery authority (such as the Directorate General of Cemeteries of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires) and Border Health (Sanidad de Fronteras), submitting the embalming (thanatopraxy) certificate, a medical certificate confirming the absence of contagious disease, a hermetically soldered zinc or metal liner inside the coffin, and the relevant consular clearance [1][3].

steps.title: Notify Social Security (ANSES / PAMI), Banks, and Insurers
steps.html:
Once the Death Certificate is issued, notify social security bodies, financial institutions, and insurers in Argentina [4][5][6]:

  • Funeral grant (Subsidio de Contención Familiar) and survivor pension with ANSES: Report the death to the Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) (toll-free helpline 130 or the Mi ANSES portal) so ongoing retirement or pension payments stop immediately and overpayments after the date of death are avoided [4][5]. The person who paid the funeral expenses of an ANSES retiree or pensioner can apply to the Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) for the Family Containment Subsidy (Subsidio de Contención Familiar) within one year [4]. Eligible surviving spouses, registered cohabiting partners, and minor or disabled children can apply for the Derivative Survivor Pension (Pensión Derivada por Fallecimiento de un Jubilado) or Direct Survivor Pension of an active worker (including benefits under International Social Security Agreements when contributions were paid in more than one country) [5][6].
  • Banks, tax authority (AFIP/ARCA), and life insurance policies: Present the Death Certificate to all Argentine banks where the deceased held accounts, fixed-term deposits, or safe-deposit boxes (the Central Bank rules require freezing individual accounts until the probate judge issues a transfer order, whereas life insurance policies with a named beneficiary are paid directly outside the probate estate) and notify the health fund and national tax authority to update the tax ID (CUIT) as an undivided estate (sucesión indivisa) [4][5].

steps.title: Complete Judicial Probate (Juicio Sucesorio) and Cross-Border Estate Coordination
steps.html:
Under Argentine succession law (Book Five of the National Civil and Commercial Code), transferring registrable assets (real estate, motor vehicles) and bank balances requires completing judicial probate before the civil courts [1][3]:

  • Intestate or testamentary judicial probate in Argentina: Unlike jurisdictions where probate is handled solely by notaries, succession proceedings in Argentina are conducted before the competent Civil Court of the deceased's last domicile with mandatory legal representation by a licensed attorney [1]. The judge orders the publication of legal notices (edictos), checks the Register of Universal Proceedings and the Register of Last Wills of the local Notary Chamber, and issues the Declaration of Heirs (Declaratoria de Herederos) (or formal approval of a notarial or holographic will), which authorizes transferring title to real estate and releasing bank funds [1].
  • Court fees, inheritance taxes, and foreign heirs or assets: Argentina does not levy a federal inheritance tax, though court filing taxes (tasa de justicia) and professional fees apply (and Buenos Aires Province levies a provincial Tax on the Free Transmission of Assets through ARBA above statutory thresholds). Heirs residing outside Argentina can be represented in the Argentine probate court through a special judicial power of attorney signed before an Argentine consulate or before a foreign notary with a Hague Apostille, and Argentine court orders or certificates needed abroad can be apostilled online via TAD with the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, Comercio Internacional y Culto (Cancillería Argentina) [3][6].

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en Argentina: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en Argentina: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su familiar en la República Argentina. Cuando ocurre una defunción en territorio argentino, es necesario cumplir en orden con la certificación médica o médico-legal, la inscripción en el Registro Civil dentro del plazo legal, la gestión funeraria de inhumación, cremación o traslado, y los trámites previsionales y sucesorios [1][3][4]. A continuación detallamos los cinco pasos oficiales y prácticos.

steps.title: Obtención del Certificado Médico de Defunción e intervención médico-legal o judicial
steps.html:
Todo trámite registral, sanitario y funerario en la Argentina exige contar primero con el Certificado Médico de Defunción y el Informe Estadístico de Defunción firmados por un médico matriculado [1]:

  • Fallecimiento por causas naturales en hospital, clínica o sanatorio: Cuando el deceso ocurre bajo asistencia médica en un establecimiento de salud público o privado (por ejemplo, en la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, la Provincia de Buenos Aires, Córdoba, Rosario o Mendoza), el médico tratante constata el óbito y extiende el Certificado Médico de Defunción tras verificar el Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI) o pasaporte de la persona fallecida [1]. Con dicho certificado, el cuerpo permanece en la morgue institucional hasta su retiro por una empresa fúnebre autorizada [1].
  • Fallecimiento en domicilio particular por enfermedad previa conocida: Si su familiar recibía atención médica domiciliaria o seguimiento regular por una patología diagnosticada, el médico de cabecera o del servicio de internación domiciliaria que lo asistía puede constatar el fallecimiento y firmar el Certificado Médico de Defunción sin necesidad de autopsia judicial [1].
  • Fallecimiento súbito, en la vía pública, sin asistencia médica o por causas violentas o dudosas: Se debe llamar de inmediato al número de emergencias policiales 911 y al servicio público de emergencias médicas (SAME 107 en CABA y municipios adheridos) [1]. En estos casos toman intervención la comisaría jurisdiccional y la fiscalía o juzgado penal en turno, que ordenan el traslado del cuerpo a la Morgue Judicial (Cuerpo Médico Forense del Poder Judicial) para practicar la autopsia médico-legal obligatoria antes de expedir el certificado forense y la orden judicial de entrega e inhumación [1].

steps.title: Inscripción del fallecimiento en el Registro Civil y obtención de la Partida de Defunción
steps.html:
Conforme al Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación y la Ley 26.413 del Registro del Estado Civil y Capacidad de las Personas, toda defunción ocurrida en la Argentina debe inscribirse dentro de las 48 horas hábiles siguientes a su constatación [1]:

  • Inscripción ante el Registro del Estado Civil y Capacidad de las Personas: La denuncia e inscripción del fallecimiento se tramita ante el Registro Civil correspondiente al lugar donde ocurrió el deceso (por ejemplo, el Registro Civil de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires o las direcciones provinciales del Registro de las Personas articuladas con el Registro Nacional de las Personas - RENAPER) [1]. En la práctica habitual, la cochería o empresa fúnebre designada por la familia presenta el Certificado Médico de Defunción y el DNI de la persona fallecida para asentar el acta y obtener de inmediato la Licencia de Inhumación o Cremación [1].
  • Obtención del Acta o Partida de Defunción y copias legalizadas: Una vez inscrito el óbito, el Registro Civil emite el Acta o Partida de Defunción oficial (que en la mayoría de las jurisdicciones, como CABA y la Provincia de Buenos Aires, se expide con firma digital válida para trámites previsionales, bancarios y judiciales) [1][3]. Si se venciera el plazo legal de 48 horas hábiles sin haberse inscrito la defunción, se requiere autorización especial del Registro Civil o resolución judicial previa [1].

steps.title: Contratación de servicios funerarios autorizados, permisos sanitarios y traslado internacional o Apostilla
steps.html:
La familia debe designar una empresa de servicios fúnebres habilitada para coordinar el sepelio, la cremación o el traslado interjurisdiccional o internacional [1][2]:

  • Selección de cochería habilitada y permisos de inhumación o cremación: Antes de contratar por cuenta propia, verifique si la persona fallecida contaba con cobertura de sepelio a través de su obra social (como PAMI), sindicato, mutual, seguro de vida o seguro de viaje. Para ubicar prestadores habilitados en todo el país, puede consultarse a la Federación Argentina de Entidades de Servicio Fúnebre y Afines (FADEDSFYA) [2]. Clarvia menciona directorios institucionales únicamente a título informativo y no recomienda, respalda ni clasifica a empresas comerciales. Con la licencia del Registro Civil, la empresa fúnebre gestiona el ingreso al cementerio o crematorio (recordando que, si medió intervención policial o judicial, la cremación exige autorización expresa del juez o fiscal interviniente) [1].
  • Traslado internacional y Apostilla de La Haya: Si la persona fallecida era ciudadana extranjera, si los restos o cenizas deben trasladarse a otro país, o si la Partida de Defunción argentina debe presentarse ante autoridades del exterior, el documento debe legalizarse con la Apostilla de La Haya electrónica a través de la plataforma Trámites a Distancia (TAD) del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, Comercio Internacional y Culto (Cancillería Argentina) [3]. Para repatriar un féretro al exterior, la empresa fúnebre tramita la autorización de traslado ante la autoridad local (como la Dirección General de Cementerios del Gobierno de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires) y la Dirección de Sanidad de Fronteras, presentando el certificado de tanatopraxia, el certificado médico de ausencia de enfermedad infectocontagiosa, el acondicionamiento en caja metálica o de zinc herméticamente soldada y la intervención consular correspondiente [1][3].

steps.title: Notificación a la seguridad social (ANSES / PAMI), bancos y aseguradoras
steps.html:
Con la Partida de Defunción emitida, corresponde notificar a los organismos previsionales, entidades financieras y compañías de seguros en la Argentina [4][5][6]:

  • Subsidio de Contención Familiar y Pensión por Fallecimiento ante ANSES: Notifique el deceso a la Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) (línea gratuita 130 o plataforma Mi ANSES) para dar de baja haberes jubilatorios en curso y evitar cobros indebidos posteriores a la fecha del fallecimiento [4][5]. La persona que acredite haber pagado los gastos de sepelio de un jubilado o pensionado puede solicitar ante la Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) el Subsidio de Contención Familiar dentro del plazo de un año [4]. Asimismo, el cónyuge, conviviente acreditado o hijos menores o con discapacidad pueden tramitar la Pensión Derivada por Fallecimiento de un Jubilado o la Pensión Directa por fallecimiento de un trabajador en actividad (aplicando también los Convenios Internacionales de Seguridad Social si existieran aportes en otro país) [5][6].
  • Entidades bancarias, tarjetas, AFIP/ARCA y seguros de vida: Presente la Partida de Defunción ante los bancos donde la persona fallecida fuera titular de cuentas, plazos fijos o cajas de seguridad (el Banco Central dispone el bloqueo de las cuentas individuales hasta la orden del juez del sucesorio, mientras que el cobro de seguros de vida con beneficiario designado se abona directamente sin entrar en la masa hereditaria) y comunique la baja ante la obra social y la autoridad tributaria nacional para actualizar el CUIT como sucesión indivisa [4][5].

steps.title: Tramitación de la sucesión judicial (declaratoria de herederos) y coordinación patrimonial
steps.html:
En el derecho argentino (Libro Quinto del Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación), la transmisión de bienes registrables (inmuebles, automotores) y saldos bancarios requiere tramitar el proceso sucesorio ante el Poder Judicial [1][3]:

  • Juicio sucesorio ab-intestato o testamentario en Argentina: A diferencia de otros países, en la Argentina las sucesiones se tramitan en sede judicial con patrocinio obligatorio de abogado matriculado ante el Juzgado Civil competente del último domicilio de la persona fallecida [1]. El juez ordena la publicación de edictos, solicita informes al Registro de Juicios Universales y al Registro de Actos de Última Voluntad del Colegio de Escribanos de la jurisdicción, y dicta la Declaratoria de Herederos (o el auto de aprobación formal del testamento por acto público u ológrafo) que habilita la inscripción de los bienes por tracto abreviado o partición [1].
  • Tasas judiciales, impuesto a la transmisión gratuita de bienes y herederos en el exterior: En el orden nacional argentino no rige un impuesto federal a las herencias, aunque se abonan la tasa de justicia y los aportes del proceso sucesorio (con excepción de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, donde ARBA recauda el Impuesto a la Transmisión Gratuita de Bienes cuando se superan los mínimos exentos). Si existen herederos domiciliados en el extranjero, pueden intervenir en el juicio sucesorio argentino mediante un poder especial judicial otorgado ante el consulado argentino o ante notario extranjero legalizado con la Apostilla de La Haya, y si la persona fallecida dejó bienes fuera de la Argentina, las partidas y testimonios judiciales argentinos se apostillan por TAD ante la Cancillería Argentina [3][6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Argentina: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Argentina: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Argentina: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand the challenges your family faces when a loved one in the Argentine Republic is diagnosed with a serious, advanced, or terminal illness. Organizing palliative medical care, advance healthcare directives, notarial powers of attorney, and social security benefits while your family member retains full legal capacity ensures that their wishes are respected and prevents court delays [1][2][4]. Below we detail the five official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Activate Home or Hospital Palliative Care and Health System Coverage
steps.html:
Argentine health legislation guarantees comprehensive access to interdisciplinary palliative care and pain management across all stages of a life-threatening or life-limiting illness [1]:

  • Mandatory coverage under the National Palliative Care Law (Law 27.678): Pursuant to National Law 27.678 and the guidelines of the National Palliative Care Program of the Ministerio de Salud de la Nación, the public health sector, national and provincial health funds (obras sociales, including INSSJP - PAMI), and private prepaid medicine companies (empresas de medicina prepaga) must provide comprehensive palliative care in outpatient, inpatient, and home hospitalization (internación domiciliaria) settings [1]. Ask the treating specialist or oncology/internal medicine team for a formal referral to the interdisciplinary Palliative Care Unit and a detailed medical history summary [1].
  • 100% coverage of essential medicines and home medical equipment: Current regulations require health funds and prepaid health plans to cover 100% of opioid analgesics and essential symptom-control medications, as well as medical supplies, oxygen therapy, orthopedic beds, and home nursing or physical therapy prescribed by the treating team [1][3]. If a national obra social or prepaid health company delays or denies coverage, families can file an expedited administrative complaint with the Superintendency of Health Services (Superintendencia de Servicios de Salud).

steps.title: Execute Advance Medical Directives and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
While the ill person retains full mental lucidity and decision-making capacity, they can record legally binding treatment preferences and appoint a healthcare representative to communicate with the medical team [2]:

  • Advance medical directives (Law 26.529 and Dignified Death Law 26.742): Under Article 11 of Patient Rights Law 26.529 (as amended by Law 26.742) and Article 60 of the National Civil and Commercial Code, any capable adult may establish advance medical directives (directivas médicas anticipadas) consenting to or refusing specific medical, preventive, or palliative treatments, as well as surgical, hydration, nutrition, or artificial resuscitation procedures when they would be extraordinary or disproportionate in an irreversible terminal condition [2]. Active euthanasia practices are prohibited under Argentine law, but refusing futile therapies and receiving comprehensive palliative symptom relief are fully enforceable statutory rights [2].
  • Formalization before a civil-law notary or court and appointing a healthcare proxy: Under Law 26.742, formal advance directives must be executed in writing before a civil-law notary (escribano público) or a first-instance judge in the presence of two witnesses, and a signed copy should also be added to the patient's medical chart [2]. In the same instrument, your family member can designate one or more trusted persons as healthcare proxies or representatives (mandatarios de salud) to ensure their directives are honored if they later become unable to express their wishes [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
If a person loses decision-making capacity without having executed valid powers of attorney, family members cannot manage property or bank accounts without filing a judicial capacity and support proceeding before a civil court [2][5]:

  • General or Special Power of Attorney by public deed before a notary (escribano público): While your family member retains full legal capacity, it is advisable to execute a General Power of Attorney for Administration and Disposition (Poder General Amplio de Administración y Disposición) or tailored special powers of attorney before a licensed notary public (through the local Colegio de Escribanos of the relevant city or province) [2][5]. If the ill person cannot travel to the notary's office for medical reasons, an Argentine escribano público can attend the private residence or hospital room in person to verify legal capacity and take the signature in the notarial protocol.
  • Social security proxy with ANSES and commercial bank mandates: For collecting retirement or pension benefits and conducting social security filings, the beneficiary can appoint a close relative as an Authorized Representative for Collection or Filings (Apoderado para Cobro o Trámites) before the Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) (using Form PS 6.4 with medical certification for homebound or hospitalized individuals) [4]. At the same time, verify with each Argentine commercial bank its specific requirements for registering authorized co-signers or powers of attorney on checking accounts, savings accounts, and safe-deposit boxes.

steps.title: Apply for Disability Certification (CUD), Disability Retirement, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
A serious or advanced illness entitles the patient to comprehensive disability coverage, social security benefits, and workplace caregiver protections in Argentina [3][4]:

  • Unique Disability Certificate (Certificado Único de Discapacidad - CUD) via ANDIS: Apply through the official portal and the Mi Argentina app for evaluation by an Interdisciplinary Assessment Board coordinated with the Agencia Nacional de Discapacidad (ANDIS) to obtain the Unique Disability Certificate (CUD) [3]. The CUD is a free official public document that guarantees under Law 24.901 100% coverage of medications, rehabilitation, home hospitalization, prescribed home caregivers or personal assistants, free public transit, and disability family allowances [3].
  • Transitional Disability Retirement (Retiro Transitorio por Invalidez) with ANSES and workplace caregiver leave: If the ill person is of working age (has not yet reached ordinary retirement age) and has a physical or intellectual work incapacity of 66% or higher certified by the Medical Commissions, they can apply for Transitional Disability Retirement (Retiro Transitorio por Invalidez) with the Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) (toll-free helpline 130 or Virtual Attention using their Social Security Key) [4]. Working family members caring for the ill person should also check the paid family-illness care leave provisions under their applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement (Convenio Colectivo de Trabajo) or public-sector employment statute.

steps.title: Organize the Will, Insurance Beneficiaries, and Property Records in Advance
steps.html:
Putting civil, financial, and testamentary documents in order brings peace of mind to the ill person and prevents unnecessary litigation or expenses for heirs [2][5]:

  • Notarial Will by Public Deed (Testamento por Acto Público) and forced heirship rules: Under the Argentine Civil and Commercial Code (Articles 2444 et seq.), Argentine succession law protects the compulsory share (porción legítima) of forced heirs (two-thirds for descendants, one-half for ascendants, and one-half for a surviving spouse), while allowing the testator to dispose freely by will of the remaining available portion (one-third or one-half, respectively). Executing a Will by Public Deed (Testamento por Acto Público) before a civil-law notary and two witnesses (and registering it in the Register of Last Wills of the local Notary Chamber) provides maximum legal certainty against loss or challenge.
  • Life insurance beneficiaries, civil status records, and cross-border coordination: Review and update in writing the named beneficiaries on life insurance policies (such as Mandatory Collective Life Insurance and private policies), as life insurance proceeds are paid directly to named beneficiaries without waiting for judicial probate. Gather the person's DNI, updated birth and marriage certificates, real estate deeds, and vehicle titles; if assets or family members are located abroad, legalize Argentine powers of attorney or public documents with an electronic Hague Apostille through the Trámites a Distancia (TAD) platform of the Argentine Foreign Ministry [5].

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación legal en Argentina: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos para la planificación médica y legal ante una enfermedad terminal en Argentina: cuidados paliativos, testamento vital (voluntades anticipadas), poderes preventivos, ayudas para cuidadores y testamento.
es.introHtml: Comprendemos la situación que atraviesa su familia cuando un ser querido recibe el diagnóstico de una enfermedad grave, avanzada o en fase terminal en la República Argentina. Organizar con antelación la atención médica paliativa, las directivas anticipadas, los poderes notariales y las prestaciones previsionales mientras su familiar conserva su plena capacidad jurídica permite asegurar que se respeten sus decisiones y evitar demoras judiciales [1][2][4]. A continuación detallamos los cinco pasos oficiales y prácticos en orden.

steps.title: Activación de cuidados paliativos domiciliarios u hospitalarios y cobertura de salud
steps.html:
El sistema sanitario argentino garantiza por ley el acceso a la atención paliativa integral y al control del dolor en todas las etapas de una enfermedad amenazante o limitante para la vida [1]:

  • Cobertura obligatoria bajo la Ley Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (Ley 27.678): Conforme a la Ley 27.678 y a los lineamientos del Programa Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos del Ministerio de Salud de la Nación, el subsector público, las obras sociales nacionales y provinciales (incluido el INSSJP - PAMI) y las empresas de medicina prepaga deben brindar cobertura integral de cuidados paliativos en modalidad ambulatoria, hospitalaria y de internación domiciliaria [1]. Solicite al médico tratante o al servicio de oncología o clínica médica la derivación formal al equipo interdisciplinario de Cuidados Paliativos y un resumen detallado de historia clínica [1].
  • Provisión de medicamentos esenciales y equipamiento en domicilio: La normativa vigente obliga a las obras sociales y prepagas a cubrir al 100 % los analgésicos opioides y medicamentos esenciales para el control de síntomas, así como insumos, oxigenoterapia, cama ortopédica y prestaciones de enfermería y kinesiología domiciliaria prescritas por el equipo tratante [1][3]. En caso de negativa o demora injustificada de una obra social nacional o empresa de medicina prepaga, la familia puede presentar un reclamo de urgencia ante la Superintendencia de Servicios de Salud.

steps.title: Otorgamiento de directivas médicas anticipadas y designación de representante sanitario
steps.html:
Mientras la persona enferma conserva plena lucidez y capacidad decisoria, puede dejar constancia legalmente vinculante de sus preferencias terapéuticas y designar a un interlocutor ante el equipo médico [2]:

  • Directivas médicas anticipadas (Ley 26.529 y Ley 26.742 de Muerte Digna): De acuerdo con el artículo 11 de la Ley 26.529 de Derechos del Paciente (modificada por la Ley 26.742) y el artículo 60 del Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación, toda persona mayor de edad y capaz puede disponer directivas médicas anticipadas sobre su salud, consintiendo o rechazando determinados tratamientos médicos, preventivos o paliativos, así como procedimientos quirúrgicos, de hidratación, alimentación o reanimación artificial cuando resulten extraordinarios o desproporcionados frente a una situación terminal e irreversible [2]. Las prácticas eutanásicas activas no están permitidas por la ley argentina, pero el rechazo de terapias fútiles y el alivio paliativo integral constituyen derechos plenamente exigibles [2].
  • Formalización ante escribano público o juzgado y designación de mandatario de salud: Para tener plena eficacia formal conforme a la Ley 26.742, la declaración de voluntad anticipada debe instrumentarse por escrito ante escribano público o ante juzgado de primera instancia con la presencia de dos testigos, e incorporarse además una copia firmada en la historia clínica del paciente [2]. En ese mismo acto, su familiar puede designar a una o más personas de confianza como representantes o interlocutores sanitarios para que velen por el cumplimiento de sus directivas en caso de incapacidad sobreviniente [2].

steps.title: Formalización de poderes notariales y autorizaciones bancarias con plena capacidad
steps.html:
Si una persona pierde su capacidad de discernimiento sin haber otorgado poderes válidos, los familiares no pueden administrar bienes ni cuentas bancarias sin promover un proceso judicial de determinación de la capacidad y designación de apoyos ante el juzgado civil [2][5]:

  • Poder General o Especial por escritura pública ante escribano: Mientras su familiar conserve su plena capacidad jurídica, es recomendable otorgar ante un escribano público matriculado (a través del Colegio de Escribanos de la ciudad o provincia correspondiente) un Poder General Amplio de Administración y Disposición o poderes especiales adaptados a sus necesidades [2][5]. Si la persona enferma no puede trasladarse a la escribanía por razones médicas, el escribano público puede constituirse en el domicilio particular o en la habitación del hospital o sanatorio para verificar su discernimiento y tomar la firma en el protocolo notarial.
  • Apoderado previsional en ANSES y autorizaciones bancarias: Para el cobro de haberes jubilatorios o pensiones y la realización de trámites previsionales, la persona titular puede designar a un familiar directo como Apoderado para Cobro o Trámites ante la Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) (utilizando la certificación de firma o el formulario PS 6.4 / médico certificante para personas imposibilitadas de movilizarse) [4]. Simultáneamente, conviene verificar en cada entidad bancaria de la Argentina los requisitos específicos para registrar autorizados o apoderados en cuentas corrientes, cajas de ahorro y cajas de seguridad.

steps.title: Solicitud de prestaciones por discapacidad (CUD), retiro por invalidez y apoyos al cuidador
steps.html:
Una enfermedad grave o avanzada da derecho a importantes coberturas integrales de discapacidad, prestaciones de seguridad social y licencias laborales en la Argentina [3][4]:

  • Certificado Único de Discapacidad (CUD) ante ANDIS y juntas evaluadoras: Solicite a través de la plataforma oficial y la aplicación Mi Argentina la evaluación por una Junta Evaluadora Interdisciplinaria coordinada con la Agencia Nacional de Discapacidad (ANDIS) para tramitar el Certificado Único de Discapacidad (CUD) [3]. El CUD es un documento público y gratuito que garantiza por la Ley 24.901 la cobertura del 100 % en medicamentos, prestaciones de rehabilitación, internación domiciliaria, cuidadores domiciliarios / asistentes personales prescritos, transporte público gratuito y asignaciones familiares por discapacidad [3].
  • Retiro Transitorio por Invalidez (ANSES) y licencias laborales para familiares: Si la persona enferma se encuentra en edad activa (no ha alcanzado aún la edad jubilatoria ordinaria) y presenta una incapacidad física o intelectual igual o superior al 66 % determinada por las Comisiones Médicas, puede gestionar el Retiro Transitorio por Invalidez ante la Administración Nacional de la Seguridad Social (ANSES) (línea 130 o Atención Virtual con Clave de la Seguridad Social) [4]. Por su parte, los familiares trabajadores que cuidan a la persona enferma deben revisar las licencias remuneradas o especiales por atención de familiar enfermo previstas en su Convenio Colectivo de Trabajo o estatuto del sector público.

steps.title: Ordenación preventiva del testamento, seguros y documentación patrimonial
steps.html:
Dejar ordenada la documentación civil, financiera y testamentaria brinda tranquilidad a la persona enferma y evita litigios o costos innecesarios a los herederos [2][5]:

  • Testamento por acto público ante escribano y porción legítima: Bajo el Código Civil y Comercial de la Nación (artículos 2444 y siguientes), el derecho sucesorio argentino protege la porción legítima de los herederos forzosos (dos tercios para los descendientes, un medio para los ascendientes y un medio para el cónyuge), permitiendo disponer libremente mediante testamento de la porción disponible restante (un tercio o un medio, según el caso). Otorgar un Testamento por Acto Público mediante escritura pública ante escribano y dos testigos (inscribiéndolo en el Registro de Actos de Última Voluntad del Colegio de Escribanos local) ofrece la máxima seguridad jurídica frente a extravíos o impugnaciones.
  • Beneficiarios de seguros de vida, documentación civil y coordinación internacional: Revise y actualice por escrito la designación de beneficiarios en pólizas de seguro de vida (obligatorios como el Seguro Colectivo de Vida Obligatorio y pólizas voluntarias), dado que dichas sumas se abonan directamente a los beneficiarios designados sin esperar al juicio sucesorio. Reúna asimismo el DNI, partidas de nacimiento y matrimonio actualizadas, títulos de propiedad de inmuebles y automotores, y si existen bienes o familiares en el extranjero, legalice los poderes o documentos públicos argentinos mediante la Apostilla de La Haya electrónica en la plataforma Trámites a Distancia (TAD) de la Cancillería Argentina [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Colombia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Colombia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Colombia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are deeply sorry for the loss of your family member in Colombia. When a death occurs in Colombian territory, families must complete the medical or forensic death certification, registration in the Civil Registry of Death within the statutory deadline, sanitary permits for burial, cremation, or international repatriation, and social security and estate succession procedures in order [1][2][3][5]. Below we detail the five official and practical steps.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death (RUAF-ND) or Forensic Autopsy Clearance
steps.html:
Every civil registration and sanitary permit in Colombia requires the official Antecedent Certificate of Death for the Civil Registry (Certificado de Defunción Antecedente para el Registro Civil), issued through the Births and Deaths module of the Single Registry of Affiliates (RUAF-ND of the Ministry of Health and Social Protection and DANE) [1][3]:

  • Natural death in a clinic, hospital, or under home medical care: When the deceased dies under medical care in a healthcare institution (Institución Prestadora de Servicios de Salud - IPS, for example in Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla, or Bucaramanga) or under home medical care with an active medical record, the attending physician verifies the death and issues the Antecedent Certificate of Death (RUAF-ND) free of charge [1][3]. Provide the deceased person's Colombian citizenship card (cédula de ciudadanía), foreigner ID card (cédula de extranjería), or passport so that personal particulars match civil registry records [1].
  • Sudden death, unattended home death, death in a public place, or violent or undetermined cause: Call the single national emergency number 123 immediately so the National Police (Policía Nacional) and the Technical Investigation Corps (CTI) of the Attorney General's Office (Fiscalía General de la Nación) can perform urgent judicial inspection acts [2]. In these cases, the body is transferred to the regional branch of the Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses for a mandatory forensic autopsy (necropsia médico-legal) [2]. Once full identity is verified and the prosecutor issues the release order, the Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses issues the antecedent death certificate and authorizes release of the body to the funeral home appointed by the family [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Within the 2-Business-Day Deadline
steps.html:
Under Decree-Law 1260 of 1970, every death occurring in Colombia must be registered within two (2) business days of learning of the death [1]:

  • Competent registry office (Registraduría or Notary): Death registration is completed before any office of the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil or before a Notary (Notaría) in the municipality or district where the death occurred (institutional inquiries regarding registry updates and cancellation of identity cards can be sent to defuncionesdnrc@registraduria.gov.co) [1]. Present the original Medical or Forensic Certificate of Death together with the deceased's identity document [1].
  • Late registration and certified copies of the Civil Registry of Death: If more than two (2) business days elapse without registration, Colombian law requires a written order from a Police Inspector (or competent judicial/forensic authority) authorizing late registration (inscripción extemporánea) [1]. Once the serial registry entry is recorded, request several certified copies (copias auténticas) of the Civil Registry of Death (Registro Civil de Defunción) for banking, pension, and succession filings, while the Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil cancels the deceased's citizenship card in the National Identification Archive (ANI) [1].

steps.title: Appoint a Licensed Funeral Home, Obtain Sanitary Permits, and Arrange Repatriation or Apostille
steps.html:
The family must appoint a licensed funeral provider in Colombia to collect the deceased, prepare final disposition, and obtain local sanitary permits [3][4]:

  • Sanitary permit for burial or cremation (Licencia de Inhumación o Cremación): Before contracting private services out of pocket, check whether the deceased held a pre-need funeral plan (plan exequial), life insurance policy, or travel assistance policy. The appointed funeral home applies to the municipal or district health authority (such as the Bogotá District Secretariat of Health / Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá through its digital portal Agilínea, or the relevant municipal health secretariat) for the Burial or Cremation Permit, submitting the RUAF-ND Death Certificate and, for cremation, the written authorization of the legally entitled family members (plus explicit prosecutor authorization whenever criminal investigation or violent death was involved) [2][3].
  • International repatriation and electronic Hague Apostille: If the deceased was a foreign citizen, if the family decides to repatriate the embalmed body in a hermetically sealed coffin or cremated ashes abroad, or if the Colombian Civil Registry of Death must be used legally in another country, obtain the online Hague Apostille (available 24/7 in PDF format with a verification code) through the official portal of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Cancillería) [4]. For international transport of casketed human remains or cremated ashes, the funeral home also secures the international sanitary transfer permit, embalming certificate, and consular clearance from the destination country [3][4].

steps.title: Notify Pension Funds (Colpensiones / AFP), Health Insurers (EPS), Banks, and Insurers
steps.html:
Once the Civil Registry of Death is issued, notify entities of the Comprehensive Social Security System and financial institutions in Colombia [1][5]:

  • Funeral grant (Auxilio Funerario) and survivor pension with Colpensiones or private pension funds (AFP): Any person who proves having paid the burial or cremation expenses of an affiliated worker or pensioner (by submitting original paid invoices and the Civil Registry of Death) is entitled to claim the statutory Funeral Grant (Auxilio Funerario) under Law 100 of 1993 (equal to the last contribution base salary or monthly pension, between 5 and 10 legal monthly minimum wages) from Colpensiones (Public Pay-As-You-Go Regime) or from the relevant private Pension Fund Administrator (Porvenir, Protección, Colfondos, or Skandia) [5]. Eligible surviving spouses or permanent partners, minor children, student children up to age 25, or disabled children can apply for the Survivor Pension (Pensión de Sobrevivientes) or pension substitution (or a lump-sum substitute indemnity / balance refund if minimum contribution weeks were not met) [5].
  • EPS, commercial banks, credit life insurance, and DIAN: Report the death to the Health Promoting Entity (EPS) and to all Colombian banks where your family member held savings or checking accounts, CDTs, or loans (and request activation of debtor group life insurance - seguro de vida grupo deudores - covering mortgage or consumer loan balances). Colombian banking regulations allow direct release of small-balance deposits without formal succession proceedings (entrega directa de depósitos sin juicio de sucesión up to the annual statutory threshold set by the Financial Superintendency), above which funds require a notarial succession deed or court judgment.

steps.title: Complete Estate Succession Before a Notary or Court and Tax Filings (DIAN)
steps.html:
Settlement of the marital or patrimonial partnership and inheritance succession in Colombia can proceed either before a notary or before a court depending on whether all heirs agree [1][4]:

  • Uncontested notarial succession (Decree 902 of 1988) vs. judicial succession: When all heirs, legatees, and the surviving spouse or permanent partner have full legal capacity and are in complete agreement, succession can be completed rapidly by public deed before a Colombian Notary (Notaría) (with mandatory representation by a licensed attorney whenever net estate assets exceed 15 legal monthly minimum wages). If there is any disagreement among heirs or a dispute over a will or estate property, judicial succession proceedings must be filed before the competent Family or Civil Court (Juzgado de Familia o Civil) of the deceased's last domicile in Colombia.
  • Tax obligations before DIAN (undivided estate RUT) and cross-border coordination: The estate representatives or heirs must update the deceased's Single Tax Registry (RUT) with the National Directorate of Taxes and Customs (DIAN) as an undivided estate (sucesión ilíquida), file income tax returns, and obtain tax clearance from DIAN before the notary or court finalizes the partition (paying occasional gain tax on inheritances - impuesto de ganancia ocasional - above statutory exemptions). If an heir resides outside Colombia, they can grant a special power of attorney to a Colombian lawyer before the nearest Colombian consulate or before a foreign notary legalized with a Hague Apostille through the channels validated by the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores [4].

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en Colombia: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en Colombia: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su familiar en Colombia. Cuando ocurre un deceso en territorio colombiano, es necesario gestionar en orden la certificación médica o médico-legal, la inscripción en el Registro Civil de Defunción dentro del plazo legal, las licencias sanitarias de inhumación, cremación o traslado, y los trámites de seguridad social y sucesión [1][2][3][5]. A continuación detallamos los cinco pasos oficiales y prácticos.

steps.title: Obtención del Certificado Médico de Defunción (RUAF-ND) o necropsia médico-legal
steps.html:
Todo trámite registral y sanitario en Colombia exige contar primero con el Certificado de Defunción Antecedente para el Registro Civil, expedido a través del módulo de Nacimientos y Defunciones del Registro Único de Afiliados (RUAF-ND del Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social y el DANE) [1][3]:

  • Fallecimiento por causas naturales en clínica, hospital o bajo atención domiciliaria: Cuando la persona fallecida muere bajo cuidado médico en una institución prestadora de servicios de salud (IPS, por ejemplo en Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla o Bucaramanga) o bajo atención domiciliaria con historia clínica activa, el médico tratante verifica el óbito y expide sin costo el Certificado de Defunción Antecedente (RUAF-ND) [1][3]. Entregue la cédula de ciudadanía, cédula de extranjería o pasaporte de la persona fallecida para que los datos coincidan exactamente con la registraduría [1].
  • Fallecimiento súbito, en domicilio sin asistencia médica, en vía pública o por causa violenta o por establecer: Se debe llamar de inmediato a la línea única de emergencias 123 para la intervención de la Policía Nacional y de los actos urgentes de policía judicial del Cuerpo Técnico de Investigación (CTI) de la Fiscalía General de la Nación [2]. En estos casos, el cuerpo es trasladado a la sede regional del Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses para practicar la necropsia médico-legal obligatoria [2]. Una vez confirmada la identidad plena y expedida la orden de entrega por el fiscal competente, el Instituto Nacional de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses emite el certificado de defunción antecedente y autoriza el retiro del cuerpo por la funeraria designada [2].

steps.title: Inscripción en el Registro Civil de Defunción dentro del plazo legal de 2 días hábiles
steps.html:
Conforme al Decreto Ley 1260 de 1970, todo fallecimiento ocurrido en Colombia debe inscribirse dentro de los dos (2) días hábiles siguientes al momento en que se tuvo noticia del hecho [1]:

  • Oficina competente (Registraduría o Notaría): La inscripción del fallecimiento se realiza ante cualquier oficina de la Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil o ante una Notaría del municipio o distrito donde ocurrió el deceso (consultas institucionales sobre actualización de registros y cancelación de cédulas a través del correo defuncionesdnrc@registraduria.gov.co) [1]. Para el registro se presenta el Certificado Médico o Forense de Defunción original y el documento de identidad de la persona fallecida [1].
  • Inscripción extemporánea y copias auténticas del Registro Civil de Defunción: Si transcurren más de dos (2) días hábiles sin haberse realizado la inscripción, la ley exige una orden escrita del inspector de policía (o autoridad judicial/médico-legal competente) para autorizar el registro extemporáneo [1]. Una vez sentado el folio con su indicativo serial, solicite varias copias auténticas del Registro Civil de Defunción, indispensables para trámites bancarios, pensionales y sucesorales, mientras la Registraduría Nacional del Estado Civil procede a cancelar por muerte la cédula de ciudadanía en el Archivo Nacional de Identificación (ANI) [1].

steps.title: Contratación de funeraria habilitada, licencias sanitarias y traslado internacional o Apostilla
steps.html:
La familia debe designar una empresa funeraria legalmente habilitada en Colombia para retirar el cuerpo, preparar la disposición final y tramitar las licencias sanitarias [3][4]:

  • Licencia sanitaria de inhumación o cremación: Antes de contratar servicios particulares, verifique si la persona fallecida contaba con un plan exequial previsor, póliza de seguro de vida o seguro de viaje. La funeraria autorizada tramita ante la autoridad sanitaria municipal o distrital (como la Secretaría Distrital de Salud de Bogotá a través de su plataforma digital Agilínea, o la secretaría de salud del municipio correspondiente) la Licencia de Inhumación o Cremación, adjuntando el Certificado de Defunción RUAF-ND y, en caso de cremación, la manifestación escrita de voluntad o autorización de los familiares legitimados (además del permiso expreso del fiscal cuando medió investigación penal o muerte violenta) [2][3].
  • Repatriación internacional y Apostilla electrónica de La Haya: Si la persona fallecida era ciudadana extranjera, si la familia decide trasladar el cuerpo embalsamado en féretro hermético o las cenizas cremadas al exterior, o si el Registro Civil de Defunción colombiano debe surtir efectos jurídicos en otro país, gestione la Apostilla de La Haya en línea (disponible las 24 horas en formato PDF con código de verificación) a través del portal oficial del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Cancillería de Colombia) [4]. Para la salida internacional de un cadáver o de restos humanos, la funeraria gestiona asimismo el permiso sanitario de traslado internacional, el certificado de tanatopraxia y la documentación consular del país de destino [3][4].

steps.title: Notificación a fondos de pensiones (Colpensiones / AFP), EPS, bancos y aseguradoras
steps.html:
Con el Registro Civil de Defunción expedido, notifique a las entidades del Sistema de Seguridad Social Integral y del sector financiero en Colombia [1][5]:

  • Auxilio funerario y pensión de sobrevivientes ante Colpensiones o fondos privados (AFP): La persona que demuestre haber sufragado los gastos de entierro o cremación de un afiliado o pensionado (presentando las facturas originales canceladas y el Registro Civil de Defunción) tiene derecho a reclamar el Auxilio Funerario previsto en la Ley 100 de 1993 (equivalente al último salario base de cotización o mesada pensional, entre 5 y 10 salarios mínimos mensuales legales vigentes) ante Colpensiones (Régimen de Prima Media) o ante la Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones privada (Porvenir, Protección, Colfondos o Skandia) [5]. Asimismo, el cónyuge o compañero(a) permanente supérstite, los hijos menores, hijos estudiantes hasta los 25 años o hijos con invalidez pueden solicitar la Pensión de Sobrevivientes o la sustitución pensional (o la indemnización sustitutiva / devolución de saldos si no se reunieron las semanas mínimas) [5].
  • EPS, bancos, seguros de vida y DIAN: Reporte el fallecimiento a la Entidad Promotora de Salud (EPS) y a los bancos colombianos donde su familiar poseía cuentas de ahorro, cuentas corrientes, CDT o créditos (solicite además la activación de los seguros de vida grupo deudores que amparan saldos de créditos hipotecarios o de consumo). En Colombia existe un límite legal para la entrega directa de saldos bancarios de baja cuantía sin juicio de sucesión (beneficio de entrega directa de depósitos hasta el tope fijado anualmente por la Superintendencia Financiera), superado el cual los fondos se entregan mediante escritura notarial o sentencia de sucesión.

steps.title: Tramitación de la herencia o sucesión ante Notaría o Juzgado y obligaciones tributarias
steps.html:
La liquidación de la sociedad conyugal o patrimonial y de la herencia en Colombia puede tramitarse por vía notarial o judicial según exista acuerdo entre los interesados [1][4]:

  • Sucesión notarial de mutuo acuerdo (Decreto 902 de 1988) frente a sucesión judicial: Si todos los herederos, legatarios y el cónyuge o compañero(a) supérstite son plenamente capaces y están de acuerdo, la sucesión se tramita de forma ágil mediante escritura pública ante una Notaría colombiana (con intervención obligatoria de abogado titulado cuando el activo líquido herencial supere los 15 salarios mínimos mensuales legales vigentes). Si existe desacuerdo entre los herederos o controversia sobre el testamento o los bienes, debe promoverse el proceso de sucesión ante el Juzgado de Familia o Civil del último domicilio del causante en Colombia.
  • Obligaciones ante la DIAN (RUT de sucesión ilíquida) y coordinación internacional: Los representantes o herederos deben actualizar el Registro Único Tributario (RUT) de la persona fallecida ante la Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) como sucesión ilíquida, presentar las declaraciones del impuesto sobre la renta por la fracción del año y obtener el paz y salvo fiscal requerido por la notaría o el juzgado antes de protocolizar la partición (aplicando el impuesto de ganancia ocasional sobre herencias cuando supere las exenciones del Estatuto Tributario). Si algún heredero reside fuera de Colombia, puede otorgar poder especial a un abogado en Colombia ante el consulado colombiano más cercano o ante notario extranjero legalizado con la Apostilla de La Haya a través de los canales validados por el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores [4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Colombia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Colombia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Colombia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand the situation your family faces when a loved one in Colombia is diagnosed with a serious, advanced, or terminal illness. Coordinating palliative care, an Advance Directive Document, notarial powers of attorney, and social security benefits while your family member retains full legal capacity ensures that their autonomy is respected and prevents legal or financial blocks [1][2][3]. Below we detail the five practical, medical, and legal steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Activate Home or Hospital Palliative Care and Health System (EPS) Coverage
steps.html:
Colombian legislation guarantees the right of every person with a chronic, degenerative, irreversible, or terminal illness to receive comprehensive palliative care and effective pain management [1][2]:

  • Mandatory coverage under the Consuelo Devis Saavedra Law (Law 1733 of 2014): Pursuant to Law 1733 of 2014 and the regulations of the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social, all Health Promoting Entities (EPS in both the contributory and subsidized regimes) and Healthcare Provider Institutions (IPS) must guarantee comprehensive palliative care in inpatient, outpatient, and home care (atención domiciliaria) settings (including care by pain and palliative care specialists, nursing, nutritional support, psychology, and social work) [1][2]. Ask the treating physician or specialist for a formal referral to your EPS's Home Palliative Care Program and an updated copy of the medical record [1].
  • Supply of opioid medications, copayment exemptions, and Supersalud protection: EPS insurers and departmental narcotics funds are required to ensure continuous availability of opioid analgesics and special-control medications for severe pain relief [1]. Furthermore, patients diagnosed with catastrophic or high-cost illnesses are exempt from copayments and moderating fees (copagos y cuotas moderadoras) for services related to their condition; if any delay or barrier arises in delivering medications or home care supplies, the family can file an urgent life-risk complaint with the National Health Superintendency (Superintendencia Nacional de Salud - Supersalud) or file a constitutional protection action (acción de tutela) to enforce the fundamental right to health.

steps.title: Execute the Advance Directive Document (DVA) and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
While the ill person retains full legal and mental capacity, they can formally record their decisions regarding future medical treatments and end-of-life care [1][2]:

  • Scope of the Advance Directive Document (Resolution 2665 of 2018): Under Law 1733 of 2014 and Resolution 2665 of 2018 issued by the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social, any capable adult - whether healthy or ill - may execute an Advance Directive Document (Documento de Voluntad Anticipada - DVA) freely and consciously stating their specific preferences regarding healthcare, acceptance or refusal of disproportionate medical treatments or life-support measures (redirection of therapeutic effort), palliative accompaniment, and decisions relating to the right to die with dignity or organ donation [1][2].
  • Three valid formalization methods and incorporation into the medical record: In Colombia, Resolution 2665 of 2018 allows formalizing the Advance Directive Document through any of three fully valid methods without requiring a lawyer: 1) before the attending physician (who records it in the clinical chart), 2) in writing before two (2) witnesses (attaching copies of the identity documents of the declarant and both witnesses), or 3) by public deed before a Notary (Notaría) [1][2]. In the same document, your family member can designate a trusted relative or representative to ensure their decisions are honored by the medical team, and should request that the DVA be incorporated into their clinical history and reported to their EPS [1][2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney, Advance Support Directives, and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
Under Law 1996 of 2019 (which strengthened the legal capacity framework in Colombia), establishing representation and support instruments while the person can unequivocally express their wishes avoids subsequent judicial proceedings [2][5]:

  • General Power of Attorney by public deed before a Notary or special power of attorney: To manage bank accounts, collect pension payments, file tax returns with DIAN, or administer real estate, it is advisable for the ill person to execute a General Power of Attorney by public deed (Poder General por escritura pública) before a Colombian Notary (or special powers of attorney with personal appearance and biometric signature/fingerprint verification) [5]. If your family member has mobility limitations or is hospitalized, you can request mobile notary service (notaría a domicilio) so the notary attends the residence or hospital room in person to verify full mental lucidity and take the biometric signature and fingerprint.
  • Support agreements or Advance Directives (Law 1996 of 2019) and bank requirements: Additionally, an advance directive or formal support agreement (acuerdo de apoyo) for future legal and financial acts can be executed before a notary or authorized conciliation center. Check directly with each Colombian commercial bank (such as Bancolombia, Davivienda, Banco de Bogotá, or BBVA) regarding any internal forms or specific clauses required in a general or special power of attorney to authorize withdrawals, CDT management, and financial transactions without operational holds.

steps.title: Apply for Sick Leave Pay, Disability Pension, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
A serious or advanced illness activates health-related wage replacements, disability pensions, and protected workplace leave in Colombia [3][4]:

  • Temporary sick pay and Disability Pension with Colpensiones or private pension funds (AFP): During the first 180 days of continuous temporary work incapacity, sick pay is covered by the EPS; from day 181 for up to an additional 360 days, while rehabilitation or loss-of-working-capacity assessment proceeds, the pension administrator pays the incapacity subsidy [3]. If the medical assessment issued by the EPS, Colpensiones, the insurer, or the Regional Disability Qualification Boards certifies a loss of working capacity of 50% or more (pérdida de capacidad laboral igual o superior al 50%), an affiliated person who meets the statutory contribution-week requirement is entitled to apply for a Common-Risk Disability Pension (Pensión de Invalidez por riesgo común) with Colpensiones (or with their private pension fund under the Individual Savings Regime), or for a substitute indemnity / balance refund via the electronic portal if minimum weeks were not reached [3][4].
  • Disability Certificate and workplace leave for family caregivers: Apply to the municipal or district health secretariat for multidisciplinary assessment for the official Disability Certificate (Resolution 113 of 2020 and updated regulations of the Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social) [1]. Likewise, working family members caring for a close relative with a terminal illness or severe medical condition are entitled to request paid leave for serious domestic calamity (grave calamidad doméstica) (protected under Article 57(6) of the Substantive Labor Code and Constitutional Court case law) as well as flexible hours or remote-work arrangements for caregivers.

steps.title: Review the Notarial Will, Insurance Beneficiaries, and Property Records in Advance
steps.html:
Organizing the will, insurance policies, and property records in advance prevents succession disputes and simplifies future procedures for the family [4][5]:

  • Open or closed will before a Notary and forced heirship rules (Law 1934 of 2018): Under the Colombian Civil Code (as amended by Law 1934 of 2018), an estate is divided into the compulsory legitimate half (mitad legitimaria - 50%) reserved for forced heirs (legitimarios, such as descendants or ascendants) and the free disposal half (mitad de libre disposición - 50%) that the testator may leave freely to any person. Executing an open will by public deed (testamento abierto por escritura pública) before a notary and three competent witnesses (or a closed will before a notary and five witnesses) while retaining full mental capacity provides complete legal certainty and is registered with the Superintendency of Notaries and Registry (Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro).
  • Life insurance beneficiaries, pension records, and cross-border coordination: Review and update in writing the named beneficiaries on individual or group life insurance policies and mortgage debtor insurance, as life insurance payouts do not enter the probate estate and are paid directly to named beneficiaries. Gather copies of the Civil Registry of Birth and Marriage (or notarial deed/conciliation record declaring a unión marital de hecho), real estate title certificates (certificados de tradición y libertad), and bank records; if assets or family members are located abroad, obtain the online Hague Apostille for Colombian powers of attorney or public deeds through the portal of the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores [5].
