title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Indonesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Indonesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Indonesia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When your family member in Indonesia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, organizing palliative care, medical representation, notarial powers of attorney, social security claims, and testamentary records while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their care preferences and avoids court guardianship delays [1][2][3][4]. Below is our 5-step official checklist.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Care, and BPJS Kesehatan or Private Coverage
steps.html:
In Indonesia, palliative medicine, oncology care, and chronic pain management are integrated into the national referral hospital network overseen by the Kementerian Kesehatan Republik Indonesia (Ministry of Health, Halo Kemenkes call center 1500-567) and financed under the National Health Insurance program [1][2]:

  • Activating JKN coverage through BPJS Kesehatan: Verify that the ill person's BPJS Kesehatan (Care Center 165 and the Mobile JKN application) membership is active and that contributions are up to date [1]. Under the tiered referral pathway (Sistem Rujukan Berjenjang), obtain a referral from the registered primary care facility (Fasilitas Kesehatan Tingkat Pertama - FKTP, such as a Puskesmas or primary clinic) to a regional Type B or Type A referral hospital (such as RSUPN Dr. Cipto Mangunkusumo or Dharmais National Cancer Center in Jakarta, RSUP Prof. Ngoerah in Bali, or RSUD Dr. Soetomo in Surabaya) that operates an integrated multidisciplinary palliative care team (Tim Terpadu Pelayanan Paliatif) [1][2].
  • Hospital-based home care and community palliative support: Many tertiary public and private hospitals in Indonesia operate Hospital Home Care (Pelayanan Kesehatan Rumah) units that provide home visits by palliative doctors and nurses, wound and catheter care, and opioid/analgesic pain management under the clinical palliative guidelines of the Kementerian Kesehatan Republik Indonesia [2].
  • Private health and critical-illness insurance coordination: If your family member also holds private medical or critical-illness coverage (Asuransi Penyakit Kritis), request an official diagnostic summary (Resume Medis) and pathology/imaging reports from the attending specialist to activate cashless hospital guarantees or lump-sum critical-illness payouts [1][2].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
Indonesia regulates medical decision-making, informed consent, and refusal of life-prolonging interventions under the Health Law (Law No. 17 of 2023) and the informed-consent regulations (Persetujuan Tindakan Kedokteran) of the Kementerian Kesehatan Republik Indonesia [2]:

  • Written refusal or limitation of medical interventions (Penolakan Tindakan Medis): While retaining full mental competence, an adult patient in Indonesia has the statutory right to receive a clear medical explanation from the attending physician (Dokter Penanggung Jawab Pelayanan - DPJP) and to sign an official hospital Refusal of Medical Action (Surat Penolakan Tindakan Kedokteran) or Do-Not-Resuscitate (Jangan Lakukan Resusitasi - DNR) directive declining invasive life-support measures such as mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or intensive-care transfer [2]. Note that active euthanasia and physician-assisted suicide are strictly prohibited under Indonesian law, whereas palliative symptom control and withholding or withdrawing futile life-prolonging procedures at the patient's or family's informed request are lawful clinical practice [2].
  • Designating a primary family medical representative (Wali / Keluarga Terdekat): Under Indonesian hospital regulations, if a patient becomes unable to communicate, physicians consult the statutory next of kin (spouse, adult child, parent, or biological sibling) [2]. To prevent disagreement among relatives, the ill person should formally name their designated primary medical spokesperson in the hospital's medical record and sign a witnessed written statement confirming their palliative care preferences before the attending physician and two witnesses [2][3].

steps.title: Execute a Notarial Power of Attorney (Akta Kuasa) and Arrange Bank Mandates
steps.html:
If an adult in Indonesia loses mental capacity without valid financial arrangements in place, family members cannot sell property or access individual bank accounts without petitioning the District Court (Pengadilan Negeri) for a formal Conservatorship / Guardianship Order (Penetapan Pengampuan / Curatele) [3]. Acting while capacity is intact avoids lengthy court proceedings:

  • Executing a Special Notarial Power of Attorney (Akta Kuasa Khusus Notariil): While the ill person is alert and retains full legal capacity (Cakap Hukum), engage a licensed Indonesian Notary (Notaris, supervised under the Ministry of Law and the Direktorat Jenderal Administrasi Hukum Umum) to draft an authentic Notarial Power of Attorney (Akta Kuasa) [3]. If the patient is hospitalized or bedridden, Indonesian Notaries within their appointed regency or municipal jurisdiction can attend the hospital bedside or residence to read and witness the deed [3].
  • Specificity requirement and statutory limits under the Civil Code (KUHPerdata): Under Indonesian law, a general power of attorney covers only routine administrative acts; any mandate to sell or encumber land (before a Land Deed Official / PPAT), operate specific bank accounts, or represent the grantor before government bodies must be drafted as a Special Power of Attorney (Surat Kuasa Khusus) explicitly listing each authorized act and asset [3]. Keep in mind that under Article 1813 of the Indonesian Civil Code (KUHPerdata), a power of attorney terminates by operation of law upon the grantor's formal interdiction/incapacity or death, and Indonesian Supreme Court jurisprudence prohibits irrevocable powers of attorney (Kuasa Mutlak) over land [3].
  • Indonesian bank mandates and joint accounts: Indonesian commercial banks generally require account holders to sign the bank's own internal power-of-attorney form (Surat Kuasa Bank) or verify a Notarial Power of Attorney directly with the branch manager while the account holder is mentally competent [3].

steps.title: Activate BPJS Ketenagakerjaan Disability Benefits and Statutory Sick Leave Protections
steps.html:
Formal-sector and voluntary participants in Indonesia's social security and labor systems can activate substantial income-replacement and medical protections during a serious illness [4][5]:

  • BPJS Ketenagakerjaan Total Permanent Disability and JHT claims: If your family member is registered with BPJS Ketenagakerjaan (Workers Social Security Agency, call center 175) and is medically certified as suffering from a Total Permanent Disability (Cacat Total Tetap) that prevents them from working:
    • Pension Security (Jaminan Pensiun - JP): The participant can claim a monthly Disability Pension (Manfaat Pensiun Cacat) via the nearest branch or the JMO app [4].
    • Old-Age Security (Jaminan Hari Tua - JHT): A participant certified with total permanent disability can withdraw 100% of their accumulated JHT savings balance immediately prior to retirement age [4].
    • Work Injury Security (Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja - JKK): If the critical condition stems from an occupational disease (Penyakit Akibat Kerja) or workplace injury, BPJS Ketenagakerjaan covers unlimited medical treatment according to clinical need along with temporary inability-to-work wage replacement (Santunan Sementara Tidak Mampu Bekerja - SSTMB) and disability lump sums [4].
  • Prolonged employee sick leave pay under the Indonesian Manpower Law: Under Article 93 of the Manpower Law (Law No. 13 of 2003), an employee who is continuously unable to work due to certified illness cannot be summarily dismissed during the first 12 months and is entitled to statutory step-down wage protection: 100% of wages for the first 4 months, 75% for the second 4 months, 50% for the third 4 months, and 25% thereafter until any formal termination with statutory severance pay takes place [4].
  • Family caregiver leave: Under Indonesian labor law, employees are entitled to statutory paid special leave when a spouse, parent, parent-in-law, or child is hospitalized or requires urgent medical attention, and civil servants (ASN/PNS) may apply for Paid Leave for Important Reasons (Cuti Karena Alasan Penting) to care for a critically ill nuclear family member [2][4].

steps.title: Organize Notarial Wills (Akta Wasiat), Civil Records, and Cross-Border Documents
steps.html:
Preparing succession, civil registry, and property documents in advance prevents disputes and account freezes later on [3][5]:

  • Executing a Notarial Will (Akta Wasiat Umum) and registration with Ditjen AHU: To ensure a will is legally indisputable in Indonesia, have it executed as a Public Notarial Will (Akta Wasiat Umum) before a licensed Notary (Notaris) in the presence of two witnesses [3]. By law, the Notary must report the execution of the will no later than the 5th day of the following month to the online Central Will Registry (Daftar Pusat Wasiat) administered by the Direktorat Jenderal Administrasi Hukum Umum (Ditjen AHU, call center 1500-105, under the Ministry of Law / Kemenkumham) [3].
  • Respecting statutory forced-heirship limits (Legitieme Portie and Islamic Law 1/3 cap): When drafting a will in Indonesia, the Notary will ensure compliance with the applicable inheritance regime: under the Compilation of Islamic Law (Kompilasi Hukum Islam) for Muslim citizens, a testamentary bequest (Wasiat) is capped at one-third (1/3) of the net estate unless all legal heirs consent, whereas under the Indonesian Civil Code (KUHPerdata) for non-Muslim citizens, statutory direct heirs (children/descendants and parents) are protected by compulsory reserve shares (Legitieme Portie) [3].
  • Updating BPJS / insurance beneficiaries, Disdukcapil records, and land titles: Verify that the ill person's Family Card (Kartu Keluarga - KK), e-KTP, and marriage/birth certificates match exactly across Disdukcapil and BPJS Ketenagakerjaan records so future survivor claims (Jaminan Kematian - JKM and Jaminan Pensiun) are not delayed by name or NIK discrepancies [4][5]. Gather original land certificates (Sertifikat Hak Milik - SHM or Hak Guna Bangunan - SHGB) and vehicle/bank records. If the ill person holds foreign citizenship (WNA), foreign assets, or family members abroad, remember that any foreign power of attorney or civil record used in Indonesia (or Indonesian notarial deed used abroad) must be legalized with a Hague Apostille through the Direktorat Jenderal Administrasi Hukum Umum (Ditjen AHU) [3].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your situation, in which Indonesian city or province is your family member receiving care, are they an Indonesian citizen (WNI) or a foreign resident (KITAS/KITAP holder), and are they covered by BPJS Kesehatan and BPJS Ketenagakerjaan?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Thailand: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Thailand. Managing a bereavement in Thailand involves sequential medical, civil registration, funeral or repatriation, social security, and judicial probate steps under Thai law. Below is our five-step guide to the official procedures and authorities in practical order.

steps.title: Obtaining Medical Certification of Death and Police or Forensic Clearance in Thailand
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or medical facility: When a person dies in a public or private hospital in Thailand, the attending physician examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1, Bai Rab Rong Kan Tai) [1]. This document states the date, time, place, and medical cause of death in Thai and is the mandatory prerequisite for civil registration [1].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: When an expected or natural death occurs at a private residence outside a hospital, a householder or relative must immediately notify the local village headman (Phu Yai Ban), sub-district headman (Kamnan), or the local police station, together with the municipal or district public health officer, so the death can be inspected and recorded on a non-hospital death notification form before moving the body [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unattended deaths: If the death is sudden, accidental, unexplained, or occurs in a hotel or public place, call the Royal Thai Police at 191 (or the Tourist Police at 1155 and emergency medical services at 1669) immediately and do not disturb the scene [1]. Under the Thai Criminal Procedure Code, an investigating police officer and a forensic physician must conduct a formal post-mortem inquiry (Chanana-sut Phlik Sop), often transferring the body to the Institute of Forensic Medicine at the Police General Hospital in Bangkok or a designated provincial forensic hospital for an autopsy and official police death report before releasing the remains [1].
  • Additional release requirement for foreign nationals: If the deceased held foreign citizenship, Thai hospitals and forensic morgues require an official consular Letter of Release (No-Objection Letter) from the relevant foreign embassy or consulate in Thailand confirming next-of-kin authorization before releasing the body [1][3].

steps.title: Registering the Death with the Civil Registry Authority and Obtaining Official Certificates
steps.html:
• Statutory 24-hour registration deadline: Under the Thai Civil Registration Act, the death must be reported within 24 hours of the time of death (or within 24 hours of discovering the body, extendable up to 7 days in remote areas where transport or forensic clearance takes longer) [1].
  • Where to register: Registration is completed at the local District Office (Amphoe in the provinces) or Bangkok District Office (Khet) oversaw by the Bureau of Registration Administration (BORA) under the Department of Provincial Administration (DOPA, citizen hotline 1548) [1]. If the death occurred in a hospital, the hospital often provides a direct liaison desk or issues the sealed Form Tor.Ror.4/1 for presentation at the District Office covering the place of death [1].
  • Required documents and issuance of Form Tor.Ror.4: Present the Medical Notification of Death (Form Tor.Ror.4/1) or police forensic report, the deceased's Thai national identity card (Bat Prachachon) and house registration book (Tabien Baan, Form Tor.Ror.14) - or the deceased's passport and embassy release letter if the deceased was a foreign national - along with the informant's identification [1]. The District Registrar cancels the deceased's civil status on the house registration record and issues the official Thai Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4, Moranabat) [1]. Request multiple certified copies and ask the District Office for an official English-language extract of the death registration if records will be used internationally [1][2].

steps.title: Arranging Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation and Document Legalization
steps.html:
• Appointing a funeral coordinator and mortuary permits: Once the District Office issues the official Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) and the burial, cremation, or transport permit, the family can arrange final disposition through a licensed funeral provider or directly with a local Buddhist temple (Wat), Christian church, Muslim mosque cemetery, or municipal cemetery in Thailand [1]. Before signing any commercial contract, verify whether the deceased held life, health, or travel assistance insurance that covers funeral or repatriation logistics.
  • Local cremation or burial in Thailand: For a traditional cremation at a Thai temple (Wat), the temple crematory administrator requires the original or certified copy of Form Tor.Ror.4 (and, for a foreign citizen, the embassy Letter of Release) before cremation can proceed [1][3]. After cremation, the temple or crematory issues an official cremation certificate confirming the identity of the cremated remains [3].
  • International repatriation of remains or cremated ashes: If the body or cremated ashes must be transported abroad, an international funeral and repatriation director in Thailand coordinates medical embalming, hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin preparation, quarantine health inspection, and export clearance with the Thai Customs Department at the departure airport (such as Suvarnabhumi Airport Customs Service Sub-Division I at +66 2-134-0490) [3]. Under Thai Customs Department rules, exporting human remains or ashes does not require a commercial Export Declaration Form, but requires originals and two copies of the hospital or police death record, Form Tor.Ror.4, the deceased's passport, the embassy permission letter, the Air Waybill, and the Export Control Document [3].
  • Consular legalization for cross-border use: Because Thailand is not a contracting state to the Hague Apostille Convention, Thai civil status documents (Form Tor.Ror.4) and certified English translations intended for legal use in another country must be authenticated by the Legalization Division of the Department of Consular Affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand in Bangkok (or its regional consular offices in Chiang Mai, Songkhla, Ubon Ratchathani, or Pattaya), followed by super-legalization at the destination country's embassy in Bangkok [2].

steps.title: Notifying Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Institutions in Thailand
steps.html:
• Social Security Office funeral grant and survivor benefits: If the deceased was an insured employee or voluntary contributor under Section 33, Section 39, or Section 40 of the Thai Social Security Act, notify the Social Security Office (SSO, hotline 1506) [4]. Eligible family members and the person who paid for the funeral can claim the statutory lump-sum funeral grant (Kha Tham Sop), the death compensation allowance (Ngoen Songkhro Korani Chara-phap lae Tai), and any lump-sum or survivor old-age pension balance within two years of the death by submitting Form Sor.Por.Sor. 2-01, Form Tor.Ror.4, proof of funeral expenses, and civil relationship records [4].
  • Public health schemes, civil service pensions, and local welfare: For retired civil servants, notify the Comptroller General's Department (CGD) or the Government Pension Fund (GPF) regarding survivor gratuity (Bamnet Tok Thod). If the deceased was an elderly citizen receiving the monthly senior living allowance under the Department of Older Persons or a member of a municipal cremation welfare association (Chapanakit Songkhro), report the death to the local municipal or sub-district administrative organization (Or.Bor.Tor. or Thesaban) to settle benefits and stop ongoing monthly payments [1][4].
  • Banks, insurers, and utility providers: Present the Death Certificate (Form Tor.Ror.4) to Thai commercial banks, life insurance companies, and telecommunications or utility providers [1]. Note that Thai banks immediately freeze sole-name accounts upon notification of death and generally require a formal court probate order (except for very small balances under internal bank indemnity thresholds) before releasing funds to heirs.

steps.title: Estate Administration, Court Probate, and Tax Obligations in Thailand
steps.html:
• Succession under the Thai Civil and Commercial Code: Under Book VI of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code (Sections 1599 to 1755), the deceased's estate devolves upon death to testamentary heirs named in a valid will or, if there is no will, to the six statutory classes of relatives (descendants, parents, full-blood siblings, half-blood siblings, grandparents, and uncles/aunts) alongside the surviving legal spouse.
  • Petitioning the Thai Court for an Estate Administrator order: Unlike jurisdictions where a notary alone can issue a certificate of inheritance, transferring sole-name Thai bank accounts, vehicles (at the Department of Land Transport), corporate shares, or land and condominium title deeds (Chanote at the Department of Lands) almost always requires a judicial probate order. An eligible heir or the named executor retains a licensed Thai attorney to petition the competent Provincial Court or Civil Court for an order appointing an Estate Administrator (Phu Chat Kan Moradok). After a mandatory public notice period and court hearing, the court issues the certificate of final decree empowering the administrator to gather and distribute the estate.
  • Final income tax and Inheritance Tax filings: Under rules enforced by The Revenue Department of Thailand, the estate administrator or heir must file a final Personal Income Tax return (Form P.N.D. 90 or 91) covering income earned by the deceased up to the date of death, as well as reporting undistributed estate income during administration [5]. In addition, under the Inheritance Tax Act B.E. 2558, if any individual heir (other than a legally married surviving spouse, who is fully exempt) receives net taxable assets exceeding 100 million THB from the deceased, that heir must file and pay Inheritance Tax (5 percent for ascendants or descendants; 10 percent for other heirs) with The Revenue Department of Thailand within 150 days of receiving the inheritance [5].
  • Cross-border coordination for foreign heirs or foreign assets: If an heir resides outside Thailand and cannot attend the Thai probate hearing in person, their power of attorney or consent affidavit signed abroad must be notarized and legalized through the Thai Embassy or Consulate in their country of residence and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand [2].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Thailand: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Thailand: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that your family member in Thailand is facing a serious, life-limiting illness and that you want to put clear medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while full decision-making capacity is intact. Taking these steps early ensures that healthcare wishes are respected and prevents administrative or banking freezes later. Below is our five-step guide to the official procedures and institutions in Thailand.

steps.title: Coordinating Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage in Thailand
steps.html:
• Hospital and community palliative care units: Ask the treating specialist at the public or private hospital in Thailand for a formal referral to its multidisciplinary Palliative Care Unit (Sun Kandoo-lae Phu Puai Raya Sut-thai / Cheewabhiban clinic) [1][3]. Under national clinical guidelines issued by the National Health Commission Office and the Ministry of Public Health, hospital palliative teams coordinate symptom control, opioid and pain management, and community home-care visits with local sub-district health promoting hospitals (Ror.Por.Sor.Tor.) [1][3].
  • Activating Universal Coverage, Social Security, or Civil Servant health entitlements: Verify which public or private healthcare scheme covers your family member in Thailand:
    • Universal Coverage Scheme (UCS / Gold Card): Administered by the National Health Security Office (NHSO, 24-hour contact center 1330), the Gold Card program covers inpatient palliative care, home nursing visits, morphine and essential symptom-relief medications, oxygen equipment, and designated hospice or community care beds for eligible Thai citizens [1].
    • Social Security Scheme and Civil Servant Medical Benefit Scheme (CSMBS): Insured private-sector workers covered by the Social Security Office (SSO, hotline 1506) and civil servants or eligible family members covered by the Comptroller General's Department receive palliative and chronic care coverage through their registered contracting hospitals [1][4].
    • Private or international health insurance: If your family member is an expatriate or holds private medical insurance in Thailand, contact the insurer's case management team early to obtain pre-authorization for inpatient palliative care or licensed home nursing services.

steps.title: Recording a Living Will (Advance Directive) and Designating a Healthcare Proxy under Section 12
steps.html:
• Right to make a Living Will under Section 12 of the National Health Act B.E. 2550 (2007): Under Section 12 of the National Health Act and the Ministerial Regulation B.E. 2553 (2010), any person in Thailand who is of sound mind and retains decision-making capacity has the statutory right to execute a written Advance Directive / Living Will (Nangsue Sadaeng Chettana Luang-na) refusing public health services that serve solely to prolong the terminal stage of life or to end severe suffering from an incurable condition [2][3].
  • Palliative care continues while futile life support is withheld: Under guidelines overseen by the National Health Commission Office, executing a Section 12 Living Will never stops pain relief, symptom control, or compassionate palliative care; it only instructs physicians regarding artificial life-prolonging interventions such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), mechanical ventilation, or artificial tube feeding at the end of life [2][3]. Active euthanasia and assisted suicide remain unlawful in Thailand, whereas honoring a patient's valid Section 12 directive is legally protected [2].
  • Appointing a healthcare spokesperson (Phu Sadaeng Chettana Thaen): Within the Section 12 Living Will form, the ill person should name one or two trusted individuals (such as a close relative or partner) as their designated healthcare proxy / spokesperson to clarify their treatment wishes and communicate with the medical team if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [2].
  • How to execute and register (paper and e-Living Will): The directive must be written and signed by the declarant while of sound mind in the presence of witnesses, specifying the declarant's identity details, specific treatment preferences, and witness signatures (a medical certificate confirming sound mind at the time of signing is advisable if serious illness is already present) [2]. Thai citizens can also register their directive digitally via the official e-Living Will platform operated by the National Health Commission Office using ThaID authentication, and a signed copy should always be handed directly to the attending physician and attached to the hospital medical record [2].

steps.title: Executing Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• General and Special Powers of Attorney under the Thai Civil and Commercial Code: Thailand does not have a single statutory "lasting power of attorney" that automatically survives severe mental incapacity without court supervision. While your family member still has full mental and legal capacity (Khwam Samat Thang Kot-mai), they can execute powers of attorney (Nangsue Mob Amnat) under Sections 797 to 832 of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code, witnessed by two witnesses (and certified by a Notarial Services Attorney registered with the Lawyers Council of Thailand if needed for formal or cross-border verification).
  • Thai commercial bank and agency-specific mandates: Thai banks rarely accept a generic private power of attorney for ongoing counter withdrawals once a customer is bedridden. While the account holder is alert and able to sign, contact each Thai bank directly to complete the bank's own official account mandate forms, set up verified digital banking access, or obtain a branch relationship visit at the hospital or home. Similarly, any future transaction involving land or a condominium unit requires the official Department of Lands Power of Attorney form (Form Tor.Dor.21 for land or Form Or.Chor.21 for condominiums) written matching the exact land office wording.
  • Court guardianship (Khwam Anuban) if capacity is lost: If the ill person later loses mental capacity completely, conventional agency mandates can be challenged or suspended under Section 826 of the Civil and Commercial Code. In that situation, a family member must petition the competent Thai Juvenile and Family Court (under Section 28 of the Civil and Commercial Code) to adjudge the person incapacitated and appoint a legal guardian (Phu Anuban) to manage their property and healthcare decisions [2][5].

steps.title: Activating Disability, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits in Thailand
steps.html:
• Social Security Office invalidity benefits (Korani Thuppholaphap): If the ill person is an insured contributor under Section 33 or Section 39 of the Social Security Act and their illness results in severe permanent functional loss, file an invalidity claim with the Social Security Office (SSO, hotline 1506) supported by a medical assessment certificate from a hospital physician [4]. Approved invalidity status provides an ongoing monthly income replacement allowance, continued medical coverage reimbursement, and caregiver support provisions [4].
  • Disability Registration Card and Department of Older Persons welfare: If the illness causes long-term physical or mobility impairment, obtain a medical certificate of disability from a public hospital and register with the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security (MSDHS, 24-hour Social Assistance Center hotline 1300) or the local municipal office to receive a Person with Disabilities ID Card and the monthly disability allowance, alongside senior welfare coordination through the Department of Older Persons (DOP) [5].
  • Community long-term care (Long-Term Care / Care Manager system): For bedridden or home-bound patients (Phu Puai Tit Tiang), contact the local municipality (Thesaban or Or.Bor.Tor.) and the National Health Security Office (1330) to request an assessment by a local Care Manager (CM) and Caregiver (CG) under the NHSO Long-Term Care (LTC) fund, which provides home visits, medical consumables, and practical relief for family caregivers [1][5].

steps.title: Reviewing the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Cross-Border Documents in Thailand
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Thai Will (Phinaikam) while capacity is clear: Review or execute a last will and testament under Book VI of the Thai Civil and Commercial Code (Sections 1646 to 1672). In Thailand, the two most reliable forms are:
    • Ordinary written will (Section 1656): Dated and signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of at least two competent witnesses who sign to certify the testator's signature (beneficiaries and their spouses must never sign as witnesses, or their bequest is void under Section 1653).
    • Public document will at the District Office (Section 1658): Declared before the District Registrar (Nai Amphoe) at the local District Office under the Department of Provincial Administration (1548) in the presence of two witnesses, recorded officially, and kept safely at the District Office.
    • Medical certificate of testamentary capacity: When a person is seriously ill or receiving strong analgesics, ask the attending hospital physician to examine the patient on the day the will is signed and issue a dated medical certificate confirming full mental clarity (Sati Samphachanya Somboon) to prevent any future challenge to the will.
  • Reviewing insurance and pension beneficiary designations: Check named beneficiaries on Thai life insurance policies, Provident Funds (Kong Thun Samrong Liang Chip), Government Pension Fund records, and Social Security Office survivor records so that benefits can be paid directly to the intended recipients [4].
  • Organizing civil records and cross-border legal documents: Gather the ill person's national ID card or passport, house registration (Tabien Baan), marriage and birth certificates, land or condominium title deeds (Chanote), vehicle registration books, and bank passbooks in one secure folder. If the family member holds assets in both Thailand and another country, practitioners generally advise maintaining separate, non-revoking wills for each jurisdiction (ensuring the Thai will explicitly governs only assets located in Thailand and does not accidentally revoke a foreign will) and having any cross-border powers of attorney authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Thailand or the relevant foreign embassy [2].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Liechtenstein: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Liechtenstein: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Liechtenstein: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member. When a death occurs in the Principality of Liechtenstein, medical certification, civil registration, municipal burial or cremation arrangements, social insurance notifications, and judicial probate proceedings follow a structured sequence. Below we explain the five main official steps and competent authorities in Liechtenstein in practical order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death in Liechtenstein
steps.html:
• Death in the National Hospital or a care home: When a patient dies at the Liechtenstein National Hospital (Liechtensteinisches Landesspital) in Vaduz or in a residential care facility of the Liechtenstein Old Age and Sickness Aid (Liechtensteinische Alters- und Krankenhilfe, LAK), the attending physician performs the post-mortem examination (Leichenschau) and issues the official medical death certificate (ärztliche Todesbescheinigung) in accordance with the guidelines of the Office of Public Health (Amt für Gesundheit) [1][3].
  • Natural death at home: If the death occurs in a private residence, immediately contact the family physician (Hausarzt) or the emergency medical service on duty (ärztlicher Notfalldienst, telephone 230 30 30) [1][3]. The deceased person must not be moved or transported before the physician has completed the examination and issued the medical death certificate [1].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained death: In the event of an accident, suicide, unclear cause of death, or discovery of a body without prior medical attendance, notify the National Police (Landespolizei) immediately via emergency number 117 (or +423 236 71 11) [1]. In such cases, the National Police, together with the public health officer at the Office of Public Health (Amt für Gesundheit) and the Public Prosecutor's Office or the Princely Court of Justice (Fürstliches Landgericht), initiates a forensic examination before releasing the body for burial or cremation [1][3][5].

steps.title: Timely Registration with the Civil Registry Office and Issuance of the Death Certificate
steps.html:
• Statutory two-day reporting deadline: Every death occurring in the Principality of Liechtenstein must be reported within two days (48 hours) to the Civil Registry Office of Liechtenstein (Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein) in Vaduz [1][2]. In practice, the medical death certificate is transmitted directly to the Civil Registry Office or handed to the next of kin or appointed funeral director in a sealed envelope for submission [1][2].
  • Documents required for registration: To register the death, the Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein requires the medical death certificate and, particularly for foreign nationals or persons born abroad, official identity documents (passport or identity card), residence permit (Ausländerausweis), and civil status records such as a birth certificate, marriage certificate, or family record book (Familienbüchlein) [1][2].
  • Issuance of the Death Certificate and notice to the municipality: Once recorded in the civil register, the Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein issues the official death certificate (Todesurkunde, available on request as an international multilingual CIEC death extract for cross-border use) [2]. At the same time, the Civil Registry Office automatically prepares the official death notice (Todesfall-Aufnahme) and forwards it to the Liechtenstein municipality of residence for estate inventory preparation as well as to the Princely Court of Justice (Fürstliches Landgericht) [1][5].

steps.title: Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation Within the Legal Framework
steps.html:
• Coordination with the municipality of residence and funeral director: Funerals at a municipal cemetery in Liechtenstein are organized in close coordination between the family, the cemetery or funeral office (Bestattungsamt) of the municipality of residence (such as Vaduz, Schaan, Triesen, Balzers, or Eschen), and a licensed funeral home (Bestattungsunternehmen) [1]. Check beforehand whether the deceased held a private funeral pre-arrangement or travel repatriation insurance.
  • Burial or cremation: Once the civil registry burial permit has been issued, either an earth burial (Erdbestattung) or cremation (Feuerbestattung - which, as Liechtenstein does not operate its own crematory, is regularly carried out at neighboring Swiss crematories such as St. Gallen, Chur, or Rüti) followed by urn interment can take place [1]. Any written disposition wishes left by the deceased during their lifetime take precedence.
  • Corpse transit permit (Leichenpass) and Apostille: If the body is to be repatriated to another country (or transported across the border for cremation), the Office of Public Health (Amt für Gesundheit) issues the international corpse transit permit (Leichenpass) based on the medical death certificate and coffin sealing confirmation [1][3]. Where Liechtenstein death certificates or judicial probate records must be presented in a foreign jurisdiction, the Government Chancellery (Regierungskanzlei) of the Liechtenstein National Administration in Vaduz affixes the Hague Apostille or consular legalization [1][2].

steps.title: Notifying the Liechtensteinische AHV-IV-FAK, Pension Funds, Health Insurers, and Banks
steps.html:
• First-pillar survivor pensions (AHV): Report the death promptly to the Old-Age, Survivors' and Invalidity Insurance Authority (Liechtensteinische AHV-IV-FAK in Vaduz, telephone +423 238 16 16) [4]. Surviving spouses, registered partners, and children of the deceased can submit an application there for a widow's, widower's, or orphan's pension (Verwitwetenrente or Waisenrente) [4]. Ongoing old-age or invalidity pensions paid to the deceased end at the conclusion of the month of death [4].
  • Occupational pension scheme (second pillar) and accident insurance: If your family member was employed or received an occupational pension, notify the relevant Liechtenstein pension fund (Pensionskasse) - and, in the event of an accidental death, the employer's compulsory accident insurer - to claim surviving spouse, partner, or orphan pensions or any lump-sum death benefit (Todesfallkapital) [1][4].
  • Compulsory health insurance (OKP) and banking institutions: Notify the deceased's health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) with a copy of the death certificate so coverage is terminated as of the date of death and any outstanding medical or nursing invoices can be settled [3]. Likewise inform Liechtenstein banks; sole-name accounts are frozen for routine withdrawals until the judicial probate certificate or decree of distribution (Einantwortungsurkunde) is presented, although documented funeral invoices can frequently be paid directly from the account [1][5].

steps.title: Probate Proceedings at the Princely Court of Justice and Cross-Border Estate Administration
steps.html:
• Ex officio initiation of probate proceedings (Verlassenschaftsabhandlung): In Liechtenstein, judicial estate proceedings are conducted ex officio by the Princely Court of Justice (Fürstliches Landgericht) in Vaduz under the General Civil Code (Allgemeines bürgerliches Gesetzbuch, ABGB) and the Non-Contentious Proceedings Act (Ausserstreitgesetz) [1][5]. Once the Civil Registry Office and the municipality of residence transmit the death notice (Todesfall-Aufnahme) and the municipal estate inventory, the Fürstliches Landgericht opens the probate file [1][5].
  • Opening of wills and declaration of acceptance (Erbserklärung): Any original last will and testament (holographic will, witnessed allographic will, public will, or inheritance contract) must be lodged with the Fürstliches Landgericht, where it is formally opened and read (Testamentseröffnung) [5]. Statutory or testamentary heirs then submit their formal declaration of acceptance of inheritance (Erbserklärung), either conditionally with the benefit of inventory (limiting liability for estate debts to the value of the inherited assets) or unconditionally [5].
  • Court certificate, decree of distribution (Einantwortung), and tax rules: Upon completion of the probate proceedings, the Fürstliches Landgericht issues the judicial decree of distribution (Einantwortungsurkunde, or an official certificate of inheritance / Amtsbestätigung for heirs and executors), which transfers legal title to bank balances, securities, and Liechtenstein real estate in the land register [5]. Liechtenstein has abolished inheritance and gift taxes; however, the Tax Administration (Steuerverwaltung) together with the municipality compiles the official tax inventory of the estate and assesses the final pro-rata income and wealth tax return up to the date of death [1].
  • Cross-border estate coordination: Because Liechtenstein, as an EEA member state, is not bound by the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012), international jurisdiction and applicable succession law in Liechtenstein are governed by the Liechtenstein Private International Law Act (IPRG) [5]. If an heir lives abroad or assets are held across multiple countries, early coordination with the judicial officer (Rechtspfleger) at the Fürstliches Landgericht or a Liechtenstein attorney or notary is advisable [5].

de.title: Was tun im Todesfall in Liechtenstein: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste nach einem Todesfall in Liechtenstein: ärztliche Totenbeschau, Beauftragung eines Bestatters, Beurkundung beim Standesamt, Hinterbliebenenrente und Nachlassverfahren.
de.introHtml: Unser aufrichtiges Beileid zum Tod Ihres Familienangehörigen. Bei einem Sterbefall im Fürstentum Liechtenstein greifen ärztliche, zivilstandsamtliche, kommunale, sozialversicherungsrechtliche und gerichtliche Verfahren ineinander. Im Folgenden erläutern wir Ihnen in fünf geordneten Schritten, welche Behörden und Abläufe in Liechtenstein massgeblich sind.

steps.title: Ärztliche Todesfeststellung und Ausstellung der ärztlichen Todesbescheinigung in Liechtenstein
steps.html:
• Todesfall im Landesspital oder in einem Pflegeheim: Versterben Patientinnen oder Patienten im Liechtensteinischen Landesspital in Vaduz oder in einer stationären Pflegeeinrichtung der Liechtensteinischen Alters- und Krankenhilfe (LAK), führt die diensthabende Ärztin oder der diensthabende Arzt die Leichenschau durch und stellt die amtliche ärztliche Todesbescheinigung nach den Vorgaben der Gesundheitsbehörde (Amt für Gesundheit) aus [1][3].
  • Natürlicher Todesfall zu Hause: Tritt der Tod in einer Privatwohnung ein, verständigen Sie umgehend die behandelnde Hausärztin, den Hausarzt oder über den ärztlichen Notfalldienst (Telefon 230 30 30) die diensthabende Notfallärztin bzw. den Notfallarzt [1][3]. Vor der ärztlichen Untersuchung und Ausstellung der Todesbescheinigung darf die verstorbene Person nicht überführt oder umgebettet werden [1].
  • Aussergewöhnlicher, plötzlicher oder ungeklärter Todesfall: Liegt ein Unfall, ein Suizid, eine unklare Todesursache oder ein Auffinden ohne ärztliche Vorgeschichte vor, ist unverzüglich die Landespolizei über den Notruf 117 (oder +423 236 71 11) zu benachrichtigen [1]. In solchen Fällen veranlasst die Landespolizei gemeinsam mit der Amtsärztin oder dem Amtsarzt (Amt für Gesundheit) und der Staatsanwaltschaft bzw. dem Fürstlichen Landgericht die rechtsmedizinische Untersuchung, bevor der Leichnam zur Bestattung freigegeben wird [1][3][5].

steps.title: Fristgerechte Meldung beim Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein und Ausstellung der Todesurkunde
steps.html:
• Gesetzliche Meldefrist von zwei Tagen: Jeder Todesfall im Fürstentum Liechtenstein muss spätestens innerhalb von zwei Tagen (48 Stunden) beim Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein in Vaduz gemeldet werden [1][2]. Der ärztliche Totenschein wird in der Praxis direkt an das Zivilstandsamt übermittelt oder den Angehörigen bzw. dem beauftragten Bestattungsunternehmen in verschlossenem Umschlag zur Vorlage ausgehändigt [1][2].
  • Erforderliche Unterlagen für die Beurkundung: Für die Registrierung benötigt das Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein die ärztliche Todesbescheinigung sowie, insbesondere bei ausländischen Staatsangehörigen oder im Ausland geborenen Personen, die amtlichen Ausweisdokumente (Reisepass oder Identitätskarte), den Ausländerausweis sowie Zivilstandsdokumente wie Geburtsurkunde, Eheschein oder Familienbüchlein [1][2].
  • Ausstellung der Todesurkunde und Weiterleitung an die Wohnsitzgemeinde: Nach der Eintragung im Zivilstandsregister stellt das Zivilstandsamt Liechtenstein die amtliche Todesurkunde (auf Wunsch auch als internationale mehrsprachige CIEC-Todesurkunde für den grenzüberschreitenden Gebrauch) aus [2]. Gleichzeitig erstellt das Zivilstandsamt von Amtes wegen die sogenannte Todesfall-Aufnahme, welche an die zuständige liechtensteinische Wohnsitzgemeinde zur Erstellung des Nachlassinventars sowie an das Fürstliche Landgericht weitergeleitet wird [1][5].

steps.title: Bestattung, Kremation oder internationale Überführung im gesetzlichen Rahmen
steps.html:
• Koordination mit der Wohnsitzgemeinde und dem Bestattungsunternehmen: Die Durchführung der Bestattung auf einem Gemeindefriedhof in Liechtenstein erfolgt in enger Abstimmung zwischen den Angehörigen, dem Friedhofsamt bzw. Bestattungsamt der jeweiligen Wohnsitzgemeinde (beispielsweise Vaduz, Schaan, Triesen, Balzers oder Eschen) und einem zugelassenen Bestattungsunternehmen [1]. Prüfen Sie vorab, ob eine private Bestattungsvorsorge oder eine Reise- bzw. Rücktransportversicherung besteht.
  • Erdbestattung oder Kremation: Nach Vorliegen der zivilstandsamtlichen Bestattungsbewilligung kann eine Erdbestattung oder eine Feuerbestattung (Kremation, die für Liechtenstein mangels eines eigenen Krematoriums regelmässig in benachbarten Schweizer Krematorien wie St. Gallen, Chur oder Rüti durchgeführt wird) mit anschliessender Urnenbeisetzung stattfinden [1]. Sofern die verstorbene Person zu Lebzeiten schriftliche Anordnungen zur Bestattungsart getroffen hat, sind diese massgeblich.
  • Leichenpass für Auslandsüberführungen und Apostille: Soll der Leichnam in ein anderes Land überführt werden (oder erfolgt der Transport zur Kremation ins Ausland), stellt das Amt für Gesundheit auf Grundlage der ärztlichen Todesbescheinigung und der Einsargungsbestätigung den internationalen Leichenpass aus [1][3]. Werden liechtensteinische Todesurkunden oder gerichtliche Nachlassdokumente in einem ausländischen Staat benötigt, versieht die Regierungskanzlei der Liechtensteinischen Landesverwaltung in Vaduz die Dokumente mit der Haager Apostille bzw. der konsularischen Beglaubigung [1][2].

steps.title: Meldung an die Liechtensteinische AHV-IV-FAK, Pensionskassen, Krankenversicherungen und Banken
steps.html:
• Hinterlassenenrenten der 1. Säule (AHV): Melden Sie den Todesfall zeitnah bei der Sozialversicherungsanstalt (Liechtensteinische AHV-IV-FAK in Vaduz, Telefon +423 238 16 16) [4]. Überlebende Ehegattinnen, Ehegatten oder eingetragene Partnerinnen und Partner sowie Kinder der verstorbenen Person können dort den Antrag auf eine Verwitwetenrente bzw. Waisenrente der Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung einreichen [4]. Laufende Alters- oder Invalidenrenten der verstorbenen Person enden mit dem Ende des Sterbemonats [4].
  • Betriebliche Personalvorsorge (2. Säule) und Unfallversicherung: Stand Ihr Familienangehöriger in einem Arbeitsverhältnis oder bezog er eine Rente aus der betrieblichen Personalvorsorge, informieren Sie die zuständige liechtensteinische Pensionskasse (sowie bei einem Unfalltod die obligatorische Unfallversicherung des Arbeitgebers), um Ehegattenrenten, Partnerrenten, Waisenrenten oder ein allfälliges Todesfallkapital geltend zu machen [1][4].
  • Obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung (OKP) und Bankinstitute: Benachrichtigen Sie die Krankenkasse der verstorbenen Person unter Vorlage der Todesurkunde, damit die Versicherung per Todestag abgerechnet und noch offene Krankheits- oder Pflegekostenrechnungen eingereicht werden können [3]. Informieren Sie ebenso die liechtensteinischen Banken; Einzelkonten werden bis zum Vorliegen der gerichtlichen Amtsbestätigung bzw. Einantwortungsurkunde für reguläre Verfügungen gesperrt, wobei begründete Bestattungsrechnungen häufig direkt ab Konto beglichen werden können [1][5].

steps.title: Verlassenschaftsverfahren beim Fürstlichen Landgericht und grenzüberschreitende Nachlassregelung
steps.html:
• Einleitung der Verlassenschaftsabhandlung von Amtes wegen: In Liechtenstein wird das Nachlassverfahren (Verlassenschaftsabhandlung) nach den Bestimmungen des Allgemeinen bürgerlichen Gesetzbuches (ABGB) und des Ausserstreitgesetzes zwingend durch das zuständige Nachlassgericht (Fürstliches Landgericht in Vaduz) geführt [1][5]. Sobald das Zivilstandsamt und die Wohnsitzgemeinde die Todesfall-Aufnahme samt Vermögensinventar übermittelt haben, eröffnet das Fürstliche Landgericht das Verfahren [1][5].
  • Testamentseröffnung und Erbserklärung: Alle vorhandenen letztwilligen Verfügungen (eigenhändiges Testament, fremdhändiges Testament, öffentliches Testament oder Erbvertrag) müssen im Original beim Fürstlichen Landgericht eingereicht werden, wo sie offiziell kundgemacht (eröffnet) werden [5]. Die gesetzlichen oder testamentarischen Erben geben im Verfahren ihre bedingte (mit Rechtswohltat des Inventars zur Haftungsbeschränkung auf den Nachlasswert) oder unbedingte Erbserklärung ab [5].
  • Amtsbestätigung, Einantwortung und Steuerrecht: Nach Abschluss der Abhandlung erlässt das Fürstliche Landgericht die gerichtliche Einantwortungsurkunde (bzw. stellt einen Erbschein oder eine Amtsbestätigung für Erben und Testamentsvollstrecker aus), mit der das Eigentum an Bankguthaben, Wertschriften und liechtensteinischen Grundstücken im Grundbuch endgültig auf die Erben übergeht [5]. Im liechtensteinischen Steuerrecht wurde die Erbschafts- und Schenkungssteuer abgeschafft; die Steuerverwaltung erstellt jedoch gemeinsam mit der Gemeinde das amtliche Nachlassinventar und veranlagt die unterjährige Schlusssteuererklärung bis zum Todestag [1].
  • Grenzüberschreitende Koordination bei Auslandsbezug: Da Liechtenstein als EWR-Mitgliedstaat nicht an die Europäische Erbrechtsverordnung (EU-ErbVO Nr. 650/2012) gebunden ist, richtet sich die internationale Zuständigkeit und das anwendbare Erbrecht in Liechtenstein nach dem liechtensteinischen Gesetz über das internationale Privatrecht (IPRG) [5]. Wohnt ein Erbe im Ausland oder befinden sich Vermögenswerte in mehreren Staaten, empfiehlt sich eine frühzeitige Abstimmung mit dem Rechtspfleger am Fürstlichen Landgericht oder einem liechtensteinischen Rechtsanwalt bzw. Notar [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Liechtenstein: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Liechtenstein: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Liechtenstein: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When your family member in Liechtenstein is facing a serious or life-limiting illness, putting early medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place provides security for everyone involved. While the ill person retains full mental capacity and legal judgment, treatment preferences, representation powers, and care benefits can be organized on a self-determined basis. Below we set out the five main official steps in the Principality of Liechtenstein in practical order.

steps.title: Coordinating Palliative Care, Spitex Home Nursing, and Health Insurance in Liechtenstein
steps.html:
• Outpatient palliative care and Spitex home nursing: Contact the treating physician early as well as the non-profit home care organization Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. (telephone +423 236 00 66), which provides outpatient nursing, oncology care, and specialized mobile palliative care at home across all eleven Liechtenstein municipalities [1][6]. In addition, the Liechtenstein National Hospital (Liechtensteinisches Landesspital) in Vaduz, the Liechtenstein Old Age and Sickness Aid (Liechtensteinische Alters- und Krankenhilfe, LAK), and the Hospice Movement Liechtenstein (Hospizbewegung Liechtenstein) offer inpatient and supportive palliative services [1].
  • Coverage under compulsory health care insurance (OKP): Coordinate with the ill person's Liechtenstein health insurance fund (Krankenkasse, supervised by the Office of Public Health, Amt für Gesundheit) regarding physician-prescribed home nursing care (Spitex), pain management therapy, medical aids, and hospital beds for home use [1][6]. Medically prescribed nursing services delivered by recognized providers such as Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. are reimbursed under the compulsory health insurance scheme [1][6].

steps.title: Written Advance Healthcare Directive and Medical Proxy Under the Patient Directive Act
steps.html:
• Binding and noteworthy advance directives under the PatVG: Under the Liechtenstein Patient Directive Act (Patientenverfügungsgesetz, PatVG), any person capable of insight and judgment can specify in writing which medical measures (such as mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, or artificial nutrition and hydration) they refuse in the event that they later lose decision-making capacity [1][2].
  • Formal requirements for a legally binding directive (verbindliche Patientenverfügung): For an advance directive in Liechtenstein to be directly binding in the strict statutory sense, the ill person must receive comprehensive medical information from a physician who certifies in writing that the declarant possesses full insight and judgment and accurately understands the medical consequences of the directive [2]. In addition, a binding advance directive must be executed with the date before an attorney, a notary, or a legally trained advisor of a recognized patient organization, and remains valid for up to eight years (or indefinitely if the declarant loses decision-making capacity in the meantime) [2]. Even a written and dated advance directive executed without those heightened formalities (beachtliche Patientenverfügung) must still be taken into account by the medical team when determining the patient's presumed will [2].
  • Designating a trusted person (Vertrauensperson) for medical decisions: In the advance directive, explicitly name one or two trusted representatives (plus an alternate) authorized to receive medical information from physicians, inspect medical records, and represent the ill person's wishes if they can no longer communicate [2]. Provide copies to the family physician, the National Hospital, and Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. [1][2][6].

steps.title: Continuing Power of Attorney, Bank Mandates, and Adult Protection at the Princely Court of Justice
steps.html:
• Executing a continuing power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht) under § 284f ABGB: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they can execute a continuing power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht) under the guardianship and adult protection provisions of the Liechtenstein General Civil Code (ABGB) [3][5]. This instrument specifies which trusted person is authorized to represent the ill person in personal care matters, nursing arrangements, and financial or property administration if legal or mental capacity is subsequently lost [3].
  • Formal requirements and registration at the Princely Court of Justice: A continuing power of attorney must either be written and signed entirely by hand by the grantor or signed before three independent witnesses; however, if it covers serious personal care interventions, permanent dissolution of the household, or extraordinary property transactions, it must be executed before a Liechtenstein attorney, a notary, or directly before the Princely Court of Justice (Fürstliches Landgericht) in Vaduz [3][5]. The activation of the continuing power of attorney (supported by a medical certificate confirming loss of capacity) can be registered with the Fürstliches Landgericht, thereby avoiding the need for a court-appointed guardian (Sachwalter) [3][5].
  • Separate bank powers of attorney at Liechtenstein banks: Because financial institutions in Liechtenstein regularly require their own internal mandate forms for ongoing account management, the ill person should also sign an unrestricted bank power of attorney directly at each Liechtenstein bank on the bank's official forms, valid across incapacity and beyond death.

steps.title: Care Allowance, Helplessness Allowance, Invalidity Benefits, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Care and attendance allowance (Betreuungs- und Pflegegeld, BPG) for home care: If the ill person requires regular assistance and care at home, an application can be submitted for the Liechtenstein Care and Attendance Allowance (Betreuungs- und Pflegegeld) [1][4]. An on-site needs assessment determines the applicable care tier to financially support home care provided by family members or recognized services such as Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. [1][6].
  • Invalidity Insurance (IV) benefits and helplessness allowance (Hilflosenentschädigung): For persons of working age, the Old-Age, Survivors' and Invalidity Insurance Authority (Liechtensteinische AHV-IV-FAK in Vaduz, telephone +423 238 16 16) assesses entitlement to an invalidity pension, medical aids, and a helplessness allowance (Hilflosenentschädigung) if the ill person permanently requires third-party assistance for everyday living activities or continuous personal supervision [4]. Persons of retirement age may also qualify for helplessness and care-related support through the AHV/IV and supplementary benefits system (Ergänzungsleistungen) [4].
  • Respite services and counseling for family caregivers: Make use of the nursing counseling offered by Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V., the municipal home care coordination office, and respite care options (such as day-care structures or short-term residential care beds at the LAK) to support caregiving relatives early [1][6].

steps.title: Early Organization of Wills, Beneficiary Designations, and Estate Records in Liechtenstein
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Will or inheritance contract under Liechtenstein law (ABGB): While full testamentary capacity is intact, your family member should review or execute a last will and testament [5]. Under the Liechtenstein General Civil Code (ABGB), a will can be written, dated, and signed entirely by hand by the testator (eigenhändiges Testament), signed in the simultaneous presence of three capable, independent witnesses (fremdhändiges Testament), or executed before a court or notary [5]. When a person is seriously ill or receiving strong pain medication, it is advisable to obtain a contemporaneous medical certificate confirming full mental and testamentary capacity and to deposit the original will officially with the Princely Court of Justice (Fürstliches Landgericht) in Vaduz [5].
  • Beneficiary designations for occupational pension funds (second pillar) and insurance: Because death benefits and lump-sum capital from occupational pension schemes (Pensionskassen, second pillar) and private life insurance policies pass according to statutory and plan-specific beneficiary rules, the ill person should check and file written beneficiary designations with their pension fund and insurers [4].
  • Document folder and cross-border estate coordination: Assemble civil status certificates, land register extracts, bank and custody account statements, insurance policies, and digital access credentials in one secure folder. If the ill person holds assets abroad or if future heirs reside outside Liechtenstein, consult a Liechtenstein attorney or notary on whether to include an explicit choice-of-law clause in the will under the Liechtenstein Private International Law Act (IPRG) [5].

closingQuestion: Is your family member currently receiving care at home in a Liechtenstein municipality or as an inpatient at the hospital, and do they already have a written advance directive (Patientenverfügung) or continuing power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht)?

de.title: Vorsorge & Administration bei schwerer Erkrankung in Liechtenstein: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste
de.cardSummary: Offizielle 5-Schritte-Checkliste bei lebensverkürzender Erkrankung in Liechtenstein: Palliativ- und Hospizversorgung, Patientenverfügung, Vorsorgevollmacht, Pflegezeit und Nachlassordnung.
de.introHtml: Wenn Ihr Familienangehöriger in Liechtenstein mit einer schweren oder lebensverkürzenden Erkrankung konfrontiert ist, schaffen frühzeitige medizinische, rechtliche und finanzielle Vorkehrungen Sicherheit für alle Beteiligten. Solange die erkrankte Person voll urteils- und handlungsfähig ist, lassen sich Behandlungswünsche, Vertretungsbefugnisse und Pflegeleistungen selbstbestimmt regeln. Im Folgenden zeigen wir Ihnen die fünf wichtigsten Schritte im Fürstentum Liechtenstein der Reihe nach auf.

steps.title: Organisation der Palliativversorgung, Spitex-Hauskrankenpflege und Krankenversicherung in Liechtenstein
steps.html:
• Ambulante Palliativpflege und Spitex zu Hause: Wenden Sie sich frühzeitig an die behandelnde Ärztin oder den behandelnden Arzt sowie an die gemeinnützige Spitex-Organisation Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. (Telefon +423 236 00 66), die in allen elf liechtensteinischen Gemeinden die ambulante Krankenpflege, onkologische Pflege und spezialisierte mobile Palliativpflege zu Hause sicherstellt [1][6]. Ergänzend bieten das Liechtensteinische Landesspital in Vaduz, die Liechtensteinische Alters- und Krankenhilfe (LAK) sowie der Verein Hospizbewegung Liechtenstein stationäre und begleitende Palliativangebote an [1].
  • Kostenübernahme durch die obligatorische Krankenpflegeversicherung (OKP): Klären Sie mit der liechtensteinischen Krankenkasse der erkrankten Person (unter Aufsicht durch das Amt für Gesundheit) die ärztlich verordneten Leistungen der häuslichen Krankenpflege (Spitex), der Schmerztherapie sowie der medizinischen Hilfsmittel und Pflegebetten ab [1][6]. Ärztlich verordnete Pflegeleistungen durch zugelassene Leistungserbringer wie die Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. werden im Rahmen der obligatorischen Krankenpflegeversicherung abgerechnet [1][6].

steps.title: Schriftliche Patientenverfügung und medizinische Vertretung nach dem Patientenverfügungsgesetz
steps.html:
• Verbindliche und beachtliche Patientenverfügung nach dem PatVG: Nach dem liechtensteinischen Gesetz über die Patientenverfügung (Patientenverfügungsgesetz, PatVG) kann jede einsichts- und urteilsfähige Person schriftlich festlegen, welche medizinischen Massnahmen (beispielsweise künstliche Beatmung, Reanimation oder künstliche Ernährung und Flüssigkeitszufuhr) sie im Fall einer späteren Entscheidungsunfähigkeit ablehnt [1][2].
  • Formvorschriften für eine verbindliche Patientenverfügung: Damit eine Patientenverfügung in Liechtenstein im Rechtssinne unmittelbar verbindlich ist, muss die erkrankte Person ausführlich durch eine Ärztin oder einen Arzt aufgeklärt werden, welcher bestätigt, dass die Person einsichts- und urteilsfähig ist und die medizinischen Folgen ihrer Verfügung zutreffend einschätzt [2]. Zudem muss die verbindliche Patientenverfügung unter Angabe des Datums vor einer Rechtsanwältin, einem Rechtsanwalt, einer Notarin, einem Notar oder einer rechtskundigen Mitarbeiterin einer Patientenorganisation errichtet werden und ist bis zu acht Jahre gültig (bzw. bleibt dauerhaft gültig, wenn die Person zwischenzeitlich die Einsichts- und Urteilsfähigkeit verliert) [2]. Auch eine ohne diese strengen Formalitäten schriftlich und datiert verfasste («beachtliche») Patientenverfügung muss vom Behandlungsteam bei der Ermittlung des Patientenwillens berücksichtigt werden [2].
  • Benennung einer Vertrauensperson für medizinische Entscheidungen: Bestimmen Sie in der Patientenverfügung ausdrücklich eine oder zwei Vertrauenspersonen (sowie eine Ersatzperson), die gegenüber den Ärztinnen und Ärzten Auskunft erhalten, Einsicht in die Krankengeschichte nehmen und den mutmasslichen Willen der erkrankten Person vertreten dürfen [2]. Übergeben Sie Kopien an die Hausärztin bzw. den Hausarzt, das Landesspital und die Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. [1][2][6].

steps.title: Vorsorgevollmacht, Bankvollmachten und Erwachsenenschutz beim Fürstlichen Landgericht
steps.html:
• Errichtung einer Vorsorgevollmacht nach dem Sachwalterrecht (§ 284f ABGB): Solange Ihr Familienangehöriger voll geschäfts- und handlungsfähig ist, kann er nach dem liechtensteinischen Sachwalterrecht im Allgemeinen bürgerlichen Gesetzbuch (ABGB) eine Vorsorgevollmacht errichten [3][5]. Darin wird festgelegt, welche Vertrauensperson die erkrankte Person in persönlichen Angelegenheiten, bei der Pflegeorganisation sowie in Vermögens- und Verwaltungsfragen vertreten soll, falls später die Geschäfts-, Einsichts- oder Urteilsfähigkeit verloren geht [3].
  • Formvorschriften und Registrierung beim Fürstlichen Landgericht: Eine Vorsorgevollmacht muss entweder eigenhändig geschrieben und unterschrieben oder vor drei unbefangenen Zeugen unterzeichnet werden; umfasst sie jedoch schwerwiegende persönliche Entscheidungen, dauerhafte Wohnungsauflösungen oder ausserordentliche Vermögensgeschäfte, muss sie vor einer Rechtsanwältin, einem Rechtsanwalt, einer Notarin, einem Notar oder direkt vor dem zuständigen Gericht (Fürstliches Landgericht in Vaduz) errichtet werden [3][5]. Das Wirksamwerden der Vorsorgevollmacht (unter Vorlage eines ärztlichen Zeugnisses) kann beim Fürstlichen Landgericht registriert werden, sodass die Bestellung eines gerichtlichen Sachwalters vermieden wird [3][5].
  • Separate Bankvollmachten bei liechtensteinischen Banken: Da Finanzinstitute in Liechtenstein im laufenden Zahlungsverkehr häufig ihre eigenen bankinternen Vollmachtsformulare verlangen, sollte die erkrankte Person zusätzlich bei jeder liechtensteinischen Bank direkt eine unbeschränkte Bankvollmacht (über den Eintritt einer Urteilsunfähigkeit und idealerweise über den Tod hinaus) auf den bankeigenen Formularen unterzeichnen.

steps.title: Pflegegeld, Hilflosenentschädigung, IV-Leistungen und Entlastung für pflegende Angehörige
steps.html:
• Betreuungs- und Pflegegeld (BPG) für die häusliche Pflege: Benötigt die erkrankte Person zu Hause regelmässige Hilfe und Betreuung, kann ein Antrag auf das liechtensteinische Betreuungs- und Pflegegeld gestellt werden [1][4]. Die Bedarfsabklärung vor Ort (Einstufung in die Pflegestufen) wird im Auftrag des Landes durch Fachpersonen durchgeführt, um die Pflege durch Angehörige oder anerkannte Dienste wie die Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V. finanziell zu unterstützen [1][6].
  • Leistungen der Invalidenversicherung (IV) und Hilflosenentschädigung: Bei Personen im Erwerbsalter prüft die Sozialversicherungsanstalt (Liechtensteinische AHV-IV-FAK in Vaduz, Telefon +423 238 16 16) den Anspruch auf eine Invalidenrente, Hilfsmittel der IV sowie eine Hilflosenentschädigung, falls die erkrankte Person für alltägliche Lebensverrichtungen dauernd auf Dritthilfe oder persönliche Überwachung angewiesen ist [4]. Auch im Rentenalter bestehen ergänzende Leistungsansprüche bei Hilflosigkeit und Pflegebedarf über das System der AHV/IV und der Ergänzungsleistungen [4].
  • Entlastungsangebote und Beratung für pflegende Angehörige: Nutzen Sie die Pflegeberatung der Familienhilfe Liechtenstein e.V., die Fachstelle für häusliche Betreuung und Pflege sowie Entlastungsdienste (wie Tagesstrukturen oder Kurzzeitpflegeplätze bei der LAK), um eine Überlastung der betreuenden Familienmitglieder frühzeitig aufzufangen [1][6].

steps.title: Frühzeitige Ordnung von Testament, Begünstigtenregelungen und Dokumenten in Liechtenstein
steps.html:
• Formgültiges Testament oder Erbvertrag nach liechtensteinischem Erbrecht (ABGB): Solange die volle Testierfähigkeit besteht, sollte Ihr Familienangehöriger prüfen, ob ein gültiges Testament vorliegt [5]. Nach dem liechtensteinischen Allgemeinen bürgerlichen Gesetzbuch (ABGB) kann ein Testament entweder vollständig eigenhändig geschrieben, datiert und unterschrieben (holographes Testament) oder fremdhändig unter gleichzeitiger Beiziehung von drei fähigen, unbefangenen Zeugen (allographes Testament) bzw. gerichtlich/notariell errichtet werden [5]. Bei schwerer Erkrankung oder hochdosierter Schmerzmedikation ist es ratsam, zeitgleich ein ärztliches Attest über die volle Urteils- und Testierfähigkeit ausstellen zu lassen und das Testament beim Fürstlichen Landgericht in Vaduz amtlich zu hinterlegen [5].
  • Begünstigtenordnung bei Pensionskassen (2. Säule) und Versicherungen: Da Guthaben und Todesfallkapitalien aus der betrieblichen Personalvorsorge (2. Säule) sowie aus privaten Lebensversicherungen eigenen Begünstigtenregeln folgen, sollte die erkrankte Person bei ihrer Pensionskasse und ihren Versicherungen prüfen und schriftlich festlegen, welche Angehörigen im Leistungsfall begünstigt sind [4].
  • Dokumentenmappe und grenzüberschreitende Nachlasskoordination: Stellen Sie Zivilstandsurkunden, Grundbuchauszüge, Bank- und Depotübersichten, Versicherungspolicen sowie Passwörter geordnet zusammen. Besitzt die erkrankte Person Vermögenswerte im Ausland oder wohnen künftige Erben ausserhalb Liechtensteins, sollte mit einem liechtensteinischen Rechtsanwalt oder Notar geprüft werden, ob im Testament eine ausdrückliche Rechtswahl nach dem liechtensteinischen Gesetz über das internationale Privatrecht (IPRG) getroffen werden soll [5].
