title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Monaco: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Monaco: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Monaco: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in the Principality of Monaco. When a death occurs in Monaco, medical certification, civil registration at the Town Hall, funeral or repatriation arrangements, social security notifications, and notarial estate administration follow a structured sequence under Monegasque law. Below is our five-step guide to completing these official procedures with the competent authorities.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death in Monaco
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or residential care facility: When a death occurs at the Princess Grace Hospital Centre (Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace, CHPG) or in a public residential care facility in the Principality (such as Résidence du Cap Fleuri or Résidence A Qietüdine), the hospital physician performs the clinical examination and issues the official medical death certificate (certificat médical de décès) [1][2]. The facility generally transmits the required documentation or hands the certificate to the family and the appointed funeral director [1][2].
  • Natural death at home: If the death occurs at a private residence in Monaco, immediately call the attending physician or the emergency medical services (Monaco Fire and Emergency Service at 18 or 112, or the mobile emergency unit of the Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace) so a licensed physician can certify the death and draw up the medical death certificate [1][2]. The body of the deceased must not be moved before this medical certification is completed [1].
  • Suspicious, accidental, or public-place death: In the event of a violent, sudden, or unexplained death or a death occurring in a public place, notify the Police Department (Direction de la Sûreté Publique, telephone 17 or +377 93 15 30 15) immediately [1][5]. Under the Monegasque Civil Code (published on the official legal portal LégiMonaco) and the Code of Criminal Procedure, a judicial police officer assisted by a forensic physician conducts a formal inquiry, and burial or transport of the body requires prior authorization from the Public Prosecutor General (Parquet Général) [1][5].

steps.title: Registering the Death at the Mairie de Monaco and Obtaining Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Competent authority and reporting timeframe: Every death occurring within the territory of Monaco must be declared promptly (in practice within 24 hours excluding weekends and public holidays, and strictly before any funeral operation) at the Civil Registry Department (Service de l'État Civil) of the Mairie de Monaco (Place de la Mairie, telephone +377 93 15 28 51) [1][2].
  • Authorized declarants and required documents: The declaration is made by a relative, an authorized representative, or, most commonly, the licensed funeral director appointed by the family [1][2]. Present to the Mairie de Monaco the medical death certificate, the declarant's identification, and the deceased person's identity and civil status records (Monegasque identity card, resident permit, passport, family record book / livret de famille, or birth and marriage certificates) [1][2].
  • Issuance of official Death Certificates (actes de décès): The civil registry officer at the Mairie de Monaco records the death and immediately issues full certified copies of the death certificate (copies intégrales de l'acte de décès) [1][2]. Additional certified copies can subsequently be requested free of charge in person, by mail, or online through the official public service portal of the Gouvernement Princier de Monaco (MonServicePublic / MonGuichet.mc) [1][2]. If the deceased was a foreign citizen, also notify their home country's consulate or embassy so the death can be recorded in their national civil registry.

steps.title: Organizing the Funeral, Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Funeral service providers in Monaco: After checking whether the deceased held a pre-paid funeral contract or travel repatriation insurance, the family coordinates funeral arrangements with the Principality's funeral operator (Société Monégasque de Thanatologie / Pompes Funèbres de Monaco), working closely with the Civil Registry Department and the Municipal Domain Department of the Mairie de Monaco [1][2].
  • Burial or cremation and municipal permits: The Mairie de Monaco issues the burial permit (permis d'inhumer) or the coffin-closing and cremation permit upon presentation of the death certificate and the medical certificate confirming no medico-legal impediment (as well as confirmation that any battery-powered pacemaker or prosthesis has been removed) [1][2]. Burials take place at the Cemetery of Monaco, while cremations are carried out at the crematory in Nice or neighboring French municipalities under Franco-Monegasque agreements, followed by placement of the urn in a columbarium niche, a family vault, or scattering of ashes at the Garden of Remembrance [2].
  • International repatriation of remains and Apostille: If the body or cremated ashes must be repatriated to another country, the health and interior authorities of the Gouvernement Princier de Monaco (Direction de l'Action Sanitaire and Département de l'Intérieur) issue the international corpse transit permit (laissez-passer mortuaire) once the remains are sealed in a hermetic coffin [1]. Where a Monegasque death certificate must be used legally abroad, the Hague Apostille is issued free of charge by the Directorate of Judicial Services (Direction des Services Judiciaires) at the Palais de Justice in Monaco [1][5].

steps.title: Notifying the Caisses Sociales de Monaco, Pension Funds, Banks, and Insurers
steps.html:
• Lump-sum death grant (capital décès) and medical reimbursements: If the deceased was an employee or retiree covered under the Monegasque general social security system, report the death to the Caisses Sociales de Monaco (CSM - Caisse de Compensation des Services Sociaux, telephone +377 93 15 43 43) [3]. Subject to contribution eligibility rules, priority dependents (unseparated surviving spouse, dependent children, or dependent ascendants) can claim the lump-sum death benefit (capital décès) as well as reimbursement of final medical expenses [3]. If the deceased was a self-employed worker insured with CAMTI/CARTI or a civil servant covered by the State Medical Benefits Office (SPME), submit the death certificate to the respective fund [1][3].
  • Survivor pensions from the Autonomous Pension Fund (CAR): For an insured private-sector employee or pensioner in Monaco, submit an application for a survivor's pension (pension de réversion for a surviving spouse or orphan's pension) and check eligibility for social allowances with the Autonomous Pension Fund (Caisse Autonome des Retraites) administered by the Caisses Sociales de Monaco [4].
  • Monegasque banks, life insurers, and employer: Provide a certified copy of the death certificate to the employer, life insurance companies, and banking institutions in Monaco [1]. Upon receiving notice of death, Monegasque banks freeze sole-name accounts held by the deceased (while generally allowing direct payment of funeral bills upon presentation of the official funeral home invoice) until the notarial succession instruments are presented [5].

steps.title: Opening and Settling the Estate Before a Notary in Monaco and Cross-Border Coordination
steps.html:
• Estate settlement through a Monegasque notary: Under the Monegasque Civil Code published on LégiMonaco, settling an estate opened in the Principality of Monaco (particularly where there is a will, real estate, substantial bank or custody accounts, or multiple heirs) is handled through one of the notarial offices (études de notaires) in Monaco [5]. The notary searches for any last will and testament (holographic, public/authentic, or mystic will), completes the formal opening of the will, draws up the deed of heirship (acte de notoriété) confirming the legal heirs, prepares the estate inventory, and drafts the distribution deeds [5].
  • Favorable inheritance tax regime in Monaco: In the Principality of Monaco, inheritance tax (droits de mutation par décès) applies only to assets located in Monaco (or having their legal situs in Monaco) and depends solely on the degree of kinship between the deceased and the heir: the rate is 0 percent (full exemption) in the direct line (between parents and children or grandparents and grandchildren) and between spouses [5]. Tax rates are 8 percent between siblings, 10 percent between uncles/aunts and nephews/nieces, 13 percent between other collateral relatives, and 16 percent between unrelated persons. The estate tax declaration must be filed with the Directorate of Tax Services (Direction des Services Fiscaux) of the Gouvernement Princier de Monaco within six months of death (or twelve months if the death occurred outside Europe) [1][5].
  • International coordination (Law No. 1.448 on Private International Law): Because Monaco is not a member of the European Union, cross-border successions in Monaco are governed by the Monegasque Code of Private International Law (Law No. 1.448), which in principle subjects the entire estate to the law of the state of the deceased's last domicile, unless the deceased made an explicit choice of their national law (professio juris) in a valid will [5]. Where heirs reside abroad or real estate or financial assets are held in France or another jurisdiction, the Monegasque notary coordinates tax filings and inheritance certificates with foreign notaries [5].

fr.title: Que faire lors d'un décès en Monaco : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes après un décès en Monaco : certificat médical de décès, choix des pompes funèbres, déclaration à l'état civil, capital décès et pensions de réversion, et règlement de la succession.
fr.introHtml: Nous vous présentons nos sincères condoléances pour le décès de votre proche en Principauté de Monaco. Lorsqu'un décès survient à Monaco, les démarches médicales, la déclaration d'état civil, l'organisation des obsèques, les notifications aux organismes sociaux et le règlement successoral suivent un ordre précis encadré par le droit monégasque. Voici notre guide en cinq étapes pour accomplir ces formalités auprès des autorités compétentes.

steps.title: Constatation médicale du décès et délivrance du certificat médical de décès à Monaco
steps.html:
• Décès en établissement hospitalier ou en maison de retraite : Lorsque le décès survient au Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace (CHPG) ou dans un établissement médico-social de la Principauté (tel que la Résidence du Cap Fleuri ou la Résidence A Qietüdine), le médecin hospitalier procède au constat clinique et établit le certificat médical de décès officiel [1][2]. L'établissement se charge généralement de transmettre directement les éléments nécessaires ou de remettre le certificat à la famille et à l'opérateur funéraire [1][2].
  • Décès naturel à domicile : Si la personne décède à son domicile privé à Monaco, appelez immédiatement le médecin traitant ou les secours médicaux d'urgence (Sapeurs-Pompiers de Monaco au 18 ou le 112, ou le SMUR du Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace) afin qu'un médecin habilité constate le décès et rédige le certificat médical de décès [1][2]. Le corps de la personne décédée ne doit pas être déplacé avant l'établissement de ce constat médical [1].
  • Décès suspect, accidentel ou sur la voie publique : En cas de mort violente, soudaine, inexpliquée ou survenue dans un lieu public, prévenez immédiatement la Direction de la Sûreté Publique (Police de Monaco au 17 ou +377 93 15 30 15) [1][5]. Conformément aux dispositions du Code civil monégasque (publié sur le portail officiel LégiMonaco) et du Code de procédure pénale, un officier de police judiciaire assisté d'un médecin légiste procède aux constatations légales, et l'inhumation ou le transport du corps est subordonné à l'autorisation du Parquet Général (Procureur Général) [1][5].

steps.title: Déclaration du décès à la Mairie de Monaco et obtention des actes de décès
steps.html:
• Autorité compétente et délai de déclaration : Tout décès survenu sur le territoire monégasque doit être déclaré rapidement (en pratique dans les 24 heures hors week-ends et jours fériés, et impérativement avant toute opération funéraire) auprès du Service de l'État Civil de la Mairie de Monaco (Place de la Mairie, téléphone +377 93 15 28 51) [1][2].
  • Personnes habilitées et pièces justificatives : La déclaration est effectuée par un membre de la famille, par un mandataire ou, le plus souvent, par la société de pompes funèbres mandatée par les proches [1][2]. Il convient de présenter à la Mairie de Monaco le certificat médical de décès, une pièce d'identité du déclarant ainsi que les documents d'état civil et d'identité de la personne décédée (carte d'identité monégasque, carte de séjour de résident, passeport, livret de famille ou acte de naissance/mariage) [1][2].
  • Délivrance des actes de décès officiels : L'officier de l'état civil de la Mairie de Monaco dresse l'acte de décès et délivre immédiatement des copies intégrales de l'acte de décès [1][2]. Des exemplaires supplémentaires peuvent ensuite être demandés gratuitement sur place, par courrier ou via le téléservice officiel du Gouvernement Princier de Monaco (portail MonServicePublic / MonGuichet.mc) [1][2]. Si la personne décédée était de nationalité étrangère, informez également son consulat ou son ambassade compétente pour la transcription consulaire du décès.

steps.title: Organisation des obsèques, inhumation, crémation ou rapatriement international
steps.html:
• Recours aux pompes funèbres à Monaco : Après avoir vérifié si la personne décédée disposait d'un contrat d'assurance obsèques ou d'une assurance rapatriement, la famille organise les funérailles avec l'opérateur funéraire de la Principauté (Société Monégasque de Thanatologie / Pompes Funèbres de Monaco), en coordination avec le Service de l'État Civil et le Service du Domaine Communal de la Mairie de Monaco [1][2].
  • Inhumation ou crémation et autorisations municipales : La Mairie de Monaco délivre le permis d'inhumer ou l'autorisation de fermeture du cercueil et de crémation sur présentation de l'acte de décès et du certificat médical attestant l'absence d'obstacle médico-légal (ainsi que le retrait éventuel de toute prothèse fonctionnant au moyen d'une pile) [1][2]. L'inhumation a lieu au Cimetière de Monaco, tandis que la crémation est effectuée au crématorium de Nice ou des communes limitrophes en vertu des accords franco-monégasques, suivie du dépôt de l'urne au columbarium, dans une sépulture familiale ou de la dispersion des cendres au Jardin du Souvenir [2].
  • Transport international de corps et apostille : Si le corps ou l'urne cinéraire doit être rapatrié vers un autre pays, les autorités sanitaires et administratives du Gouvernement Princier de Monaco (Direction de l'Action Sanitaire et Département de l'Intérieur) délivrent le laissez-passer mortuaire international après mise en bière en cercueil hermétique [1]. Pour l'utilisation juridique d'un acte de décès monégasque à l'étranger, l'Apostille de La Haye est délivrée gratuitement par la Direction des Services Judiciaires au Palais de Justice de Monaco [1][5].

steps.title: Démarches auprès des Caisses Sociales de Monaco, caisses de retraite, banques et assurances
steps.html:
• Capital décès et remboursements de soins (CCSS / CAMTI / SPME) : Si la personne décédée était salariée ou retraitée affiliée au régime général monégasque, déclarez le décès aux Caisses Sociales de Monaco (CSM - Caisse de Compensation des Services Sociaux, téléphone +377 93 15 43 43) [3]. Sous conditions d'ouverture des droits, les ayants droit prioritaires (conjoint survivant non séparé, enfants à charge ou ascendants à charge) peuvent solliciter le versement du capital décès ainsi que le remboursement des derniers frais médicaux [3]. Si le défunt était travailleur indépendant affilié à la CAMTI/CARTI ou fonctionnaire relevant du Service des Prestations Médicales de l'État (SPME), adressez l'acte de décès à la caisse correspondante [1][3].
  • Pensions de réversion de la Caisse Autonome des Retraites (CAR) : Pour un assuré ou pensionné du secteur privé monégasque, déposez une demande de pension de réversion (veuvage ou pension d'orphelin) et vérifiez l'éligibilité aux allocations sociales auprès de la Caisse Autonome des Retraites gérée par les Caisses Sociales de Monaco [4].
  • Banques monégasques, assurances et employeur : Transmettez une copie intégrale de l'acte de décès à l'employeur, aux compagnies d'assurance-vie et aux établissements bancaires de la Principauté [1]. Dès réception de l'avis de décès, les banques monégasques bloquent les comptes individuels de la personne décédée (tout en permettant généralement le règlement direct des frais d'obsèques sur présentation de la facture officielle des pompes funèbres) jusqu'à la production des pièces successorales établies par le notaire [5].

steps.title: Ouverture et règlement de la succession devant notaire à Monaco et coordination internationale
steps.html:
• Règlement successoral par un notaire monégasque : Conformément au Code civil monégasque consultable sur LégiMonaco, le règlement d'une succession ouverte en Principauté de Monaco (notamment dès qu'il existe un testament, un bien immobilier, des comptes bancaires significatifs ou plusieurs héritiers) s'effectue avec le concours de l'une des études de notaires de Monaco [5]. Le notaire recherche les dispositions de dernières volontés (testament olographe, authentique ou mystique), procède à l'ouverture du testament, établit l'acte de notoriété héréditaire confirmant la qualité des héritiers, dresse l'inventaire et prépare les actes de partage [5].
  • Fiscalité successorale très avantageuse à Monaco : En Principauté de Monaco, les droits de mutation par décès (droits de succession) ne s'appliquent qu'aux biens situés sur le territoire monégasque (ou ayant leur assiette à Monaco) et dépendent exclusivement du lien de parenté avec le défunt : le taux est de 0 % (exonération totale) en ligne directe (entre parents et enfants ou grands-parents et petits-enfants) ainsi qu'entre époux [5]. Les taux s'élèvent à 8 % entre frères et sœurs, 10 % entre oncles/tantes et neveux/nièces, 13 % entre autres collatéraux et 16 % entre personnes non parentes. La déclaration de succession doit être déposée auprès de la Direction des Services Fiscaux (Enregistrement) du Gouvernement Princier de Monaco dans les six mois suivant le décès (douze mois si le décès est survenu hors d'Europe) [1][5].
  • Coordination internationale (Loi n° 1.448 relative au droit international privé) : Monaco n'étant pas membre de l'Union européenne, le règlement des successions internationales y est régi par le Code de droit international privé monégasque (Loi n° 1.448), qui soumet en principe l'ensemble de la succession à la loi de l'État du dernier domicile du défunt, sauf choix de loi nationale par professio juris dans un testament [5]. Si des héritiers résident à l'étranger ou si des biens immobiliers ou financiers se situent en France ou dans un autre État, le notaire monégasque coordonne les déclarations fiscales et certificats successoraux avec les notaires étrangers [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Monaco: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Monaco: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Monaco: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When your family member in Monaco is diagnosed with a serious or progressive life-limiting illness, we advise organizing medical support, treatment preferences, powers of attorney, and estate arrangements as early as possible while full decision-making capacity is intact. Acting early ensures that the ill person's wishes are respected and protects the family legally and financially. Below is our five-step guide tailored to the institutional and legal framework of the Principality of Monaco.

steps.title: Coordinating Palliative Care, Home Support, and Health Coverage in Monaco
steps.html:
• Supportive and Palliative Care Department at the CHPG: Ask the treating medical team for a referral to the Supportive and Palliative Care Department (Service de Soins de Support et de Soins Palliatifs) at the Princess Grace Hospital Centre (Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace - CHPG, telephone +377 97 98 99 00) [1]. This department operates both a dedicated inpatient unit and a multidisciplinary Mobile Palliative and Supportive Care Unit (Unité Mobile de Soins Palliatifs et Supportifs, UMSPS) focused on pain management, physical comfort, and psychological support for patients and families [1].
  • Home care coordination and the Monaco Gerontological Coordination Centre (CCGM): To set up home nursing care, personal care assistants, or specialized medical equipment at home, contact the social and medico-social services outlined on the public service portal of the Gouvernement Princier de Monaco (Directorate of Social Action and Aid - Direction de l'Action et de l'Aide Sociales, DASO, and the Centre de Coordination Gérontologique de Monaco for older patients) [2].
  • 100 percent long-term illness coverage (affection de longue durée): The attending or hospital physician submits an application for co-payment exemption (exonération du ticket modérateur for serious or long-term illness) to the medical advisory board of the Caisses Sociales de Monaco (CCSS or CAMTI) or the State Medical Benefits Office (Service des Prestations Médicales de l'État, SPME) to secure full coverage for specialist treatments, nursing care, and home medical equipment [2][3].

steps.title: Recording Medical Wishes and Designating a Healthcare Proxy in Monaco
steps.html:
• Statutory focus on palliative care and pain relief: The public health and ethical framework in the Principality of Monaco guarantees the right to comprehensive pain relief and palliative support, while excluding active euthanasia or assisted suicide [1]. A patient with full decision-making capacity has the right to be informed of their diagnosis, to express treatment preferences, and to refuse disproportionate or futile life-prolonging interventions [1][5].
  • Putting written medical wishes on file: While the ill person retains full mental clarity, it is advisable to write, date, and sign a statement of end-of-life care preferences (such as limits on cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or intensive-care transfers, as well as priorities for pain control and sedation) and have it placed directly in the patient's medical file at the Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace and with their primary physician [1].
  • Written designation of a trusted person (personne de confiance): Have your family member designate in writing (dated and co-signed by the appointed person) a trusted healthcare representative (personne de confiance - a relative, spouse, or close contact) authorized to accompany them to medical consultations, receive health information with their consent, and convey their wishes to the medical team at the Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace if the patient later becomes unable to express themselves [1].

steps.title: Bank Powers of Attorney, Notarial Mandates, and Legal Protection in Monaco
steps.html:
• Bank powers of attorney at Monegasque banks: Banks in Monaco strictly require powers of attorney over current accounts, investment portfolios, and safe-deposit boxes to be executed on the bank's own internal mandate forms in the presence of a relationship officer (or via an authentic power of attorney executed before a Monegasque notary) while the account holder retains full legal capacity [5]. If the ill person can no longer travel to the bank branch, ask the bank to arrange a home or hospital visit, or arrange for a Monaco notary to attend in person [5].
  • General or special power of attorney before a Monaco notary: Under the agency (mandat) provisions of the Monegasque Civil Code (published on the official legal portal LégiMonaco), the ill person can execute an authentic general power of attorney for administration or a special notarial mandate before one of the Principality's notaries, empowering a trusted relative to manage property, sign leases, and handle ongoing financial affairs [5].
  • Judicial adult protection measures (tutelle or curatelle): Under Monegasque law, an ordinary power of attorney ceases to operate or becomes legally vulnerable if the grantor subsequently loses mental capacity [5]. If a lasting impairment of mental faculties occurs, the Court of First Instance of Monaco (Tribunal de première instance / guardianship judge) may be petitioned under the Monegasque Civil Code (Articles 410-1 et seq. on LégiMonaco) to establish a tailored judicial protection measure (judicial administrator, curatelle, or tutelle) supervised by the Monegasque courts [5].

steps.title: Activating Invalidity Benefits, Dependency Support, and Family Caregiver Aid
steps.html:
• Invalidity pension and third-party assistance supplement (CSM): If the ill person is an employee insured with the Compensation Fund for Social Services (Caisse de Compensation des Services Sociaux, CCSS) and their condition permanently reduces their earning capacity by at least two thirds, the attending physician files an invalidity application with the Caisses Sociales de Monaco (telephone +377 93 15 43 43) [3]. Where total incapacity requires another person's help to perform ordinary activities of daily living, the invalidity pension is increased by a third-party assistance supplement (majoration pour assistance d'une tierce personne) [3].
  • Autonomy benefits, disability status, and retiree social allowances: Through the support programs detailed on the MonServicePublic portal of the Gouvernement Princier de Monaco, the ill person or their family can apply to the Directorate of Social Action and Aid (DASO) and the Town Hall (Mairie de Monaco) for home-support services (autonomy allowance, home care aides, tele-alarm, meal delivery), as well as retiree social allowances administered by the Autonomous Pension Fund (CAR) of the Caisses Sociales de Monaco [2][4].
  • Support and respite resources for family caregivers: Contact the DASO of the Gouvernement Princier de Monaco and the hospital social workers at the Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace regarding home respite support, financial assistance, and psychological counseling available to family caregivers living or working in Monaco [1][2].

steps.title: Early Review of the Will, Life Insurance Beneficiaries, and Cross-Border Estate Planning
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a Will under the Monegasque Civil Code: While testamentary capacity is intact, review or execute a last will and testament with the assistance of a Monaco notary in accordance with the Monegasque Civil Code published on LégiMonaco [5]. Monegasque law recognizes three forms of wills: the holographic will (testament olographe, written, dated, and signed entirely by hand by the testator), the public/authentic will (testament par acte public, executed before a notary in the presence of witnesses), and the mystic (sealed) will [5]. When a person is seriously ill or receiving strong analgesics, an authentic notarial will (supported by a contemporaneous medical certificate confirming full mental clarity) provides the strongest protection against future legal challenges [5].
  • Forced heirship rules (réserve héréditaire) and life insurance designations: The Monegasque Civil Code protects the statutory reserved share (réserve héréditaire) of descendants (or ascendants in the absence of descendants) and defines the freely disposable portion (quotité disponible) [5]. At the same time, review the beneficiary clauses on life insurance and capitalization policies held in Monaco or abroad so they accurately reflect the ill person's current wishes.
  • Cross-border coordination (Law No. 1.448 on Private International Law): If your family member holds foreign citizenship, owns real estate or financial assets outside Monaco, or has heirs residing abroad, consult a Monegasque notary on whether to include an explicit choice-of-law clause (professio juris, electing the testator's national law to govern their succession under the Monegasque Code of Private International Law) and organize all civil status certificates and property title deeds in a single accessible file [5].

closingQuestion: Is your family member currently receiving care at home in Monaco or as an inpatient at the Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace, and have they already put bank powers of attorney or a will in place before a Monaco notary?

fr.title: Maladie en phase terminale et démarches en Monaco : liste officielle en 5 étapes
fr.cardSummary: Guide officiel en 5 étapes pour les démarches médicales et juridiques en fin de vie en Monaco : soins palliatifs, directives anticipées, procurations et mandats, congés d'aidant familial et organisation patrimoniale.
fr.introHtml: Lorsque votre proche à Monaco reçoit le diagnostic d'une maladie grave ou évolutive, nous vous conseillons d'organiser dès que possible l'accompagnement médical, les volontés de soins, les procurations et les démarches patrimoniales tant que sa pleine capacité de discernement est préservée. Cette anticipation garantit le respect des choix de la personne malade et sécurise sa famille sur le plan juridique et financier. Voici notre guide en cinq étapes adapté au cadre institutionnel de la Principauté de Monaco.

steps.title: Coordination des soins palliatifs, du maintien à domicile et de la couverture santé à Monaco
steps.html:
• Service de Soins de Support et de Soins Palliatifs du CHPG : Demandez à l'équipe médicale référente d'orienter votre proche vers le Service de Soins de Support et de Soins Palliatifs du Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace (CHPG, téléphone +377 97 98 99 00) [1]. Ce service comprend une unité d'hospitalisation dédiée ainsi que l'Unité Mobile de Soins Palliatifs et Supportifs (UMSPS), qui intervient de manière pluridisciplinaire pour la prise en charge de la douleur, le confort physique et le soutien psychologique des patients et de leurs proches [1].
  • Soins à domicile et Centre de Coordination Gérontologique de Monaco (CCGM) : Pour organiser le maintien à domicile avec des soins infirmiers, des auxiliaires de vie ou du matériel médicalisé, prenez contact avec les services sociaux et médico-sociaux présentés sur le portail du Gouvernement Princier de Monaco (Direction de l'Action et de l'Aide Sociales - DASO, et Centre de Coordination Gérontologique de Monaco lorsque la personne malade est âgée) [2].
  • Prise en charge à 100 % au titre d'une affection de longue durée (ALD / longue maladie) : Le médecin traitant ou hospitalier établit une demande d'exonération du ticket modérateur pour affection grave ou de longue durée auprès du contrôle médical des Caisses Sociales de Monaco (CCSS ou CAMTI) ou du Service des Prestations Médicales de l'État (SPME), afin d'assurer une prise en charge optimale des traitements lourds, des soins infirmiers et des équipements à domicile [2][3].

steps.title: Expression des volontés médicales et désignation de la personne de confiance à Monaco
steps.html:
• Priorité légale aux soins palliatifs et au soulagement de la douleur : Le cadre sanitaire et éthique en Principauté de Monaco consacre le droit fondamental au soulagement de la douleur et à l'accompagnement palliatif, tout en excluant l'euthanasie active ou le suicide assisté [1]. Le patient pleinement capable de discernement a le droit d'être informé de son état de santé, d'exprimer ses préférences thérapeutiques et de refuser un traitement disproportionné ou relevant d'une obstination déraisonnable [1][5].
  • Rédaction de volontés médicales écrites : Tant que la personne malade dispose de sa pleine lucidité, il est vivement conseillé de consigner par écrit, de dater et de signer ses souhaits relatifs aux traitements de fin de vie (tels que la limitation des manœuvres de réanimation, de la ventilation artificielle ou des transferts en soins intensifs, ainsi que ses priorités en matière de sédation et de confort) et de les faire verser directement à son dossier médical au Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace ainsi qu'auprès de son médecin traitant [1].
  • Désignation écrite d'une personne de confiance : Invitez votre proche à désigner par écrit (document daté et cosigné par la personne désignée) une personne de confiance (parent, conjoint ou proche de son choix) chargée de l'accompagner lors des consultations médicales, de recevoir les informations de santé avec son accord et de témoigner de sa volonté auprès de l'équipe médicale du Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace si la personne malade ne peut plus s'exprimer elle-même [1].

steps.title: Procurations bancaires, mandats notariés et protection juridique en Principauté de Monaco
steps.html:
• Procurations bancaires auprès des banques de Monaco : Les établissements bancaires monégasques exigent systématiquement que les procurations sur comptes courants, comptes-titres et coffres soient signées sur leurs propres formulaires internes en présence d'un chargé de clientèle (ou sur présentation d'une procuration authentique reçue par un notaire monégasque) tant que le titulaire jouit de sa pleine capacité juridique [5]. Si la personne malade ne peut plus se déplacer en agence, demandez à la banque d'organiser un rendez-vous à domicile ou à l'hôpital, ou faites intervenir un notaire de Monaco [5].
  • Mandat général ou spécial devant notaire monégasque : Conformément aux règles du mandat prévues par le Code civil monégasque (consultable sur le portail officiel LégiMonaco), la personne malade peut établir par acte authentique devant l'un des notaires de la Principauté une procuration générale d'administration ou un mandat spécial permettant à un proche de gérer ses biens, de signer des baux ou de régler ses affaires courantes [5].
  • Mesures judiciaires de protection des majeurs (tutelle ou curatelle) : En droit monégasque, une procuration ordinaire cesse de produire effet ou devient juridiquement fragile si le mandant perd ultérieurement ses facultés mentales [5]. Si une altération durable des facultés personnelles survient, le Tribunal de première instance de Monaco (Juge tutélaire) peut être saisi en vertu du Code civil monégasque (articles 410-1 et suivants sur LégiMonaco) pour organiser une mesure de protection judiciaire adaptée (administrateur judiciaire, curatelle ou tutelle) sous le contrôle de la justice monégasque [5].

steps.title: Activation des prestations d'invalidité, de dépendance et des aides aux proches aidants
steps.html:
• Pension d'invalidité et majoration pour tierce personne (CSM) : Si la personne malade est salariée affiliée à la Caisse de Compensation des Services Sociaux (CCSS) et que sa pathologie réduit durablement sa capacité de travail d'au moins deux tiers, le médecin traitant dépose une demande d'admission en invalidité auprès des Caisses Sociales de Monaco (téléphone +377 93 15 43 43) [3]. En cas d'incapacité absolue obligeant l'assuré à recourir à l'aide d'autrui pour accomplir les actes ordinaires de la vie courante, la pension d'invalidité est complétée par une majoration pour assistance d'une tierce personne [3].
  • Prestation d'autonomie, statut de personne handicapée et aides sociales : Par l'intermédiaire des dispositifs détaillés sur le portail MonServicePublic du Gouvernement Princier de Monaco, la personne malade ou sa famille peut solliciter auprès de la Direction de l'Action et de l'Aide Sociales (DASO) et de la Mairie de Monaco les aides au maintien à domicile (prestation d'autonomie, auxiliaires de vie, téléalarme, portage de repas) ainsi que les allocations sociales servies aux retraités par la Caisse Autonome des Retraites (CAR) des Caisses Sociales de Monaco [2][4].
  • Soutien et dispositifs pour les proches aidants : Renseignez-vous auprès de la DASO du Gouvernement Princier de Monaco et des assistantes sociales du Centre Hospitalier Princesse Grace sur les aménagements, aides financières au répit à domicile et accompagnements psychologiques destinés aux proches aidants résidant ou travaillant à Monaco [1][2].

steps.title: Vérification anticipée du testament, des assurances-vie et de la coordination internationale
steps.html:
• Rédaction ou révision d'un testament conforme au Code civil monégasque : Tant que la capacité de discernement est entière, vérifiez ou établissez un testament avec l'assistance d'un notaire de Monaco conformément au Code civil monégasque publié sur LégiMonaco [5]. Le droit monégasque reconnaît trois formes testamentaires : le testament olographe (entièrement écrit, daté et signé de la main du testateur), le testament par acte public / authentique (reçu par un notaire en présence de témoins) et le testament mystique [5]. En cas de maladie grave ou de traitement antalgique lourd, la forme authentique devant notaire (accompagnée d'un certificat médical contemporain attestant la pleine lucidité) offre la meilleure sécurité contre toute contestation ultérieure [5].
  • Réserve héréditaire et clauses bénéficiaires d'assurance-vie : Le Code civil monégasque protège la réserve héréditaire des descendants (ou, à défaut, des ascendants) et définit la quotité disponible [5]. Parallèlement, vérifiez les clauses bénéficiaires des contrats d'assurance-vie et de capitalisation souscrits à Monaco ou à l'étranger afin qu'elles reflètent exactement la volonté actuelle de votre proche.
  • Coordination internationale (Loi n° 1.448 de droit international privé) : Si votre proche possède une nationalité étrangère, détient des biens immobiliers ou financiers hors de Monaco, ou si certains héritiers résident à l'étranger, consultez un notaire monégasque pour vérifier s'il convient d'insérer dans le testament une professio juris (choix exprès de la loi nationale du testateur pour régir sa succession conformément au Code de droit international privé monégasque) et pour centraliser l'ensemble des actes d'état civil et titres de propriété [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in San Marino: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in San Marino: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for San Marino: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in the Republic of San Marino. When a death occurs on Sammarinese territory, relatives must coordinate in sequence the medical certification of death through the public healthcare system, civil registration in Borgo Maggiore, mortuary police permits, social security notifications, and tax and inheritance filings. Below we outline the five official and practical steps to follow under the legal framework of the Republic of San Marino.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Healthcare Documentation
steps.html:
• Death at the State Hospital or public residential facilities: If your family member died at the State Hospital in Cailungo or in a care facility operated by the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, hospital physicians issue the medical confirmation of death and the internal necroscopic certificate, forwarding the healthcare records needed for civil registration [2].
  • Death at a private residence: If the death occurred at home in one of the municipalities (Castelli) of the Republic of San Marino, relatives must promptly contact the attending physician or the on-call medical service of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale so a doctor can verify the death in person and complete the medical cause-of-death certificate [1] [2].
  • Sudden death or cases requiring judicial clearance: Where a death occurs without medical attendance or under circumstances requiring forensic examination, the attending doctor notifies the police authorities and the Law Commissioner (Commissario della Legge) at the Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino, which must issue a formal clearance before the body may be moved or buried [5].

steps.title: Civil Registration of Death and Official Certificates
steps.html:
• Registration at the central civil registry in Borgo Maggiore: The formal declaration of death must be filed with the Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali (located at Via Ventotto Luglio 196 in Borgo Maggiore), which holds exclusive authority to register deaths occurring in San Marino or involving resident citizens [1].
  • Documents required to register the death record: To complete the registration, you must present the necroscopic medical certificate issued by the physicians of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, the deceased person's identity documents (including the Sammarinese identity card and ISS social security code), and the valid identification of the declarant or authorized funeral representative [1] [2].
  • Requesting death certificates and civil registry extracts: Once the death act is registered, the Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali issues death certificates as well as summary or full extracts of the death record; it is advisable to request multiple original copies, as they will be required for banks, insurers, pension claims, and the mandatory inheritance tax return [1] [4].

steps.title: Funeral Arrangements, Burial or Cremation Permits, and Repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial permits and cemetery administration: The Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali also exercises mortuary police functions and administers the cemeteries of the Republic of San Marino, issuing the official burial or entombment permit for the municipal cemeteries after the mandatory medical observation period has elapsed [1].
  • Authorization for cremation: Because cremation takes place at authorized crematoria outside Sammarinese territory (typically in neighboring Italy), the competent civil registry office issues the transport and cremation authorization based on the deceased person's testamentary wishes or the joint declaration of eligible next of kin [1].
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: If your family member is to be transported across the border for burial in Italy or another country, the Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali issues the mortuary passport and coordinates public health certificates with the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, affixing a Hague Apostille where required for foreign jurisdictions [1] [2].

steps.title: Social Security Notifications, Survivor Pensions, and Banking Steps
steps.html:
• Stopping direct pensions and applying for survivor benefits: Relatives must notify the Pensions and Economic Benefits Office of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale to halt direct pension payments and prevent overpayments, while simultaneously submitting an application for a survivor or reversionary pension (pensione ai superstiti) [2] [3].
  • Eligibility rules for surviving spouses and children: Under Sammarinese social security law, eligible beneficiaries include the surviving spouse (subject to statutory marriage duration requirements and income cumulation thresholds) and dependent children under age 18, students up to age 26, or disabled dependent children, provided the deceased accrued at least 15 years of total contributions or 7 years of contributions including at least one year in the five years preceding death [3].
  • Notifying Sammarinese banks, insurers, and employers: Upon presentation of the death certificate to Sammarinese banks and financial institutions, individual accounts held by the deceased are frozen pending completion of the inheritance procedure; heirs must also request from each bank a formal statement of account balances and deposits as of the date of death, which is mandatory for the inheritance filing [4].

steps.title: Opening the Estate Succession and Filing the Inheritance Return
steps.html:
• Filing the mandatory inheritance declaration: Heirs or legatees must file the formal inheritance tax return (denuncia d'eredità) with the Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria of the Republic of San Marino, using the official forms to declare all real estate, bank accounts, corporate shares, and financial assets included in the estate [4].
  • Required attachments and will registration: The inheritance declaration submitted to the Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria must be accompanied by a certified copy of any registered will in San Marino, the official bank declarations confirming balances at the date of death, and, if the deceased was not registered in the Sammarinese population registry, an original death certificate [4].
  • Cross-border estates, foreign heirs, and court procedures: If the deceased or the heirs are foreign nationals residing outside San Marino, the filing must include a sworn affidavit of heirship (atto notorio) confirming the devolution of the estate, as well as authorization from the Council of Twelve (Consiglio dei XII) where required for real property transfers; for acceptance of an estate with benefit of inventory, appointment of estate curators, or contested probate matters, jurisdiction lies with the Civil Registry of the Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino [4] [5].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more tailored guidance, in which municipality (Castello) of San Marino did your family member reside, did the death occur in hospital or at home, and are there assets, bank accounts, or heirs located outside the Republic of San Marino?

it.title: Cosa fare quando muore un familiare in San Marino: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi dopo un decesso in San Marino: certificazione medica e visita necroscopica, scelta dell'impresa funebre, denuncia di morte allo Stato Civile, pensione ai superstiti e dichiarazione di successione.
it.introHtml: Vi esprimiamo la nostra sincera vicinanza per la perdita del vostro familiare nella Repubblica di San Marino. Quando si verifica un decesso nel territorio sammarinese, i familiari devono coordinare in sequenza gli accertamenti sanitari presso le strutture pubbliche, la denuncia anagrafica e di stato civile a Borgo Maggiore, le autorizzazioni di polizia mortuaria, le comunicazioni previdenziali e gli adempimenti fiscali e successori. Di seguito illustriamo i cinque passi ufficiali e pratici da seguire secondo l'ordinamento della Repubblica di San Marino.

steps.title: Accertamento medico del decesso e certificazione sanitaria
steps.html:
• Decesso presso l'Ospedale di Stato o strutture socio-sanitarie: Se il vostro familiare è deceduto presso l'Ospedale di Stato di Cailungo o in una struttura residenziale gestita dall'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, i medici ospedalieri redigono la constatatazione di morte e il certificato necroscopico interno, trasmettendo la documentazione sanitaria necessaria per la successiva formazione dell'atto di morte [2].
  • Decesso avvenuto presso l'abitazione privata: Qualora la morte avvenga a domicilio in uno dei Castelli della Repubblica di San Marino, i familiari devono contattare tempestivamente il medico curante o la guardia medica dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale affinché compia l'accertamento diretto della realtà della morte e rilasci la scheda sanitaria delle cause di morte [1] [2].
  • Casi di morte improvvisa o con intervento dell'autorità giudiziaria: Se il decesso avviene senza assistenza medica o in circostanze che richiedono accertamenti medico-legali, il sanitario intervenuto informa l'autorità di polizia e il Commissario della Legge presso il Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino, che deve rilasciare il nulla osta prima della rimozione della salma e della sepoltura [5].

steps.title: Denuncia di morte e rilascio dei certificati di stato civile
steps.html:
• Registrazione presso l'ufficio competente a Borgo Maggiore: La dichiarazione formalmente prevista del decesso deve essere presentata all'Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali (situato in Via Ventotto Luglio 196 a Borgo Maggiore), che detiene la competenza esclusiva per iscrivere gli atti di morte avvenuti sul territorio sammarinese o riguardanti cittadini residenti [1].
  • Documentazione richiesta per la formazione dell'atto: Per completare l'iscrizione dell'atto di morte occorre presentare il certificato medico necroscopico rilasciato dai sanitari dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, i documenti d'identità della persona deceduta (inclusa la carta d'identità sammarinese e il codice ISS) e il documento di riconoscimento del dichiarante o dell'incaricato funebre delegato [1] [2].
  • Richiesta di certificati ed estratti di morte: Una volta registrato il decesso, l'Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali rilascia i certificati di morte e gli estratti per riassunto o copia integrale dell'atto di morte; è consigliabile richiederne più esemplari originali, poiché saranno indispensabili per le pratiche bancarie, assicurative, previdenziali e per la denuncia di eredità [1] [4].

steps.title: Organizzazione delle esequie, polizia mortuaria e rimpatrio
steps.html:
• Autorizzazione alla sepoltura e gestione cimiteriale: L'Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali svolge anche le funzioni di polizia mortuaria e amministrazione dei cimiteri della Repubblica di San Marino, rilasciando il permesso ufficiale di seppellimento (inumazione o tumulazione nei cimiteri dei diversi Castelli) dopo il decorso del periodo di osservazione sanitaria [1].
  • Pratiche per la cremazione: Poiché la cremazione viene effettuata presso impianti autorizzati fuori dal territorio sammarinese (generalmente nella vicina Repubblica Italiana), l'ufficio competente rilascia l'autorizzazione al trasporto della salma e alla cremazione sulla base della volontà testamentaria della persona deceduta o della dichiarazione concorde dei familiari aventi titolo [1].
  • Trasporto internazionale della salma o delle ceneri: Se il vostro familiare deve essere trasferito oltre confine per la sepoltura in Italia o in un altro Stato estero, l'Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali rilascia il passaporto mortuario e coordina le certificazioni igienico-sanitarie con i servizi di sanità pubblica dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, applicando ove richiesto la postilla della Convenzione dell'Aia sugli atti destinati a Paesi esteri [1] [2].

steps.title: Comunicazioni previdenziali, pensioni ai superstiti e rapporti bancari
steps.html:
• Cessazione delle prestazioni dirette e domanda di reversibilità: I familiari devono comunicare il decesso all'Ufficio Prestazioni Economiche e Pensioni dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale per interrompere l'erogazione della pensione diretta ed evitare indebiti, presentando contestualmente la domanda di pensione ai superstiti (reversibilità o pensione indiretta) [2] [3].
  • Requisiti per il coniuge e i figli superstiti: Secondo la normativa previdenziale sammarinese, hanno diritto alla pensione ai superstiti il coniuge superstite (nel rispetto dei requisiti di durata del matrimonio e delle soglie di cumulabilità con altri redditi o pensioni) e i figli minori di 18 anni, gli studenti fino a 26 anni o i figli con disabilità a carico, purché la persona deceduta avesse maturato almeno 15 anni di contributi complessivi oppure 7 anni di cui almeno uno nell'ultimo quinquennio [3].
  • Notifica a banche, assicurazioni e datori di lavoro: Presentando il certificato di morte agli istituti bancari e finanziari sammarinesi, i conti individuali del defunto vengono cautelativamente bloccati fino al perfezionamento della pratica successoria; è inoltre necessario richiedere a ciascuna banca la dichiarazione formale dei saldi e dei depositi alla data del decesso, documento obbligatorio per la denuncia fiscale di eredità [4].

steps.title: Apertura della successione ereditaria e denuncia d'eredità
steps.html:
• Presentazione della denuncia d'eredità: Gli eredi o i legatari sono tenuti a presentare la dichiarazione fiscale di successione presso l'Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria della Repubblica di San Marino, utilizzando l'apposita modulistica ufficiale per elencare tutti i beni immobili, i conti bancari, le quote societarie e i diritti compresi nell'attivo ereditario [4].
  • Allegati obbligatori e ricerca testamentaria: Alla denuncia presentata all'Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria devono essere allegati la copia autentica dell'eventuale testamento registrato a San Marino, le dichiarazioni bancarie attestanti i saldi alla data del decesso e, qualora la persona deceduta non risultasse iscritta nell'anagrafe sammarinese, il certificato di morte in originale [4].
  • Coordinamento con eredi o beni all'estero e adempimenti giudiziari: Se il defunto o gli eredi sono cittadini stranieri non residenti a San Marino, la normativa richiede di allegare un atto notorio che attesti la devoluzione dell'eredità, oltre all'eventuale autorizzazione del Consiglio dei XII ove prevista per l'intestazione di immobili; per le accettazioni con beneficio d'inventario, la nomina di curatori o le controversie ereditarie è invece competente la Cancelleria Civile del Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino [4] [5].

it.closingQuestion: Per permetterci di fornirvi indicazioni ancora più mirate, in quale Castello di San Marino risiedeva il vostro familiare, il decesso è avvenuto in ospedale o a domicilio e sono presenti beni, conti bancari o eredi residenti fuori dalla Repubblica di San Marino?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in San Marino: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in San Marino: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for San Marino: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We extend our full support and solidarity as you and your family navigate a serious or progressive illness diagnosis in the Republic of San Marino. Taking action while your family member retains full legal capacity makes it possible to coordinate the public palliative and home care network, document treatment preferences, execute enforceable notarial powers of attorney and bank mandates, and organize property and estate records smoothly. Below we outline the five official and practical steps to complete in San Marino.

steps.title: Activating Palliative Care and Home or Hospital Support
steps.html:
• Specialist symptom management and pain therapy: In San Marino, public pain management and palliative care are coordinated by the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale through the UOS Medicina del Dolore, Cure Palliative e Hospice, which provides specialist control of complex pain as well as physical and psychological symptoms associated with advanced oncological or chronic degenerative conditions [1] [2].
  • Integrated home care across the municipalities (Castelli): Upon referral by the primary care physician at the local Health Center (Centro Sanitario) or by a discharging hospital ward, the multidisciplinary team of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale sets up individualized nursing, medical, and home-care plans directly at the ill person's residence, including the provision of medical equipment and assistive devices [1] [2].
  • Continuity of care between home and the State Hospital: When clinical needs require closer inpatient monitoring or temporary respite admissions for the family, the hospital service coordinates seamless transitions between home care and the dedicated wards at the State Hospital in Cailungo under public healthcare coverage [1] [2].

steps.title: Documenting Medical Treatment Wishes and Naming a Trusted Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and shared care planning: While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, they can work with the physicians of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale and the UOS Medicina del Dolore, Cure Palliative e Hospice to establish a shared care plan (pianificazione condivisa delle cure), specifying which treatments they wish to accept or refuse in later stages of the illness [1] [2].
  • Written advance treatment directives and trusted proxy: The ill person may record written instructions regarding medical interventions (such as artificial nutrition, mechanical ventilation, or invasive resuscitation) and designate a trusted representative (fiduciario) to communicate with medical staff should they later become unable to express their wishes directly [1] [2].
  • Filing directives in the medical record: It is advisable to provide copies of the written care preferences and the representative's contact details both to the primary care physician at the local Health Center and to the specialist team at the State Hospital so they are immediately accessible in the electronic clinical file [1] [2].

steps.title: Executing Notarial Powers of Attorney, Bank Mandates, and Protective Measures
steps.html:
• General or special powers of attorney before a Sammarinese notary: Because informal authorizations are insufficient for property transactions or formal legal acts, it is essential that your family member, while retaining full mental capacity, sign a general or special power of attorney (procura generale o speciale) by public deed before a notary licensed in the Republic of San Marino, who will handle mandatory registration with the Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria [4].
  • Operating mandates on Sammarinese bank accounts: We advise visiting the Sammarinese banks where the ill person holds accounts or deposits (or arranging a home signature collection where offered by the institution) to register the attorney-in-fact's specimen signature or activate a bank operating mandate for paying ongoing household and medical expenses [4].
  • Judicial protection if capacity is lost: If the illness impairs decision-making capacity before a notarial power of attorney has been executed, relatives must apply to the Civil Registry of the Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino for non-contentious judicial protection measures (volontaria giurisdizione) on behalf of a vulnerable or incapacitated adult [5].

steps.title: Applying for Disability Benefits, Attendance Allowances, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Disability assessment and attendance allowances: Patients whose serious illness substantially reduces personal autonomy may apply to the medical boards of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale for formal recognition of disability or incapacity and for associated financial benefits or attendance allowances (indennità di accompagnamento) [2] [3].
  • Home support and territorial social-health services: Through the social and healthcare services of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, families can request domestic social-care assistance, free loan of orthopedic beds and pressure-relief aids, and dedicated psychological support for both the patient and family caregivers [1] [2].
  • Caregiver leave and employment protections: Employed family members in the Sammarinese public or private sector who care for a relative with a severe disability or progressive illness can verify available paid leave, extraordinary caregiver leave, and pension contribution protections with the Economic Benefits Office of the Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale [2] [3].

steps.title: Reviewing the Will, Civil Status Records, and Estate Documentation in Advance
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a will in San Marino: While full legal capacity is intact, your family member can draft or update their will (preferably as a public notarial will with a Sammarinese notary) to govern the distribution of assets in accordance with the statutory forced-heirship shares (quote di legittima) of Sammarinese law, simplifying future filings with the Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria [4].
  • Verifying civil registry records and insurance designations: It is helpful to gather updated family status and civil registry certificates in advance from the Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali in Borgo Maggiore, and to review beneficiary designations on life insurance policies and supplementary pension funds [4] [6].
  • Coordinating cross-border assets or foreign heirs: If the ill person owns real estate, bank accounts, or business interests both in San Marino and in Italy or other countries, or if prospective heirs reside abroad, it is advisable to prepare an updated inventory of Sammarinese bank relationships and consult a notary to align Sammarinese inheritance rules with private international law and the procedural requirements of the Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino [4] [5].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more specific guidance, is your family member currently receiving care at home or at the State Hospital, are they able to sign notarial deeds in San Marino, and are there assets or family members located outside the Republic of San Marino?

it.title: Malattia terminale e adempimenti legali in San Marino: guida ufficiale in 5 passi
it.cardSummary: Guida ufficiale in 5 passi per la pianificazione medica e amministrativa in caso di malattia terminale in San Marino: cure palliative e hospice, Disposizioni Anticipate di Trattamento (DAT), procure e amministrazione di sostegno, congedi e testamento.
it.introHtml: Vi esprimiamo la nostra piena solidarietà e il nostro sostegno nell'affrontare la diagnosi di malattia grave o in fase avanzata che riguarda il vostro familiare nella Repubblica di San Marino. Quando la persona malata conserva la piena capacità di intendere e di volere, intervenire tempestivamente consente di attivare la rete pubblica di cure palliative e assistenza domiciliare, formalizzare le scelte terapeutiche, conferire procure notarili e deleghe bancarie valide e predisporre con serenità l'assetto patrimoniale. Di seguito illustriamo i cinque passi ufficiali e pratici da compiere a San Marino.

steps.title: Attivazione delle cure palliative e dell'assistenza domiciliare o ospedaliera
steps.html:
• Presa in carico specialistica e controllo dei sintomi: A San Marino la rete di terapia antalgica e cure palliative fa capo all'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale attraverso la UOS Medicina del Dolore, Cure Palliative e Hospice, che garantisce il controllo del dolore complesso e dei sintomi fisici e psicologici legati a patologie oncologiche o cronico-degenerative avanzate [1] [2].
  • Assistenza domiciliare integrata nei Castelli: Su attivazione del medico di medicina generale del Centro Sanitario territoriale o del reparto ospedaliero dimittente, l'équipe multidisciplinare dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale organizza piani personalizzati di assistenza infermieristica, medica e socio-assistenziale direttamente presso il domicilio della persona malata, fornendo anche presidi sanitari e ausili [1] [2].
  • Continuità assistenziale tra domicilio e Ospedale di Stato: Qualora il quadro clinico richieda monitoraggio intensivo o ricoveri temporanei di sollievo per la famiglia, il servizio ospedaliero coordina il passaggio tra l'assistenza territoriale e i reparti dedicati dell'Ospedale di Stato di Cailungo in regime di copertura pubblica [1] [2].

steps.title: Disposizioni sulle scelte sanitarie e designazione di una persona di fiducia
steps.html:
• Espressione del consenso informato e pianificazione condivisa delle cure: Finché il vostro familiare mantiene piena lucidità e capacità decisionale, può definire insieme ai medici dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale e della UOS Medicina del Dolore, Cure Palliative e Hospice una pianificazione condivisa del percorso clinico, precisando i trattamenti che intende accettare o rifiutare nelle fasi più avanzate della patologia [1] [2].
  • Redazione delle volontà anticipate e nomina di un fiduciario: La persona malata può mettere per iscritto le proprie direttive sulle cure mediche (come nutrizione artificiale, ventilazione meccanica o rianimazione invasiva) e indicare un fiduciario di riferimento incaricato di interloquire con il personale sanitario qualora subentri un'incapacità di esprimersi autonomamente [1] [2].
  • Inserimento nella documentazione clinica: È importante consegnare copia delle volontà scritte e dei recapiti del fiduciario sia al medico curante del Centro Sanitario sia all'équipe specialistica dell'Ospedale di Stato, affinché siano immediatamente consultabili nella cartella clinica elettronica in caso di urgenza [1] [2].

steps.title: Conferimento di procure notarili, deleghe bancarie e misure di protezione
steps.html:
• Procure speciali o generali davanti a notaio sammarinese: Poiché le deleghe informali perdono efficacia o risultano insufficienti per gli atti di straordinaria amministrazione, è fondamentale che il vostro familiare, mentre conserva la piena capacità di agire, sottoscriva una procura speciale o generale per atto pubblico davanti a un notaio iscritto nella Repubblica di San Marino, che provvederà ai relativi adempimenti di registrazione presso l'Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria [4].
  • Deleghe operative sui conti correnti bancari: Si consiglia di recarsi presso gli istituti di credito sammarinesi in cui la persona malata detiene conti o depositi (o di richiedere la raccolta della firma a domicilio ove previsto dalla banca) per depositare lo specimen di firma del procuratore o attivare una delega ad operare per il pagamento delle spese correnti e mediche [4].
  • Tutele giudiziarie in caso di perdita della capacità: Se la malattia dovesse compromettere la capacità di autodeterminazione prima del rilascio di una procura notarile, i familiari dovranno rivolgersi alla Cancelleria Civile del Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino per richiedere i provvedimenti di volontaria giurisdizione a tutela delle persone fragili o incapaci [5].

steps.title: Richiesta di prestazioni assistenziali, invalidità e sostegni per i familiari
steps.html:
• Accertamento dell'invalidità e assegni di accompagnamento: I pazienti affetti da patologie gravi che riducono drasticamente l'autonomia personale possono presentare domanda alle commissioni mediche dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale per il riconoscimento dell'inabilità o invalidità e per l'erogazione delle relative provvidenze economiche o indennità di accompagnamento [2] [3].
  • Supporto domiciliare e servizi socio-sanitari territoriali: Attraverso i servizi sociali e sanitari dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale, la famiglia può richiedere interventi di assistenza domiciliare socio-assistenziale, fornitura gratuita di letti ortopedici, presidi antidecubito e supporto psicologico dedicato sia al paziente sia ai familiari che prestano cura quotidiana [1] [2].
  • Permessi lavorativi e tutele previdenziali: I familiari lavoratori dipendenti nel settore pubblico o privato sammarinese che assistono un parente con grave disabilità o patologia ingravescente possono verificare presso l'Ufficio Prestazioni Economiche dell'Istituto per la Sicurezza Sociale i permessi retribuiti, i congedi straordinari e le tutele contributive previsti dalla normativa vigente [2] [3].

steps.title: Verifica preventiva del testamento, dello stato civile e della documentazione patrimoniale
steps.html:
• Redazione o aggiornamento del testamento a San Marino: Finché sussiste piena capacità di intendere e di volere, il vostro familiare può redigere o aggiornare il proprio testamento (preferibilmente in forma pubblica con l'assistenza di un notaio sammarinese) per regolare la distribuzione dei beni nel rispetto delle quote di legittima previste dal diritto comune sammarinese, agevolando i futuri adempimenti presso l'Ufficio del Registro e Conservatoria [4].
  • Verifica delle certificazioni anagrafiche e delle polizze: È utile raccogliere preventivamente i certificati di stato di famiglia e le risultanze anagrafiche presso l'Ufficio Stato Civile, Servizi Demografici ed Elettorali di Borgo Maggiore, oltre a controllare le designazioni dei beneficiari nelle polizze assicurative sulla vita e nei fondi previdenziali [4] [6].
  • Coordinamento per patrimoni o familiari all'estero: Se la persona malata possiede beni immobili, conti bancari o partecipazioni sia a San Marino sia in Italia o in altri Stati esteri, oppure se alcuni eredi risiedono fuori territorio, è opportuno predisporre un inventario aggiornato dei rapporti bancari sammarinesi e verificare con un notaio il coordinamento tra la legge sammarinese e le norme di diritto internazionale privato, tenendo conto delle competenze del Tribunale della Repubblica di San Marino [4] [5].

it.closingQuestion: Per permetterci di fornirvi indicazioni più specifiche, il vostro familiare è attualmente assistito a domicilio o presso l'Ospedale di Stato, conserva la piena capacità di sottoscrivere atti notarili e vi sono beni o familiari residenti fuori dalla Repubblica di San Marino?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Andorra: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Andorra: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Andorra: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our deepest condolences on the loss of your family member in the Principality of Andorra. When a death occurs on Andorran territory, relatives must coordinate in sequence the medical certification of death, registration with the central civil registry in Andorra la Vella, arrangements with an authorized funeral provider, social security and banking notifications, and notarial or judicial estate administration. Below we outline the five official and practical steps established under Andorran law.

steps.title: Obtaining the Medical Certificate of Death
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or socio-health facility: If your family member died at the Hospital Nostra Senyora de Meritxell or in a residential care center integrated within the Servei Andorrà d'Atenció Sanitària, the attending hospital physicians verify the death and directly issue the official medical death certificate required to begin civil and funeral formalities [1] [4].
  • Death at a private residence: When a death occurs at home in any of the parishes of Andorra, relatives must contact the primary care physician or the emergency medical services of the Servei Andorrà d'Atenció Sanitària so a doctor can attend the residence, confirm natural causes of death, and sign the corresponding medical certificate [1] [4].
  • Sudden, violent, or unexplained death requiring judicial involvement: Where a death occurs without prior medical attendance or where there are signs of non-natural causes, the police service intervenes alongside the forensic physician and the duty magistrate (batlle de guàrdia) of the Batllia d'Andorra, which must authorize removal of the body and issue a judicial burial or cremation clearance [1] [5].

steps.title: Registering the Death with the Civil Registry and Obtaining Certificates
steps.html:
• Mandatory declaration before the civil registry: Every death occurring in the Principality must be declared and registered with the Registre Civil d'Andorra (located in the Obac administrative building in Escaldes-Engordany / Andorra la Vella) prior to burial or cremation; in practice, the authorized funeral company usually files the initial declaration on the family's behalf [1] [2].
  • Documents required for civil registration: To register the death with the Registre Civil d'Andorra, you must submit the original medical certificate of death, the deceased person's passport or national identity document (together with their Andorran residence or social security card if resident in the country), and the identification details of the declarant [1] [2].
  • Requesting literal and multilingual death certificates: Once the registration is completed, relatives can request from the Registre Civil d'Andorra multiple copies of the full literal death certificate (certificat literal de defunció, required for domestic banks, insurers, and succession deeds) as well as international multilingual extracts when documents must be used abroad [1] [2].

steps.title: Funeral Services, Burial or Cremation Permits, and International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a funeral provider and public health permits: Following medical certification and civil registration, the funeral provider coordinates with public health and parish (Comú) authorities to transfer the deceased to the mortuary facility and obtain the burial permit for the relevant parish cemetery or the administrative authorization for cremation [1].
  • Requirements for cremation: If the wishes of the deceased person or next of kin are to proceed with cremation, the medical certificate must expressly confirm the absence of forensic impediments or incompatible implanted medical devices, supported by prior administrative clearance [1].
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: When your family member resided outside the Principality or is to be transported to Spain, France, or another country for burial, the funeral company obtains the sanitary mortuary transit permit (salvoconducto mortuorio) from the authorities of the Govern d'Andorra and arranges for the Hague Apostille to be affixed to the death certificate issued by the Registre Civil d'Andorra, coordinating any consular paperwork required by the destination country [1] [2].

steps.title: Notifying Social Security, Survivor Pensions, and Andorran Banks
steps.html:
• De-registering the insured person and claiming survivor pensions: Relatives must notify the Caixa Andorrana de Seguretat Social to close the deceased person's direct insurance or pension record and apply for survivor benefits (pensions de reversió), which include temporary or lifetime widowhood pensions (depending on age and duration of the marriage or registered partnership) and orphan pensions for minor or student children [3].
  • Funeral expense reimbursements and supplementary benefits: If the deceased contributed to or received a contributory pension under the Andorran social security system, family members who paid the funeral invoice may check with the Caixa Andorrana de Seguretat Social regarding reimbursement entitlements or death grants based on the insured person's contribution history [3].
  • Protective account freezes and bank balance certificates: Upon presenting the literal death certificate to banks and insurance companies operating in the Principality, individual accounts held by the deceased are frozen pending estate settlement, and institutions issue official certificates of balances and financial holdings as of the date of death for the estate inventory [1] [2].

steps.title: Administering the Estate and Succession in Andorra
steps.html:
• Checking the wills registry and executing notarial deeds: After the funeral, family members should contact a notary chambered in the Principality to check the wills registry of the Chamber of Notaries (Cambra de Notaris) to determine whether the deceased executed a will in Andorra, and to prepare the public deed of acceptance and distribution of the estate [1] [5].
  • Intestate succession and declaration of heirs: If your family member died without leaving a valid will, legal heirs must complete a notarial declaration of intestate heirs before an Andorran notary or, where disputes arise regarding forced-heirship shares (legítima) or asset division, bring the matter before the civil division of the Batllia d'Andorra [5].
  • Tax framework and cross-border estate coordination: Although the Principality of Andorra does not levy a direct state inheritance tax on transfers to family members, heirs must settle applicable notarial fees and parish or property transfer charges; furthermore, if real estate, bank accounts, or heirs are located outside Andorra, it is essential to coordinate the apostilled Andorran notarial deeds with the tax and succession rules of the other jurisdictions involved [2] [5].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more specific guidance, in which parish of Andorra did the death occur, was your family member a habitual resident of the Principality, and are there assets, bank accounts, or heirs located outside Andorra?
