title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Panama: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Panama: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Panama: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: At Clarvia, we understand how challenging this situation is for your family in Panama following the diagnosis of a serious or advanced illness. Below, we explain the five essential practical, medical, and legal steps to arrange in order while your family member retains full legal capacity.

steps.title: Activating Home or Hospital Palliative Care and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Integration into the National Palliative Care Program: In Panama, timely access to pain relief and comprehensive symptom management is organized through the National Palliative Care Program, coordinated jointly by the Ministry of Health of Panama (MINSA) and the Social Security Fund of Panama (CSS) [1] [2]. The attending medical specialist (oncologist, neurologist, geriatrician, or internist) must issue a clinical referral to enroll the patient in the palliative care unit of the reference hospital (such as the National Oncology Institute or regional hospitals) or in primary care home-visit teams [1].
  • Home care, controlled medication supply, and private health insurance: When the clinical condition makes it preferable to remain at home, interdisciplinary teams from the Ministry of Health of Panama (MINSA) and the home care system of the Social Security Fund of Panama (CSS) coordinate medical, nursing, social work, and psychological follow-up, as well as the controlled prescription of opioid analgesics [1] [2]. If your family member holds a private health insurance policy in Panama, you should promptly notify the insurer of the advanced diagnosis to activate home hospitalization, nursing, and medical equipment coverage [1].

steps.title: Advance Directives and Appointing a Healthcare Proxy in Panama
steps.html:
• Patient rights and prior medical directives: Under Law 68 of 2003, which regulates patient rights and obligations regarding information and free, informed decision-making in Panama, every adult of sound mind has the right to accept or refuse diagnostic or therapeutic procedures and to record in writing their preferences regarding end-of-life care [1] [3]. This document allows the patient to set clear instructions regarding the limitation of therapeutic effort, the non-application of disproportionate or invasive life-prolonging measures, and the prioritization of palliative comfort [1].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative and filing in the clinical record: While the person who is ill retains full decision-making capacity, it is strongly advisable to execute in writing (and preferably notarize before a public notary for greater evidentiary certainty) an advance medical directive expressly designating a trusted family member or representative to act as healthcare interlocutor before the medical team [1] [3]. An authenticated copy must be delivered to the attending physician for formal inclusion in the medical record at the Ministry of Health of Panama (MINSA), the Social Security Fund of Panama (CSS), or the relevant private clinic, while keeping another accessible copy at home [1] [2].

steps.title: Executing Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Authorizations
steps.html:
• Granting a general or special power of attorney before a Public Notary: Under Panamanian law, powers of representation must be formalized while the principal retains full mental and legal capacity [3] [4]. Visiting a Circuit Public Notary in Panama (or requesting that the notary travel to the home or hospital if mobility is limited) enables the execution by public deed of a General Power of Attorney or detailed special powers to manage property, represent the person before public agencies, and carry out patrimonial acts, which are recorded in the Public Registry of Panama when required by law [3] [4].
  • Bank mandates and authorized signatures: Because commercial banks in Panama generally require their own internal authorization forms in addition to notarial deeds, it is essential to arrange directly with the banks where your family member holds checking, savings, or fixed-term accounts to register authorized signatures or banking representatives [3]. Likewise, it is advisable to review and update the express designation of beneficiaries on bank accounts and savings funds to prevent future operational freezes and ensure immediate liquidity to cover medical and caregiving expenses [2] [3].

steps.title: Disability Benefits, Dependency Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Sickness allowance and disability pension with the Social Security Fund: If the person who is ill is an insured worker and the progression of the condition prevents them from continuing to work, they can apply to the Social Security Fund of Panama (CSS) for extended medical leave benefits and, following assessment by the Medical Qualifying Commission, request an ordinary Disability Pension (Pensión de Invalidez) [2]. This process requires submitting the detailed clinical history, specialist medical reports, and contribution records at the corresponding administrative agency [2] [3].
  • Disability certification and workplace protections for family caregivers: When the illness causes severe functional limitation or dependency, a disability certification can be requested from the National Secretariat for Disability (SENADIS), which provides legal protections and statutory discounts on medications and services in Panama [1] [2]. Furthermore, under Panamanian equal-opportunity legislation, workers who care for family members with duly accredited disabilities or serious illnesses are entitled to job protection against arbitrary dismissal and justified time off to accompany them to medical treatments and appointments [1] [2].

steps.title: Preventive Will Preparation, Insurance Review, and Estate Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing an open or closed will before a Public Notary: To prevent disputes or delays in future succession proceedings before the Panamanian civil courts, it is advisable for the person who is ill to execute or update their will (typically an open will by public deed before a Public Notary in the presence of qualified witnesses) while retaining full legal capacity [3] [4]. Legal vehicles recognized under Panamanian law, such as private interest foundations or trusts, may also be considered where appropriate for the family's estate structure [3].
  • Reviewing insurance policies, civil records, and international coordination: It is helpful to compile in a physical and digital folder the identity cards and civil status certificates issued by the Electoral Tribunal of Panama (Tribunal Electoral de Panamá), registered property deeds, bank contracts, and life or health insurance policies, verifying that designated beneficiaries are up to date [3] [4]. If assets are located outside Panama or heirs reside abroad, any powers of attorney or public documents intended for cross-border legal effect must carry the Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama (MIRE) [5] [6].

closingQuestion: Is your family member currently receiving care through the public network (MINSA or CSS) or in the private sector in Panama, and are there assets or family members abroad that we should factor in?

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación legal en Panamá: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos para la planificación médica y legal ante una enfermedad terminal en Panamá: cuidados paliativos, testamento vital (voluntades anticipadas), poderes preventivos, ayudas para cuidadores y testamento.
es.introHtml: Desde Clarvia lamentamos esta situación tan compleja por la que atraviesa su familia en Panamá ante el diagnóstico de una enfermedad grave o en fase avanzada. A continuación, explicamos los cinco pasos prácticos, médicos y jurídicos esenciales que conviene organizar en orden mientras la persona enferma conserva su plena capacidad de obrar.

steps.title: Activación de cuidados paliativos domiciliarios u hospitalarios y cobertura sanitaria
steps.html:
• Integración en el Programa Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos: En Panamá, el acceso oportuno al alivio del dolor y al control integral de síntomas está articulado a través del Programa Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos, coordinado conjuntamente por el Ministerio de Salud de Panamá (MINSA) y la Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) [1] [2]. El médico especialista tratante (oncólogo, neurólogo, geriatra o internista) debe emitir la hoja de referencia clínica para incorporar a la persona enferma en la unidad de cuidados paliativos del hospital de referencia (como el Instituto Oncológico Nacional o los hospitales regionales) o en los equipos de visita domiciliaria de atención primaria [1].
  • Atención domiciliaria, suministro de medicación y seguros privados: Cuando el estado clínico aconseja permanecer en el hogar, los equipos interdisciplinarios del Ministerio de Salud de Panamá (MINSA) y el sistema de atención domiciliaria de la Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) coordinan el seguimiento médico, de enfermería, trabajo social y soporte psicológico, así como la prescripción controlada de analgésicos opioides [1] [2]. Si su familiar dispone de una póliza de salud privada en Panamá, conviene notificar de inmediato a la aseguradora el diagnóstico avanzado para activar las coberturas de hospitalización domiciliaria, enfermería y equipos médicos en casa [1].

steps.title: Voluntades anticipadas y designación de representante sanitario en Panamá
steps.html:
• Derechos del paciente y directivas médicas previas: Conforme a la Ley 68 de 2003, que regula los derechos y obligaciones de los pacientes en materia de información y de decisión libre e informada en Panamá, toda persona mayor de edad y en pleno uso de sus facultades mentales tiene derecho a aceptar o rechazar procedimientos diagnósticos o terapéuticos y a dejar constancia escrita de sus preferencias sobre tratamientos al final de la vida [1] [3]. Este documento permite especificar directrices claras sobre la limitación del esfuerzo terapéutico, la no aplicación de medidas desproporcionadas o invasivas y la prioridad del confort paliativo [1].
  • Designación de interlocutor o representante sanitario e incorporación al expediente: Mientras la persona enferma conserve su capacidad de discernimiento, es altamente recomendable otorgar por escrito (y preferiblemente protocolizar ante notario público para mayor certeza probatoria) el documento de directivas médicas anticipadas, designando expresamente a un familiar o persona de confianza como representante sanitario ante el equipo médico [1] [3]. Una copia autenticada debe entregarse al médico tratante para su incorporación formal en el expediente clínico del Ministerio de Salud de Panamá (MINSA), de la Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) o de la clínica privada correspondiente, y debe conservarse otra copia accesible en el domicilio [1] [2].

steps.title: Formalización de poderes notariales y autorizaciones bancarias
steps.html:
• Otorgamiento de poder general o especial ante Notaría Pública: En el derecho panameño, los poderes de representación deben formalizarse mientras el poderdante goza de plena capacidad mental y jurídica [3] [4]. Acudir a una Notaría Pública de Circuito en Panamá (o solicitar el traslado del notario al domicilio u hospital si la movilidad está reducida) permite otorgar mediante escritura pública un Poder General o poderes especiales detallados para administrar bienes, representar a la persona enferma ante instituciones públicas y realizar actos de disposición patrimonial, los cuales se inscriben en el Registro Público de Panamá cuando la ley así lo exige [3] [4].
  • Mandatos y firmas autorizadas en entidades bancarias: Dado que las entidades bancarias panameñas suelen exigir formatos internos específicos además de las escrituras notariales, es fundamental acudir o gestionar directamente con los bancos comerciales donde la persona enferma mantenga cuentas corrientes, de ahorro o plazos fijos el registro de firmas autorizadas o apoderados bancarios [3]. Asimismo, conviene revisar y actualizar la designación expresa de beneficiarios en cuentas bancarias y fondos de ahorro para evitar bloqueos operativos futuros y asegurar la liquidez necesaria para sufragar los gastos médicos y asistenciales [2] [3].

steps.title: Prestaciones por incapacidad, dependencia y apoyos para cuidadores
steps.html:
• Subsidio por enfermedad y pensión de invalidez ante la Caja de Seguro Social: Si la persona enferma es trabajadora asegurada y la evolución de la patología le impide continuar desempeñando su actividad laboral, puede tramitar ante la Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) las incapacidades médicas prolongadas y, tras la evaluación de la Comisión Médica Calificadora, solicitar la Pensión de Invalidez por riesgo común [2]. Este trámite requiere presentar el historial clínico detallado, los informes médicos especializados y las certificaciones de cuotas aportadas en la agencia administrativa correspondiente [2] [3].
  • Acreditación de discapacidad y permisos laborales para familiares cuidadores: Cuando la enfermedad genera una limitación funcional severa o situación de dependencia, se puede gestionar la certificación ante la Secretaría Nacional de Discapacidad (SENADIS), la cual otorga acceso a protecciones legales y beneficios arancelarios en medicamentos y servicios en Panamá [1] [2]. Además, conforme a la legislación panameña de equiparación de oportunidades, los trabajadores que tengan a su cargo familiares con discapacidad o enfermedades graves debidamente acreditadas cuentan con protección laboral y permisos justificados para acompañarlos a tratamientos y consultas médicas [1] [2].

steps.title: Ordenación preventiva del testamento, seguros y documentación patrimonial
steps.html:
• Otorgamiento de testamento abierto o cerrado ante Notario Público: Para prevenir litigios o demoras en el futuro juicio sucesorio ante los tribunales civiles panameños, es aconsejable que la persona enferma otorgue o actualice su testamento (habitualmente testamento abierto por escritura pública ante Notario Público en presencia de testigos idóneos) mientras conserva íntegra su capacidad legal [3] [4]. También pueden emplearse figuras previstas en la legislación panameña, como las fundaciones de interés privado o los fideicomisos, si la estructura patrimonial familiar lo amerita [3].
  • Revisión de pólizas de seguro, activos y coordinación internacional: Conviene recopilar en un expediente físico y digital las cédulas y certificaciones de estado civil emitidas por el Tribunal Electoral de Panamá, las escrituras de propiedad inscritas, los contratos bancarios y las pólizas de seguro de vida o salud, verificando que los beneficiarios designados estén actualizados [3] [4]. Si existen bienes situados fuera de Panamá o herederos residentes en el extranjero, los poderes o documentos públicos que deban surtir efectos transfronterizos deberán contar con la Apostilla de La Haya expedida por el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Panamá (MIRE) [5] [6].

es.closingQuestion: ¿La persona enferma se atiende actualmente a través de la red pública (MINSA o CSS) o en el sector privado en Panamá, y existen bienes o familiares en el extranjero que debamos tener en cuenta?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Paraguay: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Paraguay: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Paraguay: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: At Clarvia, we extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Paraguay. Below, we explain in order the five official and practical steps that must be carried out before the Paraguayan institutions, from initial medical certification and civil registration to funeral permits, social security benefits, and judicial succession proceedings.

steps.title: Obtaining the Medical Certificate of Death
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or at home from natural causes: If the death occurs in a facility operated by the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS), the Social Security Institute (IPS), or a private hospital, the attending physician verifies the death and issues free of charge the official Medical Certificate of Death from the vital statistics subsystem [3]. When death occurs at home due to a previously treated natural illness, the attending physician certifies the cause of death and provides the original form signed and stamped with their professional license number [3].
  • Violent, sudden, or unattended death: If the death occurs suddenly without prior medical attendance, in a public place, or under suspicion of an accident or violence, the scene must not be disturbed nor should the body be moved privately [1] [3]. It is mandatory to notify the National Police and the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público - Fiscalía de turno) immediately so that the forensic physician can conduct the official examination, order an autopsy at the Judicial Morgue if necessary, and issue the medico-legal certificate together with the prosecutor's release order [1] [5].

steps.title: Registering the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Declaration before the competent civil registry office and legal deadlines: With the original medical certificate, the death must be registered before the General Directorate of the Civil Registry (REC) in the jurisdiction where the death occurred or at the registry offices located inside regional hospitals [1]. In Paraguay, registration must normally be completed within 24 to 48 hours following the death as a mandatory prerequisite for authorizing burial or cremation [1].
  • Free registration and issuance of the official death certificate: To formalize the entry in the register of deaths, the declaring family member or authorized funeral home representative must present the original Medical Certificate of Death, the Civil Identity Card (Cédula de Identidad Civil) of the deceased person, and the identity document of the declarant (accompanied by two adult witnesses where required by registry rules) [1]. Under the current fee schedule of the General Directorate of the Civil Registry (REC), registering the death and issuing the first certificate or burial permit are free of charge, and additional legalized copies can be requested for banking and inheritance procedures [1].

steps.title: Funeral Services, Health Permits, and International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a funeral provider and municipal burial or cremation licenses: Once the death is registered with the General Directorate of the Civil Registry (REC), the contracted funeral home obtains the municipal burial permit from the municipality corresponding to the chosen public or private cemetery [1] [3]. To opt for cremation, authorities require the official death certificate, the express written will of the deceased or their closest relatives, health authorization regulated by the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS), and, in cases involving prosecutorial intervention, explicit judicial authorization confirming no pending forensic inquiries remain [1] [3] [5].
  • International repatriation of remains and Hague Apostille: If the bodily remains or ashes are to be transported abroad, or if heirs outside Paraguay need to prove the death in another country, the death certificate (first authenticated by the General Directorate of the Civil Registry (REC) and the Ministry of Justice) and the embalming and transit health certificates from the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS) must receive the Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Paraguay (MRE), while also coordinating the mortuary transit permit with the destination consulate [1] [3] [4].

steps.title: Notifying Social Security, Pension Funds, and Banks
steps.html:
• Survivor benefits and funeral reimbursement with the Social Security Institute: If the deceased was an active insured worker, retiree, or pensioner under the Social Security Institute (IPS), eligible family members should apply to the Directorate of Pension Administration to report the death and claim a survivor pension (for a surviving spouse, accredited domestic partner, minor or disabled children, or dependent parents) or a lump-sum death benefit if minimum contribution years were not met [2]. Additionally, the person who paid for the funeral of an insured worker or retiree may apply to the Social Security Institute (IPS) for funeral expense reimbursement by submitting the legal invoices and the death certificate [2].
  • Commercial banks, cooperatives, and insurance companies: Using authenticated copies of the Death Certificate, family members must notify the Fiscal Pension Fund (Caja Fiscal) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (if the deceased was a civil servant), savings and credit cooperatives, commercial banks supervised by the Central Bank of Paraguay, and private insurers [1] [2]. While life insurance payouts and cooperative death subsidies with named beneficiaries are paid directly to the designated individuals, balances held in individual bank accounts are frozen until a court order or declaration of heirs is presented [5] [6].

steps.title: Estate Administration and Succession Proceedings in Paraguay
steps.html:
• Opening judicial succession proceedings before the civil courts: Under the Paraguayan Civil Code and Code of Civil Procedure, the transfer of an estate (both intestate and testate) is conducted through judicial succession proceedings filed by a licensed attorney before the Court of First Instance in Civil and Commercial Matters (or Justice of the Peace Court for smaller estates) of the deceased's last domicile, within the Judiciary of Paraguay (Supreme Court of Justice) [5] [6]. The court orders the publication of public notices (edictos) and requests reports from the Registry of Wills and the Public Registries [5] [6].
  • Declaration of heirs, asset adjudication, and international coordination: Once the notice period expires and family ties are proven using certificates from the General Directorate of the Civil Registry (REC), the judge issues the Declaration of Heirs judgment (Sentencia Declaratoria de Herederos) and, following the inventory, valuation, and partition of the estate, issues the adjudication certificate (hijuela) for registration in the General Directorate of Public Registries [1] [5] [6]. Paraguay does not levy a specific inheritance tax on the net estate, so only judicial and registry fees apply; if foreign heirs or cross-border assets are involved, powers of attorney and judicial rulings must be legalized and apostilled through the Judiciary of Paraguay (Supreme Court of Justice) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Paraguay (MRE) [4] [5].

closingQuestion: In which city or department of Paraguay did the death occur, and could you let us know whether the deceased contributed to IPS or left assets requiring international coordination?

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en Paraguay: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en Paraguay: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Desde Clarvia lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su familiar en Paraguay y le acompañamos en este momento. A continuación, explicamos de forma ordenada los cinco pasos oficiales y prácticos que deben realizarse ante las instituciones paraguayas, desde la certificación médica inicial y la inscripción registral hasta los permisos funerarios, las prestaciones de seguridad social y el juicio sucesorio.

steps.title: Obtención del certificado médico de defunción
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento en hospital o en domicilio por causas naturales: Si el deceso ocurre en un establecimiento dependiente del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS), del Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) o en un sanatorio privado, el médico tratante constata el óbito y expide gratuitamente el Certificado Médico de Defunción oficial del subsistema de estadísticas vitales [3]. Cuando la muerte acontece en el domicilio por una patología natural previamente tratada, el médico de cabecera certifica la causa del fallecimiento y entrega el formulario original firmado y sellado con su registro profesional [3].
  • Muerte violenta, súbita o sin asistencia médica previa: En caso de que el fallecimiento se produzca de manera repentina sin atención médica previa, en la vía pública o bajo sospecha de accidente o violencia, no debe alterarse el lugar ni trasladarse el cuerpo de forma particular [1] [3]. Es obligatorio dar aviso inmediato a la Policía Nacional y al Ministerio Público (Fiscalía de turno) para que el médico forense acuda al levantamiento del cadáver, disponga en su caso la autopsia en la Morgue Judicial y emita el certificado médico-legal junto con la orden fiscal de entrega [1] [5].

steps.title: Inscripción del fallecimiento en el Registro del Estado Civil
steps.html:
• Declaración ante la oficina registral competente y plazos: Con el certificado médico original, el fallecimiento debe inscribirse ante la Dirección General del Registro del Estado Civil (REC) de la circunscripción donde ocurrió el deceso o en las oficinas registrales instaladas dentro de los hospitales regionales [1]. En Paraguay, la inscripción debe efectuarse habitualmente dentro de las 24 a 48 horas siguientes al fallecimiento, como requisito indispensable previo para autorizar la inhumación o cremación [1].
  • Gratuidad de la inscripción y emisión del certificado: Para formalizar el asiento en el libro de defunciones, el familiar declarante o el representante autorizado de la empresa funeraria debe presentar el Certificado Médico de Defunción original, la Cédula de Identidad Civil de la persona fallecida y el documento de identidad del declarante (acompañado de dos testigos mayores de edad cuando la normativa registral lo requiera) [1]. Conforme al cuadro arancelario vigente de la Dirección General del Registro del Estado Civil (REC), la inscripción de la defunción y la expedición del primer certificado o permiso de inhumación son gratuitas, pudiendo solicitarse copias legalizadas adicionales para trámites bancarios y sucesorios [1].

steps.title: Servicios funerarios, permisos sanitarios y traslado internacional
steps.html:
• Contratación funeraria y licencias municipales de inhumación o cremación: Una vez inscrito el óbito en la Dirección General del Registro del Estado Civil (REC), la empresa funeraria contratada tramita la licencia de inhumación ante la Municipalidad correspondiente al cementerio público o privado elegido [1] [3]. Para optar por la cremación, se exige el certificado de defunción, la manifestación expresa del causante o de sus familiares directos, la autorización sanitaria regulada por el Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS) y, en supuestos de intervención fiscal, la autorización judicial expresa que descarte diligencias forenses pendientes [1] [3] [5].
  • Repatriación internacional de restos y Apostilla de La Haya: Si los restos mortales o las cenizas deben trasladarse al extranjero, o si existen herederos fuera de Paraguay que requieren acreditar el fallecimiento en otro Estado, el acta de defunción (previamente visada por la Dirección General del Registro del Estado Civil (REC) y el Ministerio de Justicia) y los certificados sanitarios de embalsamamiento y libre tránsito del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS) deben contar con la Apostilla de La Haya expedida por el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Paraguay (MRE), coordinando además el salvoconducto mortuorio con el consulado de destino [1] [3] [4].

steps.title: Notificación a la seguridad social, cajas de jubilaciones y bancos
steps.html:
• Prestaciones y reembolso funerario ante el Instituto de Previsión Social: Si la persona fallecida era asegurada titular activa, jubilada o pensionada del Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS), los familiares con derecho deben acudir a la Dirección de Administración de Jubilaciones para comunicar la baja y solicitar la pensión de sobrevivencia (viudez, concubinato acreditado, hijos menores o con discapacidad y padres dependientes) o la indemnización por fallecimiento cuando no se reúna la antigüedad mínima de aportes [2]. Asimismo, quien haya costeado el sepelio de un asegurado o jubilado puede gestionar ante el Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) el beneficio de reembolso por gastos funerarios presentando las facturas legales y el certificado de defunción [2].
  • Entidades bancarias, cooperativas y compañías aseguradoras: Con las copias autenticadas del Certificado de Defunción, debe notificarse el deceso a la Caja Fiscal del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (si era funcionario público), a las cooperativas de ahorro y crédito, a los bancos supervisados por el Banco Central del Paraguay y a las aseguradoras privadas [1] [2]. Mientras las indemnizaciones de seguros de vida y subsidios cooperativos con beneficiario designado se abonan directamente a los titulares nombrados, los saldos de cuentas bancarias individuales quedan bloqueados hasta la presentación de la orden judicial o declaratoria de herederos [5] [6].

steps.title: Tramitación de la herencia o sucesión en Paraguay
steps.html:
• Apertura del juicio sucesorio ante los juzgados civiles: Conforme al Código Civil y al Código Procesal Civil del Paraguay, la transmisión hereditaria (tanto en sucesiones intestadas como testamentarias) se tramita mediante juicio sucesorio patrocinado por abogado matriculado ante el Juzgado de Primera Instancia en lo Civil y Comercial (o Juzgado de Paz en cuantías menores) del último domicilio de la persona fallecida, integrado en el Poder Judicial de Paraguay (Corte Suprema de Justicia) [5] [6]. El juzgado ordena la publicación de edictos citatorios y recaba informes del Registro de Testamentos y de los Registros Públicos [5] [6].
  • Declaratoria de herederos, adjudicación y coordinación internacional: Vencido el plazo de los edictos y acreditado el vínculo mediante los certificados de la Dirección General del Registro del Estado Civil (REC), el juez dicta la Sentencia Declaratoria de Herederos y, tras el inventario, avalúo y partición de los bienes, expide el certificado de adjudicación (hijuela) para su inscripción en la Dirección General de los Registros Públicos [1] [5] [6]. En Paraguay no rige un impuesto específico a la herencia sobre el acervo sucesorio, abonándose únicamente las tasas judiciales y registrales; si existen herederos o bienes en el exterior, los poderes y resoluciones judiciales deben legalizarse y apostillarse a través del Poder Judicial de Paraguay (Corte Suprema de Justicia) y el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Paraguay (MRE) [4] [5].

es.closingQuestion: ¿En qué ciudad o departamento de Paraguay ocurrió el fallecimiento y sabrían indicarnos si la persona fallecida cotizaba en el IPS o dejó bienes que requieran coordinación con el extranjero?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Paraguay: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Paraguay: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Paraguay: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: At Clarvia, we understand how difficult this situation is for your family in Paraguay following the diagnosis of a serious or advanced illness. Below, we explain in order the five fundamental practical, medical, and legal steps to arrange while your family member retains full legal capacity.

steps.title: Activating Home or Hospital Palliative Care and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Access to the National Palliative Care Plan: In Paraguay, comprehensive pain relief and complex symptom management are organized under the National Palliative Care Plan (2024-2030) and Law No. 7340, coordinated by the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS) [1] [2]. The attending specialist physician should refer the patient to the multidisciplinary palliative care units at specialized hospitals (such as the National Cancer Institute - INCAN or regional hospitals) or coordinate follow-up with Family Health Units (USF) for home support [1] [2].
  • Social Security Institute coverage and private health plans: If your family member is an active contributor, retiree, or beneficiary of the Social Security Institute (IPS), they are entitled to inpatient coverage, controlled analgesic medication, oncology care, and home medical visits for bedridden patients or those with severely reduced mobility [3] [4]. If covered by private health insurance or prepaid medicine in Paraguay, you should submit the updated medical report to the insurer to coordinate home supplies, oxygen therapy, or home nursing care according to the policy terms [1] [2].

steps.title: Advance Directives and Appointing a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Informed consent and advance medical directives: Under the healthcare regulations of the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS) and the provisions protecting human dignity in palliative care in Paraguay, every competent adult patient has the right to receive accurate clinical information, to grant or revoke informed consent, and to express in advance their wishes regarding medical treatments they accept or refuse in advanced stages of illness [1] [2].
  • Formalization before a public notary and inclusion in the medical record: To give full evidentiary force to advance medical directives and the appointment of a trusted family member or representative as healthcare proxy (valid interlocutor before the medical team should the patient become temporarily or permanently unable to express their wishes), it is advisable to execute this declaration by public deed or notarial record before a licensed Public Notary (Escribano Público) [1] [5]. An authenticated copy should be delivered to the attending physician for mandatory inclusion in the clinical record at the Ministry of Public Health and Social Welfare (MSPyBS), the Social Security Institute (IPS), or the private hospital [1] [3].

steps.title: Executing Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Authorizations
steps.html:
• Granting a general or special power of attorney before a Public Notary: While the person who is ill retains intact decision-making capacity under the Paraguayan Civil Code, it is a priority to visit a Public Notary (or request their attendance at the home or hospital) to execute by public deed a General Power of Attorney for administration or detailed special powers of attorney [5] [6]. These powers allow the trusted representative to collect payments, represent the principal before public bodies, and manage or dispose of registrable assets, and must be registered in the Powers of Attorney section of the General Directorate of Public Registries under the Judiciary of Paraguay (Supreme Court of Justice) [5].
  • Operational authorizations with banks, finance companies, and cooperatives: Because commercial banks and savings and credit cooperatives in Paraguay normally require in-person or notarized registration of authorized signatures on their own internal forms, it is advisable to arrange co-signatories or banking representatives as early as possible [3] [5]. Likewise, retirees and pensioners of the Social Security Institute (IPS) with mobility limitations can use the biometric proof-of-life tool inside the MI IPS mobile application or register authorized representatives to collect pension payments [3] [4].

steps.title: Disability Benefits, Dependency Support, and Workplace Leave
steps.html:
• Extended medical leave allowances and disability pension with IPS: If the person who is ill is an employed contributor under the general social security scheme, they can apply to the Social Security Institute (IPS) for monetary sickness allowances during extended medical leave and, when the condition causes permanent incapacity for work, request an evaluation by the Medical Board to qualify for a Disability Pension (Jubilación por Invalidez) [3] [4]. Updated diagnostic certificates and the contribution history recorded in the social security system must be submitted [3] [4].
  • Disability certification and workplace leave for family caregivers: When the illness results in severe physical or functional dependency, a Disability Certificate can be requested from the National Secretariat for the Human Rights of Persons with Disabilities (SENADIS), which facilitates access to support programs and rehabilitative or palliative services in Paraguay [1] [2]. At the same time, working family members can coordinate with their employers for justified leave, special permissions, or flexible scheduling provided under Paraguayan labor and civil service rules to accompany close relatives undergoing serious medical treatment [1] [3].

steps.title: Preventive Will Preparation, Insurance Review, and Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing a will before a Public Notary: To ensure respect for the patrimonial wishes of the person who is ill within the mandatory forced-heirship shares (legítima) established by the Paraguayan Civil Code, it is advisable to execute a will by public act (public deed before a Public Notary and three resident witnesses) or a closed will while retaining full mental clarity [5] [6]. The will is recorded in the Registry of Wills of the Judiciary of Paraguay (Supreme Court of Justice), greatly simplifying future succession proceedings [5] [6].
  • Reviewing beneficiaries, civil status certificates, and international coordination: It is helpful to gather and verify updated birth and marriage certificates issued by the General Directorate of the Civil Registry (REC), registered property titles, and life insurance policies or cooperative funds, expressly updating beneficiary designations [5] [6]. If the person who is ill holds assets abroad or has family members residing outside Paraguay, notarial powers of attorney or public documents intended for foreign legal effect must be legalized before the Judiciary of Paraguay (Supreme Court of Justice) and apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Paraguay [5] [6].

closingQuestion: Is your family member currently receiving medical care through the Ministry of Health (MSPyBS), IPS, or private insurance in Paraguay, and are there assets or family members abroad that require coordination?

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación legal en Paraguay: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos para la planificación médica y legal ante una enfermedad terminal en Paraguay: cuidados paliativos, testamento vital (voluntades anticipadas), poderes preventivos, ayudas para cuidadores y testamento.
es.introHtml: Desde Clarvia lamentamos esta situación por la que atraviesa su familia en Paraguay ante el diagnóstico de una enfermedad grave o en etapa avanzada. A continuación, explicamos en orden los cinco pasos prácticos, médicos y jurídicos fundamentales que conviene gestionar mientras la persona enferma conserva su plena capacidad jurídica.

steps.title: Activación de cuidados paliativos domiciliarios u hospitalarios y cobertura sanitaria
steps.html:
• Acceso al Plan Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos: En Paraguay, la atención integral del dolor y el manejo de síntomas complejos se articulan bajo el Plan Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (2024-2030) y la Ley N.º 7340, coordinados por el Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS) [1] [2]. El médico especialista tratante debe derivar a la persona enferma a las unidades multidisciplinarias de cuidados paliativos de los hospitales especializados (como el Instituto Nacional del Cáncer - INCAN o los hospitales regionales) o activar el seguimiento conjunto con las Unidades de Salud de la Familia (USF) para el soporte en domicilio [1] [2].
  • Cobertura del Instituto de Previsión Social y medicina prepaga: Si su familiar es asegurado titular o beneficiario del Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS), tiene derecho a la cobertura de internación, medicación analgésica controlada, oncología y visitas médicas domiciliarias para pacientes encamados o con movilidad severamente reducida [3] [4]. En caso de contar con seguro médico privado o medicina prepaga en Paraguay, es recomendable presentar el informe médico actualizado a la entidad aseguradora para coordinar la provisión de insumos, oxígeno o enfermería domiciliaria conforme al contrato suscrito [1] [2].

steps.title: Voluntades anticipadas y designación de representante sanitario
steps.html:
• Consentimiento informado y directivas médicas anticipadas: De acuerdo con el marco normativo sanitario del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS) y las disposiciones de protección a la dignidad humana en cuidados paliativos vigentes en Paraguay, todo paciente mayor de edad y capaz tiene derecho a recibir información clínica veraz, a otorgar o revocar su consentimiento informado y a expresar anticipadamente su voluntad sobre los tratamientos médicos que desea aceptar o rechazar en fases avanzadas de la enfermedad [1] [2].
  • Formalización ante escribano público e incorporación en la historia clínica: Para dotar de plena eficacia probatoria a las directivas médicas anticipadas y a la designación de un familiar o allegado de confianza como representante sanitario (interlocutor válido ante el equipo médico en caso de que la persona enferma pierda temporal o permanentemente la posibilidad de expresarse), se aconseja otorgar dicha manifestación mediante escritura pública o acta notarial ante un Escribano Público matriculado [1] [5]. Una copia autenticada debe entregarse al médico tratante para su incorporación obligatoria en la historia clínica del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS), del Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) o del sanatorio privado [1] [3].

steps.title: Formalización de poderes notariales y autorizaciones bancarias
steps.html:
• Otorgamiento de poder general o especial ante Escribanía Pública: Mientras la persona enferma conserve intacta su capacidad de discernimiento conforme al Código Civil paraguayo, resulta prioritario acudir a un Escribano Público (o solicitar su constitución en el domicilio o centro hospitalario) para otorgar mediante escritura pública un Poder General de administración o poderes especiales detallados [5] [6]. Estos poderes permiten a la persona de confianza gestionar cobros, representar al titular ante organismos públicos y realizar actos de administración o disposición de bienes registrables, debiendo inscribirse en la sección de Poderes de la Dirección General de los Registros Públicos dependiente del Poder Judicial de Paraguay (Corte Suprema de Justicia) [5].
  • Autorizaciones operativas ante bancos, financieras y cooperativas: Dado que los bancos comerciales y las cooperativas de ahorro y crédito en Paraguay suelen exigir el registro presencial o notarial de firmas autorizadas en sus propios formularios internos, conviene tramitar cuanto antes la habilitación de cotitulares o apoderados bancarios [3] [5]. Asimismo, para los jubilados y pensionados del Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) con dificultades de desplazamiento, se puede utilizar el control biométrico de sobrevivencia en la aplicación MI IPS o gestionar apoderados autorizados para el cobro de haberes [3] [4].

steps.title: Prestaciones por incapacidad, dependencia y apoyos laborales
steps.html:
• Subsidios por reposo e invalidez en el Instituto de Previsión Social: Si la persona enferma se encuentra en relación de dependencia y aporta al régimen general, puede gestionar ante el Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) el subsidio económico por reposo médico prolongado y, cuando la patología provoque una incapacidad laboral permanente, solicitar la evaluación de la Junta Médica para acceder a la Jubilación por Invalidez [3] [4]. Es indispensable contar con los certificados de diagnóstico actualizados y el historial de aportes registrado en el sistema previsional [3] [4].
  • Certificación de discapacidad y permisos laborales para cuidadores: Cuando la enfermedad conlleva una dependencia física o funcional severa, se puede tramitar el Certificado de Discapacidad ante la Secretaría Nacional por los Derechos Humanos de las Personas con Discapacidad (SENADIS), que facilita el acceso a programas de apoyo y atención rehabilitadora o paliativa en Paraguay [1] [2]. Paralelamente, los familiares trabajadores pueden coordinar con sus empleadores las licencias, permisos justificados o adecuaciones horarias previstas en la normativa laboral y de función pública para el acompañamiento médico de familiares con enfermedades graves [1] [3].

steps.title: Ordenación preventiva del testamento, seguros y documentación
steps.html:
• Otorgamiento de testamento ante Escribano Público: Para asegurar el respeto a la voluntad patrimonial de la persona enferma dentro de los límites de las porciones legítimas de los herederos forzosos fijadas por el Código Civil paraguayo, es recomendable otorgar testamento por acto público (escritura pública ante Escribano Público y tres testigos residentes) o testamento cerrado mientras se conserve plena lucidez [5] [6]. El testamento se inscribe en el Registro de Testamentos del Poder Judicial de Paraguay (Corte Suprema de Justicia), facilitando enormemente el futuro trámite sucesorio [5] [6].
  • Revisión de beneficiarios, partidas civiles y coordinación internacional: Conviene reunir y verificar que estén actualizadas las partidas de nacimiento y matrimonio emitidas por la Dirección General del Registro del Estado Civil (REC), los títulos de propiedad inscritos y las pólizas de seguro de vida o fondos cooperativos, actualizando expresamente las designaciones de beneficiarios [5] [6]. Si la persona enferma posee bienes fuera del país o existen familiares residentes en el extranjero, los poderes notariales o documentos públicos que deban surtir efectos en el exterior deberán legalizarse ante el Poder Judicial de Paraguay (Corte Suprema de Justicia) y apostillarse ante el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Paraguay (MRE) [5] [6].

es.closingQuestion: ¿La persona enferma recibe actualmente atención médica a través del Ministerio de Salud (MSPyBS), del IPS o de un seguro privado en Paraguay, y existen bienes o familiares en el exterior que requieran coordinación?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Peru: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Peru: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Peru: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: At Clarvia, we extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Peru. Below, we explain in order the five official and practical steps that must be followed before the Peruvian authorities, covering everything from medical death certification in SINADEF and civil registration with RENIEC to funeral authorizations, pension benefits, and estate succession.

steps.title: Obtaining the Medical Certificate of Death (SINADEF)
steps.html:
• Death in a healthcare facility or at home from natural causes: When death occurs in a hospital operated by the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA), EsSalud, or a private clinic, the attending physician verifies the death and issues free of charge the General Death Certificate online through the National Computerized System of Deaths (SINADEF), providing the signed printed report to the family [1]. If the death takes place at home due to a natural illness under clinical follow-up, the attending physician or home medical service (such as PADOMI for EsSalud members) verifies the death and generates the certificate in SINADEF [1].
  • Violent, accidental, or unattended death: If death occurs suddenly without recent medical supervision, in a public place, or from external, accidental, or suspicious causes, the body must not be moved nor should direct funeral removal be arranged [1]. The National Police of Peru and the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público - Fiscalía de turno) must be notified immediately so they can order the official removal of the body and its transfer to the Medico-Legal Division (Morgue of the Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences), where the forensic pathologist will perform the statutory autopsy and issue the Death Certificate in SINADEF [1].

steps.title: Registering the Death with RENIEC and Obtaining the Official Record
steps.html:
• Automated or in-person registration of the Death Record (Acta de Defunción): Thanks to interoperability between SINADEF at the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA) and the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC), when the physician digitally signs the online certificate, the official Death Record (Acta de Defunción) is typically generated automatically in the civil registry system [1] [2]. If the medical certificate was issued manually in paper form (for example, in areas without internet connectivity), the declaring family member or authorized funeral agency must visit a registry office of the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC) or the Civil Registry Office (OREC) of the relevant municipality to register the death free of charge, normally within 48 hours of the death [2].
  • Cancellation of the DNI and requesting certified copies: For in-person registration, the declarant presents the original Medical Certificate of Death, the National Identity Document (DNI) of the deceased person (or a sworn statement of loss), and the declarant's own DNI [2]. Once the death is registered, the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC) updates the deceased's DNI status and enables the issuance of certified copies of the Death Record via its institutional web portal, branches, or multi-service kiosks, which are essential for funeral, banking, and inheritance procedures [2].

steps.title: Funeral Services, Health Permits, and International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a funeral agency and burial or cremation: With the Medical Certificate of Death and the Death Record from the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC), the family coordinates with an authorized funeral agency for mortuary preparation and burial in a municipal or private cemetery in accordance with the Law on Cemeteries and Funeral Services (Law No. 26298) [1] [2]. To carry out a cremation, regulations require sanitary authorization from the Directorate of Integrated Health Networks (DIRIS) or Regional Health Directorate of the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA), a signed request from the closest direct relative, and, where a medico-legal autopsy took place, express authorization from the provincial prosecutor in charge [1].
  • International repatriation and Hague Apostille: When bodily remains or ashes must be transported abroad, or if heirs outside Peru need to prove the death in another country, the family must obtain the sanitary permit for international transfer or cremation record from the health authority of the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA) and apostille the certified records from the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC) before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Peru (Cancillería), while coordinating the mortuary laissez-passer with the destination consulate [1] [2].

steps.title: Notifying Social Security, Pension Funds, Banks, and Insurers
steps.html:
• Funeral benefit with EsSalud and survivor pensions with ONP or AFP: The person who paid the funeral expenses of a regular insured member or pensioner of EsSalud may apply for reimbursement under the Funeral Benefit (Prestación por Sepelio) by submitting electronic payment receipts and the death record [1] [3]. Regarding pensions, if the deceased contributed to or received a pension from the National Pension System, it is mandatory to report the death to the Pension Standardization Office (ONP) and apply for survivor pensions (widowhood, orphanhood, or dependent parents) or, if there are no survivor pension beneficiaries, claim the Death Capital (Capital de Defunción) under Decree-Law No. 19990 [3] [4]. If the deceased belonged to the Private Pension System (AFP), funeral expense coverage, survivor pensions, or inheritance withdrawal of the pension fund are processed directly with the relevant AFP [3].
  • Searching bank accounts, insurance policies, and deposits via the SBS: Using the Death Record, family members can request free of charge from the Superintendency of Banking, Insurance, and AFP (SBS) the Certificate of Life and Personal Accident Insurance Policies (including mandatory employee life insurance - Seguro Vida Ley) and the Certificate of Deposits of deceased persons, which identifies all bank accounts, insurance policies, and funds held by the deceased across the Peruvian financial system [3] [5].

steps.title: Estate Administration and Succession in Peru (Notary and SUNARP)
steps.html:
• Will search and intestate succession procedure: The first succession step is to request from the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP) a Positive or Negative Certificate of Will and a Negative Certificate of Intestate Succession, along with an Index Search (Búsqueda de Índices) to identify real estate and movable property registered in the deceased's name [5] [6]. If there is no will, the forced heirs (children and descendants, parents and ascendants, or surviving spouse / registered domestic partner) can process Intestate Succession (declaration of heirs) before a Public Notary (faster non-contentious route when all heirs agree) or before the Magistrate's Court (Juzgado de Paz Letrado) of the deceased's last domicile [5] [6].
  • Registry inscription, tax rules, and heirs abroad: Once the notarial record or court judgment of intestate succession is issued (or the probate of a will is completed), it is recorded in the Registry of Intestate Successions or Registry of Wills of the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP), followed by an application to transfer ownership in the Real Property and Movable Property registries (vehicles, shares) [5] [6]. Peru does not levy an inheritance or estate tax (transfers upon death are exempt from Alcabala transfer tax), so only notarial fees and registration charges apply; if foreign heirs or foreign documents are involved, powers of attorney executed by public deed and foreign civil records must be apostilled and registered in the Registry of Mandates and Powers of the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP) [5] [6].

closingQuestion: In which province or district of Peru did the death occur, and could you let us know whether the deceased was affiliated with the ONP or an AFP, or left a will?

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en Perú: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en Perú: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Desde Clarvia lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su familiar en Perú y le acompañamos en este momento. A continuación, explicamos en orden los cinco pasos oficiales y prácticos que deben seguirse ante las entidades peruanas, abarcando desde la certificación médica en el SINADEF y el registro en el RENIEC hasta las autorizaciones funerarias, las prestaciones previsionales y la sucesión hereditaria.

steps.title: Obtención del certificado médico de defunción (SINADEF)
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento en establecimiento de salud o en domicilio por causas naturales: Cuando el deceso ocurre en un hospital del Ministerio de Salud del Perú (MINSA), de EsSalud o en una clínica privada, el médico tratante constata el óbito y emite de forma gratuita el Certificado de Defunción General en línea a través del Sistema Informático Nacional de Defunciones (SINADEF), entregando el reporte impreso y firmado a los familiares [1]. Si el fallecimiento se produce en el domicilio por una enfermedad natural bajo seguimiento clínico, el médico tratante o el servicio médico de atención domiciliaria (como PADOMI en el caso de asegurados de EsSalud) verifica el deceso y genera el certificado en el SINADEF [1].
  • Muerte violenta, accidental o sin asistencia médica previa: Si el fallecimiento sobreviene de manera repentina sin control médico reciente, en la vía pública o por causas externas, accidentales o sospechosas de criminalidad, no debe moverse el cuerpo ni contratarse el retiro funerario directo [1]. Debe comunicarse de inmediato a la Policía Nacional del Perú y al Ministerio Público (Fiscalía de turno) para que ordenen el levantamiento del cadáver y su traslado a la División Médico Legal (Morgue del Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses), donde el médico legista practicará la necropsia de ley y emitirá el Certificado de Defunción en el SINADEF [1].

steps.title: Inscripción del fallecimiento en el RENIEC y obtención del acta
steps.html:
• Inscripción automática o presencial del Acta de Defunción: Gracias a la interoperabilidad entre el SINADEF del Ministerio de Salud del Perú (MINSA) y el Registro Nacional de Identificación y Estado Civil (RENIEC), cuando el médico firma digitalmente el certificado en línea, el Acta de Defunción suele generarse de forma automatizada en el sistema registral [1] [2]. Si el certificado médico fue emitido de forma manual en formato físico (por ejemplo, en zonas sin conectividad), el familiar declarante o la agencia funeraria autorizada debe acudir a una oficina registral del Registro Nacional de Identificación y Estado Civil (RENIEC) o a la Oficina de Registros del Estado Civil (OREC) de la municipalidad correspondiente para inscribir gratuitamente el fallecimiento, habitualmente dentro de las 48 horas posteriores al deceso [2].
  • Cancelación del DNI y solicitud de copias certificadas: Para el registro presencial se presenta el Certificado de Defunción original, el Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI) de la persona fallecida (o declaración jurada de pérdida) y el DNI del declarante [2]. Una vez inscrito el óbito, el Registro Nacional de Identificación y Estado Civil (RENIEC) restringe el DNI del causante por fallecimiento y habilita la emisión de copias certificadas del Acta de Defunción a través de su plataforma web institucional, agencias o módulos multiservicio, indispensables para los trámites funerarios, bancarios y sucesorios [2].

steps.title: Servicios funerarios, permisos sanitarios y traslado internacional
steps.html:
• Contratación de agencia funeraria e inhumación o cremación: Con el Certificado de Defunción y el Acta de Defunción del Registro Nacional de Identificación y Estado Civil (RENIEC), la familia coordina con una agencia funeraria autorizada la preparación tanatológica y el sepelio en un cementerio municipal o privado conforme a la Ley de Cementerios y Servicios Funerarios (Ley N.º 26298) [1] [2]. Para realizar la cremación, se exige la autorización sanitaria de la Dirección de Redes Integradas de Salud (DIRIS) o Dirección Regional de Salud del Ministerio de Salud del Perú (MINSA), la solicitud firmada por el familiar directo más próximo y, si hubo necropsia médico-legal, la autorización expresa del fiscal provincial a cargo [1].
  • Repatriación internacional y Apostilla de La Haya: Cuando los restos mortales o las cenizas deban trasladarse al extranjero, o si existen herederos fuera del Perú que necesiten acreditar el fallecimiento en otro país, se debe tramitar la autorización sanitaria de traslado internacional o acta de cremación ante la autoridad de salud del Ministerio de Salud del Perú (MINSA) y apostillar las partidas certificadas del Registro Nacional de Identificación y Estado Civil (RENIEC) ante el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores del Perú (Cancillería), coordinando además el salvoconducto mortuorio con el consulado de destino [1] [2].

steps.title: Notificación a la seguridad social, fondos de pensiones, bancos y seguros
steps.html:
• Prestación por sepelio en EsSalud y pensiones en ONP o AFP: Quien haya sufragado los gastos funerarios de un asegurado titular regular o pensionista de EsSalud puede solicitar el reembolso de la Prestación por Sepelio presentando los comprobantes de pago electrónicos y la constancia de defunción [1] [3]. En materia previsional, si la persona fallecida aportaba o era pensionista del Sistema Nacional de Pensiones, es obligatorio registrar la baja en la Oficina de Normalización Previsional (ONP) y tramitar las pensiones de sobrevivencia (viudez, orfandad o ascendencia) o, en defecto de beneficiarios de pensión, solicitar el Capital de Defunción bajo el Decreto Ley N.º 19990 [3] [4]. Si pertenecía al Sistema Privado de Pensiones (AFP), la gestión de gastos de sepelio, pensión de sobrevivencia o entrega del fondo por herencia se realiza ante la AFP correspondiente [3].
  • Consulta de cuentas, seguros y depósitos en la SBS: Con el Acta de Defunción, los familiares pueden solicitar de forma gratuita ante la Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP (SBS) el Certificado de Pólizas de Seguro de Vida y de Accidentes Personales (incluyendo el Seguro Vida Ley para trabajadores y ex trabajadores) y la Constancia de Depósitos de personas fallecidas, lo que permite identificar todas las cuentas bancarias, seguros y fondos que mantenía el causante en el sistema financiero peruano [3] [5].

steps.title: Tramitación de la herencia o sucesión en Perú (Notaría y SUNARP)
steps.html:
• Búsqueda de testamento y trámite de sucesión intestada: El primer paso sucesorio consiste en solicitar ante la Superintendencia Nacional de los Registros Públicos (SUNARP) el Certificado Negativo o Positivo de Testamento y el Certificado Negativo de Sucesión Intestada, además de una Búsqueda de Índices para identificar los bienes muebles e inmuebles inscritos a nombre de la persona fallecida [5] [6]. Si no existe testamento, los herederos forzosos (hijos y demás descendientes, padres y ascendientes, o cónyuge / integrante sobreviviente de unión de hecho inscrita) pueden tramitar la Sucesión Intestada (declaratoria de herederos) ante un Notario Público (vía no contenciosa rápida, si hay acuerdo unánime) o ante el Juzgado de Paz Letrado del último domicilio del causante [5] [6].
  • Inscripción registral, régimen tributario y herederos en el extranjero: Una vez emitida el acta notarial o la sentencia judicial de sucesión intestada (o tramitada la comprobación y ampliación de testamento), se inscribe en el Registro de Sucesiones Intestadas o de Testamentos de la Superintendencia Nacional de los Registros Públicos (SUNARP) y posteriormente se solicita el traslado del dominio a los registros de Propiedad Inmueble y de Bienes Muebles (vehículos, acciones) [5] [6]. En el Perú no existe un impuesto a la herencia o a las sucesiones (las transferencias por causa de muerte están inafectas al Impuesto de Alcabala), debiendo abonarse únicamente los derechos notariales y las tasas registrales; si participan herederos en el exterior o existen documentos extranjeros, los poderes por escritura pública y partidas foráneas deben presentarse apostillados e inscritos en el Registro de Mandatos y Poderes de la Superintendencia Nacional de los Registros Públicos (SUNARP) [5] [6].

es.closingQuestion: ¿En qué provincia o distrito del Perú ocurrió el fallecimiento y sabrían indicarnos si la persona fallecida estaba afiliada a la ONP o a una AFP, o si dejó testamento?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Peru: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Peru: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Peru: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: At Clarvia, we understand how delicate this situation is for your family in Peru following the diagnosis of a serious or advanced illness. Below, we explain in order the five main practical, medical, and legal steps to organize while your family member retains full legal capacity.

steps.title: Activating Home or Hospital Palliative Care and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• National Palliative Care Plan under MINSA and EsSalud: In Peru, Law No. 30846 establishes the National Palliative Care Plan for Oncological and Non-Oncological Diseases, coordinated by the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA) (through specialized institutions such as the National Institute of Neoplastic Diseases - INEN, national hospitals, and the ADAMO home-care program covered by the Comprehensive Health Insurance - SIS) and by the Social Health Insurance of Peru (EsSalud) [1] [2]. The attending specialist physician must issue a clinical referral to enroll the patient in the corresponding pain therapy and palliative care unit [1].
  • Home care (PADOMI / COPHOES) and private insurance: If your family member is insured under the Social Health Insurance of Peru (EsSalud) and has severe mobility limitations, they can enroll in the Home Care Program (PADOMI) or specialized palliative support units to receive home medical and nursing visits, opioid analgesic management, and psychological support [1]. If covered by a Health Care Provider Entity (EPS) or private oncology or medical insurance in Peru, you should promptly contact the insurer to activate home hospitalization coverage and high-cost medication supply [1] [2].

steps.title: Advance Directives and Appointing a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Patient rights and advance medical directives: Under Law No. 29414 (Law Establishing the Rights of Users of Health Services) and its regulations supervised by the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA) and SUSALUD, every competent person has the right to prior, free, and express informed consent, as well as the right to accept or refuse to receive or continue medical treatment (except in public health emergencies) and to record in writing their preferences regarding clinical management and pain relief in advanced stages [1] [2].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative and notarial formalization: While the person who is ill retains full decision-making capacity (recognized and protected by Legislative Decree No. 1384 reforming the Peruvian Civil Code), it is advisable to execute in writing -preferably with a notarized signature or by public deed before a Public Notary- an advance directive and appointment of a healthcare support person or representative to act as a valid interlocutor before the medical team if they later become unable to express their wishes [1] [4]. A legalized copy should be formally added to the clinical record at the facility of the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA), the Social Health Insurance of Peru (EsSalud), or the private clinic [1] [2].

steps.title: Executing Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Authorizations
steps.html:
• Granting a power of attorney by public deed and registering with SUNARP: To prevent future financial or administrative freezes, it is a priority for the person who is ill, while retaining full mental clarity, to grant a broad general power of attorney or specific special powers by public deed before a Public Notary in Peru (who can travel to the home or hospital if the patient cannot move, verifying capacity and biometric fingerprint identity connected with the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC)) [4] [5]. This power of attorney must be registered in the Registry of Mandates and Powers of the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP) to be fully enforceable before third parties, banks, and state agencies [4] [5].
  • Advance designation of support persons and bank validation: In addition to an ordinary power of attorney, Peruvian civil law allows any adult to preventively designate before a Public Notary the person or persons who will act as their future support and safeguards (apoyos y salvaguardias), recording this act in the Personal Registry of the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP) [4]. Once registered, a certificate of validity of power of attorney (vigencia de poder) issued by the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP) should be submitted to commercial banks for internal legal validation (bastanteo de poderes) to ensure smooth operation of accounts used to cover medical expenses [4] [5].

steps.title: Disability Benefits, Dependency Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Temporary incapacity allowance and disability pension: If the person who is ill is an active worker insured with the Social Health Insurance of Peru (EsSalud), they are entitled to a monetary allowance for temporary incapacity for work starting from the 21st day of certified medical leave (the first 20 days are paid by the employer) [1]. When the Medical Evaluation Commission certifies permanent incapacity for work, the member can apply for a Disability Pension before the Pension Standardization Office (ONP) (under Decree-Law No. 19990) or before their Private Pension Fund Administrator (AFP), which also allows extraordinary withdrawal of up to 50% of pension funds in cases of accredited terminal illness or cancer diagnosis [3].
  • Paid workplace leave for family caregivers (Law No. 30012): In Peru, Law No. 30012 grants public and private sector workers the right to paid leave of up to seven calendar days (extendable against vacation entitlement or by compensatory agreement) when a direct family member is diagnosed with a serious or terminal illness, upon presenting to the employer the official medical certificate signed by an authorized healthcare professional from the Ministry of Health of Peru (MINSA), the Social Health Insurance of Peru (EsSalud), or a private clinic [1] [2].

steps.title: Preventive Will Preparation, Insurance Review, and Documentation in Peru
steps.html:
• Executing a will by public deed before a Public Notary: To simplify future estate transfer and avoid lengthy court proceedings, it is strongly advisable for the person who is ill to execute a will by public deed before a Public Notary in the presence of two qualified non-family witnesses, respecting the forced-heirship shares (legítima) set by the Peruvian Civil Code [4] [6]. The notary immediately records the existence of the will in the Registry of Wills of the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP), keeping its contents confidential during the testator's lifetime [4] [6].
  • Reviewing civil records, insurance policies, pension funds, and international coordination: It is helpful to gather and verify certified copies of birth and marriage records or registered domestic partnerships with the National Registry of Identification and Civil Status (RENIEC) and the National Superintendency of Public Registries (SUNARP), as well as updating beneficiary designations on life insurance policies, employee life insurance (Seguro Vida Ley), and pension accounts with the Pension Standardization Office (ONP) or AFP [3] [4] [5] [6]. If assets are located outside Peru or family members reside abroad, notarial powers of attorney or public documents intended for cross-border use must carry the Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Peru [4] [5].

closingQuestion: Is your family member currently receiving care through EsSalud, MINSA (SIS), or a private clinic, and are they affiliated with the ONP or an AFP in Peru?
