title: What to Do When Someone Dies in São Tomé and Príncipe: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in São Tomé and Príncipe: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for São Tomé and Príncipe: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in São Tomé and Príncipe. We know that managing medical requirements, civil registration, and succession procedures during a period of bereavement is demanding, so we have set out below the five official and practical steps that a family must follow in order in São Tomé and Príncipe.

steps.title: Medical verification of death and issuance of the medical death certificate
steps.html:
• Death occurring in a hospital facility: When a death occurs at the Ayres de Menezes Hospital (in São Tomé), the Dr. Manuel Quaresma Dias da Graça Hospital (in the Autonomous Region of Príncipe), or a district health center, the attending physician clinically verifies the death and issues the medical death certificate (certificado médico de óbito) free of charge, recording the identity of the deceased person, the date, the time, and the cause of death [1].
  • Death occurring at home: If the death occurred at home under medical care, the family must notify the district health center or local health delegate so that a clinician can verify the death and issue the medical declaration required for mortuary transfer and civil registration [1].
  • Unattended death or suspicious circumstances: Where the death occurred without prior medical attendance, as a result of an accident, or under suspicious circumstances, it is mandatory to report the matter to the National Police (Polícia Nacional) or the Judicial Police (Polícia Judiciária) and the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público) so that a forensic examination is performed before the body is released [1].

steps.title: Official death registration at the civil registry office
steps.html:
• Where to declare and statutory deadlines: The death must be declared at the Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil, located at Praça do Povo in the Água Grande District of São Tomé) or at the regional delegations and civil registry posts across the districts and the Autonomous Region of Príncipe, supervised by the Directorate-General of Registries and Notary (Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado). The declaration must be made within the statutory 48-hour period following death or medical verification [1] [2].
  • Who may declare and required documents: The declaration is made by the closest present relative, a family representative, or the authorized funeral director. You must present the medical death certificate, the personal registration booklet (cédula pessoal) or National Identity Card (Bilhete de Identidade) of the deceased person, the declarant's identification document, and the name of the cemetery where burial will take place [1] [2].
  • Issuance of the death certificate and official fees: Once the death entry (assento de óbito) is recorded by the Directorate-General of Registries and Notary, the burial permit (guia de enterramento) and the official death certificate (certidão de óbito) are issued (with standard reference fees of 75.00 Dobras for normal processing or 97.50 Dobras for urgent processing). It is advisable to request several certified copies immediately for social security, banks, and notarial proceedings [1] [2].

steps.title: Funeral arrangements, burial, and international repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial permit and municipal cemeteries: No burial may take place in a public cemetery (managed by the District Councils or the Regional Government of Príncipe) without the burial permit issued by the civil registry office and payment of the municipal burial fees. Burial is the standard practice across the archipelago, as crematoria are not in general operation [1].
  • International repatriation of mortal remains: If the family wishes to repatriate the body abroad, or bring home the mortal remains of a Santomean citizen who died outside the country (whose foreign death record is transcribed at the Central Registry Office - Conservatória dos Registos Centrais), it is necessary to obtain public health clearance, embalming and sealing in a hermetic zinc-lined coffin, and a mortuary laissez-passer (livre-trânsito mortuário) through consular channels [1] [2].
  • Legalization of documents for international use: Death certificates or powers of attorney intended to produce legal effect abroad require notarial authentication and diplomatic or consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Communities and the relevant foreign embassy or consulate [2] [3].

steps.title: Notifying social security, banks, and insurance companies
steps.html:
• Funeral grant and death benefits: When the deceased person was an insured worker or pensioner under the mandatory social security system, surviving relatives should notify the National Social Security Institute (Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social) to claim the funeral grant (subsídio de funeral) and lump-sum death benefits designed to offset immediate household expenses [4] [5].
  • Survivor pension: The surviving spouse (or recognized de facto partner), minor, student, or disabled children, and eligible dependent ascendants may apply to the National Social Security Institute for a survivor pension (pensão de sobrevivência), submitting the certified death certificate, the deceased person's identification document, marriage and birth certificates of the beneficiaries, and bank account details [4] [5].
  • Bank accounts and insurance contracts: Heirs must notify commercial banks where the deceased person held accounts or deposits, submitting the death certificate to freeze individual withdrawals and obtain date-of-death balance statements, as well as notifying insurance companies of any life policies [3] [4].

steps.title: Declaration of heirs, estate inventory, and inheritance division
steps.html:
• Notarial deed of declaration of heirs: To establish legally who the statutory or testamentary heirs of the deceased person are, the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must appear at the Notarial Office (Cartório Notarial, operating under the Directorate-General of Registries and Notary) to execute a public deed of declaration of heirs (escritura pública de habilitação de herdeiros), presenting the death certificate, birth and marriage certificates of the heirs, and a check for any registered will [1] [3].
  • Extrajudicial division or judicial inventory: Where all heirs are adults with full capacity and agree unanimously on the allocation of movable and immovable property, the deed of division (escritura de partilha) is executed directly at the Notarial Office; if there are minor heirs, incapacitated beneficiaries, or disputes among heirs, a mandatory judicial inventory (processo de inventário) must be filed with the Court of First Instance (Tribunal de Primeira Instância) [2] [3].
  • Tax obligations and foreign heirs: The head of the estate must report the succession transfer to the Tax Directorate (Direção dos Impostos) to settle applicable inheritance tax and register property transfers at the Land Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Predial). Heirs residing abroad may be represented in the declaration of heirs and division through a duly legalized public power of attorney recognized by the Notarial Office [2] [3].

closingQuestion: So that we can tailor this guidance to your family's specific situation, in which district of São Tomé or in the Autonomous Region of Príncipe did the death occur, and are there heirs or estate assets located abroad?

pt.title: O que fazer quando alguém falece em São Tomé e Príncipe: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um óbito em São Tomé e Príncipe: certificado médico de óbito, contratação de agência funerária, registo civil, subsídio por morte e pensão de sobrevivência, e habilitação de herdeiros ou inventário.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos as nossas sinceras condolências pelo falecimento do seu familiar em São Tomé e Príncipe. Sabemos que tratar das exigências médicas, registos civis e procedimentos sucessórios durante o luto é complexo, pelo que organizámos abaixo os cinco passos oficiais e práticos que a família deve seguir por ordem em São Tomé e Príncipe.

steps.title: Verificação médica do óbito e emissão do certificado médico de óbito
steps.html:
• Óbito ocorrido em unidade hospitalar: Quando o falecimento ocorre no Hospital Ayres de Menezes (em São Tomé), no Hospital Dr. Manuel Quaresma Dias da Graça (na Região Autónoma do Príncipe) ou num centro de saúde distrital, o médico de serviço verifica clinicamente o óbito e emite gratuitamente o certificado médico de óbito com a identificação da pessoa falecida, a data, a hora e a causa da morte [1].
  • Óbito ocorrido no domicílio: Se a morte ocorreu em casa sob acompanhamento médico, a família deve comunicar o sucedido ao centro de saúde ou delegado de saúde da área distrital para verificação clínica e emissão da declaração médica de óbito que permite o transporte para a morgue ou o registo civil [1].
  • Morte sem assistência médica ou sob circunstâncias suspeitas: Caso o óbito tenha ocorrido sem assistência médica prévia, por acidente ou sob suspeita de crime, é obrigatório participar o facto à Polícia Nacional ou à Polícia Judiciária e ao Ministério Público, para que seja realizada inspeção médico-legal antes da libertação do corpo [1].

steps.title: Registo oficial do óbito na conservatória do registo civil
steps.html:
• Onde declarar e prazos legais: O óbito deve ser declarado na Conservatória do Registo Civil (situada na Praça do Povo, no Distrito de Água Grande, em São Tomé) ou nas delegações regionais e postos de registo civil dos distritos e da Região Autónoma do Príncipe, sob tutela da Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado. A participação deve ser feita no prazo legal de 48 horas após o falecimento ou a verificação médica [1] [2].
  • Quem pode declarar e documentos necessários: A declaração cabe ao familiar mais próximo presente, ao representante da família ou ao encarregado do serviço funerário. São exigidos o certificado médico de óbito, a cédula pessoal ou Bilhete de Identidade da pessoa falecida, o documento de identificação do declarante e a indicação do cemitério onde se realizará a sepultura [1] [2].
  • Emissão da certidão de óbito e emolumentos: Lavrado o assento de óbito pela Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado, é emitida a guia de enterramento e a certidão de óbito (com processo normal de referência de 75,00 Dobras ou urgente de 97,50 Dobras). Recomendamos requerer desde logo várias certidões autenticadas para instruir os processos na segurança social, nos bancos e no notariado [1] [2].

steps.title: Organização do funeral, inumação e trasladação internacional
steps.html:
• Licença de inumação e cemitérios camarários: Nenhuma inumação pode realizar-se nos cemitérios públicos (geridos pelas Câmaras Distritais ou pelo Governo Regional do Príncipe) sem a guia de enterramento emitida pela conservatória do registo civil e o pagamento das taxas camarárias de sepultura. A inumação constitui a prática geral no arquipélago, não existindo instalações crematórias de uso corrente [1].
  • Trasladação internacional de restos mortais: Se a família pretender trasladar o corpo para o estrangeiro, ou repatriar os restos mortais de um cidadão são-tomense falecido fora do país (cuja transcrição corre na Conservatória dos Registos Centrais), é necessário obter autorização sanitária das autoridades de saúde pública, preparação tanatológica com encerramento em urna hermética de zinco e livre-trânsito mortuário emitido em articulação consular [1] [2].
  • Legalização de documentos para uso internacional: As certidões de óbito ou procurações que devam produzir efeitos jurídicos no estrangeiro carecem de reconhecimento notarial e legalização diplomática ou consular junto do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros, Cooperação e Comunidades e da embaixada ou consulado do país de destino [2] [3].

steps.title: Comunicação à segurança social, bancos e seguradoras
steps.html:
• Subsídio de funeral e subsídio por morte: Quando a pessoa falecida era trabalhadora inscrita ou pensionista da segurança social obrigatória, os familiares devem comunicar o óbito ao Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social para requerer o subsídio de funeral e as prestações pecuniárias por morte destinadas a compensar os encargos imediatos do agregado familiar [4] [5].
  • Pensão de sobrevivência: O cônjuge sobrevivo (ou unido de facto reconhecido), os filhos menores, estudantes ou incapacitados e, nos casos previstos na lei, os ascendentes a cargo têm direito a requerer a pensão de sobrevivência junto do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social, apresentando a certidão de óbito, o documento de identificação da pessoa falecida, certidões de casamento e nascimento dos beneficiários e comprovativo de conta bancária [4] [5].
  • Contas bancárias e contratos de seguro: Os herdeiros devem notificar os bancos comerciais onde o seu familiar detinha contas ou depósitos, entregando a certidão de óbito para bloqueio preventivo de movimentações individuais e apuramento dos saldos à data do óbito, bem como acionar eventuais apólices de seguro [3] [4].

steps.title: Habilitação de herdeiros, inventário e partilha da herança
steps.html:
• Escritura de habilitação de herdeiros: Para comprovar juridicamente a qualidade de herdeiros legitimários ou testamentários da pessoa falecida, o cabeça-de-casal deve dirigir-se ao Cartório Notarial (integrado na Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado) para lavrar a escritura pública de habilitação de herdeiros, apresentando a certidão de óbito, as certidões de nascimento e casamento dos sucessores e a verificação de eventual testamento [1] [3].
  • Partilha extrajudicial ou inventário judicial: Sendo todos os herdeiros maiores, capazes e unânimes quanto à adjudicação dos bens imóveis e móveis, a escritura de partilha é celebrada diretamente no Cartório Notarial; havendo herdeiros menores, interditos ou litígio entre os interessados, é obrigatório requerer processo de inventário junto do Tribunal de Primeira Instância [2] [3].
  • Obrigações fiscais e herdeiros no estrangeiro: O cabeça-de-casal deve participar a transmissão sucessória junto da Direção dos Impostos para liquidação do imposto sucessório devido e promover o averbamento dos imóveis na Conservatória do Registo Predial. Se algum herdeiro residir no estrangeiro, pode fazer-se representar na habilitação e partilha mediante procuração pública devidamente legalizada e reconhecida pelo Cartório Notarial [2] [3].

pt.closingQuestion: Para que possamos adaptar estas informações à situação específica da sua família, em que distrito de São Tomé ou na Região Autónoma do Príncipe ocorreu o falecimento e existem herdeiros ou bens situados no estrangeiro?

titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in São Tomé and Príncipe: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for São Tomé and Príncipe: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand what a difficult time your family is experiencing following the diagnosis of a serious or progressive illness in São Tomé and Príncipe. While the person who is ill retains full legal capacity and decision-making ability, it is essential to organize clinical care, legal representation instruments, and social and property protection in advance. Below we outline the five practical, clinical, and legal steps to follow in São Tomé and Príncipe.

steps.title: Coordinating palliative care and hospital or home medical support
steps.html:
• Hospital and district clinical coordination: The family should coordinate an ongoing care, pain-control, and symptom-management plan with the attending medical team at the Ayres de Menezes Hospital (in São Tomé), the Dr. Manuel Quaresma Dias da Graça Hospital (in Príncipe), or district health centers, requesting detailed medical reports on the diagnosis and clinical progression [4] [5].
  • Medical boards and medical evacuation: When a serious condition requires specialized treatment unavailable in the archipelago, the attending physician may refer the case to the Health Medical Board (Junta Médica de Saúde) to evaluate eligibility for medical evacuation under bilateral healthcare cooperation agreements or social security coverage [4] [5].
  • Organizing home care: To maintain comfort at home, it is advisable to keep an updated folder with all prescriptions, medical reports, district health team contacts, and civil identification documents ready for any urgent hospital visit [1] [5].

steps.title: Advance medical directives, informed consent, and healthcare proxy
steps.html:
• Written declaration of clinical preferences: Although São Tomé and Príncipe does not operate a dedicated electronic living will registry, the person who is ill may exercise the right to informed consent by signing a written declaration - with an in-person signature notarized at the Notarial Office (Cartório Notarial) - setting out instructions regarding invasive treatments, hospitalization, and comfort care [3].
  • Appointing a family medical spokesperson: While fully lucid, the person who is ill should formally designate a trusted family member as primary spokesperson before the attending physicians and hospital administration, asking that this appointment be placed in the medical file [3] [5].
  • Authorization to access medical records: It is advisable to sign an explicit written authorization enabling the designated family representative to request medical reports, laboratory results, and clinical certificates needed for medical boards or social security claims [3] [4].

steps.title: Executing a public power of attorney at a notary office and bank mandates
steps.html:
• Notarial public power of attorney: While the person who is ill enjoys full civil capacity and discernment, they should appear before the Notarial Office supervised by the Directorate-General of Registries and Notary (Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado) to execute a public power of attorney (procuração pública) granting specific powers for administrative management, tax representation, property administration, and banking operations to a trusted attorney-in-fact [1] [3].
  • Notarial attendance at home or in hospital: If the person who is ill has severely restricted mobility but remains fully lucid, the family may request that an authorized officer from the Notarial Office attend the home or hospital ward to verify the grantor's capacity and record the public instrument [3].
  • Validating bank account mandates: Because commercial banks in São Tomé and Príncipe normally require in-person registration of powers of attorney on customer signature records, it is advisable to present the public power of attorney directly at the patient's bank branch to validate account operation powers while the account holder can confirm the mandate [3].

steps.title: Claiming sickness or disability benefits and caregiver support
steps.html:
• Sickness allowance and disability pension: If the person who is ill is an insured worker under the contributory scheme and suffers a permanent reduction of working capacity exceeding two-thirds (66%) due to a non-occupational illness expected to last at least three years, they may apply for a disability pension (pensão de invalidez) or sickness allowance (subsídio de doença) from the National Social Security Institute (Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social) [4] [5].
  • Supporting documentation and proof of life: Applications submitted to the National Social Security Institute must include the National Identity Card (Bilhete de Identidade), beneficiary card, medical certificate or Health Board determination, and contribution record. Pensioners must also comply with periodic proof-of-life (prova de vida) requirements established by the institution [4] [5].
  • Workplace documentation for family caregivers: Working family members who assist the person who is ill during medical appointments, hospitalizations, or medical board assessments should request hospital attendance certificates to justify absences with their employer [5].

steps.title: Preventive preparation of wills, insurance beneficiaries, and property records
steps.html:
• Public or sealed will: To organize succession in advance within the disposable portion (quota disponível) permitted under Santomean civil law (which protects the forced share reserved for statutory heirs such as a spouse, descendants, or ascendants), the person who is ill may execute a public will (testamento público) or have a sealed will (testamento cerrado) approved at the Notarial Office, with central registration maintained by the Central Registry Office (Conservatória dos Registos Centrais) [2] [3].
  • Updating civil and land registry documents: It is prudent to verify the validity of the National Identity Card of the person who is ill and close relatives, obtain updated birth and marriage certificates from the Directorate-General of Registries and Notary, review insurance policies, and confirm property titles at the Land Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Predial) [1] [2].
  • Cross-border coordination of assets or heirs: Where there are assets, bank accounts, or heirs residing abroad, powers of attorney or public instruments executed at the Notarial Office must be legalized through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Communities and the relevant consular mission to take full legal effect abroad [2] [3].

closingQuestion: So that we can outline the most appropriate steps for your family's situation, in which district of São Tomé or in the Autonomous Region of Príncipe is the person who is ill located, and are they registered with the National Social Security Institute?

pt.title: Doença terminal e administração em fim de vida em São Tomé e Príncipe: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos para o planeamento médico e jurídico em situação de doença terminal em São Tomé e Príncipe: cuidados paliativos, diretivas antecipadas de vontade, procurações, apoios ao cuidador e organização sucessória.
pt.introHtml: Lamentamos o momento difícil que a sua família atravessa após o diagnóstico de uma doença grave ou progressiva em São Tomé e Príncipe. Enquanto a pessoa doente conserva plena capacidade de decisão e discernimento, é fundamental estruturar de forma preventiva o acompanhamento clínico, os instrumentos de representação jurídica e a proteção social e patrimonial. Apresentamos abaixo os cinco passos práticos, clínicos e legais recomendados em São Tomé e Príncipe.

steps.title: Articulação dos cuidados paliativos e acompanhamento médico domiciliário ou hospitalar
steps.html:
• Coordenação clínica hospitalar e distrital: A família deve articular o plano de tratamento continuado, controlo da dor e suporte sintomático junto da equipa médica assistente no Hospital Ayres de Menezes (em São Tomé), no Hospital Dr. Manuel Quaresma Dias da Graça (no Príncipe) ou nos centros de saúde distritais, solicitando relatórios médicos detalhados sobre o diagnóstico e a evolução clínica [4] [5].
  • Juntas médicas e evacuação sanitária: Quando o quadro clínico exige tratamentos especializados não disponíveis no arquipélago, o médico assistente pode encaminhar o processo para avaliação pela Junta Médica de Saúde com vista a eventual evacuação sanitária ao abrigo dos acordos de cooperação em saúde ou da cobertura previdenciária [4] [5].
  • Organização dos cuidados no domicílio: Para assegurar o conforto da pessoa doente em casa, convém manter um dossier atualizado com todas as prescrições, relatórios clínicos, contactos da equipa de saúde distrital e documentos de identificação prontos para qualquer urgência [1] [5].

steps.title: Registo de diretivas médicas, consentimento informado e representante para cuidados de saúde
steps.html:
• Declaração escrita de vontade clínica: Embora São Tomé e Príncipe não disponha de um registo público eletrónico específico para diretivas antecipadas de vontade, a pessoa doente pode, no exercício do seu direito ao consentimento informado, redigir uma declaração escrita - com reconhecimento presencial de assinatura no Cartório Notarial - manifestando as suas instruções quanto a tratamentos invasivos, internamentos e cuidados de conforto [3].
  • Designação de acompanhante e representante familiar: Enquanto mantém plena lucidez, a pessoa doente deve indicar formalmente um familiar de confiança como interlocutor principal perante os médicos assistentes e a direção clínica do hospital, solicitando que essa nomeação seja anexada ao processo clínico [3] [5].
  • Autorização para acesso a documentação médica: É recomendável subscrever uma autorização expressa que habilite o representante familiar a solicitar relatórios médicos, resultados de análises e atestados necessários para juntas médicas ou processos junto da segurança social [3] [4].

steps.title: Outorga de procuração pública em cartório notarial e mandatos bancários
steps.html:
• Procuração pública notarial: Enquanto a pessoa doente goza de plena capacidade civil e discernimento, deve comparecer no Cartório Notarial (sob tutela da Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado) para outorgar uma procuração pública que confira poderes especiais de gestão administrativa, representação fiscal, administração de imóveis e movimentação bancária a um procurador de confiança [1] [3].
  • Diligência notarial no domicílio ou no hospital: Se a pessoa doente tiver mobilidade severamente reduzida mas conservar inteira lucidez, a família pode requerer a deslocação externa de um funcionário autorizado do Cartório Notarial ao domicílio ou à unidade hospitalar para verificar a capacidade do outorgante e lavrar o instrumento público [3].
  • Validação de mandatos bancários: Como as instituições bancárias em São Tomé e Príncipe exigem frequentemente o registo presencial de procurações nas suas fichas de cliente, recomenda-se apresentar a procuração pública diretamente no banco da pessoa doente para validar os poderes de movimentação enquanto o titular pode confirmar o mandato [3].

steps.title: Requerimento de prestações sociais por doença ou invalidez e apoio aos cuidadores
steps.html:
• Subsídio de doença e pensão de invalidez: Se a pessoa doente é trabalhadora inscrita no regime contributivo e sofre uma redução definitiva da capacidade de trabalho superior a dois terços (66%) em consequência de doença não profissional que se presuma manter-se por pelo menos três anos, pode requerer a pensão de invalidez ou o subsídio de doença junto do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social [4] [5].
  • Documentação e prova de vida: O requerimento apresentado ao Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social deve ser acompanhado do Bilhete de Identidade, cartão de beneficiário, declaração médica ou deliberação da Junta de Saúde e histórico de contribuições. Os pensionistas devem também observar os procedimentos periódicos de prova de vida exigidos pela instituição [4] [5].
  • Apoio e justificação laboral de cuidadores familiares: Os familiares trabalhadores que prestem assistência direta à pessoa doente em consultas, internamentos ou deslocações médicas devem solicitar declarações hospitalares de acompanhamento para justificar ausências perante a entidade empregadora [5].

steps.title: Organização preventiva do testamento, beneficiários de seguros e documentação patrimonial
steps.html:
• Testamento público ou cerrado: Para organizar preventivamente a sucessão dentro dos limites da quota disponível previstos na lei civil são-tomense (salvaguardando a quota legítima reservada aos herdeiros legitimários, como cônjuge, descendentes ou ascendentes), a pessoa doente pode outorgar testamento público ou aprovar testamento cerrado no Cartório Notarial, com registo central assegurado pela Conservatória dos Registos Centrais [2] [3].
  • Regularização de registos civis e prediais: Convém verificar a validade do Bilhete de Identidade da pessoa doente e dos seus familiares, reunir certidões de nascimento e de casamento atualizadas junto da Direção-Geral dos Registos e do Notariado, rever apólices de seguro e confirmar a titularidade de imóveis na Conservatória do Registo Predial [1] [2].
  • Coordenação internacional de bens ou herdeiros: Caso existam bens, contas bancárias ou herdeiros residentes no estrangeiro, quaisquer procurações ou documentos públicos lavrados no Cartório Notarial devem ser legalizados junto do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros, Cooperação e Comunidades e da representação consular competente para produzirem plenos efeitos fora do país [2] [3].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Equatorial Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Equatorial Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Equatorial Guinea: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are deeply sorry for the death of your family member in Equatorial Guinea. Below, we explain in order the five main official medical, civil registration, funeral, social security, and succession steps to follow before the institutions of Equatorial Guinea.

steps.title: Obtaining the Medical Certificate of Death or Medico-Legal Intervention
steps.html:
• Death in a public hospital or private clinic: When a death occurs from natural causes in a hospital within the network of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare (Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social - MINSABS, such as the Regional Hospital of Malabo, the Regional Hospital of Bata, or reference medical centres such as La Paz) or in an authorised clinic, the attending physician or on-duty doctor issues the official medical certificate of death (certificado médico de defunción) confirming the identity of the deceased person, the date, the time, and the clinical cause of death [1] [5].
  • Natural death at home: If the death occurs at home, the family must notify the attending physician or go to the nearest public health centre or hospital of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare so that a qualified physician can physically verify the death and issue the medical certification required for civil registration [1] [5].
  • Violent, accidental, sudden, or unattended death: If the death occurs in a public place, by accident, suddenly without a recent medical history, or under suspicious circumstances, the body must not be moved without police and judicial intervention. The National Police, the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Fiscal), and the forensic physician attached to the competent Investigating Court (Juzgado de Instrucción) of the Administration of Justice of Equatorial Guinea (Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial) must intervene to conduct the official removal of the body, perform the medico-legal autopsy at the hospital morgue, and issue the judicial order authorising registration and burial [2] [3].

steps.title: Registering the Death with the Civil Registry of Equatorial Guinea
steps.html:
• Competent authority (District or Municipal Civil Registry): Every death occurring in national territory must be declared before the Civil Registry (Registro Civil) under the Ministry of Justice, Worship and Penitentiary Institutions and the Administration of Justice of Equatorial Guinea corresponding to the district or municipality where the death occurred (for example, in Malabo, Bata, Mongomo, Ebebiyín, or Luba) [2] [3].
  • Statutory deadlines and registration: Under the civil registration rules in force in Equatorial Guinea, the death declaration must be made immediately, normally within the first 24 to 48 hours following death and always before burial takes place; if the ordinary period elapses without registration, an administrative or judicial late-registration file (expediente de inscripción fuera de plazo) must be processed before the competent court [2] [3].
  • Required documents and Death Record: The declaring family member must present the original medical certificate of death (or judicial forensic authorisation), the Personal Identity Document (Documento de Identidad Personal - DIP) or passport of the deceased person, and the identity documents of the declarant and any witnesses required by the registry office [2] [4]. Once the entry is recorded, the Civil Registry issues the certified Death Record (certificación literal del Acta de Defunción) and the burial permit (licencia de enterramiento); it is advisable to request several certified copies for social security, banking, and inheritance procedures [2] [4].

steps.title: Funeral Services, Health Permits for Burial or Cremation, and Repatriation
steps.html:
• Funeral arrangements and burial permit: With the medical certificate of death and the burial licence issued by the Civil Registry, the family or an authorised funeral provider coordinates preservation at the hospital morgue or funeral home and obtains the municipal burial permit from the relevant City Council (such as the City Council of Malabo or Bata), complying with the public health standards of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare [1] [2].
  • Sanitary requirements for cremation: Because burial is the standard practice in the country and cremation facilities are limited, any request for cremation or transfer for incineration requires a medical certificate of natural death, express authorisation from immediate family members or a testamentary disposition, and prior judicial authorisation if the criminal courts intervened [1] [2].
  • Diplomatic legalisation and international repatriation of remains: Equatorial Guinea is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so Equatoguinean public documents intended for use abroad (or the file to repatriate a coffin or urn outside the country) require the full diplomatic legalisation chain: prior validation by the Ministry of Justice, legalisation by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Diaspora, and subsequent legalisation by the accredited foreign embassy or consulate (such as the Consulate General of Spain in Malabo when the deceased person or heirs have ties to Spain), together with the medical certificate of embalming, the certificate of sealing in a hermetic zinc-lined coffin, and the sanitary transit permit issued by the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare [1] [4].

steps.title: Notifying INSESO, Banks, Employers, and Insurers
steps.html:
• Death and survivor benefits at INSESO: If the deceased person was an active insured worker or pensioner of the National Social Security Institute (Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social - INSESO), family members must report the death at the INSESO offices in Malabo, Bata, or provincial capitals to apply for the death grant (subsidio por defunción, intended to cover funeral expenses) and survivor pensions (widowhood pension for the surviving spouse and orphanhood pension for minor or disabled children) by submitting the Death Certificate, the INSESO membership card, the family book or marriage and birth certificates, and funeral invoices [3].
  • Employment settlement and public service benefits: If your family member worked in the private sector or public administration, the death certificate must be submitted to the employer or to the Treasury and relevant ministry to collect accrued unpaid wages, unused leave, and statutory death indemnities under the General Labour Regulations [2] [3].
  • Freezing and administration of bank accounts and insurance: The death should be reported to all banks operating in Equatorial Guinea (such as BANGE, CCEI Bank GE, or Ecobank) and insurance companies; individual bank accounts held by the deceased person are preventively frozen upon notification until the heirs establish their succession title and settle applicable duties, whereas life insurance policies are paid to the beneficiaries named in the policy [2] [3].

steps.title: Estate Administration and Succession Proceedings in Equatorial Guinea
steps.html:
• Succession legal framework (testate or intestate): In Equatorial Guinea, the rules of the Hispanic-tradition Civil Code applicable in the country coexist with legally recognised customary family rules; succession opens upon death and is governed by a will executed before a Notary or, in the absence of a valid will, by the rules of intestate succession [2].
  • Declaration of heirs and partition before a Notary or Court: Where a valid will exists or all heirs are in unanimous agreement, the interested parties appear before a public Notary office under the Administration of Justice of Equatorial Guinea with the literal death certificate, verification of last wills, and birth and marriage certificates to execute the public deed of acceptance and adjudication of the estate; in the absence of a will or if disputes arise among co-heirs, an intestate declaration of heirs or probate proceeding is brought before the competent Court of First Instance and Instruction (Juzgado de Primera Instancia e Instrucción) [2] [4].
  • Inheritance duties, property registration, and heirs abroad: Before registering any transfer of real estate ownership in the Property Registry or releasing frozen bank funds, inheritance and transfer duties must be settled with the tax administration; if any heirs reside outside Equatorial Guinea, they may grant a special power of attorney for litigation and estate acceptance before an Equatoguinean consulate in their country of residence or before a foreign notary duly legalised through diplomatic channels (for instance, via the Consulate General of Spain in Malabo or the relevant diplomatic mission) [2] [4].

closingQuestion: In which city or district of Equatorial Guinea did the death occur, and do we know whether your family member contributed to the National Social Security Institute (INSESO), so that we can clarify the steps applicable to your case?

es.title: Qué hacer cuando fallece un familiar en Guinea Ecuatorial: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos tras una defunción en Guinea Ecuatorial: certificado médico de defunción, contratación de servicios funerarios, inscripción en el Registro Civil, pensiones de supervivencia e impuesto de sucesiones.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos profundamente el fallecimiento de su familiar en Guinea Ecuatorial. A continuación, explicamos en orden los cinco pasos oficiales, médicos, registrales, funerarios, previsionales y sucesorios que deben realizarse ante las instituciones ecuatoguineanas.

steps.title: Obtención del certificado médico de defunción o intervención médico-legal
steps.html:
• Fallecimiento en hospital público o clínica privada: Cuando el deceso ocurre por causas naturales en un centro hospitalario de la red del Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social (como el Hospital Regional de Malabo, el Hospital Regional de Bata o los centros hospitalarios de referencia como La Paz) o en una clínica autorizada, el médico tratante o el facultativo de guardia expide el certificado médico oficial de defunción acreditando la identidad de la persona fallecida, la fecha, la hora y la causa clínica del fallecimiento [1] [5].
  • Fallecimiento por causas naturales en el domicilio: Si la muerte sobreviene en el hogar, la familia debe avisar al médico tratante o acudir al centro de salud u hospital público más próximo del Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social para que un facultativo constate físicamente el óbito y extienda la certificación médica necesaria para el registro civil [1] [5].
  • Muerte violenta, accidental, súbita o sin asistencia médica: Si el fallecimiento se produce en la vía pública, por accidente, de forma repentina sin historial clínico reciente o bajo circunstancias sospechosas, no debe movilizarse el cuerpo sin intervención policial y judicial. Es obligatoria la actuación de la Policía Nacional, del Ministerio Fiscal y del médico forense adscrito al Juzgado de Instrucción competente de la Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial para el levantamiento del cadáver, la práctica de la autopsia médico-legal en el depósito hospitalario y la emisión de la orden judicial que autoriza la inscripción e inhumación [2] [3].

steps.title: Inscripción del fallecimiento en el Registro Civil de Guinea Ecuatorial
steps.html:
• Autoridad competente (Registro Civil del distrito o municipio): Toda defunción ocurrida en territorio nacional debe declararse ante el Registro Civil dependiente del Ministerio de Justicia, Culto e Instituciones Penitenciarias y de la Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial correspondiente al distrito o municipio donde se produjo el fallecimiento (por ejemplo, en Malabo, Bata, Mongomo, Ebebiyín o Luba) [2] [3].
  • Plazos legales e inscripción: Conforme a la normativa registral vigente en Guinea Ecuatorial, la declaración de defunción debe efectuarse de forma inmediata, habitualmente dentro de las primeras 24 a 48 horas tras el fallecimiento y siempre antes de proceder al enterramiento; si transcurre el plazo ordinario sin haberse inscrito el deceso, será necesario tramitar un expediente gubernativo o judicial de inscripción fuera de plazo ante el juzgado competente [2] [3].
  • Documentación requerida y Acta de Defunción: El familiar declarante debe presentar el certificado médico de defunción original (o la autorización judicial forense), el Documento de Identidad Personal (DIP) o pasaporte de la persona fallecida, y el documento de identidad del propio declarante y de los testigos requeridos por la oficina registral [2] [4]. Una vez practicado el asiento, el Registro Civil expide el certificado o certificación literal del Acta de Defunción y la licencia de enterramiento; recomendamos solicitar varias copias certificadas para los trámites de seguridad social, banca y herencia [2] [4].

steps.title: Servicios funerarios, permisos sanitarios de inhumación o cremación y repatriación
steps.html:
• Contratación funeraria y licencia de inhumación: Con el certificado médico de defunción y la licencia de enterramiento emitida por el Registro Civil, la familia o la empresa de pompas fúnebres autorizada coordina la conservación en el tanatorio o morgue hospitalaria y solicita el permiso municipal de inhumación ante el Ayuntamiento correspondiente (como el Ayuntamiento de Malabo o de Bata) cumpliendo las normas higiénico-sanitarias del Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social [1] [2].
  • Requisitos sanitarios para la cremación: Dado que la inhumación es la práctica habitual en el país y las instalaciones crematorias son limitadas, cualquier solicitud de cremación o traslado para incineración exige certificado médico de muerte natural, autorización expresa de los familiares directos o disposición testamentaria, y autorización judicial previa si intervino la jurisdicción penal [1] [2].
  • Legalización diplomática y traslado internacional de restos: Guinea Ecuatorial no es parte del Convenio de la Apostilla de La Haya, por lo que los documentos públicos ecuatoguineanos que deban surtir efectos en el extranjero (o el expediente para repatriar un féretro o urna fuera del país) requieren la cadena de legalización diplomática: validación previa del Ministerio de Justicia, legalización del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores, Cooperación Internacional y Diáspora, y posterior legalización ante la embajada o representación consular extranjera acreditada (como el Consulado General de España en Malabo cuando el fallecido o los herederos tienen vínculo con España), además del certificado médico de embalsamamiento, el acta de encajonamiento en féretro hermético de zinc y el salvoconducto sanitario del Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social [1] [4].

steps.title: Notificación al INSESO, bancos, empleadores y aseguradoras
steps.html:
• Prestaciones de muerte y supervivencia ante el INSESO: Si la persona fallecida era trabajadora afiliada en activo o pensionista del Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social (INSESO), los familiares deben comunicar el fallecimiento en las delegaciones de Malabo, Bata o cabeceras provinciales para solicitar el subsidio por defunción (destinado a cubrir gastos de sepelio) y tramitar las pensiones de supervivencia (pensión de viudedad para el cónyuge supérstite y pensión de orfandad para los hijos menores o incapacitados) aportando el Acta de Defunción, el carné de afiliación al INSESO, el libro de familia o actas de matrimonio y nacimiento, y las facturas funerarias [3].
  • Liquidación laboral y mutualidades públicas: Si su familiar trabajaba en el sector privado o en la administración pública, debe presentarse el certificado de defunción ante el empleador o ante la Tesorería y el ministerio correspondiente para percibir los salarios devengados pendientes, vacaciones no disfrutadas e indemnizaciones por causa de muerte previstas en el Ordenamiento General del Trabajo [2] [3].
  • Bloqueo y gestión de cuentas bancarias y seguros: Conviene notificar el deceso a todas las entidades bancarias operantes en Guinea Ecuatorial (como BANGE, CCEI Bank GE o Ecobank) y compañías aseguradoras; las cuentas individuales de la persona fallecida quedan bloqueadas preventivamente tras la notificación hasta que los herederos acrediten su título sucesorio y liquiden los derechos correspondientes, mientras que los seguros de vida se abonan a los beneficiarios designados en la póliza [2] [3].

steps.title: Tramitación de la herencia o sucesión en Guinea Ecuatorial
steps.html:
• Marco jurídico sucesorio (testamentario o abintestato): En Guinea Ecuatorial coexisten las normas del Código Civil de tradición hispánica aplicable en el país y las disposiciones consuetudinarias reconocidas por la ley en el ámbito familiar; la sucesión se abre con el fallecimiento y se rige por el testamento otorgado ante Notario o, a falta de testamento válido, por las reglas de la sucesión intestada [2].
  • Declaración de herederos y partición ante Notario o Juzgado: Cuando existe testamento o acuerdo unánime, los interesados acuden ante una Notaría pública dependiente de la Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial con el certificado literal de defunción, la certificación de si existen o no disposiciones de última voluntad y los certificados de nacimiento y matrimonio para formalizar la escritura de aceptación y adjudicación de herencia; en ausencia de testamento o si surgen controversias entre coherederos, se promueve el expediente de declaración de herederos abintestato o el juicio de testamentaría ante el Juzgado de Primera Instancia e Instrucción competente [2] [4].
  • Impuestos sucesorios, inscripción registral y herederos en el exterior: Antes de inscribir el cambio de titularidad de inmuebles en el Registro de la Propiedad o de liberar fondos bancarios, debe presentarse la liquidación de los derechos e impuestos sobre sucesiones y transmisiones patrimoniales ante la administración tributaria; si alguno de los herederos reside fuera de Guinea Ecuatorial, puede otorgar poder especial para pleitos y aceptación de herencia ante el consulado de Guinea Ecuatorial en su país de residencia o ante notario extranjero debidamente legalizado por vía diplomática (por ejemplo, a través del Consulado General de España en Malabo o la misión diplomática correspondiente) [2] [4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Equatorial Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Equatorial Guinea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Equatorial Guinea: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We are very sorry to hear about the difficult health situation your family member is facing in Equatorial Guinea. Below, we explain in order the five main practical, medical, social security, and legal steps to complete while the ill person retains full legal capacity.

steps.title: Activating Palliative Care and Coordinating Healthcare Coverage in Equatorial Guinea
steps.html:
• Public hospital network and reference centres: If the ill person is receiving care within the public system supervised by the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare (Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social - MINSABS), the attending specialist at the regional reference hospitals (such as the Regional Hospital of Malabo or the Regional Hospital of Bata) or at partner medical centres such as La Paz can establish a symptom-management plan, pain-control regimen, and outpatient or home follow-up [1] [5].
  • Medical and pharmaceutical coverage through INSESO: When your family member is an insured worker or pensioner affiliated with the National Social Security Institute (Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social - INSESO), it is advisable to submit updated medical reports to the medical directorate or provincial delegation of the institute in Malabo or Bata to process healthcare benefits, hospitalisation authorisations, supply of specialised medication, and, where clinically indicated, medical evacuation files [3].
  • Private health insurance and clinical records: If the ill person holds a private health insurance policy or corporate medical coverage, it is advisable to request a comprehensive clinical report with diagnosis and palliative care plan from the medical team to activate hospitalisation or home-care benefits, while keeping certified copies of the complete medical file [1] [5].

steps.title: Advance Medical Directives and Appointing a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Informed consent and patient autonomy: Although Equatorial Guinea does not maintain a single electronic national registry for living wills, the general principles of medical ethics and patient rights applied by the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare recognise the right of every person with full mental capacity to grant or refuse informed consent to invasive procedures and to prioritise palliative comfort measures [1] [5].
  • Notarial declaration of advance medical directives and family proxy: While the ill person retains full judgment, it is strongly advisable to execute a public deed before a Notary attached to the Administration of Justice of Equatorial Guinea (Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial) setting out advance medical instructions together with the express appointment of a trusted family member or proxy to act as interlocutor before medical teams should the patient later lose the ability to communicate [2] [4].
  • Filing with the hospital and attending physician: A certified copy of this notarial deed should be delivered to the medical directorate of the hospital, the attending physician, and the appointed proxy so that it is visibly recorded in the clinical file [1] [2].

steps.title: Executing Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Granting a general or special power of attorney before a Notary: Under the civil law in force in the country, while your family member retains intact legal capacity they may appear before a public Notary office under the Administration of Justice of Equatorial Guinea (in Malabo, Bata, or another judicial district) to execute a public deed of general power of administration or special power of attorney with express authority for administrative procedures, collection of pensions, and management or disposition of assets [2].
  • Notary visit to the hospital or home: If the illness severely restricts the ill person's physical mobility but they retain full mental lucidity confirmed by a medical certificate, the public Notary may be requested to travel to the hospital or family home to verify the grantor's capacity and authorise the signing of the deed [2].
  • Registering signatures and mandates with banks: Because banks operating in Equatorial Guinea (such as BANGE, CCEI Bank GE, or Ecobank) strictly verify powers of representation, it is advisable to present the certified copy of the notarial power of attorney immediately at each financial institution and sign their internal signature-authorisation forms while the account holder can personally ratify them [2] [4].

steps.title: Claiming Disability or Sickness Benefits and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Temporary sickness benefit: If the ill person is actively employed and contributes to the National Social Security Institute (INSESO), medical leave certificates issued by authorised physicians entitle the worker to receive temporary incapacity benefits (subsidio por incapacidad temporal) for common or occupational illness once the initial employer-paid period under labour and social security rules has elapsed [3].
  • Permanent disability pension before INSESO: When a serious or chronic illness results in a permanent reduction in working capacity, an assessment by the competent medical board of the National Social Security Institute may be requested to recognise a permanent disability pension (pensión de invalidez), submitting the hospital clinical history, identity document, and contribution records [3].
  • Employment leave for family caregivers: Family members employed in the formal sector in Equatorial Guinea may request paid or unpaid leave from their employer for the serious illness or hospitalisation of close relatives under the General Labour Regulations, presenting the medical certificate issued by the hospital of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare or the treating clinic [1] [2].

steps.title: Preventive Will Preparation, Insurance Beneficiaries, and Civil and Property Records
steps.html:
• Executing an open will before a Notary: To prevent future disputes or lengthy court proceedings, the safest course while the ill person retains full mental capacity is to execute an open will (testamento abierto) in a public deed before a Notary of the Administration of Justice of Equatorial Guinea, respecting the compulsory reserve shares (legítimas) of forced heirs under applicable civil law [2].
  • Updating insurance and contract beneficiaries: Life insurance policies, corporate group insurance, and pension plans should be reviewed to confirm that beneficiary designations are up to date, as insurance proceeds are paid directly to named beneficiaries [2] [3].
  • Reviewing Civil Registry certificates and international coordination: It is important to obtain and verify literal birth and marriage certificates from the Equatoguinean Civil Registry now to correct any spelling or date discrepancies; furthermore, if your family member holds assets or has heirs abroad, since Equatorial Guinea is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, powers of attorney or notarial deeds must be legalised through diplomatic channels before the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the relevant foreign diplomatic mission (such as the Consulate General of Spain in Malabo for matters connected with Spain) [2] [4].

es.title: Enfermedad terminal y planificación legal en Guinea Ecuatorial: lista oficial en 5 pasos
es.cardSummary: Guía oficial en 5 pasos para la planificación médica y legal ante una enfermedad terminal en Guinea Ecuatorial: cuidados paliativos, testamento vital (voluntades anticipadas), poderes preventivos, ayudas para cuidadores y testamento.
es.introHtml: Lamentamos mucho la difícil situación de salud que atraviesa su familiar en Guinea Ecuatorial. A continuación, explicamos en orden los cinco pasos prácticos, médicos, previsionales y jurídicos fundamentales que recomendamos gestionar mientras la persona enferma conserva su plena capacidad de obrar.

steps.title: Activación de cuidados paliativos y coordinación de la cobertura sanitaria en Guinea Ecuatorial
steps.html:
• Red hospitalaria pública y centros de referencia: Si la persona enferma recibe asistencia en el sistema público supervisado por el Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social, el médico especialista tratante en los hospitales regionales de referencia (como el Hospital Regional de Malabo o el Hospital Regional de Bata) o en los centros médicos concertados como La Paz puede organizar un plan de tratamiento sintomático, control del dolor y seguimiento ambulatorio o domiciliario [1] [5].
  • Cobertura médica y farmacéutica a través del INSESO: Cuando su familiar es trabajador afiliado o pensionista del Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social (INSESO), conviene acudir con los informes médicos actualizados a la dirección médica o delegación provincial del instituto en Malabo o Bata para tramitar las prestaciones de asistencia sanitaria, autorizaciones de hospitalización, suministro de medicación especializada y, cuando proceda por criterio facultativo, expedientes de evacuación sanitaria [3].
  • Seguros médicos privados e historial clínico: Si la persona enferma cuenta con una póliza de salud privada o cobertura médica corporativa, recomendamos solicitar al equipo médico un informe clínico integral con diagnóstico y pauta paliativa para activar las garantías de hospitalización o asistencia domiciliaria, conservando siempre copias autenticadas del expediente médico completo [1] [5].

steps.title: Voluntades médicas anticipadas y designación de representante sanitario
steps.html:
• Consentimiento informado y autonomía del paciente: Aunque Guinea Ecuatorial no dispone de un registro administrativo electrónico único de testamentos vitales, los principios generales de ética médica y derechos del paciente aplicados por el Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social reconocen el derecho de toda persona en pleno uso de sus facultades a otorgar o denegar su consentimiento informado frente a intervenciones invasivas y a priorizar las medidas de alivio paliativo [1] [5].
  • Declaración notarial de directrices médicas y representante familiar: Mientras la persona enferma conserva plena capacidad de juicio, es muy recomendable formalizar en escritura pública ante un Notario adscrito a la Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial una declaración de instrucciones médicas previas junto con la designación expresa de un familiar o persona de confianza como representante e interlocutor válido ante los equipos médicos en caso de pérdida sobrevenida de la capacidad de expresión [2] [4].
  • Entrega al hospital y al médico tratante: Debe entregarse copia autorizada de dicho documento notarial a la dirección médica del centro hospitalario, al médico responsable del tratamiento y al representante designado para que conste de forma visible en la historia clínica [1] [2].

steps.title: Formalización de poderes notariales y autorizaciones bancarias mientras exista plena capacidad
steps.html:
• Otorgamiento de poder general o especial ante Notario: Conforme a la legislación civil vigente en el país, mientras su familiar conserve intacta su capacidad jurídica puede comparecer ante una Notaría pública dependiente de la Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial (en Malabo, Bata u otra cabecera judicial) para otorgar escritura pública de poder general de administración o poder especial con facultades expresas para gestiones administrativas, cobro de pensiones y administración o disposición de bienes [2].
  • Desplazamiento del Notario al hospital o domicilio: Si la enfermedad limita gravemente la movilidad física de la persona enferma pero esta mantiene plena lucidez mental respaldada por certificado médico, puede solicitarse al Notario público que se traslade al centro hospitalario o al domicilio familiar para verificar la capacidad del otorgante y autorizar la firma de la escritura [2].
  • Registro de firmas y apoderamientos en entidades bancarias: Dado que los bancos que operan en Guinea Ecuatorial (como BANGE, CCEI Bank GE o Ecobank) verifican de forma estricta las facultades de representación, conviene presentar de inmediato la copia autorizada del poder notarial en cada entidad financiera y suscribir los formularios internos de autorización de firma mientras el titular puede ratificarlos personalmente [2] [4].

steps.title: Solicitud de prestaciones por incapacidad o invalidez y apoyos laborales
steps.html:
• Subsidio por incapacidad temporal por enfermedad: Si la persona enferma se encuentra en activo y cotiza al Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social (INSESO), las bajas médicas certificadas por los facultativos autorizados dan derecho a percibir el subsidio económico por incapacidad temporal por enfermedad común o profesional una vez superado el periodo inicial a cargo del empleador previsto en la normativa laboral y de seguridad social [3].
  • Pensión de invalidez permanente ante el INSESO: Cuando la evolución de la enfermedad grave o crónica produce una reducción permanente de la capacidad de trabajo, puede solicitarse ante el Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social la valoración por la comisión médica competente para el reconocimiento de la pensión de invalidez, aportando el historial clínico hospitalario, el documento de identidad y las certificaciones de cotización [3].
  • Permisos laborales para familiares cuidadores: Los familiares que trabajan por cuenta ajena en Guinea Ecuatorial pueden solicitar ante su empleador permisos retribuidos o licencias por enfermedad grave u hospitalización de parientes conforme al Ordenamiento General del Trabajo, presentando el justificante expedido por el hospital del Ministerio de Sanidad y Bienestar Social o de la clínica tratante [1] [2].

steps.title: Ordenación preventiva del testamento, seguros y documentación civil y patrimonial
steps.html:
• Otorgamiento de testamento abierto ante Notario: Para evitar litigios futuros o procedimientos judiciales largos, la vía más segura mientras la persona enferma conserva plena capacidad intelectual es otorgar testamento abierto en escritura pública ante un Notario de la Administración de Justicia de Guinea Ecuatorial, respetando el régimen de legítimas de los herederos forzosos previsto en la legislación civil aplicable [2].
  • Actualización de beneficiarios de seguros y contratos: Conviene revisar las pólizas de seguro de vida, seguros colectivos de empresa y planes de previsión para confirmar que la designación de beneficiarios esté actualizada, ya que las indemnizaciones de seguro se abonan directamente a las personas designadas [2] [3].
  • Revisión de actas del Registro Civil y coordinación internacional: Es importante recabar y verificar desde ahora las certificaciones literales de nacimiento y de matrimonio en el Registro Civil ecuatoguineano para subsanar cualquier discrepancia de nombres o fechas; asimismo, si su familiar posee bienes o familiares en el extranjero, dado que Guinea Ecuatorial no forma parte del Convenio de la Apostilla de La Haya, los poderes o documentos notariales deberán legalizarse por vía diplomática ante el Ministerio de Justicia, el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores y la representación extranjera correspondiente (como el Consulado General de España en Malabo para trámites vinculados con España) [2] [4].

titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Benin: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Benin: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Benin. Below, we explain in chronological order the five main official medical, civil registration, funeral, social security, and succession steps to complete before the Beninese institutions.

steps.title: Medical Verification of Death and Issuance of the Medical Death Certificate
steps.html:
• Death in a public hospital or private clinic: When a death occurs from natural causes in a hospital facility under the Ministry of Health of Benin (Ministère de la Santé du Bénin, such as the Hubert Koutoukou Maga National University Hospital Centre - CNHU-HKM in Cotonou, a Departmental University Hospital Centre, or a zone hospital) or in an approved private clinic, the attending or on-duty physician issues the official medical certificate of death (certificat médical de décès) confirming the cause, date, and time of death, and the body is transferred to the hospital morgue [4].
  • Natural death at home: If the deceased person passes away at home, the family must call a state-licensed physician or visit the nearest municipal health centre of the Ministry of Health of Benin so that a practitioner can clinically verify the death and issue the cause-of-death certificate required for civil registration and morgue admission [1] [4].
  • Suspicious, violent, or public-place death: In the event of an accidental death, sudden death without prior medical supervision, or any medico-legal obstacle, the body must not be moved without the intervention of the Republican Police (Police Républicaine) and the Public Prosecutor (Procureur de la République) at the competent Court of First Instance (under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice and Legislation). A judicial requisition then orders a medico-legal examination or autopsy before the prosecutor's office issues the judicial burial permit [4] [5].

steps.title: Declaring the Death with the Civil Registry and ANIP
steps.html:
• Competent authority (Municipality, district office, and ANIP): Under the Personal and Family Code (Code des personnes et de la famille) in force in the Republic of Benin and the national civil status reform, a death is declared at the civil registry centre of the municipality (mairie) or district office (arrondissement) where the death occurred, working in coordination with the National Agency for Identification of Persons (Agence Nationale d'Identification des Personnes - ANIP), which manages the National Register of Natural Persons (RNPP) and the issuance of secure civil status records [1] [2].
  • Statutory deadlines and Certificate of Non-Registration: The declaration must be made within the statutory period following the death in order to obtain the burial permit immediately. If the death was not declared within the prescribed deadline, family members must request a Certificate of Non-Registration of Death (certificat de non-enregistrement de décès, at the official fee of 2,000 FCFA) from the National Agency for Identification of Persons in order to petition the Court of First Instance for a late-registration authorisation judgment [1] [2].
  • Required documents and obtaining the secure Death Certificate: The declarant presents the medical certificate of death (or the hospital declaration form), the identity document or Personal Identification Certificate (Certificat d'Identification Personnelle - CIP) bearing the Personal Identification Number (NPI) of the deceased person, and their own identity document [1] [2]. Once the death is recorded in the RNPP, the National Agency for Identification of Persons issues the secure Death Certificate (acte de décès sécurisé, officially priced at 2,000 FCFA at the counter according to the ANIP fee schedule) [2].

steps.title: Funeral Arrangements, Sanitary Permits, and International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial permit and municipal or family burial: With the medical certificate of death and civil registration proof, the family or an approved funeral home requests the burial permit (permis d'inhumer) from the municipal hall (such as the Municipality of Cotonou, Porto-Novo, Abomey-Calavi, or Parakou), complying with the public hygiene regulations of the Ministry of Health of Benin [1] [4].
  • Health and judicial rules for cremation: Any request for cremation or transfer for incineration requires the written expression of the wishes of the deceased person or closest surviving relative, a medical certificate confirming the absence of a pacemaker and any medico-legal obstacle, and authorisation from the administrative authority and, where applicable, the Public Prosecutor [4] [5].
  • International repatriation and diplomatic legalisation: If the body or urn is to be transferred outside Benin, or if Beninese civil records must be produced abroad, the file requires a medical certificate of non-contagion, an embalming certificate (certificat de soins de conservation), placement in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin in the presence of police and public health authorities of the Ministry of Health of Benin, and a mortuary laissez-passer [4]. Furthermore, because Benin is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, documents issued by the National Agency for Identification of Persons or Beninese courts for use abroad must undergo legalisation by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs followed by super-legalisation at the consulate of the destination country [2] [5].

steps.title: Procedures with the CNSS, FNRB, Banks, and Insurance Companies
steps.html:
• Survivor pension or survivor grant at the CNSS: If your family member was an insured private-sector employee or retiree affiliated with the National Social Security Fund (Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale - CNSS), eligible survivors (unremarried surviving spouse and dependent orphans under age 21 continuing their schooling or apprenticeship, or disabled children) may claim a survivor pension (pension de survivants, if the insured person held a pension or had at least 180 months of insurance) or, failing that, a lump-sum survivor grant (allocation de survivants) [3]. The application file submitted to the National Social Security Fund includes the official CNSS claim form, the secure death certificate, the marriage certificate, the children's birth certificates, certificates of life and dependency, school attendance certificates, the insurance booklet, and the employment certificate [3].
  • Civil servants and the National Pension Fund of Benin (FNRB): When the deceased person was a civil servant or military officer affiliated with the National Pension Fund of Benin (Fonds National des Retraites du Bénin - FNRB), claimants apply to the Directorate General of Pensions and Life Annuities of the Ministry of Economy and Finance for the death lump sum (capital décès) and survivor pension [3] [5].
  • Notifying banks and insurance companies: Beninese banks and life insurance companies should be notified promptly by submitting a copy of the secure ANIP death certificate; individual accounts are frozen until estate settlement, whereas life insurance proceeds are paid directly to the beneficiaries named in the policy [2] [5].

steps.title: Opening and Settling the Estate in Benin
steps.html:
• Legal framework under the Personal and Family Code: In Benin, intestate and testate succession is governed exclusively by Law No. 2002-07 on the Personal and Family Code (as amended and supplemented by Law No. 2021-13), which establishes the rights of children (without distinction of gender or filiation), the surviving spouse, and ascendants, as well as the disposable portion where a will exists [5].
  • Inventory deed, family council minutes, and notary: To unfreeze bank accounts, collect arrears, or transfer property, the family convenes a family council whose minutes (appointing the estate administrator or guardian of minor children) are homologated by the guardianship judge or the Court of First Instance under the Ministry of Justice and Legislation (Ministère de la Justice et de la Législation), and instructs a Beninese notary to draw up the deed of hereditary notoriety (acte de notoriété héréditaire) or inventory deed and the deed of partition [3] [5].
  • Inheritance tax, land title transfer (ANDF), and heirs abroad: The inheritance tax return and registration of notarial deeds are completed with the Directorate General of Taxes (DGI) prior to transferring land titles with the National Domain and Land Agency (Agence Nationale du Domaine et du Foncier - ANDF); if an heir resides abroad, they may execute an authentic notarial power of attorney duly legalised by the territorially competent consulate of Benin to be represented before the Beninese notary or court [2] [5].

closingQuestion: In which municipality of Benin did the death occur, and do we know whether your family member was affiliated with the National Social Security Fund (CNSS) or the National Pension Fund of Benin, so that we can clarify the steps applicable to your situation?
