title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Timor-Leste: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Timor-Leste: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Timor-Leste: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Timor-Leste. To support your family through the medical certification, civil registration, funeral, social security, and succession procedures governed by the laws of the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste (in particular the Civil Code and the Civil Registration Code), we have structured the five official and practical steps below in chronological order.

steps.title: Medical Certification of Death and Issuance of the Medical Death Certificate
steps.html:
• Death occurring in a hospital or health center: When the deceased person passes away in a public healthcare facility under the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste (such as the Guido Valadares National Hospital in Dili, a regional referral hospital, or a community health center) or in a private clinic, the attending or on-duty physician performs an immediate clinical examination and issues the medical death declaration or certificate (certificado médico de óbito) [6]. This official clinical document is provided free of charge to the family and serves as the legal basis for civil death registration and release of the body from the hospital mortuary [1] [6].
  • Death occurring at home or in the community (suco or aldeia): If the death occurs at home under medical supervision, the attending physician issues the death certificate [6]. In rural areas or sucos where immediate medical attendance was unavailable at the time of a natural death, initial verification and reporting are coordinated with the local health post and community authorities (Chefe de Suco or Chefe de Aldeia) for submission to the Civil Registry Office [1] [3].
  • Violent, suspicious, or unexplained death: In the event of an accident, violent death, or suspicious death in a public place or residence, the National Police of Timor-Leste (PNTL) must be contacted immediately [1] [2]. Under the direction of the Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministério Público), the body is transferred for forensic examination or autopsy at the Guido Valadares National Hospital, and judicial authorization from the Public Prosecutor is required prior to burial [2] [6].

steps.title: Official Death Registration at the Civil Registry Office
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Civil Registration Code and the regulations of the Directorate-General for Registration and Notary Services supervised by the Ministry of Justice of Timor-Leste, any death occurring in national territory must be declared at the Civil Registry Office (Conservatória do Registo Civil) of the municipality where the death occurred or through the municipal one-stop shops integrated into the Municipal Portal of Timor-Leste (Balkaun Úniku) [1] [3]. The declaration must be made within the statutory deadline of 48 hours following death or discovery of the body [1] [3].
  • Required documents for registration: The declaring relative must present the medical death certificate (or hospital/community declaration), the Identity Card (Bilhete de Identidade), voter registration card, birth certificate, or passport of the deceased person, together with valid identification for the declarant [1] [3].
  • Issuance of the death certificate and late registration: Once the death record (assento de óbito) is entered, the Civil Registry Office issues the burial guide (guia de enterramento) and the initial death certificate (certidão de óbito) free of charge [1] [3]. If the statutory deadline has elapsed, late death registration requires an administrative justification or authorization procedure before the civil registration services of the Ministry of Justice of Timor-Leste [1] [2]. We advise requesting several certified copies of the death certificate for banks and social security filings [3] [4].

steps.title: Funeral Arrangements, Burial Permits, and International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial guide and municipal sanitary rules: No burial in a public or community cemetery in Timor-Leste may take place without the burial guide issued by the Civil Registry Office or municipal administrative authority, in compliance with public health standards overseen by the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste [1] [3] [6].
  • Transport of remains between municipalities in Timor-Leste: Whenever the family wishes to transport mortal remains from Dili to the deceased person's home municipality or suco, transport requires a hospital medical declaration confirming proper preservation and the absence of epidemic risk, coordinated with the municipal administration and health services [3] [6].
  • International repatriation and consular legalization: If the deceased person was a foreign national or if the mortal remains must be repatriated outside Timor-Leste (or from abroad into Timor-Leste), international transport requires a hermetically sealed coffin meeting international sanitary standards, a certificate of non-infectiousness issued by the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste, a mortuary transit permit (livre-trânsito mortuário), and consular registration or legalization of the death certificate at the competent embassy or consulate [1] [2] [6].

steps.title: Social Security (INSS), Banks, and Insurance Companies
steps.html:
• Survivor benefits under the contributory scheme (INSS): When the deceased person was an insured worker or pensioner under the contributory social security system, surviving relatives must report the death to the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS), supervised by the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion of Timor-Leste [4] [5]. The social security legal framework provides a survivor's pension (pensão de sobrevivência) for the surviving spouse and dependent descendants, as well as a death grant (subsídio por morte) and funeral expense reimbursement, claimed using the official forms published by the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS) [2] [4] [5].
  • Non-contributory social support (MSSI): If the deceased person received the Support Allowance for the Elderly and Disabled (SAII) or if the household faces socioeconomic vulnerability, the death must be reported to the municipal services of the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion of Timor-Leste for registry updates and potential funeral assistance [5].
  • Bank accounts and insurance policies: Heirs must notify commercial banks operating in Timor-Leste (such as BNCTL, BNU, Mandiri, or BRI) and any insurance providers by presenting the death certificate to freeze sole accounts held by the deceased and determine balances belonging to the estate [1] [2].

steps.title: Qualification of Heirs, Inventory, and Estate Partition
steps.html:
• Succession framework under the Civil Code of Timor-Leste: Succession upon death in Timor-Leste is governed by Book V of the Timorese Civil Code (Law No. 10/2011), published in the Official Gazette (Jornal da República) by the Ministry of Justice of Timor-Leste, which regulates statutory succession (protecting the forced-heirship share of the spouse, descendants, and ascendants) and testamentary succession [2].
  • Notarial qualification of heirs and partition deed: To prove heirship legally before commercial banks, property registries, and the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS), the head of the estate (cabeça-de-casal) must execute a notarial qualification of heirs (habilitação de herdeiros) at a Notary Office under the Directorate-General for Registration and Notary Services [1] [2] [4]. Where all heirs are adults with full legal capacity and in agreement, estate partition is completed by public notarial deed [1] [2].
  • Judicial inventory and cross-border coordination: If any heirs are minors or legally incapacitated, or if heirs disagree on the division of assets, a judicial inventory proceeding (inventário judicial) must be filed before the competent District Court (Dili, Baucau, Suai, or Oecusse) [2]. Where an heir resides abroad or assets are located outside Timor-Leste, the heir may grant a public power of attorney legalized through consular channels to be represented before the Timorese notary or court [1] [2].

closingQuestion: In which municipality of Timor-Leste did the death occur, and was your family member registered with the National Social Security Institute (INSS) or are there foreign heirs or assets so that we can outline your priority next steps?

pt.title: O que fazer quando alguém falece em Timor-Leste: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos após um óbito em Timor-Leste: certificado médico de óbito, contratação de agência funerária, registo civil, subsídio por morte e pensão de sobrevivência, e habilitação de herdeiros ou inventário.
pt.introHtml: Apresentamos as nossas sinceras condolências pelo falecimento do seu familiar em Timor-Leste. Para apoiar a sua família no cumprimento das formalidades médicas, de registo civil, funerárias, de segurança social e sucessórias previstas na legislação da República Democrática de Timor-Leste (nomeadamente o Código Civil e o Código do Registo Civil), estruturámos abaixo os cinco passos oficiais e práticos por ordem cronológica.

steps.title: Verificação médica do óbito e emissão do certificado médico de óbito
steps.html:
• Óbito ocorrido em hospital ou centro de saúde: Quando a pessoa falecida morre num estabelecimento público de saúde tutelado pelo Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste (como o Hospital Nacional Guido Valadares em Díli, um hospital de referência regional ou um centro de saúde comunitário) ou numa clínica privada, o médico assistente ou de serviço procede à verificação clínica imediata e emite a declaração ou certificado médico de óbito [6]. Este documento clínico oficial é entregue gratuitamente aos familiares e constitui a base legal para o assento de óbito e para a saída do corpo da morgue hospitalar [1] [6].
  • Óbito ocorrido no domicílio ou na comunidade (suco ou aldeia): Se o falecimento ocorrer em casa com acompanhamento médico, o médico assistente emite o certificado de óbito [6]. Nas áreas rurais ou sucos onde não tenha havido assistência médica imediata no momento da morte natural, a verificação e a declaração inicial são articuladas com o posto de saúde local e com as autoridades comunitárias (Chefe de Suco ou Chefe de Aldeia) para efeitos de participação à Conservatória do Registo Civil [1] [3].
  • Morte violenta, suspeita ou sem causa natural aparente: Em caso de acidente, morte violenta ou suspeita na via pública ou no domicílio, deve ser imediatamente contactada a Polícia Nacional de Timor-Leste (PNTL) [1] [2]. Sob direção do Ministério Público, o corpo é encaminhado para exame médico-legal ou autópsia forense no Hospital Nacional Guido Valadares, sendo necessária autorização judicial do Ministério Público antes da inumação [2] [6].

steps.title: Registo oficial do óbito na Conservatória do Registo Civil
steps.html:
• Entidade competente e prazo legal: Nos termos do Código do Registo Civil e da regulamentação da Direção-Geral dos Serviços de Registos e Notariado sob tutela do Ministério da Justiça de Timor-Leste, o óbito ocorrido em território nacional deve ser declarado na Conservatória do Registo Civil do município onde ocorreu o falecimento ou através dos serviços municipais integrados no Portal Municipal de Timor-Leste (Balkaun Úniku) [1] [3]. A declaração deve ser efetuada prioritariamente no prazo legal de 48 horas após o falecimento ou a verificação do óbito [1] [3].
  • Documentos necessários para o registo: O familiar declarante deve apresentar o certificado médico de óbito (ou a declaração hospitalar/comunitária), o Bilhete de Identidade, cartão eleitoral, certidão de nascimento ou passaporte da pessoa falecida, bem como o documento de identificação válido do próprio declarante [1] [3].
  • Emissão da certidão de óbito e registo tardio: Após a lavratura do assento de óbito, a Conservatória emite gratuitamente a guia de enterramento e a primeira certidão de óbito [1] [3]. Caso o prazo legal tenha sido ultrapassado, o registo de óbito fora de prazo requer procedimento administrativo de justificação ou autorização junto dos serviços de registo civil do Ministério da Justiça de Timor-Leste [1] [2]. Aconselhamos a solicitar vários exemplares autenticados da certidão de óbito para apresentar aos bancos e à segurança social [3] [4].

steps.title: Organização do funeral, inumação e trasladação internacional
steps.html:
• Guia de enterramento e regras sanitárias municipais: Nenhuma inumação em cemitério público ou comunitário em Timor-Leste pode realizar-se sem a guia de enterramento emitida pela Conservatória do Registo Civil ou autoridade administrativa municipal, respeitando as normas de saúde pública supervisionadas pelo Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste [1] [3] [6].
  • Transporte do corpo entre municípios de Timor-Leste: Sempre que a família pretenda trasladar os restos mortais de Díli para o município ou suco de origem da pessoa falecida, o transporte exige a declaração médica hospitalar de conservação e ausência de risco epidémico, articulada com a administração municipal e os serviços de saúde [3] [6].
  • Repatriação internacional e legalização consular: Se a pessoa falecida era cidadã estrangeira ou se os restos mortais tiverem de ser trasladados para fora de Timor-Leste (ou repatriados do estrangeiro para Timor-Leste), são exigidos um caixão hermético selado segundo as normas sanitárias internacionais, certificado sanitário de não infecciosidade emitido pelo Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste, livre-trânsito mortuário e o registo ou legalização consular da certidão de óbito na embaixada ou consulado competente [1] [2] [6].

steps.title: Segurança social (INSS), bancos e seguradoras
steps.html:
• Prestações por morte no regime contributivo (INSS): Quando a pessoa falecida era trabalhadora ou pensionista inscrita no regime contributivo de segurança social, os familiares sobrevivos devem comunicar o óbito ao Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste, tutelado pelo Ministério da Solidariedade Social e Inclusão de Timor-Leste [4] [5]. O regime jurídico da segurança social prevê a atribuição de pensão de sobrevivência ao cônjuge sobrevivo e aos descendentes a cargo, bem como o subsídio por morte e o reembolso ou apoio para despesas de funeral, mediante entrega dos requerimentos oficiais disponíveis no portal do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste [2] [4] [5].
  • Apoios sociais não contributivos (MSSI): Caso a pessoa falecida fosse beneficiária do subsídio de apoio a idosos e inválidos (SAII) ou se a família se encontrar em situação de vulnerabilidade socioeconómica, o óbito deve ser participado aos serviços municipais do Ministério da Solidariedade Social e Inclusão de Timor-Leste para atualização cadastral e eventual acesso a apoio social funerário [5].
  • Contas bancárias e seguros: Os herdeiros devem notificar os bancos comerciais a operar em Timor-Leste (como o BNCTL, BNU, Mandiri ou BRI) e eventuais seguradoras, apresentando a certidão de óbito para bloqueio das contas individuais da pessoa falecida e apuramento dos saldos que integrarão a herança [1] [2].

steps.title: Habilitação de herdeiros, inventário e partilha da sucessão
steps.html:
• Enquadramento sucessório no Código Civil de Timor-Leste: A sucessão por morte em Timor-Leste é regulada pelo Livro V do Código Civil timorense (Lei n.º 10/2011), publicado no Jornal da República pelo Ministério da Justiça de Timor-Leste, distinguindo a sucessão legítima (cônjuge, descendentes e ascendentes, protegidos pela quota de legítima) e a sucessão testamentária [2].
  • Habilitação de herdeiros e escritura notarial de partilha: Para comprovar legalmente a qualidade de herdeiros perante bancos, conservatórias prediais e o Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste, o cabeça-de-casal deve promover a habilitação notarial de herdeiros junto do Cartório Notarial da Direção-Geral dos Serviços de Registos e Notariado [1] [2] [4]. Havendo acordo entre todos os herdeiros maiores e capazes, a partilha dos bens móveis e imóveis realiza-se por escritura pública notarial [1] [2].
  • Inventário judicial e coordenação internacional: Se existirem herdeiros menores, interditos ou inabilitados, ou se não houver consenso quanto à partilha dos bens, é obrigatório requerer processo de inventário judicial junto do Tribunal Distrital competente (Díli, Baucau, Suai ou Oecusse) [2]. Caso algum herdeiro resida no estrangeiro ou existam bens fora de Timor-Leste, o herdeiro pode outorgar uma procuração pública devidamente legalizada pela via consular para se fazer representar no notário ou no tribunal timorense [1] [2].

pt.closingQuestion: Em que município de Timor-Leste ocorreu o falecimento e o seu familiar estava inscrito no Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social (INSS) ou existem herdeiros ou bens no estrangeiro para que possamos indicar os passos prioritários para a sua família?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Timor-Leste: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Timor-Leste: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Timor-Leste: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand the demanding circumstances your family is facing following the diagnosis of a serious or progressive illness affecting your family member in Timor-Leste. To support the coordinated organization of clinical care, powers of attorney, social security benefits, and advance estate planning while the ill person retains full decision-making capacity, we have structured the five official and practical steps applicable in Timor-Leste below.

steps.title: Coordinating Palliative Care and Hospital or Home Medical Follow-Up
steps.html:
• Clinical coordination within the public health network: In Timor-Leste, specialized medical follow-up for serious, oncological, or progressive chronic illnesses is provided through the National Health Service supervised by the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste, led by the Guido Valadares National Hospital (in Dili) and the regional referral hospitals (Baucau, Maliana, Maubisse, Suai, and Oecusse) [6]. The attending medical team establishes an individualized pain-management, symptom-control, and supportive care plan [6].
  • Home care and community health programs: Through Community Health Centers and family health outreach programs coordinated by the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste, families may request home visits by doctors and nurses for medication administration, symptom monitoring, and ongoing palliative support for the ill person [6].
  • Medical report and clinical documentation: We advise requesting a detailed medical report from the attending physician confirming the diagnosis and degree of functional incapacity, which is essential when applying for social security benefits before the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS) and the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion of Timor-Leste [4] [5] [6].

steps.title: Recording Care Preferences, Informed Consent, and a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and treatment wishes: Under the clinical and ethical standards applicable across facilities supervised by the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste and the personality rights protected by the Timorese Civil Code, no major medical intervention may be performed without the patient's free and informed consent while they retain capacity [2] [6]. The ill person may record written preferences regarding invasive interventions, priority pain relief, and their preferred setting of care (hospital or home) [6].
  • Written designation of a trusted family representative: Although Timor-Leste does not maintain a separate electronic registry for advance directives, hospital medical teams consult immediate family members whenever a patient becomes unable to express their wishes [6]. It is therefore advisable for the ill person to designate in writing a trusted family spokesperson as their clinical representative and provide a signed copy to the attending physician for inclusion in the hospital record [2] [6].
  • Access to clinical records: This written authorization may also empower the family representative to collect test results, prescriptions, and clinical reports from hospital services under the Ministry of Health of Timor-Leste [6].

steps.title: Executing a Public Power of Attorney at a Notary Office and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Bank mandates and account authorization: While your family member retains full civil capacity, they should arrange with their commercial banks in Timor-Leste (such as BNCTL, BNU, Mandiri, or BRI) to register an authorized representative or mandate holder on their bank accounts [1] [2]. This ensures uninterrupted payment of medical and household expenses and collection of salary or pension transfers [2] [4].
  • Public power of attorney at the Registration and Notary Services: For broader property and legal administration (managing real property, signing contracts, or acting before tax offices or the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS)), the ill person may execute a public power of attorney (procuração pública) at a Notary Office of the Directorate-General for Registration and Notary Services under the Ministry of Justice of Timor-Leste [1] [2]. If illness prevents travel, the family may request that a notary attend the person's residence or hospital bedside after verifying mental capacity [1].
  • Judicial interdiction or curatorship in case of supervening incapacity: If the progression of illness later deprives the ill person of the capacity to manage their person and property without a valid mandate in place, the Timorese Civil Code provides for judicial interdiction or curatorship (interdição ou inabilitação) ordered by the competent District Court with appointment of a guardian or curator [2].

steps.title: Sickness or Invalidity Social Benefits and Support for Family Caregivers
steps.html:
• Contributory social security scheme (INSS): If the ill person is an insured worker under the contributory scheme and becomes permanently unable to perform their occupation due to non-occupational illness before reaching retirement age, they may apply for an invalidity pension (pensão de invalidez, absolute or relative) from the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS) [2] [4]. Official application forms and medical board documentation requirements are available through the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS) [4].
  • Support Allowance for the Elderly and Disabled (MSSI): For Timorese citizens who do not qualify under the contributory scheme and experience severe permanent incapacity for work, the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion of Timor-Leste administers non-contributory social protection programs, including the Support Allowance for the Elderly and Disabled (Subsídio de Apoio a Idosos e Inválidos - SAII) and support for vulnerable households [5].
  • Employment leave and support for family caregivers: Employed family members in Timor-Leste may request justified leave from their employer to provide urgent assistance to a seriously ill household member in accordance with the Labor Law of Timor-Leste [2] [5].

steps.title: Advance Organization of Wills, Insurance Policies, and Civil and Property Records
steps.html:
• Verifying and updating civil registration certificates: Future social security and succession filings require that the ill person's birth and marriage records, as well as the birth records of all children, be properly registered without discrepancies in names or dates [1] [3] [4]. The family may obtain updated certificates from Civil Registry Offices or through the integrated desks of the Municipal Portal of Timor-Leste (Balkaun Úniku) [1] [3].
  • Executing a will under the Civil Code: While retaining full mental capacity, the ill person may organize the distribution of their estate by executing a public will (drawn up by a notary in the register of a Notary Office under the Ministry of Justice of Timor-Leste) or a closed will, while respecting the statutory forced-heirship share (legítima) reserved for the surviving spouse, descendants, or ascendants [1] [2].
  • Document consolidation and international coordination: We advise gathering land ownership titles, insurance policies, banking contracts, and contribution statements from the National Social Security Institute of Timor-Leste (INSS) [2] [4]. Where assets or heirs are located abroad, the Notary Office can prepare powers of attorney and testamentary provisions suitable for international recognition through consular legalization [1] [2].

pt.title: Doença terminal e administração em fim de vida em Timor-Leste: lista oficial em 5 passos
pt.cardSummary: Guia oficial em 5 passos para o planeamento médico e jurídico em situação de doença terminal em Timor-Leste: cuidados paliativos, diretivas antecipadas de vontade, procurações, apoios ao cuidador e organização sucessória.
pt.introHtml: Compreendemos a exigência do momento que a sua família atravessa perante o diagnóstico de uma doença grave ou progressiva do seu familiar em Timor-Leste. Para apoiar a organização articulada dos cuidados clínicos, a outorga de procurações, o acesso às prestações sociais e a preparação patrimonial enquanto a pessoa doente mantém plena capacidade de decisão, estruturámos abaixo os cinco passos oficiais e práticos aplicáveis em Timor-Leste.

steps.title: Articulação dos cuidados paliativos e acompanhamento médico hospitalar ou domiciliário
steps.html:
• Coordenação clínica na rede pública de saúde: Em Timor-Leste, o acompanhamento médico especializado de doenças graves, oncológicas ou crónicas progressivas é assegurado pelo Serviço Nacional de Saúde sob a tutela do Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste, tendo como unidade central o Hospital Nacional Guido Valadares (em Díli) e os hospitais de referência regional (Baucau, Maliana, Maubisse, Suai e Oecusse) [6]. A equipa médica assistente define o plano de controlo da dor, medicação sintomática e cuidados de suporte [6].
  • Cuidados domiciliários e programas comunitários: Através dos Centros de Saúde Comunitários e dos programas de saúde familiar articulados pelo Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste, a família pode solicitar visitas médicas e de enfermagem ao domicílio para administração de terapêutica, controlo de sintomas e apoio continuado à pessoa doente [6].
  • Relatório clínico e encaminhamento: Aconselhamos a solicitar ao médico assistente um relatório médico detalhado com o diagnóstico e o grau de incapacidade funcional, documento indispensável para instruir pedidos de prestações sociais junto do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste e do Ministério da Solidariedade Social e Inclusão de Timor-Leste [4] [5] [6].

steps.title: Registo de preferências clínicas, consentimento informado e representante de saúde
steps.html:
• Consentimento informado e vontade terapêutica: Nos termos das normas éticas e clínicas aplicáveis nos estabelecimentos tutelados pelo Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste e dos direitos de personalidade consagrados no Código Civil timorense, nenhuma intervenção médica relevante pode ser realizada sem o consentimento livre e esclarecido da pessoa doente enquanto esta conservar lucidez [2] [6]. A pessoa doente pode deixar registadas por escrito as suas preferências quanto a tratamentos invasivos, prioridade ao alívio da dor e local preferencial de acompanhamento (hospital ou domicílio) [6].
  • Designação escrita de familiar ou representante de confiança: Embora Timor-Leste não disponha de um registo eletrónico autónomo de testamento vital, a equipa médica consulta a família próxima sempre que o doente deixe de poder exprimir a sua vontade [6]. Por isso, é recomendável que a pessoa doente designe por escrito um familiar de referência como seu interlocutor clínico, entregando cópia assinada ao médico assistente para integração no processo hospitalar [2] [6].
  • Acesso à informação clínica: O documento escrito pode igualmente autorizar esse representante familiar a levantar exames, receitas médicas e relatórios junto dos serviços hospitalares do Ministério da Saúde de Timor-Leste [6].

steps.title: Outorga de procuração pública em cartório notarial e mandatos bancários
steps.html:
• Mandatos e autorização de movimentação bancária: Enquanto o seu familiar mantém plena capacidade civil, deve regularizar junto dos bancos comerciais em Timor-Leste (como o BNCTL, BNU, Mandiri ou BRI) a inclusão de um procurador ou titular autorizado nas contas bancárias [1] [2]. Esta medida garante o pagamento pontual de despesas médicas e familiares e o recebimento de salários ou pensões sem bloqueio [2] [4].
  • Procuração pública nos Serviços de Registos e Notariado: Para atos de administração patrimonial mais amplos (gestão de imóveis, celebração de contratos, representação perante repartições fiscais ou perante o Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste), a pessoa doente pode outorgar uma procuração pública num Cartório Notarial da Direção-Geral dos Serviços de Registos e Notariado, sob tutela do Ministério da Justiça de Timor-Leste [1] [2]. Caso a doença impeça a deslocação física, pode ser solicitada a deslocação do notário ao domicílio ou ao hospital após verificação da lucidez do outorgante [1].
  • Interdição ou inabilitação judicial em caso de incapacidade superveniente: Se a evolução da doença vier a retirar à pessoa doente a capacidade de gerir a sua pessoa e os seus bens sem que exista mandato válido, o Código Civil timorense prevê o regime de interdição ou inabilitação, requerido junto do Tribunal Distrital competente com nomeação judicial de tutor ou curador [2].

steps.title: Prestações sociais por doença ou invalidez e apoios a cuidadores
steps.html:
• Regime contributivo de segurança social (INSS): Se a pessoa doente for trabalhadora inscrita no regime contributivo e ficar permanentemente incapaz de exercer a sua profissão por motivo de doença não profissional antes de atingir a idade de reforma, pode requerer a pensão de invalidez (absoluta ou relativa) junto do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste [2] [4]. Os formulários oficiais de requerimento e a lista de documentos médicos exigidos para a junta médica encontram-se disponíveis através do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste [4].
  • Subsídio de Apoio a Idosos e Inválidos (MSSI): Para cidadãos timorenses que não reúnam condições no regime contributivo e apresentem incapacidade permanente grave para o trabalho, o Ministério da Solidariedade Social e Inclusão de Timor-Leste assegura programas não contributivos de proteção social, incluindo o Subsídio de Apoio a Idosos e Inválidos (SAII) e apoio social a agregados familiares vulneráveis [5].
  • Licenças laborais e apoio aos familiares cuidadores: Os familiares trabalhadores por conta de outrem em Timor-Leste podem solicitar ao empregador faltas justificadas para assistência inadiável a membros do agregado familiar em situação de doença grave, ao abrigo da Lei do Trabalho de Timor-Leste [2] [5].

steps.title: Organização preventiva do testamento, seguros e documentação civil e patrimonial
steps.html:
• Verificação e atualização das certidões de registo civil: A futura instrução de processos na segurança social ou em sede de sucessão exige que os assentos de nascimento e de casamento da pessoa doente, bem como os assentos de nascimento dos filhos, estejam devidamente registados e sem divergências de nomes ou datas [1] [3] [4]. A família pode solicitar certidões atualizadas nas Conservatórias ou nos balcões integrados do Portal Municipal de Timor-Leste (Balkaun Úniku) [1] [3].
  • Outorga de testamento nos termos do Código Civil: Enquanto mantiver plena capacidade de entendimento, a pessoa doente pode organizar a transmissão dos seus bens através de testamento público (lavrado pelo notário no livro de notas do Cartório Notarial do Ministério da Justiça de Timor-Leste) ou testamento cerrado, respeitando a quota de legítima reservada por lei ao cônjuge sobrevivo, descendentes ou ascendentes [1] [2].
  • Organização documental e coordenação internacional: Aconselhamos a reunir títulos de propriedade fundiária, apólices de seguro, contratos bancários e comprovativos de contribuições para o Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social de Timor-Leste [2] [4]. Caso existam bens ou herdeiros residentes no estrangeiro, o Cartório Notarial pode preparar procurações e disposições testamentárias aptas a produzir efeitos internacionais mediante legalização consular [1] [2].

pt.closingQuestion: O seu familiar está inscrito no regime contributivo do Instituto Nacional de Segurança Social (INSS) ou pretende aceder aos apoios do Ministério da Solidariedade Social e Inclusão (MSSI), e em que município de Timor-Leste precisam de organizar prioritariamente o acompanhamento médico e notarial para que possamos detalhar os próximos passos?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Malta: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Malta: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Malta: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Malta. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to manage medical certification, civil registration, funeral or repatriation arrangements, social security and financial notifications, and succession administration under Maltese law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or residential facility deaths: When a death occurs in a public hospital such as Mater Dei Hospital, Gozo General Hospital, or a licensed care facility in Malta, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official medical Certificate of Death and Cause Thereof (Form DH35) [1].
  • Deaths at home under natural circumstances: If your family member died at home from a known natural condition, contact the family doctor or the nearest public health centre immediately so a registered physician can verify the death in person and complete Form DH35 [1].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or accidental deaths: If the death was unexpected, occurred without recent medical attendance, or involved an accident, notify the Malta Police Force immediately. A Duty Magistrate will open a magisterial inquiry and order a forensic examination or autopsy at the Mater Dei Hospital mortuary before authorising the release of the medical certificate and the body [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with Identità (Public Registry)
steps.html:
• Statutory registration deadline: Under the Maltese Civil Code, a death must be declared and registered with Identità (Public Registry) within 2 working days of the medical certification, either at the Malta Public Registry in Evans Building, Valletta, or at the Gozo Public Registry in Victoria [1].
  • Required documents and identity card return: The declarant (often a relative or the authorised funeral director) submits the signed Form DH35 and must surrender the deceased person's physical Maltese identity card or residence document so the civil status record can be updated [1] [2].
  • Ordering official Acts of Death: Once the registration is processed, apply through the Servizz.gov public service portal or directly with Identità (Public Registry) to obtain official extracts or full copies of the Act of Death, which are required by banks, insurers, notaries, and pension authorities [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial and local mortuary permits: Engage a licensed funeral director in Malta to coordinate mortuary release, health clearance, and interment at the Addolorata Cemetery, a parish cemetery, or the Gozo cemetery. Burials in Malta generally take place after a minimum statutory waiting period of 24 hours from death, subject to public health authorisation [1].
  • Cremation and overseas repatriation: If your family member requested cremation abroad or if the remains must be repatriated to another country, the funeral director obtains a Port Health Office mortuary pass (laissez-passer for a corpse), an embalming and zinc-lined coffin sealing certificate, and a freedom-from-infection certificate [1].
  • Apostille and consular legalisation: When Maltese death certificates must be presented to foreign civil registries or courts outside the European Union, request an Apostille from the Ministry for Foreign and European Affairs in Valletta, or request a multilingual standard form under EU Regulation 2016/1191 for use within EU member states [1].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Banks, and Claim Grants
steps.html:
• Reporting to the Department of Social Security: Notify the Department of Social Security promptly via the Servizz.gov online reporting service (Service WEB-05264) or a local Servizz.gov hub to stop ongoing retirement, invalidity, or social assistance payments and prevent overpayments that heirs would otherwise have to refund [2] [3].
  • Survivor and widow/er pensions: A surviving spouse or registered partner, as well as eligible dependent children, can apply to the Department of Social Security for a contributory Widow's/Widower's Pension or survivor benefit, submitting the Act of Death if the death occurred abroad (for deaths registered in Malta, the registry updates are shared directly) [3].
  • Funeral Expenses Grant: The individual who paid the funeral invoice for a resident of Malta may apply online within 6 months of the funeral for the statutory Funeral Expenses Grant (calculated at 13.04% of eligible invoice costs, up to a maximum of EUR 175) by submitting fiscal receipts and the invoice breakdown [4].
  • Banking and utility notifications: Present an official Act of Death to Maltese retail banks to freeze sole accounts and verify joint account mandates, and submit Form G through ARMS Ltd or Servizz.gov to transfer residential water and electricity accounts [1] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and File the Declaration Causa Mortis
steps.html:
• Testamentary searches: Instruct a warranted Notary Public in Malta to conduct official testamentary searches at both the Public Registry and the Courts of Justice (Voluntary Jurisdiction) to establish whether the deceased left a public or secret will, or whether the estate devolves by intestate succession under the Civil Code [5].
  • Declaration Causa Mortis and succession duty: Although Malta does not levy a general inheritance tax on bank deposits, the transmission of immovable property in Malta and company shares requires a notarial Declaration Causa Mortis registered with the Malta Tax and Customs Administration under the Duty on Documents and Transfers Act (Chapter 364) [5].
  • Deadlines, valuations, and cross-border heirs: Duty on immovable property (generally 5%, or 3.5% on qualifying residential property reliefs) is assessed on an architect's (perit) market valuation as at the date of death. Filing within 6 months preserves applicable administrative rebates, whereas filing after 1 year triggers statutory interest. Heirs residing abroad may appoint a representative in Malta via a notarised and Apostilled power of attorney, and cross-border EU estates are coordinated under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation 650/2012) [5].

closingQuestion: Did the death occur in Malta or Gozo, and did the deceased leave immovable property or bank accounts in Malta or another country so we can tailor the exact succession and registration requirements?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malta: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malta: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Malta: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Malta is diagnosed with a serious or life-limiting illness, taking early medical, legal, and financial steps while the person retains full decision-making capacity ensures their care preferences and practical affairs are protected. Below, we set out the five key official steps to coordinate palliative care, medical representation, powers of attorney, social security support, and estate preparation in Malta.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care and Public Health Services
steps.html:
• Specialist community and inpatient palliative care: Request a referral from the attending consultant at Mater Dei Hospital, Sir Anthony Mamo Oncology Centre, or the family doctor to Hospice Malta, which provides free multidisciplinary home care, symptom management, day therapy, equipment loans, and family support across Malta and Gozo [1].
  • Public healthcare and community nursing: Coordinate through the Ministry for Health and Active Ageing, CommCare community nursing teams, and the Pharmacy of Your Choice (POYC) scheme so prescribed palliative medications and Schedule V entitlement cards are active for continuous symptom relief [1] [5].
  • Private health insurance notifications: If your family member holds private medical insurance, obtain pre-authorisation for home nursing, specialist consultations, or inpatient palliative care to clarify policy limits and direct-billing arrangements [5].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Medical Communication Consents
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment preferences: While Malta does not currently have a standalone statutory register for binding advance healthcare directives, an adult with full mental capacity may record written care preferences, pain-management goals, and refusal of specific invasive interventions directly in their clinical file with the treating medical team at Mater Dei Hospital or Hospice Malta [1] [5].
  • Designating a primary medical contact: Under Malta's Patient Charter and clinical governance rules, the patient should formally name a trusted family member or representative in their hospital and community care records who is authorised to receive clinical updates and participate in multidisciplinary care conferences [1] [5].
  • Coordinating emergency care plans: Ensure a written summary of current diagnoses, medication regimens, and palliative care contacts is kept at home so emergency doctors or visiting community nurses can follow the agreed clinical care plan [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Financial Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarial mandate (power of attorney): Under the Maltese Civil Code (Chapter 16), a general or special mandate (prokura) must be executed while the grantor has full mental capacity. Engage a warranted Notary Public in Malta to draft a clear power of attorney authorising a trusted representative to manage bank accounts, sign contracts, or administer immovable property, and have the notary register it on the Notarial Portal [3].
  • Appointing a social security Administrator: If the ill person requires someone to manage their pension or benefit payments, submit an Application for the Appointment of an Administrator through Servizz.gov to the Department of Social Security, supported by a certified copy of the registered Power of Attorney or medical documentation [3].
  • Bank mandates and capacity safeguards: Because an ordinary mandate in Malta can be challenged or terminated if the grantor later loses mental capacity (potentially requiring a Court of Voluntary Jurisdiction guardianship or curatorship order), visit the person's Maltese banks immediately while capacity is intact to complete each institution's own power-of-attorney verification forms [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability Allowances and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Disability and Severe Disability Assistance: Apply through Servizz.gov (Service WEB-04221) to the Department of Social Security for Disability Assistance or Severe Disability Assistance, which are assessed by an Inter-Professional Board using the functional criteria of the World Health Organization ICF framework [2].
  • Carer's Allowance and Increased Carer's Allowance: Family members or caregivers providing full-time care at home to a person with high dependency needs may apply to the Department of Social Security for the Carer's Allowance or Increased Carer's Allowance, alongside municipal subsidised home-help services through Active Ageing and Community Care [2] [3].
  • Statutory employment leave for carers: Employed family members in Malta are entitled under the Work-Life Balance for Parents and Carers Regulations to request up to 5 working days of unpaid carers' leave per year for serious medical care needs, as well as flexible working arrangements upon presenting medical certification [2].

steps.title: Organise Wills, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Drafting or reviewing a Maltese will: While the ill person retains full testamentary capacity, consult a warranted Notary Public to execute or update a public will (testment pubbliku) or secret will, ensuring compliance with Maltese reserved-portion (legitima) rules and registering the note of enrolment at the Public Registry [4].
  • Consolidating civil status and financial records: Gather current marriage or civil union certificates from the Public Registry, title deeds and site plans for immovable property in Malta, and account statements for bank holdings and Malta Government Stocks held with the Treasury of Malta so future Causa Mortis declarations can be completed without delay [4].
  • Cross-border estate and mandate coordination: If the ill person is a foreign national residing in Malta or owns assets in another country, ask the notary whether to include an explicit choice-of-law clause under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation 650/2012) and obtain an Apostille for any power of attorney that must be recognised abroad [3] [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sweden: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sweden: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Sweden: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Sweden. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to manage medical certification, civil registration with the Swedish Tax Agency, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, survivor pension notifications, and the compulsory estate inventory under Swedish law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Clinical confirmation and two-part certification: In Sweden, a physician must examine the deceased to confirm the death clinically and issue two separate statutory medical documents: the Certificate of Death (dödsbevis), which is sent immediately to the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket), and the Certificate of Cause of Death (dödsorsaksintyg), which is submitted to the National Board of Health and Welfare (Socialstyrelsen) within three weeks [1] [2].
  • Hospital, care home, or home deaths: If the death occurred in a hospital, residential care facility, or at home under palliative care, the attending or on-call municipal physician completes the examination and transmits the dödsbevis electronically to Skatteverket on the next working day [2].
  • Unexpected or unexplained deaths requiring police clearance: If the death was sudden, accidental, or could not be attributed with certainty to natural causes, the physician must report the case to the Swedish Police Authority (Polismyndigheten) before Skatteverket can authorise burial or cremation, and a forensic medical examination (rättsmedicinsk undersökning) may be ordered [2].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Certificates from Skatteverket
steps.html:
• Automatic population register update: Once Skatteverket receives the physician's dödsbevis, the death is recorded in the Swedish Population Register (folkbokföringen) without the family needing to attend a registry office in person, and that registration automatically notifies other Swedish public agencies, banks, and municipal registries [1] [2].
  • Ordering the Death Certificate with Family Investigation: Request a dödsfallsintyg med släktutredning (Death Certificate with Genealogy/Family Investigation) from Skatteverket online or by phone. This official document confirms the date of death and lists the registered legal heirs (dödsbodelägare) entitled to represent the estate before probate is completed [1].
  • Immediate estate administration: Present the dödsfallsintyg med släktutredning to Swedish banks and service providers to pay urgent funeral invoices, rent, electricity, and ongoing housing costs directly from the deceased person's accounts while the estate inventory is being prepared [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• One-month statutory burial or cremation deadline: Under the Swedish Funeral Act (begravningslagen), the body must be buried or cremated within 1 month of the date of death once Skatteverket has issued the burial or cremation certificate (intyg för gravsättning eller kremering) [2].
  • Municipal burial fee coverage: Everyone who was registered as a resident in Sweden (folkbokförd) is covered by the compulsory burial fee (begravningsavgift), which funds the burial plot or cremation facility, statutory transport from the place of death, and the ceremonial hall through the Church of Sweden (Svenska kyrkan) or the municipal cemetery authority in Stockholm and Tranås [2].
  • International repatriation and Apostille: If the deceased is to be buried abroad, a licensed funeral director (begravningsbyrå) applies to Skatteverket or the relevant county authority for a laissez-passer for a corpse (passersedel för lik), arranges embalming and a hermetically sealed coffin, and obtains an Apostille from a Swedish Notary Public (notarius publicus) or an EU multilingual form if foreign authorities require legalised civil extracts [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Social Insurance, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• State survivor pensions via Pensionsmyndigheten: When Skatteverket registers a death, Pensionsmyndigheten (the Swedish Pensions Agency) is notified automatically and assesses whether survivors living in Sweden qualify for Adjustment Pension (omställningspension for a spouse or qualifying cohabitant under age 67), Child's Pension (barnpension), or legacy Widow's Pension (änkepension). Survivors residing outside Sweden must submit a formal application to Pensionsmyndigheten [4].
  • Occupational pensions and group life insurance: Check whether the deceased held an occupational pension (tjänstepension) with repayment cover (återbetalningsskydd) or family cover (familjeskydd), or trade-union group life insurance (grupplivförsäkring, such as TGL), and notify the relevant pension administrators or insurers [2] [4].
  • Municipal funeral assistance for low-asset estates: If the estate's total assets on the date of death are insufficient to cover basic funeral costs and essential bills, stop automatic direct debits (autogiro) immediately so funeral costs retain priority, and contact the deceased's home municipality (kommun) to apply for an estate inventory declaration (dödsboanmälan) and municipal financial funeral assistance (ekonomiskt bistånd till begravningskostnader) [2] [3].

steps.title: Complete the Estate Inventory (Bouppteckning) and Distribute the Estate
steps.html:
• Mandatory three-month estate inventory: Under the Swedish Inheritance Code (ärvdabalken), the estate co-owners (dödsbodelägare) must hold an estate inventory meeting (bouppteckningsförrättning) within 3 months of the death and submit the signed Estate Inventory (bouppteckning) and certified copies of any wills to Skatteverket within 1 month after it is drawn up [3].
  • No Swedish inheritance tax: Sweden abolished inheritance tax (arvsskatt), so heirs do not pay estate duty to Skatteverket; instead, recipients inherit the deceased's tax cost basis for any future capital gains tax when property or securities are later sold [2] [3].
  • Court-appointed administrator and cross-border estates: Once Skatteverket registers the bouppteckning, it serves as the official title document to close bank accounts, re-register real estate (lagfart) with Lantmäteriet, and execute the deed of estate distribution (arvskifte) [3]. If heirs cannot agree on administration, any heir can apply to the District Court (tingsrätten) under Sveriges Domstolar to appoint an independent estate administrator (boutredningsman), or apply to Skatteverket for a European Certificate of Succession (europeiskt arvsintyg) if assets or heirs are located across other EU member states [3] [5].

closingQuestion: Was your family member registered in the Swedish Population Register (folkbokförd) at the time of death, and are all heirs and estate assets located in Sweden or also in another country?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sweden: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sweden: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Sweden: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Sweden is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, putting structured medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the person retains full decision-making capacity ensures their wishes are respected and practical affairs remain manageable. Below, we set out the five main official steps to coordinate palliative care, healthcare preferences, continuing powers of attorney, caregiver benefits, and estate planning in Sweden.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care and Municipal Home Support
steps.html:
• Regional palliative care and ASIH: Through the regional healthcare system and 1177 Vårdguiden, the treating physician can refer your family member to specialised palliative home care (avancerad sjukvård i hemmet, ASIH), municipal home healthcare (hemsjukvård), or an inpatient hospice or palliative ward [1].
  • Coordinated individual care plan (SIP): Request a Coordinated Individual Plan (samordnad individuell plan, SIP) bringing together the regional medical team and the municipality's social care caseworker (biståndshandläggare) so symptom relief, home-care assistance (hemtjänst), and assistive medical equipment in the home are seamlessly aligned [1].
  • High-cost protection and patient fees: Verify that the person's regional high-cost protection (högkostnadsskydd) for outpatient care and prescription medicines is active, and ask the municipal care coordinator whether municipal home-care fees are reduced or waived during specialised palliative care [1].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Medical Communication Consents
steps.html:
• Patient autonomy and care planning dialogues: Under the Swedish Patient Act (patientlagen), healthcare must be designed in consultation with the patient. Ask the responsible physician for a formal care-planning dialogue (brytpunktssamtal) so your family member's goals for symptom control, place of care, and limits on life-prolonging interventions are recorded directly in their electronic medical record (journal) accessible via 1177 Vårdguiden [1].
  • Limits of Swedish living wills and healthcare proxies: In Sweden, a continuing power of attorney (framtidsfullmakt) cannot legally grant a proxy the authority to consent to or refuse medical or dental treatment on the patient's behalf [2]. Because healthcare decisions rest with the licensed clinician when a patient lacks capacity, written care preferences (livsslutsdirektiv or vårdvilja) should be documented in the medical record and shared with family members to guide clinical assessments [1] [2].
  • Authorising family access to medical updates: While capacity is intact, the ill person should record explicit consent in their medical file authorising healthcare staff to share clinical updates with designated relatives despite statutory healthcare secrecy rules (offentlighets- och sekretesslagen) [1].

steps.title: Execute a Continuing Power of Attorney (Framtidsfullmakt) and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Framtidsfullmakt: Under the Swedish Continuing Powers of Attorney Act (lag (2017:310) om framtidsfullmakter), an adult with full mental capacity can appoint one or more representatives (fullmaktshavare) to manage financial and personal affairs (such as paying bills, managing bank accounts, handling tax matters, and selling property or housing rights) if they later become permanently unable to do so due to illness [2] [3].
  • Strict formal witness requirements: The framtidsfullmakt must be in writing, state explicitly that it is a framtidsfullmakt, specify who the attorney-in-fact is and what matters are covered, and be signed by the grantor in the simultaneous presence of two witnesses who are not the appointed proxy and who sign to confirm the grantor's sound mind. Guidance on activation and optional court review is provided by Sveriges Domstolar [2].
  • Immediate bank mandates and Skatteverket representation: Because Swedish banks apply strict verification rules to powers of attorney and because statutory relative authority (anhörigbehörighet under Chapter 17 of the Parental Code) covers only routine everyday household payments, register bank-specific mandates immediately while the person can still use BankID, and register a tax and administrative representative (deklarationsombud) with Skatteverket [2] [3].

steps.title: Activate Caregiver Allowance (Närståendepenning) and Sickness Benefits
steps.html:
• Close Relative Benefit (Närståendepenning): Family members, partners, or close friends who take time off work to support a severely ill person in a life-threatening condition in Sweden can apply to Försäkringskassan (the Swedish Social Insurance Agency) for närståendepenning, which provides up to 100 compensation days in total per ill person (sharable among multiple caregivers) [4].
  • Medical statement and patient consent: To apply to Försäkringskassan, obtain a physician's medical statement (läkarutlåtande för närståendepenning) confirming the life-threatening illness and submit the patient's signed consent (or medical confirmation if the patient is no longer able to give written consent) [4].
  • Sickness and disability benefits for the ill person: Ensure that the ill person's own sickness benefit (sjukpenning), sickness compensation (sjukersättning), or additional cost allowance (merkostnadsersättning) with Försäkringskassan, as well as any employer-funded collective sickness insurance (such as AGS or ITP sickness pension), are active [4].

steps.title: Review Wills, Beneficiary Clauses, and Cross-Border Estate Documents
steps.html:
• Formal requirements for a Swedish will (Testamente): Under the Swedish Inheritance Code (ärvdabalken), a valid will (testamente) must be executed in writing while the testator has full mental capacity and signed in the simultaneous presence of two qualified, independent witnesses (aged 15 or older, not spouses, close relatives, or beneficiaries under the will), as outlined by Sveriges Domstolar [5].
  • Cohabitants, marital property, and pension beneficiaries: Because unmarried cohabitants (sambor) do not inherit from each other automatically under Swedish law, a written will is essential if a cohabitant is to inherit. Review whether occupational pensions (tjänstepension) and private life insurance policies carry active survivor repayment protection (återbetalningsskydd) and updated beneficiary clauses (förmånstagarförordnande) [5].
  • Cross-border assets and storage of originals: Because Sweden has no public central registry for wills, store the original signed testamente and framtidsfullmakt safely where trusted representatives can present the physical originals. If the ill person is a foreign citizen or owns assets outside Sweden, review whether to include an explicit choice-of-law clause under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation 650/2012) [2] [5].

closingQuestion: Is your family member currently receiving care at home or in hospital in Sweden, and have they already signed a framtidsfullmakt or a written will?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Norway: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Norway: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Norway: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Norway. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to manage medical death certification, automatic civil registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, survivor benefits with NAV, and probate administration before the District Court in Norway.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Electronic medical death certificate: When a person dies in Norway, a physician must examine the body and issue the official medical death certificate (legeerklæring om dødsfall), which is transmitted electronically to the National Population Register (Folkeregisteret) and the Norwegian Cause of Death Registry (Dødsårsaksregisteret) [1] [3].
  • Deaths in hospital, nursing homes, or at home: If the death occurs in a hospital or municipal nursing home (sykehjem), the attending doctor completes the declaration directly. If the death occurs at home, contact the local municipal out-of-hours medical service (legevakt at 116 117) or the family doctor (fastlege) so a physician can attend and confirm the death [1] [3].
  • Sudden or unnatural deaths requiring police notification: Under the Norwegian Criminal Procedure Act and Health Personnel Act, if a death is sudden, unexpected, accidental, or potentially unnatural, the physician must immediately notify the Norwegian Police (Politiet). The police decide whether to order a forensic autopsy (rettsmedisinsk obduksjon) before issuing clearance for burial, cremation, or international transport [3] [5].

steps.title: Confirm Civil Registration with Skatteetaten and the District Court
steps.html:
• Automatic registration in the National Population Register: In Norway, next of kin do not normally need to visit a registry office to register a death that occurred within the country. Once the physician submits the electronic medical death certificate, Skatteetaten (the Norwegian Tax Administration) records the death in the National Population Register (Folkeregisteret) and automatically notifies the local District Court (tingretten), NAV, banks, and public agencies [1].
  • Notification to the District Court (Norges domstoler): Either the funeral director (begravelsesbyrå) or the family also notifies the local District Court or the police/lensmann office where the deceased lived, triggering the court's formal guidance letter to the registered heirs on how to settle the estate [1] [5].
  • Obtaining proof of death and probate authority: Norway does not issue a standalone civil death certificate for routine domestic use; instead, Skatteetaten confirms the registration in Folkeregisteret, and the District Court under Norges domstoler issues the official Probate Certificate (skifteattest) or Certificate of Undivided Estate (uskifteattest), which serves as the legal proof of death and representation authority for banks and foreign institutions [1] [5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Statutory 10-working-day funeral deadline: Under the Norwegian Funeral Act (gravferdsloven), burial (gravlegging) or cremation (kremasjon) must take place no later than 10 working days after the date of death, and the person assuming responsibility for the funeral (gravferdsansvarlig) submits the formal request to the municipal cemetery authority (gravplassmyndigheten / kirkevergen), usually through a licensed funeral director [3] [4].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased is to be transported out of Norway for burial abroad, the funeral director applies to the Norwegian police for a mortuary passport (likpass), obtains a public health certificate confirming no contagious hazard, and seals the body in a zinc-lined or regulations-compliant transport coffin [3].
  • Apostille and consular legalisation: When Norwegian succession or death confirmation documents (such as a skifteattest issued by the District Court or a population register printout from Skatteetaten) must be presented abroad, obtain an Apostille stamp from the County Governor (Statsforvalteren) before submitting them to foreign authorities or consulates [1] [5].

steps.title: Notify NAV, Pension Funds, and Banks
steps.html:
• Means-tested funeral grant and transport support: Apply to NAV (the Norwegian Labour and Welfare Administration) for the means-tested Funeral Grant (gravferdsstønad, up to the statutory maximum based on the estate's financial assets and insurance payouts) and for coverage of necessary domestic or cross-border transport of the deceased (stønad ved båretransport) when the person died more than 20 km from their place of residence in Norway [4].
  • Adjustment Allowance and Children's Pension: Surviving spouses, registered partners, or qualifying cohabitants under age 67 can apply to NAV for the Adjustment Allowance (omstillingsstønad), and surviving minor or student children can claim the Children's Pension (barnepensjon) [4].
  • Occupational pensions and bank account access: Check whether the deceased held public-sector occupational pension rights (such as with Statens pensjonskasse, SPK, or KLP) or private occupational pensions (tjenestepensjon) and employer group life insurance (gruppelivsforsikring). Norwegian banks automatically freeze the deceased's accounts and BankID upon notification from Folkeregisteret, while permitting direct payment of the funeral invoice from the deceased's account prior to the skifteattest [3] [4] [5].

steps.title: Settle the Estate (Dødsbo) and File Final Tax Declarations
steps.html:
• Inspecting assets and debts before assuming liability: Before deciding whether to take over the estate in private probate (privat skifte) - which makes the signing heirs personally liable for the deceased's debts - heirs can request a Preliminary Authorization to Inspect Finances (formuesfullmakt) from the District Court under Norges domstoler, use the digital estate overview (Digitalt dødsbo via Altinn where available), or ask the court to publish a 6-week preclusive creditor notice (proklama) [5].
  • 60-day deadline for Privat Skifte, Uskifte, or Offentlig Skifte: Within 60 days of the death, the heirs must submit either a Declaration of Private Probate (erklæring om privat skifte) or a surviving spouse/cohabitant's request for an Undivided Estate (uskifte) to the District Court to receive the skifteattest or uskifteattest. If the estate is insolvent or heirs disagree, they can leave the estate or request public probate (offentlig skifte) managed by a court-appointed administrator (bobestyrer) [5].
  • Inheritance tax rules, tax returns, and cross-border estates: Norway abolished inheritance tax (arveavgift), so heirs pay no estate duty, instead inheriting the deceased's tax cost basis under the continuity principle (kontinuitetsprinsippet) for future capital gains [2]. The estate's tax representative (skiftefullmektig) must check the deceased's tax return (skattemelding) with Skatteetaten and can request advance tax assessment (forhåndsfastsetting) before final distribution. Note that because Norway is not an EU member state, the EU Succession Regulation does not apply directly in Norway; instead, the Norwegian Inheritance Act (arveloven) governs estates of persons habitually resident in Norway at death, requiring cross-border coordination if real estate or heirs are located abroad [2] [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Norway: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Norway: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Norway: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Norway is diagnosed with a serious or life-limiting illness, putting structured medical, legal, and financial plans in place while the person retains full decision-making capacity ensures their personal wishes and practical affairs are protected. Below, we set out the five main official steps to coordinate palliative care, healthcare directives, continuing powers of attorney, caregiver benefits, and succession planning in Norway.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care and Municipal Health Services
steps.html:
• Municipal and specialist palliative care: Ask the regular general practitioner (fastlege) or hospital specialist team to refer your family member to the hospital's palliative care team (palliativt team) and the municipality's health and care service allocation office (tildelingskontor) for home nursing (hjemmesykepleie), municipal cancer/palliative coordinators (kreftkoordinator), or a short-term or permanent palliative care bed [4].
  • Individual Care Plan and patient fee exemptions: Request an Individual Care Plan (individuell plan) and a designated municipal care coordinator if the person requires coordinated health and social services. Under the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme (Folketrygden), patients in an established terminal or palliative phase qualify for full exemption on essential palliative prescriptions (blå resept, § 2-90) and assistive medical equipment loans from the NAV Assistive Technology Centre (Hjelpemiddelsentralen) [4].
  • Digital health portal coordination: Use the national health portal Helsenorge to review hospital appointments, active prescriptions, and shared summary care records (kjernejournal) across municipal and specialist care providers [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Digital Health Proxies
steps.html:
• Advance care planning dialogues (Forhåndssamtaler): Under the Norwegian Patient and User Rights Act (pasient- og brukerrettighetsloven), patients have the right to participate in treatment decisions and to refuse life-prolonging treatment (rett til å motsette seg livsforlengende behandling, § 4-9). Request a structured advance care planning conversation (forhåndssamtale) with the responsible doctor so the person's treatment goals and resuscitation preferences are recorded in their clinical file and kjernejournal [1] [4].
  • Granting digital proxy access on Helsenorge: While the ill person still has BankID access and full capacity, they can log in to Helsenorge directly to grant a digital power of attorney (fullmakt) allowing a trusted family member to view medical records, renew prescriptions, and communicate with healthcare services on their behalf [2].
  • Explicit health wording in a Fremtidsfullmakt: If a continuing power of attorney (fremtidsfullmakt) is also intended to give the proxy access to digital health services on Helsenorge after capacity is lost, Helsenorge requires the document to state explicitly that the proxy is authorised to represent the grantor in personal/health matters and to access health information [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute a Continuing Power of Attorney (Fremtidsfullmakt) and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Drafting a Fremtidsfullmakt while capacity is intact: Under the Norwegian Guardianship Act (vergemålsloven, Chapter 10), an adult of sound mind can execute a Continuing Power of Attorney (fremtidsfullmakt) appointing one or more proxies (fullmektig) to manage their financial and personal affairs (including bank accounts, tax filings, debts, and selling or transferring real estate identified by cadastral numbers gårdsnummer and bruksnummer) if they later lose mental capacity due to serious illness. Official formal guidance is published by Sivilrettsforvaltningen [3].
  • Strict witness formalities: The fremtidsfullmakt must be in writing, state clearly that it is to take effect once the grantor becomes incapable of looking after their own interests, and be signed by the grantor in the simultaneous presence of two witnesses aged 18 or older who are not the proxy (nor the proxy's spouse, cohabitant, parent, child, or grandchild). The witnesses must sign while the grantor is present and should record the grantor's date of birth, the witnesses' addresses, and confirmation that the grantor signed of their own free will and with full mental capacity [3].
  • Confirmation by Statsforvalteren and immediate bank mandates: Because a fremtidsfullmakt only takes effect upon loss of capacity and normally requires formal confirmation (stadfestelse av ikrafttredelse) from Statsforvalteren (the County Governor) supported by a medical certificate, also set up ordinary bank access mandates (disposisjonsrett) directly inside the person's Norwegian online bank while they can still authenticate with BankID [1] [3].

steps.title: Activate End-of-Life Care Allowance and Illness Benefits
steps.html:
• End-of-Life Care Allowance (Pleiepenger i livets sluttfase): Family members, relatives, or close friends who take time off work (at least 20% absence) to care for a person in the terminal phase of life in a private home in Norway can apply to NAV (Arbeids- og velferdsetaten) for pleiepenger i livets sluttfase, which compensates lost income up to 6G for up to 60 days in total per patient (sharable among several caregivers) [4].
  • Required medical declaration for NAV: To claim pleiepenger i livets sluttfase, the treating doctor completes the medical declaration on NAV Form 09-12.05 confirming that the patient is in the final phase of life and is being cared for in a private home rather than a hospital or nursing home [4].
  • Sickness, disability, and basic/attendance benefits: Ensure the ill person's own sickness benefit (sykepenger), work assessment allowance (arbeidsavklaringspenger, AAP), disability benefit (uføretrygd), basic benefit (grunnstønad for extra illness-related expenses), or municipal care allowance (omsorgsstønad) are activated, and check any employer occupational critical-illness or disability policies [4].

steps.title: Review Wills, Statutory Forced Heirship, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Norwegian will (Testament): Under the Norwegian Inheritance Act (arveloven), a will must be made in writing while the testator has full testamentary capacity and signed (or acknowledged) in the presence of two independent witnesses aged 18 or older who know the document is a will and sign while the testator is present, as detailed by Norges domstoler [5].
  • Forced heirship (Pliktdelsarv) and cohabitant rules: If the ill person has children or direct descendants (livsarvinger), two-thirds of the net estate is protected as statutory forced heirship (pliktdelsarv), capped at 15 times the National Insurance basic amount (15G) per child, while a spouse also holds statutory minimum inheritance and undivided-estate (uskifte) rights. Unmarried cohabitants (samboere) without common children have no automatic inheritance right unless provided for in a valid will [5].
  • Voluntary court safekeeping and cross-border assets: Ask the local District Court (tingretten) under Norges domstoler to register and store the original will in the national court register of wills for a small statutory fee so it is surfaced automatically during future probate. Because Norway is outside the EU Succession Regulation, if the ill person is a foreign national or owns property abroad, coordinate with legal counsel to ensure the Norwegian will and fremtidsfullmakt are harmonised with foreign jurisdictions [3] [5].
