title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Slovakia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Slovakia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Slovakia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Slovakia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person retains full legal capacity protects their care preferences and household stability. Below, we outline the five main official steps in chronological order under Slovak law.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist palliative and hospice referrals: Ask your family member's attending specialist or general practitioner (všeobecný lekár) for a referral to an inpatient hospice (hospic), palliative medicine department (oddelenie paliatívnej medicíny), or mobile hospice service (mobilný hospic) [1]. Under Slovak healthcare legislation overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Slovak Republic (Ministerstvo zdravotníctva Slovenskej republiky), medical palliative care and home nursing Care Agencies (Agentúra domácej ošetrovateľskej starostlivosti - ADOS) are covered through mandatory public health insurance (Všeobecná zdravotná poisťovňa, Dôvera, or Union) when prescribed by a physician [1].
  • Long-term social-health care coordination: If the ill person requires integrated nursing and personal assistance, apply simultaneously to the municipality (obec or mestská časť) or self-governing region (vyšší územný celok - VÚC) for a social care assessment (posúdenie odkázanosti na sociálnu službu) to access municipal home care services (opatrovateľská služba) or specialised residential facilities [2] [3].
  • Medical equipment and symptom management: The attending physician or palliative specialist can prescribe assistive medical devices (zdravotnícke pomôcky), such as adjustable hospital beds, oxygen concentrators, and pressure-relief mattresses, which are reimbursed in whole or in part by the patient's public health insurance fund [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Medical Information Authorisations
steps.html:
• Informed consent and refusal of treatment (Informovaný súhlas): Under Slovak Act No. 576/2004 Coll. on Healthcare, a patient with full legal capacity has the right to accept or refuse specific medical procedures in writing through an informed consent or written refusal document (revers), which must be recorded in the patient's medical documentation and electronic health record (eZdravie) [1].
  • Authorising family access to medical records: Ensure your family member signs a written authorisation at the hospital and with their general practitioner designating specific family members who may receive confidential health status updates, inspect medical records, and consult with the clinical team if the patient becomes unable to communicate [1].
  • Supportive decision-making and representation: While Slovak law does not establish a standalone statutory living will registry comparable to some other jurisdictions, recording clear written care preferences with the treating palliative team and executing a general civil power of attorney ensures the care team and family have documented guidance on symptom control, hospitalisation, and place-of-care preferences [1] [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• General and special powers of attorney (Plnomocenstvo): While your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity (spôsobilosť na právne úkony), arrange for them to sign a written power of attorney under the Slovak Civil Code authorising a trusted representative to act in administrative, tax, postal, and property matters [4] [5]. For real estate transactions, corporate actions, or broad legal certainty, have the signature officially verified (osvedčenie podpisu) or drafted as a notarial deed (notárska zápisnica) by a notary registered with the Notarial Chamber of the Slovak Republic (Notárska komora Slovenskej republiky) [5].
  • Mobile notary visits: If your family member cannot travel due to illness, a Slovak notary can conduct an official verification visit at the hospital, care facility, or private home to verify capacity and authenticate signatures on the spot [5].
  • Bank account disposal mandates (Dispozičné právo): Slovak commercial banks frequently require their own internal account mandate forms rather than a general power of attorney. Contact each bank while your family member can still sign in branch, via mobile banking, or before a notary, and verify whether you should establish joint account access or a dedicated mandate that remains operational during serious illness [4] [5].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Care Allowances, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Disability pension (Invalidný dôchodok) and sickness benefits: If your family member's illness reduces their capacity to perform gainful activity by more than 40 percent compared with a healthy person, file an application for a disability pension with the Social Insurance Agency (Sociálna poisťovňa), either at the local branch or electronically through the Central Public Administration Portal (Ústredný portál verejnej správy) [3] [4].
  • Long-term nursing allowance (Dlhodobé ošetrovné): Working family members who care for a relative with a serious palliative or severe health condition following hospitalisation (or in terminal palliative care) can claim long-term nursing benefit (dlhodobé ošetrovné) from the Social Insurance Agency for up to 90 calendar days, during which participating family caregivers can rotate care [3] [4].
  • Severe disability compensation and care allowance (Peňažný príspevok na opatrovanie): Through the Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Family of the Slovak Republic (Ministerstvo práce, sociálnych vecí a rodiny Slovenskej republiky) and the local Office of Labour, Social Affairs and Family (Úrad práce, sociálnych vecí a rodiny - ÚPSVaR), apply for a severe disability assessment (ťažké zdravotné postihnutie - ŤZP) and the monthly financial allowance for personal caring (peňažný príspevok na opatrovanie) when your family member requires high-level daily assistance (degree IV or V dependence) [2].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Cross-Border Estate Documents
steps.html:
• Executing and registering a valid will (Závet): To ensure your family member's property wishes are legally robust and cannot be misplaced, consider having a will drawn up as a notarial deed by a member of the Notarial Chamber of the Slovak Republic, which is then mandatory-registered in the Notarial Central Register of Wills (Notársky centrálny register závetov) [5]. Under the Slovak Civil Code, remember that descendants are statutory forced heirs (neopomenuteľní dedičia) entitled to a protected minimum share unless validly disinherited on strict statutory grounds [5].
  • Organising civil and property records: Gather your family member's birth certificate (rodný list), marriage certificate (sobášny list), title deeds or cadastre references (list vlastníctva), insurance policies, and pension statements, and request any missing civil registry duplicates online via the Central Public Administration Portal or through the Ministry of Interior of the Slovak Republic (Ministerstvo vnútra Slovenskej republiky) [4] [6].
  • Cross-border assets and EU succession choice of law: If your family member holds foreign nationality or owns property in another country, consult a Slovak notary regarding EU Succession Regulation (EU) No 650/2012, including whether to include an explicit choice-of-law clause (professio iuris) in the will and whether foreign powers of attorney require an Apostille [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Hungary: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Hungary: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Hungary: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Hungary. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order - covering medical death certification, civil registration, funeral and international repatriation formalities, survivor pension and administrative notifications, and notarial succession proceedings under Hungarian law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death (*Halottvizsgálati bizonyítvány*)
steps.html:
• Hospital or inpatient care institution deaths: When a death occurs in a hospital, clinic, or residential care facility in Hungary, the attending or institutional physician performs the mandatory post-mortem examination (halottvizsgálat) and records the Medical Death Certificate (Halottvizsgálati bizonyítvány) electronically in the National Electronic Health Services Space (Elektronikus Egészségügyi Szolgáltatási Tér - EESZT) [1] [2]. The hospital pathology department determines whether an institutional autopsy (kórbonctani boncolás) is required or can be waived upon written family request when the cause of death is medically unambiguous [1].
  • Deaths at home or outside a medical facility: If your family member dies at home, call the National Ambulance Service (Országos Mentőszolgálat at 104 or 112) or the on-call general practitioner (háziorvos / ügyelet) [1]. The physician conducts the external post-mortem examination on site, issues the death examination certificate via the National Electronic Health Services Space, and authorises a licensed funeral provider to transport the deceased to a mortuary cooling facility [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or forensic deaths: If the death occurred under unclear, sudden, or suspected unnatural circumstances, the examining doctor notifies the Hungarian Police (Rendőrség), which orders an official or forensic autopsy (hatósági vagy igazságügyi boncolás) before burial or cremation clearance can be granted [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registrar (*Anyakönyvvezető*)
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under Hungarian civil registration law accessible through the Central Government Portal (Magyarország.hu) and district government offices (Kormányhivatalok), the death must be reported on the first working day following the death examination and registered by the civil registrar (anyakönyvvezető) of the municipality or Budapest district where the death occurred [2] [3]. While the physician transmits the electronic medical certificate directly via the National Electronic Health Services Space, the person arranging the funeral (or the authorised funeral director) must present the deceased's personal documents to the registrar within five days [1] [2].
  • Documents required for registration: Submit the paper copies of the Medical Death Certificate (if issued in paper form alongside the electronic filing), the deceased's Hungarian identity card (személyazonosító igazolvány), address card (lakcímkártya), driver's licence, passport, birth certificate (születési anyakönyvi kivonat), and marriage certificate (házassági anyakönyvi kivonat) or final divorce/widowhood proof [2] [3].
  • Issuance of the official Death Certificate (Halotti anyakönyvi kivonat): Once registered in the Electronic Civil Registry System (Elektronikus Anyakönyvi Rendszer), the registrar issues the first original Death Certificate (halotti anyakönyvi kivonat) free of charge, invalidates the deceased's identity documents, and notifies the municipal clerk (jegyző) to initiate the estate inventory [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral service (Temetkezési szolgáltató): Under Hungarian Act XLIII of 1999 on Cemeteries and Funeral Services, human remains must be transported and prepared by a licensed funeral operator [2]. Many families grant the funeral home a written power of attorney (meghatalmazás) to collect the Medical Death Certificate from the hospital, complete civil registration with the local registrar, and obtain cemetery or crematorium permits [2].
  • Burial and cremation clearance: Inhumation (koporsós temetés) or cremation (hamvasztás) may proceed only after the examining physician (and, in forensic cases, the investigating authority) has explicitly authorised the chosen disposition method on the Medical Death Certificate [1] [2]. If the death occurred outside a hospital and cremation is requested, county public health clearance may also be required.
  • International repatriation and document legalisation: To transport a body out of Hungary, the funeral provider obtains a corpse transport permit (halottszállítási engedély) from the public health department of the competent district government office (Kormányhivatalok), using a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin [2]. For official documents used abroad, EU Member States accept the Hungarian death certificate with a multilingual standard form under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191, whereas non-EU jurisdictions require an Apostille from the Hungarian Chamber of Civil Law Notaries (Magyar Országos Közjegyzői Kamara - MOKK), the Ministry of Justice, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, or consular legalisation [2] [6].

steps.title: Notify Authorities and Claim Survivor Pensions and Local Support
steps.html:
• Reporting death of a pensioner and claiming unpaid benefits: If the deceased received a Hungarian state pension, notify the Pension Payment Directorate of the Hungarian State Treasury (Magyar Államkincstár Nyugdíjfolyósító Igazgatóság) within 15 days [4] [5]. Any pension due for the month of death that remained unpaid can be claimed by cohabiting family members in statutory order (spouse, child, grandchild, parent) within one year, or otherwise through the estate [4].
  • Survivor pensions (Hozzátartozói nyugellátások): File claims for a widow's or widower's pension (özvegyi nyugdíj), orphan's allowance (árvaellátás), or parental pension (szülői nyugdíj) with the Hungarian State Treasury either online through the Central Government Portal or at any government customer service window (Kormányablak) [3] [4] [5]. A temporary widow(er)'s pension is payable for at least one year after the spouse's death and can be revived or converted into a permanent widow(er)'s pension if statutory age, disability, or child-raising conditions are met [4] [5].
  • Municipal funeral assistance, banks, and utilities: While Hungary does not pay a universal national funeral grant, local municipal governments (helyi önkormányzat) often provide a means-tested local settlement funeral benefit (települési támogatás temetési segély) [2] [3]. Present the death certificate to Hungarian banks to freeze sole accounts and check whether any accounts carry a formal beneficiary designation on death (halál esetére szóló kedvezményezett), which allows payout outside probate, and notify utilities, insurers, and the National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV) [2] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession Proceedings (*Hagyatéki eljárás*)
steps.html:
• Municipal estate inventory (Hagyatéki leltár): In Hungary, succession proceedings are initiated ex officio without a court petition from the heirs [2] [6]. Once the civil registrar records the death, the municipal clerk (jegyző) of the deceased's last permanent Hungarian residence contacts the family to compile the official estate inventory (hagyatéki leltár) within 30 days, listing Hungarian real estate, bank accounts, vehicles, company shares, and liabilities [2] [6].
  • Exclusive competence of civil law notaries (Közjegyző): The municipal clerk forwards the completed inventory to the territorially competent civil law notary (közjegyző) operating under the Hungarian Chamber of Civil Law Notaries, assigned strictly by statutory district and month-of-death rules [6]. The notary queries the National Register of Wills (Végrendeletek Országos Nyilvántartása), schedules the probate hearing (hagyatéki tárgyalás), and issues the formal Grant of Probate (hagyatékátadó végzés) transferring legal title to the heirs [6].
  • Inheritance duty exemptions and cross-border coordination: Under Hungarian Act XCIII of 1990 on Duties, inheritance acquired by the deceased's direct-line relatives (children, grandchildren, parents, including adoptive relationships), surviving spouse, and siblings is 100 percent exempt from Hungarian inheritance duty (öröklési illeték), while other heirs generally face an 18 percent general rate (9 percent on residential property) alongside statutory notarial fees [6]. Where assets or heirs span multiple EU Member States, the Hungarian notary coordinates jurisdiction under EU Succession Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 and can issue a European Certificate of Succession (Európai Öröklési Bizonyítvány) [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Hungary: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Hungary: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Hungary: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Hungary is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and administrative arrangements in place while the ill person retains full decision-making capacity protects their care choices and financial security. Below, we set out the five main official steps in chronological order under Hungarian law.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist hospice and palliative care referrals: Ask your family member's attending specialist or general practitioner (háziorvos) for a referral to an inpatient hospice ward (bentfekvő hospice ellátás), mobile home hospice team (otthoni hospice ellátás), or specialist home nursing service (otthoni szakápolás) [1] [2]. In Hungary, prescribed medical palliative care, home hospice visits, and specialist home nursing are funded by the National Health Insurance Fund Administration (Nemzeti Egészségbiztosítási Alapkezelő - NEAK) for patients covered by mandatory public health insurance (TAJ kártya) [1] [2].
  • Medical aids and symptom management: The treating specialist or general practitioner can issue electronic prescriptions (e-Recept) via the National Electronic Health Services Space (Elektronikus Egészségügyi Szolgáltatási Tér - EESZT) for pain management medications and subsidised medical equipment (gyógyászati segédeszközök), such as adjustable hospital beds, oxygen therapy devices, and mobility aids [1].
  • Municipal and social home care (Házi segítségnyújtás): Alongside clinical care, contact the local municipal social service center (önkormányzati szociális szolgáltató) or district government office (Kormányhivatalok) via the Central Government Portal (Magyarország.hu) to request personal social home care (személyi gondozás and szociális segítés) or admission to a specialized residential care facility [2] [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Name a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Advance medical directive (Előzetes egészségügyi rendelkezés) and treatment refusal: Under Hungarian Act CLIV of 1997 on Healthcare, an adult patient with full legal capacity (cselekvőképes beteg) has the right to execute an advance directive consenting to or refusing specific medical interventions - including life-sustaining or life-saving treatments when suffering from an incurable, terminal illness that would rapidly lead to end of life even with medical care [1] [6]. To refuse life-sustaining treatment in advance, the declaration must be executed in a public deed before a civil law notary (közjegyzői okirat), in a private deed of full probative force signed by two witnesses, or personally before the attending physician, accompanied by a psychiatric and medical board certification confirming full capacity and informed decision-making [1] [6].
  • Naming a surrogate healthcare decision-maker (Meghatalmazott személy): In the same authentic instrument, your family member can designate a surrogate medical representative (helyettes döntéshozó) who is legally authorised to grant or withhold consent to medical procedures if the patient loses capacity, overriding the default statutory hierarchy of relatives [1] [6].
  • Digital health access and self-determination (EESZT Önrendelkezés): Using their Citizen Portal login (Ügyfélkapu+ or DÁP) on the National Electronic Health Services Space or in person at a government window (Kormányablak), your family member can register an authorised representative (meghatalmazott) to access their electronic medical records, discharge summaries, and e-prescriptions [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• General and special powers of attorney (Meghatalmazás): While your family member retains full legal capacity (cselekvőképesség), execute a written power of attorney under the Hungarian Civil Code (Act V of 2013) empowering a trusted family member to handle administrative, tax, postal, and property affairs [3] [6]. Under Hungarian law, a general power of attorney valid for an indefinite period (általános meghatalmazás) is valid for a maximum of five years at a time and must be drawn up in a private deed of full probative force (teljes bizonyító erejű magánokirat signed before two witnesses) or as a notarial deed (közjegyzői okirat) before a notary of the Hungarian Chamber of Civil Law Notaries (Magyar Országos Közjegyzői Kamara - MOKK) [6].
  • Advance legal declaration for future loss of capacity (Előzetes jognyilatkozat): Under the Hungarian Civil Code, an adult with full capacity can execute a preventive legal declaration (előzetes jognyilatkozat) in a notarial deed, before a guardianship authority, or before a court, naming who should serve as their guardian (gondnok) and how their personal and financial assets should be managed if capacity is ever restricted in the future; this declaration is recorded in the National Register of Advance Declarations [6].
  • Bank mandates and beneficiary designations on death: Hungarian banks strictly require their own internal account disposal mandates (rendelkezési jog) executed at a branch or via a mobile notary visit. At the same time, ask the bank about registering a statutory beneficiary designation in case of death (halál esetére szóló rendelkezés), which allows designated family members to access bank balances directly without waiting for notarial probate [6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Caregiver Allowances, and Leave
steps.html:
• Disability and rehabilitation benefits (Megváltozott munkaképességű személyek ellátásai): If your family member is of working age and has a severe health impairment verified by a comprehensive medical rehabilitation assessment, apply for disability allowance (rokkantsági ellátás) or disability pension/allowance (fogyatékossági támogatás) through the Rehabilitation Authority of the competent district government office (Kormányhivatalok) and the Hungarian State Treasury (Magyar Államkincstár) [2] [3] [4].
  • Nursing fee for family caregivers (Ápolási díj): A family member who provides permanent home care for a severely disabled or permanently ill relative requiring daily assistance can apply for the statutory Nursing Fee (ápolási díj, including increased or special nursing fee tiers emelt or kiemelt ápolási díj) at the district government office or Kormányablak, with long-term caregivers also eligible for old-age caregiver support (tartós ápolást végzők időskori támogatása) from the Hungarian State Treasury [2] [3] [4].
  • Statutory unpaid caregiver leave under the Labour Code: Under the Hungarian Labour Code, an employee is entitled to up to two years of unpaid leave (fizetés nélküli szabadság) for the personal home nursing of a relative requiring long-term care (certified by the treating physician), as well as up to five working days per year of caregiver time off (gondozói munkaidő-kedvezmény) for serious health reasons [2] [3].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Executing and registering a valid will (Végrendelet): Under the Hungarian Civil Code, a private written will (írásbeli magánvégrendelet) has strict formal requirements (either handwritten and signed from start to finish by the testator, or signed in the simultaneous presence of two witnesses with continuous page numbering), so having a public will (közvégrendelet) prepared or deposited with a notary of the Hungarian Chamber of Civil Law Notaries guarantees formal validity and mandatory registration in the National Register of Wills (Végrendeletek Országos Nyilvántartása) [6]. Note that descendants, the spouse, and parents may be entitled to a compulsory share (kötelesrész - one-third of their intestate share) unless validly disinherited [6].
  • Organising civil status and property records: Gather your family member's identity card, address card, birth and marriage certificates, land registry title deeds (tulajdoni lap), vehicle documents, and pension records from the Hungarian State Treasury [3] [5].
  • Cross-border coordination: If your family member holds foreign nationality or owns property outside Hungary, consult a Hungarian notary regarding EU Succession Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 (including whether to add an explicit choice-of-law clause to the will) and obtain an Apostille from the Hungarian Chamber of Civil Law Notaries for powers of attorney used abroad [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Slovenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Slovenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Slovenia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Slovenia. When a death occurs in the Republic of Slovenia, medical examination, civil registration in the Central Register of Deaths, funeral or repatriation arrangements, social insurance notifications, and court-supervised probate follow a structured statutory sequence. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death and Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
Under the Slovenian Rules on the Conditions and Manner of Performing the Coroner Service (Pravilnik o pogojih in načinu opravljanja mrliško pregledne službe), every death in Slovenia must be medically verified before the deceased can be transferred for burial or cremation [1][4]:

  • Death in a hospital or residential care institution: When your family member dies in a hospital (such as University Medical Centre Ljubljana or University Medical Centre Maribor) or a nursing home, the attending institutional physician performs the post-mortem examination and issues the official Death Notification and Certificate on the Cause of Death (Prijava smrti in potrdilo o vzroku smrti) [1]. Where the clinical cause of death is clear, the hospital pathology department releases the body directly to your chosen funeral provider; if the cause of death is medically unclear, a clinical autopsy may be ordered [1].
  • Expected natural death at home: Do not move the body. Contact the local community health centre (zdravstveni dom) or the regional emergency medical dispatch on 112 to summon the on-call municipal coroner physician (mrliški preglednik) [1]. Have the deceased person's national identity card (osebna izkaznica) or passport, health insurance card issued by the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia (Zavod za zdravstveno zavarovanje Slovenije - ZZZS), and medical records ready [1][4]. After examining the deceased at the place of death, the coroner physician issues the Certificate of Accomplished Coroner Examination (Potrdilo o opravljenem mrliškem pregledu), which authorizes a funeral company to transport the deceased to a mortuary, and transmits the official death report to the civil registry [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death: Call the police on 113 or emergency services on 112 immediately [1]. If the coroner physician suspects a violent, accidental, or unexplained cause of death, the police and the investigating judge (preiskovalni sodnik) of the competent District Court (okrožno sodišče) take jurisdiction and order a forensic autopsy (sodna obdukcija) at the Institute of Forensic Medicine (Inštitut za sodno medicino) before issuing clearance for burial or cremation [1][6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Administrative Unit and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
In Slovenia, deaths are recorded in the Central Register (matični register) managed by the local Administrative Units (upravne enote) and accessible via the eUprava State Portal of the Republic of Slovenia [1]:

  • Statutory deadline and filing procedure: Under the Civil Register Act (Zakon o matičnem registru), a death must be reported to the Administrative Unit (upravna enota) covering the municipality where the death occurred within 2 days of the death (or within 2 days of finding the body) [1]. In practice, the hospital, the coroner physician (mrliški preglednik), or your authorized funeral provider submits the medical death notification (Prijava smrti) directly to the competent Administrative Unit [1].
  • Obtaining extracts from the Register of Deaths: Once the death is entered in the matični register, any administrative unit in Slovenia can issue an official Extract from the Central Register of Deaths (Izpisek iz matičnega registra o smrti) [1]. Family members can request the extract in person at any upravna enota or online using a digital identity (such as SI-PASS or eOsebna) through the eUprava State Portal of the Republic of Slovenia [1].
  • Multilingual CIEC extracts and Apostille for cross-border use: If your family member held foreign nationality or left assets abroad, request an international multilingual death certificate issued on the Vienna Convention (CIEC) form (izpisek na mednarodnem obrazcu), which is accepted without translation across signatory states, or an EU Multilingual Standard Form under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 [1]. Where a non-EU country requires legalization under the 1961 Hague Convention, an Apostille stamp on civil registry extracts is issued by the District Court (okrožno sodišče) in Slovenia [1][6].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation through a Licensed Funeral Provider
steps.html:
Under the Funeral and Cemetery Services Act (Zakon o pogrebni in pokopališki dejavnosti), funeral transport and preparations must be carried out by a licensed funeral operator (izvajalec pogrebne dejavnosti), including the 24-hour mandatory municipal transport service (24-urna dežurna služba) where required [1][3]:

  • Domestic burial or cremation in Slovenia: Present the coroner's certificate (Potrdilo o opravljenem mrliškem pregledu), the deceased's identity document, and the Izpisek iz matičnega registra o smrti to your selected funeral company (such as Žale Javno podjetje in Ljubljana, Pogrebno podjetje Maribor, or a licensed regional provider listed with the Chamber of Craft and Small Business of Slovenia) [1]. For cremation (upepelitev), the coroner physician must explicitly confirm on the examination form that there are no medical or forensic impediments to cremation [1].
  • International repatriation of human remains or ashes: Slovenia is a party to the 1937 Berlin Arrangement and the 1973 Council of Europe Strasbourg Agreement on the Transfer of Corpses. To repatriate a body abroad, the funeral provider arranges sanitary preparation and placement in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, obtains the international laissez-passer for a corpse (posmrtni potni list) from the competent Slovenian authority together with hygienic-epidemiological clearance, and coordinates with the foreign embassy or consulate in Ljubljana [1]. Transporting cremated ashes (žara s pepelom) abroad requires the official death extract, the crematorium certificate of cremation, and a sealed urn accompanied by funeral transit documentation [1].

steps.title: Notify ZPIZ, ZZZS, FURS, and Banks, and Claim Survivor or Funeral Benefits
steps.html:
Once the death is recorded in the Central Population Register (Centralni register prebivalstva - CRP), several Slovenian state databases update automatically, but family members must still submit specific benefit claims and close private contracts [1][2][4]:

  • Compulsory health insurance and funeral assistance: Recording the death automatically terminates compulsory health insurance with the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia (Zavod za zdravstveno zavarovanje Slovenije - ZZZS) [4]. If the deceased met low-income social assistance thresholds under the Financial Social Assistance Act, family members who paid for the funeral may apply at the local Centre for Social Work (Center za socialno delo - CSD) for extraordinary financial social assistance in the form of a funeral grant (pogrebnina) and a one-off post-death family allowance (posmrtnina) within the statutory deadline [1][4].
  • Pensions and survivor benefits (vdovska ali družinska pokojnina): Notify the Pension and Disability Insurance Institute of Slovenia (Zavod za pokojninsko in invalidsko zavarovanje Slovenije - ZPIZ) to stop ongoing old-age or disability pension payments and claim any unpaid accrued pension up to the date of death [2][3]. Surviving spouses, registered or long-term cohabiting partners (zunajzakonski partnerji), and dependent children (generally up to age 15, or up to age 26 if in full-time education) can apply to the Pension and Disability Insurance Institute of Slovenia (in person at a ZPIZ regional unit or online via the eUprava State Portal of the Republic of Slovenia) for a widow/widower's pension (vdovska pokojnina) or family survivor's pension (družinska pokojnina) [2][3].
  • Banking, identity documents, and tax authorities: Submit the Izpisek iz matičnega registra o smrti to all Slovenian banks where the deceased held accounts; upon notification, banks freeze individual accounts and revoke powers of attorney (which terminate at death under Slovenian law unless specific contractual exceptions apply) until the final probate order is issued [5][6]. Surrender the deceased's passport and identity card (osebna izkaznica) to the Administrative Unit (upravna enota) for cancellation, and verify tax obligations with the Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia (Finančna uprava Republike Slovenije - FURS) [1].

steps.title: Complete Probate Proceedings (*Zapuščinski postopek*) and Inheritance Tax Filings
steps.html:
Under the Slovenian Inheritance Act (Zakon o dedovanju), succession is conducted through a mandatory judicial probate procedure (zapuščinski postopek) managed by the Courts of the Republic of Slovenia [5][6]:

  • Death record (smrtovnica) and ex officio court initiation: After registering the death, the registrar at the Administrative Unit compiles the official death record (smrtovnica) containing data on the deceased, known family members, wills, and approximate estate assets, and sends it ex officio within 30 days to the competent Local Court (okrajno sodišče) of the deceased's last permanent or temporary residence in Slovenia [1][6].
  • Probate hearing (zapuščinska obravnava) and Decree of Distribution (sklep o dedovanju): The Local Court (okrajno sodišče) schedules a probate hearing (zapuščinska obravnava), checks the Central Register of Wills (Centralni register oporok) maintained by the Chamber of Notaries of Slovenia (Notarska zbornica Slovenije), determines the rightful heirs under testate or statutory succession (protecting compulsory shares - nujni delež - for close relatives), and issues the formal Decree of Inheritance (sklep o dedovanju) [5][6]. Once the sklep o dedovanju becomes final (pravnomočen), the court automatically orders the Land Register (zemljiška knjiga) to transfer real estate ownership, and heirs present the final decree to banks to release funds [6].
  • Inheritance tax (davek na dediščine in darila) and cross-border estates: Under the Inheritance and Gift Taxation Act, heirs in the first hereditary order (spouses, cohabiting partners, children, and adopted children/grandchildren) are 100% exempt from Slovenian inheritance tax [6]. Other heirs are assessed by FURS based on the final court decree [6]. If assets or heirs are located in another EU Member State, the Slovenian Local Court can issue a European Certificate of Succession (Evropsko potrdilo o dedovanju) under Regulation (EU) No 650/2012, and parties may consult a notary via the Chamber of Notaries of Slovenia for estate settlement agreements [5][6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Slovenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Slovenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Slovenia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand how demanding it is when a family member in Slovenia is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness. Taking structured medical, legal, and financial steps while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity (poslovna sposobnost) ensures that their treatment preferences are respected and that family representatives can manage care, benefits, and property without requiring court-appointed guardianship. Below, we set out the five main official steps to complete in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and ZZZS Health Coverage
steps.html:
In the Republic of Slovenia, palliative care (paliativna oskrba) is recognized as a fundamental patient right and is integrated across primary, secondary, and tertiary public healthcare under the oversight of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Slovenia (Ministrstvo za zdravje) and funded through compulsory health insurance administered by the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia (Zavod za zdravstveno zavarovanje Slovenije - ZZZS) [1][2][3]:

  • Primary-level home care and community nursing (patronažna služba): Ask the ill person's chosen personal physician (izbrani osebni zdravnik) at the local community health centre (zdravstveni dom) to establish a structured palliative care plan, prescribe pain and symptom-relief medications, and issue a work order (delovni nalog) for the community nursing service (patronažna zdravstvena nega) to conduct regular home visits [1][3].
  • Mobile palliative teams and specialized hospital units: For complex symptom management, the personal physician or treating specialist can refer your family member to a regional hospital palliative team or a mobile palliative unit (mobilni paliativni tim) - such as those operating at the Institute of Oncology Ljubljana (Onkološki inštitut Ljubljana), University Medical Centre Ljubljana, University Medical Centre Maribor, or regional general hospitals - which coordinate home visits and 24-hour specialist consultation [1][2].
  • Medical technical aids and hospice care: Through the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia, the personal physician can prescribe covered medical and orthopedic aids (medicinski pripomočki, such as adjustable hospital beds, anti-decubitus mattresses, oxygen concentrators, and wheelchairs) on a ZZZS order form [3]. Families seeking inpatient or home support may also contact the Slovenian Hospice Society (Slovensko društvo Hospic / Hiša Ljubhospic), which provides multidisciplinary end-of-life care [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives (*Vnaprej izražena volja*) and Appoint a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
The Slovenian Patient Rights Act (Zakon o pacientovih pravicah - ZPacP), overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Slovenia, establishes a clear statutory procedure for advance medical directives and healthcare representation while a patient has full decision-making capacity (aged 18 or over and capable of discernment) [1][2]:

  • Appointing the patient's healthcare representative (pacientov zdravstveni pooblaščenec): Under the Patient Rights Act, your family member can execute a written power of attorney designating a trusted adult as their pacientov zdravstveni pooblaščenec to access medical records and give or withhold consent to medical procedures if the patient loses capacity to decide [1][3]. The signature on the authorization must be officially certified by a Slovenian Administrative Unit (upravna enota) or a notary from the Chamber of Notaries of Slovenia (Notarska zbornica Slovenije), and the appointment is recorded on the central ZZZS health insurance system via the health card [3][5].
  • Advance expression of medical will (vnaprej izražena volja): Under Article 34 of the Patient Rights Act, a patient suffering from a condition expected to lead to a terminal state without decision-making capacity can formally record an advance directive refusing life-prolonging medical procedures [1][2]. To be legally valid under ZPacP, the patient must first receive explanations from both their personal physician (izbrani osebni zdravnik) and the regional Representative of Patients' Rights (zastopnik pacientovih pravic), sign the prescribed statutory form before a panel, and have the directive recorded in the central health insurance registry maintained by the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia [1][3].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney (*Pooblastilo*) and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
In Slovenia, spouses and close relatives do not automatically have legal authority to manage another adult's real estate, contracts, or bank accounts if that person loses capacity, and a general power of attorney normally requires full legal capacity (poslovna sposobnost) when signed [5][6]:

  • Notarial power of attorney (notarsko pooblastilo): While your family member retains full legal capacity, arrange an appointment with a Slovenian civil-law notary through the Chamber of Notaries of Slovenia (Notaries can conduct home or hospital visits if the ill person cannot travel) [5]. Executing a notarial deed or notarially certified power of attorney ensures legal representation before public authorities, tax offices, and property registries; for selling, mortgaging, or transferring real estate registered in the Land Register (zemljiška knjiga), a specific land-registry-compliant authorization with a notarized signature is strictly required [5].
  • Dedicated bank account mandates: Slovenian commercial banks normally require account holders to sign the bank's own internal power-of-attorney card (pooblastilo za razpolaganje s transakcijskim računom) in person or via a notarized mandate specifying the exact IBAN and permitted transactions [5]. Clarify with the bank whether the authorization terminates upon death, as standard mandates cease to be valid once the account holder dies and the estate enters probate [5][6].
  • Preventing court-ordered adult guardianship (postavitev odrasle osebe pod skrbništvo): Putting comprehensive notarial and banking powers of attorney in place early avoids the need for a lengthy non-contentious court proceeding (nepravdni postopek) before the Local Court (okrajno sodišče) to appoint a legal guardian (skrbnik) if cognitive capacity declines [5].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Attendance, Long-Term Care, and Caregiver Benefits
steps.html:
Slovenia provides statutory sickness, disability, care, and family support benefits through the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia, the Pension and Disability Insurance Institute of Slovenia (Zavod za pokojninsko in invalidsko zavarovanje Slovenije - ZPIZ), and regional Centres for Social Work (Centri za socialno delo - CSD) [3][4]:

  • Temporary sickness compensation (nadomestilo plače med začasno zadržanostjo od dela) and caregiver leave: If the ill person is employed or self-employed, their personal physician issues an electronic certificate of temporary incapacity for work (eBOL), with wage compensation funded by the employer initially and subsequently by the Health Insurance Institute of Slovenia [3]. Employed close family members (such as a spouse, cohabiting partner, child, or parent) can also apply for statutory leave and wage compensation to care for an acutely ill family member (nega družinskega člana) or carer's leave under the Employment Relationships Act (Zakon o delovnih razmerjih - ZDR-1) [3].
  • Disability pension (invalidska pokojnina) and Assistance and Attendance Allowance (dodatek za pomoč in postrežbo): Where an advanced illness causes permanent disability or dependence on daily assistance in performing basic life needs, submit an application with medical documentation to the Pension and Disability Insurance Institute of Slovenia (in person at a ZPIZ unit or online via the eUprava State Portal of the Republic of Slovenia) for evaluation by the ZPIZ Disability Commission (invalidska komisija) [4][6]. Pensioners and eligible insured residents who require permanent third-party care for all or most basic life functions can claim the monthly Assistance and Attendance Allowance (dodatek za pomoč in postrežbo), and families may also consult the local Centre for Social Work (Center za socialno delo) regarding a family assistant (družinski pomočnik) or rights under the Long-Term Care Act (Zakon o dolgotrajni oskrbi) [3][4].

steps.title: Review the Will (*Oporoka*), Lifetime Property Contracts, and Civil Records
steps.html:
Organizing succession and property documentation while your family member has testamentary capacity (oporočna sposobnost) simplifies future probate (zapuščinski postopek) in Slovenia [5][6]:

  • Drafting a will (oporoka) and registration in the Central Register of Wills: Under the Slovenian Inheritance Act (Zakon o dedovanju), a testator can execute a holographic will (lastnoročna oporoka, entirely handwritten and signed by the testator), a written will before two witnesses (pisna oporoka pred pričami), a court will, or a notarial will (notarska oporoka) drafted by a notary of the Chamber of Notaries of Slovenia [5]. Having the will drawn up by or deposited with a notary ensures it is immediately recorded in the Central Register of Wills (Centralni register oporok), so the probate court automatically locates it [5]. Keep in mind Slovenian rules on compulsory shares (nujni delež) for descendants and spouses/partners [5].
  • Lifetime property agreements and Land Register (zemljiška knjiga) verification: Where appropriate, families may consult a notary of the Chamber of Notaries of Slovenia regarding lifetime contracts recognized under Slovenian law - such as a handover and distribution contract with descendants (izročilna pogodba), a maintenance contract (pogodba o preužitku), or a lifetime support contract (pogodba o dosmrtnem preživljanju) - which must be executed in strict notarial form [5]. Verify that all real estate ownership is accurately recorded in the electronic Land Register (zemljiška knjiga), check life insurance beneficiary clauses, and obtain up-to-date civil status extracts via the eUprava State Portal of the Republic of Slovenia (adding EU Regulation 650/2012 choice-of-law clauses if the person holds foreign nationality or owns property abroad) [5][6].

closingQuestion: In which Slovenian municipality is your family member receiving medical care, and are they currently employed or receiving a pension from the Pension and Disability Insurance Institute of Slovenia so we can outline the exact care and benefit applications?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Croatia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Croatia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Croatia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Croatia. When someone dies in the Republic of Croatia, medical examination by an authorized physician or coroner, registration in the Register of Deaths (matica umrlih), funeral or repatriation arrangements, social insurance updates, and notarial or court probate follow specific statutory rules. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death (*Potvrda o smrti*) and Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
Under the Croatian Healthcare Act (Zakon o zdravstvenoj zaštiti) and the Rules on Examining the Time and Cause of Death, every death in Croatia must be verified by an authorized physician or county coroner (mrtvozornik) before a funeral provider can transport the deceased [1]:

  • Death in a hospital, clinic, or social welfare institution: When a death occurs in a hospital or clinical hospital centre (klinički bolnički centar - KBC, such as KBC Zagreb, KBC Split, KBC Rijeka, or KBC Osijek), the attending physician examines the deceased, establishes the clinical cause of death, and issues the official Death Certificate (Potvrda o smrti) and the Permit for Burial or Cremation (Dozvola za ukop ili kremiranje) [1]. The hospital notifies the family and transfers the deceased to the hospital pathology department until your chosen funeral company collects the body [1].
  • Expected natural death at home: Do not move the body. Call the unified European emergency number 112 or emergency medical services (Hitna medicinska služba) on 194 to request the attendance of the authorized municipal or county coroner (mrtvozornik) [1]. Prepare your family member's Croatian identity card (osobna iskaznica) or passport, Personal Identification Number (Osobni identifikacijski broj - OIB), health insurance card issued by the Croatian Health Insurance Fund (Hrvatski zavod za zdravstveno osiguranje - HZZO), and medical discharge summaries [1][6]. After examining the deceased at the place of death, the mrtvozornik issues the Potvrda o smrti and the burial or cremation permit (Dozvola za ukop) [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death: Call the police on 192 (or 112) immediately [1]. Where the cause of death is unknown, sudden, or raises suspicion of a violent or accidental cause, the police and the State Attorney's Office (Državno odvjetništvo) conduct an investigation and order a mandatory medico-legal autopsy (sudskomedicinska obdukcija) at the competent Institute of Forensic Medicine and Criminology before issuing clearance for burial or cremation [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Office (*Matični ured*) and Obtain Official Extracts
steps.html:
In Croatia, civil registration of deaths is governed by the State Registries Act (Zakon o državnim maticama) and administered by the local Civil Registry Offices (matični uredi) integrated with the Central State Portal e-Citizens (Središnji državni portal e-Građani) [1]:

  • 3-day statutory deadline: A death must be reported to the Civil Registry Office (matični ured) responsible for the municipality or city where the death occurred (or where the body was found) within 3 days of the date of death (or finding of the body) [1]. When a person dies in a healthcare facility, the hospital reports the death electronically via the e-Prijava smrti system; when death occurs at home, family members or an authorized funeral company submit the Potvrda o smrti and the deceased's identity documents to the matični ured [1].
  • Official Death Certificate (Smrtni list) and Extract (Izvadak iz matice umrlih): Upon recording the entry in the Register of Deaths (matica umrlih), the registrar issues the official Death Certificate (Smrtni list) and the Extract from the Register of Deaths (Izvadak iz matice umrlih) [1]. Certified electronic extracts can also be downloaded with a verifiable electronic seal via the e-Matice service on the Central State Portal e-Citizens [1].
  • Multilingual extracts and Apostille for cross-border use: If your family member was a foreign national or left assets outside Croatia, ask the matični ured for an international multilingual extract issued under the 1976 Vienna CIEC Convention or an EU Multilingual Standard Form under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 [1]. Where a non-EU jurisdiction requires legalization under the 1961 Hague Convention, any Municipal Court (općinski sud) in Croatia can affix an Apostille to civil registry certificates [1][4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation through a Licensed Funeral Provider
steps.html:
Under the Croatian Funeral Services Act (Zakon o pogrebničkoj djelatnosti) and the Cemeteries Act (Zakon o grobljima), transport and preparation of the deceased must be performed by a licensed funeral company (ovlašteni pogrebnik) or municipal cemetery utility [1]:

  • Domestic burial or cremation in Croatia: Provide the coroner's Dozvola za ukop ili kremiranje and the Potvrda o smrti to a licensed funeral director (such as Gradska groblja Zagreb, Lovrinac in Split, KD Kozala in Rijeka, or an accredited private funeral provider registered with the Croatian Chamber of Trades and Crafts - Hrvatska obrtnička komora) [1]. Under Croatian sanitary rules, burial or cremation normally takes place between 24 and 48 hours after death unless preserved in a regulated mortuary facility (mrtvačnica) [1].
  • International repatriation of human remains or ashes: To transport a deceased person across international borders from Croatia, the licensed funeral provider prepares the body in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin, obtains the sanitary permit for the transport of human remains (sprovodnica za prijenos umrle osobe) from the competent county Department of Sanitary Inspection of the State Inspectorate (Državni inspektorat - sanitarna inspekcija), and coordinates any required consular laissez-passer with the foreign embassy in Zagreb [1]. Transporting an urn containing cremated ashes (urna s pepelom) requires the Izvadak iz matice umrlih, the official crematorium certificate, and a sealed urn [1].

steps.title: Notify HZMO, HZZO, the Tax Administration, and Banks, and Claim Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
Once the death is recorded in the matica umrlih, the Civil Registry updates Croatia's OIB register and central population records, but survivors must actively apply for pension benefits and notify financial institutions [1][2][3][6]:

  • Health insurance and funeral cost entitlements: Registration in the matica umrlih automatically terminates compulsory health insurance with the Croatian Health Insurance Fund (Hrvatski zavod za zdravstveno osiguranje - HZZO) [6]. Where the deceased had no income or assets and falls within social welfare categories, eligible family members may inquire at the local regional office of the Croatian Institute for Social Work (Hrvatski zavod za socijalni rad) regarding coverage of basic funeral expenses, or at the Ministry of Croatian Veterans (Ministarstvo hrvatskih branitelja) if the deceased held Croatian Homeland War veteran status [1].
  • Stopping pension payments and claiming the Survivors' Pension (obiteljska mirovina): Notify the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (Hrvatski zavod za mirovinsko osiguranje - HZMO) to stop ongoing pension disbursements and claim any unpaid accrued pension up to the date of death [2][3]. Under the Pension Insurance Act (Zakon o mirovinskom osiguranju), surviving spouses, extramarital or life partners, divorced spouses with maintenance rights, and dependent children (up to age 15, or up to age 26 while in regular education) can submit a claim to the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (at a regional HZMO office or online via e-Usluge HZMO on the Central State Portal e-Citizens) for a Survivors' Pension (obiteljska mirovina) [2][3]. Surviving spouses of retirement age who already receive their own old-age pension may qualify to receive a percentage (27%) of the deceased spouse's pension alongside their personal pension [2].
  • Banks, identity cards, and the Tax Administration (Porezna uprava): Present the Smrtni list or Izvadak iz matice umrlih to all Croatian banks where your family member held accounts; banks will freeze sole accounts and block cards and powers of attorney until a final Decree of Inheritance is presented [1][4]. Return the deceased's identity card (osobna iskaznica), passport, and driver's licence to the competent Police Administration (policijska uprava / policijska postaja) of the Ministry of the Interior (MUP) for cancellation, and check any pending tax obligations with the Croatian Tax Administration (Porezna uprava) [1].

steps.title: Complete Probate Proceedings (*Ostavinski postupak*) Before a Public Notary or Court
steps.html:
Under the Croatian Inheritance Act (Zakon o nasljeđivanju), estate administration is conducted through an official probate proceeding (ostavinski postupak) initiated ex officio [1][4][5]:

  • Preparation of the Death Record (smrtovnica) and court referral: Within 30 days of registering the death, the civil registrar (matičar) prepares the official Death Record (smrtovnica) listing the deceased's personal data, known heirs, real estate, bank accounts, and any known will, and forwards it electronically to the competent Municipal Court (općinski sud) of the deceased's last domicile in Croatia [1][4].
  • Probate hearing before a Public Notary (javni bilježnik) as court commissioner: In Croatia, the Municipal Court entrusts the conduct of uncontested probate proceedings to a local Public Notary (javni bilježnik) registered with the Croatian Notaries Chamber (Hrvatska javnobilježnička komora - HJK), acting as a court commissioner (povjerenik suda) [4][5]. The notary checks the Croatian Register of Wills (Hrvatski upisnik oporuka) maintained by the Croatian Notaries Chamber, summons the heirs to the probate hearing (ostavinska rasprava), records declarations accepting or renouncing the inheritance (nasljednička izjava), and issues the Decree of Inheritance (Rješenje o nasljeđivanju) [4][5].
  • Land Registry (zemljišne knjige), inheritance tax, and cross-border assets: Once the Rješenje o nasljeđivanju becomes final and binding (pravomoćno), the notary or court sends it ex officio to the Land Registry Department (zemljišnoknjižni odjel - gruntovnica) to transfer real estate ownership and to the Tax Administration (Porezna uprava) [4][5]. Under Croatian tax law, spouses, extramarital/life partners, and lineal descendants (children and grandchildren) are exempt from inheritance tax (porez na nasljedstva i darove), whereas other heirs pay a 4% tax on movable assets and cash exceeding the statutory threshold (or 3% real estate transfer tax on inherited real property) [1][4]. Where assets or heirs are located in another EU Member State, the Croatian court or notary can issue a European Certificate of Succession (Europska potvrda o nasljeđivanju) under Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 [4][5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Croatia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Croatia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Croatia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand how challenging it is when a family member in Croatia is facing an advanced or life-limiting illness. Putting medical care coordination, healthcare representation, notarial powers of attorney, social security benefits, and testamentary documents in order while your family member retains full legal and mental decision-making capacity (poslovna sposobnost) protects their autonomy and prevents administrative delays. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care (*Palijativna skrb*), Home Nursing, and HZZO Coverage
steps.html:
In the Republic of Croatia, palliative care is organized as a public health service under the Healthcare Act (Zakon o zdravstvenoj zaštiti) overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Croatia (Ministarstvo zdravstva) and is covered in full under compulsory health insurance administered by the Croatian Health Insurance Fund (Hrvatski zavod za zdravstveno osiguranje - HZZO) [1][2]:

  • Establishing palliative status (ICD-10 code Z51.5) and county coordinator registration: Ask the ill person's chosen family medicine doctor (izabrani liječnik obiteljske medicine) or hospital specialist to record the medical need for palliative care (diagnosis code MKB Z51.5) and refer the patient to the Centre for Coordination of Palliative Care (Centar za koordinaciju palijativne skrbi) at the county health centre (dom zdravlja) [1][2].
  • Mobile palliative teams (mobilni palijativni timovi) and home healthcare (zdravstvena njega u kući): Once registered with the county palliative coordinator, a multidisciplinary mobile palliative team (mobilni palijativni tim - MPT) coordinates specialist home visits, pain control, and symptom management alongside the community health nurse (patronažna sestra) and HZZO-contracted home nursing care (zdravstvena njega u kući bolesnika) prescribed by the family doctor [1][2].
  • Orthopedic and medical aids, transport, and inpatient hospice beds: Through the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, the family doctor or specialist issues electronic prescriptions (e-doznaka) for orthopedic and medical aids (ortopedska i druga pomagala) and free county medical equipment lending libraries (posudionica medicinskih pomagala for hospital beds, anti-decubitus mattresses, and oxygen concentrators), as well as non-emergency medical transport (sanitetski prijevoz) and referrals to hospital palliative beds or accredited hospices (such as the Marija Krucifiksa Kozulić Hospice in Rijeka or county palliative wards) [1][2].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Appoint a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
Patient autonomy, informed consent, and representation in medical decision-making in Croatia are governed by the Act on the Protection of Patients' Rights (Zakon o zaštiti prava pacijenata) and the Family Act (Obiteljski zakon) [1][4]:

  • Right to accept or refuse medical procedures: Under the Act on the Protection of Patients' Rights overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Croatia, every patient with decision-making capacity has the right to full medical information and the right to accept or refuse a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure (except where refusal would endanger the lives or health of others) by signing a formal written statement in the medical record [1].
  • Anticipated orders (anticipirana naredba) and healthcare proxy in notarial form: Under the Croatian Family Act (Obiteljski zakon), an adult who currently possesses full legal capacity (poslovna sposobnost) can execute an anticipated order (anticipirana naredba) in the form of a notarial act (javnobilježnički akt) before a Public Notary of the Croatian Notaries Chamber (Hrvatska javnobilježnička komora - HJK) [4]. Through this instrument, your family member can designate a trusted person to act as their representative or guardian for personal and healthcare decisions and express binding preferences regarding medical procedures and care arrangements in the event they later lose capacity to give informed consent [1][4].
  • Delivering copies to the clinical team: Provide certified copies of the notarial deed and written treatment preferences to the chosen family medicine physician (izabrani liječnik obiteljske medicine), the county palliative care coordinator, and the treating hospital department so they are logged in the patient's central electronic health record (e-Karton) [1][2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney (*Punomoć*) and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
Under the Croatian Obligations Act (Zakon o obveznim odnosima), a family member cannot legally manage another adult's property, official filings, or bank accounts without an explicit mandate, and a power of attorney can only be granted while the principal has full legal capacity [4]:

  • General or special notarial power of attorney (javnobilježnička punomoć): Arrange for your family member to execute a notarized power of attorney (ovjera potpisa na punomoći) or a solemnized notarial act (javnobilježnički akt) before a Public Notary registered with the Croatian Notaries Chamber [4]. If the ill person is bedridden at home or hospitalized, Croatian public notaries are legally authorized to conduct official visits outside their office (izlazak javnog bilježnika na teren) to verify identity and mental capacity and execute the mandate at the bedside [4]. For selling, gifting, or encumbering real estate in Croatia, the power of attorney must be specific (specijalna punomoć) and explicitly identify the cadastral plot and land registry entry [4].
  • Bank account mandates (punomoć po računu): Croatian banks generally require the account holder to grant a bank-specific mandate (punomoć za raspolaganje sredstvima po računu) either at a branch or via a special notarized power of attorney containing the exact IBAN and banking powers required by the bank's compliance department [4]. Note that under Croatian law, powers of attorney over bank accounts terminate automatically at the moment of the account holder's death [4][5].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Disability, Attendance Allowance, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
Croatia provides financial and care entitlements for seriously ill residents and their family caregivers through the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (Hrvatski zavod za mirovinsko osiguranje - HZMO), and the Croatian Institute for Social Work (Hrvatski zavod za socijalni rad - HZSR) [2][3][6]:

  • Temporary incapacity for work (privremena nesposobnost za rad) and family caregiver leave: If the ill person is employed, their family doctor issues medical reports (Izvješće o privremenoj nesposobnosti za rad) for paid sick leave (bolovanje), funded by the employer for the first 42 days and thereafter by the Croatian Health Insurance Fund (with 100% compensation up to the statutory cap for specific categories or after 18 months of uninterrupted oncology/serious illness treatment rules) [2]. Employed spouses or close family members can also obtain short-term paid HZZO leave to care for an acutely ill family member (njega člana obitelji) or unpaid carer's leave under the Labour Act (Zakon o radu) [2].
  • Disability pension (invalidska mirovina) and Physical Impairment Allowance: Where an advanced illness causes partial or total loss of working capacity (djelomični ili potpuni gubitak radne sposobnosti), the family doctor submits medical documentation for an expert evaluation by the Institute for Expert Evaluation, Professional Rehabilitation and Employment of Persons with Disabilities (ZOSI) through a claim filed with the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (in person or online via the Central State Portal e-Citizens) [3][6].
  • Inclusive Allowance (inkluzivni dodatak) and Parent/Carer status: Under the Inclusive Allowance Act (Zakon o inkluzivnom dodatku, which consolidated the former personal disability allowance and assistance and care allowance - doplatak za pomoć i njegu), seriously ill persons with severe functional impairments can apply at the regional office of the Croatian Institute for Social Work (Hrvatski zavod za socijalni rad) for a monthly tax-free cash benefit to cover care and disability costs, as well as social services such as home assistance (pomoć u kući) [1][3].

steps.title: Organize the Will (*Oporuka*), Croatian Register of Wills, and Property Records
steps.html:
Reviewing succession and property documentation while your family member retains testamentary capacity (oporučna sposobnost) ensures a smooth future probate process (ostavinski postupak) [4][5][6]:

  • Executing a valid will (oporuka) and registering it in the Croatian Register of Wills: Under the Croatian Inheritance Act (Zakon o nasljeđivanju), a testator can make a private holographic will (vlastoručna oporuka, entirely handwritten and signed personally), a written will before two simultaneous witnesses (pisana oporuka pred svjedocima), or a public will (javna oporuka) drafted by a Public Notary or Municipal Court judge [4][5]. Any will can be deposited with a Public Notary and recorded in the Croatian Register of Wills (Hrvatski upisnik oporuka) maintained by the Croatian Notaries Chamber, ensuring that the probate commissioner automatically locates it [4][5]. Bear in mind statutory compulsory share rules (nužni dio) for descendants and spouses/partners, as well as lifetime maintenance contracts (ugovor o doživotnom uzdržavanju or ugovor o dosmrtnom uzdržavanju), which must be solemnized by a notary or judge [4][5].
  • Checking Land Registry (zemljišne knjige) and civil status records via e-Citizens: Use the Joint Information System of Land Books and Cadastre (Zajednički informacijski sustav zemljišnih knjiga i katastra - Uređena zemlja) and the Central State Portal e-Citizens to verify that real estate ownership (vlasnički list) and civil registry records (e-Matice) are accurate and free of unrecorded transfers [5][6]. If your family member holds foreign citizenship or owns assets in another EU country, consult a notary regarding a choice-of-law clause under the EU Succession Regulation (Regulation (EU) No 650/2012) [4][5].
