title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bulgaria: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bulgaria: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Bulgaria: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Bulgaria. When a death occurs in the Republic of Bulgaria, medical certification, civil registration within the statutory 48-hour deadline, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social insurance filings, and succession procedures follow strict statutory rules under the Civil Registration Act (Закон за гражданската регистрация) and the Inheritance Act (Закон за наследството). Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Notice of Death (*Съобщение за смърт*)
steps.html:
Under the Bulgarian Civil Registration Act and regulations overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria (Министерство на здравеопазването), a physician must verify the death and issue the official Medical Notice of Death (Съобщение за смърт) before civil registration or burial can take place [1][4]:

  • Death in a hospital or inpatient medical facility: When a death occurs in a hospital, the attending physician or head of the ward verifies the death, completes the Съобщение за смърт, and transfers the body to the hospital pathology department [1][4]. If the clinical diagnosis is established and the family requests release without a clinical autopsy, the hospital director may approve an autopsy waiver request (молба за освобождаване от аутопсия) unless forensic or epidemiological grounds require an examination [4].
  • Expected natural death at home: Do not move the body. Contact the deceased person's general practitioner (общопрактикуващ лекар / личен лекар), an out-of-hours medical centre (неотложен кабинет), or emergency medical services (Спешна медицинска помощ) on 112 [1][4]. Have your family member's Bulgarian identity card (лична карта) with their Uniform Civil Number (Единен граждански номер - EGN) or foreign passport and medical records ready [1]. After examining the body, the physician issues the Съобщение за смърт [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained death: Call 112 immediately so the police (Министерство на вътрешните работи - MVR) and forensic medical authorities can attend [1][4]. Where a violent, accidental, or unexplained cause of death is suspected, an investigating authority orders a mandatory forensic autopsy (съдебномедицинска експертиза) at a hospital Department of Forensic Medicine (Съдебна медицина), and the forensic pathologist issues the Съобщение за смърт and prosecutor clearance required for burial or cremation [1][4].

steps.title: Register the Death Within 48 Hours and Obtain the Official Death Certificate (*Препис-извлечение от акт за смърт*)
steps.html:
In Bulgaria, civil registration of deaths is carried out by the municipal civil status registrar (длъжностно лице по гражданското състояние) at the municipality (община), district (район in Sofia, Plovdiv, and Varna), or mayoralty (кметство) where the death occurred, linked to the National Database "Population" (Национална база данни „Население“ - GRAO) and the Unified Portal for Electronic Administrative Services (Единен портал за достъп до електронни административни услуги - eGov.bg) [1]:

  • Strict 48-hour statutory deadline: Under Articles 54 to 61 of the Civil Registration Act (Закон за гражданската регистрация), the Act of Death (Акт за смърт) must be drawn up within 48 hours of the time of death (or within 48 hours of the forensic release if a medico-legal autopsy is performed) [1]. Present the Съобщение за смърт and the deceased's identity document to the municipal civil registry desk; the registrar cancels the identity card and issues the official Death Certificate extract (Препис-извлечение от акт за смърт) free of charge on first issuance [1].
  • Certificate of Heirs (Удостоверение за наследници): Once the death is processed in the municipal GRAO system (typically within a few working days of the Акт за смърт), legal heirs can request the official Certificate of Heirs (Удостоверение за наследници) from the municipality of the deceased's last permanent address (постоянен адрес) in Bulgaria, either in person at the municipal ESGRAON/GRAO office or online via the Unified Portal for Electronic Administrative Services using a Qualified Electronic Signature (Квалифициран електронен подпис - KEP) [1].
  • Multilingual extracts and Apostille for cross-border use: If documents must be presented outside Bulgaria, request a multilingual extract from the civil status act (многоезично извлечение от акт за гражданско състояние) under the Vienna CIEC Convention or an EU Multilingual Standard Form under Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 from the municipality [1]. Where a non-EU state requires an Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention, municipal civil status documents bearing the rectangular municipal authentication stamp receive an Apostille from the Bulgarian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Министерство на външните работи - MVRnR) or via regional governors (областни администрации) according to document category [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation Within Sanitary Timeframes
steps.html:
Under the Ordinance of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria on Sanitary and Hygienic Requirements for Cemetery Parks and Burial and Cremation of Deceased Persons, specific sanitary rules and waiting windows apply [1][4]:

  • Domestic burial or cremation in Bulgaria: Burial (погребение) may take place no earlier than 24 hours after death and no later than 48 hours after death, unless the body is preserved in a refrigerated mortuary chamber (хладилна камера) [1][4]. Appoint a municipal funeral enterprise (such as Погребални услуги - София / OP Гробищни паркове in Sofia or the municipal cemetery operator) or a licensed private funeral agency (траурна агенция), presenting the Препис-извлечение от акт за смърт [1]. For cremation (кремация), the medical doctor who issued the Съобщение за смърт must issue an explicit medical declaration confirming there is no evidence of violent death and no forensic impediment to cremation, alongside written authorization from the closest legal heir [1][4].
  • International repatriation of human remains or ashes: To transport a body out of Bulgaria, the funeral agency coordinates embalming, hermetically seals the deceased inside a zinc-lined coffin certified by the Regional Health Inspectorate (Регионална здравна инспекция - RZI) under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria, obtains a mortuary transit pass (пропуск за пренасяне на тленни останки), and secures consular clearance from the destination country's embassy in Sofia [1][4]. Transporting cremated ashes in a sealed urn requires the Death Certificate, the crematorium certificate, and sealing documentation [1].

steps.title: Notify NSSI (NOI), NHIF (NZOK), NRA (NAP), and Banks, and Claim Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
Once the Акт за смърт is entered in the GRAO national database, the National Social Security Institute (Национален осигурителен институт - NSSI / NOI) and the National Health Insurance Fund (Национална здравноосигурителна каса - NHIF / NZOK) receive automated updates, but heirs must submit formal applications to claim financial entitlements [2][3][5]:

  • One-off death grant and unpaid pension from the National Social Security Institute: If the deceased was an actively insured worker or self-insured contributor under the Social Insurance Code (Кодекс за социално осигуряване), the surviving spouse, children, and parents are entitled to a statutory one-off lump-sum bereavement benefit (еднократна помощ при смърт на осигурено лице) divided equally among them [2][3]. If the deceased was receiving a pension, heirs can submit an application (in person at a regional NSSI office or online via the NSSI portal / Unified Portal for Electronic Administrative Services) accompanied by the Удостоверение за наследници to claim any unreceived pension or allowance accrued for the month of death [3].
  • Survivor's pension (наследствена пенсия) and widow/widower's supplement (добавка от пенсията на починал съпруг): Under the Social Insurance Code administered by the National Social Security Institute, surviving children (up to age 18, or up to age 26 if in full-time study or permanently incapacitated), surviving spouses (within 5 years of standard retirement age, or earlier if incapacitated), and dependent parents can claim a Survivor's Pension (наследствена пенсия) [2]. Alternatively, a surviving spouse who receives their own pension may apply to the National Social Security Institute for the statutory widow/widower's supplement (добавка по чл. 84 от КСО - 30% of the deceased spouse's pension), which cannot be combined with a survivor's pension [2]. Notably, renouncing a debt-burdened civil estate does not deprive an eligible spouse or child of their right to a survivor's pension from NSSI [2].
  • Banks, utilities, and the National Revenue Agency (Национална агенция за приходите - NAP): Present the Препис-извлечение от акт за смърт and Удостоверение за наследници to all Bulgarian banks to freeze individual accounts and ascertain balances or liabilities [1][6]. Check with the National Revenue Agency (NAP) regarding any outstanding tax or social contribution liabilities of the deceased [1].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Notarial Wills, Property Registers, and Inheritance Tax
steps.html:
Under the Bulgarian Inheritance Act (Закон за наследството), succession opens at the moment of death at the deceased's last domicile, and heirs acquire both assets and liabilities unless they formally accept under inventory or renounce [6]:

  • Checking for a will and accepting or renouncing the estate: Any interested person with a Death Certificate can request a search in the Register of Wills (Регистър на завещанията) maintained by the Notary Chamber of the Republic of Bulgaria (Нотариална камара на Република България) and the Property Register (Имотен регистър) of the Registry Agency (Агенция по вписванията) to check whether the deceased left a notarial will (нотариално завещание) or deposited a holographic will (саморъчно завещание) for safekeeping [6]. If the estate carries known or potential debts, an heir may apply within 3 months of learning of the opening of succession to the District Judge (районен съдия) of the District Court (Районен съд) to accept the inheritance under benefit of inventory (приемане на наследство по опис, limiting liability to the value of inherited assets) or to record a formal renunciation of inheritance (отказ от наследство) in the court's special register [6].
  • Real estate partition, tax declaration (данък върху наследствата), and cross-border succession: Under the Local Taxes and Fees Act (Закон за местните данъци и такси), surviving spouses and lineal heirs (children, grandchildren, and parents) are completely exempt from Bulgarian inheritance tax [1][6]. Collateral heirs and non-relatives (or heirs required by local municipal rules to update property tax accounts - партиди - for inherited real estate) must submit a declaration to the Municipal Tax Office (Местни данъци и такси) within 6 months of the death [1]. Heirs can execute a voluntary contract for the partition of inherited property (договор за доброволна делба) before a notary of the Notary Chamber of the Republic of Bulgaria, and where assets or heirs span other EU Member States, a Bulgarian District Court can issue a European Certificate of Succession (Европейско удостоверение за наследство) under Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bulgaria: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bulgaria: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Bulgaria: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand how demanding it is when a family member in Bulgaria is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness. Completing essential medical care coordination, healthcare authorization, notarial powers of attorney, disability assessments, and testamentary steps while your family member retains full legal and mental capacity (дееспособност) ensures that their wishes are respected and that family representatives can act without legal obstacles. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, NHIF Clinical Pathways, and Home Support
steps.html:
In the Republic of Bulgaria, public medical and palliative care services are regulated by the Health Act (Закон за здравето) under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria (Министерство на здравеопазването) and funded for insured persons through the National Health Insurance Fund (Национална здравноосигурителна каса - NHIF / NZOK) [1][2][3]:

  • Outpatient pain control and GP coordination: Contact the ill person's chosen general practitioner (общопрактикуващ лекар / личен лекар) and treating specialist (such as an oncologist, neurologist, or cardiologist) to establish an individualized symptom-management plan [2][3]. For severe chronic pain, the specialist and GP coordinate the issuance of electronic prescriptions (including special yellow or green prescription protocols for opioid analgesics registered in the National Health Information System - НЗИС) and home medical visits [1][2].
  • Hospital palliative care under NHIF Clinical Pathway No. 297: For patients with advanced terminal oncology conditions who have continuous health insurance rights with the National Health Insurance Fund, a specialist or oncology committee can issue a hospital referral (Направление за хоспитализация - бланка МЗ-НЗОК № 7) for inpatient palliative care under Clinical Pathway No. 297 (Клинична пътека № 297 „Палиативни грижи при онкологично болни“) at an NHIF-contracted hospital or Comprehensive Oncology Centre (Комплексен онкологичен център - KOC) [2][3].
  • Medical aids, private hospices, and municipal home care: Through the National Health Insurance Fund and the medical expertise system, eligible patients can obtain funding for medical devices, wheelchairs, and anti-decubitus aids [3]. Because NHIF inpatient palliative pathways have statutory duration limits per calendar year, families frequently combine public coverage with licensed inpatient or home hospices (хосписи) registered under the Medical Establishments Act or municipal integrated health and social care services (патронажна грижа / асистентска подкрепа) [1][2][3].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Authorize a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
In Bulgaria, patient autonomy, informed consent, and access to medical information are governed by Articles 87 to 98 of the Health Act (Закон за здравето), overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria [1][2]:

  • Right to informed consent and refusal of medical procedures: Under Article 90 of the Health Act, any legally capable adult patient has the right to refuse proposed medical procedures or continuation of non-palliative treatment (except in statutory infectious-disease or psychiatric emergencies), provided the refusal is recorded in writing with the patient's signature in the hospital or outpatient medical chart [1][2].
  • Notarized authorization for medical representation and access to the Electronic Health Record (Електронно здравно досие): Because Bulgaria does not maintain a standalone state living-will registry, the most effective way for your family member to empower a trusted relative while mentally capable is to execute a notarized power of attorney (нотариално заверено пълномощно) before a notary of the Notary Chamber of the Republic of Bulgaria (Нотариална камара на Република България) [1][5]. This instrument should explicitly authorize the representative to receive full medical information under Article 28 of the Health Act, request certified copies of medical documentation, access the patient's electronic patient file (Електронно здравно досие) via the National Health Information System (HIS.bg) or the Unified Portal for Electronic Administrative Services (eGov.bg), and communicate treatment preferences to physicians if the patient becomes unable to speak [1][5][6].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney (*Пълномощно*) and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
Under the Bulgarian Obligations and Contracts Act (Закон за задълженията и договорите) and the Notary and Notarial Activity Act, spouses and children do not have automatic legal authority to manage another adult's property or bank accounts without a formal power of attorney granted while the principal has full legal capacity (дееспособност) [5]:

  • Notarial powers of attorney and registration in the Unity Information System: Arrange for your family member to execute a general power of attorney (общо пълномощно) for administrative representation before state and municipal bodies (such as NSSI, NHIF, NRA, and municipal authorities) and, where needed, a specific power of attorney (изрично пълномощно) before a Bulgarian notary registered with the Notary Chamber of the Republic of Bulgaria [5]. If your family member cannot visit a notary office due to illness, Bulgarian notaries are legally empowered to perform bedside notarial certifications at a home or hospital within their judicial district [5]. For any disposition or management of real estate, the notary certifies both the signature and the content of the power of attorney (едновременно удостоверяване на подпис и съдържание) and registers it in the Unity Information System (Единна информационна система) of the Notary Chamber of the Republic of Bulgaria so third parties can verify its authenticity [5].
  • Explicit bank account powers of attorney: Bulgarian commercial banks strictly require either a power of attorney signed in person on the bank's own template or a notarized specific power of attorney that lists the exact bank name, IBANs, and authorized banking operations (such as cash withdrawals, wire transfers, online banking management, and card issuance) [5]. Keep in mind that under Bulgarian civil law, any power of attorney terminates automatically upon the principal's death [5].

steps.title: Activate TELK Disability Expertise, Attendance Allowance, and Caregiver Benefits
steps.html:
Bulgaria provides medical disability certification, pension supplements, and personal assistant support through the Territorial Expert Medical Commissions (Териториална експертна лекарска комисия - TELK) under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria, the National Social Security Institute (Национален осигурителен институт - NSSI / NOI), and the Agency for Social Assistance (Агенция за социално подпомагане - ASP) [1][3][4]:

  • Applying for a TELK Expert Decision (Експертно решение на ТЕЛК): Ask the ill person's general practitioner or treating specialist to issue a medical referral for TELK (медицинско направление за ТЕЛК) [1]. The patient or their authorized representative can file the application at the Regional File of Medical Expertise (Регионална картотека на медицинската експертиза - RKME) or online through the Information System for Control of Medical Expertise (ibd.mh.government.bg) overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Bulgaria [1]. Where a patient is immobile or terminally ill, TELK can assess the case on the basis of clinical medical documentation (освидетелстване по документи) without requiring physical attendance [1].
  • Disability pension, Third-Party Assistance Supplement (добавка за чужда помощ), and financial support: Once TELK issues an Expert Decision establishing 50% or more permanently reduced working capacity (трайно намалена работоспособност), submit a claim to the National Social Security Institute for a disability pension (пенсия за инвалидност) [4]. If TELK certifies over 90% disability with determined need for third-party assistance (с определена чужда помощ), the person is entitled to the monthly Third-Party Assistance Supplement (добавка за чужда помощ under Article 103 of the Social Insurance Code) from the National Social Security Institute, monthly financial support under the Persons with Disabilities Act from the Agency for Social Assistance, and municipal Personal Assistant support (Лична помощ / Асистентска подкрепа) [1][3][4].
  • Paid sick leave (болничен лист) and family caregiver leave: For employed patients or employed family members caring for an acutely ill spouse, parent, or child, the attending physician or medical consultative commission (ЛКК) issues an electronic sick-leave certificate (електронен болничен лист), which is transmitted directly to the National Social Security Institute for payment of temporary incapacity cash benefits [4].

steps.title: Organize the Will (*Завещание*), Property Records, and Civil Status Certificates
steps.html:
Under the Bulgarian Inheritance Act (Закон за наследството), reviewing testamentary and property records while your family member retains full mental capacity prevents future disputes and delays [5][6]:

  • Notarial or holographic will (нотариално или саморъчно завещание) and reserved shares: A mentally capable adult in Bulgaria can execute a notarial will (нотариално завещание, dictated directly to a notary in the presence of two witnesses) or a holographic will (саморъчно завещание, written entirely by hand, dated, and signed by the testator), which can be handed over in a sealed envelope to any notary of the Notary Chamber of the Republic of Bulgaria for official safekeeping and immediate entry in the national Register of Wills [5]. When drafting a will or lifetime property transfer (such as a contract for transfer of real estate in exchange for care and maintenance - прехвърляне на имот срещу задължение за гледане и издръжка), consult a notary regarding statutory reserved shares (запазена част от наследството) protected for children, spouses, or parents under Article 28 of the Inheritance Act [5].
  • Verifying title deeds (нотариални актове) and GRAO family records: Check that all real estate title deeds (нотариални актове) are properly recorded in the Property Register (Имотен регистър) of the Registry Agency, and obtain updated marital and birth certificates through the local municipality or the Unified Portal for Electronic Administrative Services (eGov.bg) to confirm that all family relationships in the national GRAO database are accurate [5][6]. If your family member holds foreign citizenship or owns property in another EU Member State, ask a notary about including a choice-of-law clause under Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Estonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Estonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Estonia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member in Estonia. Navigating medical, administrative, and legal formalities after a death requires completing a clear sequence of official steps across health, civil registration, social security, and notarial institutions. Below, we outline the five essential stages to manage the practical and legal requirements in Estonia.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or care facility deaths: When a person dies in an Estonian hospital or inpatient care facility, the attending physician examines the body, establishes the cause of death, and enters a digital medical death notice directly into the Health Information System [1][2].
  • Deaths at home during medical care: If your family member passes away at home during expected medical care, contact their family physician during working hours or call the emergency number 112 so an ambulance crew can formally confirm the death and guide you on issuing the medical death statement [1][3].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unattended deaths: If the death is sudden, accidental, or occurs under unclear circumstances, you must immediately notify the Police and Border Guard Board and ambulance services via 112 [1][3]. In these cases, the body is transferred to the Estonian Forensic Science Institute to determine the cause of death before any burial or cremation permit is granted [1][3].

steps.title: Complete Civil Death Registration and Obtain Certificates
steps.html:
• Automated electronic registration: Under Estonia's proactive event services framework managed through the State Portal Eesti.ee and the Ministry of the Interior, once a healthcare provider enters the digital death notice, the death is automatically registered in the Estonian Population Register without requiring an in-person visit to a vital statistics office [1][2].
  • Initial death certificate issuance: The healthcare institution that certifies the death issues the initial paper death certificate free of charge to the next of kin, which serves as the legal authorization needed to arrange burial or cremation [2][3].
  • Exceptions requiring vital statistics registration: If the death was not registered electronically by a medical provider or occurred under exceptional circumstances, the death must be declared within seven days at a local government vital statistics office, which is overseen by the Ministry of the Interior [2]. Duplicate or multilingual extracts of the death certificate can also be requested from local vital statistics authorities for cross-border use [2].

steps.title: Arrange Funeral, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral provider: Once the initial death certificate is issued, you may contract a licensed funeral agency in Estonia to coordinate mortuary transport, coffin or urn preparation, cemetery plot booking, or cremation services [1][3].
  • Cemetery and cremation documentation: Cemetery administrators and crematoria in Estonia require the official death certificate issued by the medical institution or vital statistics office before conducting a burial or cremation [2][3].
  • International repatriation and legalization: If your family member was a foreign national or if their remains or urn must be transported outside Estonia, the funeral agency coordinates the mortuary laissez-passer, hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin requirements, and health clearance [1][2]. When Estonian civil status documents must be presented abroad outside EU multilingual standard form agreements, they may require an Apostille issued by an Estonian notary through the Chamber of Notaries or consular legalization [2][5].

steps.title: Notify Authorities and Claim Funeral Grants and Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• Automatic data sharing and bank notifications: Once the death is recorded in the Population Register, the Estonian Social Insurance Board and the Tax and Customs Board are notified automatically, which stops old-age pension payments and updates official identity records [1][4]. However, you should contact commercial banks, insurers, telecom operators, and utility providers directly with the death certificate [1].
  • Local municipal funeral grants: Estonia does not pay a single universal national funeral grant; instead, local municipalities provide a municipal funeral benefit based on the deceased's registered residence in the Population Register [1][3]. You can check eligibility and submit an application via the State Portal Eesti.ee or directly with the relevant city or rural municipality government [1][3].
  • Survivor's pension claims: Dependent children and eligible family members may qualify for a survivor's pension administered by the Estonian Social Insurance Board [4]. Applications and benefit inquiries can be submitted online through the self-service portal when a breadwinner dies [1][4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession Proceedings
steps.html:
• Opening succession with an Estonian notary: In Estonia, all inheritance and probate matters are handled exclusively by notaries belonging to the Chamber of Notaries, and a succession proceeding can be initiated at any notary office in Estonia regardless of the deceased's last address [1][5]. The notary checks the Succession Register for any domestic wills or succession contracts [5].
  • Three-month acceptance or renunciation deadline: Estonia applies an automatic acceptance system under the Law of Succession Act, meaning heirs automatically accept both the assets and debts of the estate unless they submit a notarized application to renounce the inheritance within three months of learning of the death and their right to inherit [1][5]. To protect personal assets against unknown liabilities, an heir should request an official estate inventory through the notary, which limits liability for the deceased's debts to the net value of the inherited estate [5].
  • Taxation and cross-border coordination: Estonia does not levy a separate national inheritance tax on inherited property, although subsequent sales of inherited assets may trigger income tax rules [1][5]. If heirs reside abroad or assets are located across multiple European Union member states, an Estonian notary can conduct remote video authentication or issue a European Certificate of Succession [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Estonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Estonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Estonia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When your family member in Estonia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious progressive illness, taking structured medical, legal, and administrative steps while they retain full decision-making capacity helps protect their autonomy and secure state support. Below, we set out the five key actions to coordinate healthcare, representation, social benefits, and property documents in Estonia.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Obtain a physician referral for nursing care: In Estonia, state-funded inpatient nursing care and home nursing services are financed by the Estonian Health Insurance Fund, known as Tervisekassa, and require an official digital referral from a family physician or treating medical specialist [1].
  • Set up home nursing or inpatient palliative support: Together with the referring doctor, establish an individualized care and symptom management plan covering pain relief, home nursing visits, or admission to a contracted inpatient nursing hospital [1]. For insured persons, Tervisekassa covers the majority of home nursing costs and a fixed statutory share of inpatient nursing hospital care [1].
  • Coordinate municipal social care: Alongside medical nursing funded by Tervisekassa, contact the social welfare department of the local municipality where your family member resides to arrange domestic care workers, personal assistance, or home adaptations [1][2].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Contact
steps.html:
• Document treatment wishes in the Health Portal: While your family member has full capacity, they should discuss their goals of care, resuscitation preferences, and intensive care boundaries with their treating specialist so these medical instructions are recorded in Estonia's central Health Information System and accessible to emergency and hospital clinicians [1].
  • Nominate a trusted medical contact person: Under Estonian healthcare rules, the ill person can designate a trusted family member or representative in their medical records via the national Health Portal and inform their care team at Tervisekassa contracted facilities who is authorized to receive confidential clinical updates and participate in treatment discussions if their condition deteriorates [1].
  • Review organ donation and consent declarations: The ill person can also review or update formal declarations of intention and data access permissions inside the national Health Portal using their Estonian ID card, Mobile-ID, or Smart-ID [1].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Draft a notarial power of attorney: To ensure someone can manage real estate, corporate holdings, legal filings, and official administrative representation if the ill person becomes unable to act personally, your family member should execute a notarized power of attorney through an Estonian notary registered with the Chamber of Notaries [4][5].
  • Use remote e-Notary or home notary visits: If mobility is limited, Estonian notaries from the Chamber of Notaries can conduct remote authentication via video link through the e-Notary self-service portal using an Estonian digital ID, or arrange an in-person visit to the hospital or residence [4][5].
  • Establish specific bank mandates: Because commercial banks in Estonia often apply strict verification rules to general mandates, contact each bank directly while the account holder retains full capacity to register a bank-specific power of attorney or notarized financial mandate covering bill payments and account management [4][5].

steps.title: Activate Disability Assessments, Social Benefits, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Apply for disability and work ability evaluation: Submit a joint application to the Estonian Social Insurance Board to determine the degree of disability (moderate, severe, or profound) and, for working-age individuals, an assessment of partial or no work ability [2][3]. Medical data from the Health Information System is reviewed directly during this assessment [3].
  • Claim targeted disability and technical aid benefits: Once a disability degree is established, the Estonian Social Insurance Board provides monthly social benefits for disabled persons to help offset additional expenses related to care, rehabilitation, and subsidised technical aids such as hospital beds or mobility equipment [2].
  • Access statutory caregiver leave and municipal allowances: Working family members who care for a relative with a severe or profound disability are entitled under Estonian employment law to paid statutory caregiver leave days per calendar year, and local municipalities can appoint an official caregiver and grant a municipal caregiver allowance [2][3].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Property Records, and Cross-Border Documents
steps.html:
• Execute or update a notarial or domestic will: While capacity is completely intact, your family member can execute a notarial will before an Estonian notary, which is automatically entered into the Succession Register maintained through the Chamber of Notaries and cannot be misplaced or easily contested on formal grounds [4].
  • Consolidate property and identity credentials: Gather land register details, vehicle registrations, insurance policies, pension pillar records, and valid digital authentication tools (ensuring ID card PIN codes or Smart-ID credentials remain valid for the account holder's personal use) [2][4].
  • Coordinate cross-border assets and foreign mandates: If your family member owns property outside Estonia or if designated representatives live abroad, consult a notary at the Chamber of Notaries or an Estonian foreign mission regarding European Union choice-of-law declarations, certified translations, and Apostille requirements for cross-border powers of attorney [4][5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Latvia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Latvia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Latvia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member in Latvia. Managing the medical, civil registration, social security, and succession formalities in Latvia involves a sequential process across healthcare institutions, municipal registry offices, state social insurance, and sworn notaries. Below, we set out the five key official steps to follow.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or inpatient care facility deaths: When your family member passes away in a Latvian hospital or inpatient facility, the treating physician or hospital pathology unit examines the deceased and issues the official medical certificate of the cause of death (medicīniskā apliecība par nāves cēloni), transmitting the record via the national e-health system [1].
  • Deaths at home under medical supervision: If the death occurs at home and resulted from a known illness, contact the deceased's family doctor (ģimenes ārsts), who will verify the death and issue the medical certificate of cause of death based on prior clinical records [1]. Outside consulting hours, call the emergency medical service at 113 [1].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained deaths: If the death happens suddenly outside a medical facility or involves any suspicion of external causes, immediately notify the State Police at 110 or 112 [1]. Police officers will arrange transport to the State Centre for Forensic Medical Examination for a mandatory forensic autopsy before issuing the medical death certificate [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Office
steps.html:
• Six-working-day statutory deadline: Under Latvian civil status registration rules detailed on the State Administration Services Portal Latvija.gov.lv, a death must be declared to any municipal Civil Registry Office (Dzimtsarakstu nodaļa) in Latvia no later than six working days after the death occurred or the body was found [1].
  • Required registration documents: The informant must present the medical certificate of cause of death, the deceased's Latvian passport or electronic identity card (eID), and the informant's own valid identity document [1].
  • Issuance of the official Death Certificate: Civil registration of a death is free of charge, and the municipal Civil Registry Office immediately updates the Population Register and issues the official paper or electronic Death Certificate (miršanas apliecība), which is required for burial, benefit claims, and probate [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Contracting a funeral service provider: With the medical certificate and official Death Certificate, you can engage a licensed funeral provider in Latvia to handle mortuary preparation, cemetery plot allocation with the municipal cemetery administration, or cremation at a licensed crematorium [1].
  • Cemetery and cremation permits: Municipal cemetery administrations in Latvia require the official Death Certificate before granting a burial permit, while cremation requires verifying that no forensic hold applies [1].
  • International repatriation and document legalization: If your family member was a foreign citizen or if remains or cremated ashes must be transported across borders, the funeral director coordinates the international mortuary laissez-passer and sanitary sealing requirements [1]. When Latvian civil status certificates must be presented abroad outside EU multilingual extract exemptions, an Apostille can be obtained electronically or in person through any sworn notary via the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia [5].

steps.title: Notify Authorities and Claim Funeral and Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• Automatic population register updates and bank notifications: Once the municipal Civil Registry Office registers the death, the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs and the State Social Insurance Agency receive electronic notification [1][2]. You should notify commercial banks, insurers, and utility providers directly by presenting the Death Certificate [1].
  • Claiming the state funeral allowance: Under rules overseen by the Ministry of Welfare and administered by the State Social Insurance Agency, the person who undertakes the funeral of a socially insured employee, pensioner, unemployed benefit recipient, or state social security beneficiary can claim a state funeral allowance (apbedīšanas pabalsts) within six months of the death via the State Administration Services Portal Latvija.gov.lv [1][2][3]. Local municipalities also provide supplementary municipal funeral allowances for qualifying residents [1].
  • Survivor's pension and surviving spouse allowance: Dependent children under 18 (or full-time students up to 24) can claim a survivor's pension (apgādnieka zaudējuma pensija) from the State Social Insurance Agency [4]. In addition, if the deceased received a Latvian old-age or disability pension, a surviving spouse who also receives a Latvian pension may claim a temporary twelve-month allowance equal to 50 percent of the deceased's pension within six months of death [2][4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession Proceedings
steps.html:
• Opening an inheritance case with a sworn notary: In Latvia, probate and estate succession are conducted exclusively by sworn notaries operating under the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia [5]. Heirs must submit a succession application to a sworn notary practicing in the regional court district covering the deceased's last declared place of residence in Latvia [1][5].
  • Public notice and inventory rights: The sworn notary announces the opening of the succession in the official gazette Latvijas Vēstnesis and sets a statutory deadline (typically at least three months) for heirs and creditors to come forward [5]. To avoid personal liability for the deceased's debts beyond the value of the estate, heirs must explicitly request to accept the inheritance with inventory right (ar inventāra tiesību) within two months of learning of the opening of succession [5].
  • Notarial inheritance certificate and cross-border heirs: Latvia does not levy a separate national inheritance tax on estates, though statutory notary fees and Land Register state duties apply when registering inherited real estate after the sworn notary issues the Inheritance Certificate (mantojuma apliecība) [1][5]. Heirs living abroad can participate via remote video consultation on the portal of the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia or apply for a European Certificate of Succession for cross-border EU assets [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Latvia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Latvia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Latvia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When your family member in Latvia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious progressive illness, organizing medical care, legal representation, and social protection while they retain full legal capacity safeguards their personal wishes and access to public support. Below, we outline the five essential medical, legal, and administrative steps to take in Latvia.

steps.title: Coordinate State-Funded Palliative Care and Mobile Home Care Teams
steps.html:
• Request a medical council evaluation: In Latvia, integrated multidisciplinary palliative care at home and in inpatient units is coordinated and financed by the National Health Service (Nacionālais veselības dienests) [1][2]. To access state-funded mobile palliative care teams at the patient's residence, the family doctor (ģimenes ārsts) or treating specialist submits an e-health referral to a Level IV or Level V hospital medical council [1][2].
  • Activate 24/7 mobile palliative care at home: Once a hospital medical council confirms eligibility for a life-limiting illness, a regional coordinator registers the patient for mobile team visits covering physician and nursing care, pain and symptom relief, medical equipment, psychosocial support, and social care at no patient co-payment [1][2]. Service delivery begins within 24 hours of registration or hospital discharge [1][2].
  • Arrange regular home health care (veselības aprūpe mājās): For ongoing nursing procedures such as wound care, infusions, or symptom monitoring outside the mobile team framework, the family doctor can also issue a referral for state-funded home health care contracted by the National Health Service [1][2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Appoint a healthcare representative under the Law on the Rights of Patients: While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, they can formally authorize a trusted person to access confidential medical records and make healthcare consent decisions if they become unable to express their will [1][3]. This authorization can be recorded in the national e-health portal (e-veselība) or executed as a notarized mandate through the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia [3][4].
  • Document treatment preferences with the clinical team: The ill person should discuss specific boundaries regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, artificial ventilation, and intensive care interventions with their attending specialist and mobile palliative care physician so these instructions are documented in their official clinical care plan and e-health record [1][2].
  • Verify organ and tissue directives: Any personal declarations regarding consent or refusal for post-treatment tissue use can also be reviewed directly in the national e-health system using an eID card or eParaksts signature [1][2].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and a Future Power of Attorney
steps.html:
• Establish a Future Power of Attorney (nākotnes pilnvarojums): Under Latvian Civil Law, a person with full legal capacity can execute a notarized Future Power of Attorney before a sworn notary belonging to the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia [3][4]. This instrument enters into force only if and when the principal loses the capacity to understand and direct their actions, allowing the chosen attorney-in-fact to manage property, healthcare decisions, and financial affairs without requiring court-appointed guardianship [3][4].
  • Execute immediate notarial and banking powers of attorney: For immediate assistance with property, taxes, or administrative errands while capacity is intact, your family member can also execute a standard notarized power of attorney (pilnvara), which is recorded in the official Power of Attorney Register [3][4]. Always verify directly with the ill person's commercial banks in Latvia whether they require an in-branch bank mandate or specific notarial clauses for payment authorization [3][4].
  • Use remote video notarization or home visits: As highlighted by the Ministry of Justice, if the ill person cannot travel to a notary office, a sworn notary from the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia can authenticate powers of attorney via remote video conference on the official notary portal using eParaksts, or visit the patient at home or in the hospital [3][4].

steps.title: Activate Disability Assessments, Care Allowances, and Benefits
steps.html:
• Apply for disability and special care assessment: With a referral from the family doctor, submit an application to the State Medical Commission for the Assessment of Health Condition and Working Ability (VDEĀVK) to establish a severe disability group and obtain an official opinion on the need for special care [5].
  • Claim state disability pensions and care benefits: Once VDEĀVK establishes disability status and special care needs, the State Social Insurance Agency grants and disburses the corresponding disability pension or state social security benefit alongside the monthly allowance for a person with a disability requiring care (pabalsts invalīdam, kuram nepieciešama kopšana) [5].
  • Coordinate municipal social assistance and technical aids: Contact the local municipal social service department to arrange home care assistants, municipal housing adaptation grants, and state-subsidized technical mobility aids [1][5].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Property Records, and Cross-Border Documents
steps.html:
• Draft a public notarial will or inheritance contract: While capacity is fully intact, your family member can execute a public will (publisks testaments) or an inheritance contract (mantojuma līgums) before a sworn notary of the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia [3][4]. The notary registers the document in the Public Testament Register, ensuring its validity and immediate discoverability [3][4].
  • Compile property, pension, and civil status records: Organize Land Register (Zemesgrāmata) title deeds, vehicle certificates, second- and third-pillar pension beneficiary designations, and civil status documents [4][5].
  • Coordinate cross-border representation and assets: If your family member holds assets in other countries or if their designated representative resides outside Latvia, consult a sworn notary via the Council of Sworn Notaries of Latvia and guidance from the Ministry of Justice regarding European Union succession law elections, remote digital signing, and Apostille certification for foreign use [3][4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Lithuania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Lithuania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Lithuania: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the loss of your family member in Lithuania. Managing the official medical, civil registry, funeral, social security, and succession procedures in Lithuania follows a clear institutional sequence across healthcare providers, municipal civil registries, social insurance authorities, and civil law notaries. Below, we outline the five essential official steps to take.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or inpatient facility deaths: When your family member dies in a Lithuanian hospital or nursing facility, the attending physician establishes the fact and cause of death and issues an electronic Medical Certificate of Death (medicininis mirties liudijimas) directly in the national Electronic Health Services and Cooperation Infrastructure Information System (ESPBI IS) [1][2].
  • Deaths at home during expected care: If the death occurs at home during regular medical supervision, contact the deceased's family doctor (šeimos gydytojas) during clinic hours or call the emergency number 112 [1]. Once emergency responders verify that there are no signs of external violence, the family physician issues the electronic Medical Certificate of Death based on the patient's medical records [1][2].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained deaths: If a death occurs suddenly, outside medical supervision, or under unclear circumstances, you must notify the police and ambulance services via 112 [1]. The police initiate an inquiry and refer the body to the State Forensic Medicine Service (Valstybinė teismo medicinos tarnyba) for a forensic examination before issuing the medical death certificate [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry and Centre of Registers
steps.html:
• Automated electronic transmission: In Lithuania, once a healthcare institution or forensic service enters the electronic Medical Certificate of Death into the e-health system, the data is transmitted automatically to the Population Register managed by the State Enterprise Centre of Registers and to the municipal Civil Registry Department (Civilinės metrikacijos skyrius) [1][2].
  • In-person or portal declaration when required: If a paper medical death certificate was issued exceptionally or if you need to register the death of a Lithuanian citizen that occurred abroad through a diplomatic mission under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania, the declaration must be submitted within three days of the death or of receiving the body [1][2].
  • Obtaining official civil status extracts: Lithuania no longer issues traditional paper death certificates by default; instead, you can request an official extract confirming the record of the act of death (įrašą liudijantis išrašas) or a multilingual standard form from any municipal Civil Registry Department or electronically via the State Enterprise Centre of Registers self-service portal [1][2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral provider: Once the electronic medical death certificate is issued, you can instruct a licensed funeral service provider in Lithuania to arrange mortuary care, coffin or urn selection, municipal cemetery burial permissions, or cremation [1][2].
  • Burial and cremation permits: Municipal cemetery administrators and crematoria verify the medical death certification or civil registry death extract before allocating a burial plot or performing a cremation [1][2].
  • International repatriation and document legalization: If your family member was a foreign citizen or if their body or urn must be transported abroad, the funeral provider coordinates the sanitary and epidemiological transport permit from the National Public Health Centre and hermetically sealed coffin requirements [1]. For documents traveling outside the EU multilingual extract framework, an Apostille can be obtained from any Lithuanian notary belonging to the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries or through consular legalization overseen by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania [1][4].

steps.title: Notify Authorities and Claim Funeral Grants and Survivor Pensions
steps.html:
• Automatic register updates and bank notifications: Recording the death in the Population Register maintained by the State Enterprise Centre of Registers automatically notifies the State Social Insurance Fund Board Sodra and the State Tax Inspectorate, stopping old-age pension payments [2][3][5]. You should notify commercial banks, insurers, and utility providers directly [2].
  • Claiming the municipal funeral grant (laidojimo pašalpa): In Lithuania, the person organizing the burial is entitled to a universal statutory funeral grant equivalent to 8 Basic Social Benefits (BSI), administered by the municipal social support department of the deceased's declared residence (or via the Social Support for Families Information System, SPIS) within twelve months of the death [3].
  • Claiming survivor's and orphan's pensions: Surviving spouses who have reached retirement age or have an assessed disability, as well as dependent children under 18 (or full-time students up to 24), should apply to the State Social Insurance Fund Board Sodra for a survivor's pension (našlių pensija) and orphan's pension (našlaičių pensija), plus any unpaid pension amounts owed for the month of death [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Inheritance Tax Filings
steps.html:
• Strict three-month deadline to accept or renounce the estate: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Lithuania, heirs must submit a formal declaration to accept or renounce the inheritance within three months from the date of death [4]. Succession proceedings are opened exclusively before the notary office assigned by the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries to the territory of the deceased's last declared residence [4].
  • Accepting under an estate inventory: Because accepting an inheritance outright makes an heir personally liable for the deceased's debts with their own property, heirs should request acceptance based on an official estate inventory (pagal turto aprašą), which is compiled by a bailiff upon the notary's instruction and limits debt liability strictly to the inherited assets [4].
  • Inheritance tax clearance and cross-border coordination: Spouses, children, parents, grandparents, grandchildren, and siblings are completely exempt from Lithuanian inheritance tax, as are estates whose taxable value does not exceed 3,000 EUR [5]. Non-exempt heirs must obtain a taxable value certificate (Form FR0514) and pay inheritance tax (5 percent or 10 percent on 70 percent of the estate's value) to the State Tax Inspectorate before the notary issues the Certificate of the Right of Inheritance [4][5]. Heirs living abroad can act via remote video notarization (eNotaras), consular powers of attorney, or apply for a European Certificate of Succession through the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries [1][4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Lithuania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Lithuania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Lithuania: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When your family member in Lithuania is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious progressive illness, taking structured medical, legal, and administrative steps while they retain full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps secure state-funded care and protect their legal autonomy. Below, we outline the five essential steps to coordinate palliative care, legal mandates, disability support, and estate documents in Lithuania.

steps.title: Coordinate State-Funded Palliative Care and Home Nursing Services
steps.html:
• Obtain a referral for Compulsory Health Insurance coverage: In Lithuania, inpatient supportive treatment and nursing care (stacionarinė slauga ir palaikomasis gydymas), multidisciplinary palliative care (paliatyvioji pagalba), and outpatient home nursing (ambulatorinės slaugos paslaugos namuose) are financed by the Compulsory Health Insurance Fund administered by the National Health Insurance Fund [1][2]. Access requires an active referral from the patient's family physician (šeimos gydytojas) or treating specialist [1][2].
  • Choose an inpatient, day-care, or home palliative care provider: For patients with progressive life-limiting conditions whose active curative options are exhausted, the National Health Insurance Fund covers inpatient hospice and palliative units as well as multidisciplinary home palliative care teams (comprising a physician, nurse, nursing assistant, psychologist, and social worker) without rigid duration limits, provided the facility holds a contract with a Territorial Health Insurance Fund [1][2].
  • Activate outpatient home nursing (ASPN): While your family member remains at home, their family doctor clinic coordinates regular outpatient home nursing visits for pain control, infusions, catheter or wound management, and vital sign monitoring at zero extra cost for insured residents [1][2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Designate a patient representative in the e-health portal: Under Lithuania's Law on the Rights of Patients and Compensation for the Damage to Their Health, while your family member has full capacity, they can designate a trusted spouse, partner, or representative inside the national Electronic Health Services and Cooperation Infrastructure Information System (esveikata.lt) or in their clinic records so that person can access medical information and participate in clinical decisions [1][2].
  • Document palliative and resuscitation preferences: The ill person should discuss their treatment goals, pain management preferences, and boundaries regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation or intensive life-sustaining interventions with their attending specialist so these clinical instructions are recorded in their medical file [1][2].
  • Execute a notarized Advance Instruction (išankstinis nurodymas): Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Lithuania, an adult with full legal capacity can execute a notarized Advance Instruction before a notary of the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries [4]. This binding document specifies how personal care, medical consent, and property administration must be handled, and names the preferred representative or guardian, if the person later loses decision-making capacity [4][5].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Execute a notarized power of attorney (įgaliojimas): For real estate transactions, asset administration, tax representation, and official procedures, your family member should execute a notarized power of attorney before a Lithuanian notary belonging to the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries [4]. All notarized mandates and Advance Instructions are registered in the official Register of Powers of Attorney maintained by the State Enterprise Centre of Registers [4][5].
  • Use electronic powers of attorney or remote video notarization: For simpler administrative errands and receiving correspondence, the ill person can register an electronic power of attorney online via the portal of the State Enterprise Centre of Registers (igaliojimai.lt) [5]. For full notarial acts when mobility is restricted, a notary from the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries can conduct a remote video consultation via the eNotaras platform or visit the patient at home or in the hospital [4].
  • Verify commercial bank mandate rules: Contact each commercial bank in Lithuania where your family member holds accounts to verify whether they require a specific in-bank authorization or explicit notarial banking clauses to manage daily payments and online banking while capacity is intact [4][5].

steps.title: Activate Participation Level Assessments, Care Compensations, and Benefits
steps.html:
• Apply for disability and participation level assessment: Request the treating physician to submit medical documentation digitally to the Agency for the Protection of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, known as ANTA (Asmens su negalia teisių apsaugos agentūra) [3]. ANTA assesses the person's participation level (dalyvumo lygis, which replaced the former working capacity level) and evaluates special needs for first- or second-level individual care or assistance compensation [3].
  • Claim targeted nursing or care compensations: Once ANTA establishes a need for permanent nursing (slaugos) or assistance (priežiūros/pagalbos), submit an application through the Social Support for Families Information System (spis.lt) or the local municipality to receive monthly targeted compensations (tikslinės kompensacijos) calculated from the statutory targeted compensation base [3].
  • Claim sickness or work incapacity pensions via Sodra: Working-age individuals who have lost 45 percent or more of their participation level and meet social insurance contribution requirements should apply to the State Social Insurance Fund Board Sodra for a social insurance work incapacity pension, while employed family caregivers can claim temporary sickness benefits from Sodra when caring for a seriously ill family member [3].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Records, and Cross-Border Estate Documents
steps.html:
• Execute an official notarial will or register a personal will: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they can execute an official will (oficialusis testamentas) before a notary of the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries, or deposit a handwritten personal will for safekeeping [4]. The notary records the will in the Register of Wills administered by the State Enterprise Centre of Registers so it is automatically located when succession opens [4][5].
  • Organize property titles and beneficiary records: Gather Real Property Register extracts from the State Enterprise Centre of Registers, vehicle certificates, life insurance contracts, and second- or third-pillar pension fund agreements [4][5].
  • Coordinate cross-border assets and foreign representatives: If family members or property are located outside Lithuania, consult a notary of the Lithuanian Chamber of Notaries regarding European Union choice-of-law provisions in the will, remote eNotaras authentication, and Apostille certification for powers of attorney used abroad [4][5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Serbia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Serbia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Serbia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Serbia. When a death occurs in the Republic of Serbia, families must complete a sequence of medical, civil registration, municipal mortuary, social insurance, and notarial succession procedures governed by Serbian statutory law. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death (Potvrda o smrti)
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or clinical center: If your family member died in a public hospital, clinical center, or licensed inpatient facility under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Serbia (Ministarstvo zdravlja Republike Srbije), the attending physician establishes the fact and cause of death and issues the official medical death certificate (Potvrda o smrti) directly through the institutional medical registry [1].
  • Death at home: When a death occurs at a private residence, the family must contact the municipal community health center (Dom zdravlja) or emergency medical service (Hitna pomoć) so an authorized coroner-physician (lekar mrtvozornik) appointed by the municipality can examine the body in person and issue the Potvrda o smrti [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unattended death: Do not move the body or disturb the premises. Notify the local police (Policija - 192) and emergency medical services (194) immediately. Where the cause of death is unclear, sudden, or potentially unnatural, the public prosecutor or coroner orders a forensic examination or autopsy (obdukcija) at a forensic medicine institute before releasing the body and issuing the Potvrda o smrti [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Registrar (Matičar)
steps.html:
• Statutory 3-day reporting deadline: Under the Serbian Law on Civil Registers (Zakon o matičnim knjigama), a death must be reported to the municipal civil registrar (Matična služba) in the municipality or city (opština or grad) where the death occurred, or where the body was found, within 3 days of the date of death (or within 24 hours in urgent burial circumstances) [2]. For deaths in healthcare institutions, the hospital administration typically transmits the notice electronically to the registrar, though the family or authorized funeral provider must still finalize the registration details.
  • Required documents for civil registration: Present the signed Potvrda o smrti, the deceased's Serbian biometric identity card (lična karta) or passport, birth certificate (Izvod iz matične knjige rođenih), and marriage certificate (Izvod iz matične knjige venčanih) if applicable, along with the informant's valid identity document [2].
  • Obtaining official death certificates: Once the death is recorded in the Register of Deaths (Matična knjiga umrlih), request multiple originals of the official death certificate (Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih). If your family member held foreign nationality or had assets abroad, request an international multilingual death certificate (Međunarodni izvod iz matične knjige umrlih on the Vienna Convention form) or obtain an Apostille stamp from the competent Basic Court (Osnovni sud) in Serbia [2] [5]. Digital civil status services and pension records are also coordinated via the Office for IT and eGovernment (eUprava Portal) [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a public utility or licensed funeral enterprise: In Serbia, municipal cemeteries are managed by public utility funeral enterprises (Javno komunalno preduzeće - JKP Pogrebne usluge, such as JKP Pogrebne usluge Beograd or the corresponding municipal JKP), while private licensed funeral operators may assist with transport and preparation [1] [2]. Burial may take place only after the coroner or attending physician has issued the Potvrda o smrti and the burial permit (Dozvola za sahranjivanje) is cleared, typically no earlier than 24 hours after death [1].
  • Cremation requirements: If cremation (kremacija) is planned (available at major facilities such as Lešće or Novo groblje in Belgrade and Novi Sad), the funeral authority requires the Potvrda o smrti, proof that no forensic impediment exists, and either written pre-death instructions from the deceased or a formal declaration signed by the closest next of kin, alongside verification that any cardiac pacemaker has been removed [1].
  • International repatriation of remains (Sprovodnica): To transport human remains into or out of Serbia, the family's funeral director must obtain a mortuary laissez-passer (Sprovodnica za prenos posmrtnih ostataka) cleared by the border sanitary inspectorate of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Serbia, requiring hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin preparation, a sanitary certificate confirming absence of contagious disease, the Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih, and consular clearance from the destination or origin embassy [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Insurance, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral expense reimbursement (Naknada pogrebnih troškova): If the deceased was a pension recipient or insured contributor, the person who paid for the funeral may claim the statutory lump-sum funeral grant from the Republic Fund for Pension and Disability Insurance (Republički fond za penzijsko i invalidsko osiguranje - RF PIO) by submitting the Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih, original itemized fiscal funeral invoices (fiskalni isečak i račun), and the claimant's bank account card [3] [4].
  • Survivor pension (Porodična penzija): Eligible family members (surviving spouse or recognized cohabiting partner meeting statutory age or incapacity criteria, children in full-time education up to age 26, or dependent parents) can apply for a survivor pension (Porodična penzija) at the local branch of the Republic Fund for Pension and Disability Insurance (Republički fond za penzijsko i invalidsko osiguranje - RF PIO) or via the eUprava portal, while cross-border bilateral social security pension coordination is handled in cooperation with the Social Insurance Institute (Zavod za socijalno osiguranje) [2] [3] [4].
  • Health insurance, banks, and municipal tax: The civil registrar's electronic entry automatically updates the central population registry, which notifies the Republic Fund for Health Insurance (RFZO). However, heirs should present the death certificate directly to Serbian commercial banks to freeze individual accounts and stop recurring direct debits, and notify the local Municipal Tax Administration (Lokalna poreska administracija) regarding property tax (porez na imovinu) pending succession [2] [3].

steps.title: Complete Probate and Estate Succession (Ostavinski postupak)
steps.html:
• Ex officio initiation via the death record (Smrtovnica): Within 30 days of registering the death, the municipal registrar compiles an official estate and family summary (Smrtovnica) and forwards it ex officio to the competent Basic Court (Osnovni sud) according to the deceased's last permanent residence (prebivalište) in Serbia [5] [6].
  • Proceedings before a Public Notary (Javni beležnik): Under Serbia's Law on Non-Contentious Proceedings and the Law on Inheritance (Zakon o nasleđivanju), the Basic Court entrusts the estate inventory and probate hearing (ostavinska rasprava) to an appointed public notary registered with the Public Notary Chamber of Serbia (Javnobeležnička komora Srbije) acting as court commissioner (poverenik suda) [5] [6]. Heirs present property title deeds from the Republic Geodetic Authority (RGZ - Katastar nepokretnosti), bank balance statements, vehicle registration documents, and any last will (zaveštanje / testament) to receive the formal Decree of Inheritance (Rešenje o nasleđivanju) [5] [6].
  • Inheritance tax (Porez na nasleđe) and foreign heirs: First-degree heirs (prvi nasledni red: spouse and children) and parents inheriting from children are exempt from Serbian inheritance tax; second-degree heirs pay 1.5%, and more distant or unrelated beneficiaries pay 2.5%, declared to the Tax Administration (Poreska uprava) within 30 days of the Rešenje o nasleđivanju becoming final (pravosnažno) [6]. Heirs residing outside Serbia may participate via a notarized and Apostilled special power of attorney (specijalno punomoćje za davanje nasledničke izjave) certified before a Serbian consulate or foreign notary [5] [6].
