title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Serbia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Serbia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Serbia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Serbia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while your family member retains full legal capacity (poslovna sposobnost) protects their autonomy and eases the practical burden on caregivers. Below, we outline the five essential steps to coordinate care, treatment preferences, representation, social benefits, and estate documentation in the Republic of Serbia.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and RFZO Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Primary home medical care (Kućno lečenje i nega): Start with the patient's chosen primary care physician (izabrani lekar) at the municipal community health center (Dom zdravlja). Under the healthcare system supervised by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Serbia (Ministarstvo zdravlja Republike Srbije), the izabrani lekar issues referrals for the municipal home treatment and nursing service (Služba za kućno lečenje i zdravstvenu negu) to provide pain management, infusion therapy, wound care, and symptom monitoring at home [1] [2].
  • Inpatient palliative units: For complex symptom stabilization that cannot be managed at home, the attending specialist or izabrani lekar can issue an inpatient referral (uput za bolničko lečenje) to specialized palliative care units (jedinice za palijativno zbrinjavanje) within regional general hospitals or clinical centers [1] [2].
  • Mandatory health insurance coverage and exemptions: Through the Republic Fund for Health Insurance (Republički fond za zdravstveno osiguranje - RFZO), patients diagnosed with severe or advanced oncological and systemic illnesses are entitled to prescription analgesics (including opioid pain relief on special duplicate prescriptions), medical aids (medicinsko-tehnička pomagala), and exemption from statutory co-payments (oslobođenje od plaćanja participacije) upon presenting the relevant specialist diagnosis [2] [6].

steps.title: Record Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Patient autonomy under the Law on Patients' Rights: In Serbia, the Law on Patients' Rights (Zakon o pravima pacijenata) guarantees every patient with decision-making capacity the right to informed consent (pristanak na medicinsku meru) and the right to refuse proposed medical procedures, even when treatment is life-sustaining, provided the physician fully explains the medical consequences and records the refusal in the official medical chart [6].
  • Designating a trusted person for medical information and consent: While Serbia does not have a standalone statutory registry for living wills, a patient with full capacity may formally authorize a family member or trusted representative to receive confidential medical updates and participate in treatment discussions under the Law on Patients' Rights [1] [6]. Families should execute both a written authorization filed in the hospital and Dom zdravlja medical record and a notarized medical representation authorization (ovlašćenje / punomoćje) before a public notary so treating clinicians have clear documentation if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [5] [6].
  • Organizing clinical handovers: Keep a consolidated medical folder at home containing the latest specialist reports (izveštaj lekara specijaliste), medication schedule, allergy profile, and emergency directives so visiting Hitna pomoć or home-care teams can honor the care plan immediately [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Punomoćje): Under Serbian civil law, a valid power of attorney can only be granted while the principal (vlastodavac) possesses full mental and legal capacity (poslovna sposobnost). Arrange an appointment with a public notary registered with the Public Notary Chamber of Serbia (Javnobeležnička komora Srbije) in the patient's municipality [5]. If the ill person cannot travel due to mobility limitations, Serbian public notaries are legally authorized to conduct an official out-of-office visit (izlazak javnog beležnika na teren) at the patient's home or hospital ward [5].
  • General vs. special powers of attorney: Distinguish between a general power of attorney (opšte punomoćje) for routine administrative representations (collecting mail, communicating with utilities, tax offices, or health funds) and a solemnized or special notarial power of attorney (specijalno punomoćje) required for selling or encumbering real estate, managing business shares, or representing the person in court proceedings [5].
  • Direct bank account authorization (Ovlašćenje po računu): Serbian commercial banks frequently require either their own in-branch account mandate form or a strictly worded notarial punomoćje specifying the exact bank and account numbers. Completing the bank's specific account card authorization while your family member is able to sign avoids any need for lengthy judicial guardianship (lišenje poslovne sposobnosti i postavljanje staraoca) before the Basic Court [5].

steps.title: Activate Caregiver Allowance, Disability Benefits, and Statutory Leave
steps.html:
• Monetary allowance for assistance and care of another person (Novčana naknada za pomoć i negu drugog lica): Insured persons and pensioners who, due to severe illness or physical impairment, are immobile, blind, unable to feed or dress themselves independently, or undergoing permanent dialysis can apply for the monthly care and assistance allowance (tuđa nega i pomoć) through the Republic Fund for Pension and Disability Insurance (Republički fond za penzijsko i invalidsko osiguranje - RF PIO) [3] [4]. Submit the application form along with original specialist medical documentation and hospital discharge summaries (otpusna lista) so the RF PIO medical commission (organ veštačenja) can assess eligibility; home medical assessment can be requested if the patient is bedridden [3] [4].
  • Disability pension (Invalidska penzija) and municipal social support: If your family member is still of working age and has experienced a complete loss of working capacity (potpuni gubitak radne sposobnosti), they may apply for a disability pension via RF PIO or inspect contribution records on the eUprava portal [3] [4]. Additionally, the local Center for Social Work (Centar za socijalni rad) administers supplementary caregiver allowances (uvećani dodatak za pomoć i negu drugog lica) and municipal home help (pomoć u kući) for qualifying households [3].
  • Statutory family care leave (Odsustvo sa rada radi posebne nege ili nege člana uže porodice): Under the Serbian Labor Law (Zakon o radu) and Health Insurance Law, employed close family members may obtain paid temporary incapacity leave (bolovanje radi nege člana uže porodice) issued by the izabrani lekar and medical commission via RFZO, as well as unpaid leave options from their employer to care for a seriously ill relative [2] [6].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid will (Zaveštanje / Testament): Under the Serbian Law on Inheritance (Zakon o nasleđivanju), a person aged 15 or older who is capable of reasoning (sposoban za rasuđivanje) may execute a will in several recognized forms, including a holographic will (svojeručno zaveštanje written entirely by hand and signed by the testator), a written will before two witnesses (pisano zaveštanje pred svedocima), a judicial will (sudsko zaveštanje), or a public notarial will (javnobeležničko zaveštanje) recorded in the official registry maintained by the Public Notary Chamber of Serbia [5]. A notarial will provides the highest evidentiary security against future validity challenges.
  • Lifetime support or gift agreements: Where appropriate, Serbian law also regulates the Contract on Lifetime Support (Ugovor o doživotnom izdržavanju) and Contract on Distribution of Property During Lifetime (Ugovor o ustupanju i raspodeli imovine za života), both of which must be solemnized by a public notary (javni beležnik) to have legal effect [5].
  • Consolidating civil and property records: Verify that real estate ownership is accurately registered in the Republic Geodetic Authority cadastre (Katastar nepokretnosti - RGZ), gather birth and marriage certificates, list all bank accounts and insurance policies, and ensure any cross-border powers of attorney carry an Apostille stamp if assets or family representatives are located outside Serbia [4] [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bosnia and Herzegovina: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bosnia and Herzegovina: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Bosnia and Herzegovina: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Because legal, health, civil registration, and social insurance competences in Bosnia and Herzegovina are administered at the entity level - across the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Federacija Bosne i Hercegovine - FBiH), Republika Srpska (RS), and the Brčko District (Brčko distrikt BiH) - the exact offices depend on the municipality or city where the death occurred and where your family member resided. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death (Potvrda o smrti)
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or clinical center: When a death occurs in a public hospital, cantonal hospital (kantonalna bolnica), or university clinical center (such as KCUS Sarajevo, UKC Tuzla, SKB Mostar, or UKC Republike Srpske in Banja Luka), the attending physician establishes the cause of death and issues the official medical death certificate (Potvrda o smrti) and the statistical death report (Statistički list o slučaju smrti) [1].
  • Death at home: If your family member died at a private residence, contact the municipal community health center (Dom zdravlja) or emergency medical service (Hitna pomoć - 124) immediately. An authorized municipal coroner-physician (mrtvozornik) appointed by the local authority must examine the body in person to verify natural causes and issue the Potvrda o smrti before the body may be moved to a mortuary [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unattended death: Do not move the body or disturb the surroundings. Report the death immediately to the local police (Policija - 122) and emergency medical services (124). Where a violent, sudden, or unexplained death is suspected, the cantonal or district prosecutor orders a forensic examination or autopsy (obdukcija) before releasing the remains and issuing the medical clearance for burial [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Registry (Matični ured)
steps.html:
• Statutory reporting deadlines: Under the entity laws on civil registers (Zakon o matičnim knjigama in FBiH, Republika Srpska, and Brčko District), a death must be declared to the municipal civil registry office (Matični ured or Matična služba) of the municipality (općina / opština) or city (grad) where the death occurred within 3 days of the death (or within 24 hours when urgent sanitary burial regulations apply) [1] [2]. If the death occurred in a healthcare facility, the hospital notifies the registrar electronically or in writing, and a family member or authorized funeral representative completes the formal registration.
  • Required civil registration documents: Bring the medical Potvrda o smrti, the deceased's Bosnian identity card (lična karta / osobna iskaznica) and passport, birth certificate (Izvod iz matične knjige rođenih / Rodni list), marriage certificate (Izvod iz matične knjige vjenčanih / Vjenčani list) if married, and the informant's valid identity document [1] [2].
  • Obtaining official death certificates: Upon entry into the Register of Deaths (Matična knjiga umrlih), the registrar issues the official death certificate (Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih / Smrtni list). Request several original copies, as well as a multilingual international extract (Međunarodni izvod iz matične knjige umrlih under the Vienna Convention) if the deceased held foreign nationality or owned assets abroad [1] [2]. Where an Apostille is required for non-convention jurisdictions, legalization is performed by the competent Municipal Court (Općinski sud in FBiH) or Basic Court (Osnovni sud in Republika Srpska) [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral or religious burial society: Municipal cemeteries and mortuaries are operated by public utility companies (Javno komunalno preduzeće - JKP, such as KJKP Pokop in Sarajevo or Gradsko groblje in Banja Luka), licensed private funeral firms, or confessionally organized burial societies (such as Jedileri, Bakije, Pokop, or parish cemetery boards) [1]. Burial takes place once the Potvrda o smrti and burial permit (Dozvola za ukop / sahranu) have been issued, generally between 24 and 48 hours after death.
  • Cremation and cross-border cremation arrangements: Because Bosnia and Herzegovina currently has limited operational crematorium infrastructure, families arranging cremation often coordinate transport through a licensed funeral operator to an accredited crematorium in a neighboring jurisdiction (such as Zagreb or Novi Sad) using a mortuary transit permit, or bury cremated urns at designated municipal cemetery plots [1].
  • International repatriation (Sprovodnica): Transporting human remains across the borders of Bosnia and Herzegovina requires a mortuary passport (Sprovodnica za prenos posmrtnih ostataka), sanitary clearance from the entity health inspectorate confirming placement in a hermetically soldered zinc liner, the Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih, and consular authorization from the relevant diplomatic mission [1].

steps.title: Notify Pension Funds, Health Insurance, CIPS, and Banks
steps.html:
• Survivor pension (Porodična penzija / mirovina) and funeral expense grants: In the Federation of BiH, eligible family members (surviving spouse or cohabiting partner meeting statutory age or incapacity thresholds, children in full-time education up to age 26, or dependent parents) submit applications to the cantonal branch of the Federalni zavod za penzijsko i invalidsko osiguranje (FZ MIO/PIO), which also processes funeral assistance reimbursements (posmrtnina / naknada pogrebnih troškova) for qualifying deceased pensioners [3] [4]. In Republika Srpska, survivor pension and funeral claims are filed with the Fond za penzijsko i invalidsko osiguranje Republike Srpske (Fond PIO RS) [5]. Required documents include the official application form, Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih, marriage or birth certificates proving family relationship, school enrollment certificates for student children, and a bank transaction account confirmation [3] [4] [5].
  • Identity cancellation (CIPS / IDDEEA) and health insurance: Following civil death registration, the municipal Matični ured transmits the death record to deregister residency and invalidate the deceased's identity card and passport in the central IDDEEA / CIPS database, as well as to terminate mandatory health insurance with the cantonal health insurance institute (Zavod zdravstvenog osiguranja) or the Republika Srpska Health Insurance Fund [1].
  • Commercial banks and municipal utilities: Present an original Izvod iz matične knjige umrlih to every bank in Bosnia and Herzegovina where your family member held accounts, loans, or safe-deposit boxes so individual accounts are frozen pending the final probate decree, and update municipal utility accounts (elektroprivreda, water, heating, telecoms) [2] [6].

steps.title: Complete Probate and Estate Succession (Ostavinski postupak)
steps.html:
• Ex officio preparation of the death inventory (Smrtovnica): Within 30 days of recording the death in the Matična knjiga umrlih, the municipal civil registrar prepares the official death inventory (Smrtovnica) listing known heirs, real estate, and movable assets, and forwards it ex officio to the competent Municipal Court (Općinski sud in FBiH), Basic Court (Osnovni sud in Republika Srpska), or Basic Court of Brčko District, as tracked on the judicial portal of the Visoko sudsko i tužilačko vijeće Bosne i Hercegovine (Pravosudje.ba) [2].
  • Succession hearings before a Public Notary (Notar): Under the Inheritance Laws (Zakon o nasljeđivanju) of FBiH, Republika Srpska, and Brčko District, the court routinely delegates the conduct of uncontested probate proceedings (ostavinski postupak) to an appointed public notary acting as court commissioner (povjerenik suda), registered with the Notarska komora Federacije Bosne i Hercegovine (or the Notary Chamber of Republika Srpska) [2] [6]. Heirs must bring land registry extracts (zk. izvadak from the Zemljišnoknjižni ured and Posjedovni list from the cadastre), bank certificates, vehicle ownership cards, and any written will (testament / oporuka) so the notary can issue the Decree of Inheritance (Rješenje o nasljeđivanju) [2] [6].
  • Inheritance tax and foreign heirs: Inheritance tax rules vary by entity and canton: first-degree heirs (prvi nasljedni red: spouse, children, and parents in most cantons and Republika Srpska) are generally exempt from inheritance tax (porez na nasljeđe), while more distant heirs must report the final Rješenje o nasljeđivanju to the relevant Tax Administration (Porezna uprava FBiH or Poreska uprava RS) [1] [6]. Heirs living abroad may give their inheritance declaration (nasljednička izjava) via a notarized and Apostilled special power of attorney (specijalna punomoć) or before a consular mission of Bosnia and Herzegovina [2] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bosnia and Herzegovina: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bosnia and Herzegovina: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Bosnia and Herzegovina: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Bosnia and Herzegovina is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, organizing medical care, legal representation, and social protection while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity (poslovna sposobnost) protects their wishes and prevents administrative delays. Because healthcare, social welfare, and pension systems in Bosnia and Herzegovina operate across the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH), Republika Srpska (RS), and the Brčko District, we set out the five key steps below with the specific entity institutions.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Primary care and home nursing (Kućna njega i liječenje): Coordinate first with your family member's registered family medicine team (tim porodične / obiteljske medicine) at the local municipal health center (Dom zdravlja). The family physician arranges home medical visits (kućne posjete), community nursing care (patronažna služba), pain management, and infusion therapy for patients who cannot travel to clinics [1] [2].
  • Inpatient palliative care and hospice centers: For specialized symptom control, the family doctor or attending specialist issues a referral (uputnica) to regional palliative care departments or hospices (such as the University Clinical Center Tuzla Palliative Care Center, Lubin hospice/palliative units in Sarajevo and Mostar, or palliative beds within UKC Republike Srpske and regional hospitals) [1] [2].
  • Health insurance coverage of medications and medical aids: In the Federation of BiH, tertiary health rights and inter-cantonal funds are coordinated by the Zavod zdravstvenog osiguranja i reosiguranja Federacije Bosne i Hercegovine alongside the ten cantonal health insurance institutes (kantonalni zavodi zdravstvenog osiguranja), whereas in Republika Srpska coverage is administered by the Fond zdravstvenog osiguranja Republike Srpske [1] [2]. Patients with severe oncological or advanced illnesses qualify for exemption from co-payments (oslobađanje od participacije), essential opioid analgesics on special prescriptions, and orthopedic or nursing aids (ortopedska i druga pomagala) [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Authorize a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and refusal of treatment under patients' rights laws: Under the Law on the Rights, Obligations and Responsibilities of Patients in the Federation of BiH (Zakon o pravima, obavezama i odgovornostima pacijenata) and the corresponding healthcare legislation in Republika Srpska, a patient with decision-making capacity has the statutory right to be fully informed, to consent to proposed medical procedures, or to refuse specific treatments by signing a written declaration in the medical file [1] [2].
  • Designating a proxy for medical information and substitute decisions: While Bosnia and Herzegovina does not maintain a centralized electronic living-will registry, a patient with intact legal capacity can designate a family member or trusted representative in writing within their hospital and Dom zdravlja records to receive confidential medical documentation and communicate treatment wishes [1] [5]. Executing a notarized authorization (notarski ovjerena punomoć / izjava) before a public notary further ensures that hospitals recognize the designated representative if the patient's ability to communicate declines [5].
  • Maintaining an accessible clinical dossier at home: Keep all specialist findings (nalazi i mišljenja specijaliste), hospital discharge letters (otpusno pismo), active therapy lists, and emergency contact details in a single folder at the patient's bedside for emergency medical teams (Hitna pomoć - 124) [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Arranging a public notary appointment or home/hospital visit: Under the Laws on Notaries (Zakon o notarima) in both entities and Brčko District, a power of attorney (punomoć) is valid only if executed while the principal (vlastodavac) is mentally competent and capable of understanding the legal act. Contact a notary registered with the Notarska komora Federacije Bosne i Hercegovine (or the Notary Chamber of Republika Srpska) [5]. If your family member is bedridden or hospitalized, public notaries are authorized to perform an official out-of-office attendance (izlazak notara na teren at the home or hospital room) to verify identity and legal capacity in person [5].
  • General administrative vs. special notarial powers of attorney: A certified general power of attorney (opća / opšta punomoć) enables a family representative to deal with health insurance funds, pension institutes, telecoms, utilities, and municipal offices. However, any transaction involving real estate transfer, mortgages, corporate shares, or representation in non-contentious judicial proceedings requires a special notarized or solemnized power of attorney (specijalna notarska punomoć) explicitly enumerating each legal act [5] [6].
  • Bank account mandates (Punomoć za raspolaganje računom): Commercial banks in Bosnia and Herzegovina generally require the account holder to sign the bank's internal account mandate card or present a specific notarial power of attorney citing the exact IBAN/transaction account numbers. Putting this mandate in place early avoids the need for a judicial deprivation-of-capacity and guardianship proceeding (postupak oduzimanja poslovne sposobnosti i postavljanja staratelja) through the Municipal/Basic Court and Center for Social Work [5] [6].

steps.title: Activate Caregiver Allowances, Disability Benefits, and Statutory Leave
steps.html:
• Allowance for care and assistance by another person (Dodatak za njegu i pomoć od strane drugog lica): Individuals whose severe illness or physical impairment requires permanent daily assistance from another person can apply for the statutory care and assistance allowance (tuđa njega i pomoć) and civilian disability assessment through their municipal Center for Social Work (Centar za socijalni rad) and the medical disability assessment institutes (Institut za medicinsko vještačenje zdravstvenog stanja in FBiH or commissions in Republika Srpska) [1] [2] [3].
  • Disability pension (Invalidska penzija / mirovina) and pensioner support: If your family member is an active insured worker who has suffered a permanent loss of working capacity, an application for a disability pension can be submitted to the Federalni zavod za penzijsko i invalidsko osiguranje (FZ MIO/PIO) in FBiH or to the Fond PIO Republike Srpske, using the official pension and medical assessment forms [3] [4].
  • Paid sick leave and family care leave for employed caregivers: Under the entity Labor Laws (Zakon o radu) and Health Insurance Laws, an employed spouse or close relative caring for a seriously ill family member can apply through their family medicine doctor for temporary incapacity leave to care for an immediate family member (privremena spriječenost za rad radi njege člana uže porodice / bolovanje), or request statutory paid/unpaid family care leave from their employer [1] [2].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Records, and Property Titles
steps.html:
• Executing a legally valid will (Testament / Oporuka): Under the Inheritance Laws (Zakon o nasljeđivanju) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, any person aged 15 or older with sound judgment (sposoban za rasuđivanje) may make a will. Recognized forms include a handwritten holographic will (svojeručni testament written and signed entirely in the testator's handwriting), a written will signed before two simultaneous witnesses (pisani testament pred svjedocima), a judicial will recorded at the Municipal or Basic Court (sudski testament), or a notarial will (notarski testament) drafted and registered by a notary of the Notarska komora Federacije Bosne i Hercegovine or Republika Srpska [5] [6].
  • Property lifetime contracts: Remember that under Bosnian inheritance law, mandatory heirs (nužni nasljednici, such as spouse and children) have statutory forced-share rights unless property is transferred under a notarized Contract on Lifetime Support (Ugovor o doživotnom izdržavanju) or Contract on Distribution of Estate During Lifetime (Ugovor o ustupanju i raspodjeli imovine za života) [5] [6].
  • Verifying land registry, civil status, and cross-border documents: Check that real property is cleanly registered in both the court land registry (Zemljišnoknjižni ured of the Municipal/Basic Court) and municipal cadastre (Katastar), assemble current birth and marriage extracts (Rodni list, Vjenčani list), and obtain an Apostille from the competent court on any power of attorney that must be used outside Bosnia and Herzegovina [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Montenegro: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Montenegro: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Montenegro: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Montenegro. When a death occurs in Montenegro (Crna Gora), families must complete a sequence of medical certification, civil registration with the Ministry of the Interior (MUP), funeral or repatriation clearance, pension and social insurance notifications, and notarial estate succession proceedings. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death (Potvrda o smrti)
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or clinical center: If your family member died in the Clinical Center of Montenegro (Klinički centar Crne Gore - KCCG in Podgorica) or a regional general or special hospital (opšta ili specijalna bolnica) operating under the healthcare network of the Government of Montenegro (Vlada Crne Gore), the attending physician establishes the cause of death and issues the official medical death certificate (Potvrda o smrti) and statistical death report [1].
  • Death at home: When a death occurs at a private residence, contact the municipal community health center (Dom zdravlja) or the Institute for Emergency Medical Assistance (Zavod za hitnu medicinsku pomoć - 124) immediately. An authorized physician or municipal coroner (mrtvozornik) must examine the body in person to verify natural causes and issue the Potvrda o smrti before the deceased can be transferred to a mortuary [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unattended death: Do not move the body or disturb the surroundings. Immediately notify the Montenegrin Police Directorate (Uprava policije - 122) and emergency medical services (124). When the cause of death is sudden, violent, or unknown, the state prosecutor orders a medico-legal examination or forensic autopsy (obdukcija) prior to releasing the body and issuing the Potvrda o smrti [1].

steps.title: Register the Death in the Civil Register of Deaths (Matični registar umrlih)
steps.html:
• Statutory 3-day reporting deadline: Under the Montenegrin Law on Civil Registers (Zakon o matičnim registrima), the fact of death must be reported to the regional unit or branch (područna jedinica ili filijala) of the Ministry of the Interior (Ministarstvo unutrašnjih poslova - MUP Crne Gore) in the municipality where the death occurred (or where the body was found) within 3 days of death, or before burial if burial occurs earlier [2]. Healthcare institutions report hospital deaths ex officio, while the family or authorized funeral representative completes the formal registration.
  • Required civil registration documents: Present the medical Potvrda o smrti, the deceased's Montenegrin biometric identity card (lična karta) or passport, birth certificate (Izvod iz matičnog registra rođenih), marriage certificate (Izvod iz matičnog registra vjenčanih) if applicable, and the informant's valid identity document [2].
  • Obtaining official death certificates: Once the death is entered into the Civil Register of Deaths (Matični registar umrlih - MRU), request multiple original copies of the official death extract (Izvod iz matičnog registra umrlih) via the MUP counter or through the e-services of the Government of Montenegro (Vlada Crne Gore) [2]. If the deceased was a foreign citizen or left assets abroad, request a multilingual international extract on the Vienna Convention form (Međunarodni izvod iz registra umrlih) or obtain an Apostille stamp from the competent Basic Court (Osnovni sud) listed on the Judicial Portal of Montenegro (Sudovi Crne Gore) [2, 5] [5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a municipal funeral utility: In Montenegro, municipal cemeteries and chapel facilities are managed by local public utility enterprises (Komunalno preduzeće / Pogrebne usluge, such as Pogrebne usluge d.o.o. Podgorica or the corresponding municipal utility in Nikšić, Bar, Budva, Kotor, or Herceg Novi), alongside licensed private funeral operators [1]. Burial takes place after the Potvrda o smrti and burial permit (Dozvola za sahranu) have been issued, typically 24 to 48 hours after death.
  • Cremation arrangements: Because Montenegro does not currently operate a domestic crematorium, families choosing cremation engage a licensed funeral provider to obtain a mortuary transit permit (Sprovodnica) and transport the deceased to an accredited crematorium in a neighboring jurisdiction (such as Belgrade or Novi Sad in Serbia, or Zagreb in Croatia), after which the urn may be returned to Montenegro without sanitary restrictions for interment [1, 2].
  • International repatriation of remains (Sprovodnica): Transporting human remains across Montenegrin borders requires an official mortuary laissez-passer (Sprovodnica za prenos posmrtnih ostataka), clearance from the border health and sanitary inspection confirming placement in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, the Izvod iz matičnog registra umrlih, and authorization from the relevant diplomatic or consular mission [1, 2].

steps.title: Notify Fond PIO, Health Insurance, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Reimbursement of funeral expenses (Naknada pogrebnih troškova): If the deceased was a pension recipient of the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of Montenegro (Fond penzijskog i invalidskog osiguranja Crne Gore - Fond PIO), the person who paid the funeral expenses may submit a claim within 60 days of the date of death to the regional branch of Fond PIO [3]. Required documents include the application form, Izvod iz matičnog registra umrlih, original itemized funeral company invoices (računi pogrebnog preduzeća), and the applicant's bank account details [3].
  • Survivor pension (Porodična penzija): Eligible family members (surviving spouse or cohabiting partner meeting statutory age or disability criteria, children up to age 19 or up to age 24/25 while in full-time education, or children permanently incapable of independent life and work) apply for a survivor pension at the regional unit of the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of Montenegro (Fond penzijskog i invalidskog osiguranja Crne Gore - Fond PIO) by presenting the Izvod iz matičnog registra umrlih, birth and marriage extracts, school certificates for student children, and the deceased's employment/insurance records [4].
  • Health insurance, banks, and municipal tax: Entry into the MUP Matični registar umrlih automatically updates the central population registry and notifies the Health Insurance Fund of Montenegro (Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje Crne Gore - FZO), though families should still notify commercial banks in Montenegro directly with an original death extract so accounts are frozen pending probate, and inform the municipal tax office regarding real estate tax (porez na nepokretnosti) [2, 5].

steps.title: Complete Probate and Estate Succession (Ostavinski postupak)
steps.html:
• Ex officio initiation via the death record (Smrtovnica): After recording the death in the Matični registar umrlih, the MUP registrar prepares the official death inventory (Smrtovnica) and transmits it ex officio within 30 days to the competent Basic Court (Osnovni sud) listed on the Judicial Portal of Montenegro (Sudovi Crne Gore), determined by the deceased's last domicile (prebivalište) or the location of Montenegrin real estate [2, 5].
  • Succession before a Public Notary (Notar): Under Montenegro's Law on Non-Contentious Proceedings (Zakon o vanparničnom postupku) and Law on Inheritance (Zakon o nasljeđivanju), the Basic Court entrusts the probate hearing (ostavinski postupak) to an appointed public notary acting as court commissioner (povjerenik suda), governed by the Notary Chamber of Montenegro (Notarska komora Crne Gore) [5, 6] [6]. Heirs present real estate title sheets (list nepokretnosti from the Real Estate Administration - Uprava za nekretnine), bank balance confirmations, vehicle registration cards, and any written will (testament) so the notary can issue the Decree of Inheritance (Rješenje o nasljeđivanju) [5, 6].
  • Inheritance tax (Porez na nasljeđe) and foreign heirs: Under Montenegrin tax law, first-degree heirs (prvi nasljedni red: children and spouse) and parents inheriting real estate are exempt from real estate transfer and inheritance tax (porez na promet nepokretnosti po osnovu nasljeđa), whereas other heirs pay the statutory 3% rate declared to the Tax Administration (Poreska uprava Crne Gore) within 15 days of the final Rješenje o nasljeđivanju [5, 6]. Foreign heirs or heirs residing abroad may participate via a notarized and Apostilled special power of attorney (specijalno punomoćje za davanje nasljedničke izjave) [5, 6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Montenegro: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Montenegro: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Montenegro: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Montenegro is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, putting medical coordination, legal representation, and social protection in place while your family member retains full legal capacity (poslovna sposobnost) protects their personal autonomy and prevents procedural bottlenecks. Below, we set out the five key medical, legal, and administrative steps to take in Montenegro (Crna Gora).

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and FZO Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Primary care and home nursing (Jedinica za patronažu i kućno liječenje): Begin with your family member's chosen primary care physician (izabrani doktor za odrasle) at the municipal community health center (Dom zdravlja). Within the public healthcare structure supervised by the Government of Montenegro (Vlada Crne Gore), the izabrani doktor prescribes symptom management and issues work orders for the home nursing and treatment unit (patronažna služba i kućno liječenje) to administer pain relief, infusions, wound care, and regular clinical monitoring at home [1] [2].
  • Hospital specialist and palliative care: When inpatient symptom stabilization is required, the izabrani doktor issues an electronic referral (uput) to the regional general hospital (opšta bolnica), special hospital (such as Brezovik in Nikšić), or the Clinical Center of Montenegro (Klinički centar Crne Gore - KCCG in Podgorica) [1] [2].
  • Mandatory health insurance coverage and medical aids: Through the Health Insurance Fund of Montenegro (Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje Crne Gore - FZO), insured patients with severe oncological or advanced progressive illnesses receive full coverage for essential analgesics, exemption from statutory health service co-payments (oslobađanje od plaćanja participacije), and approval for medical-technical aids (medicinsko-tehnička pomagala such as hospital beds, antidecubitus mattresses, oxygen concentrators, and mobility aids) [2].

steps.title: Record Treatment Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Patient autonomy under the Law on Patients' Rights: Under the Montenegrin Law on Patients' Rights (Zakon o pravima pacijenata), every patient who is capable of reasoning (sposoban za rasuđivanje) holds the right to informed consent (pristanak na medicinsku mjeru) and the right to refuse proposed medical interventions by signing an explicit written statement in their medical record after the attending physician explains the clinical consequences [1] [2].
  • Authorizing a trusted representative for medical information and decisions: Because Montenegro does not operate a separate national living-will registry, a patient with full capacity should formally name a trusted family member or proxy in their Dom zdravlja and hospital medical chart who is authorized to inspect medical documentation and receive clinical updates [1] [2]. In addition, executing a notarized medical representation authorization (notarski ovjereno punomoćje / izjava) before a Montenegrin public notary provides clear legal authority if the patient's capacity to communicate later diminishes [5].
  • Keeping a consolidated clinical file at home: Maintain an up-to-date bedside folder containing all specialist reports (izvještaji ljekara specijaliste), discharge summaries (otpusne liste), active medication lists, and health card details for rapid access by emergency medical teams (Zavod za hitnu medicinsku pomoć - 124) [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Arranging a notary appointment or home/hospital visit: Under Montenegrin civil and notarial law, a power of attorney (punomoćje) can only be granted while the principal (vlastodavac) possesses full mental and legal capacity (poslovna sposobnost). Contact a public notary registered with the Notary Chamber of Montenegro (Notarska komora Crne Gore) [5]. If your family member cannot visit a notary's office due to illness or hospitalization, Montenegrin notaries are legally empowered to conduct an official out-of-office attendance (službena radnja van notarske kancelarije) at the patient's home or hospital ward [5].
  • General vs. special notarial powers of attorney: A certified general power of attorney (opšte punomoćje) covers routine representation before the Health Insurance Fund, Fond PIO, municipal authorities, and utility companies. However, selling or encumbering real estate, managing company shares, or making high-value legal dispositions requires a special notarized power of attorney (specijalno punomoćje or notarial deed) explicitly stating the authorized transactions [5]. Under the Montenegrin Law on Obligations (Zakon o obligacionim odnosima), a power of attorney generally terminates upon death unless explicitly structured for specific continuing acts allowed by law [5].
  • Bank account mandates (Ovlašćenje po računu): Commercial banks in Montenegro typically require the account holder either to sign the bank's internal account authorization card or to provide a specific notarial punomoćje identifying the exact bank and account numbers. Completing this while capacity is intact avoids having to petition the Basic Court (Osnovni sud) for formal deprivation of legal capacity and guardianship appointment (oduzimanje poslovne sposobnosti i postavljanje staraoca) [5] [6].

steps.title: Activate Caregiver Allowances, Disability Benefits, and Statutory Leave
steps.html:
• Allowance for care and assistance of another person (Dodatak za njegu i pomoć): Under Montenegro's social and child protection and pension frameworks, individuals who require permanent daily care and assistance from another person due to severe illness or physical impairment may apply for the monthly care and assistance allowance (tuđa njega i pomoć) through the competent municipal Center for Social Work (Centar za socijalni rad) or, for eligible pension beneficiaries, via the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of Montenegro (Fond penzijskog i invalidskog osiguranja Crne Gore - Fond PIO), subject to assessment by the socio-medical commission (socijalno-ljekarska komisija) [3] [4].
  • Disability pension (Invalidska penzija): If your family member is of working age and has experienced a complete loss of working capacity (potpuni gubitak radne sposobnosti), they can submit an application with specialist medical dossiers to the regional unit of the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of Montenegro (Fond penzijskog i invalidskog osiguranja Crne Gore - Fond PIO) for a disability pension evaluation [3] [4].
  • Paid caregiver sick leave (Privremena spriječenost za rad radi njege člana uže porodice): Under the Montenegrin Labor Law (Zakon o radu) and Mandatory Health Insurance Law, an employed close family member caring for a seriously ill relative may obtain temporary paid medical leave (bolovanje radi njege člana uže porodice) authorized by the primary care physician and the FZO medical commission, as well as statutory unpaid leave options from their employer [1] [2].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing a valid will (Testament / Zavještanje): Under the Montenegrin Law on Inheritance (Zakon o nasljeđivanju), any person aged 15 or older who is capable of reasoning may execute a will. Recognized forms include a handwritten holographic will (svojeručni testament written and signed entirely by hand), a written will before two witnesses (pisani testament pred svjedocima), a judicial will (sudski testament), or a notarial will (notarski testament) drafted and registered by a public notary of the Notary Chamber of Montenegro (Notarska komora Crne Gore) [5].
  • Lifetime support or property distribution contracts: Where families wish to regulate lifetime care and property transfer outside forced-heirship claims (nužni dio), Montenegrin law provides for the Contract on Lifetime Support (Ugovor o doživotnom izdržavanju) and Contract on Distribution of Property During Lifetime (Ugovor o ustupanju i raspodjeli imovine za života), both of which must be solemnized before a notary [5].
  • Consolidating civil registry and property records: Verify that real property ownership is accurately recorded in the Real Estate Administration cadastre (Uprava za nekretnine - List nepokretnosti), obtain updated birth and marriage extracts from the Ministry of the Interior (MUP) civil registry [6], and ensure any cross-border powers of attorney carry an Apostille from the competent Basic Court (Osnovni sud) if assets or family representatives are located abroad [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in North Macedonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in North Macedonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for North Macedonia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in North Macedonia. When a death occurs in the Republic of North Macedonia, families must complete a sequence of medical, civil, funeral, social security, and succession procedures regulated under national law. Below, we outline the five official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or clinical facility: When your family member dies in a public or licensed private healthcare institution in North Macedonia, the attending physician examines the body and issues the official medical confirmation of death (Потврда за смрт) together with the statistical death report (Пријава за смрт) under the standards of the Ministry of Health of North Macedonia [1]. The hospital administration transmits the medical documentation directly or releases it to the family for civil registration [1] [2].
  • Death at home: If your family member passes away at a private residence, you must immediately call the Emergency Medical Service (Итна медицинска помош, telephone 194) or the municipal coroner doctor (мртвопроверител) appointed by the local health center [1]. The examining doctor verifies the cause and time of death on site and completes the medical death certificate required for burial and civil registration [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained death: Where the death is sudden, occurs outside medical supervision without clear natural causes, or involves suspected trauma, the police (telephone 192) and the competent public prosecutor must be notified [1]. A forensic autopsy is conducted at the Institute of Forensic Medicine, Criminology and Medical Deontology before the body and medical certificate are released [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and authority: Under the Law on Management of Registers of Births, Marriages, and Deaths, a death must be reported to the Office for Management of Registers of Births, Marriages and Deaths (Управа за водење на матичните книги - UVMK) in the municipality where the death occurred or where the deceased was buried within 3 days of the death or the discovery of the body [2] [3].
  • Required documentation: To register the death with the Office for Management of Registers of Births, Marriages and Deaths, the informant (a relative, household member, healthcare institution, or authorized funeral representative) submits the medical confirmation of death, the deceased's national identity card (лична карта) or passport, the birth certificate and marriage certificate (if applicable), and the informant's valid identification [2] [3].
  • Issuance of official death certificates: Once the registrar records the entry in the Death Register (Матична книга на умрените), the Office for Management of Registers of Births, Marriages and Deaths issues the official Death Certificate (Извод од матичната книга на умрените), which can also be requested electronically via the National e-Services Portal [2] [3]. If documents must be used abroad, you can request a multilingual extract on the Vienna Convention form or obtain an Apostille from the competent Basic Court and the Ministry of Justice [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral operator: Under the Law on Cemeteries and Funeral Services, burial and transport of human remains within North Macedonia must be carried out by a licensed municipal or private funeral operator (погребално претпријатие), such as AD Butel in Skopje or the local public utility enterprise (ЈКП) managing municipal cemeteries [1] [2].
  • Burial permits and cemetery rules: Burial takes place only after the medical examiner or healthcare facility has issued the burial permit confirming that at least 24 hours have elapsed since death (unless sanitary regulations require earlier or later interment) and the death has been reported to the civil registrar [1] [2]. Because North Macedonia currently does not operate a domestic crematorium, families seeking cremation must arrange cross-border transport of the deceased to a licensed crematorium in a neighboring country [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or is to be buried or cremated abroad, the licensed funeral director obtains a mortuary passport (Спроводница за пренос на посмртни останки) and sanitary clearance from the State Sanitary and Health Inspectorate under the Ministry of Health of North Macedonia, seals the body in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin, and coordinates the consular laissez-passer with the destination country's embassy [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Pension cancellation and survivor benefits: If the deceased was an insured worker or pensioner, you must notify the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of North Macedonia (Фонд на пензиското и инвалидското осигурување на Северна Македонија - PIOM) at its regional branch [4]. Eligible surviving family members (spouse, children, or dependent parents meeting statutory age or disability criteria) may apply to the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of North Macedonia for a family survivor pension (семејна пензија) [3] [4].
  • Solidarity funeral grant: Where the deceased was a pensioner enrolled in the solidarity fund administered through the pension system, family members who paid for the funeral may submit the original death certificate, funeral invoices, and bank account details to claim the statutory lump-sum funeral assistance (посмртна помош) [4].
  • Health insurance, identity documents, and bank accounts: The Health Insurance Fund of North Macedonia (Фонд за здравствено осигурување) updates its insured register upon civil death registration, terminating active coverage [2] [6]. You should also notify the Ministry of Interior to cancel the identity card and passport, inform the Public Revenue Office (Управа за јавни приходи) and municipal property tax office regarding ongoing tax obligations, and present the death certificate to commercial banks to freeze individual accounts and halt standing orders pending probate [2] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession Proceedings
steps.html:
• Initiation of probate and succession: Under the Law on Inheritance and the Law on Non-Contentious Procedure, the civil registrar or interested heirs submit the death certificate and death record (смртовница) containing data on surviving heirs, known assets, and any testament to the Basic Court (Основен суд) in the municipality of the deceased's last domicile [2] [5].
  • Notarial probate hearing: The Basic Court assigns the succession case (оставинска постапка) to an authorized public notary registered with the Notary Chamber of North Macedonia, acting as a court trustee (довереник на судот) [5]. The notary schedules a succession hearing, verifies any will, records heir declarations accepting or renouncing their inheritance share under statutory forced-heirship rules, and issues the formal Decision on Inheritance (Решение за наследување) [5].
  • Property registration, inheritance tax, and cross-border heirs: Once the Decision on Inheritance becomes final, the notary transmits it to the Agency for Real Estate Cadastre to update property title deeds and to the municipal tax administration to assess inheritance and gift tax (first-line heirs - spouse and children - are generally exempt from municipal inheritance tax on inherited residential property under statutory thresholds, while second-line and third-line heirs pay 2% to 3% or 4% to 5%) [5]. Heirs residing outside North Macedonia may participate by granting a notarized and Apostilled special power of attorney (специјално полномошно) to a representative in North Macedonia [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in North Macedonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in North Macedonia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for North Macedonia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in North Macedonia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person retains full mental and legal capacity helps ensure that care preferences and financial affairs are respected. Below, we outline the five essential official steps to coordinate care, legal mandates, benefits, and advance planning in the Republic of North Macedonia.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist palliative and home medical care: Through the primary care physician (матичен лекар) and attending specialist, your family member can be referred to specialized palliative care units (such as the PHI Specialized Hospital for Geriatric and Palliative Medicine "13 Noemvri" in Skopje or regional general hospital palliative wards) and mobile home nursing services (домашна посета и патронажна служба) regulated by the Ministry of Health of North Macedonia [1].
  • Mandatory public health insurance coverage: The Health Insurance Fund of North Macedonia (Фонд за здравствено осигурување на Република Северна Македонија - FZOM) covers approved inpatient palliative care, oncology and symptom-management medications on the positive drug list, orthopedic and medical aids, and prescribed home treatment visits for insured individuals [1] [2].
  • Co-payment exemptions and private care options: Insured persons with severe chronic or malignant conditions often qualify for statutory exemptions from health service co-payments (партиципација) through the Health Insurance Fund of North Macedonia [2]. Families supplementing public care with licensed private home-care agencies or private hospital services should obtain itemized medical reports to support social and disability benefit claims [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Patient autonomy and informed consent: Under the Law on Protection of Patients' Rights (Закон за заштита на правата на пациентите) overseen by the Ministry of Health of North Macedonia, every patient with decision-making capacity has the right to be fully informed about their diagnosis and prognosis and to accept or refuse specific medical interventions or life-prolonging procedures in writing [1].
  • Written statement of treatment preferences: While North Macedonia does not maintain a standalone national living-will registry, your family member can execute a written, signed statement of medical treatment preferences and have a public notary registered with the Notary Chamber of North Macedonia certify the signature or solemnize the declaration so that attending physicians have clear proof of prior wishes [1] [3].
  • Designating a healthcare proxy or representative: Under the Law on Protection of Patients' Rights, the patient may formally designate a trusted adult representative (законски застапник или овластено лице) in medical records and via a notarized authorization to receive confidential medical data and communicate treatment decisions if the ill person later loses the ability to express consent [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Notarized general or special power of attorney: Under the Law on Obligations and the Law on Notariat, a power of attorney (полномошно) must be signed while your family member possesses full legal capacity (деловна способност) [3]. A public notary from the Notary Chamber of North Macedonia can prepare or solemnize a general or special power of attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage real estate, tax filings, administrative applications, and legal representation [3].
  • Home or hospital bedside notarization: If your family member cannot travel due to serious illness, you may request an official out-of-office visit from a local public notary registered with the Notary Chamber of North Macedonia to verify identity and legal capacity and execute the power of attorney at the hospital or home [3].
  • Bank account mandates: Commercial banks in North Macedonia typically require either their own internal account authorization form (овластување за располагање со трансакциска сметка) signed by the account holder or a specific notarized power of attorney explicitly enumerating banking powers (withdrawals, bill payments, and online banking access) [3]. Because standard mandates may be challenged if legal capacity is later lost without formal guardianship, setting up dedicated bank mandates early is essential [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Dependency, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Allowance for assistance and care by another person: When a serious illness leaves your family member unable to perform basic daily activities independently, they can apply for the statutory monthly allowance for assistance and care by another person (надоместок за помош и нега од друго лице) through the local Center for Social Work under the policy framework of the Ministry of Social Policy, Demography and Youth [4]. Eligibility is assessed by an expert medical commission based on specialist documentation and Barthel Index functional evaluation [4].
  • Disability pension and bodily impairment rights: If your family member is of working age and has permanently lost work capacity, an application can be submitted through the primary physician and the Pension and Disability Insurance Fund of North Macedonia (Фонд на пензиското и инвалидското осигурување на Северна Македонија - PIOM) for a disability pension (инвалидска пензија) or compensation for bodily impairment [4] [5].
  • Sick leave and family caregiver leave: Employed patients are entitled to paid temporary incapacity leave (боледување) approved initially by the primary physician and extended by the medical commission of the Health Insurance Fund of North Macedonia [2]. Employed family members caring for an acutely ill immediate relative may also request statutory paid or unpaid family care leave under the Law on Labor Relations and the Health Insurance Fund rules [2] [4].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing a valid will: Under the Law on Inheritance (Закон за наследување), a capable adult in North Macedonia may execute a holographic will (своерачен тестамент, handwritten and signed in full by the testator), a written will before two witnesses, or a court/notarial will (судски или нотарски тестамент) recorded by a judge or a public notary from the Notary Chamber of North Macedonia [3]. Keeping note of mandatory forced-heirship shares (нужен дел) for spouses and children prevents subsequent succession disputes [3].
  • Consolidating civil status and property records: Verify that birth and marriage certificates are current with the Office for Management of Registers of Births, Marriages and Deaths (Управа за водење на матичните книги - UVMK) and the National e-Services Portal, and verify that real estate title deeds (имотен лист) match current ownership in the Agency for Real Estate Cadastre [6].
  • Cross-border coordination: If family representatives or assets are located outside North Macedonia, ensure that powers of attorney and civil status extracts carry an Apostille from the Basic Court or Ministry of Justice (or consular legalization where required) and certified translations so they are immediately recognized across jurisdictions [3] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Albania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Albania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Albania: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Albania. Navigating the immediate medical, civil, funeral, social security, and succession requirements in the Republic of Albania involves specific statutory deadlines and digital procedures through national institutions. Below, we explain the five official and practical steps to follow in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or clinical facility: When a person dies in a public or licensed private hospital in Albania, the attending physician confirms the death and issues the official Medical Death Certificate (Skeda e Vdekjes / Raporti Mjekësor i Vdekjes) under the protocols of the Ministry of Health and Social Protection [1]. The hospital also transmits the electronic death notification to the civil registry system and provides the signed medical form required for burial and civil registration [1] [2].
  • Death at home: If your family member passes away at a private residence, you must contact the National Medical Emergency Center (Qendra Kombëtare e Urgjencës Mjekësore, telephone 127) or the family physician at the local municipal health center (Qendra Shëndetësore) [1]. The examining doctor verifies the death on site, rules out non-natural causes, and completes the official medical certificate of death (Skeda e Vdekjes) [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained death: Where the death is sudden, unnatural, or occurs under unknown circumstances outside medical supervision, you must notify the State Police (Policia e Shtetit, telephone 129) [1]. The prosecutor orders an examination by the Institute of Forensic Medicine (Instituti i Mjekësisë Ligjore), which issues the forensic death report and burial clearance once the examination concludes [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and authority: Under Law No. 10129 on Civil Status (Për Gjendjen Civile), a death occurring inside Albania must be declared at the local Civil Status Office (Zyra e Gjendjes Civile) of the municipality or administrative unit where the death occurred or where the deceased was registered within 10 days of the death (or within 60 days if the death occurred abroad and is registered via an Albanian consular mission) [2].
  • Required documentation: A family member, household member, or authorized funeral representative submits the original Medical Death Certificate (Skeda e Vdekjes) signed by the physician or forensic examiner, the deceased's biometric identity card (Letërnjoftim) or passport, and the informant's identification document to the Civil Status Office [2].
  • Obtaining official death certificates via e-Albania: Once the civil registrar records the Act of Death (Akti i Vdekjes) in the National Registry of Civil Status, the deceased is deregistered from the active population register, and family members can immediately download the official Death Certificate (Certifikatë nga akti i vdekjes) with a legally binding electronic seal through the e-Albania Government Portal [2]. Multilingual certificates and Apostille legalization (via the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs) can also be requested for international use [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral agency and burial permit: Families engage a licensed private funeral service agency (agjenci funerale) or the municipal funeral and cemetery administration (such as Agjencia e Shërbimeve Funerale in the Municipality of Tirana) [1] [2]. Burial in a public or municipal cemetery requires the burial permit (Leje Varrimi) issued upon presentation of the Medical Death Certificate and civil declaration [1] [2]. Because Albania does not currently operate a domestic crematorium, cremation requests require international transport of remains to a licensed crematorium in a neighboring country [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign citizen or is to be buried or cremated outside Albania, the funeral agency coordinates the international mortuary passport (Leje kalimi kufitar për trupin e të ndjerit), sanitary-epidemiological sealing certification in a hermetically soldered zinc-lined coffin under the State Health Inspectorate and the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, and consular clearance from the destination embassy [1] [2].
  • Legalization of documents for cross-border transport: For repatriation abroad, the Albanian Death Certificate, medical certificate proving the absence of contagious disease, and embalming certificate must carry an Apostille stamp from the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs along with certified translations [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Health, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral expense grant (Shpërblimi për rast vdekjeje): Under Albania's social insurance legislation administered by the Social Insurance Institute (Instituti i Sigurimeve Shoqërore - ISSH), when an insured employee, pensioner, or dependent family member dies, the person who bore the funeral costs is entitled to a statutory lump-sum funeral grant equal to one month's minimum old-age pension [3] [4]. Applications are submitted online via the e-Albania Government Portal or at the regional ISSH directory with the death certificate and funeral payment invoices [2] [3] [4].
  • Family survivor pension (Pensioni familjar): Surviving spouses, orphan children (up to age 18, or up to age 25 if enrolled in full-time daytime study), and dependent parents or grandchildren meeting statutory criteria may apply for a monthly family survivor pension (pensioni familjar) from the Social Insurance Institute through its online e-Albania integration [3] [4].
  • Health insurance, tax, and bank notifications: Deregistration in the National Registry of Civil Status updates the Compulsory Health Care Insurance Fund (FSDKSH), while families must present the Death Certificate to commercial banks to freeze individual bank accounts, stop automatic debits, and obtain account balance statements as of the date of death for succession proceedings [2]. Any active sole proprietorship (person fizik) registered with the National Business Center (QKB) and the General Directorate of Taxes must also be closed or transferred [2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession Proceedings
steps.html:
• Issuance of the Certificate of Inheritance by a public notary: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Albania and Law No. 110/2018 on Notariat, non-contentious succession proceedings are conducted directly by a public notary registered with the National Chamber of Notaries of Albania (Dhoma Kombëtare e Noterisë) [5].
  • Verification of wills and statutory heirs: Heirs submit a formal request to an Albanian notary along with the Death Certificate, family composition certificate (Certifikatë familjare) from the e-Albania Government Portal showing all legal heirs, and property documents [2] [5]. The notary searches the National Register of Wills (Regjistri Kombëtar i Testamenteve) to check for any notarial or special will, verifies statutory forced-heirship protections (rezerva ligjore) for minor or disabled heirs, and issues the Notarial Certificate of Inheritance (Dëshmia e Trashëgimisë) [5].
  • Renunciation, property registration, and cross-border coordination: Under the Albanian Civil Code, an heir who wishes to renounce the inheritance (heqja dorë nga trashëgimia) must make a formal declaration before a notary within 3 months of learning of the opening of the succession (or 6 months if residing abroad) [5]. Once the Certificate of Inheritance is issued, the notary files it with the State Cadastre Agency (ASHK) to transfer real estate ownership and allows heirs to claim bank balances; heirs living abroad may act through a notarized and Apostilled power of attorney (prokurë e posaçme) [2] [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Albania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Albania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Albania: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Albania is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, organizing medical support, legal representation, social security benefits, and property records while the ill person retains full decision-making capacity helps protect their autonomy and family stability. Below, we set out the five key medical, legal, and administrative steps in the Republic of Albania.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public palliative and oncology care: Under Law No. 138/2014 on Palliative Care in the Republic of Albania, governed by the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, patients with life-limiting illnesses are entitled to multidisciplinary symptom management, pain control, and psychosocial support through regional hospital palliative units, the Oncology Service at Mother Teresa University Hospital Center (QSUT), and home-based palliative teams (shërbimi paliativ në banesë) [1].
  • Compulsory health insurance coverage and drug reimbursement: Through a referral from the family physician (mjeku i familjes) and specialist medical commission, the Compulsory Health Care Insurance Fund (Fondi i Sigurimit të Detyrueshëm të Kujdesit Shëndetësor - FSDKSH) covers approved inpatient consultations, diagnostic workups, and full or partial reimbursement for palliative and pain-relief medications on the national reimbursement list (Lista e Barnave të Rimbursueshme) [1] [2].
  • Home care and non-governmental hospice services: In major municipalities, public home nursing is supplemented by licensed non-profit hospice providers (such as Ryder Albania and Mary Potter Palliative Care Center) operating in coordination with the Ministry of Health and Social Protection [1]. Keeping certified copies of all hospital discharge summaries (fletëdalje nga spitali) and oncology commission decisions (vendim i komisionit onkologjik) is essential for subsequent benefit applications [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and patient rights: Under Law No. 10107 on Healthcare in the Republic of Albania and Law No. 138/2014 on Palliative Care, every patient with mental capacity has the statutory right to receive comprehensive medical information and to give or withhold informed consent (pëlqimi i informuar) for any proposed medical treatment or invasive intervention [1].
  • Written statement of medical preferences: Because Albania does not maintain a central electronic living-will register, a patient who wishes to record specific end-of-life treatment preferences or refusals of extraordinary life-sustaining measures should execute a written declaration before a public notary registered with the National Chamber of Notaries of Albania (Dhoma Kombëtare e Noterisë) and provide copies to the family physician and treating hospital [1] [3].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative: Under Albania's palliative care and healthcare rules, while your family member retains full legal capacity (zotësia e plotë për tëepruar), they can formally name a trusted adult representative via a notarial authorization (prokurë e posaçme për përfaqësim mjekësor) and record that representative in the clinical file so doctors have an authorized contact if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Notarized general or special power of attorney (Prokurë): Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Albania and Law No. 110/2018 on Notariat, any power of attorney authorizing another person to manage real estate, pensions, taxes, or legal transactions must be executed as a notarial act while the principal has full mental and legal capacity [3].
  • Bedside notarization at home or in hospital: If serious illness prevents your family member from visiting a notary office in person, Law No. 110/2018 permits a public notary from the National Chamber of Notaries of Albania to conduct an official out-of-office attendance at the patient's residence or hospital ward, verify identity and mental capacity, and register the power of attorney in the electronic notarial system (NISA) [3].
  • Bank account mandates: Commercial banks in Albania require either an internal bank mandate signed by the account holder at the branch or a specific notarial power of attorney (prokurë e posaçme bankare) that explicitly lists the bank name, account numbers, and permitted actions (withdrawals, transfers, e-banking management, and pension collection) [3]. Because powers of attorney under the Albanian Civil Code can be affected if legal incapacity is later declared by a court without guardianship arrangements, completing bank mandates promptly is critical [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Dependency, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Disability pension (Pensioni i invaliditetit): Insured workers of working age who become partially or totally unable to work due to severe illness may apply for a disability pension (pensioni i invaliditetit) and supplementary care allowance through the Medical Commission for the Determination of Work Ability (KMCAP) under the Social Insurance Institute (Instituti i Sigurimeve Shoqërore - ISSH) [4] [5]. Applications and medical files are submitted electronically via the e-Albania Government Portal [4] [5].
  • Social disability and personal caregiver allowance (Pagesa e aftësisë së kufizuar dhe ndihmësit personal): Regardless of contributory pension history, patients assessed with severe functional impairment under the biopsychosocial or medical evaluation commissions supervised by the Ministry of Health and Social Protection and State Social Service (Shërbimi Social Shtetëror) may qualify for a monthly disability benefit and a dedicated financial allowance for a personal caregiver (pagesa për kujdestarin) [1] [5].
  • Temporary medical incapacity and family care leave: Employed patients receive paid medical leave (raport mjekësor për paaftësi të përkohshme në punë) via the Social Insurance Institute and the e-Albania Government Portal, while employed family members caring for a dependent relative are entitled to statutory paid and unpaid family care leave under the Labor Code of the Republic of Albania [4] [5].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing a notarial or holographic will: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Albania, a person with full legal capacity may execute a notarial will (testament me akt noterial) before a public notary from the National Chamber of Notaries of Albania, which is immediately registered in the National Register of Wills (Regjistri Kombëtar i Testamenteve), or a holographic will written, dated, and signed entirely by hand [3]. Testators must respect the statutory legal reserve (rezerva ligjore), which protects minor children, disabled direct heirs, and unborn heirs from disinheritance [3].
  • Verifying civil status and cadastral title records: Through the e-Albania Government Portal, your family member or their authorized representative should download current birth, marriage, and family composition certificates (Certifikatë familjare) to ensure all family relationships are accurately recorded in the National Registry of Civil Status, and verify real estate ownership certificates (certifikatë pronësie) with the State Cadastre Agency (ASHK) [6].
  • Cross-border legal and asset coordination: If family representatives or assets are situated outside Albania, ensure that powers of attorney and civil status documents are legalized with an Apostille stamp through the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and translated by a certified translator licensed by the Ministry of Justice [3] [6].
