ru.title: Тяжёлое заболевание и юридические формальности (Россия): официальный чек-лист в 5 шагов
ru.cardSummary: Официальное руководство в 5 шагов при тяжёлом или неизлечимом заболевании (Россия): паллиативная медицинская помощь, информированное согласие и доступ к медкарте, нотариальные доверенности, оформление инвалидности и составление завещания.
ru.introHtml: Когда у вашего родственника в России диагностировано тяжелое или прогрессирующее заболевание, ограничивающее продолжительность жизни, своевременное оформление медицинских, юридических и социальных документов в период, когда болеющий человек полностью сохраняет гражданскую дееспособность, помогает защитить его пожелания относительно лечения и обеспечить бесперебойное управление финансовыми делами. Ниже мы излагаем пять основных шагов, которые следует выполнить последовательно в соответствии с законодательством Российской Федерации.

steps.title: Координация паллиативной помощи, патронажного ухода на дому и медицинского полиса
steps.html:
• Законное право на бесплатную паллиативную медицинскую помощь: В соответствии со статьей 36 Федерального закона № 323-ФЗ «Об основах охраны здоровья граждан в Российской Федерации» пациенты с неизлечимыми прогрессирующими заболеваниями имеют право на бесплатную амбулаторную и стационарную паллиативную медицинскую помощь, купирование боли (включая назначение сильнодействующих и наркотических анальгетиков) и психологическую поддержку в соответствии с порядками, которые утверждает Министерство здравоохранения Российской Федерации [1].
  • Заключение врачебной комиссии и постановка на учет: Обратитесь к лечащему врачу-терапевту или врачу-онкологу территориальной поликлиники для проведения врачебной комиссии (либо получения заключения онколога при уже подтвержденном диагнозе) с целью выдачи медицинского заключения об оказании паллиативной помощи и прикрепления вашего родственника к кабинету паллиативной помощи, выездной патронажной службе на дому или специализированному хоспису системы ведомства - Министерство здравоохранения Российской Федерации [1].
  • Полис обязательного медицинского страхования (ОМС) и социальное обслуживание на дому: Проверьте актуальность полиса обязательного медицинского страхования (ОМС) через Единый портал государственных и муниципальных услуг (Госуслуги) и подайте заявление в районный орган социальной защиты населения или комплексный центр социального обслуживания населения (КЦСОН) для предоставления надомного социального обслуживания и услуг сиделки [1] [2].

steps.title: Оформление информированного добровольного согласия и доступа к врачебной тайне
steps.html:
• Информированное добровольное согласие и отказ от медицинского вмешательства: Согласно статье 20 Федерального закона № 323-ФЗ совершеннолетний дееспособный гражданин имеет право подписать информированное добровольное согласие на медицинское вмешательство либо письменный отказ от определенных видов вмешательства, которые подлежат обязательному приобщению к медицинской карте в учреждении, подведомственном органу - Министерство здравоохранения Российской Федерации [1].
  • Разрешение родственникам на доступ к сведениям, составляющим врачебную тайну: Поскольку статья 13 Федерального закона № 323-ФЗ строго запрещает разглашение врачебной тайны без согласия пациента, болеющему человеку следует прямо указать в письменном информированном добровольном согласии в поликлинике и стационаре фамилии и контактные данные доверенных родственников или представителей, которым разрешено получать сведения о состоянии здоровья, результаты обследований, выписки и рецепты [1].
  • Принятие медицинских решений при утрате способности выражать волю: Российское законодательство не предусматривает отдельного института медицинского представителя по зарубежному образцу, заменяющего судебную опеку при утрате пациентом сознания; в неотложных ситуациях, когда пациент не способен выразить свою волю и не имеет законного представителя, решение о медицинском вмешательстве принимает консилиум врачей или лечащий (дежурный) врач по правилам, которые устанавливает Министерство здравоохранения Российской Федерации, что делает заблаговременные письменные отметки в медицинской карте особенно важными [1].

steps.title: Удостоверение нотариальных доверенностей и банковских распоряжений
steps.html:
• Нотариально удостоверенная генеральная или специальная доверенность: В соответствии со статьями 185 и 185.1 Гражданского кодекса Российской Федерации, пока ваш родственник полностью сохраняет ясность сознания и дееспособность, оформите нотариальную доверенность у нотариуса, чью деятельность объединяет Федеральная нотариальная палата (нормативный надзор осуществляет Министерство юстиции Российской Федерации), уполномочив доверенное лицо управлять имуществом, обращаться в государственные органы и представлять интересы в Социальном фонде России (СФР) и налоговых органах [3] [4] [5].
  • Выезд нотариуса на дом или в стационар: Если по состоянию здоровья болеющий человек не может посетить нотариальную контору, любого нотариуса местного нотариального округа (Федеральная нотариальная палата) можно пригласить на дом, в больницу или хоспис для установления дееспособности и удостоверения доверенности на выезде [5]. Если из-за физической слабости или нарушения моторики гражданин при ясном сознании не может собственноручно расписаться, документ в присутствии нотариуса может подписать рукоприкладчик [5]. При нахождении пациента на стационарном лечении, когда незамедлительный вызов нотариуса затруднен, доверенность на получение пенсий, пособий и корреспонденции также может удостоверить главный врач стационара на основании пункта 3 статьи 185.1 Гражданского кодекса РФ [1] [5].
  • Банковские доверенности: Зарегистрируйте нотариальную доверенность или оформите внутрибанковскую доверенность непосредственно в российских коммерческих банках, чтобы уполномоченный представитель мог без перебоев оплачивать счета, распоряжаться вкладами и получать денежные средства [5].

steps.title: Оформление инвалидности (МСЭ), социальных выплат и поддержки ухаживающих лиц
steps.html:
• Медико-социальная экспертиза (МСЭ): Обратитесь в поликлинику для формирования электронного направления по форме № 088/у в бюро медико-социальной экспертизы (МСЭ) с целью установления I, II или III группы инвалидности и разработки индивидуальной программы реабилитации или абилитации инвалида (ИПРА), дающей право на бесплатное получение технических средств реабилитации (ТСР), функциональных кроватей и средств ухода через Социальный фонд России (СФР) [1] [4].
  • Пенсия по инвалидности и ежемесячная денежная выплата (ЕДВ): После внесения сведений об инвалидности в Федеральный реестр инвалидов подайте заявление через Единый портал государственных и муниципальных услуг (Госуслуги) или клиентскую службу Социального фонда России (СФР) для назначения страховой или социальной пенсии по инвалидности и ежемесячной денежной выплаты (ЕДВ), включающей набор социальных услуг (НСУ) с бесплатным лекарственным обеспечением по рецептам [2] [4].
  • Выплаты по уходу и трудовые гарантии для родственников: В соответствии с правилами, которые применяет Социальный фонд России (СФР), за уход за инвалидом I группы начисляются установленные законом выплаты к пенсии и пенсионные коэффициенты (1,8 пенсионного коэффициента за каждый полный год ухода), а работающие родственники вправе оформить отпуск без сохранения заработной платы продолжительностью до 14 календарных дней в году (или более по коллективному договору) либо режим неполного рабочего времени на основании статей 93 и 128 Трудового кодекса РФ [2] [4].

steps.title: Проверка завещания, документов ЗАГС и документов на имущество
steps.html:
• Нотариальное удостоверение завещания: Согласно главе 62 Гражданского кодекса Российской Федерации действительное завещание должно быть совершено лично и удостоверено нотариусом, входящим в структуру - Федеральная нотариальная палата (либо в исключительных случаях в стационаре - главным или дежурным врачом больницы с обязательной последующей передачей нотариусу), при условии полной дееспособности завещателя [5]. Российские нотариусы также предлагают видеофиксацию процедуры удостоверения завещания для защиты воли завещателя от возможного оспаривания по статье 177 Гражданского кодекса РФ [5].
  • Право на обязательную долю в наследстве: При составлении завещания у нотариуса (Федеральная нотариальная палата) учитывайте положения статьи 1149 Гражданского кодекса РФ, согласно которой несовершеннолетние или нетрудоспособные (пенсионного возраста либо с инвалидностью) дети, супруг и родители завещателя наследуют независимо от содержания завещания не менее половины доли, которая причиталась бы каждому из них при наследовании по закону [5].
  • Проверка регистрации недвижимости и трансграничных документов: Проверьте актуальность записей о праве собственности на недвижимость в Едином государственном реестре недвижимости (ЕГРН / Росреестр) через Единый портал государственных и муниципальных услуг (Госуслуги), а если доверенности или свидетельства ЗАГС потребуются за рубежом, оформите апостиль через Министерство юстиции Российской Федерации или нотариальные действия через Консульский департамент Министерства иностранных дел Российской Федерации [2] [3] [6].

ru.closingQuestion: Чтобы мы могли точнее адаптировать эти шаги, уточните, пожалуйста, в каком городе или субъекте Российской Федерации ваш родственник получает лечение, требуется ли организация выезда нотариуса на дом или в больницу и находятся ли кто-либо из членов семьи или активы за пределами России?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Antigua and Barbuda: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Antigua and Barbuda: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Antigua and Barbuda: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Antigua and Barbuda. Below, we outline the five main official and practical steps to follow in order, from medical death certification and civil registration to funeral or repatriation arrangements, social security benefit claims, and High Court probate.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or inpatient death: When a death occurs at Sir Lester Bird Medical Centre (formerly Mount St. John's Medical Centre) or a private clinic in Antigua and Barbuda, the attending medical practitioner issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death required under the statutory framework published by the Ministry of Legal Affairs, Public Safety and Labour of Antigua and Barbuda [1] [3].
  • Death at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home, notify the Royal Police Force of Antigua and Barbuda and the deceased's attending physician or district medical officer immediately [1] [3]. Where the person was under recent medical care for a diagnosed natural illness, the physician examines the deceased and issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [3].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained death: Where a death occurs suddenly, by accident, or without recent medical attendance, the police report the case to the Coroner's Office for a post-mortem examination (autopsy) by a government pathologist before the Coroner issues the certificate and burial or release order [1] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: Civil registration of deaths in Antigua and Barbuda is administered by the Civil Registry at the Registrar General's Department on High Street, St. John's, operating under the Government of Antigua and Barbuda and the Civil Registration and Vital Statistics framework published by the Ministry of Legal Affairs, Public Safety and Labour of Antigua and Barbuda [1] [2] [3]. For deaths occurring on Barbuda, initial reporting may also be coordinated through the local island administration [1] [2].
  • Statutory deadline and informant duties: Under the Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Act, a death occurring in Antigua and Barbuda must be reported promptly to the Registrar (statutorily within five days of the death or the Coroner's finding), either by a surviving relative, a person present at the death, or an authorized funeral director via the Civil Registry Information System [1] [2] [3].
  • Required documents and certified extracts: Submit the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's Certificate), the deceased's passport or national identification card, and the informant's valid photo identification to the Civil Registry under the Government of Antigua and Barbuda to obtain the burial permit and official certified copies of the death certificate [1] [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Appoint a licensed funeral home in Antigua and Barbuda to transfer your family member's remains, obtain the Registrar's burial order (or Coroner's cremation clearance), and schedule interment at a public or parish cemetery [1] [3]. Clarvia does not endorse or rank commercial funeral directors.
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: If your family member's remains or cremated ashes must be repatriated abroad, the licensed funeral director coordinates an embalming certificate, a public health certificate of non-infectious disease from the Chief Medical Officer under the Government of Antigua and Barbuda, a hermetically sealed zinc-lined casket (for uncremated remains), and customs export clearance through V.C. Bird International Airport [2] [3].
  • Apostille legalization for foreign use: Because Antigua and Barbuda is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, any official death certificate or probate document needed in another Convention country should be legalized with a Hague Apostille issued by the Registrar of the High Court under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court [3] [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Institutions
steps.html:
• Social Security Funeral Grant: Under the Social Security Act, the person who has paid or assumed responsibility for the funeral expenses of an eligible insured contributor or pensioner may claim the statutory Funeral Grant (a lump-sum payment of 2,500 XCD) from the Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board by submitting the Funeral Grant claim form, the official death certificate, and itemized funeral receipts [4].
  • Survivor's Pension or Grant: Eligible surviving spouses (widows or widowers), dependent children under age 16 (or up to age 18/21 if in full-time education), or dependent parents of a deceased insured person may apply to the Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board for a monthly Survivor's Pension or lump-sum Survivor's Grant [5]. Claims should be filed within three months of death to prevent loss of retroactive benefit payments [5].
  • Medical Benefits Scheme, banks, and Inland Revenue: Present certified copies of the death certificate to the Medical Benefits Scheme, the Inland Revenue Department, the Electoral Commission, and local commercial banks in Antigua and Barbuda to cancel identification cards, settle final tax obligations, and freeze sole bank accounts pending probate [2] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and High Court Probate
steps.html:
• Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration: Under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules 2017, an executor named in a valid will must apply to the Probate Registry of the High Court of Justice (Antigua and Barbuda Circuit of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court) for a Grant of Probate, whereas if the deceased died intestate (without a will), the next of kin applies for Letters of Administration [6].
  • Filing requirements and newspaper notice: Through an attorney-at-law admitted in Antigua and Barbuda, file the application, the original will (if any), the official death certificate, an oath of the executor or administrator, a declaration of the value of the estate, and proof of publication of the statutory notice to creditors and claimants in the Official Gazette and a local newspaper as required by the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court [6].
  • Stamp duty and cross-border estate resealing: Antigua and Barbuda does not levy an inheritance or estate tax, though statutory court filing fees and stamp duties apply when transferring real property or registering estate instruments [1] [6]. If a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration was already issued by a court in the United Kingdom or another Commonwealth jurisdiction, an application may be made to the High Court of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court to reseal the foreign grant in Antigua and Barbuda, or via a notarized, apostilled Power of Attorney if the executor resides abroad [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Antigua and Barbuda: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Antigua and Barbuda: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Antigua and Barbuda: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Antigua and Barbuda is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person retains full mental and legal capacity ensures that their wishes and household stability are protected. Below, we set out the five key steps to complete in order under the laws of Antigua and Barbuda.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Medical Benefits Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and specialist oncology care: Coordinate inpatient and outpatient symptom management, pain relief, and palliative support through Sir Lester Bird Medical Centre (formerly Mount St. John's Medical Centre), the Cancer Centre Eastern Caribbean, and community health clinics operating under the Ministry of Health, Wellness, Social Transformation and the Environment of the Government of Antigua and Barbuda [1].
  • Medical Benefits Scheme (MBS) registration: Ensure the ill person is actively registered with the Medical Benefits Scheme under the Government of Antigua and Barbuda, which provides financial assistance, prescription medication coverage at MBS pharmacies, and specialist support for qualifying chronic and life-limiting conditions including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes [1] [2].
  • Home nursing and community care: Request a discharge or outpatient care plan from the attending physician at Sir Lester Bird Medical Centre to coordinate district public health nurse visits, home-based nursing support, and medical equipment in Antigua or Barbuda [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Authorize Healthcare Communication
steps.html:
• Documenting informed consent and treatment preferences: Under common-law medical consent principles applied in Antigua and Barbuda, a patient with full mental capacity has the right to consent to or refuse specific medical treatments (including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or artificial nutrition) and to have those written directives entered directly into their clinical file at Sir Lester Bird Medical Centre or their private clinic under the Government of Antigua and Barbuda [1].
  • Appointing a designated medical contact and representative: Because Antigua and Barbuda does not have a standalone statutory Living Will Registry, the ill person should sign a written medical authorization at the treating hospital and clinic naming one or more trusted family members who may receive confidential medical records, attend specialist consultations, and communicate treatment preferences to the care team if the patient becomes unable to speak for themselves [1] [4].
  • Sharing signed copies with physicians and family: Provide signed, witnessed copies of the written care preferences to the attending physician, the primary family caregiver, and the person's attorney-at-law so that all parties have immediate access during medical emergencies [1] [4].

steps.title: Execute Valid Powers of Attorney and Banking Mandates
steps.html:
• Drafting and executing a Power of Attorney: While your family member retains full mental and legal capacity, instruct an attorney-at-law in Antigua and Barbuda to prepare a formal Power of Attorney under the laws published by the Ministry of Legal Affairs, Public Safety and Labour of Antigua and Barbuda, authorizing a trusted attorney-in-fact to manage bank accounts, real property, utilities, and legal filings [4] [5].
  • Notarization and High Court / Land Registry recording: A Power of Attorney intended for property transactions, land dealings, or legal representation before the High Court of Justice under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court must be executed as a deed in the presence of witnesses (or before a Notary Public) and registered at the High Court Registry and the Land Registry in St. John's [4] [5].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates: Because local commercial banks in Antigua and Barbuda often require their own internal account mandate forms or certified copies of a registered Power of Attorney, visit or contact each bank while capacity is intact to verify signature specimens and ensure uninterrupted access to funds for medical and household expenses [1] [5].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Social Security Sickness Benefit: If the ill person is under pensionable age (65) and experiences short-term loss of earnings due to certified medical incapacity, file a Sickness Benefit claim (accompanied by a medical certificate from the attending physician) with the Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board within the statutory filing window (starting from the fourth day of continuous incapacity for up to 26 weeks) [2] [3].
  • Social Security Invalidity Pension or Grant: If the illness results in permanent or long-term inability to work after Sickness Benefit is exhausted (typically after at least six months of continuous incapacity), apply to the Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board under the Social Security Act (Cap. 408) for an Invalidity Pension (where at least 150 to 250 weekly contributions have been paid) or a lump-sum Invalidity Grant [2] [3].
  • Representative payee and workplace leave arrangements: If the ill person cannot attend the Antigua and Barbuda Social Security Board offices in person, complete an agency authorization so a designated representative can collect benefit payments, and review the Antigua and Barbuda Labour Code with employers regarding certified sick leave and family caregiving arrangements [2] [3] [4].

steps.title: Review and Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a valid will under the Wills Act (Cap. 473): Under Section 7 of the Wills Act (Cap. 473) published by the Ministry of Legal Affairs, Public Safety and Labour of Antigua and Barbuda, a will is valid only if it is in writing and signed at the foot or end thereof by the testator (or by another person in the testator's presence and by their direction) in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent witnesses, who must attest and subscribe the will in the presence of the testator [4]. Ensure that neither a beneficiary nor the spouse of a beneficiary acts as an attesting witness, as doing so voids any gift to that beneficiary under Section 13 of the Wills Act [4].
  • Organizing civil registry and land title records: Assemble originals or certified copies of birth and marriage certificates from the Civil Registry under the Government of Antigua and Barbuda, Land Registry certificates of title (by Parish, Registration Section, Block, and Parcel number), insurance policies, and bank account statements so the appointed executor can later comply with the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules 2017 [1] [4] [5].
  • Cross-border powers of attorney and Apostilles: If family members, executors, or assets are located abroad, arrange for any Power of Attorney or legal instrument executed in Antigua and Barbuda to receive a Hague Apostille from the Registrar of the High Court under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court, or ensure foreign powers of attorney are apostilled in their country of origin for recognition in Antigua and Barbuda [4] [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bahamas: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bahamas: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Bahamas: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in The Bahamas. Navigating the medical, civil, funeral, financial, and probate procedures across New Providence, Grand Bahama, or the Family Islands requires following a clear legal sequence. Below, we outline the five essential official and practical steps to manage these affairs under Bahamian law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a hospital or medical facility such as Princess Margaret Hospital in Nassau or Rand Memorial Hospital in Freeport, the attending physician issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1]. This signed medical certificate is the mandatory foundational record required before civil registration or burial arrangements can proceed [1].
  • Deaths at home under medical care: If your family member died at home from natural causes while under active medical care, contact the attending physician or nearest community health clinic immediately so the doctor can examine the deceased and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or non-natural deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, without recent medical attendance, or under accidental or suspicious circumstances, notify the Royal Bahamas Police Force immediately [2]. The case is referred to H.M. Coroner under the Coroners Act, and the body is transferred to the hospital morgue for a forensic post-mortem examination before the Coroner issues the certificate permitting registration and burial [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Registrar General's Department
steps.html:
• Where to register: Every death occurring in The Bahamas must be officially recorded with the Registrar General's Department in Nassau or Freeport, or with the local Family Island Administrator's Office if the death occurred on a Family Island [1] [2].
  • Submission of the medical certificate: In practice, the licensed funeral director or mortician appointed by the family submits the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death to the Death Registry section of the Registrar General's Department, though a qualified informant or next of kin may also complete the registration directly [1] [2].
  • Obtaining official death certificates: Once the Registrar enters the particulars into the official death register, you can request certified copies of the Death Certificate either in person at the Registrar General's Department or online through the Bahamas Government MyGateway portal [2] [3]. The statutory government fee is BSD 10.00 per certified copy, and it is advisable to order at least five to eight certified copies for banks, insurance claims, and court filings [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Appointing a licensed funeral home: Engage a licensed Bahamian mortician or funeral home early, as mortuary facilities, burial permits, and cemetery scheduling in New Providence and the Family Islands are coordinated through registered funeral providers [1] [2].
  • Burial and cremation permits: No interment or cremation may take place until the medical cause of death has been certified, the Coroner has granted clearance where required, and the civil registration authority has issued the official burial or cremation permit [1] [2].
  • International repatriation and Apostille authentication: If your family member was a foreign national or if their remains or cremated ashes must be repatriated abroad, the funeral home coordinates embalming certificates, a hermetically sealed casket certificate for air transit, and public health clearance [1]. Because The Bahamas is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, certified death certificates issued by the Registrar General's Department can be authenticated with an Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for legal recognition abroad [3].

steps.title: Notify the National Insurance Board, Banks, and Authorities
steps.html:
• National Insurance Funeral Benefit: If the deceased was an insured contributor under the social security scheme, the person who paid or is responsible for paying the funeral bill can apply to the National Insurance Board of The Bahamas for the lump-sum Funeral Benefit using Form B.51 [4] [5]. You must submit the certified Death Certificate, itemized funeral receipts or invoices, and valid identification [4] [5].
  • National Insurance Survivors Benefit: Surviving dependents of an insured contributor who paid at least 150 contributions may claim a monthly Survivors Benefit from the National Insurance Board of The Bahamas using Form B.56 [4] [5]. Statutory priority applies to the widow or widower, dependent children under age 16 (or under age 21 if in full-time education), qualifying orphans, and dependent parents [4].
  • Identity, tax, and financial notifications: Surrender the deceased's Bahamian passport and driver's license to the relevant issuing authorities, notify commercial banks and life insurers to freeze sole accounts and process policy payouts, and check whether any real property tax updates are required with the Department of Inland Revenue [3] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain a Grant of Representation
steps.html:
• Supreme Court Probate Division jurisdiction: Estate administration in The Bahamas is governed by the Probate and Administration of Estates Act and overseen by the Probate Registry of the Supreme Court of The Bahamas in Nassau (along with sub-registries in Freeport and the Family Islands) [6].
  • Grant of Probate vs. Letters of Administration: If the deceased left a valid will, the named executor applies to the Supreme Court of The Bahamas for a Grant of Probate [6]. If the deceased died intestate (without a will), the next of kin applies for Letters of Administration under the Inheritance Act [6]. Notice of the intended application must be advertised in the official Gazette and local newspapers before the grant is issued [6].
  • Zero inheritance tax and cross-border resealing: The Bahamas does not levy a general inheritance tax or estate duty on personal estates, though court probate fees and property transfer taxes or stamp duties may apply to real estate conveyances [6]. If the deceased held a foreign grant of probate from another Commonwealth jurisdiction or the United Kingdom or United States, the Supreme Court of The Bahamas can reseal or recognize foreign grants to release Bahamian bank accounts and real property [6].

cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Bahamas: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in The Bahamas is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, taking early medical, legal, and financial steps while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their autonomy and prevents court delays. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to coordinate care, legal mandates, benefits, and estate documents in The Bahamas.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and tertiary clinical care: Coordinate symptom management, oncology support, and palliative care referrals through the Public Hospitals Authority network, including Princess Margaret Hospital in New Providence, Rand Memorial Hospital in Grand Bahama, or local Family Island community clinics, as well as the National Health Insurance Authority where applicable [1].
  • Home nursing and support services: Request written care plans, prescription schedules, and medical summaries from the treating specialist so community health nurses or private home-care providers can manage pain relief and comfort care at home [1].
  • Private health insurance and catastrophic coverage: If your family member holds a private individual or group medical insurance policy, contact the insurer early to confirm pre-authorization rules for home nursing, palliative medications, durable medical equipment, and inpatient hospice or specialist care [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment preferences: While The Bahamas follows English common law principles rather than a single standalone living will statute, an adult with full mental capacity may execute a written advance medical directive stating their wishes regarding life-sustaining interventions, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, artificial nutrition, and pain management [1] [4].
  • Appointing a medical spokesperson: Your family member should clearly designate a trusted relative or representative in writing to communicate with attending physicians and hospital teams if they become unable to express medical decisions directly [1].
  • Clinical and family accessibility: Provide signed copies of the written medical preferences and representative contact details to the primary physician, the hospital medical records department, and close relatives so clinical teams have immediate access during an emergency [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Powers of Attorney Act requirements: Under Bahamian law, a Power of Attorney must be executed while the donor still possesses full mental and legal capacity [4]. Standard general powers of attorney cease to be effective if the donor subsequently loses mental capacity unless structured in accordance with statutory enduring or security provisions recognized under Bahamian law [4].
  • Execution and registration with the Registrar General's Department: To be legally effective for real property transactions and formal legal dealings in The Bahamas, a Power of Attorney should be drafted by a Bahamian Counsel and Attorney, executed as a deed in the presence of witnesses, and lodged for recording with the Deeds and Documents section of the Registrar General's Department [1] [4].
  • Bank mandates and joint account access: Because commercial banks in The Bahamas enforce strict verification protocols, visit each bank while your family member has capacity to complete the bank's own third-party mandate forms or account signing authorities so household bills and medical costs can be paid without interruption [1].

steps.title: Activate National Insurance Sickness and Invalidity Benefits
steps.html:
• Short-term Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an insured contributor under age 65 who becomes temporarily unable to work due to illness, they can apply to the National Insurance Board of The Bahamas for a weekly Sickness Benefit, supported by medical certificates issued by their attending physician [2] [3].
  • Long-term Invalidity Benefit: If the condition permanently prevents your family member from engaging in gainful employment before age 65 and they satisfy the minimum contribution requirements (at least 150 paid contributions), they can apply to the National Insurance Board of The Bahamas for a monthly Invalidity Benefit using the official claim form and medical assessment report [2] [3] [5].
  • Authorized payment collection and workplace leave: If your family member is physically unable to visit a local office or bank, the National Insurance Board of The Bahamas permits an authorized agent or representative to collect or manage benefit filings using prescribed authorization forms, while employed caregivers should review family or medical leave arrangements with their employer [3] [5].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Beneficiary Designations, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Reviewing or drafting a Bahamian Will: Under the Wills Act of The Bahamas, a valid will must be in writing and signed by the testator in the presence of two independent witnesses who are present at the same time and who do not benefit under the will [6]. Preparing a clear, properly witnessed will ensures smooth administration before the Probate Division of the Supreme Court of The Bahamas [6].
  • Life insurance, pensions, and property deeds: Review beneficiary designations on life insurance policies and occupational pension plans, and gather original real property conveyances, share certificates, and real property tax assessment numbers in a secure folder [1] [6].
  • Vital records and cross-border coordination: Verify that certified copies of birth and marriage certificates are up to date through the Registrar General's Department or the MyGateway portal [1] [4]. If your family member owns assets outside The Bahamas, coordinate with legal counsel in each jurisdiction so the Bahamian will and foreign estate instruments do not inadvertently revoke one another [6].

cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Barbados: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Barbados. Dealing with medical certification, civil registration, funeral arrangements, social security claims, and estate administration across the parishes of Barbados follows a structured legal sequence. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to guide your family through the process.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Bridgetown, a district hospital, or a private clinic, the attending physician completes and signs the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and the Notice of Death [1] [2].
  • Expected deaths at home: If your family member died at home from natural causes while under regular medical care, contact the attending physician immediately so they can examine the body and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [2].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or unnatural deaths: If the deceased was not attended by a physician during their final illness, or if the death was sudden, accidental, or unnatural, notify the Barbados Police Service immediately [1]. The matter is referred to the Coroner under the Coroners Act for an inquiry and post-mortem examination before a Coroner's certificate is issued to authorize registration and burial [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Registration Department
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and registry offices: Under the Vital Statistics Registration Act of Barbados, every death must be registered within five days of its occurrence [1] [2]. Deaths occurring in District A (St. Michael) are registered at the Registration Department located in the Supreme Court Complex on White Park Road in St. Michael, while deaths in outer parishes may be registered at the respective District Registration Office [1] [2].
  • Filing the registration: In most cases, the licensed funeral director appointed by the family presents the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, the Notice of Death, and the deceased's Barbados National Identification Card or passport to the Registrar to record the death and obtain the burial order [1] [2].
  • Ordering official death certificates: Once the death is entered into the register, you can apply to the Registration Department for certified copies of the Death Certificate [1] [2]. The official fee is BDS 5.00 per copy (or BDS 1.00 for pensioners), and it is advisable to obtain five to eight certified copies for banks, insurance companies, and court probate filings [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Appointing a licensed funeral director: Select a licensed Barbadian funeral home to coordinate mortuary care, civil registration, and interment at a public or parish cemetery or cremation at a licensed crematorium [1] [2].
  • Burial and cremation permits: No burial or cremation may proceed in Barbados without the official certificate of registration issued by the Registration Department (or the Coroner's order for burial where an inquest is pending) [1]. Cremations require additional medical and statutory declarations to confirm that no further forensic examination is needed [1].
  • International repatriation and Apostille certification: If the deceased was a foreign national or if their remains or cremated ashes are to be transported abroad, the funeral home coordinates embalming certification, a hermetically sealed shipping casket, and port health clearance from the Ministry of Health and Wellness [1] [2]. Because Barbados is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, certified death certificates can receive an Apostille through the Registration Department or Ministry of Foreign Affairs for international legal use [1] [2].

steps.title: Claim National Insurance Benefits and Notify Institutions
steps.html:
• National Insurance Funeral Grant: If the deceased or their spouse was an insured contributor who met the statutory contribution requirements, the person who paid or is legally liable to pay the funeral expenses can claim the flat-rate Funeral Grant of BDS 2,220 from the National Insurance and Social Security Service [3]. You must file the Funeral Grant claim form within one year of the death, enclosing the certified Death Certificate, original itemized funeral receipt or invoice, the claimant's National ID card, and the deceased's national insurance number [3].
  • Survivors' Grant and Pension: A surviving spouse (married or qualifying common-law spouse who cohabited for at least five years) and dependent children under age 16 (or up to age 25 if in full-time education, or invalid children of any age) may claim a Survivors' Benefit from the National Insurance and Social Security Service if the deceased qualified for an invalidity or old-age contributory pension [4].
  • Tax, identity, and banking notifications: Notify the Electoral and Boundaries Commission to cancel the National Identification Card, return the deceased's passport to the Barbados Immigration Department, inform the Barbados Revenue Authority regarding final income or land tax obligations, and present certified death certificates to local banks and credit unions [2] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate through the Supreme Court Probate Unit
steps.html:
• Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration: To administer bank accounts, shares, or real property in Barbados, the personal representative must apply to the Supreme Court Registry Probate Unit at the Supreme Court Complex on White Park Road [5]. If the deceased left a valid will, the executor applies for a Grant of Probate; if the deceased died intestate, the next of kin applies for Letters of Administration under the Succession Act [5].
  • Public notice and court fees: Before filing the application with the Supreme Court Registry Probate Unit, notice of intention to apply for a grant must be published in the Official Gazette and a local newspaper to allow creditors or interested parties to respond [5]. Probate registry fees are calculated on a sliding scale based on the net value of the estate under the Supreme Court (Non-Contentious) Probate Rules [5].
  • No inheritance tax and foreign grant resealing: Barbados does not levy an inheritance tax or estate duty, though property transfer taxes and stamp duties apply when transferring real estate [5]. If the deceased lived abroad and a grant of probate was already issued in another Commonwealth country, the United Kingdom, or a recognized jurisdiction, the Supreme Court Registry Probate Unit can reseal the foreign grant so Barbadian assets can be transferred [5].

titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Barbados: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Barbados: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Barbados is diagnosed with a serious or life-limiting illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity ensures their wishes are respected and avoids administrative delays. Below, we outline the five key official and practical steps to manage care, powers of attorney, social security support, and estate preparation in Barbados.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public healthcare and polyclinic referrals: Coordinate specialist oncology, symptom relief, and community nursing support through the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Bridgetown and the parish polyclinics operated under the Ministry of Health and Wellness [1]. Polyclinic district nursing services and the Barbados Drug Service formulary assist residents with ongoing pain management and chronic care medications [1].
  • Community palliative and home-care coordination: Ask the attending specialist at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital or private clinic for a comprehensive written medical summary, medication schedule, and home-care plan so family caregivers and community nurses can manage symptoms safely at home [1].
  • Private medical insurance review: If your family member holds private health or critical-illness insurance, contact the insurer early to verify coverage limits and pre-authorization procedures for home nursing, medical equipment, and specialist consultations [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Proxy
steps.html:
• Written advance medical statement: Under Barbadian common law principles, an adult with full mental capacity may record their healthcare preferences in writing, setting out their instructions regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial hydration, and comfort-focused palliative care [1] [4].
  • Naming a healthcare spokesperson: Your family member should designate a trusted relative or representative in writing who can communicate with attending doctors at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital or private clinics if your family member becomes unable to speak for themselves [1].
  • Sharing copies with clinical teams: Provide signed copies of the written care preferences and emergency contact hierarchy to the primary physician, hospital medical records unit, and immediate relatives so medical staff can consult them promptly when clinical decisions arise [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Property Act and Powers of Attorney requirements: In Barbados, a Power of Attorney must be executed while the donor possesses full mental capacity to understand the nature and effect of the instrument [4]. To authorize an attorney-in-fact to manage real estate, legal affairs, and financial assets, the Power of Attorney must be executed as a deed in the presence of an attorney-at-law or notary public and qualified witnesses [4].
  • Recording with the Registration Department: To be legally valid for real property transactions and accepted by public authorities and financial institutions across Barbados, the executed Power of Attorney must be stamped and recorded with the Registration Department at the Supreme Court Complex on White Park Road [4].
  • Commercial bank and credit union mandates: Barbadian commercial banks and credit unions often require their own internal account mandate forms or joint-signing verifications in addition to a registered Power of Attorney; complete these directly with each financial institution while your family member is able to attend or sign [4].

steps.title: Activate National Insurance Sickness and Invalidity Benefits
steps.html:
• Short-term Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an employed or self-employed insured contributor under pensionable age who becomes incapable of work due to illness, they can apply to the National Insurance and Social Security Service for a Sickness Benefit [2] [3]. Claims must be supported by an official medical certificate signed by a registered medical practitioner and submitted within the statutory timeframe [2].
  • Long-term Invalidity Benefit: If your family member has been medically certified as permanently incapable of work due to a chronic or life-limiting illness after exhausting sickness benefit entitlement and has paid at least 150 contributions, they can apply to the National Insurance and Social Security Service for an Invalidity Pension (or a lump-sum Invalidity Grant if they have between 50 and 149 contributions) [3].
  • Authorized collection and caregiver arrangements: Where illness prevents the claimant from transacting business in person, the National Insurance and Social Security Service allows an appointed agent to submit claims or receive payments on the insured person's behalf upon filing the required medical and authorization forms [2] [3].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Executing or updating a Will under the Succession Act: Under the Succession Act of Barbados, a valid will must be in writing and signed by the testator in the presence of at least two independent witnesses present at the same time [5]. Because the Succession Act also provides statutory legal rights to a surviving spouse and dependent children, reviewing the will with a Barbadian attorney-at-law ensures smooth administration through the Supreme Court Registry Probate Unit [5].
  • Beneficiary nominations and credit union shares: Review beneficiary nominations on life insurance policies, occupational pensions, and Barbadian credit union accounts (where statutory nomination forms allow designated funds to pass directly to nominees) [3] [5].
  • Vital records and cross-border property: Gather original title deeds, land tax bills, and certified birth and marriage certificates from the Registration Department [4] [5]. If your family member holds assets or bank accounts outside Barbados, ensure any foreign powers of attorney or wills are coordinated and authenticated with an Apostille where required [4] [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Belize: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Belize: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Belize: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Belize. Managing the medical certification, civil registration, funeral or repatriation permits, social security claims, and estate probate across Belize's districts follows specific statutory rules and deadlines. Below, we outline the five key official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital in Belize City, a regional public hospital, or a private clinic, the attending registered medical practitioner issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1].
  • Expected deaths at home: If your family member died at home from natural causes while under the care of a registered physician, notify the doctor immediately so they can examine the deceased and sign the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or non-natural deaths: If the death occurred suddenly, without recent medical attendance, or under accidental or unnatural circumstances, notify the Belize Police Department immediately [1] [2]. The case is referred to the Coroner and the National Forensic Science Service for a post-mortem examination, after which the Coroner issues the official certificate authorizing death registration and burial [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Vital Statistics Unit
steps.html:
• Statutory registration requirement: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act of Belize, every death must be registered with the Vital Statistics Unit under the Attorney General's Ministry in Belize City or at the corresponding District Registry Office (in Belmopan, Corozal, Orange Walk, Cayo, Stann Creek, or Toledo) within the statutory period of five days [1] [2].
  • Filing the death registration: A qualified informant (such as an adult relative present at the death, the occupier of the premises, or the person arranging the funeral) presents the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, the deceased's Belize Social Security Card or passport, and the informant's own valid identification to the Vital Statistics Unit [1] [2].
  • Obtaining official death certificates: Once the Registrar records the entry in the civil register, apply to the Vital Statistics Unit for multiple certified copies of the Original Death Certificate [1] [2]. Certified copies are required in original form by the Belize Social Security Board, commercial banks, and the High Court General Registry [1] [3] [5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral provider: Appoint a licensed funeral home in Belize to handle mortuary preparation, transportation of remains, and coordination with municipal or village cemetery authorities [1].
  • Burial and cremation permits: No interment or cremation may take place until the death has been certified and registered (or cleared by the Coroner) and the burial or cremation permit has been issued by the registrar or municipal authority [1] [2].
  • International repatriation and Apostille authentication: If your family member was a foreign citizen or if their body or cremated remains must be transported outside Belize, the funeral home coordinates embalming certification, a hermetically sealed casket for international air cargo, and an export permit from the Ministry of Health and Wellness [1] [2]. Because Belize is a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Death Certificates issued by the Vital Statistics Unit can be authenticated with an Apostille through the Attorney General's Ministry or Ministry of Foreign Affairs for legal recognition abroad [1] [2].

steps.title: Claim Belize Social Security Board Benefits and Notify Institutions
steps.html:
• Social Security Funeral Grant (Form FG.1): If the deceased was an insured contributor (or the spouse or dependent child of an insured contributor), the person who paid or is responsible for paying the funeral expenses can claim a lump-sum Funeral Grant from the Belize Social Security Board using Form FG.1 [3]. You must submit the Original Death Certificate from the Vital Statistics Unit, original funeral receipts or invoices in the claimant's name, and the deceased's Social Security Card within six months of the date of death (claims filed after 12 months are forfeited) [3].
  • Survivors' Benefit (Form SVB1): A surviving widow or widower (including a qualifying common-law spouse), dependent children under age 18 (or up to age 21 if in full-time education), or dependent parents may apply to the Belize Social Security Board for a monthly Survivors' Pension or Grant using Form SVB1 [4]. Claims should be filed within 13 weeks of the date of death along with original birth, death, and marriage certificates or common-law declarations [4].
  • Tax, land, and banking notifications: Notify commercial banks and credit unions in Belize to freeze sole accounts and process designated beneficiary payouts, inform the Belize Tax Service Department regarding any final tax obligations, and surrender the deceased's passport to the Department of Nationality and Passports [1] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate through the Belize Judiciary General Registry
steps.html:
• Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration: Under the Administration of Estates Act of Belize, transferring bank accounts, shares, or land registered in the deceased's sole name requires a court grant from the Probate Section of the General Registry of the Belize Judiciary (High Court of Belize) [5]. If the deceased left a valid will, the executor applies for a Grant of Probate; if there is no will, the rightful heirs apply for Letters of Administration [5].
  • Gazette notices and estate valuation: The application to the General Registry of the Belize Judiciary requires filing the original Death Certificate, an inventory and valuation of the estate, and statutory notices published in the Government Gazette and a local newspaper to invite any creditor claims or caveats [5].
  • Estate duty abolition and cross-border resealing: Belize has abolished estate duty on estates of persons dying after the statutory abolition threshold, though court filing fees and land transfer stamp duties apply when transferring real property titles at the Lands and Surveys Department [5]. If a foreign grant of probate was issued in another Commonwealth jurisdiction, the United Kingdom, or a recognized court abroad, the High Court of the Belize Judiciary can reseal the foreign grant to administer Belizean assets [5].

cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Belize: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Belize is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, organizing medical care, legal representation, social security benefits, and estate documents while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents legal complications. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to take in Belize.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public hospitals and National Health Insurance clinics: Coordinate specialist medical evaluations, pain management, and ongoing clinical care through Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital in Belize City, regional public hospitals across the districts, and primary care clinics participating in the National Health Insurance scheme administered alongside the Belize Social Security Board [1] [2].
  • Home-based care and symptom management: Obtain a detailed written treatment summary and prescription regimen from the attending physician so community nurses, non-governmental palliative care teams, and family caregivers can manage comfort care and medications at home [1].
  • Private medical and critical-illness insurance: If your family member is covered under a private individual or employer group health insurance policy, contact the insurer early to confirm coverage and pre-authorization requirements for specialist care, home nursing, and medical equipment [1].

steps.title: Document Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Written advance medical statement: Under Belizean common law principles, an adult with full mental capacity may record a written statement of their medical preferences regarding life-sustaining treatments, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, artificial nutrition, and palliative comfort measures [3] [4].
  • Designating a medical spokesperson: Your family member should clearly name a trusted relative or representative in writing who can communicate with attending doctors and hospital teams if your family member becomes unable to make or communicate healthcare decisions directly [3] [4].
  • Providing copies to physicians and family: Keep signed copies of the medical preference statement and emergency contact details with the treating doctor, the hospital medical records office, and close family members so clinical staff can consult them immediately when needed [3].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Power of Attorney execution and recording: In Belize, a Power of Attorney must be signed while the donor has full mental and legal capacity [3] [5]. For an attorney-in-fact to manage land, legal filings, and property affairs across Belize, the Power of Attorney must be executed as a deed before a Justice of the Peace, Notary Public, or Attorney-at-Law and recorded at the Deeds Registry within the General Registry of the Belize Judiciary (or registered at the Lands and Surveys Department for registered land parcels) [3] [5].
  • Enduring capacity considerations: Because a standard general power of attorney under common law may be affected if the donor subsequently loses mental capacity, consult a Belizean Attorney-at-Law promptly while your family member has full capacity to structure appropriate property, trust, or mandate arrangements [5].
  • Commercial bank and credit union mandates: Commercial banks and credit unions in Belize enforce strict anti-money-laundering and signatory verification rules; visit each institution while your family member is able to complete the bank's specific third-party authorization or joint signatory forms [3] [5].

steps.title: Activate Belize Social Security Board Sickness and Invalidity Benefits
steps.html:
• Short-term Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an insured contributor under age 65 who becomes temporarily incapable of work due to illness, they can claim a weekly Sickness Benefit from the Belize Social Security Board by submitting an official medical certificate completed by a registered medical practitioner within four days of the incapacity [1].
  • Long-term Invalidity Benefit (Form INV1): If your family member is under age 60, has been medically certified by a Social Security Medical Board as permanently unable to perform any gainful employment due to chronic or serious illness, and meets the statutory contribution thresholds (such as 150 paid contributions since 1981), they can apply to the Belize Social Security Board for a monthly Invalidity Pension or one-time Invalidity Grant using Form INV1 [2]. The claim should be filed within 13 weeks following 26 consecutive weeks of illness [2].
  • Authorized representative filings: If your family member is unable to attend a branch office in person, the Belize Social Security Board allows an authorized family member or agent to submit medical certificates and manage benefit disbursements using prescribed authorization documentation [1] [2].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, and Civil Status Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Will under the Wills Act: Under the Wills Act of Belize, a valid will must be in writing and signed by the testator in the presence of two or more independent witnesses who are present at the same time and who do not benefit under the will [5]. Having a clear, properly witnessed will streamlines future estate administration through the General Registry of the Belize Judiciary [5].
  • Credit union nominations and insurance policies: Review beneficiary designations on life insurance policies, pension accounts, and Belizean credit union accounts (where statutory nomination forms allow designated savings and death benefits to pass directly to named beneficiaries outside probate) [2] [5].
  • Vital records and cross-border assets: Verify that original birth and marriage certificates are accurate and available through the Vital Statistics Unit under the Attorney General's Ministry [3] [4], and organize original land certificates or title deeds in a safe place [5]. If your family member owns assets or resides partly abroad, coordinate with legal counsel so any foreign powers of attorney or wills are properly authenticated with an Apostille [3] [5].

cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Dominica: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Dominica. Below we outline the five official and practical steps required to obtain medical certification, complete civil death registration, arrange funeral or international repatriation services, notify social security and tax institutions, and administer the estate under Dominican law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at the Dominica-China Friendship Hospital in Roseau, the Reginald Fitzroy Armour Hospital in Portsmouth, or a district health facility supervised by the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Social Services, the attending physician examines the body and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [3].
  • Expected deaths at home: If your family member died at home while under active medical care for a diagnosed condition, contact the treating physician or the nearest district medical officer immediately so that a doctor can confirm the death and issue the medical certificate required for civil registration [1] [3].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or accidental deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, without recent medical attendance, or under unnatural circumstances, notify the Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force immediately [2] [3]. Police officers refer the case to the District Coroner, who may order a post-mortem examination before releasing the body and issuing the Coroner's certificate authorizing registration and burial [2].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Where and when to register: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act of Dominica, every death must be reported to the District Registrar for the parish or registration district where the death occurred, or centrally at the Registry Division on Dame Eugenia Charles Boulevard in Roseau [1] [2]. A relative present at the death, an person in attendance during the last illness, or an adult occupier of the premises must register the death within the statutory timeframe prior to interment [1] [2].
  • Required documentation: The informant must present the signed Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's order), the deceased's national identification card, birth certificate, or passport, and valid identification for the informant [1] [2].
  • Ordering certified copies: Once the entry is recorded in the civil register, request multiple certified copies of the Death Certificate through the Registry Division or the Government of Dominica e-Services portal (nominally EC$5.00 per certified extract), as banks, pension bodies, and probate courts require original sealed certificates [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Engage a licensed funeral home in Dominica to coordinate mortuary care and transport [3]. The District Registrar or Coroner issues a Burial Order once the cause of death is certified, which must be presented to the cemetery authority or municipal council before burial can take place [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's remains must be transported abroad, the licensed funeral director coordinates with the Environmental Health Department under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Social Services to obtain an official embalming certificate, a non-contagious disease certificate, a hermetically sealed casket inspection certificate, and a burial transit or export permit [3].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Dominica is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. If certified Death Certificates or mortuary documents must be used in another convention country, have them authenticated with an Apostille through the Ministry of National Security and Legal Affairs or the Registry Division, and notify the relevant foreign embassy or consulate if the deceased held foreign nationality [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral Grant and survivor benefits: Report the death to Dominica Social Security at its Roseau Head Office or Portsmouth sub-office [4]. If the deceased was an insured contributor with at least 26 paid weekly contributions, or the spouse or dependent child of an insured person, the person who paid or is liable to pay the funeral expenses can file a Funeral Grant Claim Form (Form FG 1) within 6 months of the death, attaching the official Death Certificate, the deceased's birth certificate and Social Security card, and itemized funeral receipts [4]. Surviving spouses and eligible dependent children should also apply for Survivor's Benefits [4].
  • Tax and revenue clearance: Notify the Inland Revenue Division in Roseau to update the deceased's taxpayer record, file any final personal income tax return for the year of death, and settle outstanding tax liabilities [6].
  • Financial institutions and identity records: Present certified copies of the Death Certificate to commercial banks, credit unions, and insurance companies in Dominica to freeze individual accounts and verify joint or beneficiary arrangements, and surrender the deceased's Dominican passport and Electoral Office identification card for cancellation [1] [2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Probate Proceedings
steps.html:
• Testate vs. intestate succession: Estate administration in Dominica is governed by the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules [5]. If your family member left a valid Will, the named executor applies to the High Court of Justice at the Registry Division for a Grant of Probate; if the deceased died without a Will, the closest eligible next-of-kin applies for Letters of Administration [2] [5].
  • Filing and valuation requirements: Applications are typically prepared by an attorney-at-law admitted in Dominica and filed through the High Court registry or the court's electronic litigation portal [2] [5]. The application package includes the original Will (if any), the official Death Certificate, an Oath of Executor or Administrator, an Affidavit of Due Execution, a detailed inventory and valuation of movable and immovable estate assets, and proof of statutory notice publication [5] [6].
  • Cross-border estates and foreign grants: Although Dominica does not levy a separate inheritance tax, statutory court probate fees, stamp duties, and property transfer fees administered with the Inland Revenue Division and the Lands and Surveys registry apply when transferring real estate [2] [6]. If a Grant of Probate was already issued by a court in another Commonwealth or foreign jurisdiction, an attorney can apply to the High Court of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court to reseal the foreign grant or obtain an ancillary grant covering Dominican assets [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Dominica: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Dominica: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Dominica: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Dominica is diagnosed with a serious, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the person retains full mental and decision-making capacity protects their wishes and secures essential support. Below we outline the five official steps we outline for care coordination, advance treatment directives, powers of attorney, social security benefits, and estate preparation in Dominica.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and community palliative care: Coordinate symptom management, pain relief, and specialist referrals through the Dominica-China Friendship Hospital in Roseau or the regional health centres managed by the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Social Services [2]. Primary care teams and district nurses provide community follow-up, wound care, and medication monitoring across Dominica's seven health districts [2].
  • Home nursing and oncology support: Connect with district community health nurses under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Social Services and local patient support organizations, such as the Dominica Cancer Society, to arrange home visits, medical equipment loans, and family caregiver guidance [2].
  • Health insurance and medical cost coordination: Review any private medical or critical-illness insurance policies held by your family member to confirm coverage for inpatient treatment, prescription medications, home nursing, or overseas tertiary care referrals, and verify public hospital fee exemptions that apply to insured contributors and pensioners [2] [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Appoint a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written statement of treatment preferences: While Dominica does not have a single standalone statute governing living wills, an adult with full mental capacity may execute a written advance healthcare directive setting out informed consent or refusal regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and palliative sedation [2].
  • Designating a healthcare spokesperson: Nominate a trusted primary and alternate family representative in writing to communicate with attending physicians if the ill person becomes unable to express medical decisions directly, and ask the treating physician to witness and record capacity at the time of signing [2] [3].
  • Clinical file lodging: Provide signed copies of the advance treatment statement and representative contact details to the attending hospital team at the Dominica-China Friendship Hospital, the district health centre supervised by the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Social Services, and all close relatives so that clinical teams can consult the document immediately during an emergency [2].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• General or specific Power of Attorney: Under Dominican law, a Power of Attorney must be executed as a formal deed while the grantor retains full legal and mental capacity, witnessed and attested before a Notary Public, Justice of the Peace, or attorney-at-law, and registered with the Registry Division on Dame Eugenia Charles Boulevard in Roseau [1].
  • Real property and legal authority: Ensure the deed explicitly authorizes the appointed attorney-in-fact to manage real estate, sign legal instruments, deal with utility providers, and represent the grantor before public authorities including the Registry Division and the Inland Revenue Division [1] [6].
  • Direct banking and credit union mandates: Because commercial banks and credit unions in Dominica often require their own internal third-party mandate forms or joint-signatory verification, accompany your family member - or arrange a home or hospital visit with a bank officer and medical capacity letter - to register signing authority before capacity declines [1].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Short-term Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an employed or self-employed contributor who becomes incapable of work due to illness, file a Sickness Benefit claim with Dominica Social Security using the prescribed medical certification forms [3] [4]. Sickness Benefit is paid at 60 percent of Average Weekly Insurable Earnings for up to 26 weeks (156 days) of medically certified incapacity [3].
  • Long-term Invalidity Benefit: When a life-limiting illness causes permanent incapacity for work before retirement age and the contributor meets the minimum contribution thresholds, submit an application for an Invalidity Pension or Invalidity Grant to Dominica Social Security, supported by medical reports for evaluation by the board's medical referee [3] [4].
  • Social welfare and caregiver arrangements: For individuals with limited social insurance coverage or high care needs, contact the Social Welfare Division within the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Social Services regarding public assistance grants, and ask employers about contractual compassionate or family medical leave for caregivers [2] [3].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Cross-Border Estate Documents
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid Will: Work with a Dominican attorney-at-law to prepare or update a Last Will and Testament that complies with formal execution rules - signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of two independent adult witnesses - so that future administration under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules proceeds smoothly [1] [5].
  • Gathering civil status and tax records: Obtain certified copies of birth and marriage certificates from the Registry Division or via the Government of Dominica e-Services portal, consolidate land certificates of title or conveyances, and verify tax compliance and filing records with the Inland Revenue Division [1] [6].
  • Cross-border assets and foreign documents: Review named beneficiaries on life insurance policies, credit union shares, and pension accounts with Dominica Social Security [3]. If your family member holds assets or family ties outside Dominica, ensure powers of attorney and civil documents are authenticated with a Hague Apostille through the Registry Division and aligned with estate counsel in each relevant jurisdiction [1] [5].
