title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Grenada: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Grenada: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Grenada: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Grenada. Below we outline the five official and practical steps required under Grenadian law to obtain medical certification of death, complete civil registration, arrange burial, cremation, or international repatriation, notify national insurance and tax authorities, and administer the estate.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or health facility deaths: When a death occurs at the General Hospital in St. George's, the Princess Alice Hospital in Mirabeau, the Princess Royal Hospital in Carriacou, or a clinic supervised by the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs, the attending medical practitioner certifies the cause of death and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death required under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act (Cap. 280) [1] [2].
  • Expected deaths at home: If your family member passed away at home after a documented illness under a physician's care, contact the treating doctor or the District Medical Officer immediately to examine the deceased and issue the medical cause-of-death certificate [1] [2].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or unnatural deaths: When a death occurs suddenly, without recent medical attendance, or under accidental or suspicious circumstances, notify the Royal Grenada Police Force immediately [1]. The police report the matter to the District Coroner, who orders an autopsy by a pathologist before issuing the Coroner's warrant for burial and registration [1].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and informant: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act (Cap. 280), every death occurring in Grenada must be reported to the District Registrar of the parish where the death occurred within five days of the death [1]. A relative present at the death, a person in attendance during the last illness, or an adult occupier of the house where the death took place serves as the statutory informant [1].
  • Central registration and documents required: Bring the signed Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's certificate), the deceased's birth certificate, passport, or voter identification card, and the informant's valid photo identification to the District Registrar or the Registrar General's Department under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs in St. George's [1] [2].
  • Issuance of Burial Order and certified extracts: Upon registering the death, the District Registrar issues the official certificate of registration (Burial Order) required for interment and provides certified copies of the Death Certificate, which you should order in multiple originals for banking, insurance, and probate filings [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Appoint a licensed funeral home in Grenada to handle mortuary preparation and transport [2]. Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, no burial or cremation may proceed without presenting the District Registrar's certificate of registration or the Coroner's order to the person officiating or managing the cemetery or crematorium [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's remains are to be repatriated abroad, the funeral director coordinates with the Chief Medical Officer and Environmental Health officers within the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs to obtain an official embalming certificate, a freedom-from-infectious-disease certificate, a hermetically sealed casket certificate, and an export permit [2].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Grenada is a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Certified Death Certificates and civil status documents destined for use abroad should be authenticated with an Apostille through the Supreme Court Registry or Ministry of Foreign Affairs in St. George's, and the relevant foreign embassy or consulate should be notified if the deceased was a foreign national [1] [5].

steps.title: Notify National Insurance, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral Grant and survivor benefits: Notify the National Insurance Scheme under the National Insurance Act (Cap. 205) [3] [4]. The person who paid or is liable to pay funeral costs for an insured contributor, pensioner, or eligible spouse can submit a Funeral Grant claim (Form NI8) to the National Insurance Scheme within three months of the date of death, enclosing the official Death Certificate, itemized funeral home receipts, and identification cards [3] [4]. Surviving spouses and dependent children should also apply for Survivor's Benefits [3] [4].
  • Tax notification and clearance: Report the death to the Inland Revenue Division (Ministry of Finance) in St. George's or via the G-TAX portal to update the deceased's tax account, file any final income tax return, and check property tax balances [6].
  • Financial institutions and identity documents: Provide certified Death Certificates to Grenadian banks, credit unions, and life insurers to freeze sole accounts and process beneficiary claims, and surrender the deceased's passport and national voter ID card to the relevant issuing authorities [1].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Probate Proceedings
steps.html:
• Grant of Probate vs. Letters of Administration: Estate succession in Grenada is administered through the Supreme Court Registry of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court in St. George's under the Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates Rules [5]. Where the deceased left a valid Will, the named executor applies for a Grant of Probate; where there is no Will, the entitled next-of-kin applies for Letters of Administration [5].
  • Court filing and inventory requirements: Applications are prepared with a Grenadian attorney-at-law and filed with the Supreme Court Registry, accompanied by the original Will (if applicable), the certified Death Certificate, Executor's or Administrator's Oath, Affidavit of Due Execution, and a sworn declaration and valuation of the estate's real and personal property [5].
  • Tax clearance and cross-border resealing: While Grenada does not impose a general inheritance tax on beneficiaries, estate filings require statutory court fees, stamp duties, and property transfer tax clearance through the Inland Revenue Division before real estate deeds are conveyed [5] [6]. If a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration has already been issued by a court in another Commonwealth or foreign country, an attorney can apply to the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court in Grenada to reseal the foreign grant so local assets can be transferred [5].

cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Grenada: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Grenada is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the person retains full mental and decision-making capacity ensures their preferences are respected and support systems are activated without delay. Below we outline the five official steps we outline for palliative care coordination, advance medical directives, powers of attorney, social security benefits, and estate planning in Grenada.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and community health services: Coordinate pain management, oncology follow-up, and symptom control through the General Hospital in St. George's, the Princess Alice Hospital in St. Andrew, the Princess Royal Hospital in Carriacou, and the community health centres operated by the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs [1].
  • Home nursing and palliative support: Connect with district community health nurses under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs as well as local non-profit care networks such as the Grenada Cancer Society to arrange home visits, palliative medication schedules, and caregiver assistance [1].
  • Private insurance and treatment coverage: Review any private health or critical-illness insurance policies held by your family member to verify coverage for inpatient care, prescription medications, home nursing, and medical travel, and ensure medical referrals are documented by the attending consultant physician [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance medical directive: While Grenada does not have a standalone statute dedicated exclusively to living wills, an adult with full mental capacity can sign a written advance medical statement under common-law principles of informed consent and refusal, detailing preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial feeding, and comfort-focused care [1].
  • Naming a healthcare proxy: Nominate a trusted family member or representative in writing to communicate with physicians if the ill person loses the ability to speak for themselves, and ask the attending physician to confirm mental capacity in the medical record when the directive is signed [1].
  • Clinical record integration: Provide copies of the signed advance treatment directive and representative contact details to the treating hospital team under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs, the local district medical officer, and close relatives so the document is immediately accessible in an emergency [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Formal Power of Attorney deed: Under Grenadian law, a Power of Attorney authorizing a representative to manage property, legal affairs, and financial transactions must be executed as a deed while the grantor still has full mental and legal capacity, witnessed before a Notary Public, Justice of the Peace, or attorney-at-law, and registered at the Supreme Court Registry (Deeds and Land Registry) in St. George's [4] [5].
  • Scope of financial and property authority: Ensure the Power of Attorney explicitly covers real estate management, tax filings with the Inland Revenue Division, utility accounts, and representation before public agencies [4] [6].
  • Bank and credit union mandates: Commercial banks and credit unions in Grenada typically require their own account mandate forms in addition to a registered Power of Attorney; arrange for your family member to sign bank authorization forms in person or via a bank-approved home or hospital visit while capacity is intact [4].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Short-term Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an insured employed or self-employed contributor who cannot work due to illness, submit a Sickness Benefit claim with medical certification to the National Insurance Scheme under the National Insurance Act (Cap. 205) [2] [3]. Sickness Benefit replaces a statutory portion of insurable earnings for up to 26 weeks of certified incapacity [2] [3].
  • Long-term Invalidity Pension or Grant: If the condition results in permanent incapacity for work prior to pensionable age and the contributor satisfies the contribution requirements under the National Insurance Act, apply to the National Insurance Scheme for an Invalidity Pension or lump-sum Invalidity Grant supported by specialist medical reports [2] [3].
  • Public assistance and caregiver leave: Where additional support is required, inquire with social development and community care programs linked to the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs, and coordinate with employers regarding contractual family medical or compassionate leave for primary caregivers [1] [2].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Estate Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing or updating a Will: Instruct a Grenadian attorney-at-law to draft or review your family member's Last Will and Testament while testamentary capacity is clear (ideally supported by a contemporaneous physician's certificate), ensuring execution before two independent witnesses in accordance with the rules applied by the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court [4].
  • Consolidating civil status and tax records: Obtain certified copies of birth and marriage certificates through the Registrar General's office under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Religious Affairs [1] [5], gather property deeds and land titles, and verify that personal and property tax accounts are current on the G-TAX portal of the Inland Revenue Division [6].
  • Beneficiaries and cross-border coordination: Confirm beneficiary designations on life insurance policies, credit union accounts, and pension records with the National Insurance Scheme [3]. If family members, executors, or assets are located outside Grenada, ensure powers of attorney and civil documents carry a Hague Apostille so cross-border administration under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court rules proceeds without delay [4] [5].

cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Guyana: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Guyana. Below we outline the five official and practical steps required under Guyanese law to obtain medical certification of death, register the death with the civil registry, arrange burial, cremation, or international repatriation, claim social security benefits, and administer the estate.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at the Georgetown Public Hospital Corporation, a regional hospital, or a private medical facility regulated by the Ministry of Health, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [6].
  • Expected deaths at home: If your family member died at home while under medical supervision for a diagnosed illness, notify the treating physician or Government Medical Officer immediately so that the doctor can verify the death and issue the signed Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [6].
  • Sudden, unnatural, or uncertified deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, outside medical care, or by accident, notify the Guyana Police Force immediately [1]. The police arrange for the remains to be transferred to an authorized hospital mortuary and refer the case to a Coroner for a post-mortem examination by a Government Pathologist, after which the Coroner issues the order for burial and death registration [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Statutory registration with the General Register Office: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act (Cap. 44:01), every death in Guyana must be reported to the District Registrar of the registration division where the death occurred and recorded centrally with the General Register Office (Ministry of Home Affairs, GPO Building, Robb Street, Georgetown) [1] [2].
  • Required documents and timelines: The informant (a relative present at the death, person present during the last illness, occupier of the premises, or person causing the body to be buried) submits the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death or Coroner's Certificate along with the deceased's national identification card, birth certificate, or passport [1]. If a death is not registered within twelve months, a specialized Late Registration of a Death application with supporting affidavits and hospital or burial records is required [2].
  • Ordering certified Death Certificates: Once the registration is completed, apply to the General Register Office for multiple official certified copies of the Death Certificate (GYD $300 standard processing fee per certificate), which are mandatory for social security claims, bank closures, and probate filings [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: Engage a licensed funeral parlour in Guyana to manage mortuary care and funeral arrangements [1] [6]. Present the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death or Coroner's Order to the District Registrar and local municipal or Neighbourhood Democratic Council authority to obtain the official Burial Order or cremation authorization prior to interment [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's remains are to be transported outside Guyana, the funeral director coordinates with the Chief Medical Officer and Port Health authorities at the Ministry of Health to secure an official embalming certificate, a freedom-from-communicable-disease certificate, a hermetically sealed casket inspection certificate, and a burial transit/export permit [6].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Guyana is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Certified Death Certificates and civil status documents intended for use in another convention country should be authenticated with an Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Georgetown, and the relevant foreign embassy or high commission should be notified if the deceased was a foreign citizen [1].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral Benefit and Survivor's Benefit: Report the death to the National Insurance Scheme [3]. If the deceased was an insured contributor with at least 50 paid contributions (or the spouse of an insured contributor), the person who paid or is responsible for the funeral expenses can file Claim Form FB1 (Claim for Funeral Benefit) with the National Insurance Scheme, attaching the original Death Certificate, medical cause-of-death certificate, itemized funeral receipts, and NIS cards [3]. Surviving spouses and eligible dependents should also submit claims for Survivor's Pension or Grant [3].
  • Tax notifications and Statement of Affairs: Notify the Guyana Revenue Authority to update the deceased's Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) record and file any outstanding income tax returns up to the date of death [4].
  • Banks, pensions, and identity documents: Present certified Death Certificates to commercial banks, the New Building Society, credit unions, and the Ministry of Human Services and Social Security (if the deceased received the Old Age Pension) to close accounts and settle survivor entitlements, and surrender the deceased's national ID card and Guyanese passport [1] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Probate Proceedings
steps.html:
• Statement of Assets and Process Fee with the GRA: Before applying to the court for estate representation under the Deceased Persons Estates' Administration Act (Cap. 12:01), the executor or administrator must file a Statement of Assets and Liabilities with the Estate Duty Section of the Guyana Revenue Authority [4]. Estates valued up to GYD $100,000 pay no fee, while estates exceeding GYD $100,000 are subject to a statutory process fee of 0.5 percent (half of one percent) of the gross estate value to obtain the Certificate of Valuation and tax clearance [4].
  • Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration: Once cleared by the Guyana Revenue Authority, an attorney-at-law files the application with the Probate Division of the High Court of the Supreme Court of Judicature (and the Deeds and Commercial Registry) in Georgetown, Berbice, or Essequibo [4] [5]. If the deceased left a valid Will, the named executor applies for a Grant of Probate; if the deceased died intestate, the next-of-kin in statutory priority (surviving spouse, children, parents, or siblings) applies for Letters of Administration [4] [5].
  • Cross-border estates and foreign grants: Transferring immovable property in Guyana (whether held by Transport or Certificate of Title) requires advertising and passing an Estate Transport or registering transmission once the court grant issues [4] [5]. If a Grant of Probate was issued in a Commonwealth or foreign jurisdiction, a Guyanese attorney can apply to the High Court of the Supreme Court of Judicature to reseal the foreign grant or obtain an ancillary grant for assets in Guyana [5].

cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Guyana: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Guyana is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the person retains full mental and decision-making capacity protects their wishes and secures timely support. Below we outline the five official steps we outline for palliative care coordination, advance medical directives, powers of attorney, social security benefits, and estate planning in Guyana.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and specialist medical services: Coordinate oncology, symptom control, and pain management through the Georgetown Public Hospital Corporation, regional hospitals, and community health facilities supervised by the Ministry of Health [1].
  • Hospice, home care, and community support: Connect with specialized palliative and oncology care teams - including the Cancer Institute of Guyana and charitable home-care programs - alongside regional health officers from the Ministry of Health to organize home nursing visits, analgesic prescriptions, and assistive medical equipment [1].
  • Medical assistance and insurance coverage: Review any private group or individual health insurance policies held by your family member, and inquire with the Ministry of Health Medical Treatment Department regarding financial assistance grants available to Guyanese citizens facing severe or life-limiting medical conditions [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Appoint a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance medical directive: While Guyana does not have a standalone statute dedicated solely to living wills, an adult with full mental capacity can execute a written statement of treatment preferences under common-law principles of informed consent and refusal, specifying instructions on cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and palliative comfort care [1].
  • Designating a medical spokesperson: Nominate a trusted primary and alternate family representative in writing to communicate with physicians if the ill person becomes unable to speak for themselves, and ask the attending physician to document mental capacity in the clinical notes when the directive is signed [1].
  • Filing with clinical teams: Provide signed copies of the advance treatment statement and representative contact details to the treating hospital team under the Ministry of Health, the family physician, and close relatives so the document can be consulted immediately during an emergency [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarial Power of Attorney and Deeds Registry filing: Under the Powers of Attorney Act (Cap. 5:08) of Guyana, a General or Special Power of Attorney must be executed while the donor retains full mental and legal capacity, signed before a Notary Public, Justice of the Peace, or Commissioner of Oaths, and recorded with the Deeds and Commercial Registry Authority (connected with the High Court of the Supreme Court of Judicature) to be valid for property and legal transactions [5].
  • Real property and tax representation: Ensure the registered Power of Attorney explicitly authorizes the attorney-in-fact to manage bank accounts, deal with land Transports or Certificates of Title, and represent the donor before the Guyana Revenue Authority [4] [5].
  • Commercial bank and building society mandates: Because commercial banks and the New Building Society in Guyana enforce strict verification procedures for third-party representatives, arrange for your family member to complete bank-specific mandate forms or register the recorded Power of Attorney directly with each financial institution while capacity is intact [5].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Short-term Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an employed or self-employed contributor under age 60 who becomes incapable of work due to illness, submit a Sickness Benefit claim with medical certificates to the National Insurance Scheme [2] [3]. Sickness Benefit is payable from the fourth day of certified incapacity for up to 26 weeks [2].
  • Long-term Invalidity Pension or Grant: When a serious illness lasts beyond 26 weeks and renders an insured person under age 60 permanently incapable of work, apply to the National Insurance Scheme for an Invalidity Pension (requiring at least 250 contributions, of which at least 150 must be paid contributions) or an Invalidity Grant (if between 50 and 249 contributions were made) [3].
  • Public assistance and caregiver arrangements: For individuals needing additional social protection, contact the Ministry of Human Services and Social Security regarding Permanent Disability or Public Assistance grants, and coordinate with employers regarding family medical or compassionate leave for primary caregivers [1] [2].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid Will: Instruct an attorney-at-law in Guyana to prepare or update a Last Will and Testament under the Wills Act (Cap. 12:02) while testamentary capacity is intact - signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of two independent witnesses - to streamline future administration before the Supreme Court of Judicature and the Guyana Revenue Authority [4] [5].
  • Securing civil status and property records: Obtain certified copies of birth and marriage certificates from the General Register Office in Georgetown [6], locate original property Transports, Certificates of Title, or leases, and verify Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and tax compliance records with the Guyana Revenue Authority [4].
  • Beneficiaries and cross-border coordination: Review named beneficiaries on life insurance policies, pension plans, and records with the National Insurance Scheme [2] [3]. If family members, attorneys-in-fact, or assets are located outside Guyana, ensure powers of attorney executed abroad are notarized, authenticated with a Hague Apostille, and recorded at the Deeds Registry in Guyana so cross-border transactions proceed smoothly [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Jamaica: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Jamaica: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Jamaica: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Jamaica. To help your family navigate the legal, medical, and estate administration procedures in chronological order, we have outlined the five main official steps below.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or clinical facility: When your family member dies under medical care at a public hospital or private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health and Wellness, the attending physician issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [5]. You or your appointed funeral director will need this signed medical certificate to proceed with civil registration and burial arrangements [1].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home while under regular care for a documented illness, contact the treating physician immediately to examine the body and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1]. You should also notify the nearest Jamaica Constabulary Force station so officers can record the unattended home death and confirm that no suspicious circumstances exist [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, accidentally, or without recent medical attendance, report it immediately to the Jamaica Constabulary Force [1]. The police refer the case to the parish Coroner for a post-mortem examination, after which the Coroner issues a Coroner's Certificate or Burial Order authorizing registration and disposition of the remains [1].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Where and when to register: Under the Registration (Births and Deaths) Act, every death in Jamaica must be reported to the Local District Registrar in the registration district where the death occurred, under the authority of the Registrar General's Department [1] [2]. While the medical certificate or Coroner's order should be delivered within five days of the death, formal registration with the Local District Registrar is completed so the entry can be transmitted to the central registry [1] [2].
  • Required documentation: The informant (such as a surviving relative, person present at the death, or authorized funeral director) must present the signed Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's documentation), along with the deceased's full name, date and place of birth, occupation, and government-issued identification [1] [2].
  • Ordering certified death certificates: Once the Local District Registrar records the death and issues the counterfoil receipt, you can apply to the Registrar General's Department at Twickenham Park, St. Catherine, or any regional branch office for official certified copies of the Death Certificate [1] [2]. Request several certified copies, as banks, pension offices, and the probate court each require originals [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral home: Appoint a licensed Jamaican funeral director early to manage mortuary transfer, refrigerated storage, and preparation of the body [1]. Burial in a public or parish cemetery or cremation requires the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death or Coroner's Burial Order, alongside municipal health and parish council cemetery permits [1] [5].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's body or cremated ashes must be transported out of Jamaica, the funeral home must obtain an export and public health transit permit from the Ministry of Health and Wellness, an embalming certificate (for coffined remains), a certificate of non-infectious disease, and a sealing certificate from public health authorities [5].
  • Consular notification and document authentication: If your family member held foreign nationality or if Jamaican death certificates must be presented in another country, contact the relevant foreign embassy or high commission in Kingston and submit the certified Death Certificate from the Registrar General's Department to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade for an Apostille or consular legalization [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Tax, and Financial Institutions and Claim Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• National Insurance Scheme (NIS) Funeral Grant and survivor benefits: Notify the Ministry of Labour and Social Security to halt any ongoing retirement or invalidity pension payments and apply for statutory survivor benefits [3]. If the deceased or their spouse met the contribution conditions under the National Insurance Scheme, the person who paid or assumed responsibility for the burial costs can submit the NIS Funeral Grant claim form together with the certified Death Certificate and itemized funeral receipts within the statutory filing window [3]. Surviving spouses and dependent children may also claim a Widow's or Widower's Benefit or Orphan's Benefit through the Ministry of Labour and Social Security [3].
  • Tax, identity, and public records: Notify Tax Administration Jamaica to update the deceased's Taxpayer Registration Number (TRN) record and settle any outstanding income or property tax obligations [4]. You should also return the deceased's Jamaican passport for cancellation and notify the Electoral Office of Jamaica and any public-sector pension authority.
  • Banks, credit unions, and insurers: Present a certified Death Certificate to all commercial banks, credit unions, and life insurance companies in Jamaica. Sole accounts in the deceased's name will be frozen until an executor or administrator presents a court grant, whereas life insurance policies with named beneficiaries generally pay out directly upon verification of the death certificate [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain Probate or Letters of Administration
steps.html:
• Testate vs. intestate succession: If your family member left a valid Will, the named executor applies for a Grant of Probate [4]. If your family member died without a Will (intestate), the surviving spouse or next of kin under the Intestates' Estates and Property Charges Act applies for Letters of Administration [4]. For intestate estates where minors are beneficiaries or no family member steps forward, the Administrator-General's Department administers the estate.
  • Court jurisdiction and Transfer Tax: Estate applications are filed with the Probate and Family Division of the Supreme Court of Judicature of Jamaica (or the local Parish Court for smaller estates within statutory monetary thresholds) [4]. Before distributing or transferring real property and shares, the personal representative must file a Revenue Affidavit with the Stamp Duty and Transfer Tax Section of Tax Administration Jamaica to pay Transfer Tax on Death and applicable estate stamp duties [4].
  • Cross-border estates and foreign heirs: If your family member owned assets in Jamaica but already has a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration issued by a court in a Commonwealth country or the United Kingdom, that foreign grant can often be resealed at the Supreme Court of Judicature of Jamaica under the Probates (Re-Sealing) Act [4]. Foreign heirs executing estate documents abroad must have their signatures notarized and authenticated by Apostille or Jamaican consular certification [4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Jamaica: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Jamaica: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Jamaica: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Jamaica is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, taking early medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person retains full decision-making capacity helps protect their comfort and autonomy. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and specialist palliative care: Ask the treating specialist or hospital team under the Ministry of Health and Wellness for a formal palliative care referral [5]. Specialist inpatient and outpatient pain and symptom management is coordinated through regional public hospitals (including the Kingston Public Hospital, the Hope Institute Hospital in Kingston, and the University Hospital of the West Indies), alongside community health centres and charitable hospice providers such as the Jamaica Cancer Society [5].
  • Home nursing and continuity of care: Request a written care summary, prescription schedule for controlled pain medications, and home-visit coordination with the local parish health department and district community health aides so that symptom management can continue safely at home [5]. Ensure the primary home physician is registered and willing to attend the home regularly [5].
  • National Health Fund (NHF) and private insurance: Register your family member with the National Health Fund under the Ministry of Health and Wellness to receive statutory subsidies on prescription medications and medical supplies for chronic and life-limiting conditions, and notify any private health insurer to pre-authorize home nursing or inpatient care [5].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance care plan: While Jamaica does not have a single standalone statute governing living wills, patients with full mental capacity have a common-law and constitutional right to consent to or refuse medical treatment [1] [5]. Work with the treating physician to record your family member's explicit instructions regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, pain relief, and preferred place of care (home versus hospital) in their clinical file [5].
  • Designating a medical proxy: Have your family member sign a written statement naming a trusted spokesperson (and an alternate) to communicate with medical teams at the Ministry of Health and Wellness or private hospitals if your family member becomes unable to speak for themselves [1] [5].
  • Distribution to care teams: Provide signed copies of the advance care preferences and next-of-kin contact details to the attending physician, the hospital medical records department, and all household caregivers so emergency responders respect the patient's documented wishes [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a Power of Attorney: While your family member still has full mental capacity, instruct an attorney-at-law to draft a formal Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted agent (donee) to manage bank accounts, bill payments, tax filings, and property matters [1] [2]. In Jamaica, a Power of Attorney signed on the island must be executed in the presence of a Justice of the Peace or a Notary Public [1] [2].
  • Mandatory stamping and registration: To be legally valid and accepted by financial institutions or government agencies in Jamaica, the executed Power of Attorney must first be submitted to the Stamp Office of Tax Administration Jamaica for assessment and payment of stamp duty, and then recorded at the Island Records Office of the Registrar General's Department in Twickenham Park, St. Catherine [1] [2] [4].
  • Real property and bank mandates: If the attorney-in-fact will manage or sell registered land under the Registration of Titles Act, an original or certified copy of the Power of Attorney must also be deposited with the Office of Titles at the National Land Agency [2]. In addition, visit your family member's Jamaican commercial banks and credit unions early to complete their institution-specific third-party signing mandates while capacity is intact [1].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Critical-Illness, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• National Insurance Scheme (NIS) Invalidity Benefit: If your family member has contributed to the National Insurance Scheme and is under pensionable age and permanently unable to work due to illness, submit an Invalidity Benefit claim (with medical certification from the attending doctor) to the Ministry of Labour and Social Security [3]. If your family member is already receiving an NIS retirement or invalidity pension, inquire about appointing an authorized agent to collect payments if they become housebound [3].
  • Public assistance and disability support: Register eligible individuals with the Jamaica Council for Persons with Disabilities under the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and check eligibility for Programme of Advancement Through Health and Education (PATH) or social assistance grants for vulnerable households [3].
  • Private critical-illness policies and workplace leave: Review any employer group health, critical-illness, or permanent-disability insurance policies for accelerated living-benefit payouts, and coordinate family medical leave or flexible working arrangements with employers in Jamaica [3].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a Will: Under the Wills Act of Jamaica, a valid Will must be in writing and signed by the testator in the presence of two independent witnesses who are present at the same time and who also sign in the testator's presence (neither witness nor their spouse should be a beneficiary) [1] [4]. Confirm that capacity is contemporaneously documented by a medical practitioner if your family member is seriously ill when signing [1].
  • Civil status and land title verification: Gather certified copies of birth and marriage certificates from the Registrar General's Department and verify that real estate Duplicate Certificates of Title held with the National Land Agency (and Taxpayer Registration Number records) accurately reflect current ownership and joint-tenancy arrangements [2] [4]. Update named beneficiaries on life insurance policies, credit union shares, and approved superannuation or pension funds.
  • Cross-border coordination: If your family member holds assets outside Jamaica or if a Power of Attorney is executed overseas for use in Jamaica, it must be notarized and authenticated by an Apostille or a Jamaican diplomatic or consular mission before being stamped and recorded at the Registrar General's Department and the National Land Agency [1] [2].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Saint Kitts and Nevis: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Saint Kitts and Nevis: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Saint Kitts and Nevis: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Saint Kitts and Nevis. To help you manage the immediate medical, civil, funeral, and succession procedures in order, we have set out the five main official steps below.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or clinical facility: When your family member dies at a public or private medical facility in the Federation - such as the Joseph N. France General Hospital in Basseterre (Saint Kitts) or the Alexandra Hospital in Charlestown (Nevis) under the Ministry of Health - the attending medical practitioner issues the official Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death [1] [4].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home while under medical care for a known illness, contact the treating physician or district medical officer immediately to examine the body and complete the Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death [1] [4]. You should also notify the Royal St. Christopher and Nevis Police Force so officers can attend the residence and confirm there are no suspicious circumstances [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was unexpected, accidental, or occurred without recent medical attendance, notify the Royal St. Christopher and Nevis Police Force immediately [1]. The police report the death to the District Magistrate acting as Coroner, who may order a forensic post-mortem examination before issuing a Coroner's Certificate and Burial Order [1].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Where and when to register: Under the Registration of Births, Deaths and Marriages Act of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis, every death must be registered with the District Registrar or the Registrar General's Office in Basseterre (for Saint Kitts) or the Registrar General Department in Charlestown (for Nevis) within the statutory registration period (normally within five days of the death or upon receipt of the Coroner's certificate) [1].
  • Required documentation: A qualified informant (such as a relative present at the death, an occupant of the house, or the person causing the body to be buried) must present the signed Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death or Coroner's Order, along with the deceased's official identification, birth certificate, or passport [1].
  • Obtaining certified copies: Once the entry is recorded in the civil register, apply to the Registrar General's Office of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis for multiple certified copies of the Death Certificate, which are required for social security claims, bank notifications, and court probate filings [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Appointing a licensed funeral provider: Engage a licensed funeral home in Saint Kitts or Nevis to handle mortuary transfer, embalming, and cemetery or cremation arrangements [1] [2]. Burial or cremation cannot take place without the Registrar's Certificate of Registration of Death or the Coroner's Burial Order, together with public health clearance from the environmental health authorities under the Ministry of Health [1] [4].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's body or cremated remains must be transported abroad, the funeral director coordinates with the Chief Medical Officer at the Ministry of Health to obtain an official burial-transit and export permit, an embalming certificate, a certificate of non-contagious disease, and ahermetic coffin sealing certificate for customs and airline clearance [4].
  • Consular notification and Apostille legalization: When the deceased was a foreign citizen or when Saint Kitts and Nevis death certificates must be used in another jurisdiction, notify the relevant foreign embassy or consulate and obtain an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Legal Department of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [1].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Tax, and Financial Authorities and Claim Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• Social Security Funeral Grant and Survivor Pension: Report the death to the St. Christopher and Nevis Social Security Board to stop any ongoing retirement or invalidity pension and claim survivor entitlements [2]. Under the Social Security (Benefits) Regulations, a one-off Funeral Grant is payable upon the death of an insured contributor, pensioner, or their spouse if the contribution requirements are met [2]. Submit the Funeral Grant Claim Form (Form FG1) to the St. Christopher and Nevis Social Security Board within six months of the date of death, enclosing the original Death Certificate and itemized funeral invoices or receipts [2]. Eligible surviving spouses and dependent children should also apply for a Survivor's Benefit (Widow's/Widower's Allowance or Child's Allowance) [2].
  • Tax, identity, and public records: Notify the Inland Revenue Department of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis to settle any final tax obligations, return the deceased's national identification card and passport for cancellation, and inform the Electoral Office [1].
  • Banks, credit unions, and insurers: Provide certified copies of the Death Certificate to all commercial banks, credit unions, and insurance companies in Saint Kitts and Nevis. Sole bank accounts will remain frozen until a court grant of representation is produced, while life insurance policies with named beneficiaries are processed directly with the insurer [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain Probate or Letters of Administration
steps.html:
• Grants of Probate and Letters of Administration: Estate succession in the Federation is governed by the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules and filed with the High Court Registry in Basseterre (Saint Kitts circuit) or Charlestown (Nevis circuit) [3]. If your family member left a valid Will, the named executor applies for a Grant of Probate (using Form P1); if your family member died intestate (without a Will), the next of kin applies for Letters of Administration (using Form P2) [3].
  • Court filings and estate valuations: The application to the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court High Court Registry must include the original Will (if any), a certified copy of the Death Certificate, a Certificate of Search confirming no prior grant or caveat has been filed, the Oath of the Executor or Administrator, and a Declaration and Account of the Estate detailing the value of all property in Saint Kitts and Nevis [3]. While Saint Kitts and Nevis does not levy a general inheritance tax on beneficiaries, court filing fees and statutory stamp duties apply to estate filings and real property transfers [3].
  • Cross-border estates and resealing foreign grants: If a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration has already been issued by a court in another Commonwealth jurisdiction or the United Kingdom, an attorney-at-law in Saint Kitts and Nevis can apply to the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court High Court Registry to reseal the foreign grant so local real estate and bank assets can be administered [3].

France (JNF) General Hospital in Basseterre (Saint Kitts) or the Alexandra Hospital in Charlestown (Nevis) [1]. Ask for a dedicated pain and symptom management schedule and written discharge or outpatient guidance [1].
  • Community health and home nursing support: Register your family member with the local district health centre under the Ministry of Health so community public health nurses and district medical officers can monitor the patient at home, manage prescriptions, and maintain clinical records [1].
  • Health insurance and medical assistance: Review coverage under any private or employer group health insurance plan for home nursing, medical equipment, and specialist consultations, and inquire with the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Social Development regarding public pharmaceutical assistance programs [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Proxy
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment preferences: While Saint Kitts and Nevis does not have a standalone statutory living-will registry, competent adults have the common-law right to give or withhold informed consent to medical procedures [1] [4]. While your family member has full mental capacity, prepare a signed written statement setting out their preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial hydration and nutrition, palliative sedation, and preferred place of care [1].
  • Naming a healthcare spokesperson: Include in the written directive the name and contact details of a primary and alternate medical representative whom hospital physicians and community health teams under the Ministry of Health should consult if your family member becomes unable to communicate [1].
  • Filing with clinical providers: Provide signed copies of the advance care plan to the attending physician, the medical records unit at JNF General Hospital or Alexandra Hospital, and household caregivers [1].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a Power of Attorney: While your family member still possesses full legal and mental capacity, instruct a licensed attorney-at-law in Saint Kitts and Nevis to prepare a formal Power of Attorney under the laws of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis [3] [4]. The instrument authorizes a trusted agent (donee) to manage bank accounts, pay household and medical bills, and handle real property or business affairs [3] [4].
  • Execution, stamping, and registration: A Power of Attorney executed in the Federation must be properly witnessed, stamped for stamp duty at the Inland Revenue Department, and registered at the High Court Registry / Deeds and Land Registry of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis (in Basseterre for Saint Kitts or Charlestown for Nevis) to be legally effective for property and official transactions [3] [4].
  • Commercial bank and Social Security mandates: Contact your family member's local commercial banks and credit unions to complete their internal third-party account mandate forms while capacity is intact, and ask the St. Christopher and Nevis Social Security Board about appointing an authorized representative to receive benefit payments if the beneficiary becomes physically unable to transact [2].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Social Security Sickness and Invalidity Benefits: If your family member is an insured contributor under age 62 who has had to stop working due to illness, submit a Sickness Benefit claim to the St. Christopher and Nevis Social Security Board for short-term income replacement (up to 26 weeks) [2]. Once incapacity has lasted at least 26 weeks and is certified as likely to be permanent, apply for the long-term Invalidity Benefit (which requires at least 150 paid contributions) or an Age Pension if your family member has reached retirement age [2] [3].
  • Medical certification and representative collection: Claims to the St. Christopher and Nevis Social Security Board must be supported by official medical certificates signed by a registered medical practitioner [2].
  • Private insurance and family caregiver arrangements: Check private life or critical-illness insurance policies for accelerated terminal-illness or critical-illness benefits, and coordinate workplace leave arrangements for family caregivers [1] [2].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Preparing or updating a Will: Under the Wills Act and the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules, a valid Will in Saint Kitts and Nevis must be in writing and signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent witnesses who also sign in the testator's presence (beneficiaries and their spouses must not act as witnesses) [4]. Ask the attending doctor to document testamentary capacity in the medical notes at the time the Will is signed [4].
  • Organizing civil status and title records: Locate original or certified copies of birth and marriage certificates from the Registrar General's Office of the Government of Saint Kitts and Nevis, along with Certificates of Title or Deeds of Conveyance, insurance policies, and bank records [3] [4]. Review named beneficiaries on life insurance and credit union accounts so those funds can pass outside probate [4].
  • Cross-border assets and foreign documents: If your family member holds assets outside the Federation or if a Power of Attorney is signed abroad for use in Saint Kitts and Nevis, ensure the document is notarized and legalized with an Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention before registration at the High Court Registry under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court [3] [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Saint Lucia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Saint Lucia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Saint Lucia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Saint Lucia. To help you navigate the required medical, civil registration, funeral, and succession procedures in chronological order, we have outlined the five main official steps below.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or clinical facility: When your family member dies in a hospital or health facility in Saint Lucia - such as the Owen King European Union (OKEU) Hospital in Castries or St. Jude Hospital in Vieux Fort - the attending medical practitioner issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [4].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home while under medical care for a documented illness, notify the treating physician or District Medical Officer immediately to examine the body and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, and report the home death to the nearest Royal Saint Lucia Police Force station so officers can confirm no suspicious circumstances exist [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was unexpected, unnatural, or occurred without recent medical attendance, contact the Royal Saint Lucia Police Force immediately [1]. The police refer the case to the District Coroner, who orders a post-mortem examination before issuing the Coroner's Certificate and Warrant to Bury [1].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Where and when to register: Under the Civil Status Act of Saint Lucia, every death must be registered with the District Registrar in the registration district where the death occurred and recorded centrally with the Civil Status Registry (located on Brazil Street, Castries) [1]. Statutory rules require registration before burial (or within five days of the death notice, and no later than six months before late-registration penalties apply) [1].
  • Required documentation: A qualified informant (such as a relative present at the death, a person living in the same house, or the funeral director) must present the signed Medical Certificate of Cause of Death or Coroner's Certificate, together with the deceased's national identification card, passport, and birth or marriage certificate [1].
  • Ordering certified Death Certificates: Once the District Registrar registers the death and issues the Certificate of Registration of Death (Permit for Burial), apply to the Civil Status Registry in Castries (or via the Government of Saint Lucia DigiGov portal) for several official certified copies of the Death Certificate, which are needed for benefits, banking, and succession [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Engaging a licensed funeral home: Appoint a licensed funeral home in Saint Lucia to manage mortuary transfer, preservation of the body, and cemetery or cremation bookings [1] [2]. A burial or cremation cannot proceed without the District Registrar's Permit for Burial or the Coroner's Warrant to Bury, as well as municipal cemetery and environmental health permits from the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Elderly Affairs [1] [4].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's body or cremated ashes must be repatriated outside Saint Lucia, the funeral director coordinates with the Chief Medical Officer at the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Elderly Affairs to obtain an official Permit to Export Human Remains, an embalming certificate, a freedom-from-infection certificate, and a coffin-sealing certificate for customs and airline clearance [4].
  • Consular notification and Apostille legalization: If the deceased was a foreign national or if Saint Lucian civil status documents must be used abroad, notify the relevant foreign embassy or consulate and submit the certified Death Certificate from the Civil Status Registry to the Registry of the High Court or Ministry of External Affairs for an Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention [1] [4].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Tax, and Financial Authorities and Claim Survivor Benefits
steps.html:
• National Insurance Corporation (NIC) Funeral Grant and Survivor's Benefit: Notify the National Insurance Corporation to stop any ongoing retirement or invalidity pension and claim statutory death benefits [2] [3]. If the deceased was an insured contributor or pensioner (or the spouse or dependent child of an insured person), the individual who paid or is responsible for the funeral costs can submit the Funeral Grant Claim Form (Form FB1) to the National Insurance Corporation, enclosing the certified Death Certificate, original funeral receipts or invoices, and valid photo identification [2] [3]. Surviving spouses and dependent children should also inquire with the National Insurance Corporation regarding a Survivor's Pension or Widow's/Widower's Grant [2] [3].
  • Tax, identity, and electoral records: Notify the Inland Revenue Department of the Government of Saint Lucia to close or settle the deceased's income and property tax accounts, return the deceased's Saint Lucian passport and national ID card for cancellation, and notify the Electoral Department [1] [4].
  • Banks, credit unions, and insurance companies: Present certified copies of the Death Certificate to all commercial banks, credit unions, and insurers in Saint Lucia. Sole accounts in the deceased's name will be frozen pending a court Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration, while life insurance policies with named beneficiaries are paid directly to the beneficiaries [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain Probate or Letters of Administration
steps.html:
• Mixed civil-law and probate framework: Estate succession in Saint Lucia is governed by the Civil Code of Saint Lucia alongside the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules, administered through the Registry of the High Court in Castries [4]. Saint Lucia recognizes both standard English-form Wills (signed before two witnesses) and Notarial Wills executed before a Notary Royal [4].
  • Applying for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration: If your family member left a valid Will, the named executor engages an attorney-at-law or Notary Royal to apply to the Registry of the High Court for a Grant of Probate [4]. If your family member died intestate (without a Will), the lawful heirs under the Civil Code apply for Letters of Administration [4]. The application requires a Registry search certificate (including a check of the Deeds and Mortgages Registry), the original Will (if any), the certified Death Certificate, and an inventory and valuation of the estate [4].
  • Cross-border estates and foreign heirs: If your family member held real estate or bank accounts in Saint Lucia and a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration was already issued in another Commonwealth country or the United Kingdom, your Saint Lucian attorney can apply to the Registry of the High Court to reseal the foreign grant [4]. Powers of attorney or succession deeds signed by heirs living abroad must be notarized and authenticated by Apostille [4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Saint Lucia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Saint Lucia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Saint Lucia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Saint Lucia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, organizing medical care, legal representation, and benefit entitlements while the ill person still retains full decision-making capacity helps protect their comfort and autonomy. Below, we explain the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and specialist symptom management: Work with your family member's treating specialist at the Owen King European Union (OKEU) Hospital in Castries, St. Jude Hospital in Vieux Fort, or Tapion Hospital to establish a comprehensive pain and symptom management plan [3]. Request a written clinical summary and medication schedule from the attending team [3].
  • Community wellness centres and home care: Register your family member with the nearest Community Wellness Centre under the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Elderly Affairs of the Government of Saint Lucia so district medical officers and community health nurses can coordinate home visits, wound or symptom care, and prescription renewals [3]. Non-governmental support organizations such as the Saint Lucia Cancer Society also assist families with palliative care guidance and equipment.
  • Health insurance and pharmaceutical support: Notify your family member's private or employer group health insurer to pre-authorize home nursing or inpatient care, and check eligibility for subsidized medications through public health pharmacies and the National Insurance Corporation health programs [1] [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance care preferences: While Saint Lucia does not maintain a standalone statutory registry for living wills, adults with full mental capacity have the right under Saint Lucian law to consent to or refuse medical treatment [3] [4]. While your family member retains clear decision-making capacity, help them sign a written statement detailing their wishes regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition and hydration, pain relief, and whether they prefer to be cared for at home or in hospital [3].
  • Designating a medical proxy: Include in the written statement the name and contact details of a trusted family member or representative (and an alternate) who is authorized to speak with hospital doctors and the Ministry of Health, Wellness and Elderly Affairs care teams if the ill person becomes unable to communicate [3].
  • Sharing with care providers: Provide copies of the signed preferences to the attending physician, the hospital medical records department, and all household caregivers so emergency personnel honour your family member's documented wishes [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a Notarial Power of Attorney (Mandate): Under the Civil Code of Saint Lucia, a Power of Attorney (mandate) must be executed while the grantor (principal) still possesses full mental and legal capacity [4]. Engage a practicing attorney-at-law / Notary Royal in Saint Lucia to prepare a formal Notarial Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted agent to manage bank accounts, pay medical and household expenses, and handle property or official filings [4].
  • Registration at the Registry of Deeds and Mortgages: For a Power of Attorney in Saint Lucia to be relied upon for real property transactions or official registry filings, it must be executed in authentic notarial form (or duly witnessed and authenticated) and registered at the Registry of Deeds and Mortgages / Registry of the High Court in Castries under the Government of Saint Lucia [3] [4].
  • Commercial bank and benefit mandates: Visit your family member's commercial banks and credit unions in Saint Lucia early to complete their institution-specific third-party signing mandates while capacity is intact, and contact the National Insurance Corporation to inquire about authorizing a representative to collect benefit payments if the claimant cannot attend in person [1] [2].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• National Insurance Corporation (NIC) Sickness Benefit: If your family member is an insured contributor who is temporarily unable to work due to illness, submit a Sickness Benefit claim with a medical certificate signed by a registered medical practitioner to the National Insurance Corporation [1] [2]. Sickness Benefit is payable for up to 26 weeks after a three-day waiting period [1] [2].
  • Transition to NIC Invalidity Benefit: If the illness renders your family member permanently incapable of work beyond 26 weeks and they are under pensionable age and meet the statutory contribution thresholds under the National Insurance Corporation Act, apply to the National Insurance Corporation for a long-term Invalidity Pension or Invalidity Grant [1] [2].
  • Private critical-illness policies and caregiver leave: Review any private life or critical-illness insurance policies for accelerated living-benefit payouts upon a terminal or critical diagnosis, and coordinate workplace leave arrangements for family caregivers under the Saint Lucia Labour Code [2] [3].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Executing or updating a Will: Under the Civil Code of Saint Lucia, a testator with full mental capacity can execute either a Notarial Will (made before a Notary Royal and a second Notary or two witnesses, which does not require formal witness proof after death) or an English-form Will signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of two independent witnesses [4]. Ask the attending physician to record a contemporaneous note confirming testamentary capacity when the Will is signed [4].
  • Verifying civil status and land registry records: Obtain up-to-date certified copies of birth and marriage certificates from the Civil Status Registry in Castries, and verify Land Registry Parcel Numbers and title records for any real property in Saint Lucia [4]. Review named beneficiaries on life insurance policies, credit union shares, and pension plans [1] [4].
  • Cross-border coordination: If your family member owns assets outside Saint Lucia or if a Power of Attorney is signed abroad for use in Saint Lucia, the foreign instrument must be notarized and legalized with an Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention before being registered before a Notary Royal and the Registry of Deeds and Mortgages in Castries [3] [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. Navigating medical, civil, and legal formalities across Kingstown or the Grenadine islands requires following a specific statutory sequence so that burial, social security claims, and estate administration can proceed without delay. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps in the order they must be completed.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or institutional deaths: When a death occurs at Milton Cato Memorial Hospital in Kingstown, a district hospital, or a private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [3].
  • Deaths at home under medical care: If your family member died at home from natural causes while under recent treatment by a registered physician, contact that physician or the District Medical Officer immediately so they can attend, verify the death, and issue the medical cause-of-death certificate required for civil registration [1] [3].
  • Sudden, unexpected, or unattended deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, unexplained, or occurred without a physician having treated the deceased recently, notify the Royal Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Police Force and the district Coroner (ordinarily the District Magistrate) before moving the body [1]. The Coroner may direct a post-mortem examination by a forensic pathologist before issuing a Coroner's warrant or certificate permitting registration and burial [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and mandatory registration: Under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, every death occurring in the state must be registered, and registration should take place within three (3) days of the death [1]. By law, no burial or cremation may take place until the death has been duly registered or authorized by the Registrar or Coroner [1]. Late registration after twelve months requires explicit written authority from the Registrar General and payment of prescribed late fees [1].
  • Qualified informants: The death may be registered by a relative present at the death or in attendance during the last illness, a relative residing in the same registration district, a person present at the death, the occupier of the house or institution where the death occurred, or the person causing the body to be buried [1].
  • Where to register and obtain certificates: In Kingstown, registration and certificate applications are handled at the Civil Registry Department (High Court / Registry Office) [1] [2]. In outer districts and the Grenadines (such as Bequia, Union Island, Canouan, and Mustique), initial registration is completed through the District Registrar at the District Revenue Office or Post Office [1]. Certified extracts of the death certificate are issued by the Civil Registry Department for an official fee of EC $15.00 per copy [2]. We advise ordering several certified copies immediately for banking, social security, and court probate filings [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: Once the death is registered, the Registrar (or the Coroner, where an inquest is opened) issues the official certificate for burial [1]. A licensed funeral home in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines coordinates mortuary care, cemetery booking with the municipal or town board authorities, and environmental health clearance [1] [3].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member is to be repatriated abroad (or brought to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines from overseas), the funeral director must obtain an official Death Certificate from the Civil Registry Department, a medical certificate confirming the body is free of communicable disease and has been properly embalmed in a hermetically sealed casket, and an export/transit permit from the Chief Medical Officer at the Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment [2] [3].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. If certified death certificates or court documents must be used in another Hague Convention country, request an Apostille certificate through the Registrar of the High Court / Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Kingstown [2] [5].

steps.title: Notify National Insurance Services, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• National Insurance Funeral Grant and Survivor Benefits: Report the death promptly to the National Insurance Services (NIS) in Kingstown [4]. If the deceased met the statutory contribution conditions (or was receiving an NIS pension or employment injury benefit), the person who paid or is responsible for the funeral expenses can apply for the NIS Funeral Grant by submitting the official claim form, the certified Death Certificate, and itemized funeral invoices within six months of death [4]. Surviving spouses and dependent children may also claim an NIS Survivor's Benefit [4].
  • Identity, voter, and tax cancellation: Surrender the deceased's national identification card to the Electoral Office, present the passport for cancellation at the Passport and Immigration Department, and notify the Inland Revenue Department to close income tax and property tax accounts [1] [2].
  • Banks, credit unions, and insurers: Provide certified copies of the Death Certificate to all local commercial banks, credit unions (such as the General Employees Co-operative Credit Union), and life insurance companies [2]. Individual accounts held solely in the deceased's name will be frozen until an official Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration is produced [1] [2] [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain Probate or Letters of Administration
steps.html:
• Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court probate jurisdiction: Estate succession in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is supervised by the High Court of Justice (Probate Division) of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court, administered through the High Court Registry in Kingstown under the Administration of Estates Act and the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (Non-Contentious Probate and Administration of Estates) Rules [1] [5].
  • Grant of Probate vs. Letters of Administration: If your family member left a valid Will, the named executor applies to the High Court Registry for a Grant of Probate [1] [5]. If the deceased died intestate (without a Will), the next-of-kin applies for Letters of Administration following the statutory order of priority [1] [5].
  • Estate duty declaration and cross-border resealing: Applications require the certified Death Certificate, the original Will (if any), an Inventory and Declaration of the Value of the Estate for stamp/estate duty assessment, and newspaper advertisements for creditors [1] [2] [5]. Where a Grant of Probate or Administration has already been issued by a court in another Commonwealth jurisdiction, it can be resealed by the High Court in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines to release local real estate or bank assets [5].

closingQuestion: Could you let us know whether the death occurred in Kingstown or on one of the Grenadine islands, and whether your family member left a Will or held assets outside Saint Vincent and the Grenadines so we can tailor the exact registration and probate requirements?
