title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Libya: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Libya: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Libya: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Libya. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order to obtain medical certification, register the death, arrange burial or international repatriation, notify social security and financial institutions, and administer the estate under Libyan law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public hospital or licensed private clinic overseen by the Health Information and Documentation Center and the Ministry of Health in Libya, the attending physician examines the deceased and issues the official medical death notification (Tabligh Wafat) stating the clinical cause, date, and hour of death [1] [2] [6].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home from natural causes, a physician from the local public health center or municipal polyclinic must be called to verify the death and issue the medical report required for civil registration, or two adult witnesses must accompany the informant to the municipal registry office with a clinical confirmation [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, or lacked prior medical attendance, the local police station and the Public Prosecution (Al-Niyaba Al-Amma) must be notified immediately [1]. The Public Prosecution orders a forensic medical examination before issuing a formal burial and registration clearance [1].
  • Required identification: Keep the deceased's National Number (Al-Raqam Al-Watani), Libyan National ID card or passport, and the informant's identification ready for the certifying doctor and hospital administration [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Authority
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and competent office: Under Libyan Law No. 36 of 1968 on Civil Status, a death occurring in Libya must be reported to the local branch of the Civil Registry Authority (Maslahat Al-Ahwal Al-Madaniya) in the municipality where the death occurred within 24 hours, or up to 7 days in remote localities [1] [2].
  • Authorized informants: The declaration may be made by an adult next of kin, a household member present at the death, the hospital director, or an authorized representative holding a notarized power of attorney [1].
  • Updating the Family Book and National Number record: Upon receiving the medical death notification and the deceased's identity documents, the Civil Registry Authority records the death in the civil register, updates the family's civil status record (Kutaib Al-Aila), deactivates the National Number, and issues official Death Certificates (Shahadat Wafat) [1] [2].
  • Late registration procedure: If the statutory reporting period is missed, registration requires an administrative verification or a summary ruling from the competent primary court before the civil registrar can issue the certificate [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Mortuary Permits, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Municipal burial permit: No burial may take place in Libya without a formal Burial Permit (Tasrih bil-Dafn) issued by the local Civil Registry Authority branch or authorized by the Public Prosecution in forensic cases [1]. Local municipal cemetery administrations arrange burial in accordance with statutory public health rules and religious rites [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or if the family wishes to transport the body abroad, the family or an appointed international funeral director must obtain an embalming certificate and a non-contagious disease clearance from the municipal health office, a transit permit (Laissez-Passer for a corpse) from the Libyan authorities, and consular clearance from the destination country's embassy [1] [2].
  • Document legalization: Libya is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consequently, any Libyan Death Certificate, medical report, or succession deed intended for use abroad must be authenticated by the Libyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation and subsequently legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Social Security survivor pension and funeral grant: Under Libyan Law No. 13 of 1980 on Social Security, when an insured worker or pensioner dies, eligible dependents must notify the Social Security Fund (Sanduq Al-Daman Al-Ijtima'i) [3] [4]. The Social Security Fund pays a statutory lump-sum funeral grant to cover immediate burial costs and calculates monthly survivor pensions for eligible widows, widowers, minor or student children, unmarried daughters, and dependent parents [4] [5].
  • Required claim dossier: To claim survivor benefits from the Social Security Fund, submit the official Death Certificate, an updated family status extract from the Civil Registry Authority, the LegalHeirs Determination Deed (Faridat Al-Waratha), and bank account details for the beneficiaries [2] [4] [5].
  • Banks, employers, and public agencies: Present certified copies of the Death Certificate to the deceased's employer (to settle final wages and end-of-service indemnities), commercial banks in Libya (which freeze individual accounts pending the court succession order), the Tax Department, and the Traffic Licensing Department if vehicles were registered in the deceased's name [2] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain the Court Succession Certificate
steps.html:
• Sharia Court determination of heirs (Faridat Al-Waratha): Estate succession in Libya is governed by statutory inheritance provisions derived from Islamic jurisprudence and administered by the Personal Status Chamber of the competent Primary Court (Mahkamat Al-Ahwal Al-Shakhsiya) [1] [3]. An adult heir or legal representative petitions the court with the Death Certificate, the Family Book extract, and two credible witnesses to obtain the official Determination of Heirs decree (Hujjat Hasr Al-Waratha / Faridat Al-Waratha), which lists all legal heirs and their exact statutory fractional shares [1] [2].
  • Validation of wills (Wasiya): If the deceased left a written will, it is enforceable under Libyan law up to one-third of the net estate after funeral expenses and debts are paid (unless all adult heirs consent to a larger bequest), and must be presented to the Personal Status Court for validation [1] [3].
  • Asset inventory, minors, and transfer of property: If any heir is a minor or lacks legal capacity, the court and guardianship authorities supervise the inventory and safeguarding of their share [3]. Once debts are settled, heirs present the Faridat Al-Waratha to commercial banks to release funds and to the Socialist Real Estate Registration and Documentation Authority to transfer real property titles [1] [2].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign assets: Heirs residing outside Libya may appoint a local lawyer or relative in Libya through a special Power of Attorney (Tawkil Khas) notarized abroad and legalized by the Libyan Embassy and the Libyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs [2].

ar.title: ماذا تفعل عند وفاة أحد الأقارب في ليبيا: الدليل الرسمي في 5 خطوات
ar.cardSummary: دليل رسمي من 5 خطوات بعد الوفاة في ليبيا: التبليغ الطبي عن الوفاة وتصريح الدفن، ترتيبات الجنازة، تسجيل الوفاة في الأحوال المدنية، مستحقات التقاعد والضمان الاجتماعي، وحصر الإرث والبنوك.
ar.introHtml: نتقدم إليكم بخالص التعازي وصادق المواساة في وفاة فقيد أسرتكم في دولة ليبيا. نوضح فيما يلي الخطوات الإدارية والقانونية الرسمية الخمس بالترتيب الزمني لاستخراج الشهادة الطبية للوفاة، وتسجيل الواقعة مدنياً، وترتيب الدفن أو نقل الجثمان دولياً، وإخطار هيئات الضمان الاجتماعي والمصارف، وإدارة التركة وفقاً للقانون الليبي.

steps.title: استخراج التبليغ الطبي عن الوفاة
steps.html:
• الوفيات داخل المستشفيات والمصحات: عند وقوع الوفاة في مستشفى عام أو مصحة خاصة مرخصة تخضع لإشراف مركز المعلومات والتوثيق الصحي ووزارة الصحة في ليبيا، يقوم الطبيب المعالج بفحص المتوفى وإصدار تبليغ الوفاة الطبي الرسمي الذي يوضح السبب السريري للوفاة وتاريخها وساعتها [1] [2] [6].
  • الوفيات في المنزل لأسباب طبيعية: إذا توفي فرد أسرتكم في المنزل لأسباب طبيعية، يتعين استدعاء طبيب من المركز الصحي العام المحلي أو العيادة المجمعة بالبلدية للتحقق من الوفاة وإصدار التقرير الطبي اللازم للقيد المدني، أو حضور شاهدين بالغين مع المبلِّغ أمام مكتب السجل المدني البلدي مرفقاً بالتأكيد الطبي [1] [2].
  • الوفيات المفاجئة أو العرضية أو غير المفسرة: إذا كانت الوفاة مفاجئة أو ناتجة عن حادث أو دون متابعة طبية سابقة، يجب إبلاغ مركز الشرطة المحلي والنيابة العامة على الفور [1]. وتأمر النيابة العامة بإجراء الكشف الطبي الشرعي قبل إصدار تصريح رسمي بالدفن والقيد المدني [1].
  • وثائق إثبات الهوية المطلوبة: ينبغي تجهيز الرقم الوطني للمتوفى وبطاقة الهوية الوطنية الليبية أو جواز السفر، بالإضافة إلى إثبات هوية المبلِّغ لتقديمها للطبيب الفاحص وإدارة المستشفى [1] [2].

steps.title: تسجيل الوفاة لدى مصلحة الأحوال المدنية
steps.html:
• المهلة القانونية والمكتب المختص: بموجب القانون الليبي رقم 36 لسنة 1968 بشأن الأحوال المدنية، يجب التبليغ عن الوفاة الواقعة في ليبيا لدى الفرع المحلي التابع لجهة مصلحة الأحوال المدنية في البلدية التي حدثت فيها الوفاة خلال أربع وعشرين ساعة، أو خلال مدة تصل إلى سبعة أيام في المناطق النائية [1] [2].
  • الأشخاص المكلفون بالتبليغ قانوناً: يجوز تقديم البلاغ من قبل أحد الأقارب البالغين، أو أحد المقيمين مع المتوفى في مسكن واحد ممن حضروا الوفاة، أو مدير المستشفى، أو ممثل قانوني مفوض بموجب توكيل رسمي موثق [1].
  • تحديث كتيب العائلة وقيد الرقم الوطني: فور استلام تبليغ الوفاة الطبي ومستندات هوية المتوفى، تقوم مصلحة الأحوال المدنية بقيد الوفاة في السجل المدني، وتحديث سجل الأسرة في كتيب العائلة، وإيقاف الرقم الوطني للمتوفى، وإصدار شهادات الوفاة الرسمية [1] [2].
  • إجراءات القيد المتأخر (ساقط القيد): في حال انقضاء المهلة القانونية المقررة للتبليغ، يتطلب تسجيل الوفاة إجراء تحقق إداري أو استصدار أمر قضائي من المحكمة الجزئية أو الابتدائية المختصة قبل أن يتمكن أمين السجل المدني من إصدار الشهادة [1].

steps.title: ترتيب إجراءات الدفن وتصاريح المقابر أو نقل الجثمان دولياً
steps.html:
• تصريح الدفن البلدي: لا يجوز إجراء أي دفن في ليبيا دون الحصول على تصريح بالدفن رسمي صادر عن الفرع المحلي لجهة مصلحة الأحوال المدنية أو مأذون به من النيابة العامة في الحالات الجنائية والشرعية [1]. وتتولى إدارات المقابر البلدية المحلية ترتيب الدفن وفقاً لاشتراطات الصحة العامة والشعائر الدينية [1] [2].
  • نقل الجثمان دولياً إلى الخارج: إذا كان المتوفى أجنبي الجنسية أو رغبت الأسرة في نقل الجثمان إلى خارج ليبيا، يجب على الأسرة أو مكتب نقل الجثامين الدولي المفوض استخراج شهادة تحنيط وشهادة خلو من الأمراض المعدية من مكتب الصحة البلدي، وتصريح مرور جثمان من السلطات الليبية المختصة، وموافقة قنصلية من سفارة دولة المقصد [1] [2].
  • تصديق المستندات الرسمية: ليبيا ليست طرفاً في اتفاقية لاهاي لعام 1961 (الأبوستيل). وبناءً على ذلك، فإن أي شهادة وفاة ليبية أو تقرير طبي أو فريضة شرعية يُراد استخدامها في الخارج يجب تصديقها أولاً من وزارة الخارجية والتعاون الدولي الليبية ثم تصديقها من سفارة أو قنصلية الدولة المقصودة [2].

steps.title: إخطار صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي والضرائب والمصارف
steps.html:
• معاش المستحقين ومنحة الجنازة من الضمان الاجتماعي: بموجب قانون الضمان الاجتماعي الليبي رقم 13 لسنة 1980، عند وفاة المضمون العامل أو صاحب المعاش، يتعين على المستحقين إخطار صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي [3] [4]. ويصرف صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي منحة جنازة مقطوعة لتغطية نفقات الدفن العاجلة، كما يحتسب المعاشات الشهرية للمستحقين من الأرامل والأبناء القصر أو الطلبة والبنات غير المتزوجات والوالدين المعالين [4] [5].
  • ملف المطالبة بالمستحقات الضمانية: للمطالبة بمستحقات الخلف لدى صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي، يجب تقديم شهادة الوفاة الرسمية، ومستخرج حديث للوضع العائلي من مصلحة الأحوال المدنية، وحجة حصر الورثة (فريضة الورثة)، وبيانات الحسابات المصرفية للمستفيدين [2] [4] [5].
  • المصارف وجهات العمل والمؤسسات العامة: يجب تقديم نسخ مصدقة من شهادة الوفاة إلى جهة عمل المتوفى (لتسوية المرتبات النهائية ومكافأة نهاية الخدمة)، والمصارف التجارية في ليبيا (التي تقوم بتجميد الحسابات الفردية لحين إبراز الفريضة الشرعية الصادرة عن المحكمة)، ومصلحة الضرائب، وقسم التراخيص والمرور إذا كانت هناك مركبات مسجلة باسم المتوفى [2] [3].

steps.title: إدارة التركة واستخراج فريضة الورثة من المحكمة
steps.html:
• استخراج فريضة الورثة من محكمة الأحوال الشخصية: تخضع المواريث في ليبيا لأحكام الشريعة الإسلامية المقننة، وتختص بها دائرة الأحوال الشخصية في المحكمة المختصة [1] [3]. ويتقدم أحد الورثة البالغين أو ممثلهم القانوني بطلب إلى المحكمة مرفقاً بشهادة الوفاة ومستخرج كتيب العائلة وشهادة شاهدين عدلين لاستصدار حجة حصر الورثة الرسمية (فريضة الورثة)، التي تحدد جميع الورثة الشرعيين وأنصبتهم الشرعية الدقيقة [1] [2].
  • إثبات وتنفيذ الوصايا: إذا ترك المتوفى وصية مكتوبة، فإنها تنفذ بموجب القانون الليبي في حدود ثلث صافي التركة بعد سداد نفقات التجهيز والديون (إلا إذا أجاز جميع الورثة البالغين ما زاد على الثلث)، ويجب عرضها على محكمة الأحوال الشخصية لإثباتها [1] [3].
  • جرد التركة وحماية أموال القصر ونقل الملكية: إذا كان بين الورثة قاصر أو فاقد للأهلية، تشرف المحكمة والهيئة العامة لشؤون القاصرين على جرد حصته وحفظها [3]. وبعد سداد الديون، يقدم الورثة فريضة الورثة إلى المصارف التجارية لصرف الأموال وإلى مصلحة التسجيل العقاري والتوثيق لنقل ملكية العقارات [1] [2].
  • الورثة المقيمون في الخارج والأصول الأجنبية: يحق للورثة المقيمين خارج ليبيا تفويض محامٍ محلي أو قريب في ليبيا بموجب توكيل خاص يوثق في الخارج ويصدق من السفارة الليبية ووزارة الخارجية الليبية [2].

ar.closingQuestion: ما هي البلدية المعنية في ليبيا، وهل كان فقيد أسرتكم يحمل جنسية أجنبية أو ترك أصولاً أو ورثة خارج ليبيا لنأخذ ذلك في الاعتبار ضمن هذه الإجراءات؟

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Libya: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Libya: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Libya: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that your family member in Libya has been diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness. Below, we set out the five main medical, legal, and administrative steps to organize while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity under Libyan law.

steps.title: Coordinate Specialist Medical Care, Pain Management, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public tertiary and oncology care: In Libya, patients diagnosed with serious or life-limiting conditions receive public treatment through major regional hospitals and specialized institutes overseen by the Ministry of Health and the Health Information and Documentation Center [1]. For oncology patients, the National Cancer Control Authority coordinates chemotherapy, radiotherapy, supportive symptom relief, and unified patient registration across specialized cancer centers in Tripoli, Benghazi, Sabratha, and Misrata [1] [2].
  • Symptom control and home-based care: Because standalone inpatient hospices are limited in Libya, supportive care and prescription pain management are coordinated directly through hospital oncology or internal medicine departments [1] [2]. Families should request a comprehensive clinical report (Taqrir Tibbi Mufassal) and an itemized medication plan from the treating consultant so that community clinics or home-visiting nurses can safely administer supportive care [1] [2].
  • Medical treatment committees and health coverage: Citizens registered with a valid National Number are entitled to free treatment in public facilities, and complex cases requiring specialized procedures may be referred to Ministry of Health medical committees or supported through employer or private medical insurance policies [1] [3].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Family Medical Spokesperson
steps.html:
• Statutory framework for medical consent: Under Libyan medical responsibility rules and public health regulations, a patient who retains mental capacity holds the primary right to give or withhold informed consent for surgical and clinical procedures [1] [3].
  • Written care preferences: Although Libyan legislation does not establish a standalone statutory registry for living wills or Do-Not-Resuscitate orders, your family member can sign a written statement of treatment preferences and discuss palliative goals of care directly with the attending hospital physician so that those wishes are documented in the clinical file [1] [2].
  • Designating a medical proxy or representative: While capacity is intact, your family member can execute a notarized authorization naming a trusted adult relative as their primary medical representative to receive confidential clinical updates, request medical files, and coordinate with hospital medical committees if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarial Powers of Attorney (Tawkil Rasmi): Under the Libyan Civil Code and notarial laws, a Power of Attorney is only valid if executed while the principal possesses full mental and legal capacity (Ahliya Kamila) [3]. Your family member should appear before a licensed Libyan Notary Public (Muharrir Uqud) - or arrange a home or hospital bedside visit by a notary - to execute either a General Power of Attorney (Tawkil Aam) for routine administration or a Special Power of Attorney (Tawkil Khas) explicitly authorizing property transactions or litigation [3].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Libyan commercial banks frequently require either their own internal account mandate form signed in person by the account holder or a recent Special Power of Attorney that explicitly names the bank and lists permitted actions (such as withdrawing pension deposits, managing standing orders, and requesting statements) [3].
  • Consequences of losing capacity without a mandate: Remember that under Libyan civil law, a Power of Attorney terminates if the principal loses legal capacity or passes away; if capacity is lost before arrangements are made, relatives must petition the Personal Status Court for a formal guardianship or curatorship order (Hajr / Qiwama) to manage assets [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Chronic Illness Benefits, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Social Security disability pension: Under Libyan Law No. 13 of 1980 on Social Security, an insured worker whose illness results in severe or total incapacity to work may apply to the Social Security Fund (Sanduq Al-Daman Al-Ijtima'i) for a disability pension [4] [5]. A medical board appointed by the Social Security Fund evaluates the clinical dossier and determines the degree of disability and whether the patient requires the regular assistance of another person for daily living activities [4] [5] [6].
  • Constant-attendance supplement and social care: Where the medical commission confirms that the insured person requires continuous daily care from a caregiver, Law No. 13 of 1980 provides for an additional care allowance increase of up to 25 percent of the pension, alongside social care services administered by the Social Security Fund [4] [6] [7].
  • Paid sick leave for employed patients and caregivers: Under Libyan labor and civil service rules, an employed patient is entitled to statutory paid sick leave upon submitting certified medical reports, while employed family caregivers can request compassionate leave or unpaid family care leave through their employer's human resources department [3] [4].

steps.title: Organize Civil Status Records, Wills (Wasiya), and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Verify Civil Registry and Family Book records: Ensure that all family members, marriages, and births are accurately recorded in the Family Book (Kutaib Al-Aila) and the National Number database at the Civil Registry Authority, as these records form the legal basis for future pension and succession claims [3].
  • Drafting a valid will (Wasiya) under Libyan law: Under Libyan personal status law, a person of sound mind may execute a formal written will (Wasiya) notarized before a Notary Public or registered with the Personal Status Court [3]. Under statutory Sharia succession rules, testamentary bequests are valid up to one-third of the net estate (after debts and caregiving costs) and cannot alter the fixed fractional shares of legal heirs unless the adult heirs consent after the testator's lifetime [3].
  • Consolidate property deeds and cross-border documents: Gather original real estate title deeds, vehicle ownership books, bank account numbers, and social security registration cards in a secure folder [3] [5]. If family members or assets are located outside Libya, remember that Libya is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so any cross-border Power of Attorney or estate document must be legalized through the Libyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant foreign embassy [3].

closingQuestion: Which city in Libya is your family member receiving care in, and is your family member insured under the Social Security Fund or holding assets or family ties outside Libya?

ar.title: المرض العضال والإجراءات القانونية والطبية في ليبيا: الدليل الرسمي في 5 خطوات
ar.cardSummary: دليل رسمي من 5 خطوات للتخطيط الطبي والقانوني في حالات المرض المتقدم في ليبيا: الرعاية التلطيفية والمنزلية، القرارات الطبية وتعيين المفوض الصحي، الوكالات الرسمية، إجازات المرافق وتنظيم الوصية.
ar.introHtml: ندرك أن أحد أفراد أسرتكم في دولة ليبيا قد شُخصت إصابته بمرض متقدم أو مهدد للحياة. نوضح فيما يلي الخطوات الطبية والقانونية والإدارية الخمس الرئيسية التي ينبغي تنظيمها بينما لا يزال فرد أسرتكم متمتعاً بكامل أهليته العقلية والقانونية لاتخاذ القرار وفقاً للقانون الليبي.

steps.title: تنسيق الرعاية الطبية التخصصية وإدارة الألم والتغطية الصحية
steps.html:
• الرعاية التخصصية وعلاج الأورام في القطاع العام: يتلقى المرضى المشخصون بحالات مرضية خطيرة أو مهددة للحياة في ليبيا العلاج الحكومي عبر المستشفيات المرجعية الكبرى والمعاهد التخصصية الخاضعة لإشراف وزارة الصحة وجهة مركز المعلومات والتوثيق الصحي [1]. وبالنسبة لمرضى الأورام، تتولى الهيئة الوطنية لمكافحة السرطان تنسيق العلاج الكيميائي والإشعاعي والرعاية الداعمة لتخفيف الأعراض والتسجيل الموحد للمرضى في مراكز علاج الأورام المتخصصة في طرابلس وبنغازي وصبراتة ومصراتة [1] [2].
  • السيطرة على الأعراض والرعاية المنزلية: نظراً لمحدودية دور الرعاية التلطيفية المستقلة في ليبيا، يتم تنسيق الرعاية الداعمة ووصف مسكنات الألم مباشرة عبر أقسام الأورام أو الباطنة في المستشفيات [1] [2]. وينبغي للأسرة طلب تقرير طبي مفصل وخطة دوائية موثقة من الطبيب الاستشاري المعالج ليتمكن أطباء العيادات المجتمعية أو فرق التمريض المنزلي من تقديم الرعاية الداعمة بأمان [1] [2].
  • اللجان الطبية العلاجية والتغطية الصحية: يحق للمواطنين المسجلين برقم وطني ساري المفعول تلقي العلاج المجاني في المرافق الصحية العامة، كما يمكن إحالة الحالات المعقدة التي تتطلب إجراءات تخصصية إلى اللجان الطبية بوزارة الصحة أو تغطيتها عبر وثائق التأمين الطبي الخاصة أو التابعة لجهات العمل [1] [3].

steps.title: توثيق التفضيلات العلاجية وتسمية المتحدث الطبي باسم الأسرة
steps.html:
• الإطار القانوني للموافقة الطبية المستنيرة: بموجب قواعد المسؤولية الطبية ولوائح الصحة العامة في ليبيا، يتمتع المريض الكامل الأهلية العقلية بالحق الأصيل في منح أو حجب الموافقة المستنيرة على الإجراءات الجراحية والسريرية [1] [3].
  • تدوين الرغبات العلاجية خطياً: على الرغم من أن التشريعات الليبية لا تنشئ سجلاً قانونياً مستقلاً لوصايا الحياة أو أوامر عدم الإنعاش، يمكن لفرد أسرتكم توقيع إفادة خطية بتفضيلاته العلاجية ومناقشة أهداف الرعاية التلطيفية مباشرة مع الطبيب المعالج بالمستشفى بحيث يتم توثيق هذه الرغبات في الملف السريري للمريض [1] [2].
  • تعيين وكيل أو ممثل طبي من الأسرة: أثناء سلامة الأهلية القانونية، يمكن لفرد أسرتكم تحرير تفويض موثق يسمي قريباً بالغاً موثوقاً به كممثل طبي رئيسي لتلقي التقارير السريرية السرية وطلب الملفات الطبية والتنسيق مع اللجان الطبية بالمستشفى إذا تعذر على المريض التواصل لاحقاً [1] [3].

steps.title: تحرير التوكيلات الرسمية والتفويضات المصرفية أثناء اكتمال الأهلية
steps.html:
• التوكيلات الرسمية الموثقة لدى محرر العقود: بموجب القانون المدني الليبي وقوانين التوثيق، لا يصح التوكيل إلا إذا أُبرم والموكل متمتع بالأهلية العقلية والقانونية الكاملة [3]. وينبغي لفرد أسرتكم الحضور أمام محرر عقود مرخص في ليبيا - أو ترتيب انتقال محرر العقود إلى المنزل أو المستشفى - لإبرام توكيل عام للإدارة المعتادة أو توكيل خاص ينص صراحةً على التصرفات العقارية أو التقاضي [3].
  • تفويضات المصارف التجارية: تشترط المصارف التجارية الليبية في كثير من الأحيان إما توقيع صاحب الحساب شخصياً على نموذج التفويض المصرفي الداخلي المعتمد لدى المصرف أو إبراز توكيل خاص حديث يذكر اسم المصرف صراحةً ويحدد الصلاحيات المسموح بها (مثل سحب المعاشات المودعة وإدارة أوامر الدفع وطلب كشوف الحساب) [3].
  • الآثار القانونية لفقدان الأهلية دون تفويض: تجدر الإشارة إلى أنه بموجب القانون المدني الليبي، ينتهي العمل بالتوكيل إذا فقد الموكل أهليته القانونية أو توفي؛ وفي حال فقدان الأهلية قبل اتخاذ الترتيبات اللازمة، يتعين على الأقارب التقدم بطلب إلى محكمة الأحوال الشخصية لاستصدار حكم بالحجر أو القوامة لإدارة الأموال [3].

steps.title: تفعيل معاشات العجز ومنافع الأمراض المزمنة ودعم مقدمي الرعاية
steps.html:
• معاش العجز الصحي من الضمان الاجتماعي: بموجب قانون الضمان الاجتماعي الليبي رقم 13 لسنة 1980، يحق للمضمون العامل الذي يؤدي مرضه إلى عجز شديد أو كلي عن العمل التقدم بطلب إلى صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي للحصول على معاش عجز صحي [4] [5]. وتتولى لجنة طبية معينة من قبل صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي تقييم الملف الطبي وتحديد درجة العجز وما إذا كان المريض يحتاج إلى الاستعانة الدائمة بشخص آخر للقيام بأعباء الحياة اليومية [4] [5] [6].
  • إعانة المرافقة الدائمة والرعاية الاجتماعية: عندما تقرر اللجنة الطبية أن المضمون يحتاج إلى رعاية يومية مستمرة من مرافق، ينص القانون رقم 13 لسنة 1980 على منح علاوة رعاية إضافية تصل إلى خمسة وعشرين بالمائة من قيمة المعاش، إلى جانب خدمات الرعاية الاجتماعية التي يديرها صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي [4] [6] [7].
  • الإجازات المرضية المدفوعة للمرضى العاملين ومقدمي الرعاية: بموجب قوانين العمل والخدمة المدنية الليبية، يستحق المريض العامل إجازة مرضية مدفوعة الأجر عند تقديم تقارير طبية معتمدة، بينما يمكن لأفراد الأسرة العاملين الذين يتولون رعايته طلب إجازة اضطرارية أو إجازة رعاية أسرية بدون مرتب عبر إدارة الموارد البشرية في جهة عملهم [3] [4].

steps.title: تنظيم قيود الأحوال المدنية والوصايا ومستندات الملكية
steps.html:
• التحقق من قيود السجل المدني وكتيب العائلة: ننصح بالتأكد من تسجيل جميع أفراد الأسرة وحالات الزواج والمواليد بدقة في كتيب العائلة وقاعدة بيانات الرقم الوطني لدى مصلحة الأحوال المدنية، إذ تشكل هذه السجلات الأساس القانوني لأي مطالبات مستقبلية بالمعاشات أو المواريث [3].
  • تحرير وصية صحيحة وفق القانون الليبي: بموجب قانون الأحوال الشخصية الليبي، يجوز للشخص كامل الأهلية العقلية تحرير وصية مكتوبة موثقة أمام محرر عقود أو مسجلة لدى محكمة الأحوال الشخصية [3]. ووفقاً لقواعد الميراث الشرعية المقررة قانوناً، تصح الوصية في حدود ثلث صافي التركة (بعد سداد الديون ونفقات الرعاية والتجهيز) ولا تغير الأنصبة الشرعية المقررة للورثة إلا إذا أجازها الورثة البالغون بعد وفاة الموصي [3].
  • جمع سندات الملكية والمستندات العابرة للحدود: يُستحسن حفظ شهائد الملكية العقارية الأصلية وكتيبات ملكية المركبات وأرقام الحسابات المصرفية وبطاقات التسجيل الضماني في ملف آمن [3] [5]. وإذا كان هناك أفراد أسرة أو أصول خارج ليبيا، يُراعى أن ليبيا ليست طرفاً في اتفاقية لاهاي للأبوستيل، ولذلك يجب تصديق أي توكيل أو مستند عابر للحدود عبر وزارة الخارجية الليبية والسفارة الأجنبية المعنية [3].

ar.closingQuestion: في أي مدينة في ليبيا يتلقى فرد أسرتكم الرعاية الطبية، وهل هو مضمون لدى صندوق الضمان الاجتماعي أو يمتلك أصولاً أو روابط أسرية خارج ليبيا؟

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Botswana: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Botswana: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Botswana: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Botswana. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order to obtain medical certification, register the death, arrange burial or international repatriation, claim pension and survivor benefits, and report the estate to the Master of the High Court in Botswana.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification or Traditional Authority Confirmation of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or clinical facility: When a death occurs in a public hospital, district clinic, or private hospital in Botswana, the attending medical officer examines the deceased and issues the official medical Notice of Death (Form CR B-2 / Death Notification tear-off) certifying the cause, date, and place of death [1].
  • Deaths at home or outside a health facility: If your family member died at home or outside a medical institution in a village or rural area, the family must obtain a written Letter of Confirmation of Death from the local traditional authority (Kgosi / Dikgosi), accompanied by a formal statement from the informant and statements from two independent adult witnesses holding valid national identity cards (Omang) [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unnatural deaths: If the death was unexpected, accidental, or lacked prior medical attendance, the Botswana Police Service must be notified immediately to open an inquest docket and arrange a post-mortem examination by a forensic pathologist before releasing the body and issuing the medical death notification [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Department of Civil and National Registration
steps.html:
• Statutory 30-day registration deadline: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Cap. 30:01), every death occurring in Botswana must be registered within 30 days at a regional or district office of the Department of Civil and National Registration [1].
  • Required documents for timely registration: The informant (a next of kin, spouse, adult relative, or person authorized in writing by the family) must submit the medical Death Notification tear-off (or Kgosi confirmation letter and witness statements for non-institutional deaths), the deceased's original Botswana National Identity Card (Omang) for citizens or valid passport for non-citizens, and the informant's own valid Omang or passport [1].
  • Late registration (after 30 days): If a death is reported more than 30 days after occurrence, it is classified as a late registration and requires an official hospital or Kgosi confirmation letter, formal declarant and witness statements with certified ID copies, and administrative clearance by the Registrar before the official Death Certificate is issued [1].
  • Collection of the Death Certificate: The processed Death Certificate may only be collected by an immediate next of kin or a representative holding written family authorization and presenting a valid Omang or passport [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial order and licensed funeral parlours: Once the medical Death Notification or Death Certificate is issued by the Department of Civil and National Registration, a licensed funeral director in Botswana can transfer the deceased from the hospital mortuary and coordinate a municipal or village cemetery burial permit or cremation clearance [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported outside Botswana, the appointed funeral provider must obtain an official Death Certificate, a non-infectious disease certificate from the Ministry of Health port health authorities, an embalming certificate, a removal/export permit, and consular clearance from the destination country's high commission or embassy [1].
  • Apostille and document authentication: Botswana is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Official Botswana Death Certificates and court succession documents required for legal use in another Apostille convention country can be authenticated with a Hague Apostille through the Administration of Justice or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while documents going to non-Apostille countries require diplomatic legalization [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Pension Funds, Employers, Banks, and Tax Authorities
steps.html:
• Botswana Public Officers Pension Fund (BPOPF) and occupational pensions: If the deceased was a public servant or pensioner covered by the Botswana Public Officers Pension Fund, survivors must submit a Death Notification form, the Disposal of Death Benefits Questionnaire, certified copies of the Death Certificate, marriage certificate, and beneficiaries' Omang cards or birth certificates [3]. Under the Retirement Funds Act, pension death benefits are investigated and distributed equitably by the Board of Trustees to verified dependants and nominees rather than falling automatically into the general civil estate [3].
  • Employer terminal benefits and commercial banks: Notify the deceased's employer to claim accrued leave pay, terminal gratuities, or group life assurance proceeds, and present certified copies of the Death Certificate to commercial banks in Botswana, which freeze individual accounts until an executor or Master's representative is formally appointed [2] [4].
  • Botswana Unified Revenue Service (BURS) and identity records: The Department of Civil and National Registration cancels the deceased's Omang upon registration, and the executor or family representative must notify the tax authority to finalize any outstanding income tax assessments [1] [2].

steps.title: Report and Administer the Estate Before the Master of the High Court
steps.html:
• Mandatory 14-day estate reporting: Under the Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 31:01), when a person dies leaving property or a will in Botswana, the death and estate must be reported within 14 days to the Office of the Master of the High Court (located in Gaborone, Francistown, Lobatse, or Maun) [2] [4] [5].
  • Civil vs. customary estates: Civil marriage estates, testate estates (where the deceased left a valid Last Will and Testament), and complex commercial estates fall under the jurisdiction of the Office of the Master of the High Court, whereas estates of citizens subject solely to customary law without a civil will may be administered through the local Customary Court (Kgotla) with referral to the Master where financial institutions require formal Letters of Administration [2] [4] [5].
  • Required estate opening dossier and Next-of-Kin Meeting: To open an estate file with the Office of the Master of the High Court, submit the Death Notice form, certified Death Certificate, original Will (if testate), a preliminary Inventory of all movable and immovable assets and liabilities, marriage certificate, and certified ID copies of the next of kin [2] [5] [6]. For intestate estates, the Master convenes a Next-of-Kin Meeting to select an Executor Dative, issues Letters of Administration, and reviews the final Liquidation and Distribution Plan before assets and Deeds Registry property titles are transferred to heirs [2] [4] [6].

closingQuestion: Which district or city in Botswana did the death occur in, and did your family member leave a written will, a public or private pension, or assets subject to civil or customary estate administration?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Botswana: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Botswana: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Botswana: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that your family member in Botswana has been diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness. Below, we set out the five key medical, legal, and administrative steps to organize in order while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity in Botswana.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home-Based Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public hospital and community home-based care: In Botswana, patients facing serious or life-limiting conditions receive specialist treatment and pain management through referral hospitals (such as Princess Marina Hospital in Gaborone and Nyangabgwe Referral Hospital in Francistown) alongside district Community Home-Based Care (CHBC) teams coordinated with local clinics [1] [2]. Ask the treating specialist for a written clinical summary, a symptom and pain management protocol, and a referral to the local clinic's home-based care nurse or a licensed community hospice program [1].
  • Medical aid schemes and dread-disease benefits: If your family member belongs to a Botswana medical aid society (such as BPOMAS, BOMaid, or Pula Medical Aid), notify the scheme's case management unit immediately to unlock oncology, chronic medication, or home-nursing benefits and verify annual benefit ceilings [1] [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and written care directives: Under Botswana's Public Health Act and medical ethics rules, an adult patient who retains mental capacity has the right to accept or refuse medical interventions [1] [2]. While Botswana does not have a standalone statutory registry for living wills, your family member can sign a written advance medical directive stating preferences regarding intensive care, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and palliative pain relief, and provide signed copies to the attending physician and close family members [1] [2].
  • Designating a family medical spokesperson: While capacity is intact, your family member should execute a signed written authorization naming a trusted adult relative as their primary healthcare contact so hospital clinicians can share confidential medical records and consult that representative if the patient can no longer communicate [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• General and Special Powers of Attorney: Under Roman-Dutch common law as applied in Botswana, a Power of Attorney is valid only while the principal (grantor) possesses full mental capacity [2] [4]. Your family member should sign a General Power of Attorney for routine financial administration and, if immovable property or land transactions may be required, a Special Power of Attorney attested by two competent adult witnesses or a Notary Public in compliance with Deeds Registry rules [2] [4].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Commercial banks in Botswana generally require their own internal third-party mandate or signatory form to be signed in person (or verified via a bank official's home or hospital visit) alongside certified copies of both parties' National Identity Cards (Omang) or passports [1] [2].
  • Important legal limitation on enduring capacity: Under Botswana common law, a standard Power of Attorney does not survive supervening mental incapacity; if the principal loses mental capacity, the Power of Attorney lapses by operation of law and family members must apply to the High Court of Botswana (in consultation with the Office of the Master of the High Court) for the appointment of a Curator Bonis to administer the patient's property and financial affairs [2] [4] [5].

steps.title: Activate Ill-Health Retirement, Disability Benefits, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Ill-health retirement and pension nominations (BPOPF and private funds): If your family member is an active public officer or member of the Botswana Public Officers Pension Fund (or another occupational retirement fund regulated under the Retirement Funds Act), request a medical board assessment for ill-health retirement benefits and review any group critical-illness or permanent disability cover attached to employment [3]. At the same time, submit an updated Nomination of Beneficiaries Form and annuity election form with the Botswana Public Officers Pension Fund so the Board of Trustees has a current record of financial dependants and nominees [3].
  • Statutory sick leave and caregiver arrangements: Under the Employment Act of Botswana, employed patients are entitled to statutory paid sick leave upon producing a certificate from a registered medical practitioner, while family caregivers should apply through their employer's human resources department for compassionate leave or flexible caregiving arrangements [1] [3].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Documents, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Verify national identity and civil registry records: Confirm that your family member's Botswana National Identity Card (Omang), birth certificate, and civil or customary marriage certificates are up to date with the Department of Civil and National Registration, and that all minor or dependent children's birth certificates accurately reflect parentage [1].
  • Execute a valid Last Will and Testament: Under the Wills Act (Cap. 31:04), a valid will in Botswana must be in writing and signed at the end by the testator (and on every preceding page if more than one page) in the simultaneous presence of two independent witnesses aged 14 or older who also sign in the testator's presence [2] [4] [5]. Note that anyone who witnesses a will (or their spouse) is disqualified from inheriting or serving as executor under that will [2] [4].
  • Clarify civil vs. customary property and cross-border assets: Prepare a clear written inventory of bank accounts, cattle holdings, Tribal Land Board certificates, Deeds Registry title deeds, and life insurance policies so the future executor can meet the statutory 14-day reporting requirement at the Office of the Master of the High Court [2] [4] [5]. If family members or assets are located outside Botswana, documents executed in Botswana can be certified with a Hague Apostille through the Administration of Justice for cross-border legal recognition [2] [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Eritrea: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Eritrea. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order to obtain medical certification, register the death with the regional administration, arrange burial or international repatriation, notify pension and banking institutions, and administer the estate under Eritrean law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Sub-Zoba Confirmation
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public referral or regional hospital (such as Orotta National Referral Hospital or Halibet Hospital in Asmara) overseen by the Ministry of Health in Eritrea, the attending physician examines the deceased and issues the official hospital medical death certificate (Dead Body Certificate) stating the cause, date, and time of death [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home from natural causes, the family must report the passing to the local administrative area (Kebabi) and the Sub-Zoba Administration, bringing adult witnesses who can attest to the death so the local administration can issue an official letter confirming the event [1] [3] [4].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, or unattended by a physician, the Eritrean Police Force must be notified immediately [1]. The police refer the body to a government hospital mortuary (such as Orotta Hospital in Asmara) for a forensic post-mortem examination and issue a formal police report before the body is released for burial or civil registration [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Public Registration Office
steps.html:
• Reporting through the Sub-Zoba and Zoba Administration: Under the Civil Code of the State of Eritrea and municipal civil registration rules, the informant (a next of kin, family representative, or authorized agent) takes the hospital medical death certificate (or witness statements and local administration confirmation) along with the deceased's Eritrean National Identity Card or passport to the local Sub-Zoba Administration to obtain an acknowledgement letter, and then submits the file to the regional Public Registration Office (Zoba Administration) [1] [3] [4].
  • Statutory registration timeframe and late filings: While civil registration provisions establish a primary reporting window of 30 days, notifications submitted after the initial period are processed through the Public Registration Office upon presentation of the hospital record or verified witness statements from the Sub-Zoba Administration [3] [4].
  • Issuance of the official Death Certificate: Once verified, the Public Registration Office records the death in the regional civil register, retains or cancels the deceased's local identity documents, and issues official Death Certificates in Tigrinya, Arabic, or English upon request [1] [3] [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Mortuary Clearance, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial permits: Hospital mortuaries in Eritrea (primarily located in Asmara and regional capitals) release the body once hospital charges are settled and the medical death certificate and Sub-Zoba burial authorization are issued [1]. Cremation facilities do not operate in Eritrea, so local interment takes place in designated municipal or religious cemeteries [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or diaspora national and the family wishes to repatriate the remains abroad, a specialized funeral and repatriation coordinator must obtain the official Death Certificate from the Public Registration Office, an embalming certificate and coffin sealing clearance from the Orotta Hospital pathology department and the Ministry of Health, a police clearance if applicable, and customs export clearance for air transport via Asmara International Airport [1] [2].
  • Document legalization (non-Apostille jurisdiction): Eritrea is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Any Eritrean Death Certificate, medical certificate, or court succession document intended for legal use abroad must first be authenticated by the Consular and Legal Affairs Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Asmara and then legalized by the foreign embassy or consulate representing the destination country [1].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• National Pension Scheme and public sector survivor benefits: Under the National Pension Scheme Establishment Proclamation (Proclamation No. 135/2003) and the Public Sector Pension Scheme Proclamation (Proclamation No. 136/2003), overseen by the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (also referred to as the Ministry of Labour and Human Welfare), eligible survivors of a covered civil servant, military member, or private-sector contributor may claim survivor pensions and statutory death benefits [5] [6]. Eligible dependents include the surviving spouse, minor or student children, and dependent parents [5] [6].
  • Commercial Bank of Eritrea and Housing and Commerce Bank: Present the official Death Certificate and the court-issued Certificate of Heirship to the Commercial Bank of Eritrea or the Housing and Commerce Bank of Eritrea to freeze individual accounts, verify balances, and transfer funds to the recognized heirs [1] [3].
  • Diaspora status and tax clearances: If the deceased held an Eritrean National ID and resided abroad, Eritrean administrative authorities and banks generally verify whether statutory diaspora rehabilitation tax clearances (the 2 percent diaspora tax) are in order before completing domestic property transfers or estate distributions in Eritrea [1] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain a Certificate of Heirship from the Zoba Court
steps.html:
• Succession and Probate before the Zoba Court: Inheritance and estate administration in Eritrea are governed by the Civil Code of the State of Eritrea (Book II on Family and Successions), alongside recognized customary and Sharia personal status rules where applicable [3] [4]. To establish legal authority over the estate, the heirs or their legal representative must petition the competent regional court (Zoba Court) for a formal Certificate of Heirship (Succession Certificate) confirming the identity of the lawful heirs and their respective shares, or validating the deceased's written will [1] [3].
  • Court verification and witness testimony: The Zoba Court reviews the Death Certificate from the Public Registration Office, family civil status records, any testamentary instrument, and sworn witness testimony, and publishes a notice allowing potential claimants or creditors to come forward before issuing the final succession decree [3] [4].
  • Transferring real property and cross-border representation: With the final Zoba Court succession decree, heirs can register the transfer of houses, land leases, or business licenses with the Cadastral Office and municipal land authorities [3]. Heirs living outside Eritrea can execute a Power of Attorney before an Eritrean Embassy or Consulate abroad (subsequently authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and registered with the Public Notary in Asmara) to authorize a local representative in Eritrea to complete the court and banking procedures on their behalf [1] [3].

closingQuestion: Which Zoba or city in Eritrea did the death occur in, and did your family member hold foreign citizenship or leave bank accounts or real property in Eritrea that require diaspora consular powers of attorney?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eritrea: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Eritrea: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that your family member in Eritrea has been diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness. Below, we set out the five main medical, legal, and administrative steps to organize in order while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity under Eritrean law.

steps.title: Coordinate Hospital Care, Symptom Management, and Public Health Coverage
steps.html:
• National referral and regional hospitals: In Eritrea, specialist medical care, chronic disease management, and inpatient supportive care are delivered primarily through public health facilities overseen by the Ministry of Health, led by Orotta National Referral Hospital and Halibet Hospital in Asmara as well as zonal referral hospitals across the six administrative regions (Zobas) [1] [2].
  • Palliative symptom control and home care: Because standalone private hospices do not operate in Eritrea, symptom relief, pain medication prescribing, and home follow-up plans are coordinated directly through the treating physician at the national or regional hospital in partnership with local community health clinics [1] [2]. Ask the hospital medical team for a comprehensive written medical summary, an ongoing analgesic and medication prescription schedule, and clear instructions for readmission if acute symptoms arise [1] [2].
  • Subsidized public healthcare fees: Public hospital and clinic services in Eritrea are heavily subsidized by the state, with modest statutory co-payments waived for patients holding a verified indigence or social-assistance certificate issued through their local Sub-Zoba Administration and the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare [1] [3].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Family Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Patient consent and clinical communication: Under Eritrean medical practice and civil law principles, an adult patient with intact mental capacity has the right to be informed of their diagnosis and to consent to or decline medical procedures [1] [2]. In practice, physicians in Eritrean hospitals work closely with the patient and senior family members when making major clinical decisions for advanced illness [1].
  • Written care preferences and designated spokesperson: Although Eritrea does not maintain a formal statutory registry for living wills or advance directives, your family member can sign a written statement expressing their preferences regarding invasive interventions, hospitalization, and comfort care, and place a copy in their hospital medical chart [1] [2]. While capacity is intact, your family member should also execute a written authorization designating a trusted adult relative in Eritrea as their primary medical contact to receive clinical reports and communicate with hospital medical boards [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Public Notary registration (Wekillina): Under the Civil Code of the State of Eritrea, an agency mandate or Power of Attorney (Wekillina) is legally valid only if granted while the principal retains full mental and legal capacity [4]. Your family member must appear before the Public Notary Office (under the Ministry of Justice / Zoba judicial administration) with their Eritrean National Identity Card and two witnesses to execute a notarized General Power of Attorney for routine administration or a Special Power of Attorney explicitly authorizing property sales, court representation, or banking transactions [4].
  • Mandates at the Commercial Bank of Eritrea and Housing and Commerce Bank: State banking institutions in Eritrea enforce strict in-person verification rules for account withdrawals and transfers [4]. While your family member is still able to attend in person (or receive an authorized official visit), register an explicit bank mandate or notarized Special Power of Attorney directly with the branch where their accounts are held [4].
  • Consequences of supervening incapacity: Under the Eritrean Civil Code, an ordinary Power of Attorney ceases to have effect if the grantor loses mental capacity; if capacity is lost without prior arrangements, family members must petition the Zoba Court for a formal judicial interdiction and guardianship order before they can manage bank accounts or immovable property [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Sick Leave, and Social Welfare Support
steps.html:
• National Pension Scheme invalidity benefits: Under the National Pension Scheme Establishment Proclamation (Proclamation No. 135/2003) and the Public Sector Pension Scheme Proclamation (Proclamation No. 136/2003), supervised by the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare, an insured public-sector or formal private-sector worker who becomes permanently incapable of gainful employment due to serious illness may apply for a permanent disability (invalidity) pension following certification by an official medical board [3] [5].
  • Paid sick leave under labour law: Under the Labour Proclamation of Eritrea (Proclamation No. 118/2001) and civil service regulations, an employed patient is entitled to statutory sick leave upon submitting a medical certificate from an authorized government hospital, while family caregivers can apply to their employer for compassionate or unpaid family leave [3] [5].
  • Community and disability support programmes: For vulnerable households or patients requiring mobility aids and community-based rehabilitation support, the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare coordinates community-based social protection and support through regional Zoba and Sub-Zoba social welfare offices [3].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Civil Status Records, and Cross-Border Property Documents
steps.html:
• Verify civil status records with the Public Registration Office: Ensure that your family member's Eritrean National Identity Card, birth record, marriage certificate, and family residence registry at the Sub-Zoba Administration and the regional Public Registration Office are complete and consistent in spelling across Tigrinya, Arabic, and English documents [4] [6].
  • Executing a valid Will under the Eritrean Civil Code: Under Book II of the Civil Code of the State of Eritrea, a person of sound mind may execute a formal Public Will (read and signed in the presence of a judge, public notary, or four witnesses, or two witnesses if deposited in a public registry) or a wholly handwritten Holographic Will that explicitly states the day, month, and year it is written and is signed by the testator [4] [6]. Having the will formally registered and deposited with the Public Notary or Zoba Court registry prevents later authenticity disputes [4].
  • Consolidate property titles and diaspora documentation: Gather original urban house title deeds (Cadastro), land lease certificates, bank passbooks, and pension records [4] [5]. If family members reside in the diaspora and will need to act on behalf of the patient or estate in Eritrea, note that Eritrea is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention: any Power of Attorney or civil document executed abroad must be signed or legalized at an Eritrean Embassy or Consulate, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Asmara, and accompanied by proof of current diaspora status (including clearance of the 2 percent rehabilitation tax where required for domestic property transactions) [3] [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Eswatini: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Eswatini: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Eswatini: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Eswatini. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order to handle medical certification, civil registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social security and financial notifications, and estate administration under the laws of the Kingdom of Eswatini.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or medical facility deaths: When your family member dies in a public referral hospital, regional health centre, or private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health under the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Notification of Death (Confirmation of Death) [1][5]. You will need to present the deceased's Eswatini Personal Identity Number (PIN) card or passport so hospital records match civil registry files [1][5].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: If a natural death occurs at home, the family must notify both the local traditional authority (the Chief's runner, umgijimi, or Indvuna at the local Umphakatsi) and the Royal Eswatini Police Service [1][5]. The local traditional authority issues a confirmation letter verifying the community death, and the body is transferred to an accredited mortuary where a medical officer completes the death notification form [1][5].
  • Unnatural, sudden, or unexplained deaths: If the death is sudden, accidental, or lacks recent medical attendance, the Royal Eswatini Police Service must be called to the scene before the remains are moved [5]. A police dossier is opened and a state pathologist conducts a medico-legal post-mortem examination to establish the cause of death before releasing the body and issuing the medical clearance required for civil registration [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Issuing authority and statutory timeframe: All deaths occurring in Eswatini must be registered with the Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Department of the Ministry of Home Affairs, accessible through regional service centres of the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini in Mbabane, Manzini, Nhlangano, and Siteki [1][5]. Under the Births, Marriages and Deaths Registration Act, notification should be completed promptly - typically within 30 days of death - prior to final burial or repatriation [1][5].
  • Required documentation: An informant (next of kin, surviving spouse, adult relative, or authorised funeral representative) must submit the original Medical Notification of Death, the deceased's national identity card (or passport for foreign nationals), the informant's identity document, and, for rural or community deaths, the supporting confirmation letter from the traditional authority or police report [1][5].
  • Official Death Certificate (Form BMD-7): Once the entry is recorded in the National Population Register, the Ministry of Home Affairs surrenders the deceased's national ID card and issues the official computerised Death Certificate (Form BMD-7) and a Burial Order [1][5]. It is advisable to request several certified copies at the regional office, as pension administrators, banks, and the courts each require certified originals [1][2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: A licensed funeral parlour in Eswatini can only release remains for interment or cremation after receiving the official Burial Order and Death Certificate [1][5]. Burials in urban municipal cemeteries require a municipal grave permit, whereas burials on Swazi Nation Land are coordinated with the local Chiefdom (Umphakatsi) alongside the civil Burial Order [1][5].
  • Cross-border repatriation of remains: If your family member's remains are to be repatriated out of Eswatini (for example, to South Africa, Mozambique, or overseas), the licensed funeral director must secure an embalming certificate, a non-infectious disease clearance from an environmental health officer of the Ministry of Health, a sealing certificate for a zinc-lined or hermetically sealed coffin, and a Removal/Export Permit from the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Royal Eswatini Police Service [1][4][5].
  • Consular notifications and Apostille legalisation: When the deceased is a foreign national or when Eswatini death certificates must be presented in another jurisdiction, the relevant foreign diplomatic mission or the Kingdom of Eswatini High Commission can assist with consular mortuary transit documentation [4][5]. Because Eswatini is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, official Death Certificates and court documents intended for use in another Apostille country should be legalised with an Apostille certificate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation or the Registrar of the High Court [1][2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension Funds, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• Private-sector provident fund claims: If the deceased was employed in the private or formal non-governmental sector, survivors should submit a Survivor's Benefit and Funeral Grant claim to the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF), known locally as Lidlelantfongeni [3]. Claims require the certified Death Certificate, certified ID copies of the deceased and claimants, marriage certificate or children's birth certificates, employer confirmation, and beneficiary bank details [3].
  • Public-sector pension and death benefits: If your family member was a civil servant, teacher, or uniformed officer, the family must notify the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) to stop salary or retirement annuity overpayments and claim the statutory death gratuity, funeral benefit, and surviving spouse and dependents' pensions [1][3].
  • Tax, banking, and insurance notifications: Present the certified Death Certificate to commercial banks in Eswatini to freeze individual accounts and verify whether a credit life or funeral insurance policy is attached to any account or loan [2][5]. The estate representative must also notify the Eswatini Revenue Service (ERS) to reconcile final income tax liabilities and obtain tax clearance before final estate distribution [1][2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession
steps.html:
• Reporting to the Master of the High Court: Under Eswatini's Administration of Estates Act, every deceased estate must be reported to the Master of the High Court within 14 days of the date of death [2]. Reporting is completed at the Master's Office in Mbabane or regional sub-offices by filing a Death Notice, a preliminary Inventory of Assets and Liabilities, the original Death Certificate, marriage certificate, and the original Last Will and Testament (if the deceased died testate) [2].
  • Appointment of an Executor and dual legal system: Following a next-of-kin meeting convened before the Master of the High Court, the Master issues Letters of Administration (or Letters of Executorship) authorising the executor to collect assets, advertise for debtors and creditors in the Government Gazette and local newspapers, and lodge a Liquidation and Distribution Account [2]. Eswatini operates a dual legal framework in which civil or Roman-Dutch common law estates are administered under statutory probate rules, while certain customary property on Swazi Nation Land is addressed in coordination with family councils and traditional authorities under the supervision of the Master's Office [1][2].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign assets: If an heir resides outside Eswatini or if the estate includes assets in South Africa or another foreign jurisdiction, foreign grants of probate must be resealed or recognised through the High Court of Eswatini, and powers of attorney signed abroad must carry an Apostille or consular authentication [1][2][5].

titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Eswatini: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Eswatini: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that managing a serious or life-limiting diagnosis for your family member in Eswatini requires timely coordination across medical, legal, and financial institutions. Below, we outline the five key steps to complete in order while your family member still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and specialist clinical referrals: Through facilities overseen by the Ministry of Health under the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini - including Mbabane Government Hospital, Raleigh Fitkin Memorial Hospital in Manzini, and decentralized regional health centres supported by the World Health Organization (WHO) PEN-Plus chronic care framework - families can request a formal palliative care and pain management plan [1][5]. Attending physicians can prescribe essential symptom-control medications, including oral morphine regimens dispensed through public hospital pharmacies [1][5].
  • Home-based hospice and nursing care: Ask the treating hospital's oncology or chronic care unit for a clinical referral to community palliative providers such as Eswatini Hospice at Home or regional rural health motivators (bagcugcuteli), who coordinate home nursing visits, symptom relief, caregiver training, and medical equipment loans across Eswatini's four regions [1][5].
  • Medical aid and public healthcare financing: If your family member belongs to a private medical aid scheme (such as Eswatini Med), submit the specialist's clinical report early to activate chronic illness management or home-nursing benefits. For public patients lacking private coverage, confirm eligibility for state-subsidised hospital care or the Phalala Special Medical Aid Fund if specialised tertiary treatment is required [1][5].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Medical Contacts
steps.html:
• Written clinical care preferences: Eswatini does not have a single standalone statute governing living wills, so advance treatment preferences operate through constitutional rights to bodily integrity and Ministry of Health patient-consent standards under the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini [1][5]. While your family member has full capacity, they should sign a dated written statement detailing their wishes regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and preferred place of care (home versus hospital) [1][5].
  • Designating a primary medical spokesperson: Hospital admission teams in Eswatini rely on the designated next of kin recorded in the patient's medical file when consulting the family on urgent clinical care [1][5]. Your family member should explicitly name their primary medical spokesperson and an alternate contact in writing, have the document witnessed by two independent adults and countersigned by the treating doctor, and place copies in both the hospital chart and the home care folder [1][5].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• General or Special Power of Attorney: Under Eswatini's Roman-Dutch common law framework, a Power of Attorney (Procuratie) allows your family member (the principal) to authorise a trusted agent to manage property, sign legal instruments, and conduct administrative affairs [1][2]. To ensure formal validity, the Power of Attorney should be drafted by an admitted attorney or notary public in Eswatini and signed by the principal in the presence of two competent witnesses while mental capacity is medically documented [2].
  • Important capacity rule under Eswatini law: Because Eswatini common law does not recognise an automatic enduring power of attorney that survives supervening mental incapacity, a standard Power of Attorney lapses if the principal later loses mental capacity [2]. If capacity is lost, family members must petition the High Court of Eswatini (in consultation with the Master of the High Court) to appoint a curator bonis to manage financial affairs [2].
  • Bank account mandates and signatory setup: Commercial banks in Eswatini enforce strict anti-money-laundering and mandate verification rules. While your family member is still able to visit the branch or meet a mobile relationship manager, they should execute the bank's specific third-party signing mandate, register online banking access, and update Personal Identity Number (PIN) KYC records [1][2].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Pension Provisions, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Private-sector invalidity and medical benefits: If your family member has contributed to the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF), check eligibility for an Invalidity Benefit if the illness renders them permanently incapable of gainful employment [3]. An application requires a formal medical board or specialist assessment certifying permanent incapacity, alongside the member's PIN card and employment records [3].
  • Public-sector medical boarding and retirement: Civil servants and public employees covered by the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) who can no longer perform their duties due to severe illness may apply through their ministry's human resources department and a government medical board for ill-health retirement pensions and lump-sum gratuities [1][4].
  • Social grants and workplace caregiver leave: For vulnerable citizens without formal pension coverage, the Deputy Prime Minister's Office under the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini administers the Disability Grant and Old Age Grant [1]. Employed family caregivers should review their employment contracts and the Employment Act to arrange compassionate leave, paid annual leave, or flexible working schedules [1].

steps.title: Organise the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Last Will and Testament: Under the Eswatini Wills Act, a person with testamentary capacity should execute a written Will signed at the end of the document (and on every preceding page) in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent competent witnesses who are not beneficiaries (and whose spouses are not beneficiaries) [2]. Clear testamentary provisions help streamline subsequent supervision by the Master of the High Court [2].
  • Updating pension and insurance nominations: Benefits held with the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF), the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF), or group life insurers are governed by statutory trust and nomination rules rather than solely by the Will [3][4]. While capacity is intact, your family member should file updated beneficiary nomination forms and verify that all dependents' birth and marriage certificates are registered with the Ministry of Home Affairs [1][3][4].
  • Consolidating property and cross-border records: Assemble title deeds for urban freehold land, bank statements, vehicle registration books, and marriage certificates (specifying whether married under civil rites in or out of community of property, or under Swazi Law and Custom) in a secure folder [1][2]. If assets or family members are located outside Eswatini, obtain Apostille authentication on powers of attorney and coordinate separate situs-compliant wills where needed [1][2].
