title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Lesotho: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Lesotho: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Lesotho: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Lesotho is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while they retain full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their autonomy and prevents future family or administrative disputes. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to coordinate palliative care, advance medical directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation in the Kingdom of Lesotho.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public, CHAL, and specialist palliative care services: You can request a clinical referral from your family member's treating doctor to palliative and chronic-care teams operating within public district hospitals and Queen 'Mamohato Memorial Hospital in Maseru (overseen by the Ministry of Health), Christian Health Association of Lesotho (CHAL) facilities, or community hospice programs such as Starlight Oasis of Hope Hospice [3] [4]. These teams coordinate pain relief (including regulated opioid analgesics), symptom management, and community home-based nursing visits [3].
  • Cross-border tertiary medical referrals: For specialized oncology, radiotherapy, or advanced palliative interventions not available locally, the Ministry of Health in Lesotho coordinates public patient referrals to accredited tertiary hospitals in Bloemfontein, South Africa, while private medical-aid members (such as Mamoth or South African cross-border schemes) should obtain early pre-authorization for home nursing, oxygen, and palliative care [3] [4].
  • Maintaining civil identity records for clinical access: Ensure that your family member's Lesotho National Identity Card issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs is current and accessible, as public hospital subsidies, cross-border referral permits, and social protection benefits require valid national identification [1] [4].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Proxy
steps.html:
• Informed consent and patient autonomy under Lesotho law: Under Lesotho's Roman-Dutch common law and Ministry of Health clinical governance frameworks, a mentally competent adult patient has the legal right to give or withhold informed consent to medical treatment and to express advance preferences regarding end-of-life care [2] [3].
  • Signing a written Advance Medical Directive (Living Will): While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, they can sign a written Advance Care Directive setting out their wishes on cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition and hydration, pain control, and whether they prefer to be cared for at home or in hospital [2] [3].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative in clinical files: Your family member should name a trusted primary and alternate family representative in writing, have the directive signed in the presence of two independent adult witnesses, and lodge copies with their treating physician at the Ministry of Health or CHAL hospital so the clinical team has clear written authority if decision-making capacity later declines [2] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a General or Special Power of Attorney: While your family member has full mental capacity, they should instruct a legal practitioner or Notary Public admitted in Lesotho to prepare a General or Special Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted agent to manage bank accounts, pay medical bills, and handle property or administrative matters [2]. Under Lesotho's Registration of Deeds Act, 1967, a Power of Attorney used for immovable property or formal registry acts must be properly attested by two competent witnesses or a Notary Public and registered where required [2].
  • Curatorship rules if mental capacity is lost: Under Roman-Dutch common law as applied in Lesotho, an ordinary Power of Attorney lapses automatically if the principal becomes mentally incapacitated [2]. Once capacity is lost, family members must apply to the High Court of Lesotho (in consultation with the Master of the High Court under the Administration of Estates and Inheritance Act, 2024) for the appointment of a curator bonis (to manage property and finances) or curator personae (for personal and care decisions) [2].
  • Bank operating mandates: Because commercial banks in Lesotho (such as Standard Lesotho Bank, Nedbank Lesotho, FNB Lesotho, and PostBank) enforce strict internal mandate procedures, your family member should visit their branch in person (or arrange a domiciliary bank visit) to sign third-party signing mandates while still lucid and able to sign [2] [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Ill-Health Retirement, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Occupational ill-health retirement and disability benefits: If your family member is a public servant covered by the Public Officers' Defined Contribution Pension Fund or a private-sector employee covered by an occupational pension or provident fund, they can apply for ill-health early retirement or permanent disability benefits upon certification by a registered medical board [2] [4]. Cross-border mineworkers or former mineworkers diagnosed with qualifying occupational or terminal illnesses should also check benefit entitlements through TEBA / the Mineworkers Provident Fund [4].
  • Social assistance and disability grants: The Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development (formerly the Ministry of Social Development) administers the Severe Disability Grant and the Child Grants Programme for vulnerable households, while citizens aged 70 and above qualify for the non-contributory Old Age Pension [2] [4]. Applications require a valid Lesotho National ID Card from the Ministry of Home Affairs and clinical certification from a government medical officer [1] [4].
  • Workplace leave and tax compliance: Under the Labour Code Order, 1992 (and updated labour legislation), employees in Lesotho have statutory entitlements to paid sick leave and may arrange compassionate or unpaid family leave with their employer [2]. If your family member operates a business or earns taxable income, an authorized representative can manage ongoing tax filings with Revenue Services Lesotho [5].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Will under the Administration of Estates and Inheritance Act, 2024: Lesotho's Administration of Estates and Inheritance Act, 2024 modernized succession law, abolished discriminatory customary male-primogeniture rules, and established clear standards for both testate and intestate succession [2]. While of sound mind, your family member should execute a written will signed in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent competent witnesses (who must not be beneficiaries under the will) and may lodge a copy with their legal practitioner or the Office of the Master of the High Court [2].
  • Updating pension and funeral policy beneficiary nominations: Because occupational pension death benefits, group life policies, and funeral insurance policies pay out directly to nominated beneficiaries, your family member should review and update all nomination forms with their pension fund and insurer so that surviving spouses and children are accurately recorded [2] [4].
  • Consolidating civil identity records, Land Administration Authority leases, and cross-border assets: Verify that birth certificates, marriage certificates, and Lesotho National ID Cards for all family members are up to date with the Ministry of Home Affairs [1]. Gather original Land Leases registered with the Land Administration Authority (LAA), vehicle registration books, and tax records with Revenue Services Lesotho [2] [5]. If your family member holds assets or bank accounts in South Africa or abroad, ensure any cross-border Power of Attorney or will is notarized and authenticated with a Hague Apostille so it is recognized without delay [2] [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Liberia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Liberia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Liberia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Liberia. To help your family manage the legal, medical, and practical requirements in order, we have set out the five main official steps under Liberian law below.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or licensed medical facility: When a person dies in a hospital or clinic in Liberia, the attending physician examines the body and issues a formal Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1]. You should confirm that the deceased's full legal name, age, nationality, date and hour of death, and clinical cause of death match their official identification before leaving the health facility [1].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: If your family member died at home from a known natural illness, you should notify the nearest recognized health facility or county health team under the Ministry of Health so a licensed medical officer can verify the death or issue the required medical confirmation, supported where applicable by community or magisterial affidavits [1].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or non-natural deaths: Under Liberia's Public Health Law and criminal procedure rules, any sudden, accidental, unexplained, or suspicious death must be reported immediately to the Liberia National Police and the county coroner before the body is moved or prepared for burial [1]. The coroner conducts an inquest and, where necessary, orders a forensic post-mortem examination before issuing a coroner's clearance certificate [1].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: Civil registration of deaths in Liberia is administered by the Bureau of Vital Statistics within the Ministry of Health at its central headquarters in Congo Town, Monrovia, and through decentralized County Service Centers [1].
  • Statutory reporting and required documentation: Deaths should be declared promptly by the next of kin, surviving relative, or authorized funeral representative [1]. To complete the registration and obtain an official biometric or certified Death Certificate, the informant must present the original hospital Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or coroner's certificate and supporting court affidavit for out-of-facility deaths), the deceased's national identification card, voter registration card, or passport, the informant's valid photo identification, and the official Government of Liberia revenue receipt issued by the Liberia Revenue Authority [1, 5].
  • Certified copies for legal and financial administration: You should request multiple certified copies of the official Death Certificate from the Ministry of Health, as separate originals are required for probate court filings, pension claims, and bank account closures [1, 4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial and mortuary permits: A licensed funeral home in Liberia coordinates transfer to an approved mortuary, embalming, and cemetery interment [1]. Cemetery authorities require the official Death Certificate or burial permit issued following verification by the Ministry of Health and local municipal authorities before interment can proceed [1].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If your family member's remains must be repatriated abroad, the licensed funeral director must obtain an official Death Certificate, an embalming and non-contagious disease certificate from the Ministry of Health, a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin certificate, and customs transit clearance [1, 6].
  • Apostille and diplomatic authentication: Liberia is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Monrovia serves as the designated Competent Authority to issue Apostille certificates on Liberian public documents, including death certificates and probate orders, for use in other convention countries [6]. If the destination country is not party to the Apostille Convention, documents must undergo consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant foreign embassy [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• Social security survivor and funeral benefits: If the deceased was employed in the formal public or private sector and contributed to the National Pension Scheme or was covered under the Employment Injury Scheme, surviving dependents should notify the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation [2]. Under the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation statutory benefit framework, eligible widows, widowers, and dependent children may claim a Survivor's Pension or lump-sum survivor benefit, and a funeral grant is payable where death resulted from a covered work-related injury [2, 3]. Claims require the official Death Certificate, marriage or birth records proving dependency, employment confirmation, and completed claim forms [3].
  • Tax closure and clearance: The family or appointed estate representative should notify the Liberia Revenue Authority to update the deceased's Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) record, settle any outstanding personal income or real property tax liabilities, and obtain tax clearance where required for estate asset transfers [5].
  • Banks, insurers, and identity cancellation: Present the certified Death Certificate to commercial banks, mobile money providers, and life insurance companies in Liberia to freeze sole accounts, verify policy beneficiaries, and ascertain the balances to be included in the estate inventory [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Probate Procedures
steps.html:
• Probate jurisdiction: Estate administration and succession in Liberia are governed by the Decedents Estates Law (Title 8 of the Liberian Code of Laws Revised) and fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Monthly and Probate Court in Montserrado County or the respective provisional Monthly and Probate Courts and Circuit Courts across Liberia's counties, supervised by The Judiciary of Liberia [4].
  • Testate vs. intestate succession: If the deceased left a valid written will, the nominated executor petitions the Monthly and Probate Court to prove the will and obtain Letters Testamentary [4]. If the deceased died intestate (without a will), the surviving spouse, adult children, or next of kin petition the court for Letters of Administration [4]. Under the Decedents Estates Law and the Equal Rights of the Customary Marriage Law, both statutory and customary surviving spouses and children enjoy protected inheritance shares [4].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign assets: If an heir or executor resides outside Liberia, they may appoint a local legal representative or attorney-in-fact in Liberia through a notarized Power of Attorney that carries an Apostille or consular legalization acknowledged through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [4, 6]. Conversely, foreign probate grants covering assets in Liberia must be ancillary-probated before the Monthly and Probate Court [4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Liberia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Liberia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Liberia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that managing a serious or life-limiting medical diagnosis for your family member in Liberia requires timely legal, clinical, and financial coordination. While the ill person retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity, we have outlined the five official steps below in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and referral clinical pathways: Primary and tertiary clinical care in Liberia is overseen by the Ministry of Health through county hospitals, faith-based health facilities, and national referral centers such as the John F. Kennedy Medical Center in Monrovia [1]. Your family member should request a comprehensive written clinical summary, treatment plan, and symptom-management protocol from their attending specialist [1].
  • Home-based palliative care and pain management: Because dedicated inpatient hospice facilities are limited in Liberia, supportive and palliative care is typically coordinated between hospital outpatient oncology or chronic-disease units, community health teams under the Ministry of Health, and licensed private or faith-based home nursing providers [1]. Ensure that prescriptions for controlled analgesics and essential supportive medications are issued by an authorized physician in compliance with national pharmaceutical regulations [1].
  • Private health insurance and employer medical schemes: If the ill person holds private medical insurance or is covered under an employer-sponsored corporate health plan, notify the insurer early to obtain pre-authorization for inpatient admissions, specialist consultations, or home nursing care [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment preferences: Liberia does not have a standalone living will statute, so medical decision-making relies on general common-law principles of informed consent and patient autonomy supervised under the regulatory standards of the Ministry of Health [1]. While your family member has full capacity, they should sign a clear written statement of medical treatment preferences specifying their wishes regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, artificial life support, invasive interventions, and palliative comfort measures [1].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative: To avoid uncertainty among relatives if the ill person later loses the ability to communicate, they should formally designate a trusted adult as their primary healthcare proxy and next-of-kin medical decision-maker in a notarized written instrument [1, 4].
  • Hospital file integration: Provide signed copies of the advance treatment statement and healthcare proxy designation to the attending physician, hospital administration, and family caregivers so that clinical teams can verify the authorized representative immediately during an emergency [1].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• General or special power of attorney: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they should execute a formal Power of Attorney before a commissioned Notary Public or legal counsel in Liberia, authorizing a trusted agent to manage real property, sign legal instruments, collect income, and deal with public authorities [4, 5]. For real estate transactions or long-term property administration, the Power of Attorney should be probated and registered through the Monthly and Probate Court under The Judiciary of Liberia to ensure third-party enforceability [4].
  • Commercial bank account mandates: Liberian commercial banks frequently require account holders to sign the bank's own internal third-party mandate or signatory card in person, alongside presenting a notarized and probated Power of Attorney and valid national identification, before allowing a representative to operate accounts or pay medical bills [4].
  • Tax representation: A notarized authorization also enables the designated representative to manage ongoing tax filings, real estate tax payments, and Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) compliance through the Liberia Revenue Authority [5].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Benefits, Workplace Protections, and Caregiver Arrangements
steps.html:
• Social security invalidity and employment injury benefits: If your family member is a registered contributor under the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation and becomes permanently incapable of gainful employment due to a non-occupational illness or an occupational disease, they may apply for an Invalidity Pension or Disability Benefit under the National Pension Scheme or Employment Injury Scheme [2, 3] [2]. Claims submitted to the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation require certified medical board assessments confirming permanent incapacity, contribution records, and employer verification [3].
  • Statutory sick leave and employment entitlements: Under Liberia's Decent Work Act, employees in the formal sector are entitled to paid sick leave upon presentation of a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner, and employers must respect statutory medical incapacity procedures before terminating employment on health grounds [1, 2].
  • Caregiver leave Arrangements: Because Liberian statutory law does not provide a separate state-funded family caregiver allowance, relatives caring for the ill person should negotiate paid annual leave, compassionate leave, or flexible working arrangements directly with their employer, supported by hospital medical documentation [1].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Drafting a valid will: Under Liberia's Decedents Estates Law (Title 8 of the Liberian Code of Laws Revised), a person of sound mind aged 18 or older may execute a written Last Will and Testament signed by the testator in the presence of at least two attesting witnesses who sign in the testator's presence [4]. Having the will drafted with legal counsel ensures compliance with statutory spousal and family protection rules supervised by The Judiciary of Liberia [4].
  • Updating pension and insurance beneficiaries: Review and update the nominated beneficiary records directly with the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation, private pension administrators, and life insurance companies, as designated statutory and policy payouts are processed through beneficiary records [2, 3].
  • Civil status, land deeds, and cross-border authentication: Gather original marriage certificates, birth certificates of children, probated land deeds, and tax receipts issued by the Liberia Revenue Authority in a secure file [4, 5]. If powers of attorney or civil status documents must be used outside Liberia, or if foreign powers of attorney must be used in Liberia, ensure they carry an Apostille certificate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Liberia's Competent Authority under the Hague Apostille Convention) or consular legalization [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Malawi: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Malawi: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Malawi: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Malawi. To help your family navigate the official legal, medical, and practical requirements in order, we have set out the five main steps under Malawian law below.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or health facility: When a person dies in a public, CHAM (Christian Health Association of Malawi), or private hospital supervised by the Ministry of Health, the attending clinician completes Section 2 (Medical Certification of Cause of Death) of Death Report Form NR10, while the family informant completes Section 1 [1] [2] [5]. Ensure that the deceased's name, date of birth, and National ID details on Form NR10 match their official identification card [1].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: Under the National Registration Act, when a natural death occurs at home or in a village outside a medical facility, the informant reports the death to the traditional authority (Village Headman) or community registration desk using Form NR10C [1] [2]. The local leader verifies the death and countersigns the notification for civil registration [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or suspicious deaths: Any unexpected, violent, traffic-related, or unexplained death must be reported immediately to the Malawi Police Service before the body is moved [1] [5]. The police refer the body to a district or central hospital under the Ministry of Health for a forensic post-mortem examination and medical report before burial clearance or death registration can proceed [1] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the National Registration Bureau
steps.html:
• Statutory 6-week deadline and authority: Civil death registration in Malawi is administered by the National Registration Bureau through its 28 District Registration Offices, health facility registration desks, and post offices [1]. Under the National Registration Act, registering a death within 6 weeks of occurrence is free of charge for Malawian citizens; registrations submitted after 6 weeks incur statutory late registration fees, and foreign national registrations carry a prescribed administrative fee [1].
  • Mandatory informant and identity documents: The informant (a surviving spouse, parent, adult relative, or person present at the death) must submit the completed Form NR10 or Form NR10C, the deceased's original Malawian National ID card (or birth certificate if under age 16, or passport for a foreign citizen), and the informant's own National ID card, phone number, and signature or thumbprint [1] [2].
  • Collecting the official Death Registration Certificate: Only the registered informant listed on Form NR10 or Form NR10C is permitted to collect the official Death Registration Certificate from the National Registration Bureau, which is mandatory for pension claims, bank closures, and estate probate [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: For burials within a municipal or city council cemetery (such as in Lilongwe, Blantyre, Mzuzu, or Zomba) or cremation at an approved crematorium, the family or licensed funeral service provider presents the medical death notification (Form NR10) or police clearance to obtain the municipal burial or cremation permit and mortuary release [1] [5].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if their remains must be transported outside Malawi, a licensed funeral director must obtain the official Death Registration Certificate from the National Registration Bureau, an embalming and non-infectious disease certificate from a Ministry of Health port health officer, a coffin sealing certificate, and customs clearance from the Malawi Revenue Authority [1] [5] [7].
  • Apostille and document legalization: Malawi is a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Public documents issued in Malawi, including Death Registration Certificates and High Court probate orders, can be authenticated with an Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the High Court registry under The Judiciary of Malawi for recognition in other convention countries [1] [6].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• National ID cancellation: Upon registration of the death, the National Registration Bureau records the death in the National Registration and Identification System and retains or cancels the deceased's National ID card [1].
  • Mandatory occupational pension death benefits: Under the Pension Act (No. 6 of 2011), formal-sector employers in Malawi are required to maintain pension and group life assurance coverage for employees [4]. Notably, Section 86 of the Pension Act provides that pension death benefits and nominated life assurance proceeds do not automatically form part of the general deceased estate if valid beneficiary nominations exist; instead, the pension fund trustee distributes benefits in accordance with the deceased member's nomination form and statutory dependency rules within the statutory timeframe [4].
  • Tax and financial institutions: Notify the Malawi Revenue Authority using the Death Registration Certificate to close or update the deceased's Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and resolve any outstanding income or business tax liabilities [7]. Present the Death Registration Certificate to commercial banks and mobile money operators to freeze individual accounts pending estate administration [3] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Succession Procedures
steps.html:
• Governing succession statute: Succession, wills, and estate administration in Malawi are governed by the Deceased Estates (Wills, Inheritance and Protection) Act (No. 14 of 2011), which protects surviving spouses and children and strictly criminalizes unlawful seizure of estate property ('property grabbing') [3].
  • Probate and Letters of Administration: For larger estates, testate estates (where the deceased left a valid written will), or estates involving formal land titles and bank accounts, the executor or surviving family petitions the High Court of Malawi under The Judiciary of Malawi for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration [3] [6]. Smaller estates falling within statutory thresholds may be administered locally through the District Commissioner's institutional estate mechanisms or designated subordinate courts [3] [6].
  • Estate duty and cross-border coordination: Before distributing estate assets, the administrator must address applicable estate duty assessments or clearances required under Malawian law and the Malawi Revenue Authority [3] [7]. If an heir or executor resides abroad, they may act through a Malawian legal practitioner using a notarized and Apostilled Power of Attorney, and foreign probate grants covering assets in Malawi can be resealed by the High Court of Malawi under The Judiciary of Malawi [3] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malawi: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malawi: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Malawi: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that supporting your family member after a serious or life-limiting diagnosis in Malawi requires timely clinical, legal, and financial planning. While the ill person retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity, we have outlined the five official steps below in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and specialist palliative care services: Malawi integrates palliative care into its national public health framework under the Ministry of Health, with dedicated multidisciplinary palliative care clinics operating at central referral hospitals (including Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital in Blantyre, Kamuzu Central Hospital in Lilongwe, Mzuzu Central Hospital, and Zomba Central Hospital) as well as district hospitals and accredited non-profit hospice providers [5]. Request an official clinical summary and symptom-management plan from the attending specialist [5].
  • Home-based care and pain relief: Hospital palliative teams and community health nurses coordinated through the Ministry of Health provide outpatient and home-based pain control, including regulated oral morphine and supportive nursing guidance for family caregivers [5].
  • Private medical schemes: If your family member is enrolled in a private medical aid society in Malawi (such as MASM or Liberty Health) or an employer-sponsored healthcare plan, contact the scheme administrator early to confirm coverage limits for specialist consultations, chronic medication, and home nursing care [5].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Written advance medical treatment preferences: Although Malawi does not have a standalone living will statute, clinical care is governed by patient autonomy and informed consent standards enforced by the Ministry of Health [5]. While your family member has full decision-making capacity, they should sign a written statement of medical preferences detailing their instructions regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, intensive care ventilation, palliative pain relief, and preferred place of care [5].
  • Designating a medical representative: To ensure clear communication with doctors if the ill person becomes unable to speak for themselves, they should execute a written and witnessed authorization naming a trusted adult as their primary healthcare proxy and clinical next of kin [5] [6].
  • Filing with clinical teams: Provide signed copies of the advance treatment statement and healthcare proxy appointment to the attending physician, hospital palliative care unit, and key family members so the document is immediately accessible in the patient's medical record [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Formal Power of Attorney: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they should instruct a licensed legal practitioner or Notary Public in Malawi to draft and witness a General or Special Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage property, sign legal contracts, and handle financial affairs [6]. Powers of Attorney affecting registered land or formal estates should be stamped and registered with the Deeds Registry and recognizable before courts supervised by The Judiciary of Malawi [6].
  • Bank account operating mandates: Commercial banks in Malawi generally require the account holder to complete the bank's specific third-party mandate or joint-signatory forms in person (or through a verified bedside visit) accompanied by a valid Malawian National ID card issued by the National Registration Bureau, rather than relying solely on a general Power of Attorney [1] [6].
  • Tax administration authority: The appointed representative should also be authorized to manage Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) filings, rental or business tax returns, and tax clearances with the Malawi Revenue Authority [7].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Pension Benefits and Workplace Protections
steps.html:
• Occupational invalidity and ill-health retirement benefits: Under the Pension Act (No. 6 of 2011), registered pension schemes in Malawi provide for early retirement or invalidity pension payouts when a member becomes permanently incapacitated by physical or mental infirmity before normal retirement age [4]. To initiate an ill-health retirement or permanent disability claim with the pension fund trustee or insurer, the member must submit certified medical board reports from a registered medical practitioner under the Ministry of Health confirming permanent incapacity for work [4] [5].
  • Statutory sick leave and employment rights: Under Malawi's Employment Act, formal-sector employees are entitled to statutory paid and unpaid sick leave upon providing medical certification, and employers must follow fair medical capability assessment procedures [4] [5].
  • Family caregiver leave arrangements: Because Malawian legislation does not provide a state-funded caregiver allowance, employed family members caring for the ill person should arrange compassionate leave, annual leave, or flexible working hours with their employer, supported by hospital documentation from the Ministry of Health [5].

steps.title: Review the Will, Pension Nominations, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Executing a valid written will: Under the Deceased Estates (Wills, Inheritance and Protection) Act (No. 14 of 2011), any person of sound mind aged 18 or older may execute a written Will signed by the testator in the presence of at least two competent independent witnesses who attest the signature in the testator's presence [3]. Under the Act, a testator should make reasonable provision for surviving spouses and dependent children, and a valid will can be deposited for safekeeping with the High Court Registry under The Judiciary of Malawi [3] [6].
  • Updating pension beneficiary nominations: Section 86 of the Pension Act (No. 6 of 2011) establishes that pension death benefits and group life benefits are paid according to the member's pension nomination form and statutory dependency rules rather than passing slowly through general estate probate [4]. Your family member should review and update their official beneficiary nomination form directly with their employer and pension fund administrator [4].
  • Securing National ID, title deeds, and cross-border documents: Verify that the ill person and all immediate family members hold valid National ID cards or birth certificates issued by the National Registration Bureau, and organize original land title deeds, bank statements, and Malawi Revenue Authority tax records in one secure file [1] [2] [7]. If powers of attorney or property documents involve relatives or assets outside Malawi, arrange Apostille authentication through the High Court under The Judiciary of Malawi or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Mauritius: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Mauritius: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Mauritius: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Mauritius. To help your family navigate the legal, civil status, and financial steps in order, we have set out the five main official procedures under Mauritian law below.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or private clinic: When a person dies in a public hospital under the Ministry of Health and Wellness or in a licensed private clinic in Mauritius, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death [1] [5]. Verify that the deceased's full name, National Identity Card (NIC) number, age, and date and time of death are recorded accurately on the certificate [1].
  • Natural deaths at home: If your family member passed away at home, a registered private medical practitioner or a government medical officer from the nearest regional hospital under the Ministry of Health and Wellness must be called to examine the body and issue the Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death [1] [5].
  • Sudden, accidental, or suspicious deaths: Under Mauritian law, if the death is sudden, violent, accidental, or of unknown cause, you must immediately notify the Mauritius Police Force before the body is moved [1]. The police report the matter to the District Magistrate and arrange transfer to the Police Medical Officer / Forensic Science department for an autopsy before issuing an order authorizing registration and burial [1] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Status Division
steps.html:
• Statutory 24-hour to 48-hour registration window: Under the Civil Status Act, a death in Mauritius must be registered at the Civil Status Division office of the district where the death occurred or where the deceased last resided before any burial or cremation takes place (normally within 24 to 48 hours of death, with weekend and public holiday service desks operating for urgent burial permits) [1] [2].
  • Informant and mandatory documents: One declarant (a surviving relative, spouse, or person possessing knowledge of the deceased's civil status details) must appear before the Civil Status Officer and present: (a) the original Medical Certificate of the Cause of Death issued by the doctor, (b) the deceased's birth certificate, marriage certificate (if applicable), and National Identity Card (or passport for a non-citizen), and (c) the declarant's own National Identity Card [1].
  • Official Death Certificates and Burial Permit: Registration of death and the issuance of the Burial or Cremation Permit and initial Death Certificate extract by the Civil Status Division are free of charge [1]. Request several official extracts of the Death Certificate for banking, pension, and succession formalities [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Under the Civil Status Act and Public Health regulations enforced by the Ministry of Health and Wellness, no interment or cremation may take place earlier than 24 hours after death (unless ordered earlier by a Sanitary Authority on public health grounds) and never without the Burial or Cremation Permit issued by the Civil Status Division [1] [5]. For cremation, an additional medical certificate and sanitary clearance are required [1] [5].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or their remains must be repatriated abroad, a licensed funeral director coordinates embalming, a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin certificate, a non-contagious disease and export permit from the Sanitary Authority of the Ministry of Health and Wellness, and customs clearance [1] [5].
  • Apostille authentication: Mauritius is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Official multilingual or English/French Death Certificates issued by the Civil Status Division and succession documents can be authenticated with an Apostille through the Prime Minister's Office (Defense and Home Affairs Division) in Port Louis for legal recognition abroad [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, the Mauritius Revenue Authority, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• Funeral grant and survivor pensions: Under the National Pensions Act and the Social Contribution and Social Benefits Act administered by the Ministry of Social Integration, Social Security and National Solidarity and the Mauritius Revenue Authority, the Civil Status Division updates the Central Population Database upon death registration so basic retirement pensions are stopped automatically to prevent overpayments [1] [3] [4]. Eligible surviving spouses and orphans may claim a Widow's/Surviving Spouse's Pension, Orphan's Allowance, Industrial Injury Death Benefit, and a statutory Funeral Grant by applying at their local Social Security Office with the Death Certificate, marriage certificate, and National Identity Cards [3] [4].
  • Income tax and CSG final filings: The heirs or estate representative must notify the Mauritius Revenue Authority to file any final income tax return of the deceased up to the date of death and settle or claim any tax balances [4].
  • Banks and insurers: Present the official Death Certificate from the Civil Status Division to commercial banks and insurance companies in Mauritius to block sole accounts and request a formal certificate of account balances as at the date of death [1] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Succession Procedures
steps.html:
• Civil Code succession rules and Affidavit of Prescription/Succession: Estate succession in Mauritius is governed by the Code Civil Mauricien (which protects forced-heirship reserved shares - la réserve héréditaire - for children and provides statutory rights for the surviving spouse) and procedural rules overseen by the Supreme Court of Mauritius [6].
  • Notarial deed of notoriety and Affidavit of Succession: To unlock bank accounts, transfer vehicles, or convey immovable property, the heirs must establish their legal quality as heirs through an Acte de Notoriété (Deed of Notoriety) or an Affidavit of Succession drawn up by a Mauritian Notary or Attorney-at-Law and sworn before the Master and Registrar of the Supreme Court of Mauritius [6]. If the deceased left a holograph or mystic will, it must be presented to the Master and Registrar of the Supreme Court of Mauritius to be opened and deposited with a notary [6].
  • Inheritance tax and cross-border heirs: Mauritius has abolished inheritance and estate duty on successions, though standard registration and transcription duties apply when transferring immovable property [4] [6]. Heirs residing abroad can execute a notarized and Apostilled Power of Attorney (Procuration) appointing a representative or notary in Mauritius to sign succession deeds on their behalf [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Mauritius: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Mauritius: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Mauritius: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that supporting your family member following a serious or life-limiting medical diagnosis in Mauritius requires coordinated clinical, legal, and financial planning. While the ill person retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity, we have outlined the five official steps below in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Medical Visits, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public healthcare and specialist oncology/palliative units: Public hospitals and regional health centers under the Ministry of Health and Wellness (including Victoria Hospital in Candos, Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam National Hospital in Pamplemousses, Dr. A. G. Jeetoo Hospital in Port Louis, Flacq Hospital, and Jawaharlal Nehru Hospital in Rose Belle) provide free inpatient and outpatient specialist care, pain management, and supportive services for citizens and residents [5]. Obtain a detailed written medical report and symptom-control schedule from the treating specialist [5].
  • Domiciliary medical visits and home nursing: For patients who are bedridden or severely mobility-impaired, the Ministry of Health and Wellness and the Ministry of Social Integration, Social Security and National Solidarity coordinate domiciliary medical visits (where government medical officers visit severely disabled or elderly patients at home) alongside accredited non-governmental palliative care providers [3] [5].
  • Private clinic and health insurance coverage: If your family member wishes to receive care at a private clinic or home nursing service covered by private health insurance, contact the insurer early to confirm policy limits for oncology, palliative care, and inpatient hospitalization [5].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Written statement of medical treatment preferences: Mauritius does not currently have a standalone statutory living will regime, so clinical decision-making is governed by medical ethics and patient informed consent rules overseen by the Ministry of Health and Wellness [5]. While your family member has full capacity, they should sign a written declaration setting out their preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and palliative pain relief [5].
  • Designating a trusted medical spokesperson: To assist doctors if the ill person becomes unable to communicate their wishes directly, they should execute a signed and witnessed written authorization naming a trusted adult relative or representative as their primary clinical contact and healthcare spokesperson [5] [6].
  • Filing in hospital records: Provide copies of the signed treatment preferences and representative designation to the attending consultant, private clinic or public hospital medical records unit, and immediate family caregivers [5].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Notarial or private Power of Attorney (Procuration): Under the Code Civil Mauricien (Articles 1984 et seq.), while your family member retains full mental and legal capacity, they should execute a formal Procuration (Power of Attorney) before a Mauritian Notary (Notaire) or Attorney-at-Law authorizing a trusted representative (mandataire) to manage immovable property, collect income, pay medical expenses, and deal with administrative authorities [6]. Any Procuration intended to authorize the sale, mortgage, or transfer of land or buildings in Mauritius must be executed as an authentic notarial deed [6].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Mauritian commercial banks require account holders to complete the bank's specific third-party power-of-attorney or signatory mandate form (presenting both the principal's and representative's National Identity Cards issued by the Civil Status Division) before allowing a representative to operate accounts [1] [6].
  • Tax and revenue representation: Authorize the designated representative to handle ongoing income tax returns, e-filing, and social benefit records with the Mauritius Revenue Authority [4].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Pensions, Carer's Allowance, and Workplace Protections
steps.html:
• Basic Invalid's Pension and Carer's Allowance: Under the National Pensions Act and the Social Contribution and Social Benefits Act administered by the Ministry of Social Integration, Social Security and National Solidarity and paid in coordination with the Mauritius Revenue Authority, a person aged under 60 who is certified by the Medical Board as permanently or substantially incapacitated (at least 60% disabled for at least 12 months) is eligible for the Basic Invalid's Pension (and contributory invalidity benefits where applicable) [3] [4]. If the ill person requires constant personal attendance by another person to perform daily living activities - whether under age 60 receiving an Invalid's Pension or aged 60 and above receiving the Basic Retirement Pension - the Medical Board can approve an additional monthly Carer's Allowance (enhanced invalidity/severe disability allowance) as well as incontinence or assistive-device support [3] [4].
  • Application procedure: Submit the claim at the nearest local Social Security Office with the applicant's National Identity Card, birth certificate issued by the Civil Status Division, bank account details, and treating doctor's medical certificate from the Ministry of Health and Wellness [1] [3] [5].
  • Employment sick leave and medical board protections: Under Mauritius's Workers' Rights Act, employees are entitled to paid sick leave and cannot be dismissed for ill health without proper medical evaluation and statutory severance or retirement protections [3] [4].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Forced-Heirship Planning, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Drafting a valid Will under the Code Civil Mauricien: In Mauritius, a testator of sound mind may execute a Will in one of the forms recognized by the Code Civil Mauricien: an Authentic Will (testament par acte public) dictated before a Mauritian Notary and witnesses, a Holograph Will (testament olographe) written, dated, and signed entirely in the testator's own handwriting, or a Mystic Will [6]. Because Mauritian succession law enforces strict forced-heirship reserved portions (la réserve héréditaire) for children and protected rights for a surviving spouse, we advise consulting a Mauritian Notary so bequests remain within the disposable quota (la quotité disponible) and avoid later litigation before the Supreme Court of Mauritius [6].
  • Insurance and pension beneficiary designations: Verify and update nominated beneficiaries on private life insurance policies, superannuation funds, and employer occupational pension schemes [3] [4].
  • Civil status and property dossier: Gather up-to-date birth and marriage certificates from the Civil Status Division, National Identity Cards, original notarial title deeds (contrats de vente), and Mauritius Revenue Authority tax statements in a single organized folder [1] [2] [4] [6]. If powers of attorney or property documents must be used outside Mauritius, obtain an Apostille certificate through the Prime Minister's Office in Port Louis [1] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Namibia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Namibia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Namibia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Namibia, we can guide you through the official medical, civil registration, funeral, social security, and estate administration procedures in the order they must be completed.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or health facility deaths: If your family member died in a state hospital or private clinic under the supervision of the Ministry of Health and Social Services, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death along with the Notification of Death form [1] [6].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If the death occurred at home and your family member was under recent medical care for a known illness, contact the treating physician or the nearest state clinic to confirm the death. If no doctor can immediately certify natural causes at home, notify the Namibian Police Force (NAMPOL) so officers can inspect the scene and authorize removal to a state mortuary [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under Namibia's Inquests Act, any sudden, unnatural, or accidental death must be reported immediately to the Namibian Police Force. Police forensic pathology services transport the deceased to a state mortuary for a medico-legal post-mortem examination and issue an official police report and mortuary clearance before civil registration can proceed [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: All deaths occurring in Namibia must be registered under the Births, Marriages and Deaths Registration Act with the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security [1] [2]. When a death occurs in an urban area, notice should be given within 24 to 72 hours (or up to 14 days in rural districts) and always before burial takes place [1].
  • Required documents for registration: A surviving relative or authorized informant must visit a regional civil registration office or hospital sub-office of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security and present: (a) the completed Notification of Death form and medical report from the certifying doctor (or the police report and forensic post-mortem clearance if the death occurred outside a hospital or under unnatural circumstances), (b) the original Namibian National Identity Card, full birth certificate, or passport of the deceased, and (c) the original identity document or passport of the family member registering the death [1] [2].
  • Issuance of the Death Certificate and Burial Order: Initial registration and issuance of the official Death Certificate and Burial Order are free of charge [1]. It is advisable to consider requesting several certified copies of the full Death Certificate at the time of registration, as banks, pension funds, and the court require certified originals [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Engage a licensed funeral undertaker in Namibia to transfer your family member to a mortuary and coordinate with the municipal cemetery or traditional authority. A cemetery or crematorium cannot proceed without the official Burial Order issued upon civil registration [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported outside Namibia, the funeral director must obtain: (a) a certified Death Certificate from the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security [1], (b) an embalming and non-infectious disease certificate plus an export/removal permit from the environmental health division of the Ministry of Health and Social Services [6], (c) a sealing certificate confirming the body is enclosed in a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin, and (d) consular clearance or a laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy or high commission.
  • Apostille and document legalization: Because Namibia is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Namibian Death Certificates and estate records intended for use in another Apostille country should be authenticated with an Apostille through the Ministry of Justice or the Registrar of the High Court [3]. For non-Apostille countries, documents require diplomatic or consular legalization.

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• Social Security Commission claims: If the deceased was employed in Namibia and registered under the Maternity, Sick, and Death (MSD) Fund or the Funeral Benefit Scheme, eligible dependents or the person who paid funeral expenses can claim a death and funeral benefit from the Social Security Commission [5]. Claims must be submitted on the prescribed MSD claim forms with certified copies of the Death Certificate, deceased's ID, claimant's ID, and marriage or birth certificates proving dependency [5].
  • Government Institutions Pension Fund benefits: If your family member was a civil servant, public sector employee, or state retiree, notify the human resources department of the participating employer and submit funeral benefit, spouse's pension, and child's pension claims to the Government Institutions Pension Fund [4]. Required documents include certified copies of the Death Certificate, National IDs, full birth certificates of minor or student children, marriage certificate, and a bank confirmation letter [4].
  • Old-age social grant, tax, and banking notifications: If the deceased received a state old-age or disability social grant, notify the Ministry of Gender Equality, Poverty Eradication and Social Welfare immediately to stop overpayments. Notify the Namibia Revenue Agency (NamRA) for final income tax assessment, and present the Death Certificate to Namibian commercial banks so individual accounts are frozen pending estate administration [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession
steps.html:
• Reporting the estate to the Master of the High Court: Under the Administration of Estates Act 66 of 1965, every deceased estate in Namibia with assets must be reported within 14 days of death to the Master of the High Court (under the Ministry of Justice) in Windhoek or Oshakati, or to the local Magistrate's Court for smaller regional estates [3].
  • Required probate filings: The surviving family or nominated executor must lodge a Death Notice (Form D1), the original Last Will and Testament (if the deceased left a will), a Next-of-Kin Affidavit (if intestate), a preliminary Inventory of all movable and immovable assets, and a nomination for the appointment of an executor [3].
  • Letters of Executorship vs. Letters of Authority: For estates exceeding the statutory small-estate threshold, the Master of the High Court issues formal Letters of Executorship, requiring the executor (assisted by a Namibian legal practitioner, trust company, or auditor) to publish notices to creditors in the Government Gazette and a local newspaper and lodge a Liquidation and Distribution Account [3]. For smaller estates below the statutory threshold, the Master issues simplified Letters of Authority under Section 18(3) of the Act [3].
  • Taxation and cross-border coordination: Namibia does not levy a separate statutory estate duty or inheritance tax on beneficiaries, though estate administration fees, Master's fees, and deeds registry transfer fees apply [3]. If an heir resides abroad or if the deceased held foreign assets, a foreign grant of probate can be resealed by the Master of the High Court in Namibia, or an heir living outside Namibia can execute a special Power of Attorney (authenticated by Apostille) authorizing a Namibian attorney to represent their succession share [3].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Namibia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Namibia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Namibia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Namibia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, we can help you organize the essential medical, legal, financial, and administrative arrangements in sequence while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public healthcare and clinical referrals: In the public health sector, the Ministry of Health and Social Services oversees pain management, oncology referrals (including the Dr. AB May Cancer Care Centre at Windhoek Central Hospital), and symptom control across state hospitals and regional clinics [1]. Ask the treating specialist for a written clinical summary, a comprehensive symptom and pain-relief plan, and a direct referral to outpatient or community support [1].
  • Community palliative care and home nursing: For home-based nursing, psychosocial counseling, caregiver guidance, and medical equipment loans, contact Palliative Care Namibia (working alongside the Cancer Association of Namibia and regional community health networks), which coordinates interdisciplinary palliative care and family support across Namibia [2].
  • Public and private medical aid coverage: If your family member is a public servant or dependent covered by the Public Service Employees Medical Aid Scheme (PSEMAS), or holds private coverage through a Namibia Financial Institutions Supervisory Authority (NAMFISA) registered medical aid fund, ask the attending physician to submit a chronic and serious-illness pre-authorization request so oncology medications, home oxygen, and palliative nursing visits are approved without interruption [1, 2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance medical directive (Living Will): While Namibia does not yet have a standalone statute dedicated exclusively to living wills, patient autonomy and informed consent are protected under common law, constitutional rights to dignity and bodily integrity, and the Patient Charter of the Ministry of Health and Social Services [1]. While your family member has full mental capacity, they can sign a written Advance Healthcare Directive stating their wishes regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and comfort-focused palliative care [1, 2].
  • Medical capacity and witnessing: To ensure treating physicians and hospitals respect the directive without dispute, have the attending doctor confirm in the medical file that the patient was of sound mind when signing, and have two independent adult witnesses (who are not beneficiaries of the estate) co-sign the document [1].
  • Appointing a healthcare spokesperson: Include in the directive the name and contact details of a trusted primary and alternate family representative authorized to communicate with medical teams, access clinical records, and express the patient's wishes if they later become unable to speak for themselves [1, 2]. Provide copies to the treating hospital, family doctor, and household caregivers.

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Special and General Powers of Attorney: Under Namibian common law, a Power of Attorney must be executed while the principal has full mental capacity. Your family member should work with a Namibian legal practitioner or notary public to sign a General Power of Attorney (or a Specific Power of Attorney for property and administrative filings) authorizing a trusted agent to manage day-to-day financial, tax, and administrative affairs [6].
  • Important legal limitation on incapacity: Because standard common-law powers of attorney in Namibia do not automatically remain valid if the principal later loses mental capacity entirely, families facing progressive cognitive decline should consult a legal practitioner early regarding inter vivos trust structures or High Court curator bonis appointments overseen by the Master of the High Court [6].
  • Bank mandates and Deeds Registry requirements: Namibian commercial banks generally require the account holder to sign the bank's own internal third-party signing mandate and complete biometric or in-branch verification while still able to appear or sign. If an agent will need to sell, mortgage, or transfer immovable property registered at the Deeds Registry, a Special Power of Attorney must be drafted by a conveyancer and attested by two competent witnesses or a commissioner of oaths [6].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Sick Leave, and Social Security Benefits
steps.html:
• Social Security Commission sickness and disability benefits: If your family member is an employed contributor to the Maternity, Sick, and Death (MSD) Fund, they can claim paid sick leave benefits and, if medically certified as permanently unable to work, a disability benefit from the Social Security Commission [5]. Applications must include the prescribed MSD claim forms, certified identity documents, employer confirmation, and a detailed medical assessment from the treating physician [5].
  • Government Institutions Pension Fund ill-health and disability benefits: If the ill person is a civil servant or public-sector employee contributing to the Government Institutions Pension Fund, contact the employer's human resources office to initiate a medical board assessment for ill-health retirement or permanent disability income benefits (which provide ongoing income protection while preserving member coverage) [4].
  • State Disability Grant: For Namibian citizens or permanent residents aged 16 to 59 who do not have sufficient occupational cover and are certified by a state medical officer as temporarily or permanently disabled due to severe illness, an application can be submitted for the statutory Disability Grant administered by the Ministry of Gender Equality, Poverty Eradication and Social Welfare [3].
  • Caregiver leave arrangements: Family members employed in Namibia should coordinate compassionate or family responsibility leave with their employers under the Labour Act and collective agreements, supported by a medical certificate from the patient's treating doctor [1, 5].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid Will: Under the Wills Act 7 of 1953 (as applied in Namibia), a valid will must be in writing and signed at the end by the testator (and on every preceding page if more than one page) in the simultaneous presence of at least two competent witnesses aged 14 or older who also sign in the testator's presence [6]. Critically, a witness (or their spouse) cannot inherit or be nominated as executor under the will, so always use independent witnesses [6].
  • Pension and insurance beneficiary nominations (outside the estate): Review and update the official Expression of Wish / Beneficiary Nomination forms held by the Government Institutions Pension Fund [4], the Social Security Commission [5], and any private retirement annuity or life insurer. Pension fund death benefits are distributed by the fund trustees to dependents and nominees rather than passing solely through the will [4].
  • Consolidating vital identity and property documents: Assemble a secure folder containing the original Namibian National ID Card, full Birth Certificate, Marriage Certificate (and antenuptial contract if married out of community of property), title deeds, vehicle registration papers, and a list of bank accounts so the estate can later be reported smoothly to the Master of the High Court [6].
  • Cross-border assets and foreign family members: If the ill person owns assets outside Namibia or if a nominated executor or beneficiary lives abroad, ensure that separate situs wills or cross-border powers of attorney are coordinated and authenticated with a Hague Apostille through the High Court or Ministry of Justice [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nigeria: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nigeria: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Nigeria: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Nigeria, we can guide you through the official medical certification, civil registration, funeral or repatriation permits, pension and social insurance notifications, and probate procedures in the order they should be handled.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: If your family member died in a federal teaching hospital, state general hospital, or licensed private medical facility regulated under the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the attending medical practitioner examines the body and issues an official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [2] [3].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If the death occurred at home after a documented illness, transfer the deceased to a recognized hospital mortuary or summon the attending physician to verify the death and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death. Where no doctor treated the deceased recently, the local police division must be notified to issue a police extract before a public hospital doctor can certify the death [1] [3].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under Nigerian coroner laws, any sudden, unnatural, or accidental death must be reported immediately to the Nigeria Police Force. The police issue a formal Police Report and refer the case to the Coroner and a government pathologist for an autopsy before a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and burial clearance can be released [1] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the National Population Commission
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Births, Deaths, Etc. (Compulsory Registration) Act, all deaths in Nigeria must be registered with the National Population Commission, which operates the Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (eCRVS) platform and local government registration centers nationwide [1]. Statutory registration should be completed within 48 hours of a death in an urban or hospital setting or within 30 days at a local registration center (late registration requires a supporting affidavit and administrative clearance) [1].
  • Required documents for registration: A surviving family member or informant must provide: (a) the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's Certificate and Police Report), (b) the National Identification Number (NIN) issued by the National Identity Management Commission (or valid passport/voter card) of both the deceased and the informant [1] [6], and (c) personal particulars of the deceased including date, time, and place of death.
  • Official Certificate of Registration of Death: Upon verification, the National Population Commission issues the official Certificate of Registration of Death (Form D2) [1] [3]. Request multiple certified copies or keep the verified digital certificate accessible, as Pension Fund Administrators, commercial banks, and State High Court Probate Registries require the National Population Commission certificate rather than a hospital medical note alone [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: Engage a licensed funeral home in Nigeria to manage mortuary preservation and obtain a municipal burial or cremation permit from the relevant Local Government Area (LGA) health department using the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and the Death Certificate from the National Population Commission [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the body or cremated ashes must be repatriated outside Nigeria, the funeral director must obtain: (a) the official Death Certificate from the National Population Commission [1], (b) an embalming certificate, non-infectious disease clearance, and Port Health Services export permit under the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare [2], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate confirming hermetically sealed zinc-lined containment, and (d) a consular mortuary transit permit or laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy or high commission in Abuja or Lagos.
  • Document authentication and consular legalization: Nigeria is not currently a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Therefore, Nigerian Death Certificates, Coroner reports, and court probate grants intended for official use abroad must first be authenticated by the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja and then legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country.

steps.title: Notify Pension, Social Insurance, Identity, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) death benefits: If your family member was an active or retired employee in the public or private sector holding a Retirement Savings Account (RSA), notify their employer and Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) under the regulatory framework of the National Pension Commission [3] [4]. Under the Pension Reform Act, survivor benefits include the accumulated RSA balance plus proceeds from the mandatory employer Group Life Insurance policy (for death in active service), paid to the beneficiaries named in a probated will or to the surviving spouse, children, or recorded next-of-kin upon presentation of Letters of Administration [3] [4].
  • Employees' Compensation Scheme claims: If the death resulted from a workplace injury, occupational disease, or work-related transit accident, the employer and surviving dependents should file a death compensation claim with the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund, which provides monthly survivor compensation and funeral support to eligible dependents [5].
  • Identity, tax, and banking notifications: Report the death to the National Identity Management Commission to update the deceased's NIN status [6], notify the relevant State Internal Revenue Service (SIRS) or Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) to close out personal income tax records, and notify commercial banks to freeze individual accounts until probate or Letters of Administration are granted [3] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain Probate or Letters of Administration
steps.html:
• Jurisdiction of the State High Court Probate Registry: Formal estate administration in Nigeria is overseen by the Probate Registry of the State High Court (or the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja) where the deceased was domiciled or held property [3] [4].
  • Testate estates (Grant of Probate): If your family member left a valid Will, the named executors must apply to the Probate Registry for a Grant of Probate by filing the original Will, the Death Certificate from the National Population Commission, executor and witness affidavits, and an inventory and valuation of movable and immovable assets [1, 3, 4].
  • Intestate estates (Letters of Administration): If your family member died without a Will, the surviving spouse, adult children, or statutory next-of-kin must apply to the State High Court Probate Registry for Letters of Administration [3] [4]. The registry publishes a statutory notice in a national newspaper or gazette inviting objections (usually for 21 days) before issuing the grant [4].
  • Estate fees and cross-border coordination: While Nigeria does not impose a separate federal inheritance tax, State High Court Probate Registries charge a statutory estate fee (commonly 5% to 10% depending on the state) on the assessed value of the estate before sealing the grant. If an executor or heir resides outside Nigeria, they can execute a notarized Power of Attorney (legalized at a Nigerian embassy or high commission abroad) appointing a Nigerian legal practitioner to process probate or reseal a foreign grant in Nigeria.

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your exact situation, in which Nigerian state (or the FCT) did your family member pass away, and did they hold a Retirement Savings Account regulated by the National Pension Commission?
