title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nigeria: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nigeria: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Nigeria: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Nigeria is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, we can help you coordinate the key medical, legal, financial, and administrative steps in sequence while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Pain Management, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist palliative care units: The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, together with the National Cancer Control Programme, coordinates oncology and palliative care services across federal teaching hospitals and tertiary medical centers in Nigeria (such as University College Hospital Ibadan, Lagos University Teaching Hospital, National Hospital Abuja, and University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital Enugu) [1, 2]. Ask the primary specialist for a formal referral to the hospital's multidisciplinary Pain and Palliative Care Unit for symptom control, regulated oral opioid pain relief, and home-care guidance [1, 2].
  • Hospice and home nursing support: Where the patient prefers care at home, coordinate through the hospital palliative team and accredited community hospice providers affiliated with the Hospice and Palliative Care Association of Nigeria (HPCAN) to arrange home nursing visits, caregiver training, and medical equipment [2].
  • National Health Insurance Authority and HMO coverage: Review your family member's enrollment under the National Health Insurance Authority (established under the NHIA Act 2022), state social health insurance agencies, or private Health Maintenance Organizations (HMOs) [3]. Request that the treating consultant submit clinical reports for chronic, oncology, or catastrophic health fund coverage so eligible hospital admissions, medications, and supportive therapies are pre-authorized [1, 3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Appoint a Medical Proxy
steps.html:
• Patient autonomy and written treatment preferences: Under Nigeria's National Health Act 2014 and constitutional protections of personal dignity, every mentally competent adult has the right to participate in healthcare decisions and to give or refuse informed consent to medical treatment [1]. While your family member has full capacity, they can sign a written Advance Healthcare Directive recording their preferences on cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, intensive care admission, and comfort-focused palliative care [1, 2].
  • Designating a Healthcare Proxy (Medical Representative): In the same directive, the ill person should nominate a trusted primary and alternate family representative authorized to receive confidential medical disclosures, consult with doctors, and make treatment decisions if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [1].
  • Physician attestation and notarization: Because clinical teams in Nigeria often consult extended family members during serious illness, having the attending consultant document the patient's mental capacity in the hospital case file and having the directive signed before a Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths helps prevent family disputes and gives clear legal reassurance to medical staff [1].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Power of Attorney for property and administration: While your family member retains full legal capacity, instruct a Nigerian legal practitioner (Solicitor and Advocate of the Supreme Court of Nigeria) to draft a formal Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted agent to manage financial obligations, collect rents, represent the principal before government agencies, and handle property matters [4].
  • Execution by deed, stamping, and registration: If the Power of Attorney authorizes the agent to execute deeds or deal with land and real estate, it must be executed as a Deed (signed, sealed, and delivered), attested by a Notary Public, magistrate, or judge, stamped at the Federal or State Stamp Duties Office, and registered at the relevant State Lands Registry.
  • Commercial bank mandates and common-law capacity limits: Nigerian commercial banks frequently require the account holder to execute the bank's specific Third-Party Mandate Form and complete Bank Verification Number (BVN) and National Identification Number (NIN) biometric confirmation in person or through a branch relationship manager while capacity is intact. Because an ordinary common-law Power of Attorney in Nigeria can be challenged if the donor subsequently loses mental capacity, establish clear joint or mandated operating accounts and consult a solicitor early regarding a living trust if long-term cognitive incapacity is anticipated.

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Pension, Disability, and Workplace Benefits
steps.html:
• Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) invalidity and medical retirement: If your family member holds a Retirement Savings Account (RSA) regulated by the National Pension Commission, an employee who is certified by a properly constituted medical board as no longer mentally or physically capable of carrying out the functions of their office due to total or permanent disability may access their RSA balance under the Revised Regulation on the Administration of Retirement and Terminal Benefits [4]. Contact the employer and the Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) to initiate medical board certification for invalidity retirement [4].
  • Employees' Compensation Scheme disability claims: If the severe illness or permanent disability is occupational or work-related, file a disability compensation and medical expense claim with the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund under the Employees' Compensation Act [5].
  • Employer sick leave and caregiver arrangements: Review the ill person's employment contract or Public Service Rules regarding extended paid medical leave and medical board evaluations, and obtain an official medical report from the treating tertiary hospital so employed family caregivers can request compassionate or family leave from their employers [1, 5].

steps.title: Review the Will, RSA Beneficiary Records, and Vital Documents
steps.html:
• Executing or updating a valid Will: Under the Wills Act and applicable State Wills Laws (such as the Wills Law of Lagos State), a valid will must be in writing and signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent adult witnesses, who must also sign in the testator's presence (witnesses and their spouses must not be beneficiaries) [4]. For enhanced security against later tampering or contestation, the original sealed Will can be lodged for safekeeping during the testator's lifetime at the Probate Registry of the State High Court.
  • Updating PFA next-of-kin and insurance records: Ensure that the named beneficiaries and next-of-kin records held by the Pension Fund Administrator under the supervision of the National Pension Commission [4] and by the employer's Group Life Insurance underwriter match the ill person's wishes, and verify that all family members' names match their official civil registration records with the National Population Commission [6].
  • Cross-border assets and diaspora family coordination: Assemble original Certificates of Occupancy, registered deeds of assignment, share certificates, and civil status records in a secure file [6]. If family members, executors, or assets are located outside Nigeria, remember that Nigeria is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so cross-border powers of attorney or legal instruments must be notarized and legalized through a Nigerian embassy or high commission abroad (or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja).

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance to your family's circumstances, in which Nigerian state is your family member receiving care, and are they covered under the National Health Insurance Authority or a Retirement Savings Account regulated by the National Pension Commission?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Rwanda: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Rwanda: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Rwanda: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Rwanda, we can guide you through the official medical certification, civil death registration on IremboGov, funeral or repatriation permits, social security claims, and succession procedures in the order they must be completed.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or health facility: If your family member died in a district hospital, referral hospital, or accredited health center regulated by the Ministry of Health, the attending physician examines the body, records the medical cause of death directly in the National Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) electronic system, and issues an official Medical Death Certificate [1] [6].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If the death occurred at home (in a village or cell), immediately notify the Village Leader (Umukuru w'Umudugudu) and the Cell Executive Secretary (Umunyamabanga Nshingwabikorwa w'Akagari) along with at least two adult witnesses so the death can be verified locally and reported to the Sector Civil Registrar [1] [5].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or suspicious deaths: Any sudden, unnatural, or unexplained death must be reported immediately to the Rwanda National Police (RNP) and the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB). Authorities transfer the deceased to the Rwanda Forensic Institute (RFI) or a referral hospital mortuary for a medico-legal post-mortem examination and issue official forensic clearance before burial or registration can proceed [5] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry via IremboGov
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Law Governing Persons and Family overseen by the Ministry of Justice, all deaths occurring in Rwanda must be declared to the Civil Status Officer at the Sector (Umurenge) office or health facility within 30 days of the death [1] [5].
  • Electronic registration and NIDA update: Once a health facility or Sector Civil Registrar records the death in the CRVS system, the deceased's National Identification Agency (NIDA) record is automatically updated [1]. To obtain the official Death Record or Death Certificate (Icyemezo cy'uwitabye Imana), a family member applies online through the IremboGov e-government portal (or with the assistance of an Irembo agent) using the deceased's National ID number or Child Application Number [1] [2].
  • Fees and processing time: The electronic Death Certificate application on IremboGov is processed by the Sector Executive Secretary (typically within 1 working day) and delivered digitally with a verifiable QR code and document number [2]. Save and print multiple copies, as banks, pension authorities, and Sector offices require the official IremboGov Death Certificate [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Coordinate mortuary transfer and burial arrangements with a licensed funeral service provider and the local Sector or District administration. Public cemeteries in Kigali and across Rwandan districts require the medical death notification or the official Death Certificate and municipal burial authorization before interment [1] [6].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be repatriated outside Rwanda, the funeral director must obtain: (a) the official Death Certificate via IremboGov [2], (b) an embalming certificate, non-infectious disease clearance, and mortuary export authorization from the Ministry of Health [6], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate confirming hermetically sealed zinc-lined containment for air freight, and (d) a consular mortuary laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy or high commission in Kigali.
  • Apostille and document legalization: Rwanda is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Rwandan Death Certificates, notarial acts, and succession certificates intended for official use in another Apostille member state can be authenticated with an e-Apostille applied for through IremboGov and issued by the Ministry of Justice or Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• Rwanda Social Security Board funeral grant and survivor benefits: If the deceased was an active contributor or retired pensioner under the national pension scheme, eligible survivors (surviving legal spouse, qualifying children, or surviving parents if there is no spouse or child) can claim a Survivor's Pension or survivor lump-sum allowance and a statutory funeral grant from the Rwanda Social Security Board [3]. Claims are submitted through the Imisanzu digital portal or an RSSB branch using the deceased's RSSB number and National ID, the official IremboGov Death Certificate, the Certificate of Succession, and a Certificate of Being Alive for the beneficiaries [2] [3].
  • Occupational hazards death benefits: If the death resulted from a workplace accident or occupational disease, notify the employer and file a work-injury survivor claim with the Rwanda Social Security Board within the statutory reporting period [3].
  • Tax, health insurance, and banking notifications: Notify the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) if the deceased held a Tax Identification Number (TIN) or operated a registered business, update dependent records under the RSSB Medical Scheme (RAMA) or Community-Based Health Insurance (Mutuelle de Sante), and present the Death Certificate to commercial banks and SACCOs to freeze individual accounts pending succession clearance [2] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain the Certificate of Succession
steps.html:
• Family Council (Inteko y'Umuryango) and Certificate of Succession: Under Rwandan succession law (Law Governing Matrimonial Regimes, Donations and Successions) and the Law Governing Persons and Family overseen by the Ministry of Justice, the surviving family convenes a formal Family Council meeting to identify the rightful heirs, review any valid Will, and appoint an estate liquidator or administrator [4] [5].
  • Applying for the Certificate of Succession on IremboGov: Using the signed minutes of the Family Council meeting, the deceased's Death Certificate, and the heirs' National IDs, the appointed representative applies online through IremboGov for an official Certificate of Succession (Icyemezo cy'izungura), which is verified and issued by the Sector Executive Secretary [4].
  • Probate of wills, land transfer, and dispute resolution: If the deceased left a notarial or holograph Will, it is opened and executed in accordance with Rwandan succession rules reserving protected portions for legal heirs [5]. Land titles are transferred to the heirs through the National Land Authority (via IremboGov land succession transfer services). Any contested succession disputes that cannot be resolved by the Family Council or local Abunzi mediation committees (within their statutory monetary jurisdiction) are referred to the competent Primary or Intermediate Court of the Judiciary of Rwanda [5].
  • Taxation and cross-border coordination: Rwanda does not levy a separate statutory inheritance tax on estates passing to legal heirs, though standard notarial and land title transfer fees apply [4] [5]. If an heir resides abroad, they can execute a notarized Power of Attorney at a Rwandan embassy or high commission (or authenticated by Apostille) authorizing a representative in Rwanda to sign Family Council and succession transfer documents on their behalf [4] [5].

titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Rwanda: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Rwanda: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Rwanda is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, we can help you coordinate the essential medical, legal, financial, and administrative steps in order while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Support, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Integrated hospital and community palliative care: Rwanda integrates palliative care and pain management (including regulated oral morphine access) across all levels of the public health system through the Non-Communicable Diseases Division of the Rwanda Biomedical Centre [1]. Request a formal clinical referral from your family member's treating physician at a district or referral hospital (such as King Faisal Hospital, Kigali University Teaching Hospital - CHUK, Butaro Cancer Center of Excellence, or Rwanda Military Hospital) to the hospital's multidisciplinary palliative care desk [1].
  • Home-based care and community health workers: At the sector and village level, hospital palliative teams coordinate with community health workers and specialized home-care nurses (including the Rwanda Palliative Care and Hospice Organization) to provide home symptom management, psychosocial counseling, and family caregiver training [1].
  • Public and community health insurance coverage: Verify that your family member's health insurance contributions are active with the Rwanda Social Security Board under either the formal sector Medical Scheme (RAMA) [2] or the Community-Based Health Insurance scheme (Mutuelle de Sante / CBHI) [3]. Ensure that referrals from the health center to the district and referral hospital follow the required referral pathway so hospitalization, pain medications, and specialist treatments remain covered [2, 3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written medical preferences and informed consent: Under Rwandan healthcare regulations and the Law Governing Persons and Family overseen by the Ministry of Justice, every patient who possesses mental capacity has the right to be informed of their diagnosis and to consent to or refuse proposed medical interventions [1, 6]. While your family member has full capacity, they can sign a written statement of treatment preferences detailing their wishes regarding intensive care, resuscitation, artificial life support, and comfort-focused palliative care [1].
  • Designating a trusted family medical proxy: In the written directive and the hospital admission record, the ill person should explicitly name a primary and alternate adult family representative (trusted person of confidence) authorized to receive medical updates from doctors and communicate healthcare decisions if the patient later loses the ability to speak or decide [1, 6].
  • Clinical and notarial documentation: Ask the attending specialist to note the patient's decision-making capacity in the clinical file and place a signed copy of the advance medical preferences and representative designation in the hospital record, keeping duplicate copies with the family caregiver [1].

steps.title: Execute Notarized Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Procuration): While your family member retains full legal capacity, they should execute an authentic Power of Attorney (Inyandiko mpamo y'ubuhagararire / Procuration) authorizing a trusted representative to manage bank accounts, administrative filings, tax obligations, and property transactions [5, 6].
  • Applying for public or private notary services via IremboGov: In Rwanda, notarization of a Power of Attorney is initiated online through the IremboGov portal under Notary Services [5]. Depending on the purpose of the mandate, the document can be notarized before a Sector or District public notary (for domestic civil and land matters), a notary at the Ministry of Justice (for documents with international effect), or a licensed private notary [5, 6]. If the ill person is hospitalized or homebound, a notary can arrange a bedside attendance to verify identity and mental capacity before witnessing the signature.
  • Commercial bank mandates: Rwandan commercial banks and microfinance institutions (SACCOs) require the account holder to register a formal third-party account mandate or notarized Power of Attorney and verify the agent's National ID while the principal is still able to consent [5].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Pension, Workplace, and Social Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Rwanda Social Security Board invalidity pension: If your family member is a registered contributor under the national pension scheme who becomes permanently incapacitated and unable to engage in remunerated employment before reaching standard retirement age, they can apply for an Invalidity Pension from the Rwanda Social Security Board [4]. The claim requires a formal medical evaluation by an RSSB-approved physician confirming permanent physical or mental invalidity, along with contribution records and National ID verification [4].
  • Continued medical coverage for invalidity pensioners: Beneficiaries receiving an invalidity or retirement pension under the Rwanda Social Security Board pension scheme remain eligible for medical coverage under the RSSB Medical Scheme [2, 4].
  • Occupational disease benefits and caregiver leave: If the life-limiting illness is work-related, file an occupational hazard claim with the Rwanda Social Security Board [4]. Employed family caregivers should obtain an official medical certificate from the treating hospital to arrange authorized family or compassionate leave with their employer.

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Drafting a valid Will under Rwandan law: Under Rwandan succession law (Law Governing Matrimonial Regimes, Donations and Successions) and the Law Governing Persons and Family overseen by the Ministry of Justice, a person with full mental capacity may execute an authentic (notarial) Will before a notary via IremboGov or a dated and signed holograph (handwritten) Will [5, 6]. Note that Rwandan succession law protects the statutory reserved portion for legal heirs (children and surviving spouse) and respects the applicable matrimonial property regime (community of property, limited community, or separation of property) [6].
  • Verifying civil registry and land records: Check on IremboGov that the ill person's National ID, marriage certificate, and children's birth records are accurately linked in the National Identification Agency (NIDA) registry, and gather Unique Parcel Identifiers (UPIs) and land e-titles registered with the National Land Authority [5, 6].
  • Updating RSSB and insurance beneficiary records: Confirm that dependent and spouse details registered with the Rwanda Social Security Board [4] and private insurers are up to date.
  • Cross-border assets and diaspora family members: Because Rwanda is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, powers of attorney or estate documents executed in Rwanda for use abroad can be authenticated with an e-Apostille via IremboGov and the Ministry of Justice, while family members living abroad can execute powers of attorney at a Rwandan embassy or high commission [5, 6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Seychelles: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Seychelles: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Seychelles: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Seychelles. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - from medical certification and civil status registration within the statutory window to funeral arrangements, survivor pension notifications, and succession under the Civil Code of Seychelles.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: When a death occurs at Seychelles Hospital on Mahe, Baie Ste Anne Hospital on Praslin, La Digue Hospital, or a private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [3]. Under current procedures, healthcare personnel also transmit an electronic death notification directly to the Civil Status Office to prepare the civil register entry [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (expected or natural causes): If your family member passed away at home under ongoing medical supervision, contact the regional community health centre under the Ministry of Health or the treating physician so a doctor can verify the death and issue the medical certificate [2] [3].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Where a medical certificate cannot be issued immediately - or if the death was sudden, accidental, or unattended by a physician - the informants must notify the Seychelles Police Force before any civil declaration takes place [1] [2]. Police authorities coordinate with the forensic pathologist and judicial authorities under the Supreme Court of Seychelles for an inquiry or post-mortem examination before releasing the body and issuing medical clearance for registration [1] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Status Office
steps.html:
• Statutory 24-hour deadline: In Seychelles, a death must normally be declared and registered at the Civil Status Office (under the Division of Immigration and Civil Status) within 24 hours of the passing [1] [2]. The main office is located at Independence House in Victoria, Mahe, with branch civil status services available on Praslin and La Digue and weekend/public holiday standby hours for urgent burial clearances [1] [2].
  • Two informants required: Formal registration requires the physical presence of two adult informants (typically close relatives or next of kin who have knowledge of the deceased's civil particulars) [1] [2].
  • Required documentation: The two informants must present the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, the National Identity Card (or passport) of the deceased, the deceased's birth and marriage certificates if available, and the valid National Identity Cards of both informants [1] [2].
  • Issuance of certificates and burial permit: Upon completing the entry, the Civil Status Officer issues the initial official Death Certificate and the statutory Burial Permit [1] [2]. Additional certified copies of the death certificate can be ordered in person at the Civil Status Office or online through the Seychelles e-Government CertExpress service (typically SCR 50 per copy) for banking, pension, and succession filings [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Mandatory permit before disposition: Under Seychelles law, no burial, cremation, or removal of human remains may take place until the Civil Status Office has registered the death and issued the official Burial Permit [1] [2].
  • Local burial or cremation: Once the Burial Permit is issued, the family coordinates with licensed funeral service providers, mortuary administration under the Ministry of Health, and the cemetery or crematorium authorities on Mahe, Praslin, or La Digue to schedule the funeral rites and grave allocation [1] [3].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or the family wishes to repatriate remains abroad, a licensed funeral director must obtain an embalming certificate and public health non-infection clearance from the Ministry of Health, an export permit and coffin sealing verification, and a laissez-passer for human remains from the relevant foreign embassy or consulate [1] [3].
  • Apostille and document legalisation: Because Seychelles is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, official Seychelles death certificates intended for use in another Apostille country must receive an Apostille stamp through the Foreign Affairs department or the registrar of the Supreme Court of Seychelles; for non-Apostille destinations, consular legalisation is required [1] [5].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Social Security, Tax, and Banking Institutions
steps.html:
• Seychelles Pension Fund (SPF) benefits: Notify the Seychelles Pension Fund promptly by submitting the certified Death Certificate, the deceased's National Identity Card, and claimant identity and civil status records [4]. Depending on contribution history and family status, the Seychelles Pension Fund administers the Surviving Spouse's Pension, Children's Pension for eligible minor or student dependents, or a pre-retirement or post-retirement death gratuity/lump-sum refund where no qualifying dependents survive [4].
  • Social welfare and funeral assistance: Where a household qualifies for statutory social assistance or funeral support, notify the Agency for Social Protection alongside the Civil Status Office funeral coordination unit [2] [4].
  • Banks, insurers, and tax authorities: Present certified copies of the Death Certificate to all commercial banks in Seychelles (where individual accounts are frozen pending executor or succession documentation), life and credit insurers, the Seychelles Revenue Commission to settle any outstanding tax obligations, and utility or telecommunications providers [2] [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession Under the Civil Code
steps.html:
• Governing succession law: Estate administration and inheritance in Seychelles are governed by Book III of the Civil Code of Seychelles Act 2020 [5]. Seychelles law enforces forced heirship rules (the statutory reserve or reserve hereditaire), protecting reserved shares for surviving children and, where applicable, the surviving spouse, meaning a testator may freely dispose of only the disposable portion (quotite disponible) by will [5].
  • Testate vs. intestate procedures: If your family member left a valid authentic, mystic, or holographic will, it must be presented to a Seychelles notary or proved before the Supreme Court of Seychelles so the appointed testamentary executor can act [5]. If the deceased died intestate (without a will) and the estate includes immovable property (land or real estate in Seychelles) or contested claims, the heirs must petition the Supreme Court of Seychelles to appoint a fiduciary executor to administer and distribute the estate [5].
  • Fiduciary administration and property transfers: Under the Civil Code of Seychelles, co-heirs hold immovable property through a fiduciary mechanism rather than direct undivided co-ownership; the appointed executor or notary pays verified estate debts, settles stamp or registration duties at the Land Registrar, and transfers or distributes the net estate to the lawful heirs [5].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign assets: Heirs residing outside Seychelles may execute a notarised power of attorney (legalised with a Hague Apostille) authorising a local legal practitioner or notary to represent them before the Supreme Court of Seychelles, while foreign assets generally require separate ancillary succession proceedings in the jurisdiction where those assets are located [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Seychelles: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Seychelles: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Seychelles: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Seychelles is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking structured medical, legal, and financial steps while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their autonomy and secures essential household support. Below, we outline the five key steps in chronological order under the institutional and legal framework of Seychelles.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public hospital and community palliative care: Healthcare in Seychelles is constitutionally guaranteed and delivered primarily through the Health Care Agency under the Ministry of Health [3]. Your family member's treating specialist at Seychelles Hospital in Victoria (or at Baie Ste Anne Hospital on Praslin or La Digue Hospital) can establish a multidisciplinary symptom-management, oncology, or palliative care plan and refer the patient to the district community health centre for home-based nursing visits and domiciliary pain relief [3].
  • Hospice and respite care coordination: For patients requiring inpatient supportive care or complex symptom control, ask the hospital medical social work team under the Ministry of Health about admission to specialised palliative or rehabilitative wards (such as the North East Point Hospital and Hospice facility on Mahe) and equipment loans for home mobility and nursing care [3].
  • Private insurance and overseas medical treatment: If your family member holds private medical or critical-illness insurance, obtain written clinical summaries from the treating consultant early to pre-authorise private clinic consultations, home nursing coverage, or specialized treatment under the Ministry of Health overseas medical referral programme if indicated [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Documenting clinical treatment wishes: Seychelles does not have a standalone living-will statute separate from its general civil and medical consent framework, so patient autonomy is governed by informed consent principles and the Civil Code of Seychelles Act 2020 [3] [5]. While your family member has full capacity, they should record a clear, signed written statement of their medical preferences - covering pain and symptom management, artificial life-prolonging interventions, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and preferred place of care (home versus hospital) [3] [5].
  • Integration into Ministry of Health clinical records: Provide copies of this signed statement to the lead hospital consultant and the district health centre team at the Ministry of Health so that clinical goals of care and escalation ceilings are formally noted in the patient's medical file [3].
  • Designating a primary medical spokesperson: Under the agency and mandate provisions of the Civil Code of Seychelles Act 2020, your family member can designate a trusted adult relative or representative in writing to communicate with physicians and receive confidential clinical updates if the patient later becomes unable to speak for themselves [3] [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Mandate (Power of Attorney) under the Civil Code: Articles 1984 and following of the Civil Code of Seychelles Act 2020 govern the contract of mandate (power of attorney), by which a principal authorises an agent (mandataire) to act on their behalf in financial, administrative, and property matters [5]. Crucially, the principal must possess full mental capacity at the moment the mandate is executed [5].
  • Notarial execution for property and formal acts: While a general mandate may be written under private signature for routine administration, any power of attorney authorising the sale, mortgage, or transfer of immovable property (land or real estate in Seychelles) or formal representation before public registries must be executed as an authentic deed before a Seychelles notary or attorney-at-law and registered with the Registrar General at the Supreme Court of Seychelles [2] [5].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates: Commercial banks in Seychelles often require their own internal account mandate or third-party signatory forms in addition to a general power of attorney; arrange for your family member to sign these bank-specific forms in person (or via a domiciliary bank visit with a medical certificate of capacity) while capacity is undisputed [5].
  • Limits of ordinary mandates upon incapacity: Under the Civil Code, a standard mandate may be challenged or terminated if the principal loses legal capacity unless structured appropriately; if capacity is already declining and formal protective representation is needed, families must petition the Supreme Court of Seychelles for judicial guardianship or curatelle measures [5].

steps.title: Activate Incapacity Pensions, Disability Support, and Caregiver Assistance
steps.html:
• Seychelles Pension Fund (SPF) Incapacity Pension: If your family member is a contributor under retirement age who has become permanently incapable of work due to serious illness, apply to the Seychelles Pension Fund for an Incapacity Pension [4]. The application requires identity documentation, employment contribution records, and a comprehensive medical report evaluated by the Seychelles Pension Fund medical board [4].
  • Home carer scheme and social protection: Through the Agency for Social Protection and community social services, families caring for a severely ill or bedridden person at home can apply for disability support allowances or the statutory Home Carer scheme, which provides financial support for an approved domiciliary caregiver [2] [4].
  • Employment leave and workplace protections: Employed patients and family caregivers should review statutory sick leave entitlements and compassionate or unpaid family-care arrangements with their employer, supported by medical certificates issued through the Ministry of Health [3] [4].

steps.title: Review the Will, Forced Heirship Rules, Beneficiary Designations, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Reviewing or drafting a will under Seychelles law: Book III of the Civil Code of Seychelles Act 2020 recognises three forms of wills: the authentic will (dictated before a notary), the mystic (secret) will, and the holographic will (which must be entirely handwritten, dated, and signed by the testator in person) [5]. Reviewing the will with a Seychelles notary ensures it complies with statutory forced heirship rules (reserve hereditaire), which reserve fixed portions of the estate for surviving children and protect spousal rights [5].
  • Updating pension and insurance nominations: Verify that beneficiary nomination forms filed with the Seychelles Pension Fund and any private life insurance policies are current, as nominated pension gratuities and life policies follow statutory scheme rules [4] [5].
  • Organising civil status and property records: Gather and verify original birth certificates, marriage certificates, and National Identity Cards through the Civil Status Office (using the eGov CertExpress portal if replacements are needed), alongside land title deeds (transcription or Land Register certificates) [1] [2].
  • Cross-border coordination: If your family member holds assets abroad or if prospective executors live outside Seychelles, ensure foreign powers of attorney and estate documents are prepared with a Hague Apostille through the Supreme Court of Seychelles so they are recognised across jurisdictions [1] [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sierra Leone: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sierra Leone: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Sierra Leone: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Sierra Leone. Below, we outline the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - from obtaining medical cause-of-death certification and registering the death with the National Civil Registration Authority to arranging the funeral or repatriation, claiming social security survivor benefits, and administering the estate.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or health-facility deaths: When a death occurs in a government hospital (such as Connaught Hospital in Freetown or a regional district hospital) or a licensed private clinic regulated by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, the attending physician examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [2]. This certificate records the clinical cause, date, and place of passing and is required before the mortuary releases the body or civil registration is completed [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (expected or natural causes): If your family member passed away at home in Freetown or a provincial district without a physician present, notify the nearest Peripheral Health Unit (PHU) or district medical officer under the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, as well as the local ward or chiefdom authority, so a medical officer or authorised health worker can verify the death and issue the medical notification [1] [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was unexpected, occurred in an accident, or had no recent medical attendance, report it immediately to the Sierra Leone Police [1] [2]. Police authorities refer unnatural or unexplained deaths to the Coroner under the Judiciary of Sierra Leone and the government forensic pathologist at Connaught Hospital for a post-mortem examination before issuing a coroner's certificate and burial order [2] [4].

steps.title: Register the Death with the National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA)
steps.html:
• Compulsory civil registration: Under the National Civil Registration Act, 2016, the registration of all deaths occurring in Sierra Leone is compulsory and is administered by the National Civil Registration Authority [1]. Families should report the death at the nearest NCRA district office (located in Freetown and across all district headquarters) as soon as the medical or coroner's certificate is issued, and within the statutory registration period to avoid late-registration affidavit requirements [1].
  • Required documents and informant details: A close relative or adult informant who was present at the death or responsible for the funeral arrangements must present the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's order/community notification form for rural deaths), the deceased's National Identification Card or National Identification Number (NIN) record, and the informant's valid photo ID [1].
  • Issuance of official Death Certificate: Once the entry is recorded in the civil register, the National Civil Registration Authority issues the official Death Certificate and updates the national identity database [1]. It is advisable to consider obtaining several certified copies of the NCRA Death Certificate immediately, as banks, pension authorities, and the probate registry each require certified originals [1, 3, 4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial and municipal cemetery permits: Before burial can take place in Freetown (under the Freetown City Council cemetery administration) or in a district or chiefdom cemetery, the family or licensed funeral home must present the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, the NCRA registration confirmation, and a mortuary release clearance to obtain a municipal Burial Permit [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or the family wishes to transport human remains out of Sierra Leone (via Freetown International Airport at Lungi), engage an experienced funeral director to obtain an official embalming certificate, a public health non-infection and coffin-sealing certificate from the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, an NCRA Death Certificate, a police/coroner clearance certificate, and a consular mortuary laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy or high commission [1] [2].
  • Document legalisation (Non-Apostille jurisdiction): Because Sierra Leone is not currently a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Sierra Leonean death certificates and court documents intended for official use abroad must undergo diplomatic authentication through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Freetown followed by consular legalisation at the embassy or high commission of the destination country [1] [4].

steps.title: Notify NASSIT, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• NASSIT survivor benefits and pension claims: If your family member contributed to or received a pension from the National Social Security and Insurance Trust, notify the nearest NASSIT regional office promptly [3]. Under the NASSIT Act, 2001, eligible dependents (surviving spouse and dependent children) may claim a Survivor's Pension (where the member met the minimum contribution threshold, typically 60 months of contributions) or a lump-sum Survivor's Grant [3]. Claimants must submit the NASSIT claim form, the NCRA Death Certificate, the deceased's NASSIT membership card, marriage and birth certificates of dependents, and passport photographs [1] [3].
  • Civil service or employer death gratuities: If the deceased was employed in the public service or formal private sector, notify the employer's human resources department and the Accountant General's Department to claim any terminal salary, accrued leave, or workplace funeral assistance [3].
  • Commercial banks, insurers, and tax clearance: Notify all Sierra Leonean commercial banks, mobile money providers, life insurers, and the National Revenue Authority [1] [4]. Banks will freeze sole accounts upon notification of death and will release funds above minor statutory thresholds only upon presentation of a High Court Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration [4] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Obtain Probate or Letters of Administration
steps.html:
• Governing statutory framework: Estate administration in Sierra Leone is governed by the Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 45), as amended by the Administration of Estates (Amendment) Act, 2006, together with the landmark Devolution of Estates Act, 2007 (Act No. 21 of 2007), which unified intestate succession rules across statutory, customary, and religious marriages to protect surviving spouses, children, and dependents [5] [6].
  • Testate estates (Grant of Probate): If your family member left a valid written will, the named executor(s) must apply to the Probate Registry of the High Court under the Judiciary of Sierra Leone (or through the Office of the Administrator and Registrar-General in Freetown) for a Grant of Probate [4, 5, 6].
  • Intestate estates (Letters of Administration): If the deceased died without a will, the surviving spouse, adult children, or statutory next of kin under the Devolution of Estates Act, 2007 apply to the High Court under the Judiciary of Sierra Leone or the Administrator and Registrar-General for Letters of Administration [4, 5, 6]. Notice of the application is published in the Sierra Leone Gazette to allow any caveats before the grant is sealed, and estate fees are assessed under the Administration of Estates (Amendment) Act, 2006 [6].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign grants: Where an heir or executor resides abroad, they may appoint an attorney-in-fact in Sierra Leone via a notarised and consular-legalised power of attorney; conversely, a Commonwealth or UK grant of probate may be resealed by the High Court of Sierra Leone to administer local assets [4, 5, 6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sierra Leone: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sierra Leone: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Sierra Leone: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Sierra Leone is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while your family member still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their wishes and prevents administrative delays for the household. Below, we set out the five key steps in chronological order under the institutional and legal framework of Sierra Leone.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital specialist and palliative care: Coordinate an integrated symptom-management and supportive care plan through the treating consultant at a tertiary government hospital overseen by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation (such as Connaught Hospital in Freetown or regional government hospitals in Bo, Kenema, and Makeni) or an accredited private clinic [2]. Ask the clinical team for a written medical summary detailing diagnosis, pain-control prescriptions, and home nursing requirements [2].
  • Hospice and community home-based care: In the Western Area and major districts, hospital social work and oncology units under the Ministry of Health and Sanitation coordinate referrals to specialist palliative and home-based care providers (such as The Shepherd's Hospice in Freetown and community health nurse teams) for domiciliary symptom management, analgesic supervision, and family caregiver training [2].
  • Health insurance and medical cost planning: If your family member is covered by a private health insurance policy or an employer medical scheme, submit the specialist's clinical report early to pre-authorise inpatient stays, diagnostic imaging, and home care supplies [2] [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written statement of medical treatment preferences: Sierra Leone does not currently have a standalone statutory living-will regime separate from common-law informed consent rules, so it is essential for your family member to record their treatment wishes in writing while they have full mental capacity [2] [4]. This signed document should state preferences regarding pain and symptom relief, hospital admission versus home care, and whether to withhold invasive life-prolonging interventions when recovery is no longer possible [2].
  • Designating a primary family healthcare spokesperson: In hospital practice across facilities supervised by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, clinicians consult the patient's designated next of kin when the patient can no longer communicate [2]. Having your family member sign a formal letter naming a primary and alternate medical representative - witnessed by two independent adults and placed in the hospital medical file - prevents disputes among extended relatives [2] [4].
  • Physician confirmation of capacity: When executing both healthcare instructions and legal mandates during serious illness, ask the attending doctor at the Ministry of Health and Sanitation facility or private clinic to record a contemporaneous note confirming that the patient is lucid, oriented, and capable of making autonomous decisions [2].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Executing a formal Power of Attorney: Under Sierra Leonean common-law and statutory practice overseen by the Judiciary of Sierra Leone, a person with full mental capacity may execute a Power of Attorney by deed, authorising a trusted attorney-in-fact to manage bank accounts, collect income, pay medical bills, and administer property [4].
  • Registration with the Office of the Administrator and Registrar-General: To ensure legal enforceability - especially where the attorney-in-fact may need to deal with land, leases, or third-party institutions - the Power of Attorney should be drafted by a legal practitioner, signed and witnessed before a Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths, and registered as a statutory instrument at the Office of the Administrator and Registrar-General in Freetown [4] [6].
  • Direct commercial bank signatory mandates: Commercial banks in Sierra Leone apply strict verification procedures to third-party powers of attorney; while your family member retains capacity, contact each bank directly to complete the bank's own third-party mandate or joint-signatory forms and register the National Identification Number (NIN) issued by the National Civil Registration Authority for both the account holder and the authorised representative [1] [4].
  • Legal limits if capacity is lost: Because standard common-law powers of attorney in Sierra Leone can be affected if the donor subsequently loses mental capacity, completing direct bank mandates and establishing clear trust or joint-account arrangements while capacity is intact avoids the need for complex High Court applications before the Judiciary of Sierra Leone [4].

steps.title: Activate NASSIT Invalidity Benefits and Workplace Support
steps.html:
• NASSIT Invalidity Pension or Invalidity Grant: If your family member is an active or past contributor under the age of 60 who has been rendered permanently incapable of gainful employment due to serious illness, apply to the National Social Security and Insurance Trust for an Invalidity Pension (available where the member has at least 60 monthly contributions, including 12 within the 36 months preceding invalidity) or a lump-sum Invalidity Grant if contribution thresholds are not fully met [3].
  • Medical Board assessment: Claims filed with the National Social Security and Insurance Trust must be supported by a comprehensive medical certificate from the treating practitioner and are evaluated by the NASSIT Medical Board to certify permanent incapacity [2] [3].
  • Employer sick leave and medical boarding: For civil servants and formal-sector employees, coordinate with the employer's human resources department regarding paid statutory sick leave, compassionate caregiver leave, or formal medical boarding procedures so that employment terminal benefits and NASSIT entitlements are preserved [2] [3].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Records
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid Will: Under the Devolution of Estates Act, 2007 (Act No. 21 of 2007) and the Wills Act rules applied by the Judiciary of Sierra Leone, a will must be in writing and signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent witnesses (who must not be beneficiaries or spouses of beneficiaries) [4] [5]. Note that under the Devolution of Estates Act, 2007, a court may make reasonable financial provision from an estate if a will fails to provide adequately for a dependent spouse, child, or parent [5].
  • Safe custody and statutory registration: A completed will can be lodged for safe custody with the Probate Registry of the High Court under the Judiciary of Sierra Leone or with the Office of the Administrator and Registrar-General under the Administration of Estates framework [4] [6].
  • Updating NASSIT and insurance nominations: Verify that survivor and beneficiary nomination records with the National Social Security and Insurance Trust and private insurers accurately list the spouse and dependent children, supported by civil birth and marriage certificates issued by the National Civil Registration Authority [1, 3, 5].
  • Cross-border assets and consular legalisation: Compile all title deeds, survey plans, and bank records; if any family representatives or assets are located abroad, remember that Sierra Leone is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so powers of attorney executed abroad for use in Sierra Leone must be notarised and legalised through the relevant Sierra Leone embassy or high commission [4] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Somalia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Somalia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Somalia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Somalia. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order - covering medical certification of cause of death, municipal civil registration and identity records, burial or international repatriation clearances, employment and social protection notifications, and estate succession.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical facility deaths: When a death occurs in a public or referral hospital overseen by the Ministry of Health and Human Services (such as Medina Hospital, Banadir Hospital, or Erdogan Referral Hospital in Mogadishu, or regional general hospitals across the Federal Member States) or a licensed private clinic, the attending physician examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Notification and Certificate of Cause of Death [3].
  • Deaths at home (natural or expected causes): Because Islamic custom in Somalia requires prompt burial, when a family member dies at home of natural causes, families should immediately request a physician from the nearest hospital or district health centre under the Ministry of Health and Human Services, or obtain a signed witness attestation from the local district commissioner (Guddoomiyaha Degmada) and two adult male or community witnesses confirming the identity and natural passing of the deceased [1] [3].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was unnatural, accidental, or occurred under suspicious circumstances, it must be reported immediately to the Somali Police Force and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) before burial [1] [3]. Police and judicial authorities coordinate with a government medical officer under the Ministry of Health and Human Services to conduct a medico-legal examination and issue formal police clearance for burial and civil registration [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Registry and NIRA
steps.html:
• Municipal civil status registration: Official civil registration of deaths is carried out through the local municipal government civil status directorate - such as the Banadir Regional Administration (Mogadishu Municipality) Directorate of Civil Registration or the respective district municipality in the Federal Member States - in coordination with the Federal Government CRVS framework [1] [2]. Even where burial takes place immediately on the day of passing, the family should register the death as soon as possible to obtain the official Municipal Death Certificate (Warqadda Dhimashada) required for court and banking procedures [1].
  • Required documents and witnesses: The informant (typically a close adult relative) must present the hospital Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or district witness attestation and police clearance), the deceased's Somali passport or National Identity Card issued by the National Identification and Registration Authority, the informant's own identity document, and two adult witnesses [1] [2].
  • Updating the foundational National ID register: Once the municipal death certificate is issued, notify the National Identification and Registration Authority so that the deceased's biometric National ID record is formally deactivated in the federal population registry [1] [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial procedures: In accordance with Islamic rites in Somalia, cremation is not practiced, and burial (Janaaso) normally takes place within 24 hours of death at a designated municipal or community cemetery after obtaining the hospital medical release (or police clearance in non-natural deaths) and notifying the local district administration [1] [3].
  • International repatriation of remains: When a foreign national dies in Somalia or a Somali diaspora family wishes to repatriate remains abroad (typically via Aden Adde International Airport in Mogadishu or major regional airports), a hospital mortuary and licensed logistics provider must secure: (1) a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and a public health non-infection and embalming/hermetic coffin-sealing certificate from the Ministry of Health and Human Services, (2) a municipal Death Certificate, (3) CID/police clearance and airport customs export authorization, and (4) a consular laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy [1] [3].
  • Document legalisation (Non-Apostille jurisdiction): Somalia is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [1]. Consequently, Somali death certificates, heirship certificates, and court orders intended for use abroad must be authenticated by the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Mogadishu, and then legalised by the embassy or consulate of the destination country (frequently processed via accredited missions in Mogadishu or Nairobi) [1].

steps.title: Notify Employment, Social Protection, and Banking Institutions
steps.html:
• Workplace and civil service death benefits: Somalia does not yet operate a universal contributory national pension fund for all private-sector workers, though labour standards and social protection frameworks are expanding under the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs in partnership with the International Labour Organization [4] [5]. If the deceased was a federal civil servant, member of the security forces, or formal-sector employee under the Somali Labour Code, notify the employing ministry or company human resources department and the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs to claim unpaid wages, terminal service gratuities, and any occupational survivor compensation [4] [5].
  • Vulnerable household social protection: Where the passing leaves dependent children or vulnerable household members without income, families may inquire with the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs regarding federal social safety net and cash-transfer programmes (such as the national Baxnaano social protection programme) [4] [5].
  • Banks, remittance accounts, and mobile money: Present the Municipal Death Certificate, the NIRA identity record, and the court succession certificate to Somali commercial banks (such as Premier Bank, IBS Bank, Salaam Somali Bank, or Dahabshiil Bank) and mobile money operators (such as Hormuud EVC Plus) to freeze sole accounts and transfer balances to the verified estate representative [1] [2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession Before the District Court
steps.html:
• Governing succession law (Shari'ah and statutory courts): In Somalia, inheritance and estate succession are governed by Islamic Shari'ah principles (predominantly following the Shafi'i school of jurisprudence) applied by the statutory District Courts (Maxkamadda Degmada) [1]. Before any distribution to heirs, the estate must pay in strict priority: (1) reasonable burial expenses, (2) verified debts owed by the deceased, and (3) valid testamentary bequests (Wasiyyah), which under Shari'ah cannot exceed one-third (1/3) of the net estate and cannot be made in favour of a fixed legal heir without the consent of all other adult heirs after death [1].
  • Obtaining the Certificate of Legal Heirs and Estate Distribution: The family must petition the competent District Court with the Municipal Death Certificate, identity documents from the National Identification and Registration Authority, and two credible male witnesses to obtain an official Certificate of Heirship (Caddeynta Dhaxalka / Tarika) confirming the surviving legal heirs and their fixed mathematical shares (Fara'id) [1] [2].
  • Public notary and property transfers: Once the District Court issues the succession ruling, a licensed Somali Public Notary (Nootaayo) prepares the formal transfer deeds for real estate, business shares, and land titles, while guardians are appointed under judicial supervision for any minor heirs [1].
  • Cross-border diaspora heirs and foreign assets: Somali heirs living in the diaspora can execute a Power of Attorney (Wakaalad) before a notary and Somali embassy abroad (authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Mogadishu) authorising a local representative in Somalia to appear before the District Court and banks on their behalf [1].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Somalia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Somalia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Somalia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Somalia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking structured medical, legal, and administrative steps while your family member still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity (Ahliyyah) helps protect their wishes and avoids legal complications for the family. Below, we outline the five key steps in chronological order under the institutional and legal framework of Somalia.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital specialist and supportive care: Coordinate a comprehensive symptom-management and clinical care plan through a major public referral hospital overseen by the Ministry of Health and Human Services (such as Erdogan Referral Hospital, Medina Hospital, or Banadir Hospital in Mogadishu, or regional general hospitals across the Federal Member States) or an accredited private hospital [3]. Request a detailed written medical report in English and Somali summarizing the diagnosis, medication regimen, and supportive care needs [3].
  • Home-based nursing and pain management: Because dedicated standalone hospice facilities are limited in Somalia, supportive end-of-life care is primarily delivered at home with the support of outpatient hospital physicians, private home-nursing teams, and community health workers coordinated under the Ministry of Health and Human Services framework [3]. Ensure the treating physician establishes a clear home pain-management and emergency contact protocol [3].
  • Medical referrals and private health coverage: If your family member holds private medical or Takaful health coverage, or if the family is coordinating specialized treatment abroad, obtain official clinical referral documentation and fit-to-travel assessments from the treating consultant at the Ministry of Health and Human Services facility early [3].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Family Medical Spokesperson
steps.html:
• Documenting clinical care preferences: Somalia does not have a standalone statutory living-will act; instead, clinical decision-making is guided by medical ethics, patient consent, and Islamic bioethical principles applied in hospitals regulated by the Ministry of Health and Human Services [3]. While your family member possesses full mental capacity, they can record a clear written statement of their care preferences, including pain relief priorities, preferred location of care (home versus hospital), and wishes regarding invasive interventions when medical treatment is deemed clinically futile [3].
  • Designating a trusted medical representative (Wakiil): In Somali clinical practice, hospital physicians rely on the patient's adult next of kin (Walii) when the patient can no longer communicate [3]. To ensure clarity - particularly where immediate family members live in different cities or in the diaspora - your family member should sign a witnessed written authorization naming a primary local medical spokesperson and provide a copy to the hospital's lead physician [1] [3].
  • Medical certification of mental capacity: When signing healthcare authorizations, powers of attorney, or property documents during serious illness, ask the attending physician at the Ministry of Health and Human Services hospital or clinic to issue a dated medical certificate confirming that the patient is fully lucid, oriented, and of sound mind (Miyir qaba) at the time of execution [3].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney (*Wakaalad*) and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Executing a formal Wakaalad before a Somali Public Notary: Under Somali civil and Shari'ah agency law, a person with full mental and legal capacity may execute a formal Power of Attorney (Wakaalad Sharci ah) appointing a trusted agent (Wakiil) to manage financial affairs, collect rents or business income, pay medical expenses, and represent them before public authorities [1]. To be legally recognised across Somalia, the Wakaalad must be executed before a licensed Somali Public Notary (Nootaayo) in the presence of two adult witnesses, referencing the principal's and agent's identity cards issued by the National Identification and Registration Authority (or valid Somali passports) [1] [2].
  • Registering bank and mobile money mandates: Somali commercial banks (such as Premier Bank, IBS Bank, Salaam Somali Bank, and Dahabshiil Bank) and mobile money platforms (such as Hormuud EVC Plus) require strict identity and signatory verification [1] [2]. While your family member retains capacity, arrange for them to register their authorized representative directly with each bank (either in person or through a domiciliary notary and bank officer visit) so household and medical funds remain accessible [1] [2].
  • Protecting validity if capacity declines: Under Islamic jurisprudence and Somali civil practice, an ordinary agency mandate (Wakaalad) can be suspended or terminated if the principal completely loses mental capacity (Ahliyyah), requiring the local District Court (Maxkamadda Degmada) to appoint a judicial guardian (Walii) [1]. Completing direct bank signatory arrangements and notarised mandates while capacity is certified by a physician avoids urgent court guardianship petitions [1] [3].

steps.title: Activate Workplace Sick Leave, Disability Support, and Social Protection
steps.html:
• Labour law sick leave and workplace entitlements: If your family member is employed in the federal civil service or the formal private sector, review statutory sick leave, medical incapacity protections, and employment benefits regulated by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs in alignment with International Labour Organization labour standards [4] [5]. Provide the employer with official medical certificates from the Ministry of Health and Human Services facility to protect salary continuation or qualify for medical retirement benefits [3] [4].
  • Social protection for vulnerable households: While Somalia is still developing a comprehensive national contributory disability insurance scheme, the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs oversees national social protection policies and targeted safety-net cash transfer programmes (such as Baxnaano) for vulnerable households facing severe economic hardship or chronic incapacity [4] [5].
  • Caregiver leave and family coordination: Employed family caregivers in Somalia should request compassionate or family-care leave arrangements through their employer's human resources office, supported by hospital documentation confirming the patient's need for full-time care [3] [4].

steps.title: Organize the Will (*Wasiyyah*), Identity Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Rules governing a Somali Will (Wasiyyah): Estate succession in Somalia is governed by Islamic Shari'ah inheritance rules (Fara'id), which allocate fixed statutory shares to legal heirs (such as the spouse, children, and parents) [1]. While your family member has full capacity, they may execute a formal written Will (Dardaaran or Wasiyyah) before a Public Notary (Nootaayo) and two credible witnesses to: (1) record all outstanding personal debts, trusts (Amaano), and receivables owed to or by them, (2) appoint a trusted executor (Wasi) to administer the estate and care for minor children, and (3) make discretionary bequests of up to one-third (1/3) of the net estate to non-heirs or charitable causes (bequests to legal heirs or exceeding one-third require the post-facto consent of all adult heirs) [1].
  • Caution regarding dispositions during terminal illness (Marad al-Mawt): Under Shari'ah principles applied by Somali courts, gratuitous gifts (Hibah) or below-market property transfers made during a final mortal illness (Marad al-Mawt) are legally treated as testamentary bequests and are restricted to the one-third limit to protect the fixed rights of legal heirs [1].
  • Securing identity and property title records: Ensure your family member's biometric National ID Card with the National Identification and Registration Authority, passport, marriage certificates, and notarised land title deeds (Sabarloog / Waraaqaha Lahaanshaha Dhulka) are organized and stored safely [1] [2].
  • Cross-border diaspora coordination: Because Somalia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, any Power of Attorney executed by family members in the diaspora for use in Somalia must be notarised abroad and legalised through a Somali embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Mogadishu [1].
