title: What to Do When Someone Dies in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for South Sudan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in South Sudan. Below we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - covering medical certification, civil registration, funeral or international repatriation formalities, survivor pension and institutional notifications, and succession proceedings before the courts of South Sudan.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Police Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public teaching hospital (such as Juba Teaching Hospital), a state hospital, or a licensed clinic under the oversight of the Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization Country Office for South Sudan [4], the attending physician issues a signed Medical Notification and Certificate of Cause of Death recording the deceased's full name, age, nationality, date and hour of death, and clinical cause of death [4].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: If your family member died at home in an urban residential quarter or rural payam, the family must obtain a written confirmation letter from the local neighbourhood chief (Boma or Payam administrator) and present the deceased or clinical records at the nearest government hospital or primary health facility so a medical officer can verify the death and issue the medical notification [4] [5].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under the South Sudan Penal Code Act 2008 and Code of Criminal Procedure Act 2008, any unexpected, violent, or unattended death must be reported immediately to the South Sudan National Police Service before the body is moved [6]. A police investigator and public prosecutor open an inquest file and authorize a forensic post-mortem examination at a designated public hospital mortuary before issuing a police burial or release clearance [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: Civil registration of vital events is governed by the South Sudan Civil Registry Act 2018 and administered by the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration under the Ministry of Interior, alongside technical civil-documentation support from UNHCR South Sudan [5].
  • Statutory deadline and informant rules: Under the Civil Registry Act 2018, a death occurring in an urban area should be declared within 30 days of occurrence (with extended administrative windows permitted for remote rural counties or conflict-affected areas upon presentation of a local chief's attestation and hospital record) [5]. The declaration may be made by the surviving spouse, an adult relative, the household head, or an authorized legal representative.
  • Required documents and official certificates: The informant must present the hospital Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or police inquest release order), the deceased's South Sudan Nationality Certificate or National Identity Card and passport, and the informant's valid identity document [5]. Request multiple certified extracts of the official Death Certificate from the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration, as originals are required by banks, pension boards, and probate courts [5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial permits: Before interment in a municipal or community cemetery in Juba or a state capital, the family must present the medical death notification or civil registration receipt and police clearance (where applicable) to the municipal public health office and cemetery administration to obtain a formal burial permit [4] [6]. Cremation facilities are extremely limited in South Sudan, and families seeking cremation typically arrange cross-border transport to a neighbouring jurisdiction with licensed crematoria [6].
  • Mortuary preparation and international repatriation: If the deceased is to be repatriated abroad, the body must be embalmed at an approved hospital mortuary (such as Juba Teaching Hospital or a licensed international medical evacuation and funeral provider) [6]. You must obtain an official Embalming Certificate, a Ministry of Health Non-Contagious Disease and Public Health Transit Permit, a hermetically sealed coffin certificate inspected by health and customs officers at Juba International Airport, and an export permit [4] [6].
  • Consular legalization (non-Hague Apostille jurisdiction): South Sudan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consequently, South Sudanese death certificates, medical certificates, and court documents intended for use abroad must undergo chain authentication: verification by the issuing ministry, authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Juba, and final consular legalization by the foreign embassy or consulate (such as the U.S. Embassy in South Sudan or relevant diplomatic mission) [6].

steps.title: Notify Pension Funds, Employers, Banks, and Public Authorities
steps.html:
• Public service survivor benefits: If the deceased was a civil servant or public-sector employee, survivors must notify the South Sudan Pension Fund and the Ministry of Finance and Planning under the Civil Service Pensions Scheme Act 2013 (Act No. 31 of 2013) and the Pension Funds Act 2012 (Act No. 32 of 2012) [1] [2]. Eligible dependants (surviving spouse, minor children, or dependent parents) may claim the survivor pension or lump-sum death gratuity upon submitting the official Death Certificate, employment service record, marriage or birth certificates, and court succession orders [1] [2].
  • Private-sector terminal dues: Where the deceased was employed in the private or non-governmental sector under the Labour Act 2017 (Act No. 64 of 2017), the employer must calculate and disburse accrued wages, unused annual leave, and statutory severance or death-in-service benefits to the lawful heirs or court-appointed estate administrator [3].
  • Identity cancellation, tax, and banking closure: Surrender the deceased's passport and national identity card to the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration for cancellation [5]. Notify commercial banks in South Sudan and the National Revenue Authority to freeze sole accounts pending presentation of formal Letters of Administration [1].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Cross-Border Probate
steps.html:
• Court-supervised probate and Letters of Administration: In South Sudan, banks, land registries, and the South Sudan Pension Fund will not release estate assets or death gratuities without a formal court order [1] [2]. If your family member left a valid written will, the executor petitions the High Court of South Sudan (or competent County Judge) for a Grant of Probate; if the deceased died intestate, the family petitions the court for Letters of Administration [1] [5].
  • Interplay of statutory and customary succession law: Under the Transitional Constitution and judiciary rules, succession to registered urban land, bank accounts, and civil service pensions requires formal court administration, while family elders and customary courts often participate in verifying the schedule of lawful heirs (list of dependants) before the statutory judge issues final Letters of Administration [1] [5]. South Sudan does not levy a standalone national inheritance tax, though court filing fees and land-title transfer fees apply.
  • Foreign heirs and cross-border assets: Heirs residing outside South Sudan may appoint a local advocate or family representative in Juba through a written Power of Attorney notarized in their country of residence and legalized by a South Sudanese embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation [6]. Conversely, if South Sudanese court probate orders must be produced abroad, have them authenticated by the Judiciary, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the destination country's diplomatic mission [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in South Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for South Sudan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in South Sudan is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, taking early medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full decision-making capacity helps protect their care preferences and financial security. Below we outline the five essential steps to coordinate healthcare, treatment directives, legal representation, employment or invalidity benefits, and estate documentation in South Sudan.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Symptom Management, and Medical Coverage
steps.html:
• Public and specialist hospital referral: Tertiary clinical care and symptom management in South Sudan are centered at Juba Teaching Hospital and state referral hospitals operating under the Ministry of Health with technical support from the World Health Organization Country Office for South Sudan [4] and the WHO Regional Office for Africa [5]. Request a comprehensive written clinical summary, diagnostic report, and pain-management plan from the lead attending specialist [4] [5].
  • Home-based care and humanitarian health networks: Because dedicated inpatient hospice facilities are scarce in South Sudan, families managing complex chronic or life-limiting conditions outside hospital wards frequently coordinate outpatient analgesic prescribing, community nursing visits, and medical equipment through accredited faith-based hospitals, international medical NGOs, and primary healthcare clinics [4] [5].
  • Health insurance and medical evacuation planning: South Sudan does not yet operate a universal public health insurance fund for the general population. If your family member holds private international medical insurance or employer-sponsored coverage under the Labour Act 2017 [3], notify the insurer early to pre-authorize inpatient care, specialist medications, or cross-border medical referral to regional tertiary centres in Kenya or Uganda [3] [4].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Spokesperson
steps.html:
• Written statement of medical preferences: South Sudan does not have a standalone statute governing living wills or statutory advance healthcare directives. While your family member has full mental capacity, it is advisable to consider drafting a clear written Statement of Medical Treatment Preferences specifying their wishes regarding invasive life-sustaining interventions, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, pain relief, and preferred place of care (hospital versus home), signed before two independent witnesses and a legal advocate [4] [5].
  • Appointing a family medical representative: In clinical practice across South Sudanese hospitals, physicians consult the patient's designated next of kin or senior family spokesperson when the patient can no longer communicate [4]. Naming a specific primary and alternate healthcare representative in writing - and lodging a signed copy directly in the hospital medical file with the attending physician - reduces the risk of family disagreement during urgent clinical transitions [4] [5].
  • Physician attestation of capacity: Ask the treating doctor at the hospital or clinic to record a contemporaneous note in the clinical chart confirming that the ill person was fully oriented and had intact decision-making capacity on the date the care preferences and representative designation were signed [4].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Formal Power of Attorney while capacity is intact: Under South Sudanese contract and civil procedure principles, a Power of Attorney is valid only if executed while the principal understands the nature and effect of the authorization. Engage a licensed advocate and Commissioner for Oaths (or High Court notary in Juba) to draft a comprehensive Special or General Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage real property, sign administrative filings, and deal with government ministries [1] [6].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates: Commercial banks operating in South Sudan generally require account holders to sign the bank's own internal third-party mandate or signatory resolution forms in person (or via a verified bedside bank visit) rather than relying solely on a general legal Power of Attorney. Arrange this directly with the branch manager while your family member is able to sign and present their valid National Identity Card or passport [6].
  • Safeguarding against incapacity: Because an ordinary agency mandate can be challenged if the principal subsequently loses mental capacity, ask the advocate to document medical proof of capacity alongside the notarized deed and register any property-related mandate with the High Court land and deeds registry [1] [6].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Pensions, Sick Leave, and Workplace Protections
steps.html:
• Public-sector invalidity and medical retirement benefits: If the ill person is a civil servant or public employee, review their entitlements under the Civil Service Pensions Scheme Act 2013 (Act No. 31 of 2013) administered alongside the Ministry of Finance and Planning [1] and the Pension Funds Act 2012 (Act No. 32 of 2012) [2]. A contributor who becomes permanently incapable of discharging public service duties due to severe physical or mental infirmity certified by an official Medical Board is eligible to apply for an invalidity pension or medical retirement gratuity [1] [2].
  • Paid sick leave and employment protections in the private sector: Under the Labour Act 2017 (Act No. 64 of 2017), employees in the formal private and NGO sectors are entitled to statutory paid sick leave upon presenting a certificate from a registered medical practitioner [3]. The Labour Act 2017 also regulates termination on grounds of certified medical incapacity and requires full settlement of accrued wages, leave pay, and severance entitlements [3].
  • Caregiver leave arrangements: Employees caring for a seriously ill family member may request compassionate leave, paid annual leave, or flexible working arrangements from their employer in accordance with the Labour Act 2017 and internal human-resources policies [3].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Beneficiary Nominations, Civil Records, and Cross-Border Documents
steps.html:
• Verify foundational civil identity documents: Ensure the ill person and all dependants hold valid South Sudan Nationality Certificates, National Identity Cards, birth certificates, and marriage records issued or verified through the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration, with guidance available via UNHCR South Sudan [6]. Correcting spelling discrepancies now prevents severe delays later before pension boards and courts [1] [6].
  • Update pension and employer beneficiary nominations: Under the Civil Service Pensions Scheme Act 2013 and the Pension Funds Act 2012, verify that the employee's official record of dependants and nominated beneficiaries on file with their employing ministry and the South Sudan Pension Fund is current and signed [1] [2].
  • Drafting a valid written will and cross-border legalization: Work with a licensed South Sudanese advocate to execute a written will witnessed by at least two independent adults who are not beneficiaries, clearly inventorying urban land leases, bank accounts, and personal property [1] [6]. Because South Sudan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, any foreign Power of Attorney or civil record from abroad must be legalized by the relevant South Sudanese embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Juba to be recognized locally [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Sudan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Sudan. Below we set out the five official medical, civil registration, funeral or repatriation, social insurance, and estate succession steps in chronological order under Sudanese law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Police Forensic Clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public teaching hospital, state hospital, or licensed private clinic operating under the Federal Ministry of Health and supported by the World Health Organization Country Office for Sudan [3] [4], the attending physician examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Notification of Death (Ikhbar Wafah) and Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [2] [3].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home in an urban quarter or rural locality, obtain an administrative attestation from the local Popular Committee (Lajna Sha'biya) or locality administrator confirming the identity and residence of the deceased, and bring a government medical officer from the nearest public health centre to verify natural causes and issue the medical death notification [2] [5].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under Sudan's Criminal Procedure Act 1991, any sudden, unnatural, violent, or unattended death must be reported immediately to the Sudan Police Force before the body is moved [6]. The police open an investigation file, refer the body to a forensic mortuary (Mashraha) for a medico-legal autopsy ordered by the Public Prosecution, and issue a formal police burial and release permit once forensic clearance is complete [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Sudanese Civil Registry Act 2011, all deaths occurring in Sudan must be registered with the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan (under the Ministry of Interior) [2] [5]. Statutory rules require reporting a death within 15 days of occurrence at the local civil registry office (with administrative late-registration procedures available through a locality committee or court attestation where conflict or displacement delayed filing) [2] [5].
  • Required documents for registration: An adult surviving relative, spouse, or authorized representative must present: (a) the hospital Medical Notification of Death or police prosecutor clearance, (b) the deceased's Sudanese National Number (Al-Raqam Al-Watani) or National Identity Card and passport, and (c) the informant's valid National Identity Card and two witnesses where required for community deaths [2] [5].
  • Obtaining official Death Certificates: Upon registration, the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan records the death against the deceased's National Number in the central civil register and issues the official Death Certificate (Shahadat Wafah) [2]. It is advisable to request several certified copies immediately, as courts, pension funds, and commercial banks require original stamped certificates [2] [5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial procedures: Present the Medical Notification of Death or civil registration certificate (and police release order, if applicable) to the municipal public health office and cemetery administration to obtain a local burial permit [3] [6]. In accordance with local custom and public health practice in Sudan, interment typically takes place within 24 hours of death [6]. Dedicated cremation facilities are generally unavailable in Sudan, and families seeking cremation usually arrange international transport of remains [6].
  • Mortuary preparation and international repatriation: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be repatriated abroad, the body must be prepared and embalmed at an authorized hospital mortuary [6]. The funeral representative must obtain: (a) an official Death Certificate from the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan [2], (b) an Embalming Certificate and a Non-Contagious Disease and Public Health Transit Permit from the Federal Ministry of Health [3] [4], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate inspected by port health and customs officials (such as at Port Sudan New International Airport or Khartoum), and (d) a consular mortuary transit permit from the destination country's diplomatic mission [6].
  • Consular legalization (non-Hague Apostille jurisdiction): Sudan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Any Sudanese Death Certificate, medical record, or court succession decree intended for use abroad must be authenticated first by the issuing authority, then legalized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of the Sudan, and finally legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Insurance, Pension Funds, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Private-sector survivor pension and death benefits: If the deceased was employed in the formal private sector or state-owned enterprises, notify the National Social Insurance Fund under the Social Insurance Act 1990 (as amended in 2016) [1]. When an insured contributor dies (having met the qualifying contribution months or dying as a result of work injury), eligible survivors - including the widow or widower, dependent sons under age 18 (or up to age 26 if full-time students, or without age limit if permanently disabled), unmarried daughters, and dependent parents - are entitled to a monthly survivor pension calculated as a statutory percentage of the deceased's insured earnings, split according to the statutory Sharia inheritance schedule [1].
  • Public-sector civil service pensions: If your family member was a federal or state civil servant, public teacher, or government pensioner, notify the National Pensions and Social Insurance Fund (Public Sector Pensions Administration) to claim the public-service survivor pension and any accrued terminal gratuity [1].
  • Identity cancellation, tax, and banking closure: Surrender the deceased's passport and National Identity Card to the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan for cancellation [2], notify the Sudan Taxation Chamber regarding any sole-proprietorship or property tax accounts, and present the Death Certificate to Sudanese commercial banks so sole accounts are frozen pending a court succession order [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession Decree, and Cross-Border Probate
steps.html:
• Personal Status Court succession decree (Ishhad Shar'i): In Sudan, no commercial bank, land registry (Tasjeelat Al-Aradi), or pension authority will distribute estate assets without an official judicial succession decree [1] [5]. For Muslim estates, the family petitions the Personal Status Court (Mahkamat Al-Ahwal Al-Shakhsiya) under the Muslim Personal Status Act 1991 for a Sharia Inheritance Certificate (Ilm الوراثة / Ishhad Shar'i); for non-Muslim estates, heirs petition the Civil Court (Non-Muslim Personal Status circuit) or apply the Non-Muslims Estates Administration Act [5] [6].
  • Probate steps and estate distribution: All adult heirs (or their legal representatives) appear before the judge with two credible witnesses who know the family, the official Death Certificate from the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan [2], and family civil identity records referenced by UNHCR Sudan [5]. The judge verifies the lawful heirs, records any valid bequest (Wasiya, which under Sharia rules is capped at one-third of the net estate after funeral expenses and debts unless all adult heirs consent), and issues the formal estate inventory and distribution order (Harصر Al-Tarika) [5]. Sudan does not levy a separate national inheritance tax, though statutory court fees and land-registration transfer fees apply.
  • Foreign heirs and cross-border assets: An heir living outside Sudan may appoint a licensed Sudanese advocate or relative through a Special Power of Attorney (Tawkil Khas) notarized abroad and legalized by a Sudanese embassy and the Sudanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs [6].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical Death CertificateImmediately upon deathAttending Hospital Physician / Federal Ministry of Health / Police Forensic Mortuary
2. Civil Death RegistrationWithin 15 days of deathCivil Registry Authority of Sudan (Ministry of Interior)
3. Burial or Repatriation PermitWithin 24 hours (burial) or prior to air transitMunicipal Public Health Office / Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Foreign Embassy
4. Survivor Pension NotificationPromptly after obtaining Death CertificateNational Social Insurance Fund / Public Sector Pensions Administration
5. Judicial Succession DecreeBefore releasing bank accounts or land titlesPersonal Status Court (Mahkamat Al-Ahwal Al-Shakhsiya) or Civil Probate Court

ar.title: ماذا تفعل عند وفاة أحد الأقارب في السودان: الدليل الرسمي في 5 خطوات
ar.cardSummary: دليل رسمي من 5 خطوات بعد الوفاة في السودان: التبليغ الطبي عن الوفاة وتصريح الدفن، ترتيبات الجنازة، تسجيل الوفاة في الأحوال المدنية، مستحقات التقاعد والضمان الاجتماعي، وحصر الإرث والبنوك.
ar.introHtml: نتقدم إليكم بخالص التعازي والمواساة في وفاة أحد أفراد أسرتكم في السودان. نوضح فيما يلي الخطوات الرسمية الخمس المتعلقة بالتوثيق الطبي، وتسجيل الوفاة في السجل المدني، وإجراءات الدفن أو نقل الجثمان دولياً، والتأمين الاجتماعي، وحصر الإرث وتصفية التركة وفق الترتيب الزمني المنصوص عليه في القوانين السودانية.

steps.title: استخراج الإخطار الطبي بالوفاة أو تصريح الأدلة الجنائية والشرطة
steps.html:
• الوفيات داخل المستشفيات أو المرافق الطبية: عند وقوع الوفاة في مستشفى تعليمي حكومي أو مستشفى ولائي أو عيادة خاصة مرخصة تعمل تحت إشراف وزارة الصحة الاتحادية وبدعم من المكتب القطري لمنظمة الصحة العالمية في السودان [3] [4]، يقوم الطبيب المعالج بفحص المتوفى وإصدار الإخطار الطبي الرسمي بالوفاة (إخبار وفاة) والشهادة الطبية لسبب الوفاة [2] [3].
  • الوفيات في المنزل لأسباب طبيعية: إذا توفي أحد أفراد أسرتكم في المنزل داخل حي حضري أو محلية ريفية، يجب الحصول على إفادة إدارية من اللجنة الشعبية المحلية أو إدارة المحلية تؤكد هوية المتوفى ومحل إقامته، مع استدعاء ضابط طبي حكومي من أقرب مركز صحي عام للتحقق من أن الوفاة طبيعية وإصدار الإخطار الطبي بالوفاة [2] [5].
  • الوفيات المفاجئة أو العرضية أو غير المبررة: بموجب قانون الإجراءات الجنائية السوداني لعام 1991، يجب إبلاغ قوات الشرطة السودانية فوراً عن أي وفاة مفاجئة أو غير طبيعية أو ناتجة عن عنف أو حادث قبل تحريك الجثمان [6]. وتفتح الشرطة بلاغ تحقيق، وتحيل الجثمان إلى المشرحة لإجراء التشريح الطبي الشرعي بأمر من النيابة العامة، ثم تصدر تصريحاً رسمياً بالدفن وتسليم الجثمان فور استكمال الإجراءات الجنائية [6].

steps.title: تسجيل الوفاة لدى هيئة السجل المدني السودانية
steps.html:
• الجهة المختصة والمهلة القانونية: بموجب قانون السجل المدني السوداني لعام 2011، يجب تسجيل جميع الوفيات التي تقع في السودان لدى هيئة السجل المدني السودانية التابعة لوزارة الداخلية [2] [5]. وتلزم القواعد القانونية بالإبلاغ عن الوفاة خلال 15 يوماً من تاريخ وقوعها لدى مكتب السجل المدني المحلي (مع إتاحة إجراءات التسجيل المتأخر إدارياً عبر إفادة لجنة المحلية أو إشهاد المحكمة في الحالات التي يتأخر فيها الإبلاغ بسبب النزاعات أو النزوح) [2] [5].
  • المستندات المطلوبة للتسجيل: يتعين على أحد الأقارب البالغين أو الزوج أو الممثل المفوض تقديم: (أ) الإخطار الطبي بالوفاة الصادر من المستشفى أو تصريح النيابة والشرطة، (ب) شهادة الرقم الوطني السوداني للمتوفى أو البطاقة القومية وجواز السفر، و(ج) البطاقة القومية السارية للمُبلِّغ وشاهدين عند الاقتضاء في حالات الوفيات المجتمعية [2] [5].
  • استخراج شهادات الوفاة الرسمية: عقب التسجيل، تقوم هيئة السجل المدني السودانية بتقييد واقعة الوفاة مقابل الرقم الوطني للمتوفى في السجل المدني المركزي وإصدار شهادة الوفاة الرسمية [2]. ويُنصح بطلب عدة نسخ مصدقة على الفور، نظراً لأن المحاكم وصناديق المعاشات والمصارف التجارية تشترط تقديم نسخ أصلية مختومة [2] [5].

steps.title: ترتيب إجراءات الدفن أو الحرق أو نقل الجثمان دولياً
steps.html:
• إجراءات الدفن المحلي: يُقدَّم الإخطار الطبي بالوفاة أو شهادة التسجيل المدني (إلى جانب أمر تسليم الجثمان الصادر من الشرطة عند الاقتضاء) إلى مكتب الصحة العامة بالمحلية وإدارة المقابر لاستخراج تصريح الدفن المحلي [3] [6]. ووفقاً للأعراف المحلية والممارسات الصحية في السودان، يتم الدفن عادةً خلال 24 ساعة من الوفاة [6]. ولا تتوفر بصفة عامة مرافق مخصصة لحرق الجثامين في السودان، ولذلك تلجأ الأسر الراغبة في ذلك عادةً إلى ترتيب نقل الجثمان إلى الخارج [6].
  • تجهيز الجثمان ونقله دولياً إلى الخارج: إذا كان المتوفى مواطناً أجنبياً أو إذا لزم نقل الجثمان إلى خارج البلاد، فيجب تجهيز الجثمان وتحنيطه في مشرحة مستشفى معتمدة [6]. ويتعين على ممثل الأسرة استخراج المستندات التالية: (أ) شهادة وفاة رسمية من هيئة السجل المدني السودانية [2]، و(ب) شهادة تحنيط وشهادة خلو من الأمراض المعدية وتصريح نقل صحي من وزارة الصحة الاتحادية بالتنسيق مع المعايير التي يدعمها المكتب القطري لمنظمة الصحة العالمية في السودان [3] [4]، و(ج) شهادة إغلاق وختم التابوت بعد فحصها من قبل سلطات الحجر الصحي والجمارك بالمنافذ (مثل مطار بورتسودان الدولي الجديد أو الخرطوم)، و(د) تصريح مرور قنصلي للجثمان من البعثة الدبلوماسية لدولة المقصد [6].
  • التصديق القنصلي (دولة غير منضمة لاتفاقية لاهاي للأبوستيل): السودان ليس طرفاً في اتفاقية لاهاي للأبوستيل لعام 1961. ولذلك يجب أولاً توثيق أي شهادة وفاة سودانية أو تقرير طبي أو إعلام وراثة قضائي يُراد استخدامه في الخارج من الجهة المصدرة له، ثم تصديقه من وزارة الخارجية في جمهورية السودان، وأخيراً تصديقه من سفارة أو قنصلية دولة المقصد [6].

steps.title: إخطار التأمين الاجتماعي وصناديق المعاشات والضرائب والمصارف
steps.html:
• معاشات الورثة ومزايا الوفاة في القطاع الخاص: إذا كان المتوفى يعمل في القطاع الخاص الرسمي أو الشركات المملوكة للدولة، فيجب إخطار الصندوق القومي للتأمين الاجتماعي بموجب قانون التأمين الاجتماعي لعام 1990 (وتعديلاته لعام 2016) [1]. وعند وفاة المؤمن عليه (بعد استيفاء أشهر الاشتراك المؤهلة أو نتيجة إصابة عمل)، يستحق الورثة المؤهلون - وهم الأرملة أو الأرمل، والأبناء المعالون دون سن 18 عاماً (أو حتى سن 26 عاماً للطلاب المتفرغين للدراسة، أو دون حد عمري في حال العجز الدائم)، والبنات غير المتزوجات، والوالدان المعالان - معاشاً شهرياً للورثة يُحتسب بنسبة قانونية من أجر المتوفى الخاضع للتأمين ويُوزع وفق جدول الأنصبة الشرعية المعتمد لدى الصندوق القومي للتأمين الاجتماعي [1].
  • معاشات الخدمة المدنية في القطاع العام: إذا كان المتوفى موظفاً في الخدمة المدنية الاتحادية أو الولائية أو معلماً حكومياً أو صاحب معاش حكومي، فيجب إخطار الصندوق القومي للمعاشات والتأمينات الاجتماعية (إدارة معاشات القطاع العام) للمطالبة بمعاش الورثة وأي مكافأة نهاية خدمة مستحقة [1].
  • إلغاء وثائق الهوية وإخطار الضرائب والمصارف: يجب تسليم جواز سفر المتوفى وبطاقته القومية إلى هيئة السجل المدني السودانية لإلغائهما [2]، وإخطار ديوان الضرائب السوداني بشأن أي حسابات ضريبية لمؤسسات فردية أو عقارات، وتقديم شهادة الوفاة إلى المصارف التجارية السودانية لتجميد الحسابات الفردية لحين صدور إعلام الوراثة القضائي [5].

steps.title: إدارة التركة وإصدار الإشهاد الشرعي للوراثة والإجراءات العابرة للحدود
steps.html:
• الإشهاد الشرعي للوراثة أمام محكمة الأحوال الشخصية: في السودان، لا تقوم أي مصارف تجارية أو مكاتب تسجيلات الأراضي أو هيئات المعاشات بصرف أموال التركة أو نقل ملكيتها دون حكم قضائي رسمي بحصر الورثة [1] [5]. وبالنسبة لتركات المسلمين، تتقدم الأسرة بطلب إلى محكمة الأحوال الشخصية بموجب قانون الأحوال الشخصية للمسلمين لعام 1991 لاستخراج إشهاد شرعي بالوراثة (إعلام الوراثة)؛ أما بالنسبة لتركات غير المسلمين، فيتقدم الورثة إلى المحكمة المدنية (دائرة الأحوال الشخصية لغير المسلمين) أو تطبق أحكام قانون إدارة تركات غير المسلمين [5] [6].
  • إجراءات حصر التركة وتوزيعها: يمثل جميع الورثة البالغين (أو وكلاؤهم القانونيون) أمام القاضي برفقة شاهدين عدلين يعرفون الأسرة، مع تقديم شهادة الوفاة الرسمية الصادرة عن هيئة السجل المدني السودانية [2]، ومستندات الحالة المدنية للأسرة المشار إليها في إرشادات المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين في السودان [5]. ويتحقق القاضي من الورثة الشرعيين، ويثبت أي وصية صحيحة (وهي محدودة شرعاً بثلث صافي التركة بعد سداد نفقات التجهيز والديون ما لم يجزها جميع الورثة البالغين)، ثم يصدر أمر حصر التركة وتوزيعها [5]. ولا يفرض السودان ضريبة وطنية مستقلة على الميراث، وإنما تُطبق الرسوم القضائية القانونية ورسوم نقل الملكية لدى تسجيلات الأراضي.
  • الورثة المقيمون في الخارج والأصول العابرة للحدود: يجوز للوارث المقيم خارج السودان توكيل محامٍ سوداني مرخص أو أحد الأقارب بموجب توكيل خاص يتم توثيقه لدى كاتب العدل في الخارج وتصديقه من السفارة السودانية ووزارة الخارجية السودانية [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sudan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Sudan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Sudan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their care preferences and secures family entitlements. Below we set out the five main steps to coordinate clinical care, treatment directives, legal powers of attorney, disability benefits, and estate planning in Sudan.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Symptom Relief, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist oncology and palliative care services: Tertiary symptom management, pain control, and supportive care in Sudan are coordinated through federal and state teaching hospitals and specialized oncology centres operating under the Federal Ministry of Health, supported by the World Health Organization Country Office for Sudan [3] and the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean [4]. Ask the attending specialist for a complete written medical report, diagnostic summary, and outpatient analgesic regimen [3] [4].
  • Public health coverage under the National Health Insurance Fund: If the ill person is insured under Sudan's National Health Insurance Fund (administered alongside the social protection framework) or holds private medical coverage, submit the specialist medical report to verify coverage for hospital admissions, essential palliative medications, and home-based nursing supplies [1] [3].
  • Home care and humanitarian health continuity: Where inpatient beds or specialist clinics are disrupted, coordinate community nursing, pain medication refills, and medical referrals through state hospital outpatient clinics and international medical partners supported by the World Health Organization Country Office for Sudan [3] [4].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Family Healthcare Spokesperson
steps.html:
• Written statement of medical care preferences: Sudanese law does not provide a standalone statutory living-will registry. While your family member retains full mental capacity, it is advisable to prepare a clear written Statement of Medical Care Preferences setting out their wishes regarding invasive life-prolonging interventions, intensive-care admission, pain management, and preferred place of care (home versus hospital), signed in the presence of two adult witnesses [3] [4].
  • Designating a medical spokesperson (Wali or authorized family representative): In Sudanese hospital practice, attending physicians consult the patient's nearest adult family guardian or designated representative when the patient can no longer communicate [3] [4]. Naming a primary and alternate family medical spokesperson in writing and placing a signed copy in the hospital clinical file helps guide clinicians and avoid family uncertainty during urgent medical decisions [3].
  • Medical attestation of capacity: Request that the treating physician record a dated clinical entry in the hospital file confirming that the ill person had intact mental capacity when signing their care preferences and representative designation [3].

steps.title: Execute Valid Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Authenticated Power of Attorney (Tawkil Rasmi): Under Sudan's Civil Transactions Act 1984, a Power of Attorney must be executed while the principal holds full legal and mental capacity (Ahliya Kamila). Engage a licensed Sudanese advocate and Commissioner for Oaths (Muwathiq) to draft and authenticate a Special or General Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage real estate, deal with government authorities, and handle financial affairs [5] [6].
  • Commercial bank account mandates: Sudanese commercial banks frequently require account holders to sign the bank's own internal signatory mandate or verify a specific banking Power of Attorney before the branch compliance officer while presenting a valid National Identity Card or Sudanese National Number (Al-Raqam Al-Watani) [2] [6]. Complete this directly with the bank while your family member is able to appear or receive an authorized bank officer visit [6].
  • Protecting property and administrative continuity: Because an ordinary agency mandate in Sudan terminates or may be contested if the principal later loses mental capacity, ensure the advocate attaches a contemporary medical certificate of mental capacity to the authenticated Power of Attorney and registers any real-property mandate with the Land Registration Office (Tasjeelat Al-Aradi) [5] [6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Medical Board Evaluations, and Workplace Leave
steps.html:
• Permanent disability pension under the National Social Insurance Fund: Under Sudan's Social Insurance Act 1990 (as amended in 2016), an insured private-sector worker who is assessed by the official Medical Board as having a permanent total or partial incapacity for work before reaching normal retirement age is entitled to claim a monthly disability pension from the National Social Insurance Fund [1]. The claim requires the employer's contribution record, National Number certificate, and the official Medical Board certificate confirming permanent incapacity [1].
  • Public-sector medical retirement and sick leave: Civil servants and public-sector employees diagnosed with a severe or life-limiting illness may apply for statutory paid sick leave and, if certified permanently unfit for service by the General Medical Commission (Al-Qumisyun Al-Tibbi), medical retirement pension and gratuity through the Public Sector Pensions Administration [1] [6].
  • Caregiver leave arrangements: Family members employed in Sudan may request compassionate leave, paid annual leave, or unpaid family-care leave from their employer upon presenting the hospital specialist's medical certificate confirming the patient's dependency and care needs [1] [3].

steps.title: Organize Wills (*Wasiya*), Civil Status Records, and Cross-Border Documentation
steps.html:
• Verify civil identity and family records: Confirm that the ill person and all dependants hold accurate National Number certificates (Al-Raqam Al-Watani), National Identity Cards, marriage certificates (Qasimat Zawaj), and birth certificates issued by the Civil Registry Authority of Sudan [2], with documentation guidance also accessible through UNHCR Sudan [5]. Resolving any spelling or date discrepancies while the person is alive avoids later delays before courts and pension offices [2] [5].
  • Drafting a valid bequest (Wasiya) and asset inventory: Under the Muslim Personal Status Act 1991, a testator may execute a written bequest (Wasiya) disposing of up to one-third of the net estate (after debts and expenses) without requiring heirs' consent, while the remaining two-thirds passes according to statutory inheritance shares; non-Muslim citizens may execute a written will governed by the Non-Muslims Estates Administration rules before a licensed advocate or civil court notary [5] [6].
  • Cross-border legalization: Because Sudan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, any Power of Attorney, medical report, or civil status record executed abroad for use in Sudan (or executed in Sudan for use abroad) must be legalized through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant diplomatic mission [5] [6].

ar.title: المرض العضال والإجراءات القانونية والطبية في السودان: الدليل الرسمي في 5 خطوات
ar.cardSummary: دليل رسمي من 5 خطوات للتخطيط الطبي والقانوني في حالات المرض المتقدم في السودان: الرعاية التلطيفية والمنزلية، القرارات الطبية وتعيين المفوض الصحي، الوكالات الرسمية، إجازات المرافق وتنظيم الوصية.
ar.introHtml: عند تشخيص إصابة أحد أفراد الأسرة في السودان بمرض متقدم أو مهدد للحياة أو عضال، فإن استكمال الإجراءات الطبية والقانونية والمالية الأساسية بينما لا يزال المريض متمتعاً بكامل أهليته العقلية والقانونية لاتخاذ القرار يحمي رغباته العلاجية ويصون حقوق الأسرة. نوضح فيما يلي الخطوات الخمس الرئيسية لتنسيق الرعاية التلطيفية، والتوجيهات الطبية المسبقة، والتوكيلات القانونية، ومعاشات العجز، وتنظيم الوصية والوثائق في السودان.

steps.title: تنسيق الرعاية التلطيفية وتخفيف الأعراض والتغطية التأمينية الصحية
steps.html:
• خدمات الأورام المتخصصة والرعاية التلطيفية: يتم تنسيق علاج الأعراض المتقدمة والسيطرة على الألم والرعاية الداعمة في السودان من خلال المستشفيات التعليمية الاتحادية والولائية ومراكز الأورام المتخصصة العاملة تحت إشراف وزارة الصحة الاتحادية، بدعم من المكتب القطري لمنظمة الصحة العالمية في السودان [3] والمكتب الإقليمي لشرق المتوسط التابع لمنظمة الصحة العالمية [4]. يُنصح بطلب تقرير طبي مفصل ومكتوب من الطبيب الأخصائي المعالج يتضمن ملخص التشخيص وخطة صرف المسكنات للعيادات الخارجية [3] [4].
  • التغطية الصحية العامة عبر الصندوق القومي للتأمين الصحي: إذا كان المريض مؤمناً عليه لدى الصندوق القومي للتأمين الصحي في السودان (الذي يُدار ضمن منظومة الحماية الاجتماعية) أو لديه تأمين طبي خاص، فيجب تقديم التقرير الطبي التخصصي للتحقق من تغطية التنويم بالمستشفيات والأدوية التلطيفية الأساسية ومستلزمات التمريض المنزلي [1] [3].
  • الرعاية المنزلية واستمرارية الخدمات الصحية الإنسانية: في الحالات التي تتأثر فيها أقسام التنويم أو العيادات التخصصية، يمكن تنسيق خدمات التمريض المجتمعي وتجديد وصفات أدوية تسكين الألم والتحويلات الطبية عبر العيادات الخارجية بالمستشفيات الولائية والشركاء الطبيين الدوليين المدعومين من المكتب القطري لمنظمة الصحة العالمية في السودان [3] [4].

steps.title: توثيق الرغبات الطبية المسبقة وتعيين متحدث طبي باسم الأسرة
steps.html:
• بيان مكتوب بتفضيلات الرعاية الطبية: لا يتضمن القانون السوداني سجلاً قانونياً مستقلاً لوصايا الحياة الطبية. ولذلك، بينما لا يزال فرد أسرتكم متمتعاً بكامل أهليته العقلية، يُنصح بإعداد بيان مكتوب وواضح بتفضيلات الرعاية الطبية يحدد رغباته بشأن التدخلات الطبية الغازية لإطالة الحياة، والدخول إلى العناية المركزة، وتسكين الألم، ومكان الرعاية المفضل (المنزل أو المستشفى)، وتوقيعه بحضور شاهدين بالغين [3] [4].
  • تعيين متحدث طبي أو ولي مفوض عن الأسرة: في الممارسة الطبية بالمستشفيات السودانية، يتشاور الأطباء المعالجون مع أقرب ولي بالغ للمريض من أفراد الأسرة أو ممثله المعين عندما يفقد المريض القدرة على التواصل [3] [4]. ويساعد تعيين متحدث طبي أساسي وآخر بديل من الأسرة كتابياً وإيداع نسخة موقعة في الملف السريري بالمستشفى على إرشاد الأطباء وتجنب الخلاف أو التردد الأسري أثناء القرارات الطبية العاجلة [3].
  • الإشهاد الطبي على كمال الأهلية: يُستحسن الطلب من الطبيب المعالج تدوين ملاحظة سريرية مؤرخة في ملف المستشفى تؤكد تمتع المريض بكامل الإدراك والأهلية العقلية وقت توقيع تفضيلات الرعاية وتعيين الممثل الطبي [3].

steps.title: إبرام التوكيلات المالية والقانونية الرسمية والتفويضات المصرفية
steps.html:
• التوكيل الرسمي الموثق: بموجب قانون المعاملات المدنية السوداني لعام 1984، يجب إبرام التوكيل القانوني بينما يتمتع الموكل بالأهلية القانونية والعقلية الكاملة (الأهلية الكاملة). ويُنصح بالاستعانة بمحامٍ سوداني مرخص وموثق معتمد (أمين وثائق) لصياغة وتوثيق توكيل خاص أو عام يفوض ممثلاً موثوقاً بإدارة العقارات، ومراجعة الجهات الحكومية، وتسيير الشؤون المالية [5] [6].
  • تفويضات الحسابات لدى المصارف التجارية: تشترط المصارف التجارية السودانية غالباً حضور صاحب الحساب لتوقيع نموذج التفويض الداخلي المعتمد لدى المصرف أو التحقق من توكيل مصرفي خاص أمام موظف الالتزام بالفرع مع إبراز البطاقة القومية السارية أو شهادة الرقم الوطني السوداني الصادرة عن هيئة السجل المدني السودانية [2] [6]. وينبغي استكمال هذا الإجراء مباشرة مع المصرف بينما لا يزال المريض قادراً على الحضور أو استقبال زيارة رسمية من موظف المصرف المفوض [6].
  • حماية الممتلكات واستمرارية الإدارة: نظراً لأن الوكالة العادية في السودان قد تنقضي أو يُطعن فيها إذا فقد الموكل أهليته العقلية لاحقاً، يجب التأكد من إرفاق شهادة طبية حديثة تثبت كمال الأهلية العقلية بالتوكيل الرسمي الموثق، وتسجيل أي وكالة تتعلق بالعقارات لدى مكتب تسجيلات الأراضي [5] [6].

steps.title: تفعيل معاشات العجز وتقييمات القومسيون الطبي وإجازات الرعاية
steps.html:
• معاش العجز الدائم لدى الصندوق القومي للتأمين الاجتماعي: بموجب قانون التأمين الاجتماعي السوداني لعام 1990 (المعدل في عام 2016)، يحق للعامل المؤمن عليه في القطاع الخاص الذي يثبت القومسيون الطبي الرسمي إصابته بعجز كلي أو جزئي مستديم عن العمل قبل بلوغ سن التقاعد القانونية المطالبة بمعاش عجز شهري من الصندوق القومي للتأمين الاجتماعي [1]. ويتطلب الطلب تقديم سجل اشتراكات صاحب العمل، وشهادة الرقم الوطني، وشهادة القومسيون الطبي الرسمية التي تثبت العجز المستديم [1].
  • التقاعد الطبي والإجازات المرضية في القطاع العام: يحق لموظفي الخدمة المدنية والعاملين في القطاع العام المصابين بمرض شديد أو مهدد للحياة التقدم بطلب للحصول على إجازة مرضية مدفوعة الأجر قانوناً، وفي حال ثبوت عدم لياقتهم الطبية للخدمة بصفة دائمة بقرار من القومسيون الطبي العام، يحق لهم المطالبة بمعاش التقاعد الطبي ومكافأة نهاية الخدمة عبر إدارة معاشات القطاع العام [1] [6].
  • ترتيبات إجازة مرافق المريض: يمكن لأفراد الأسرة العاملين في السودان طلب إجازة مرافقة مريض أو إجازة سنوية مدفوعة الأجر أو إجازة رعاية أسرية غير مدفوعة الأجر من جهة العمل بعد تقديم شهادة طبية من الأخصائي بالمستشفى تؤكد حاجة المريض إلى الرعاية والمرافقة [1] [3].

steps.title: تنظيم الوصية الشرعية وسجلات الحالة المدنية والوثائق العابرة للحدود
steps.html:
• مراجعة وثائق الهوية المدنية وسجلات الأسرة: يجب التحقق من حيازة المريض وجميع المعالين لشهادات الرقم الوطني الصحيحة، والبطاقات القومية، وقسائم الزواج، وشهادات الميلاد الصادرة عن هيئة السجل المدني السودانية [2]، مع الاستفادة من إرشادات التوثيق المتاحة عبر المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين في السودان [5]. إن تصحيح أي أخطاء إملائية أو فروق في التواريخ أثناء حياة الشخص يجنب الأسرة تأخيرات طويلة لاحقاً أمام المحاكم ومكاتب المعاشات [2] [5].
  • صياغة الوصية الشرعية وجرد الأصول: بموجب قانون الأحوال الشخصية للمسلمين لعام 1991، يجوز للموصي تحرير وصية مكتوبة في حدود ثلث صافي التركة (بعد سداد الديون والنفقات) دون توقف على إجازة الورثة، بينما يوزع الثلثان الباقيان وفق الأنصبة الشرعية للميراث؛ أما المواطنون غير المسلمين فيجوز لهم تحرير وصية مكتوبة تخضع لقواعد إدارة تركات غير المسلمين أمام محامٍ مرخص أو موثق بالمحكمة المدنية [5] [6].
  • التصديق العابر للحدود: نظراً لأن السودان ليس طرفاً في اتفاقية لاهاي للأبوستيل لعام 1961، فإن أي توكيل رسمي أو تقرير طبي أو مستند حالة مدنية يتم تحريره في الخارج لاستخدامه في السودان (أو تحريره في السودان لاستخدامه في الخارج) يجب تصديقه عبر وزارة الخارجية والبعثة الدبلوماسية المعنية [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tanzania: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Tanzania. Below we outline the five official medical, civil registration, funeral or international repatriation, social security, and probate steps in chronological order under the laws of the United Republic of Tanzania.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Police Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or health facility deaths: When a death occurs in a national referral hospital (such as Muhimbili National Hospital), regional referral hospital, district hospital, or licensed private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health and supported by the World Health Organization Country Office for Tanzania [5], the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Notification of Death form) [1] [4].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: If your family member died at home from natural causes in Mainland Tanzania or Zanzibar, notify the local village or street executive officer (Mtendaji wa Mtaa / Kijiji) or Sheha (in Zanzibar) and report the death to the nearest government health facility and local police station so a medical officer can confirm the death and issue the official death notification [1] [4].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under Tanzania's Inquests Act (Cap. 24), any sudden, violent, accidental, or unnatural death must be reported immediately to the Tanzania Police Force [6]. Police officers inspect the scene, transfer the body to a designated public hospital mortuary for a forensic post-mortem examination, and issue Police Form 99 (PF 99) and a coroner's burial or release order once the examination is complete [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: In Mainland Tanzania, compulsory registration of deaths is governed by the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Cap. 108) and administered by the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency [1] [4]. (If the death occurred in Zanzibar, civil registration is handled by the Zanzibar Civil Status Registration Agency under its corresponding statute.)
  • Statutory deadline and required documents: A death occurring in Tanzania must be registered within 30 days of occurrence [4]. A surviving spouse, adult relative, or authorized informant submits the application at the District Registrar's office or via the eRITA online portal of the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency, presenting: (a) the hospital Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Police Form 99 and post-mortem report for non-hospital/unnatural deaths), (b) a confirmation letter from the local Ward or Street Executive Officer (Mtendaji wa Kata/Mtaa) for community deaths, (c) the deceased's National Identification Authority (NIDA) ID card, passport, or voter ID, and (d) the informant's valid identity document [1] [4].
  • Official Death Certificate issuance: Upon verification and payment of the modest statutory fee, the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency issues the official Death Certificate (Cheti cha Kifo) and Burial Permit [1] [4]. Request multiple certified copies of the Death Certificate, as banks, pension funds, and probate courts require certified originals [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: Municipal cemeteries, crematoria (such as Hindu Mandal crematoria in Dar es Salaam and major cities), and community burial grounds require the official Burial Permit issued by the hospital mortuary, municipal health officer, or civil registrar before interment or cremation can take place [1] [6].
  • Mortuary preparation and international repatriation: If your family member was a foreign citizen or if remains must be repatriated abroad, engage a licensed funeral home or hospital mortuary service in Tanzania [6]. You must obtain: (a) a certified Death Certificate from the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency [1], (b) an official Embalming Certificate and a Non-Infectious Disease / Export Permit from the Ministry of Health (Port Health Services) [5] [6], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate inspected by health and customs officers at Julius Nyerere International Airport or Kilimanjaro International Airport, and (d) a consular mortuary transit permit (laissez-passer) from the destination country's high commission or embassy [6].
  • Document legalization (non-Hague Apostille jurisdiction): Tanzania is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consequently, Tanzanian Death Certificates, medical certificates, and court probate orders intended for use abroad must be verified by the issuing agency, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation in Dar es Salaam or Dodoma, and legalized by the foreign embassy or high commission of the destination country (such as the U.S. Embassy in Tanzania or relevant diplomatic mission) [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Security Funds, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• Private-sector survivor and funeral benefits (NSSF): If the deceased was employed in the private or non-governmental sector, notify the National Social Security Fund under the National Social Security Fund Act (Cap. 50) [2] [3]. Eligible survivors (widow or widower, dependent children under age 18 or up to age 21 in full-time education, or dependent parents) can claim the Funeral Grant (reimbursing immediate burial expenses upon presenting the Death Certificate and burial permit) as well as the monthly Survivor's Pension or special lump-sum grant from the National Social Security Fund [2] [3].
  • Public-sector survivor benefits (PSSSF): If your family member was a civil servant or public-sector employee, notify the Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF) under the Public Service Social Security Fund Act 2018 to claim the statutory funeral grant, death gratuity, and survivor pension benefits [3].
  • Tax, identity, and bank notifications: Notify the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) to settle any final personal income tax or business TIN obligations, surrender the deceased's passport to the Immigration Department and NIDA card for cancellation, and present the certified Death Certificate to Tanzanian commercial banks so sole accounts are frozen pending court appointment of an estate administrator [1] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Cross-Border Succession
steps.html:
• Applicable succession regime and court jurisdiction: Estate administration in Mainland Tanzania is governed by the Probate and Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 352) and supervised by the Judiciary of Tanzania (High Court of Tanzania, District Courts, or Primary Courts depending on estate value and applicable personal law - statutory, customary, or Islamic law) [1]. Alternatively, families may appoint the Administrator-General within the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency to administer complex or contested estates [1].
  • Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration: No commercial bank, land registry, or social security fund in Tanzania will release estate funds to heirs without a formal court grant plus confirmed Minutes of the Family Meeting (Muhtasari wa Kikao cha Familia) [1] [2]. If the deceased left a valid Will, the executor petitions the court for a Grant of Probate; if intestate, the family holds a formal family meeting to nominate an administrator, files the petition with the court, publishes a statutory citation to creditors and heirs in the Government Gazette or local newspaper, and obtains Letters of Administration [1].
  • Estate inventory, taxes, and cross-border coordination: Tanzania abolished standalone estate duty, though court filing fees, capital gains or stamp duty on property transfers, and outstanding Tanzania Revenue Authority tax liabilities must be cleared before final distribution. The appointed executor or administrator must file a complete Estate Inventory within six months and a final Administration Account with the court [1]. Foreign grants of probate from Commonwealth or reciprocating jurisdictions may be resealed by the High Court of Tanzania, and heirs living abroad may execute a notarized and consulate-legalized Power of Attorney appointing a Tanzanian advocate to act on their behalf [1] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Tanzania: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Tanzania is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their care wishes and financial security. Below we explain the five essential steps to coordinate palliative care, treatment preferences, powers of attorney, invalidity benefits, and estate preparation in the United Republic of Tanzania.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist oncology and palliative care services: In Tanzania, tertiary palliative care, pain management, and supportive services are coordinated through Ocean Road Cancer Institute, Muhimbili National Hospital, zonal referral hospitals (such as KCMC in Moshi and Bugando Medical Centre in Mwanza), and faith-based hospital home-care teams operating under the Ministry of Health with technical partnership from the World Health Organization Country Office for Tanzania [5] [6]. Request a comprehensive written medical summary, diagnostic staging report, and pain-relief prescription plan from the attending specialist [5].
  • Public and private health insurance pre-authorization: If the ill person is insured with the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF), covered under the National Social Security Fund Social Health Insurance Benefit (SHIB) [2] [3], or enrolled in a private medical plan, submit the specialist clinical report early to pre-authorize oncology or palliative treatments, inpatient admissions, and long-term medications [2] [5].
  • Community and home-based palliative support: Ask the hospital palliative care unit to link your family with accredited regional home-based care nurses and palliative care associations in Tanzania for home symptom monitoring and analgesic continuity [5].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Written statement of medical treatment preferences: Tanzania does not yet have a dedicated statute codifying formal living wills or statutory advance directives, though national palliative care guidelines under the Ministry of Health emphasize patient autonomy and informed consent [5]. While your family member retains full mental capacity, it is advisable to prepare a clear written Statement of Medical Preferences specifying their choices regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, pain management, and preferred place of care, signed before two independent witnesses and a Commissioner for Oaths [5] [6].
  • Appointing a family medical spokesperson: In Tanzanian clinical practice, hospital teams consult the patient's designated next of kin (Ndugu wa Karibu) when the patient can no longer communicate [5]. Explicitly naming a primary and alternate healthcare representative in writing - and filing a signed copy in the hospital medical record with the attending doctor - prevents ambiguity among extended family members during critical care decisions [5].
  • Clinical documentation of capacity: Ask the treating specialist to enter a contemporaneous note in the patient's medical chart confirming that the ill person had full mental clarity and decision-making capacity on the date the treatment preferences were signed [5].

steps.title: Execute Valid Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Registered Power of Attorney while capacity is intact: Under Tanzanian contract and land registration law (including the Registration of Documents Act, Cap. 117, and the Land Registration Act, Cap. 334), a Power of Attorney is valid only when executed while the donor possesses sound mind and full legal capacity [1] [6]. Engage a licensed Tanzanian Advocate and Notary Public to draft a Special or General Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage bank transactions, business filings, and property matters [1] [6].
  • Mandatory registration for property transactions: If the representative may need to deal with registered land or real estate in Tanzania, the Power of Attorney must be formally stamped for stamp duty and registered with the Registrar of Titles / Registrar of Documents within the statutory registration window [1] [6].
  • Commercial bank signatory mandates: Tanzanian commercial banks typically require account holders to complete the bank's own third-party signatory mandate in person (or via an arranged home/hospital visit by bank relationship officers) accompanied by the account holder's National Identification Authority (NIDA) ID card [6]. Complete this directly with the bank while your family member can still sign and verify biometrics [6].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Pensions, Paid Sick Leave, and Caregiver Entitlements
steps.html:
• Private-sector invalidity pension (NSSF): Under the National Social Security Fund Act (Cap. 50), an insured member who suffers permanent total or partial incapacity for work before pensionable age - certified by a recognized medical board - is entitled to claim an Invalidity Pension (if minimum contribution requirements of at least 180 months, or at least 36 months with 12 months in the preceding 36 months, are met) or an Invalidity Special Lump Sum from the National Social Security Fund [2] [3].
  • Public-sector invalidity benefits (PSSSF): Civil servants and public employees assessed by a government Medical Board as permanently incapable of continuing public service due to severe illness qualify for medical retirement and invalidity benefits through the Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF) [3].
  • Statutory sick leave and workplace protections: Under Tanzania's Employment and Labour Relations Act (Cap. 366), formal-sector employees are entitled to at least 126 days of statutory sick leave in any 36-month leave cycle (the first 63 days at full wages and the second 63 days at half wages) upon presenting a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner [3] [6]. Caregivers employed in Tanzania may request compassionate leave, paid annual leave, or flexible working arrangements with their employer [6].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Drafting and safeguarding a valid Will with RITA: Under Tanzania's Probate and Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 352) and Indian Succession Act rules applicable in Tanzania, a written Will must be signed by the testator while of sound mind in the presence of at least two independent witnesses (for customary or statutory wills, witnessing requirements must be strictly observed so the Will cannot be set aside during probate) [1]. The Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency offers an official Will writing verification and safe-custody service to safeguard original Wills against loss or tampering [1] [4].
  • Update pension and insurance dependant records: Review and update the official list of nominated dependants and beneficiaries on file with the National Social Security Fund [2] [3], PSSSF, NHIF, and any private life insurance policies, and ensure all family members hold accurate birth and marriage certificates issued by the Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency [1] [4].
  • Cross-border coordination: Because Tanzania is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, any Power of Attorney or civil document executed outside Tanzania for use locally must be notarized and legalized by a Tanzanian embassy or high commission and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation, in line with the institutional governance framework documented by the World Bank Tanzania Country Office [6].

1. Palliative Care & NHIF/SHIB ApprovalImmediately upon specialist diagnosisAttending Specialist / Ministry of Health Hospital / NHIF
2. Written Medical Preferences & ProxyWhile mental capacity is fully intactAttending Physician / Hospital Medical Record
3. Power of Attorney & Bank MandateWhile legal capacity and NIDA biometrics are intactLicensed Advocate & Notary Public / Registrar of Documents / Bank
4. Statutory Sick Leave & Invalidity Claim126-day sick leave cycle; upon Medical Board assessmentEmployer / National Social Security Fund (NSSF) / PSSSF
5. Will Execution & Safe CustodyWhile testator retains sound disposing mindRegistration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA)

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Uganda: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Uganda: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Uganda: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Uganda. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order - covering medical certification, civil registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social security and financial notifications, and estate succession.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Death in a hospital or health facility: When your family member dies in a public or private hospital in Uganda, the attending medical officer examines the deceased and issues a formal Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (HMIS Form 100) [1] [2]. The health facility also generates an official Death Notification Record confirming the clinical cause, place, and time of death [1] [2].
  • Death at home or in the community: If your family member dies at home from natural causes outside a medical facility, the death must be reported immediately to the Local Council I (LC1) Chairperson and the sub-county chief, town clerk, or municipal division officer [1] [2]. The local administration verifies the event and issues a formal notification letter so the body can be transferred to a public health facility or mortuary for medical verification [1] [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death is sudden, unnatural, accidental, or occurs without recent medical attendance, you must report it immediately to the Uganda Police Force [2]. Police authorities open an inquiry and issue Police Form 48B requesting a medico-legal post-mortem examination by a police surgeon or government pathologist before a cause-of-death report and burial clearance are released [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent civil registration authority: Under the Registration of Persons Act, 2015, all deaths occurring in Uganda must be registered with the National Identification and Registration Authority [1] [2]. Certain historical civil status and document registration functions also interface with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau [3].
  • Statutory reporting deadlines: Notification of a death should be made immediately after the event, and formal civil registration with the National Identification and Registration Authority must be completed within three months of the date of death [1] [2]. Late registration after the statutory window requires additional supporting affidavits and administrative verification [2].
  • Required documents for registration: The informant (such as a close relative or person present at the death) must complete the prescribed Death Registration Form (Form 14) and submit it to the nearest district office of the National Identification and Registration Authority [1] [2]. You must attach the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death or post-mortem report, the Death Notification Record from the hospital or sub-county/town clerk, a copy of the deceased's National Identification Card or National Identification Number (NIN), and the informant's valid identification document [1] [2].
  • Issuance of the official Death Certificate: Upon verification and payment of the statutory registration fee (UGX 5,000 for Ugandan citizens or USD 40 for foreign nationals), the National Identification and Registration Authority enters the event into the National Identification Register, deactivates the deceased's National Identification Number, and issues the official Death Certificate [1] [2]. It is advisable to consider obtaining several certified copies for banking, pension, and probate filings [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: A licensed funeral home or hospital mortuary will release the body only after receiving the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or police post-mortem clearance), the hospital or mortuary discharge slip, and a local burial or cremation permit [1] [2]. Urban burials in municipal cemeteries and cremations require a municipal permit from the relevant city or municipal council health department [2].
  • Engaging a licensed funeral director: Licensed funeral service providers in Uganda coordinate mortuary preservation, coffin preparation, domestic transport clearance, and cemetery or ancestral burial ground logistics in compliance with public health standards [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported abroad, the funeral director must obtain an embalming certificate, a non-infectious disease and public health clearance certificate from the Ministry of Health, a coffin sealing certificate inspected by health and customs officers, and an export permit [2].
  • Consular legalization of documents: Because Uganda is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Ugandan Death Certificates and civil documents issued by the National Identification and Registration Authority or certified via the Uganda Registration Services Bureau for use abroad must undergo diplomatic authentication through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Uganda followed by consular legalization at the embassy or high commission of the destination country, which also issues a consular mortuary laissez-passer [1, 2, 3].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• National Social Security Fund survivor benefits: If your family member contributed to the private-sector social security scheme, eligible dependents (surviving spouse, children, or dependent parents) can claim the Survivors Benefit from the National Social Security Fund [4]. Claimants must submit the official Death Certificate, proof of identity and relationship, an employer or Local Council introduction letter, and bank account verification [1] [4]. For benefit balances of UGX 10 million or above, the National Social Security Fund requires certified Letters of Administration or a Grant of Probate, and for claims above UGX 50 million, a Certificate of No Objection from the Administrator General [4] [5].
  • Public service pensions: If the deceased was a civil servant or public pensioner, the family must notify the Ministry of Public Service and the deceased's employing ministry to process any statutory death gratuity and survivor pension entitlements [5].
  • Tax, banking, and corporate notifications: You should notify the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) so a legal representative can reconcile final income tax obligations and deactivate the deceased's Tax Identification Number (TIN) once estate administration concludes, as well as the Uganda Registration Services Bureau if the deceased held company shares or registered business interests [3] [5]. Commercial banks and insurers will freeze individual accounts upon presentation of the Death Certificate until formal court succession grants are presented [5] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Probate
steps.html:
• Intestate estates and the Administrator General: Under the Succession Act (Cap. 162) and the Administrator General's Act, if your family member died without leaving a valid will (intestate), the death must be reported to the Office of the Administrator General (under the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs) [5] [6]. Following a family meeting and verification of surviving spouses, lineal descendants, and dependent relatives, the Administrator General issues a Certificate of No Objection allowing the family's chosen representatives to petition the court for Letters of Administration (or administers the estate directly where appropriate) [5] [6].
  • Testate estates (Probate): If the deceased left a valid will naming executors, the executors do not require a Certificate of No Objection from the Administrator General unless the will is contested or omits executors [5] [6]. Instead, the executors petition directly for a Grant of Probate [5] [6].
  • Court jurisdiction and filing: Petitions for Grants of Probate or Letters of Administration are filed with the Judiciary of Uganda - specifically the Family Division of the High Court (or the Chief Magistrate's Court or Magistrate Grade I Court, depending on the monetary value of the estate) [5] [6]. After the court publishes a mandatory 14-day notice of application in the Uganda Gazette or a national newspaper and confirms no caveat has been lodged, the court issues the grant, requiring the administrator or executor to file an inventory within six months and a final account within twelve months [5] [6].
  • Estate duty, land transfers, and cross-border coordination: Uganda does not levy a separate inheritance tax, though stamp duty and land registry transfer fees apply when transmitting real property into beneficiaries' names [5] [6]. If an heir resides outside Uganda or if the deceased held foreign assets, a foreign-based executor or beneficiary may act through a notarized and consulate-legalized power of attorney registered with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau, and foreign probate grants from Commonwealth or reciprocating jurisdictions may be resealed by the High Court under the Probates (Resealing) Act [3, 5, 6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance, did your family member pass away in a hospital or at home in Uganda, and did they leave a valid will?
