title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Uganda: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Uganda: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Uganda: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Uganda is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal capacity protects their autonomy and secures essential support. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and specialist palliative care teams: In Uganda, palliative care is integrated into the national healthcare delivery system across regional referral hospitals, the Uganda Cancer Institute, and accredited specialist centres such as Hospice Africa Uganda, supported by the Palliative Care Association of Uganda [1] [2]. Request a formal clinical referral from your family member's attending specialist to establish a multidisciplinary symptom-management and pain-relief care plan (including regulated access to oral morphine and community outreach nursing) [1] [2].
  • Home-based nursing and hospice registration: Accredited hospice teams in Kampala and regional centres provide home visits, family caregiver training, and outpatient symptom control so your family member can receive coordinated medical care at home while maintaining clinical records at their referral hospital [1] [2].
  • Public and private health coverage verification: Public health facilities in Uganda provide baseline inpatient and outpatient services, while private health insurance schemes (regulated by the Insurance Regulatory Authority of Uganda) or employer medical schemes cover specialist consultations, oncology, and inpatient care subject to policy limits [3] [4]. Ensure your family member's National Identification Number (NIN) issued by the National Identification and Registration Authority is accurately recorded on all clinical files and insurance claims [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Recording treatment preferences while capacity is intact: Under the Uganda Patients' Rights and Responsibilities Charter and common-law principles of informed consent, an adult with full mental capacity has the right to accept or refuse specific medical treatments and to document preferences regarding resuscitation, intensive care, and palliative comfort measures [2] [5].
  • Designating a healthcare proxy or next-of-kin representative: Uganda does not have a standalone living-will statute, so medical providers rely on written advance care statements alongside the designated next of kin recorded in the patient's hospital file [2] [5]. While your family member has full decision-making capacity, they should execute a written and witnessed medical directive and formally nominate a trusted adult representative in their clinical records to communicate with doctors if they later lose the ability to speak for themselves [3] [5].
  • Sharing copies with clinical teams: Provide signed copies of the written care preferences and next-of-kin nomination to the attending physician, the palliative care team, and the designated family representative so instructions are immediately accessible during emergencies [2] [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a Power of Attorney: While your family member retains full mental capacity, they can execute a formal Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative (attorney-in-fact) to manage property, sign legal documents, and conduct financial transactions on their behalf [3] [5].
  • Mandatory registration with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau: To be legally enforceable for official, banking, and property transactions in Uganda, a Power of Attorney must be signed before a witness (and attested by an Advocate or Notary Public/Commissioner for Oaths), stamped for stamp duty via the Uganda Revenue Authority, and formally registered in the Registry of Documents at the Uganda Registration Services Bureau [3]. For transactions involving registered land under the Registration of Titles Act, a specific Power of Attorney must also be registered with the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development [3] [6].
  • Direct bank mandates and capacity limits: Commercial banks in Uganda generally require account holders to complete the bank's own third-party mandate or signatory forms in person (or via a bank-verified bedside visit) alongside presenting a Power of Attorney registered with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau [3]. Under Ugandan law, an ordinary Power of Attorney ceases to operate if the donor loses mental capacity or upon death, so bank account mandates and benefit arrangements should be established promptly while capacity is clear [3] [5].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Benefits, Critical-Illness Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• National Social Security Fund Invalidity Benefit and Midterm Access: If your family member is a contributing member of the National Social Security Fund who becomes permanently incapable of any normal gainful employment due to physical or mental disability, or suffers a serious illness, they can apply for the Invalidity Benefit [4]. Claimants must submit an NSSF claim form, a valid National ID confirmed by the National Identification and Registration Authority, bank details, and comprehensive medical reports for assessment by the Fund's medical board [1] [4].
  • Public service medical board retirement: If the ill person is a public officer, they may apply through their ministry and the Ministry of Public Service for retirement on medical grounds following examination by an official government Medical Board to unlock early pension and gratuity entitlements [5].
  • Workplace leave and private insurance benefits: Under the Employment Act, 2006, employees in Uganda are entitled to statutory paid sick leave upon presenting medical certification, and family caregivers may negotiate compassionate or annual leave with their employers [4]. You should also review any private life, mortgage, or critical-illness insurance policies for accelerated terminal-illness or permanent-disability payouts [4] [5].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Cross-Border Estate Documents
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid Will under the Succession Act: Under the Succession Act (Cap. 162), any person of sound mind aged 18 or older may execute a written Will to appoint executors, name guardians for minor children, and specify how property should be distributed (while respecting statutory protections for the principal residential property and dependent family members) [5] [6]. The Will must be signed by the testator in the presence of at least two witnesses present at the same time, who must also sign in the testator's presence [5] [6].
  • Safekeeping and optional registration of the Will: A signed Will may be deposited for safekeeping with an advocate, the Uganda Registration Services Bureau, or the Office of the Administrator General, which collaborates with the Judiciary of Uganda when succession proceedings later take place [3, 5, 6].
  • Consolidating civil identity and property records: Gather original National Identification Cards and birth or marriage certificates issued by the National Identification and Registration Authority, registered land titles, company share certificates filed with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau, and updated beneficiary nomination forms filed with the National Social Security Fund [1, 3, 4].
  • Cross-border coordination: If family members or assets are located outside Uganda, ensure that any foreign Power of Attorney intended for use in Uganda is notarized, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalised at the relevant Ugandan embassy or high commission, and registered with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau, and coordinate separate situs Wills if immovable property is held abroad [3, 5, 6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance, is your family member covered by the National Social Security Fund or a public service pension scheme in Uganda, and do they need to register a Power of Attorney or update a Will?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Zambia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Zambia, we can guide you through the official medical certification, civil registration, funeral or repatriation, social security, and estate administration procedures in the order they must be completed.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical Certification of DeathImmediately upon deathMinistry of Health / Zambia Police Service
2. Civil Death RegistrationWithin 24 hours to 30 days (before burial)Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship
3. Burial, Cremation, or RepatriationAfter Burial Order is issuedLocal Municipal Council / Ministry of Health
4. Social Security, Pension, and TaxPromptly after Death Certificate issuanceNational Pension Scheme Authority / Zambia Revenue Authority
5. Estate Administration and ProbateWithin 14 to 30 days of deathHigh Court of Zambia / Administrator-General

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: When your family member dies in a public hospital or accredited private medical facility supervised by the Ministry of Health, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death along with the hospital notification of death record [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If the death occurred at home and the deceased had been receiving regular medical care for a documented chronic illness, contact the treating clinician or nearest public health centre to confirm the cause of death. If no medical officer can certify natural causes at the home, notify the nearest station of the Zambia Police Service (Brought-In-Dead procedure) so police officers can issue a police report and authorize transfer to a public hospital mortuary for examination [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unnatural deaths: Under Zambia's Inquests Act, any sudden, accidental, violent, or unexplained death must be reported immediately to the Zambia Police Service. A coroner or state forensic pathologist conducts a post-mortem examination at a designated public hospital mortuary and issues forensic clearance and the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death before civil registration can take place [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadlines: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Cap. 51), every death in Zambia must be registered with the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship (under the Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security) [1] [2]. Notice of death should be given within 24 to 72 hours for urban deaths before burial (and within 14 to 30 days where a sub-centre notice is forwarded to the Registrar) [1] [2].
  • Required documents for registration: A surviving relative or authorized informant must attend the nearest district registration office of the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship and present: (a) the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (and police post-mortem report if applicable), (b) the deceased's original Green National Registration Card (NRC) or passport, which is surrendered for cancellation, and (c) the informant's own valid National Registration Card or passport [1] [2].
  • Burial Order and official Death Certificate: Upon registration, the registrar issues a Death Record / Burial Permit authorizing interment or cremation, followed by the official Death Certificate [1] [2]. It is advisable to request several certified copies of the Death Certificate, as banks, pension institutions, and the probate registry require certified originals [1] [5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Engage a licensed funeral service provider or municipal mortuary in Zambia to coordinate burial or cremation with the local city or municipal council cemetery authority [2]. No burial or cremation may proceed at a public cemetery without presenting the official Burial Permit and Death Record issued by the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported outside Zambia, the funeral director must obtain: (a) an official Death Certificate from the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship [1], (b) an embalming certificate and non-communicable disease clearance from a public health officer of the Ministry of Health [2], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate confirming hermetically sealed zinc-lined containment for air cargo, (d) an export/removal permit from the Ministry of Health and Zambia Revenue Authority customs clearance, and (e) a consular mortuary laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy or high commission [2] [6].
  • Document authentication and legalization: Because Zambia is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Zambian Death Certificates and probate records intended for use abroad must be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Lusaka and then legalized by the embassy or high commission of the destination country [5] [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• National Pension Scheme Authority benefits: If the deceased was employed in the formal sector and contributed to the statutory social security system, eligible survivors can claim both a Funeral Grant and a Survivor's Pension or Survivor's Lump Sum from the National Pension Scheme Authority [3] [4]. Submit the claim with certified copies of the Death Certificate, the deceased's National Registration Card, marriage certificate or birth certificates of dependent children, and claimant banking details [3] [4].
  • Public service pensions and health insurance: If the deceased was a civil servant or public sector retiree, notify the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) or Local Authorities Superannuation Fund (LASF) to process death gratuities and survivor pensions [3]. You should also notify the National Health Insurance Management Authority (NHIMA) and any Workers' Compensation Fund Control Board account (if death resulted from an occupational accident or disease) [2] [3].
  • Tax and banking notifications: Notify the Zambia Revenue Authority to reconcile final income tax obligations and obtain tax clearance where estate assets or property transfers are involved, and provide the Death Certificate to all Zambian commercial banks so individual accounts are frozen pending formal estate letters [5] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession
steps.html:
• Testate vs. intestate legal framework: Succession in Zambia is governed by the Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act (Cap. 60) where the deceased left a valid Will, and by the Intestate Succession Act (Cap. 59) where the deceased died without a Will [5]. Under the Intestate Succession Act, statutory distribution rules allocate specified percentages of the estate to surviving children, the surviving spouse, parents, and dependents while protecting the family homestead [5].
  • Probate and Letters of Administration: To access bank accounts, pension estate payouts, or registered land, the nominated executor or surviving family must apply to the Probate Registry of the High Court of Zambia (or the Subordinate/Local Court for smaller estates within statutory monetary jurisdiction) for a Grant of Probate (if there is a Will) or Letters of Administration (if intestate) [5]. Alternatively, families may instruct the Office of the Administrator-General to administer the estate [5].
  • Estate tax and cross-border property transfers: Zambia does not levy a standalone inheritance duty on beneficiaries, though Property Transfer Tax administered by the Zambia Revenue Authority and court probate fees may apply to specific transfers unless covered by statutory succession exemptions [5] [6]. If heirs live abroad or the deceased held foreign assets, a Commonwealth or foreign grant of probate may be resealed by the High Court of Zambia under the Probates (Resealing) Act, or foreign heirs may execute a notarized and legalized Power of Attorney appointing a Zambian legal practitioner [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Zambia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
When a family member in Zambia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and secures family support. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative Care and Health CoverageImmediately after diagnosisMinistry of Health / National Health Insurance Management Authority
2. Advance Medical DirectivesWhile mental capacity is intactMinistry of Health / Attending Hospital Clinical Team
3. Financial and Legal Powers of AttorneyBefore loss of legal capacityMinistry of Lands and Natural Resources / Commercial Banks
4. Invalidity Benefits and Caregiver LeaveUpon medical board certificationNational Pension Scheme Authority / Employer
5. Will, Civil Status, and Estate PrepWhile testamentary capacity is clearHigh Court of Zambia / Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist palliative and oncology care: In Zambia, multidisciplinary palliative care and pain management (including regulated access to oral morphine and symptom control) are delivered through tertiary public referral hospitals such as the University Teaching Hospital (UTH) and the Cancer Diseases Hospital (CDH) in Lusaka, provincial hospitals under the Ministry of Health, and accredited community hospices coordinated with the Palliative Care Alliance Zambia [2] [6]. Request a formal clinical referral from your family member's attending specialist to establish an integrated inpatient and home-based nursing plan [2].
  • National Health Insurance Management Authority coverage: Verify that your family member's contributions and registration with the National Health Insurance Management Authority (NHIMA) are active so inpatient care, diagnostic imaging, and approved medications at NHIMA-accredited public and private facilities are covered [2] [6].
  • Private medical schemes: If the ill person holds private medical insurance or employer health coverage, request written pre-authorization for specialist oncology, palliative admissions, or home nursing care, and ensure their Green National Registration Card (NRC) number matches all clinical records [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment preferences while capacity is intact: Zambia does not have a standalone living-will statute, so treatment decisions are governed by constitutional rights to personal autonomy, common-law informed consent principles, and clinical guidelines overseen by the Health Professions Council of Zambia and the Ministry of Health [2] [5]. While your family member retains full mental capacity, they can sign a written statement of medical preferences covering cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and palliative comfort care [2].
  • Designating a healthcare proxy or next-of-kin spokesperson: Your family member should formally name a primary adult next of kin or medical representative in their hospital file and in a signed, witnessed written instrument so clinicians have clear authority on whom to consult if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [2] [5].
  • Lodging copies with the care team: Provide signed copies of the advance care preferences and representative designation to the attending physician, the hospital medical records unit, and key family members to prevent uncertainty during acute medical episodes [2].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a formal Power of Attorney: While your family member has full mental and legal capacity, they may execute a general or special Power of Attorney under Seal authorizing a trusted attorney-in-fact to manage bank accounts, pay medical bills, and sign legal documents in Zambia [5] [6]. The instrument should be drafted by a legal practitioner and executed before a Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths [5].
  • Mandatory registration for property and official transactions: Under the Lands and Deeds Registry Act (Cap. 185), any Power of Attorney that authorizes transactions involving land or registered property in Zambia must be formally registered in the Miscellaneous Register at the Lands and Deeds Registry of the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources [5] [6].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates and capacity rules: Commercial banks in Zambia generally require the account holder to sign the bank's own third-party mandate or joint-signatory forms in person (or through a verified hospital bedside visit by bank officials) alongside presenting a notarized Power of Attorney [5] [6]. Because a standard common-law Power of Attorney in Zambia ceases to have legal effect if the donor loses mental capacity, bank mandates and payment arrangements should be completed early while capacity is clear [5].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Benefits, Critical-Illness Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• National Pension Scheme Authority Invalidity Benefits: If your family member is a contributing member of the National Pension Scheme Authority who is assessed as permanently incapable of gainful employment due to severe physical or mental illness before reaching normal retirement age, they can claim an Invalidity Pension (if minimum contribution requirements are met) or an Invalidity Lump Sum [3] [4]. Applications require an official NAPSA claim form, the member's National Registration Card, bank account verification, and a comprehensive medical assessment certified by a registered medical practitioner and the authority's medical board [3] [4].
  • Public service medical retirement: Civil servants and public sector workers covered by the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) or Local Authorities Superannuation Fund (LASF) may apply for retirement on medical grounds following examination by a government Medical Board constituted by the Ministry of Health [2] [3].
  • Statutory sick leave and compassionate workplace arrangements: Under Zambia's Employment Code Act, 2019, employees are entitled to statutory paid sick leave upon producing a medical certificate from a registered health practitioner, and employed family caregivers can apply for compassionate leave or paid annual leave to support a critically ill dependent [3] [6].

steps.title: Review and Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Will under the Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act: While your family member possesses full testamentary capacity, it is advisable to review or execute a written Will under the Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act (Cap. 60), which is overseen by the High Court of Zambia [5]. To be valid, a written Will must be signed by the testator in the presence of two competent independent witnesses present at the same time (who are not beneficiaries or spouses of beneficiaries), and it may be sealed and lodged for safekeeping with the Probate Registry of the High Court of Zambia or a law firm [5].
  • Updating statutory pension and insurance nominations: Because pension benefits with the National Pension Scheme Authority and group life policies rely on member records, the ill person should update their beneficiary nomination forms and family details directly with the pension fund and insurer [3] [4].
  • Consolidating civil identity and cross-border records: Gather the original Green National Registration Card (NRC), birth and marriage certificates issued by the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship, Certificate of Title deeds, and Zambia Revenue Authority TPIN records [1] [5]. If family members or assets are located outside Zambia, ensure any foreign Power of Attorney is notarized and legalized at a Zambian diplomatic mission, and coordinate separate situs Wills for foreign real estate [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Zimbabwe: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Zimbabwe: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Zimbabwe: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Zimbabwe, we can guide you through the official medical certification, civil registration, funeral or repatriation, social security, and estate administration procedures in the order they must be completed.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical Certification of DeathImmediately upon deathMinistry of Health and Child Care / Zimbabwe Republic Police
2. Civil Death RegistrationWithin 30 days of death (and before burial)Civil Registry Department
3. Burial, Cremation, or RepatriationAfter Burial Order is issuedLocal Municipal Authority / Ministry of Health and Child Care
4. Social Security, Pension, and TaxWithin 12 months for funeral grant; promptly for pensionsNational Social Security Authority / Zimbabwe Revenue Authority
5. Estate Administration and ProbateWithin 14 days of deathMaster of the High Court

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: If your family member died in a government hospital, mission hospital, or private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health and Child Care, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (BD12 / Death Notice form) [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): When a death occurs at home in an urban or rural community, report the death to the nearest station of the Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) or traditional leader (in rural districts) and present the deceased's medical treatment cards if they were under care for a known illness [1] [2]. If a doctor cannot immediately certify natural causes, police officers arrange removal to a public hospital mortuary for medical confirmation [1] [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unnatural deaths: Under Zimbabwe's Inquests Act, any unexpected, accidental, or unexplained death must be reported immediately to the Zimbabwe Republic Police. A state pathologist or government medical officer conducts a medico-legal post-mortem examination and issues a police clearance and Medical Certificate of Cause of Death before civil registration can proceed [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Chapter 5:02), every death occurring in Zimbabwe must be registered with the Civil Registry Department (under the Ministry of Home Affairs and Cultural Heritage) within 30 days of the death, and a Burial Order must be obtained before interment [1] [5].
  • Required documents for registration: A surviving relative or authorized informant must visit a provincial or district office (or hospital sub-office) of the Civil Registry Department and submit: (a) the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (BD12) issued by the hospital or post-mortem doctor (plus the police report for home or sudden deaths), (b) the deceased's original Zimbabwean National Identity Card, birth certificate, or passport for cancellation, and (c) the informant's own valid National Identity Card or passport [1] [5].
  • Burial Order and official Death Certificate: Upon registration, the Registrar issues a Burial Order authorizing burial or cremation and processes the official Death Certificate [1] [5]. It is advisable to request several certified copies of the Death Certificate, as banks, pension institutions, and the court require certified originals [1] [6].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation: Engage a registered funeral assurance provider or licensed funeral undertaker in Zimbabwe to transfer the deceased from the mortuary and book a burial plot or crematorium slot with the local city, town, or rural district council [1] [2]. Cemeteries and crematoria require the official Burial Order issued by the Civil Registry Department before any service takes place [1] [5].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or if the remains must be transported outside Zimbabwe, the funeral director must obtain: (a) a certified Death Certificate and Burial/Removal Order from the Civil Registry Department [1], (b) an embalming certificate and non-infectious disease public health permit from the environmental health directorate of the Ministry of Health and Child Care [2], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate confirming a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin for international transport, (d) customs export clearance from the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority, and (e) consular clearance from the destination country's embassy.
  • Document authentication and legalization: Because Zimbabwe is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Zimbabwean Death Certificates and probate orders intended for use abroad must be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Trade in Harare and then legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country [5] [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• National Social Security Authority benefits: If the deceased contributed to the Pension and Other Benefits Scheme, eligible survivors or the person who paid funeral expenses can claim a Funeral Grant and a Survivor's Benefit (monthly pension or lump-sum grant for spouses, dependent children, or registered dependents) from the National Social Security Authority [3] [4]. Submit Form P9/P10 with certified copies of the Death Certificate, the deceased's National ID, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates, and bank account verification [3] [4].
  • Public Service Commission and occupational pensions: If your family member was a civil servant or state pensioner, notify the Public Service Commission (Pensions Office) and their employing ministry to process the death gratuity and surviving spouse/child pensions [3]. Also notify any private occupational pension fund, medical aid society, or funeral policy provider [3] [4].
  • Tax and banking notifications: Notify the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) to settle final income tax obligations and estate duty clearance, and present the Death Certificate to all Zimbabwean commercial banks so individual accounts are frozen pending appointment of an executor [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession
steps.html:
• Reporting the estate within 14 days: Under the Administration of Estates Act (Chapter 6:01), every deceased estate in Zimbabwe must be reported within 14 days of the death to the Master of the High Court (in Harare, Bulawayo, Masvingo, Mutare, or Chinhoyi) or to the nearest Magistrate's Court [6].
  • Required filings and appointment of an executor: The surviving family or nominated executor must file a Death Notice, a preliminary Inventory of all movable and immovable property, the original Will (if the deceased died testate under the Wills Act, Chapter 6:06), or attend an Edict Meeting convened by the Master of the High Court to appoint an Executor Dative (if intestate under the Deceased Estates Succession Act, Chapter 6:02) [6]. The Master issues Letters of Administration authorizing the executor to gather assets, advertise for creditors and debtors in the Government Gazette and a local newspaper, and lodge a Liquidation and Distribution Account [6].
  • Estate duty and cross-border coordination: Estate Duty in Zimbabwe is assessed under the Estate Duty Act (Chapter 23:03) subject to statutory family rebates and exemptions for the principal family residence, and an Estate Duty Clearance Certificate is required before immovable property can be transferred at the Deeds Registry [6]. Where heirs reside abroad or foreign grants of probate must be recognized in Zimbabwe, the High Court can reseal Commonwealth or foreign probate grants, or foreign beneficiaries can act through a Zimbabwean legal practitioner under a notarized and legalized Power of Attorney [6].

titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zimbabwe: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Zimbabwe: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
When a family member in Zimbabwe is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, legal, and financial arrangements while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their wishes and secures family support. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to take in order.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative Care and Medical AidImmediately after diagnosisMinistry of Health and Child Care / Hospice and Palliative Care Association
2. Advance Medical DirectivesWhile mental capacity is intactMinistry of Health and Child Care / Attending Clinical Team
3. Financial and Legal Powers of AttorneyBefore loss of legal capacityDeeds Registry / Commercial Banks
4. Invalidity Benefits and Sick LeaveUpon medical certificationNational Social Security Authority / Employer
5. Will, Civil Status, and Estate PrepWhile testamentary capacity is clearMaster of the High Court / Civil Registry Department

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and community palliative care services: In Zimbabwe, multidisciplinary palliative care, symptom management, and regulated pain relief are delivered through central and provincial hospitals under the Ministry of Health and Child Care alongside accredited community hospices such as Island Hospice and Healthcare (coordinated with the Hospice and Palliative Care Association of Zimbabwe) [2] [6]. Ask the attending specialist or oncologist for a formal palliative care referral so inpatient and home-based nursing teams can coordinate care [2].
  • Medical aid society and public health coverage: If your family member belongs to a registered medical aid society in Zimbabwe (such as PSMAS, Cimas, or First Mutual Health), contact the society's case-management unit to pre-authorize oncology treatments, home nursing visits, and chronic medication benefits [2] [6]. Ensure the patient's Zimbabwean National Identity Card number issued by the Civil Registry Department is accurately recorded on all clinical and insurance files [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Recording treatment preferences while capacity is intact: Zimbabwe does not have a standalone living-will statute; instead, medical decision-making is governed by constitutional rights to bodily integrity, common-law informed consent principles, and the Patients' Charter administered by the Ministry of Health and Child Care and the Medical and Dental Practitioners Council of Zimbabwe [2] [5]. While your family member retains full mental capacity, they can sign a clear written statement of treatment preferences covering cardiopulmonary resuscitation, intensive care ventilation, and palliative comfort measures [2].
  • Designating a medical spokesperson or next of kin: Because clinicians look to the documented next of kin when a patient can no longer communicate, your family member should formally record their chosen adult medical representative in their hospital file and in a signed, witnessed written statement shared with the attending physician and family [2] [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a General or Special Power of Attorney: While your family member has full mental and legal capacity, they can sign a General or Special Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative (agent) to manage financial affairs, pay medical bills, and administer property in Zimbabwe [5] [6]. The Power of Attorney must be signed by the principal in the presence of two competent witnesses or attested before a Notary Public / Commissioner of Oaths [5].
  • Registration with the Deeds Registry for immovable property: Under Zimbabwe's Deeds Registries Act (Chapter 20:05), if the Power of Attorney authorizes the agent to transfer, mortgage, or deal with registered land or immovable property, the instrument must be drafted with conveyancing precision and registered at the Deeds Registry in Harare or Bulawayo [5] [6].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates and capacity rules: Commercial banks in Zimbabwe require the account holder to complete the bank's own mandate or third-party signatory forms in person (or through a verified bedside visit by bank officers) alongside presenting the Power of Attorney [5] [6]. Under Roman-Dutch common law applied in Zimbabwe, an ordinary Power of Attorney lapses if the principal loses mental capacity (requiring High Court appointment of a curator bonis if capacity is lost), so banking mandates should be established promptly while capacity is intact [5].

steps.title: Activate Invalidity Benefits, Critical-Illness Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• National Social Security Authority Invalidity Benefits: If your family member contributed to the Pension and Other Benefits Scheme and becomes permanently incapable of work due to physical or mental illness before age 60, they can apply for an Invalidity Pension or Invalidity Grant from the National Social Security Authority [3] [4]. Claims must be filed on Form P9/P10 accompanied by the claimant's National Identity Card, bank account details, and a medical report completed by a registered medical practitioner for review by the authority's medical board [3] [4].
  • Public service medical retirement: Civil servants who can no longer perform their duties due to advanced illness may apply through their ministry and the Public Service Commission for retirement on medical grounds following examination by a government Medical Board convened under the Ministry of Health and Child Care [2] [3].
  • Statutory sick leave and compassionate leave: Under Zimbabwe's Labour Act (Chapter 28:01), employees are entitled to up to 90 days of paid sick leave on full pay (and a further 90 days on half pay) within a one-year period when supported by a registered medical practitioner's certificate, and employed family caregivers may apply for special compassionate leave or annual leave [3] [6].

steps.title: Review and Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Will under the Wills Act: While your family member possesses full testamentary capacity (aged 16 or older and of sound mind), it is advisable to prepare or update a written Will in strict compliance with the Wills Act (Chapter 6:06) [5]. The testator must sign every page of the Will (and at the end) in the presence of at least two competent independent witnesses present at the same time, who must also sign in the presence of the testator [5].
  • Safekeeping with the Master of the High Court: During their lifetime, a testator may lodge their original sealed Will for safe custody with the Master of the High Court upon payment of the prescribed statutory fee, or keep it with their legal practitioner or bank [5].
  • Consolidating civil identity and cross-border records: Gather the original Zimbabwean National Identity Card, birth certificate, and marriage certificate issued by the Civil Registry Department, original Title Deeds, pension beneficiary nomination forms filed with the National Social Security Authority, and Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) tax records [1] [3]. If family members or assets are located outside Zimbabwe, ensure any foreign Power of Attorney intended for use in Zimbabwe is notarized and legalized through a Zimbabwean embassy, and coordinate separate situs Wills for foreign property [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Afghanistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Afghanistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Afghanistan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Afghanistan. Navigating medical certification, civil registration, burial or international repatriation, institutional notifications, and succession procedures in Afghanistan requires coordinating with public health facilities, provincial civil registration offices, and local Sharia courts. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public or private hospital or clinic supervised by the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan, the attending physician issues a formal medical death notification (cause-of-death certificate) recording the deceased person's full identity details, date and hour of death, and clinical cause of death [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home or in the community: When your family member dies at home without an attending physician, a medical practitioner from the nearest provincial hospital or Basic Package of Health Services clinic, coordinated alongside World Health Organization Afghanistan health reporting standards, can examine the body or review clinical records to issue a medical notification, supplemented by written confirmation from local community elders (Maliks or Wakils of the Gozar) and two adult witnesses [2] [3].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death is sudden, unnatural, or occurs outside medical supervision under unclear circumstances, local police and forensic medical examiners (Teb-e-Adli) under the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan must inspect the body and issue a forensic clearance certificate before burial or civil registration can proceed [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent civil registration authority: Civil registration of vital events is administered by the National Statistics and Information Authority (NSIA) through its Civil Registration and Vital Statistics directorates in Kabul and provincial or district registration offices [2] [4].
  • Statutory reporting procedure and documents: A close relative or authorized representative should report the death to the local office of the National Statistics and Information Authority as soon as practicable (traditionally within the statutory reporting window following burial) by presenting the medical death notification or community witness attestation, the deceased person's original national identity document (Tazkira or electronic e-Tazkira), and the informant's own Tazkira [2] [4].
  • Issuance of official death certificates: Once verified and recorded in the civil register, the National Statistics and Information Authority cancels the deceased person's Tazkira for active use and issues official death certificates (Wafat-Nama), which are required for pension claims, banking procedures, and court succession filings [2] [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial arrangements: Under local custom and public health regulations in Afghanistan, interment in a municipal or community cemetery typically takes place within 24 hours of death once the medical notification or forensic clearance is issued [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported abroad, the family or an international funeral assistance coordinator must obtain an official death certificate from the National Statistics and Information Authority, a public health non-contagion and embalming/hermetic sealing certificate from the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan, customs transit clearance for the zinc-lined coffin, and a consular mortuary laissez-passer from the destination country's diplomatic mission [1, 2, 4].
  • Document legalization: Because international recognition of civil and court documents issued in Afghanistan typically requires full diplomatic authentication rather than a single Apostille stamp, original death certificates and medical records intended for foreign authorities must be certified by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Kabul and legalized by the relevant foreign embassy or consulate [2] [4].

steps.title: Notify Public Authorities, Pension Funds, and Banks
steps.html:
• Identity, tax, and public service records: Present the official death certificate issued by the National Statistics and Information Authority to provincial municipal offices, utility providers, and tax departments to close outstanding individual obligations and update property occupancy rolls [4].
  • Public-sector survivor pensions and benefits: If the deceased was a civil servant, teacher, or public retiree registered under the national pension scheme (administered through the General Directorate of Pension Treasury under the Ministry of Finance and labor regulations published by the Ministry of Justice of Afghanistan), eligible surviving dependents - such as a non-working spouse, minor children, or dependent parents - may apply for a survivor pension or lump-sum death benefit by submitting the death certificate, pension book, and court certificate of legal heirs [4] [5].
  • Commercial bank accounts: Notify all commercial banks in Afghanistan where the deceased held accounts. Banks freeze individual accounts upon notification of death and release funds only upon presentation of the official death certificate and a court-issued certificate of inheritance (Hasr-e-Warasat) [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession
steps.html:
• Court certificate of legal heirs (Hasr-e-Warasat): Under the Civil Code and statutory rules overseen by the Ministry of Justice of Afghanistan, heirs must petition the competent primary family or civil court (Mahkama-e-Wasaia wa Mawaris) to obtain an official Certificate of Inheritance (Hasr-e-Warasat / Warasat-Khat) [5]. The court requires the death certificate from the National Statistics and Information Authority, the Tazkira of the deceased and each heir, and the sworn testimony of witnesses confirming the complete list of surviving legal heirs [4] [5].
  • Distribution of estate shares and property registration: Succession in Afghanistan follows statutory forced-heirship shares (Faraid) after settlement of funeral expenses, verified debts, and any valid testamentary bequest (Wasiyyat, capped at one-third of the net estate unless consented to by all adult heirs) [5]. Immovable property transfers (Qabala-e-Shar'i) and court registration fees are processed through the primary court and provincial land registry [5].
  • Cross-border heirs and powers of attorney: If an heir resides outside Afghanistan or if assets span multiple jurisdictions (where UNHCR Afghanistan also provides legal documentation guidance for displaced and returning families), the absent heir may execute a specific Power of Attorney (Wakalat-Nama) before an Afghan diplomatic mission or recognized notary abroad so a local representative can represent them in the Hasr-e-Warasat and property partition proceedings [5] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Afghanistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Afghanistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Afghanistan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Afghanistan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their care preferences and secure family assets. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Support, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public oncology and palliative care services: Specialized symptom management, pain relief, and supportive care are coordinated through tertiary public hospitals under the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan, including the National Cancer Control Programme units in Kabul (such as Jamhuriat Hospital and Ali Abad Teaching Hospital) and regional provincial referral hospitals [1] [2].
  • Multidisciplinary symptom management and home care: Through clinical capacity programs supported by the World Health Organization Afghanistan, hospital oncology teams provide outpatient pain-management regimens, family caregiving instruction, and psychosocial guidance so that patients who prefer to remain at home can receive structured symptom support [1] [2].
  • Health coverage and humanitarian medical assistance: Public hospital consultations and basic essential medicines under the Essential Package of Hospital Services are subsidized by the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan, though families often supplement specialized medications through private pharmacies or humanitarian health programs coordinated with World Health Organization Afghanistan partners [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Spokesperson
steps.html:
• Written medical preferences: Afghanistan does not have a standalone statutory living-will registry, so while your family member retains full mental capacity, it is advisable to consider recording clear written treatment preferences - such as consent to or refusal of invasive resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, or intensive-care transfer - in the clinical file held by the attending physician under the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan [1] [2].
  • Family medical representative (Wali or designated proxy): In Afghan clinical practice, doctors consult the patient directly while capacity is intact and otherwise rely on the senior close family representative or a formally designated agent to confirm consent for surgical or palliative interventions [1] [3].
  • Hospital care directive documentation: Providing the treating hospital team with a signed statement naming the primary family contact and backup decision-maker helps prevent delays or disagreements among relatives during medical emergencies [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Court-registered Power of Attorney (Wakalat-Nama): Under the Civil Code and judicial procedures overseen by the Ministry of Justice of Afghanistan, a person who holds full mental capacity (Ahliyat) can execute an official general or specific Power of Attorney (Wakalat-Nama / Khat-e-Wakalat) before a primary court registration office (Wasaia waWathiqa-jat) [3].
  • Verification of identity and witnesses: To execute a court-registered Wakalat-Nama, both the principal (the ill person) and the appointed representative must present valid national identity cards (Tazkira or e-Tazkira) issued by the National Statistics and Information Authority, along with two adult witnesses and recent passport photographs [3] [4].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Because commercial banks in Afghanistan frequently require account holders to appear in person or provide a bank-verified mandate coupled with a court-certified Wakalat-Nama, your family member should register an authorized signatory directly at their bank branch while still able to travel or arrange a home verification visit [3] [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Critical-Illness, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Public-sector medical retirement and disability benefits: If your family member is a current or former public employee covered by the public pension system regulated under laws published by the Ministry of Justice of Afghanistan, a medical commission under the Ministry of Public Health of Afghanistan can certify permanent work incapacity or severe illness to activate early disability retirement benefits [1] [3].
  • Workplace medical leave: Under Afghan labor regulations, employees facing serious illness or caring for an immediate family member may request certified medical leave or unpaid family care leave supported by an official hospital medical certificate [1] [3].
  • Humanitarian and protection assistance: For vulnerable households, returnees, or internally displaced families coping with severe chronic illness or disability, UNHCR Afghanistan and partner protection networks provide targeted vulnerability assessments, cash-for-health referrals, and civil documentation assistance [5].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Testamentary bequests (Wasiyyat) and statutory succession rules: Under the Civil Code of Afghanistan administered via the Ministry of Justice of Afghanistan, at least two-thirds of a person's net estate passes automatically to statutory legal heirs under fixed Faraid shares, while up to one-third of the net estate may be freely bequeathed by a formal written and witnessed will (Wasiyyat-Nama), and any lifetime gift (Hiba) or property settlement must be completed and delivered while the donor has full legal capacity [3].
  • Consolidating identity and property deeds: Verify that your family member's Tazkira and family civil records with the National Statistics and Information Authority match the names recorded on official property title deeds (Qabala-e-Shar'i), customary deeds (Qabala-e-Urfi), and bank accounts so future succession filings are not delayed by spelling or identity discrepancies [3] [4].
  • Cross-border family members and assets: If designated representatives or future heirs live abroad, ensure that powers of attorney and civil status records from the National Statistics and Information Authority are authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant diplomatic mission so they can be used across jurisdictions [3, 4, 5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Armenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Armenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Armenia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Armenia. Navigating medical certification, civil registration, burial or international repatriation, survivor benefits, and notarial succession in the Republic of Armenia involves coordinating with healthcare institutions, the Civil Status Acts Registration Agency, social security offices, and licensed notaries. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a licensed medical facility overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Armenia, the attending physician or hospital pathology unit records the death in the national electronic health system (ArMed) and issues an official Medical Certificate of Death [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member dies at home from a documented natural illness, immediately contact the emergency medical service (1-03) and the local territorial polyclinic where the deceased was registered under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Armenia so a physician can confirm the death and issue the electronic and paper Medical Certificate of Death [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: When a death occurs suddenly, outside medical supervision, or under unclear circumstances, the Police of the Republic of Armenia must be notified to inspect the scene and refer the body to the Scientific-Practical Center of Forensic Medicine for a mandatory forensic autopsy before a forensic medical death certificate is issued [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Status Registry
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: State registration of death is carried out by the Civil Status Acts Registration Agency operating under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia, through unified public service offices (Hartak service centers), regional civil registry offices, or online via the electronic government portal [1] [3].
  • Statutory filing procedure and required documents: Under the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Acts of Civil Status (published on the Armenian Legal Information System), an application for state registration of death should be submitted promptly after the medical certificate is issued by presenting the Medical Certificate of Death, the deceased person's passport or identification card (which is retained for cancellation), and the applicant's identification document [1, 3, 4].
  • Official State Death Certificate: State registration of death and issuance of the official Death Certificate (delivered electronically with a verifiable QR code and in printed form) are free of state duty [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial arrangements: Once the Civil Status Acts Registration Agency under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia issues the official State Death Certificate, the family or a licensed municipal funeral service provider uses that certificate to secure a cemetery plot permit and schedule interment [1] [3].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If your family member was a foreign citizen or if the remains must be repatriated abroad, a licensed international funeral director must obtain the official State Death Certificate, a sanitary-epidemiological and embalming certificate confirming that the remains have been hermetically sealed in a zinc-lined coffin, customs clearance, and consular transit authorization in coordination with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia and the destination country's embassy [1] [5].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Because Armenia is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, official civil status certificates issued under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia can receive an electronic Apostille (e-Apostille) for use in other Apostille member states, or consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia for non-member states [3] [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Lump-sum funeral benefit and survivor pensions: Notify the Unified Social Service under the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs to terminate the deceased person's ongoing pension and claim the statutory one-time funeral grant (Thaghman npast) if the deceased was a state pensioner or insured worker [6] [7]. Eligible dependents - such as minor children, full-time students up to age 23, or qualifying surviving spouses and parents - may also apply through any territorial center of the Unified Social Service for a survivor labor pension or social benefit for the loss of a breadwinner [6] [7].
  • Mandatory funded pension inheritance: Under the Law on Funded Pensions available on the Armenian Legal Information System, accumulated mandatory pension fund units held in the deceased person's individual pension account at the Central Depository of Armenia are inheritable and may be claimed once the notarial inheritance certificate is issued [4] [6].
  • Banks, tax authorities, and identity records: Civil registration automatically updates the State Register of Population, but families should present the State Death Certificate directly to commercial banks in Armenia to freeze individual accounts and obtain balance statements as of the date of death [1] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession
steps.html:
• Strict 6-month statutory deadline to accept inheritance: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia (accessible via the Armenian Legal Information System), heirs by will or by law must formally accept the inheritance within 6 months from the date of death by filing a written declaration with a licensed notary operating under the oversight of the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia [3] [4].
  • Certificate of Right to Inheritance: After verifying the death certificate, kinship records, will searches, and asset certificates (including real estate extracts from the Cadastre Committee), the notary issues the official Certificate of Right to Inheritance (Zharangutyan iravunki vkayakan) once the 6-month period closes [3] [4]. Armenia does not levy a separate inheritance or estate tax on inherited property, though standard notarial tariffs and Cadastre state registration fees apply [4].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign powers of attorney: If an heir lives outside Armenia, they can execute a notarized Power of Attorney before the6-month deadline expires - either at an Armenian embassy or consulate under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia, or before a foreign notary with an Apostille and certified Armenian translation - authorizing a local representative in Armenia to accept the inheritance and register inherited property on their behalf [3, 4, 5].

titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Armenia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Armenia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Armenia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their care wishes and avoid administrative hurdles for the family. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Support, and State Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Outpatient mobile and inpatient palliative care: Under clinical protocols established by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Armenia, patients with progressive, life-limiting illnesses are eligible for specialized palliative medical care and maintenance services, delivered either through mobile home-visiting teams attached to local polyclinics or inpatient palliative units such as the V. A. Fanarjyan National Center of Oncology [1] [2].
  • Polyclinic referral and registration: To activate state-supported palliative care and regulated pain-relief prescriptions, the attending polyclinic specialist or oncologist records the clinical referral in the national ArMed electronic health system using the patient's passport/ID card and Public Services Number (PSN) [1] [2].
  • Basic Benefit Package (Petպatver) coverage: Patients who hold a certified disability status or qualify under targeted state-guaranteed medical care categories managed by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Armenia receive subsidized hospital and palliative services under the State Order (Petpatver), which can be supplemented by voluntary private health insurance policies [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Patient rights and informed consent: Under the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Medical Assistance and Service to the Population (published on the Armenian Legal Information System), every patient with decision-making capacity has the statutory right to give or refuse informed consent to medical intervention and to designate trusted individuals who may receive confidential clinical information [2] [3].
  • Designating a medical proxy and recording treatment wishes: While Armenian law does not establish a separate statutory living-will registry, your family member can sign a written consent and treatment preference statement in their hospital or polyclinic chart under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Armenia and execute a notarized mandate naming a trusted medical representative to communicate with physicians if they later lose the ability to speak for themselves [1, 2, 3].
  • Strictly prohibited interventions: Euthanasia and physician-assisted suicide are strictly prohibited under Armenian medical law, but patients retain the right to refuse disproportionate invasive procedures and to receive comprehensive pain and symptom relief [2] [3].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Liazoragir): Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, a Power of Attorney affecting property rights, state registries, social security representation, or banking transactions must be certified by a licensed notary operating under the oversight of the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia while the principal retains full mental and legal capacity [3] [4].
  • Home or hospital bedside notarization: If your family member is physically unable to visit a notary office due to serious illness but remains mentally lucid and capable of expressing their will, a notary registered with the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia can be scheduled to visit the hospital or home to verify capacity and execute the Liazoragir in person [4].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Because Armenian banks strictly verify the scope and validity period of powers of attorney, it is advisable to consider executing both a broad notarial Liazoragir and any bank-specific account mandate required by your family member's commercial bank while capacity is undisputed [3] [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability Assessment, Social Benefits, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• e-Disability functionality assessment: Apply through the Unified Social Service under the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs for a medico-social functionality assessment (Anzi funktsionalutyan gnahatum) based on the treating physician's electronic referral [5] [6]. A certified profound or severe functionality limitation entitles the ill person to a state disability pension or allowance, free or subsidized essential medicines, and state-guaranteed medical care [2, 5, 6].
  • Caregiver leave and social care programs: Employed family members who care for a seriously ill relative may request temporary incapacity/care leave certified by the treating medical institution or unpaid family leave under the Labor Code, and vulnerable seniors or persons with severe disabilities can apply through the Unified Social Service for home social-care support programs [5] [6].
  • Representing the beneficiary: If the ill person has executed a notarized Power of Attorney, their designated representative can submit benefit applications and manage pension disbursements at any territorial center of the Unified Social Service [4, 5, 6].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Notarized Will (Ktak) and mandatory shares: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia (available on the Armenian Legal Information System), a will (Ktak) must be executed in writing and certified by a notary under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia while the testator has full legal capacity [3] [4]. Note that minor children and disabled or retirement-age children, spouses, and parents of the testator remain entitled to a statutory mandatory share (Partadir bazhin) equal to at least half of what they would inherit by law [3].
  • Verifying civil status and Cadastre titles: Check that birth, marriage, and identity records held by the Civil Status Acts Registration Agency under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia match the ownership certificates registered with the Cadastre Committee, and review beneficiary records on bank deposits and funded pension accounts [3] [4].
  • Cross-border coordination: If designated representatives, family members, or assets are located outside Armenia, powers of attorney and civil documents can be authenticated with an electronic Apostille (e-Apostille) through the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Armenia or coordinated through consular services of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia [4] [7].

Handling medical death certification, civil registration, burial or international repatriation, survivor benefits, and notarial estate succession in the Republic of Azerbaijan requires coordinating with public healthcare institutions, civil registry offices at ASAN Service centers, social protection offices, and licensed notaries. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public or private hospital operating under the clinical standards of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Management Union of Medical Territorial Units (TABIB), the attending physician or hospital pathology unit records the death in the electronic health information system and issues the official Medical Certificate of Death (Ölüm haqqında tibbi şəhadətnamə) [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member dies at home from a documented natural illness, immediately contact the emergency medical service (103 or 113) and the local territorial polyclinic overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan so a physician can examine the body, verify natural causes, and register the electronic and paper Medical Certificate of Death [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death is sudden, occurs outside medical supervision, or involves any suspicion of external causes, the police and prosecutor's office must be notified immediately to inspect the scene and refer the body to the Public Legal Entity "Forensic Medical Expertise and Pathological Anatomy Association" under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan for a mandatory forensic autopsy before the medical death certificate is issued [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Status Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Family Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Cabinet of Ministers regulations, state registration of death is carried out by Civil Status Acts Registration (VVADQ) offices under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan, including desks inside regional ASAN Service (ASAN xidmət) centers and via the Electronic Government Portal [1] [3]. In practice, families register the death promptly once the medical certificate is issued so burial or transit permits can be completed without delay [1].
  • Required documents for registration: A family member or authorized representative must present: (a) the electronic or original Medical Certificate of Death issued by the medical facility, (b) the deceased person's national identity card (Şəxsiyyət vəsiqəsi) or passport (which is surrendered for official cancellation), and (c) the informant's own identity document [1] [3].
  • Official State Death Certificate: State registration of death and issuance of the official State Death Certificate (Ölüm haqqında şəhadətnamə) by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan are exempt from state duty [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial arrangements: Once the Civil Status Acts Registration office under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan issues the State Death Certificate (or the medical death certificate is verified in the electronic registry), the family presents it to the municipal cemetery administration (Bələdiyyə) to obtain a burial plot allocation and register the interment [1] [5].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported outside Azerbaijan, a licensed international funeral provider must obtain: (a) the official State Death Certificate from the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan [1] [3], (b) a sanitary-epidemiological and non-infectious disease permit and embalming certificate under the oversight of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan confirming that the body is hermetically sealed in a zinc-lined coffin [2], and (c) customs clearance plus consular transit documents from the destination country's embassy.
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Because Azerbaijan is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, public documents - look first at civil status certificates and notarial records issued under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan, or documents authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan depending on document category - must bear an official Apostille for recognition in other Convention states, or consular legalization for non-party states [3].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral allowance (Dəfn müavinəti): If the deceased was an insured employee, old-age or disability pensioner, or recipient of targeted social allowances, the person who undertook the funeral expenses may claim a statutory lump-sum funeral benefit from the State Social Protection Fund (Dövlət Sosial Müdafiə Fondu - DSMF) through any DOST (Dayanıqlı və Operativ Sosial Təminat) Center or ASAN Service center [1] [4].
  • Survivor pension for loss of breadwinner (Ailə başçısını itirməyə görə əmək pensiyası): Eligible surviving dependents - including minor children under age 18 (or up to age 23 if enrolled in full-time education), disabled dependents, and qualifying surviving spouses or parents of retirement age - can apply to the State Social Protection Fund for a survivor labor pension or social allowance [4] [5]. Since electronic civil death registration transmits data via the national e-government platform, many funeral grant and survivor benefit entitlements are initiated proactively, though families should verify bank payout details at a DOST Center [1] [4].
  • Commercial banks and tax obligations: Present the State Death Certificate to commercial banks in Azerbaijan so individual accounts and credit obligations are frozen pending notarial succession, and notify the State Tax Service if the deceased operated as an individual entrepreneur (Fərdi sahibkar) or held rental/business tax obligations [1] [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession
steps.html:
• Strict 6-month deadline to accept inheritance: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan, succession proceedings are administered by a licensed notary office (Notariat ofisi) operating under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan at the place where the inheritance opened (the deceased person's last permanent residence in Azerbaijan) [1] [3]. Heirs by will (Vəsiyyətnamə) or by law must formally accept the inheritance within 6 months from the date of death by filing a notarized declaration or taking actual possession of estate property [1] [3].
  • Certificate of Right to Inheritance: After the 6-month statutory period closes, the notary verifies kinship documents, checks the unified electronic register of wills, obtains real estate extracts from the State Service on Property Issues, and issues the official Certificate of Right to Inheritance (Miras hüququ haqqında şəhadətnamə) [1] [3]. Under the Tax Code of Azerbaijan, direct inheritance transfers to family members are exempt from personal income or inheritance tax, though statutory state duties and notarial fees apply when issuing the inheritance certificate and re-registering property titles [3] [5].
  • Cross-border heirs and foreign powers of attorney: If an heir resides outside Azerbaijan, they can execute a special Power of Attorney (Etibarnamə) before the 6-month deadline expires - either via the Electronic Notary (Mobil Notariat) system if they hold a valid Azerbaijani ID, at an Azerbaijani embassy or consulate under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan, or before a foreign notary with a Hague Apostille and certified Azerbaijani translation - authorizing a representative in Azerbaijan to open the succession file [1] [3].
