title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Azerbaijan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Azerbaijan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Azerbaijan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Azerbaijan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their care preferences and prevent administrative delays for the family. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Support, and Compulsory Health Insurance
steps.html:
• Oncological and palliative medical care: Under the Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan "On Protection of Public Health" and clinical programs overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Management Union of Medical Territorial Units (TABIB), patients with advanced oncological or life-limiting conditions receive specialized inpatient and outpatient symptom management through the National Center of Oncology and regional polyclinics [1] [2].
  • Compulsory Health Insurance (İcbari Tibbi Sığorta) coverage: Register and verify your family member's referral through their primary healthcare physician at the local polyclinic so hospital treatments, diagnostic procedures, and covered medications under the State Agency on Mandatory Health Insurance Benefit Package and state-funded oncology programs of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan are properly authorized [1] [2].
  • Regulated pain relief at home: For patients managed at home, the treating oncologist and local territorial polyclinic operating under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan issue specialized prescriptions and monitoring records for strong analgesics in accordance with national clinical protocols [2].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Patient rights and informed consent: Under the Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan "On Protection of Public Health," every patient who possesses decision-making capacity has the statutory right to receive comprehensive medical information, to give or refuse written informed consent to medical interventions, and to designate trusted family members or representatives who are authorized to receive confidential clinical updates [2] [3].
  • Written treatment preferences and medical representation: While Azerbaijani legislation does not maintain a standalone living-will registry, your family member can record signed treatment consent or refusal statements directly in their clinical chart overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan and execute a notarized Power of Attorney (Etibarnamə) under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan authorizing a trusted representative to access medical records and communicate with healthcare providers [1] [2] [3].
  • Statutory boundaries on end-of-life care: Active euthanasia and assisted suicide are strictly prohibited under Azerbaijani law, while comprehensive palliative pain management and the patient's right to decline disproportionate invasive procedures are protected [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Etibarnamə): Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Law "On Notary," any Power of Attorney authorizing representation before banks, real estate registries, tax offices, or social protection bodies must be certified by a licensed notary operating under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan while the principal retains full mental and legal capacity [1] [3].
  • Electronic Notary (Mobil Notariat) and bedside notarization: If your family member holds a valid Azerbaijani identification card, many standard administrative powers of attorney can be executed digitally via the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan Mobil Notariat application or the Electronic Government Portal [1] [3]. For broad property or financial powers of attorney when the ill person cannot travel due to serious illness, a licensed notary can be requested to visit the hospital or residence in person to verify mental capacity and certify the instrument at the bedside [1] [3].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Because Azerbaijani commercial banks strictly scrutinize general powers of attorney for account withdrawals and transfers, it is advisable to verify whether your family member's bank requires specific account-operation clauses in the notarial Etibarnamə or an in-bank mandate executed while capacity is undisputed [1] [5].

steps.title: Activate Disability Assessment, Social Allowances, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Electronic disability assessment (TSİ): Ask the treating medical institution under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan to submit an electronic medical-social referral (Forma 88) so the State Medical-Social Expertise and Rehabilitation Agency can evaluate the degree of impairment of body functions [1] [2] [4].
  • Disability pensions and first-degree care allowance: When a severe functional impairment ( historically Group I disability / 81-100% impairment of body functions) is certified, the ill person becomes eligible for a labor disability pension or social disability benefit administered by the State Social Protection Fund through any DOST (Dayanıqlı və Operativ Sosial Təminat) Center or ASAN Service center [1] [4] [5]. In addition, a statutory monthly presidential care allowance is available for individuals providing direct care to a person with an 81-100% functional impairment [4] [5].
  • Workplace caregiver protections: Under the Labor Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan, employed family members caring for a seriously ill relative certified by a medical institution may request statutory short-term unpaid family leave or flexible work arrangements, as well as temporary incapacity certificates when applicable [4].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Notarized Will (Vəsiyyətnamə) and mandatory inheritance shares: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan, a will must be executed in writing and certified by a notary under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan while the testator has full legal capacity [1] [3]. Keep in mind that the testator's children, parents, and spouse remain protected by statutory mandatory share (Məcburi pay) rules under the Civil Code, entitling them to half of the share they would have received under intestate succession regardless of the will's terms [3].
  • Organizing civil status and property titles: Verify via the Electronic Government Portal that birth and marriage certificates held by the Civil Status Acts Registration offices under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan match the ownership extracts (Çıxarış) recorded with the State Service on Property Issues, and review beneficiary records on bank deposits and insurance policies [1] [3] [5].
  • Cross-border powers of attorney and Apostille authentication: If a designated representative, family member, or asset is located outside Azerbaijan, powers of attorney and civil documents can be authenticated with a 1961 Hague Convention Apostille through the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Azerbaijan (for judicial and notarial acts) or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan (for designated administrative documents and consular services) [3].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bangladesh: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bangladesh: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Bangladesh: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Bangladesh, the legal and administrative procedures follow a structured sequence across medical authorities, local government civil registries, municipal burial or cremation management, financial institutions, and the civil courts. Below, we set out the five official steps in chronological order so your family can handle each requirement clearly.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Forensic Clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public medical college hospital, district hospital, or licensed private clinic under the supervision of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the attending registered physician issues a formal Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) [1]. Before leaving the hospital, verify that the deceased's full legal name, National Identity Card (NID) or passport number, age, and exact time and cause of death match official identity records [1, 2].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home without a doctor present, obtain a written death attestation from a registered physician who treated the deceased or notify the local City Corporation ward councillor, Pourashava (municipality) councillor, or Union Parishad member, who can issue a local death verification slip required for civil registration [2, 3].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death is unexpected, accidental, or unattended by a physician, notify the local police station (thana) immediately. Under the Code of Criminal Procedure, police prepare a formal inquest report (surathal) and transfer the body to a government hospital mortuary under the Directorate General of Health Services for a medico-legal post-mortem examination before issuing a police burial or cremation clearance certificate [1].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry (BDRIS)
steps.html:
• Statutory 45-day deadline: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act, 2004, every death in Bangladesh must be reported to the local Registrar within 45 days of the date of death [2]. Registration within 45 days is free of charge; late registration after 45 days requires a late fee and supporting explanation [2].
  • Where and how to register: Applications are submitted through the Birth and Death Registration Information System (BDRIS), managed by the Office of the Registrar General, Birth and Death Registration, and processed locally at the relevant City Corporation zone office, Pourashava, Union Parishad, or Cantonment Board where the death occurred or where the deceased resided [2, 3].
  • Required documents and bilingual certificates: Submit the hospital MCCD (or graveyard/crematorium receipt or ward councillor attestation), a copy of the deceased's Birth Registration Certificate or NID, Holding Tax payment receipt as proof of address, and the informant's NID and mobile number [2, 3]. Request the official Death Certificate issued in both Bengali and English from the Office of the Registrar General, Birth and Death Registration so it can be used seamlessly across banks, courts, and foreign authorities [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: In urban areas (such as Dhaka North, Dhaka South, or Chattogram City Corporations) and Pourashavas, present the hospital MCCD and the deceased's NID to the municipal graveyard (gorosthan) or crematorium (shoshan) authority to obtain a burial or cremation receipt [2, 3]. Retain this official receipt carefully, as BDRIS registrars require it if civil registration is completed after the funeral [3].
  • International repatriation of human remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or if the remains must be transported abroad, coordinate through a licensed international funeral director and the relevant embassy in Dhaka. International air cargo repatriation requires an official MCCD, a BDRIS English Death Certificate, a formal embalming certificate and coffin sealing certificate from an authorized hospital mortuary under the Directorate General of Health Services, a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the local police and Ministry of Home Affairs, and customs/port health clearance at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport [1, 3, 6].
  • Document legalization and Apostille: When Bangladeshi death or succession documents must be presented abroad, have them verified and attested (or Apostilled) through the Consular and Welfare Wing of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka [6].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Social Welfare, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Social safety net and welfare allowances: If the deceased received an Old Age Allowance, Disability Allowance, or other public benefit, notify the local Upazila or Urban Social Services Office under the Department of Social Services [4]. Where the deceased leaves behind an eligible surviving spouse in financial need, inquire with the Department of Social Services about the Widow and Destitute Women Allowance or family welfare grants [4].
  • Pensions, benevolent funds, and employment benefits: If the deceased was a civil servant, contact the Chief Accounts and Finance Officer (CAFO) and the Bangladesh Employees Welfare Board to claim the lump-sum burial grant, benevolent fund grant, gratuity, and family pension. If the deceased was enrolled in the Universal Pension Scheme, notify the National Pension Authority, and for private-sector employees, submit the death certificate to the employer's HR department to claim group life insurance and Provident Fund balances [3, 4].
  • Banking and tax closure: Present the official BDRIS Death Certificate to all banks, Mobile Financial Services (such as bKash or Nagad), and the Directorate of National Savings (for Sanchayapatra savings certificates) to freeze sole accounts and verify whether valid nominee (nominee) designations are on file [3, 5]. A legal representative must also file the deceased's final income tax return with the National Board of Revenue (NBR).

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession Certificate, or Probate
steps.html:
• Personal law and municipal Warishan Certificate: In Bangladesh, inheritance distribution follows the deceased's personal religion-based law (Muslim Personal Law / Faraid, Hindu Law, or Christian/general rules under the Succession Act, 1925) [5]. As a first step, obtain a Relationship / Legal Heir Certificate (Warishan Certificate) signed by the City Corporation Mayor/Ward Councillor, Pourashava Mayor, or Union Parishad Chairman listing all surviving legal heirs [5].
  • Court Succession Certificate for movable assets: While banks and savings authorities may release certain balances to a registered nominee as trustee for the legal heirs, releasing unnominated bank accounts, shares, or financial securities requires a formal Succession Certificate issued by the competent Joint District Judge Court (under the supervision of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh) pursuant to Part X of the Succession Act, 1925 [5].
  • Probate, Letters of Administration, and land mutation: If the deceased left a valid Will (or if full estate administration is required), petition the District Court for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration under the Succession Act, 1925, paying the applicable ad valorem court fee (Bangladesh imposes no separate standalone inheritance tax, though court fees and land transfer fees apply) [5]. To transfer real estate (namjari / mutation), submit the BDRIS Death Certificate, Warishan Certificate, title deeds, and any registered Partition Deed (Bontonnama) to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) office [3, 5]. Heirs residing abroad can execute a Power of Attorney attested by a Bangladesh Embassy or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs so a local representative can complete court and land mutation filings on their behalf [6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor these steps to your situation, did the death occur in a hospital or at home in Bangladesh, and did your family member leave bank accounts, savings certificates (Sanchayapatra), or land that will require a court Succession Certificate or land mutation?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bangladesh: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bangladesh: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Bangladesh: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Bangladesh is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, taking early, structured action while your family member still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps secure symptom relief, protect financial and property management, and prevent complex court bottlenecks later. Below, we outline the five key medical, legal, and administrative steps in order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialized public palliative care centers: In Bangladesh, tertiary specialist care is anchored by the Department of Palliative Medicine at Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University (BSMMU) in Dhaka, as well as oncology and palliative care units within government medical college hospitals overseen by the Directorate General of Health Services [1] [2]. Ask your family member's treating specialist for a formal palliative care referral and an updated clinical summary detailing diagnosis, pain-management regimens, and home care needs [1] [2].
  • Home-based nursing and symptom control: Both Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University and accredited community hospices and home-care nursing providers in major cities offer outpatient symptom management and home visits for housebound patients [1] [2]. Confirm that opioid analgesics (such as oral morphine) are prescribed by an authorized specialist with proper hospital documentation [1] [2].
  • Public and private health coverage: Public hospital inpatient and outpatient consultations under the Directorate General of Health Services are heavily subsidized, while private hospital admissions or critical-illness insurance claims require pre-authorization, diagnostic histopathology or imaging reports, and an itemized physician treatment plan [1].

steps.title: Record Treatment Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Legal status of advance directives in Bangladesh: Bangladesh does not currently have a standalone statutory Living Will Act. Instead, medical treatment decisions are governed by general principles of informed consent and clinical ethics administered under the Directorate General of Health Services and the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC) [1].
  • Documenting care preferences while capacity is intact: While your family member has full mental capacity, it is advisable to consider preparing a written, signed, and witnessed statement of medical treatment preferences (covering intensive care admission, mechanical ventilation, resuscitation, and preferred place of care) and placing a copy directly in the hospital medical file at Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University or the treating hospital [1] [2].
  • Designating a primary family medical spokesperson: In Bangladeshi hospital practice, attending physicians consult the designated next-of-kin or family representative recorded on the hospital admission and consent forms when a patient becomes unable to communicate [1]. Explicitly name one primary family decision-maker (and an alternate) on the hospital's official consent record so clinical teams have a single, unambiguous point of contact [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Why acting before incapacity is critical: Under Bangladeshi law, a person must be of sound mind to execute a valid Power of Attorney (Am-Mukhtarnama or Khas-Mukhtarnama) [3]. Obtain a dated medical certificate of mental capacity from the attending specialist at the time of signing to protect the document against any future challenge [1] [3].
  • General and Special Powers of Attorney: Governed by the Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882 and the Power of Attorney Act, 2012 (alongside the Power of Attorney Rules, 2015), a Special Power of Attorney authorizes specific administrative or financial acts, while a General Power of Attorney authorizes broader management [3] [6]. Any Power of Attorney involving immovable property (land or apartments) must be executed on prescribed stamp paper and compulsorily registered before the local Sub-Registrar Office (where the Sub-Registrar can also be requested on commission to visit a housebound patient at home or in hospital) [3].
  • Cross-border powers of attorney and bank operating mandates: If a family member or co-owner lives abroad, a Power of Attorney signed outside Bangladesh must be attested by the relevant Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission and verified by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka within the statutory timeframe [6]. For bank accounts and Sanchayapatra savings certificates, accompany the ill person (or arrange a home branch visit) to submit the bank's specific mandate form or convert accounts to "Either or Survivor" joint operation while ensuring all beneficiary (nominee) forms are updated [3].

steps.title: Activate Critical-Illness Grants, Disability Allowances, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• One-time medical financial grant for serious illness: The Department of Social Services (under the Ministry of Social Welfare) administers a statutory one-time financial assistance grant (typically BDT 50,000) for patients diagnosed with six specified life-threatening conditions: cancer, kidney disease, liver cirrhosis, stroke-induced paralysis, congenital heart disease, and thalassemia [4]. Applications are submitted through the local Upazila or Urban Social Services Office with specialist medical certification and the patient's National Identity Card (NID) [4].
  • Disability identification and allowances: If the illness causes severe physical impairment, register your family member under the Disability Identification Survey managed by the Department of Social Services (Suborno Nagorik card) to access the Disability Allowance and public hospital priority services [4].
  • Employment leave and benevolent fund support: For public-sector employees, the Bangladesh Employees Welfare Board provides medical grants from the Benevolent Fund, and civil service rules permit extended medical leave on medical board certification. Private-sector workers and family caregivers must coordinate medical or casual leave directly with their employer's HR department.

steps.title: Organize Wills, Personal Law Estate Rules, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Verify identity and civil registry consistency: Check that your family member's name, date of birth, and parents' names are spelled identically across their National Identity Card (NID), passport, Birth Registration Certificate, bank records, and land title deeds (khatian and dalil), correcting any discrepancy now while the person can sign applications [5].
  • Wills and personal law limits under the Succession Act, 1925: Inheritance and testamentary rules in Bangladesh depend on the person's religious personal law alongside the Succession Act, 1925 [5]. Under Sunni Muslim personal law, a testator may bequeath up to one-third (1/3) of the net estate by Will (Wasiyat) without the consent of legal heirs, whereas bequests exceeding one-third or made to an existing legal heir require the post-transfer consent of the other legal heirs; by contrast, lifetime gifts (Heba or Heba-bil-Ewaj) registered at the Sub-Registrar Office take effect immediately during the donor's lifetime [5]. Under Hindu, Christian, or general rules governed by the Succession Act, 1925, verify formal attestation requirements (signed by the testator in the presence of at least two witnesses) [5].
  • Organize an accessible master folder of assets: Compile original land deeds, mutation (namjari) records,latest Holding Tax receipts, bank account details, Sanchayapatra certificates, and insurance policies, and coordinate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation rules if foreign assets or overseas family members are involved [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Bhutan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Bhutan, the official procedures follow a clear sequence across medical authorities, Gewog or Thromde civil registration offices, municipal cremation or burial management, national pension and insurance bodies, and the courts. Below, we set out the five main steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Forensic Clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital (JDWNRH) in Thimphu, the regional referral hospitals in Mongar or Gelephu, or any Dzongkhag (district) hospital under the Ministry of Health, the attending medical officer issues an official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) and a hospital death notification slip [1] [5]. Before leaving the hospital, verify that the deceased's full name, Citizen Identity Card (CID) number or passport number, date of birth, and time of death match official civil records [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home in a rural Gewog or urban Thromde, notify the nearest Basic Health Unit (BHU) or district hospital under the Ministry of Health so a health official can verify the death, and inform the local Tshogpa (village representative) and Gup (Gewog head) to obtain the local administration attestation required for civil registration [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death is sudden, accidental, or unattended by a medical professional, report it immediately to the nearest Royal Bhutan Police (RBP) station. Police officers conduct an inquest and coordinate with forensic medical staff under the Ministry of Health for a medico-legal examination before issuing official clearance to release the body [1] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and 30-day statutory deadline: Under Bhutan's Civil Registration and Census Rules and Regulations, every death must be registered with the Department of Civil Registration and Census (under the Ministry of Home Affairs) through the deceased's permanent Gewog administration or Thromde civil registration office within 30 days of the date of death [2].
  • Late registration rules: Registration within 30 days is routine; if reported between 30 days and one year after death, the application requires verification by the Dzongkhag or Thromde Civil Registration and Census Committee, while reports submitted after one year require direct approval from the Department of Civil Registration and Census [2].
  • Required documents and official certificates: Submit the hospital Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Basic Health Unit and Gup/Tshogpa verification for a home death), the deceased's original Citizen Identity Card (CID), household census details, and the informant's CID [2]. Once recorded in the Bhutan Civil Registration System (BCRS) or through the G2C Citizen Services portal, obtain certified copies of the official Death Certificate and census update from the Department of Civil Registration and Census [2].

steps.title: Arrange Cremation, Burial, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local cremation or burial permits: In Bhutan, cremation at a designated public crematorium (ro-khang) is the most common practice, scheduled in accordance with traditional Buddhist astrological calculation (tsi) or Hindu funeral rites in southern Dzongkhags. Present the hospital death slip or official Death Certificate to the Thromde or Dzongkhag municipal office managing the crematorium or burial ground to book the facility and obtain the cremation or burial permit [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or if the remains must be repatriated outside Bhutan, coordinate through the relevant foreign embassy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade, and the Ministry of Health [1] [6]. International transport via Paro International Airport requires an official Death Certificate, an embalming and hermetic coffin-sealing certificate, a non-infectious disease public health clearance from the Ministry of Health, police and immigration exit clearance, and consular authorization from the destination country [1] [6].
  • Document legalization for cross-border use: Bhutan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consequently, Bhutanese death certificates and court succession orders intended for use abroad must be authenticated by the Notary Public of the Royal Court of Justice and legalized by the Consular Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade before diplomatic attestation by the destination country's mission [3] [6].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Insurance, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• National Pension and Provident Fund claims: If your family member was a civil servant, armed forces member, or corporate employee contributing to the National Pension and Provident Fund, surviving family members or nominated beneficiaries should file for the statutory funeral grant, family/survivor pension, and accumulated provident fund balance with the National Pension and Provident Fund [4]. Required documents include the Death Certificate, deceased's CID, nominee's CID, marriage or relationship verification, and bank account details [4].
  • Rural Life Insurance and Group Insurance Scheme: Bhutanese citizens registered in the household census are covered under the Rural Life Insurance Scheme (Semso) administered through the Royal Insurance Corporation of Bhutan (RICB), and public employees are additionally covered under the Group Insurance Scheme (GIS) [2] [4]. Claims are submitted through the Gewog Gup or Thromde office and the nearest RICB branch with the official Death Certificate and census record [2] [4].
  • Banking, tax, and identity closure: Present the Death Certificate and court or nominee documentation to Bhutanese banks (such as Bank of Bhutan, Bhutan National Bank, or Druk PNB) to freeze sole accounts and process nominee releases, and notify the Department of Revenue and Customs if the deceased held a registered business or Personal Income Tax (PIT) account [3] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Land Mutation
steps.html:
• Governing succession law and court probate: Estate succession in Bhutan is governed by the Inheritance Act of Bhutan 1980, the Land Act of Bhutan 2007, and the Civil and Criminal Procedure Code, overseen by the Royal Court of Justice through the local Dzongkhag Court or Dungkhag Court [3].
  • Wills (Kachem) and intestate family agreements: If the deceased left a valid written or registered Will (Kachem), or if the surviving legal heirs execute a mutually agreed family partition deed, the instrument is presented to the Dzongkhag Court or Dungkhag Court under the Royal Court of Justice for verification and issuance of a succession order [3]. Where heirs cannot agree or where bank or corporate assets lack a registered nominee, the Dzongkhag Court adjudicates the distribution among the surviving spouse, children, or statutory heirs under the Inheritance Act of Bhutan 1980 [3].
  • Land (Thram) transfer, tax rules, and foreign heirs: To transfer land or real property (Thram inheritance mutation), submit the Death Certificate, census record, family consensus or court order from the Royal Court of Justice, and land ownership records through the Gewog or Thromde land sector to the National Land Commission, which observes a statutory 30-day public notice period before updating the Thram [2] [3]. Bhutan does not levy a standalone inheritance tax or estate duty, though standard land transfer and court registration fees apply [3]. If an heir lives abroad, they may execute a Power of Attorney legalized through a Bhutanese Embassy or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade so a representative in Bhutan can sign court and Thram transfer filings [3] [6].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical certification of deathImmediately upon deathMinistry of Health / JDWNRH or District Hospital [1]
2. Civil death registrationWithin 30 days of deathDepartment of Civil Registration and Census (Gewog / Thromde) [2]
3. Cremation, burial, or repatriationBefore funeral or export of remainsThromde / Dzongkhag Administration & Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade [1] [6]
4. Pension and insurance benefitsPromptly after obtaining Death CertificateNational Pension and Provident Fund & RICB [4]
5. Estate probate and Thram land transferWithin statutory notice period for land mutationRoyal Court of Justice (Dzongkhag Court) & National Land Commission [3]

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Bhutan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Bhutan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking structured medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps ensure comfortable symptom control, valid financial representation, and clear property arrangements. Below, we set out the five key steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialized palliative care and home visits: Under Article 9 of the Constitution of the Kingdom of Bhutan, the state provides free access to basic public health services across both modern allopathic and traditional medicine (Sowa Rigpa) overseen by the Ministry of Health [1] [5]. Specialized inpatient and outpatient palliative care, oncology symptom control, and home-based palliative nursing visits in Thimphu are anchored by the Palliative Care Unit at Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital (JDWNRH), while regional referral hospitals in Mongar and Gelephu and district hospitals coordinate pain management and home support in the Dzongkhags [1] [5].
  • Opioid pain relief and clinical referrals: Ask the treating specialist at Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital or the district hospital for a formal palliative care plan, including prescribed pain-relief medications (such as oral morphine) and home-care nursing coordination [1] [5].
  • Government medical referrals abroad: If the ill person requires specialized tertiary treatment not available in Bhutan, the Medical Referral Committee under the Ministry of Health reviews eligibility for state-funded referral and patient escort support to empaneled referral hospitals in India [1].

steps.title: Record Treatment Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Legal status of advance healthcare directives: Bhutan does not currently have a standalone statutory Living Will Act. Clinical decision-making and end-of-life care are governed by medical ethics and patient-consent standards administered under the Ministry of Health and the Bhutan Medical and Health Council [1] [5].
  • Documenting medical preferences while capacity is intact: While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, it is advisable to prepare a clear written statement of treatment preferences covering intensive care interventions, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, artificial life support, and preferred place of care (hospital vs. home), signed by the ill person and placed directly in their medical chart at Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital or the treating district hospital [1] [5].
  • Designating a primary family medical representative: In Bhutanese hospital practice, physicians rely on the designated next-of-kin or patient attendant recorded on the hospital admission and consent forms when a patient can no longer communicate [1]. Explicitly record one primary family spokesperson (and a backup representative) with the hospital care team so doctors have clear authority for clinical consultations [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Court-verified Power of Attorney: Under the Evidence Act of Bhutan 2005 and the Civil and Criminal Procedure Code of Bhutan, a Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted relative to manage finances, land filings, or administrative matters is only valid if executed while the principal is of sound mind [3]. Obtain a dated medical certificate from the attending physician confirming mental capacity on the date of execution [1] [3].
  • Execution and registration before the court: Prepare the Power of Attorney on official legal stamp paper (Chetham), have it signed or thumb-printed by the ill person in the presence of competent witnesses, and register or notarize it before the Notary Public division of the local Dzongkhag Court or Dungkhag Court under the Royal Court of Justice [3]. For housebound or hospitalized patients, request guidance from the court registry on hospital or home verification procedures [3].
  • Bank account mandates and cross-border powers of attorney: Contact the ill person's commercial banks in Bhutan (such as Bank of Bhutan, Bhutan National Bank, or T Bank) to update operating mandates, convert individual accounts to joint "Either or Survivor" operation if appropriate, and verify registered account nominees [3] [4]. If a representative or family co-owner resides outside Bhutan, any Power of Attorney executed abroad must be authenticated through a Bhutanese Embassy or the Consular Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade [6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Pension Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• National Pension and Provident Fund invalidity benefits: If your family member is an active member of the National Pension and Provident Fund (covering civil servants, armed forces, and state/corporate employees) and becomes permanently incapacitated for work due to serious illness, they may apply for permanent invalidity pension benefits or provident fund withdrawals supported by a Medical Board certificate issued under the Ministry of Health [1] [4].
  • Caregiver and medical leave entitlements: Under the Bhutan Civil Service Rules and Regulations (BCSR) and the Labour and Employment Act of Bhutan 2007, employed patients and family caregivers can apply for paid medical leave, maternity/paternity or family care leave, and medical escort leave when accompanying a referred patient [1] [4].
  • Insurance and welfare support: Review active life or critical-illness policies with the Royal Insurance Corporation of Bhutan (RICB) or Bhutan Insurance Limited, and if the family faces severe financial hardship due to protracted terminal illness, consult the local Gup or Dzongkhag administration regarding social welfare support [2] [4].

steps.title: Organize Wills, Beneficiary Designations, and Civil and Land Records
steps.html:
• Verify civil registry and Citizen Identity Card records: Confirm that your family member's name, date of birth, and household relationships are accurately recorded in the Bhutan Civil Registration System managed by the Department of Civil Registration and Census, resolving any spelling or census discrepancies while the person can still authorize corrections [2].
  • Executing a valid Will (Kachem) under the Inheritance Act of Bhutan 1980: Under the Inheritance Act of Bhutan 1980, a person of sound mind may execute a written Will (Kachem) specifying how their movable assets and real property (Thram land and houses) should be distributed [3]. To prevent future disputes among heirs, the Kachem should be drafted clearly, affixed with a legal stamp (Chetham), signed by the testator and witnesses, and registered with the Dzongkhag Court under the Royal Court of Justice [3].
  • Updating pension nominees and land (Thram) documentation: Ensure that beneficiary (nominee) forms are up to date with the National Pension and Provident Fund, the Royal Insurance Corporation of Bhutan Group Insurance Scheme, and commercial banks [4]. Gather original Thram land certificates, tax receipts, and loan clearance records, and coordinate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade if any assets or heirs are located outside Bhutan [3] [6].

3. Court-notarized Power of Attorney & bank mandatesBefore any loss of legal capacityRoyal Court of Justice (Dzongkhag Court Notary) & Banks [3]
4. Invalidity pension and caregiver leave claimsUpon Medical Board certificationNational Pension and Provident Fund & Employer HR [4]
5. Will (Kachem), nominees, and census checkWhile capacity is intactRoyal Court of Justice & Department of Civil Registration and Census [2] [3]

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Brunei: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Brunei Darussalam, the legal and practical procedures follow a clear statutory sequence across the public hospital system, the national civil registry, religious or municipal burial authorities, the national provident fund, and the Civil and Syariah Courts. Below, we set out the five main steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death or Coroner Clearance
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at Raja Isteri Pengiran Anak Saleha (RIPAS) Hospital in Bandar Seri Begawan, the district hospitals in Kuala Belait, Tutong, or Temburong, or a specialist center overseen by the Ministry of Health, the attending medical officer examines the deceased, updates the national Bru-HIMS electronic record, and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [5]. Before leaving the hospital, verify that the deceased's full legal name, Smart Identity Card (IC) number or passport number, and time of death match official identity records [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home, notify the Royal Brunei Police Force (RBPF) and emergency medical services immediately. Police officers and medical personnel inspect the scene and transport the deceased to the nearest government hospital mortuary under the Ministry of Health so a government medical officer can confirm the cause of death [1] [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under the Inquests Act (Chapter 6) and the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Chapter 79), any unnatural, sudden, or unattended death is referred by the Royal Brunei Police Force to the Coroner's Court (under the State Judiciary Department) and the Forensic Pathology Unit at RIPAS Hospital [1] [3]. The Coroner authorizes a medico-legal post-mortem examination if required and issues a Coroner's Order for Burial before civil registration and release of the body can proceed [1] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Within 24 Hours
steps.html:
• Competent authority and 24-hour statutory deadline: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Chapter 79), every death in Brunei Darussalam must be reported within 24 hours of the death (and before burial takes place) to a Deputy Registrar of Births and Deaths under the Department of Immigration and National Registration (Jabatan Imigresen dan Pendaftaran Kebangsaan - JIPK, Ministry of Home Affairs) [2]. Registration counters operate at the Department of Immigration and National Registration headquarters and district branches, at government hospital registration units (including RIPAS Hospital), and at designated police stations [1] [2].
  • Required documents for registration: A surviving family member or authorized informant must present: (a) the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death issued under the Ministry of Health (or the Coroner's Order), (b) the deceased's original Smart Identity Card (yellow for citizens, purple for permanent residents, or green for foreign residents), birth certificate, passport, and marriage certificate (if applicable), and (c) the informant's original Smart Identity Card [1] [2].
  • Burial Permit and Death Certificate: Upon registration, the Deputy Registrar records cancellation of the deceased's Smart Identity Card and issues two official documents: the statutory Burial Permit (Sijil Kebenaran Mengebumikan Mayat) required to proceed with the funeral, and the official Death Certificate (Sijil Kematian) [2]. Request several certified copies of the Death Certificate for pension, banking, and probate filings [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local Muslim and non-Muslim funeral arrangements: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act (Chapter 79), no body may be buried or disposed of without the official Burial Permit [2]. For Muslim decedents, families coordinate ritual washing, shrouding, jenazah prayers, and prompt burial at a gazetted Muslim cemetery through the hospital Pengurusan Jenazah unit and the Ministry of Religious Affairs. For non-Muslim decedents, families engage a licensed funeral director to coordinate mortuary preparation and burial or cremation with the relevant district municipal or community cemetery.
  • International repatriation of human remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported outside Brunei Darussalam via Brunei International Airport, the funeral director must obtain: (a) the official Death Certificate and passport cancellation from the Department of Immigration and National Registration [2], (b) an Export Permit for Human Remains, a Non-Infectious Disease Certificate, and an Embalming and Hermetic Coffin Sealing Certificate from the Port Health and Environmental Health divisions of the Ministry of Health [1] [5], (c) police clearance and Royal Brunei Customs export clearance, and (d) consular clearance from the destination country's embassy or high commission in Bandar Seri Begawan [6].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Because Brunei Darussalam is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Bruneian Death Certificates and court probate grants intended for use in another Apostille convention country can be authenticated with an official Apostille issued through the Supreme Court Registry under the State Judiciary Department [3]. For countries outside the Apostille Convention, documents require consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [6].

steps.title: Notify Pension (TAP / SPK), Social Welfare, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Employees Trust Fund (Tabung Amanah Pekerja) and SPK claims: If the deceased was a citizen or permanent resident employed in the public or private sector, surviving nominated beneficiaries or next-of-kin should notify the Employees Trust Fund (Tabung Amanah Pekerja) to claim accumulated balances and survivor/death benefits under the Employees Trust Fund (TAP), Supplemental Contributory Pensions (SCP), or the National Retirement Scheme (Skim Persaraan Kebangsaan - SPK) [4]. Submit the official Death Certificate, the deceased's and claimants' Smart Identity Cards, marriage or birth certificates proving relationship, and bank account documentation [4].
  • Old Age Pension and social welfare notifications: If the deceased received the universal Old Age Pension (Pencen Umur Tua) or Disability Allowance under the Old Age and Disability Pensions Act (Chapter 18), notify the Department of Community Development (Jabatan Pembangunan Masyarakat - JAPEM, under the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports) immediately to stop monthly payments and inquire about statutory funeral assistance or widow and orphan welfare support [4]. For public servants, also notify the Public Service Department and Treasury Department regarding death-in-service gratuity or derivative pension entitlements [4].
  • Banks and financial institutions: Present the certified Death Certificate to all Bruneian banks (such as Baiduri Bank, Bank Islam Brunei Darussalam - BIBD, or Standard Chartered Bank) and Takaful or insurance providers. Individual bank accounts are frozen upon notification of death and released only upon presentation of a formal court Grant of Probate, Letters of Administration, or small-estate order from the State Judiciary Department [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Syariah (*Faraid*) Succession
steps.html:
• Probate and Letters of Administration under Chapter 11: Estate administration in Brunei Darussalam is governed by the Probate and Administration Act (Chapter 11) and overseen by the Probate Registry of the Supreme Court under the State Judiciary Department [3]. The executor named in a Will petitions for a Grant of Probate, while the next-of-kin of an intestate deceased petitions for Letters of Administration (or summary administration through the Probate Officer for smaller estates), submitting the Death Certificate, a complete Schedule of Assets and Liabilities, and sureties where required [3].
  • Muslim estates (Faraid) vs. non-Muslim estates: For Muslim decedents, while the Civil Probate Registry under the State Judiciary Department issues the Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration needed to collect bank balances and transfer property titles, the distribution shares among surviving legal heirs are governed by Islamic inheritance law (Faraid) [3]. The family or administrator must obtain an official Faraid Certificate (Sijil Faraid) from the Syariah Subordinate Court or Syariah High Court (within the State Judiciary Department) verifying each legal heir's statutory fraction, and any Islamic Will (Wasiat) is limited to one-third (1/3) of the net estate unless all Faraid heirs consent [3]. For non-Muslim decedents, testamentary and intestate succession are governed by the Wills Act (Chapter 193) and the Probate and Administration Act (Chapter 11) [3].
  • Estate duty abolition, land transfer, and foreign heirs: Brunei Darussalam abolished statutory estate duty for deaths occurring on or after 1 January 2014, so beneficiaries pay only court probate filing fees and Land Department registration fees when transferring land titles (EDR / Land Code filings) [3]. If an executor or heir resides abroad, a foreign Grant of Probate from a Commonwealth jurisdiction may be resealed by the High Court under the Probate and Administration Act (Chapter 11), or a foreign heir may execute a Power of Attorney (authenticated with an Apostille or through a Brunei diplomatic mission under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs) authorizing a local representative in Brunei [3] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Brunei: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Brunei: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Brunei Darussalam is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking early, structured steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps coordinate specialist palliative care, establish valid financial powers of attorney, access statutory disability and retirement benefits, and organize personal-law succession documents. Below, we set out the five key steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public palliative care and specialist oncology centers: In Brunei Darussalam, citizens and permanent residents receive heavily subsidized public healthcare overseen by the Ministry of Health and tracked through the national Bru-HIMS electronic medical record system [1] [5]. Specialized inpatient and outpatient palliative care is delivered through the Palliative Care Unit at Raja Isteri Pengiran Anak Saleha (RIPAS) Hospital in Bandar Seri Begawan and The Brunei Cancer Centre (TBCC) at Pantai Jerudong Specialist Centre, alongside district hospitals in Kuala Belait, Tutong, and Temburong [1] [5].
  • Home-based nursing and symptom control: Ask the treating specialist under the Ministry of Health for a formal referral to the Palliative Care Service and the Home Based Nursing Division, which provides home nursing visits, wound and catheter care, medical equipment loan support, and supervised opioid pain management for housebound patients across all four districts [1] [5].
  • Private insurance and foreign residents: If your family member holds a green Smart Identity Card (foreign resident) or private critical-illness insurance, request a detailed clinical summary, histopathology report, and itemized treatment plan from the attending consultant to secure pre-authorization for inpatient or palliative care [1] [5].

steps.title: Record Treatment Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Legal status of advance directives in Brunei Darussalam: Brunei Darussalam does not currently enact a standalone statutory Advance Medical Directive or Living Will Act. Instead, end-of-life clinical decisions are governed by medical ethics, informed consent principles, and clinical guidelines administered by the Ministry of Health and the Brunei Medical Board [1] [5].
  • Recording care preferences in Bru-HIMS while capacity is intact: While the ill person retains full decision-making capacity, it is advisable to discuss goals of care directly with the attending specialist and palliative care team (covering cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, intensive care admission, and preferred place of care) so these preferences are documented clearly in the patient's Bru-HIMS clinical record at the Ministry of Health [1] [5].
  • Designating a primary family spokesperson: In Bruneian hospital practice, physicians consult the primary next-of-kin or designated family caregiver listed in the hospital admission and Bru-HIMS record if the patient loses the ability to communicate [1]. Explicitly name one primary family medical contact (and a secondary contact) so the clinical team has an unambiguous representative [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Statutory Powers of Attorney under Chapter 13: Under the Powers of Attorney Act (Chapter 13), a donor can only execute a valid Power of Attorney while possessing full mental capacity [3]. Obtain a dated medical certificate from the attending physician at the Ministry of Health confirming that your family member is of sound mind on the date the instrument is signed [1] [3].
  • Execution and Supreme Court registration: To ensure the Power of Attorney is accepted by government land registries, banks, and courts, have it drafted by an Advocate and Solicitor, signed by the donor in the presence of a Commissioner for Oaths, Magistrate, or Notary Public, and deposited for registration in the Registry of the Supreme Court under the State Judiciary Department pursuant to the Powers of Attorney Act (Chapter 13) [3].
  • Bank account mandates and cross-border authentication: Contact your family member's commercial banks in Brunei Darussalam (such as Bank Islam Brunei Darussalam - BIBD, Baiduri Bank, or Standard Chartered Bank) while capacity is intact to review signing mandates or arrange a hospital/home visit by bank officers [3]. Because Brunei Darussalam is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, any Power of Attorney executed for use abroad (or executed overseas for use in Brunei) can be authenticated with an Apostille through the State Judiciary Department or legalized through a Brunei diplomatic mission under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [3] [6].

steps.title: Activate Incapacitation Withdrawals, Disability Pensions, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Employees Trust Fund (Tabung Amanah Pekerja) incapacitation withdrawal: If your family member is a member of the Employees Trust Fund (Tabung Amanah Pekerja) under the TAP, SCP, or National Retirement Scheme (Skim Persaraan Kebangsaan - SPK) and is certified by a Government Medical Board under the Ministry of Health as permanently incapacitated from engaging in further employment, they can apply for an early Incapacitation Withdrawal of their accumulated fund balance [1] [4].
  • Statutory Disability Allowance and Carer Allowance: Under the Old Age and Disability Pensions Act (Chapter 18), eligible citizens and permanent residents certified with permanent severe disability may apply through the Pensions Section of the Department of Community Development (Jabatan Pembangunan Masyarakat - JAPEM, Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports) for the monthly Disability Allowance (Elaun Kurang Upaya) and the statutory Carer Allowance (Elaun Penyedia Penjagaan) [4].
  • Employment medical leave: Public-sector officers are eligible for extended certified medical leave under the General Orders upon Medical Board review, while private-sector employees are entitled to paid sick and hospitalization leave under the Employment Order, 2009 [1] [4].

steps.title: Organize Wills (*Wasiat*), *Hibah*, Nominees, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Verify Smart Identity Card and civil registration records: Check that the ill person's name, Smart Identity Card (IC) number, and family particulars match across records held by the Department of Immigration and National Registration, bank accounts, and Land Department title deeds (EDR), correcting any spelling discrepancy while the person can still sign applications [2].
  • Muslim estate planning (Wasiat, Faraid, and Hibah) vs. non-Muslim Wills: Succession rules in Brunei Darussalam follow a dual legal framework overseen by the State Judiciary Department [3]. For Muslims, intestate distribution follows Islamic inheritance law (Faraid) administered by the Syariah Courts; a Muslim testator may execute a written Wasiat (Islamic Will) for up to one-third (1/3) of their net estate in favor of non-Faraid beneficiaries without heir consent (bequests above one-third or to legal heirs require the consent of all Faraid heirs after death), or may execute an inter vivos gift (Hibah) or Wakaf while of sound mind [3]. For non-Muslims, a formal written Will executed under the Wills Act (Chapter 193) must be signed by the testator in the presence of at least two simultaneous witnesses who are not beneficiaries [3].
  • Update TAP/SPK nominees and compile asset records: Confirm that beneficiary (nominee) designations are updated with the Employees Trust Fund (Tabung Amanah Pekerja) and Takaful or life insurance providers [4]. Compile original land title deeds, vehicle ownership cards, bank statements, and liabilities in a secure folder, and coordinate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Apostille registry if the person holds assets or family ties outside Brunei Darussalam [3] [6].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative care and home nursing referralUpon diagnosis of advanced illnessMinistry of Health (RIPAS / TBCC / Home Nursing) [1] [5]
2. Bru-HIMS care preferences & family spokespersonWhile decision-making capacity is intactMinistry of Health / Treating Clinical Team [1]
3. Registered Power of Attorney & bank mandatesBefore any loss of legal capacityState Judiciary Department (Supreme Court Registry) & Banks [3]
4. TAP/SPK incapacitation & JAPEM disability claimsUpon Government Medical Board certificationEmployees Trust Fund (Tabung Amanah Pekerja) & JAPEM [4]
5. Wasiat / Hibah or Will, nominees & IC checkWhile capacity is intactState Judiciary Department & Department of Immigration and National Registration [2] [3]

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Cambodia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Cambodia. Below we outline the five official and practical steps required in order under Cambodian administrative and civil law to obtain medical certification, register the death, arrange the funeral or international repatriation, notify social security and tax authorities, and administer the estate.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: When a death occurs in a public referral hospital, provincial hospital, or licensed private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health, the attending physician examines the body and issues an official Medical Notification of Death (or death confirmation letter) recording the clinical cause, date, and time of death [1]. You should request multiple signed and stamped copies, as both the local civil registrar and funeral providers require an original or certified medical document [1].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home in a village (Phum) or urban neighborhood, notify the village chief (Me Phum) and the nearest public health center immediately [1] [2]. A public health practitioner or local administrative official will verify the circumstances of the natural death and issue a confirmation letter so the commune or Sangkat office can proceed with civil registration [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred suddenly, in a traffic or workplace accident, or outside medical supervision, you must notify the Cambodian National Police under the Ministry of Interior before the body is moved [2]. The judicial police and a forensic medical examiner conduct an on-scene examination or autopsy at a designated public hospital, and the prosecutor attached to the provincial or municipal court of first instance must issue a formal clearance before burial, cremation, or repatriation is permitted [2] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: Under the Law on Civil Registration, Vital Statistics and Identification administered by the General Department of Identification within the Ministry of Interior, deaths must be registered with the Civil Registrar (the Commune Chief or Chao Sangkat) in the commune or Sangkat where the death occurred or where the deceased held permanent residence [2].
  • Statutory registration deadline: The family or household representative should declare the death within 15 days of the date of death [2]. If the statutory 15-day period passes without registration, late registration requires an additional administrative verification procedure at the commune or district (Khan / Srok) level [2].
  • Required documents and Death Certificate issuance: Bring the hospital Medical Notification of Death or village chief's confirmation letter, the deceased's Khmer National Identity Card, the household Family Book (Sievphov Krousar) or Residence Book (Sievphovulnakpheap), and the informant's identity card [2]. The Civil Registrar records the entry in the official death register, issues the official Death Certificate (Sambot Moronakpheap), and updates the Family Book [2]. If the deceased was a foreign national, the death is registered through the local Sangkat and communicated to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation and the relevant foreign embassy in Phnom Penh [2].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or Buddhist pagoda cremation: Once the medical death confirmation and commune civil registration permit are issued, you may engage a licensed funeral service provider or coordinate directly with a local pagoda (Wat) or municipal cemetery committee [1] [2]. Cremation at a pagoda crematorium or burial in a designated cemetery requires presentation of the official commune permit confirming that no forensic or police hold remains open [2].
  • International repatriation of human remains or ashes: If the deceased's remains or cremated ashes must be transported out of Cambodia, a specialized international funeral director must obtain a sanitary certificate of non-infectious disease and an embalming/hermetic coffin sealing certificate through a facility authorized by the Ministry of Health, along with customs export clearance and police transit authorization [1] [2].
  • Consular legalization of Cambodian documents: Cambodia is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consequently, any Cambodian Death Certificate, medical certificate, or succession record needed in another country must first be certified by the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Phnom Penh and then legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country [2] [3].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• National Social Security Fund (NSSF) funeral grant and survivor pension: If your family member was a registered private-sector employee, civil servant, or pensioner covered by the National Social Security Fund (NSSF), notify the NSSF promptly [4] [5]. Under the NSSF Pension Scheme and Occupational Risk Scheme, eligible survivors (surviving spouse and dependent children) may claim a lump-sum funeral grant (death benefit) and monthly survivor pension benefits or a survivor allowance by submitting the Death Certificate, NSSF membership card, Family Book, and marriage or birth certificates [4] [5]. Work-related deaths must be reported to the NSSF immediately (within 48 hours of the fatal occupational incident) to trigger employment injury survivor benefits [5].
  • Banking and insurance notifications: Present the official Death Certificate and Family Book to all commercial banks and microfinance institutions in Cambodia where the deceased held individual or joint accounts [3]. Banks will freeze sole accounts pending formal succession documentation or a court order, while life insurance policies pay directly to the named beneficiary upon submission of the Death Certificate and medical cause-of-death report.
  • Tax and property records: If the deceased owned registered real estate, operated a sole proprietorship, or held taxpayer registration, notify the General Department of Taxation so that ongoing business tax obligations are closed and property transfer tax requirements are properly assessed during estate settlement [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Property Transfer
steps.html:
• Governing succession rules under the Civil Code: Inheritance in Cambodia is governed by Book Seven (Succession) of the Cambodian Civil Code administered under the framework of the Ministry of Justice [3]. Succession opens at the deceased's last permanent domicile immediately upon death [3]. If the deceased left a valid notarialwill, public will, or handwritten (holographic) will, testamentary distribution applies subject to the statutory reserved portion (legitime) protecting immediate heirs [3]. In intestate succession, heirs inherit in statutory ranks: first, the deceased's children (or their lineal descendants by representation); second, lineal ascendants; and third, siblings, with the surviving spouse always inheriting alongside whichever rank applies [3].
  • Notarial or commune heirship certification and court probate: For undisputed family estates, heirs commonly establish their status through a Certificate of Heirs attested by the local Commune/Sangkat council or a licensed Cambodian notary public, or obtain a court confirmation from the competent Provincial or Municipal Court of First Instance under the Ministry of Justice if banks or cadastral offices require judicial authorization [2] [3].Heirs may accept the estate unconditionally, accept with benefit of inventory (limiting liability for the deceased's debts to estate assets) within three months of learning of the opening of succession, or renounce the inheritance in court [3].
  • Property transfer tax and cross-border coordination: While Cambodia does not levy a standalone estate duty, transferring immovable property (hard-title land or condominiums) or company shares from a deceased owner to heirs is subject to the 4% Stamp Duty (registration tax on transfer of ownership) administered by the General Department of Taxation, subject to statutory exemptions and relief rules for direct family inheritance between parents, children, and spouses [6]. If heirs reside outside Cambodia, they may execute a Power of Attorney before a notary in their country of residence, have it legalized through the Cambodian embassy abroad, and appoint a representative in Cambodia to complete tax filings and cadastral title transfers [3] [6].

closingQuestion: Which province or municipality in Cambodia did the death occur in, and was your family member a Cambodian citizen or a foreign national so we can tailor the exact civil registration, NSSF, and succession requirements?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Cambodia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Cambodia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Cambodia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, taking timely medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and prevents court or banking blocks later. Below we outline the five official and practical steps to follow in order under Cambodian law.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public referral hospitals and palliative services: Coordinate specialist oncology, pain management, and supportive care through national or provincial public referral hospitals overseen by the Ministry of Health (such as Calmette Hospital, Khmer-Soviet Friendship Hospital, or provincial referral centers) as well as accredited non-governmental home-care and hospice teams operating in Phnom Penh and provincial centers [1]. Ask the treating physician to issue a comprehensive medical summary, symptom-management plan, and prescriptions for controlled analgesics under Ministry of Health clinical protocols [1].
  • National Social Security Fund (NSSF) Health Care Scheme: If the ill person is a registered private-sector worker, civil servant, public employee, or pensioner covered by the National Social Security Fund (NSSF), verify coverage under the NSSF Health Care Scheme [4] [5]. Contracted public and private health facilities provide inpatient treatment, outpatient specialist consultations, chronic disease management, and emergency medical transport directly billed to the NSSF upon presentation of the NSSF membership card and Khmer National Identity Card [4] [5].
  • Health Equity Fund (HEF) and private insurance: For low-income households holding an IDPoor card, the Health Equity Fund covers user fees at public health centers and referral hospitals under the Ministry of Health [1] [5]. If the ill person holds private inpatient or international medical evacuation insurance, obtain prior written authorization before transferring to private palliative care or home-based nursing [1].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Proxy
steps.html:
• Written statement of medical treatment preferences: While Cambodia does not have a standalone statutory Living Will Registry, patient consent and medical decision-making are governed by Ministry of Health medical ethics rules and the general provisions on personal rights under the Cambodian Civil Code administered by the Ministry of Justice [1] [3]. While the ill person retains full decision-making capacity, they should sign a written statement of treatment preferences specifying wishes regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and pain relief [1] [3].
  • Designating a family medical representative: In Cambodian clinical practice, physicians consult the patient directly while capable and rely on the designated spouse or closest adult family member listed in the hospital chart and Family Book (Sievphov Krousar) when the patient can no longer communicate [1] [2]. We suggest formally naming a primary and alternate healthcare representative in a written mandate signed by the ill person and placing copies directly into the hospital medical record with the attending physician [1] [3].
  • Hospital medical records and discharge documentation: Request certified copies of diagnostic pathology reports, imaging summaries, and ongoing prescription regimens from the treating hospital so that community health centers or home-care physicians have immediate clinical continuity [1].

steps.title: Execute Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Mandate and Power of Attorney under the Cambodian Civil Code: Under Book Four (Obligations) of the Cambodian Civil Code overseen by the Ministry of Justice, a competent adult may grant a mandate (Power of Attorney) authorizing a trusted representative to manage bank accounts, pay medical bills, lease or sell property, and handle administrative filings [3]. Crucially, the principal must have full mental capacity at the moment of signing; once capacity is lost, a standard mandate cannot be validly executed and family members may face lengthy guardianship (curatorship) proceedings before the Provincial or Municipal Court of First Instance [3].
  • Notarial execution for immovable property and formal transactions: For transactions involving hard-title real estate, corporate shares, or significant assets, execute an authentic Power of Attorney before a licensed Cambodian notary public or have the signature certified through the local Commune or Sangkat office under the Ministry of Interior [2] [3].
  • Commercial bank account mandates: Cambodian commercial banks and microfinance institutions frequently require account holders to sign the bank's own internal mandate form in person (or before a bank officer visiting the hospital/home) rather than relying solely on a general power of attorney [3]. Arrange for the ill person to add an authorized signatory or update joint-account operating instructions while they are still able to sign and verify their identity [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability, Critical-Illness, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• NSSF invalidity pension and sickness allowances: If the illness results in permanent loss of working capacity for an insured worker, apply to the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) for medical assessment of invalidity (disability) benefits under the NSSF Pension Scheme or daily sickness/medical leave allowances under the Health Care Scheme [4] [5]. An NSSF medical committee evaluates the treating physician's report to determine eligibility for ongoing disability pension payments or lump-sum support [4].
  • Employment leave and caregiver arrangements: Family members employed in the formal sector in Cambodia may request paid special leave or annual leave adjustments under the Cambodian Labor Law to care for a seriously ill immediate family member [4]. Keep official medical certificates issued by a Ministry of Health facility to substantiate employer leave requests [1] [4].
  • Social assistance and disability registration: Households facing severe financial hardship due to long-term illness or disability can register with their local Commune or Sangkat council under the Ministry of Interior to be assessed for national social assistance cash transfers and disability support programs [2] [5].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Valid forms of wills under the Cambodian Civil Code: Book Seven (Succession) of the Cambodian Civil Code recognizes three primary forms of ordinary wills: a Notarial Will (dictated to a notary in the presence of two witnesses), a Holographic Will (written entirely by hand, dated, and signed by the testator), and a Secret Will [3]. Executing a Notarial Will before a licensed notary under the Ministry of Justice is advisable to minimize later authenticity disputes, while ensuring the distribution respects the statutory reserved portion (legitime) guaranteed to descendants, parents, or the spouse [3].
  • Civil registry and identity verification: Verify that the ill person's Khmer National Identity Card, Birth Certificate, Marriage Certificate, and household Family Book (Sievphov Krousar) held under the Ministry of Interior contain consistent spelling of names and dates of birth [2]. Correcting discrepancies at the Commune/Sangkat office while the person is alive is significantly faster than rectifying civil status records after death [2].
  • Property titles, tax records, and cross-border assets: Consolidate original cadastral hard titles, vehicle registration cards, insurance policies, and tax registration certificates issued by the General Department of Taxation [6]. Knowing the registration status of land and business assets helps the family prepare for the 4% property transfer stamp duty rules and statutory family inheritance exemptions administered by the General Department of Taxation [6]. If family members or assets are located outside Cambodia, note that Cambodia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so powers of attorney or estate documents crossing borders must undergo consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant embassy [2] [3].
