title: What to Do When Someone Dies in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for China: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in China. Below we outline the five official and practical steps required in order under the laws and administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China to obtain medical certification, cancel household registration, arrange cremation or international repatriation, claim social insurance benefits, and administer the estate.

steps.title: Obtain the Medical Certificate of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or medical facility deaths: When a death occurs in a hospital or healthcare institution regulated by the National Health Commission, the attending physician immediately issues the unified Medical Certificate of Death (Inference) (Siwang Yixue Zhengming (Tuiduan) Shu) in multiple official counterfoils [1] [2]. This certificate is the foundational legal document required for household registration cancellation, funeral home reception, and cremation authorization [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died naturally at home, contact the sub-district community health service center (Shequ Weisheng Fuwu Zhongxin) or township health center immediately [1] [2]. A community medical practitioner examines the body, reviews prior medical history and neighborhood committee confirmation, and issues the official Medical Certificate of Death (Inference) [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or non-natural deaths: If the death occurred suddenly without clear medical cause, in a traffic or workplace accident, or under suspicious circumstances, you must immediately report it to the local Public Security Bureau (PSB) police station (Paichusuo) by calling 110 before moving the body [1]. Forensic medical examiners of the Public Security Bureau investigate the scene and issue a Forensic Death Certificate (Fayi Siwang Zhengming), which replaces the hospital certificate for civil deregistration and cremation clearance [1].

steps.title: Register the Death and Cancel Household Registration (Hukou)
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: In China, death registration and cancellation of household registration (Hukou Zhuxiao) are administered by the local Public Security Bureau (PSB) police station (Paichusuo) where the deceased held permanent household registration (Hukou) [1].
  • Statutory registration deadline: Under the Regulations on Household Registration of the People's Republic of China, the head of the household, close relative, or neighborhood committee must report the death and cancel the deceased's Hukou within one month in urban areas (and before burial/cremation in municipalities where police verification on the death certificate stub is required for the funeral home) [1].
  • Required documents and certificate verification: Present the Medical Certificate of Death (Inference) (specifically the counterfoil designated for household registration cancellation and the cremation counterfoil), the deceased's Household Register booklet (Hukoubu), the deceased's Resident Identity Card (Shenfenzheng), and the informant's identity card [1]. The Public Security Bureau cancels the deceased's entry in the Hukoubu, collects the deceased's Resident Identity Card, stamps the cremation counterfoil of the death certificate, and issues an official Proof of Household Cancellation (Hukou Zhuxiao Zhengming) [1]. If the deceased was a foreign citizen, the death must be reported promptly to the Exit-Entry Administration of the Public Security Bureau and the deceased's embassy or consulate [1].

steps.title: Arrange Cremation, Burial, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Mandatory cremation in designated areas and funeral parlors: Under the Regulations on Funeral and Interment Control supervised by the Ministry of Civil Affairs, cremation is mandatory across all cities and densely populated areas in China, whereas earth burial is restricted to designated rural or ethnic minority regions [1] [4]. Only licensed municipal funeral parlors (Binyiguan) are authorized to transport human remains and perform cremations [1]. Present the PSB-stamped cremation counterfoil of the Medical Certificate of Death to the funeral parlor to schedule cremation and receive the official Cremation Certificate (Huohua Zhengming), which is needed to inter ashes in a public cemetery (Gongmu) and to claim social security benefits [1] [3].
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: If a foreign national dies in China or if remains/ashes must be transported internationally, transport must be coordinated through an authorized international funeral transport agency, Customs quarantine authorities, and the local foreign affairs office, accompanied by a Medical Certificate of Death, embalming or cremation certificate, and customs quarantine permit [1] [2].
  • Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention: China is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (effective November 2023) [1]. If a Chinese death certificate, notarial death certificate (Siwang Gongzhengshu), or succession document must be used in another Apostille member country, first have the document notarized at a Chinese Notary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) and then obtain an Apostille (Fujia Zhengming) from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or an authorized provincial Foreign Affairs Office [1].

steps.title: Notify Social Insurance, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral subsidy and one-time bereavement benefit: If the deceased participated in China's Urban Employee Basic Endowment Insurance or Urban and Rural Resident Basic Pension Insurance overseen by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, eligible survivors may claim a statutory Funeral Subsidy (Sangzang Buzhujin) and a One-Time Bereavement Payment (Fuxujin), along with the refund of the individual pension account balance [3] [4]. Submit the Medical Certificate of Death, Cremation Certificate, Hukou cancellation proof, and survivor relationship proof to the local Social Insurance Administration Center (Shebao Zhongxin) or via the municipal Government Service Center (Zhengwu Fuwu Zhongxin) single-window (Shenhou Yijianshi / One-Stop Bereavement Service) [1] [3].
  • Medical insurance and housing provident fund: Settle final inpatient hospital bills through the Basic Medical Insurance system before closing the deceased's medical insurance individual account, and apply to the local Housing Provident Fund Management Center (Zhufang Gongjijin Guanli Zhongxin) to withdraw the deceased's remaining Housing Provident Fund balance [3] [4].
  • Bank account inquiries and tax closure: Under joint regulations of the People's Bank of China and banking regulators, a spouse, child, or parent may present a death certificate and relationship proof at any commercial bank to query all accounts held in the deceased's name; streamlined small-balance withdrawals (generally up to RMB 50,000 per institution) are available without full notarial probate, whereas larger balances require a Notarial Certificate of Inheritance or court judgment [1] [5]. If the deceased operated an individual business or owed personal income tax, notify the State Taxation Administration bureau to complete tax deregistration [1].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession under the Civil Code
steps.html:
• Succession rules under Book Six of the PRC Civil Code: Inheritance in China is governed by Book Six (Succession) of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, overseen by the judicial system and the Ministry of Justice [1] [5]. If the deceased left a valid will (notarial, handwritten, printed, audio-visual, or nuncupative will meeting statutory witness formalities) or a legacy-support agreement, testamentary succession applies [5]. In intestate succession, First-Order Statutory Heirs are the spouse, children, and parents of the deceased, who inherit in equal shares; Second-Order Heirs (siblings, paternal/maternal grandparents) inherit only if no first-order heir survives [5].
  • Notarial Certificate of Inheritance vs. People's Court litigation: Where all heirs agree on the division of the estate, the standard non-contentious procedure is to apply to a Notary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) under the Ministry of Justice in the locality where the deceased was domiciled or where real estate is located for a Notarial Certificate of Inheritance (Jicheng Quan Gongzhengshu) [1] [5]. All statutory heirs must appear in person (or via legalized Power of Attorney) to confirm acceptance or written renunciation of inheritance [5]. For real estate transfers between statutory heirs, direct registration at the Municipal Real Estate Registration Center (Budongchan Dengji Zhongxin) is also available, or heirs may petition the local Primary People's Court if a dispute exists [1] [5].
  • Estate taxes, property transfer fees, and cross-border heirs: China currently levies no inheritance tax or estate duty [1] [4]. Furthermore, when statutory heirs (spouse, children, parents, siblings, grandparents) inherit real estate title, the transfer is exempt from Deed Tax (Qishui) and Personal Income Tax under State Taxation Administration rules, though registration administrative fees and stamp duty apply (and capital gains tax may apply if the heir later sells a non-primary residence) [1]. Heirs residing abroad must execute a Power of Attorney or Statement of Acceptance/Renunciation of Inheritance, have it Apostilled (or legalized by a Chinese embassy/consulate if in a non-Apostille country), and submit it with a certified Chinese translation [1] [5].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Obtain Medical Certificate of Death (Inference)Immediately upon deathNational Health Commission Hospital / Community Health Center / Public Security Bureau (110)
2. Cancel Household Registration (Hukou)Within 30 days (before cremation in most cities)Local Public Security Bureau Police Station (Paichusuo)
3. Complete cremation and obtain Cremation CertificateTypically within 3 to 7 days of deathMunicipal Funeral Parlor (Binyiguan) under Ministry of Civil Affairs
4. Claim Funeral Subsidy, Bereavement Payment & Housing FundWithin 3 to 6 months of death (varies by province)Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (Shebao Zhongxin)
5. Obtain Notarial Certificate of Inheritance & transfer titleWithin 60 days of death for renunciation; no fixed deadline for title transferNotary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) under Ministry of Justice / Real Estate Registration Center

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in China: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for China: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in China is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full civil capacity (Wanquan Minshi Xingwei Nengli) ensures their care preferences are respected and avoids complex court guardianship or asset freezes later. Below we outline the five official and practical steps to take in order under the laws of the People's Republic of China.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Basic Medical Insurance
steps.html:
• Hospital palliative care (Anning Liaohu) and community health services: The National Health Commission oversees specialized palliative and hospice care (Anning Liaohu) wards in tertiary public hospitals, oncology centers, and sub-district community health service centers (Shequ Weisheng Fuwu Zhongxin) across major Chinese municipalities [1] [2]. Request a formal clinical summary, pain-management registration (for outpatient or home-based opioid analgesics using specialized prescription cards), and a referral for home-bed medical services (Jiating Bingchuang) [1] [2].
  • Outpatient Major/Chronic Disease Registration (Menman / mente): Under China's Basic Medical Insurance system (Urban Employee or Urban-Rural Resident schemes), apply at the treating hospital's medical insurance office or local healthcare security bureau (Yibao Ju) for Outpatient Special/Major Illness (Menzhen Teshu Jibing) certification [3] [4]. Once approved, high-cost outpatient oncology, dialysis, and palliative treatments are reimbursed at inpatient rates, and Critical Illness Insurance (Dabing Yibao) automatically provides secondary reimbursement above the annual deductible threshold [3] [4].
  • Cross-province direct medical billing: If the ill person travels to another city (such as Beijing, Shanghai, or Guangzhou) for specialist treatment, register for Cross-Region Direct Settlement (Yidi Jiuyi Beian) via the National Healthcare Security Platform so hospital bills are settled directly without upfront reimbursement delays [1] [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Appoint an Adult Guardian
steps.html:
• Living wills (Shengqian Yuzhu) and medical informed consent: Under Book Four (Personality Rights, Article 1006 and medical liability rules) of the PRC Civil Code, patients hold the right to be informed of their condition and make autonomous treatment choices, or to authorize a close relative to exercise medical consent when incapable [1] [5]. Furthermore, municipal legislation in Shenzhen (under the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Medical Regulations) explicitly recognizes binding Living Wills (Shengqian Yuzhu) regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive intubation, and life-sustaining interventions, while Mainland Living Will Promotion Associations provide standardized Five Wishes (Wuge Yuanwang) directives used across Chinese hospitals [1] [2].
  • Voluntary Adult Guardianship (Yiding Jianhu) under Article 33 of the Civil Code: A cornerstone of end-of-life planning in China is Voluntary Adult Guardianship (Yiding Jianhu) under Article 33 of the PRC Civil Code [5]. Any adult with full civil capacity may negotiate in writing with a spouse, adult child, other close relative, or trusted individual/organization to serve as their guardian once they partially or completely lose civil capacity [5]. We suggest executing a Notarial Voluntary Guardianship Agreement (Yiding Jianhu Xiyi Gongzheng) at a Notary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) overseen by the Ministry of Justice so that hospitals, banks, and nursing facilities immediately recognize the appointed guardian's authority to sign medical consent forms and manage personal care [1] [5].
  • Designating the hospital emergency contact: Ensure the appointed voluntary guardian or healthcare proxy is explicitly named in the hospital admission file as the authorized medical decision-maker (Shouquan Weituoren) [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Notarial Power of Attorney (Weituo Gongzheng): While the ill person retains full mental capacity, execute a formal Power of Attorney before a Notary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) under the Ministry of Justice authorizing a trusted representative to handle banking, tax filings, social insurance claims, and property management [1] [5]. Notaries verify the principal's mental capacity (often recording audio-video evidence at the notary office or via a bedside hospital visit) [5].
  • Precaution regarding real estate and banking rules: In China, commercial banks and Municipal Real Estate Registration Centers (Budongchan Dengji Zhongxin) strictly scrutinize powers of attorney and require a specific Notarial Power of Attorney for selling or mortgaging property [1] [5]. Because standard agency mandates face legal challenges if the principal loses capacity, pairing a Notarial Power of Attorney with a Notarial Voluntary Guardianship Agreement (Article 33 of the Civil Code) and a Notarial Supervision/Property Management clause provides seamless legal continuity [5].
  • Digital payment and bank account liquidity: Verify that the ill person's Resident Identity Card (Shenfenzheng) is valid and has not expired, ensure mobile phone numbers linked to bank accounts, WeChat Pay, and Alipay are registered in good standing, and maintain adequate liquidity in an accessible account for ongoing medical and caregiving expenses [1] [5].

steps.title: Activate Long-Term Care Insurance, Disability Benefits, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Long-Term Care Insurance (Changqi Huli Baoxian): Across dozens of Chinese pilot and roll-out cities (including Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Qingdao) administered alongside the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and Healthcare Security authorities, insured individuals who become severely disabled or bedridden due to terminal or chronic illness for six months or more can apply for a formal Barthel Index / Activities of Daily Living (ADL) assessment [3] [4]. Once certified, Long-Term Care Insurance covers 70% to 90% of home nursing visits or institutional hospice nursing costs [3] [4].
  • Work-incapacity retirement (Bing退) and disability allowances: If the ill person is below statutory retirement age and enrolled in Urban Employee Basic Endowment Insurance, they may apply to the local Labor Capacity Appraisal Committee (Laodong Nengli Jianding Weiyuanhui) under the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security for a Certification of Complete Loss of Labor Capacity [3]. This enables early illness retirement (Bingtui) or invalidity allowance (BingcanJintie) payments [3]. Disabled Person's Federation (Canlian) registration also provides local nursing subsidies.
  • Statutory parental care leave for employed children: Most Chinese provinces grant employees (especially only children, and increasingly non-only children) between 5 and 20 days of paid Parental Nursing Leave (Huli Jia) per year when a parent is hospitalized with a serious illness [1] [3]. Retain the hospital admission certificate to claim this statutory paid leave from employers [1] [3].

steps.title: Prepare a Valid Will and Organize Civil Status and Property Records
steps.html:
• Six statutory forms of wills under Book Six of the PRC Civil Code: The PRC Civil Code recognizes six valid forms of wills: Notarial Will (Gongzheng Yizhu), Holographic Will (Zishu Yizhu, handwritten, signed, and dated year-month-day by the testator), Printed Will (Dayin Yizhu, requiring two witnesses present throughout who sign and date every page), Audio-Visual Will (Luyin Luxiang Yizhu, requiring two witnesses appearing in the recording), Will Written on Behalf of Testator (Daishu Yizhu, two witnesses), and Nuncupative/Oral Will (Koutou Yizhu, valid only in an acute emergency with two witnesses) [5]. While the Civil Code abolished the rule that a Notarial Will automatically overrides later non-notarial wills, executing a Notarial Will at a Notary Public Office under the Ministry of Justice remains the most reliable way to prevent later challenges over capacity or witness defects [5].
  • Reconciling Hukou and kinship proofs: Gather the ill person's Household Register (Hukoubu), Resident Identity Card, Marriage Certificate, Real Estate Ownership Certificates (Budongchan Quanzheng), and archival personnel records (Renshi Dang'an) proving parent-child relationships [1] [5]. Because historical Hukou splits often leave older parents and adult children on separate household booklets, obtaining a Notarial Certificate of Kinship (Qinshu Guanxi Gongzheng) or verifying police/personnel archives while the ill person is alive avoids major bottlenecks during post-death estate administration [1] [5].
  • Cross-border assets and Apostille coordination: China imposes no inheritance tax, and real estate inherited by statutory heirs is exempt from Deed Tax [1] [4]. If family members reside abroad or hold foreign citizenship, powers of attorney or kinship documents executed outside China should be Apostilled under the 1961 Hague Convention (or consularly legalized if from a non-Apostille state) and accompanied by a certified Chinese translation [1] [5].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Register Outpatient Major Illness & palliative careImmediately upon diagnosisNational Health Commission Hospital / Healthcare Security Bureau
2. Execute Living Will & Voluntary Guardianship (Art. 33)While retaining full civil capacityNotary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) under Ministry of Justice
3. Execute Notarial Power of Attorney & banking arrangementsBefore any loss of mental or legal capacityNotary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) / Commercial Banks
4. Apply for Long-Term Care Insurance & incapacity appraisalUpon meeting ADL disability or incapacity criteriaMinistry of Human Resources and Social Security / Labor Appraisal Committee
5. Execute a Civil Code Will & verify kinship/Hukou recordsWhile retaining full testamentary capacityNotary Public Office (Gongzhengchu) / Public Security Bureau

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Fiji: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Fiji. Below we outline the five official and practical steps required in order under Fijian law to obtain medical certification of death, register the death with the Civil Registry, arrange burial, cremation, or international repatriation, claim Fiji National Provident Fund benefits and notify tax authorities, and administer the estate.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or health center deaths: When a death occurs in a divisional hospital (such as Colonial War Memorial Hospital in Suva, Lautoka Hospital, or Labasa Hospital), sub-divisional hospital, or private clinic overseen by the Ministry of Health and Medical Services, the attending medical officer examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD) [1]. Request multiple certified copies, as the original is required to register the death and obtain burial or cremation clearance [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home from a known natural illness, notify the nearest sub-divisional health center or treating physician and the local Fiji Police Force station immediately [1]. If the deceased was under recent medical care, the attending medical officer may issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death; otherwise, the body is transferred to the nearest public hospital mortuary for medical verification [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: Under Fiji's Inquests Act, any sudden, accidental, violent, or unexplained death (including deaths occurring without recent medical attendance) must be reported immediately to the Fiji Police Force [1] [2]. Police officers secure the scene and transfer the deceased to a public hospital mortuary, where a forensic pathologist performs a post-mortem examination under the authority of the Resident Magistrate acting as Coroner before releasing the body and issuing the medical/coronial certificate for registration [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) Registry
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, all deaths occurring in Fiji must be registered with the Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) Registry under the Ministry of Justice (or at a Divisional/District Registrar office or Post Fiji agency point in outer islands and rural districts) [2].
  • Statutory registration deadline: The next of kin, relative present at the death, or person arranging the funeral must register the death within 2 months (60 days) of the date of death [2]. In practice, registration is completed within a few days of death because the official Death Certificate is needed for funeral permits, pension claims, and banking notifications [2] [3]. Late registration after two months requires a statutory declaration and formal approval by the Registrar-General [2].
  • Required documents and Death Certificate issuance: Present the original Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD), the deceased's Birth Certificate, Marriage Certificate (if applicable), Voter Identification Card or Fijian passport, and the informant's valid photo ID [2]. Upon registration, the BDM Registry issues the official Death Certificate [2]. If the deceased was an iTaukei (indigenous Fijian) landowner, the Death Certificate should also be presented to the Native Lands Commission (Vola ni Kawa Bula / VKB registry) to update customary lineage records [2] [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: Under the Public Health Act and Burial and Cremation Act administered by the Ministry of Health and Medical Services and municipal councils, burial takes place in an authorized municipal, religious, or village cemetery [1] [2]. For cremation (whether at a municipal crematorium such as Nasinu or a traditional cremation site), you must obtain a formal Cremation Permit from the Divisional Medical Officer or police authority confirming that the cause of death has been medically certified and no coronial inquiry is pending [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of human remains or ashes: If the deceased was a foreign national or if remains/ashes must be repatriated abroad, a licensed funeral director coordinates with the Ministry of Health and Medical Services (for a Free From Infection Certificate, Embalming Certificate, and Coffin Sealing Certificate), the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service, and the relevant foreign High Commission or Embassy in Suva [1] [5].
  • Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention: Fiji is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [2]. Any Fijian Death Certificate, Coroner's report, or High Court probate grant required for legal use in another Apostille member country can be authenticated with an official Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Suva (or the designated Competent Authority), eliminating the need for multi-step consular legalization in treaty states [2].

steps.title: Claim FNPF Funeral Assistance and Survivor Benefits and Notify Tax and Banks
steps.html:
• Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) Funeral Assistance and Death Benefit: If the deceased was a member of the Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF), notify FNPF promptly [3]. FNPF provides a statutory Funeral Assistance Grant (Special Death Benefit) (FJD 2,000 for active eligible members under the Special Death Benefit scheme) to help cover immediate funeral expenses, in addition to the full balance of the member's FNPF preserved and general accounts plus any additional Special Death Benefit lump sum (up to FJD 8,500 subject to annual scheme rules) paid to the valid nominated beneficiaries [3]. If no valid FNPF nomination exists on file, FNPF pays the balance via the High Court probate grant or the Public Trustee [2] [3].
  • Social welfare and Accident Compensation Commission Fiji (ACCF): If the deceased received the Social Pension Scheme or Poverty Benefit Scheme under the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection, notify the Department of Social Welfare to close the allowance [3] [4]. If the death resulted from a motor vehicle, workplace, or school accident in Fiji, survivors may claim a statutory lump-sum accidental death compensation payment from the Accident Compensation Commission Fiji (ACCF) [3] [4].
  • Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) and banking notifications: Present the Death Certificate to all commercial banks in Fiji (such as BSP, ANZ, Westpac, BRED Bank, or HFC Bank) to freeze individual accounts pending estate administration [2] [5]. Notify the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) using the deceased's Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to file any final income tax return and obtain tax clearance for estate distribution [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Succession
steps.html:
• Probate and Letters of Administration under the Succession, Probate and Administration Act: Estate administration in Fiji is governed by the Succession, Probate and Administration Act and overseen by the Probate Registry of the High Court of Fiji (within the Judicial Department / Ministry of Justice framework) [2].
    • Testate estates (with a valid Will): The named executor applies to the High Court of Fiji for a Grant of Probate, which includes publishing a mandatory 14-day Notice of Intention to Apply in a national newspaper to allow creditors or claimants to lodge caveats [2].
    • Intestate estates (no Will): The surviving spouse or next of kin applies to the High Court for Letters of Administration, or entrusts the estate to the Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited (which holds statutory authority to administer intestate and small estates across Fiji) [2]. Under statutory intestacy rules, the surviving spouse receives the personal chattels, a statutory pecuniary legacy, and a share of the residuary estate alongside surviving children [2].
  • Taxation of estates and property transfers: Fiji does not levy an inheritance tax or estate duty, and Capital Gains Tax (CGT) transmitted by reason of death to an executor or beneficiary is deferred/exempt at the time of inheritance under Fiji Revenue and Customs Service rules [5]. However, stamp duty and registration fees apply when registering a Transmission by Death on Freehold, State Lease, or iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB) leases at the Office of the Registrar of Titles [2] [5].
  • Cross-border estates and Resealing of Foreign Grants: Under Fiji's British and Colonial Probates Act, a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration issued by a court in a recognized Commonwealth jurisdiction (such as Australia, New Zealand, or the United Kingdom) can be resealed by the High Court of Fiji to administer Fijian bank accounts or land without starting a full local probate proceeding from scratch [2]. Heirs residing abroad may appoint an attorney in Fiji via an Apostilled Power of Attorney [2].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Fiji: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Fiji is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, completing essential medical, financial, and legal planning while the ill person still retains full mental and legal capacity ensures their wishes are respected and prevents accounts or superannuation funds from being frozen without accessible nominations. Below we outline the five official and practical steps to take in order under Fijian law.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public divisional hospitals and community outreach: The Ministry of Health and Medical Services provides inpatient oncology, pain management, and supportive care free of charge to Fijian citizens at major divisional hospitals (Colonial War Memorial Hospital in Suva, Lautoka Hospital, and Labasa Hospital) as well as sub-divisional hospitals and community health centers [1]. Ask the treating specialist to prepare a written clinical summary, prescription schedule for pain-relief medications under the Medicinal Products Act, and a referral to district community health nurses for home-based monitoring [1].
  • Cancer and palliative support services: Coordinate alongside public hospital teams with accredited community support organizations (such as the Fiji Cancer Society) that assist patients with home visits, medical equipment loans (hospital beds, wheelchairs, oxygen concentrators), and transport to treatment [1] [2].
  • Private health insurance and FNPF Medical Early Withdrawal: If the ill person holds private health or critical-illness insurance, obtain prior authorization for private hospital admissions or overseas medical treatment [1] [3]. Additionally, members of the Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) can apply for Medical Assistance Early Withdrawal from their FNPF General Account (or Preserved Account for approved life-threatening conditions) to fund specialized local or overseas medical treatment certified by a Ministry of Health medical board [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Proxy
steps.html:
• Written Advance Healthcare Directive and treatment preferences: In Fiji, patient consent and refusal of medical treatment are governed by common-law principles of bodily autonomy and Ministry of Health and Medical Services clinical consent policies, alongside mental health and capacity safeguards [1] [2]. While the ill person retains full decision-making capacity, they should sign a written statement of treatment preferences recording their instructions regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and palliative sedation [1].
  • Designating a primary healthcare representative: Appoint a trusted spouse, adult child, or relative in writing as the primary medical contact and decision-maker, and ask the attending medical officer at the divisional or private hospital to file a signed copy directly inside the patient's clinical chart [1].
  • Medical records portability: Obtain certified copies of diagnostic pathology reports, imaging summaries, and current medication lists so home-care nurses and emergency medical officers have immediate visibility of the treatment plan [1].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Power of Attorney under the Property Law Act and Powers of Attorney Act: Under Fijian law (overseen by the High Court of Fiji and the Registrar of Titles under the Ministry of Justice), an adult with full mental capacity may execute a formal Power of Attorney appointing a trusted attorney-in-fact to manage financial affairs, pay bills, deal with government agencies, and manage real estate [2].
  • Important capacity and registration rules in Fiji: A general Power of Attorney in Fiji must be signed by the donor in the presence of a qualified witness (such as a Solicitor/Barrister, Notary Public, Justice of the Peace, or Commissioner for Oaths) while the donor has full mental capacity [2]. If the Power of Attorney authorizes any dealing with registered land (Freehold, State Lease, or iTaukei lease), it must be formally registered with the Office of the Registrar of Titles [2]. Because traditional common-law powers of attorney can be affected if the donor loses mental capacity, seek advice from a Fijian legal practitioner or the Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited on structuring enduring financial arrangements before capacity declines [2].
  • Commercial bank account mandates: Fijian commercial banks (BSP, ANZ, Westpac, BRED Bank, HFC Bank) require account holders to verify their identity and sign bank-specific third-party authority forms or joint-account mandates [2] [5]. Arrange for the ill person to add an authorized signatory or establish a dedicated medical-expense account while they are able to sign and complete biometric/ID verification [2] [5].

steps.title: Activate FNPF Incapacity Benefits, Disability Allowances, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) Full Withdrawal on Medical Incapacity: Under the Fiji National Provident Fund Act, a member who is certified by an FNPF-approved medical board as permanently physically or mentally incapacitated from ever engaging in further employment is entitled to withdraw 100% of their FNPF total balance (both Preserved and General Accounts) during their lifetime [3]. Crucially, check with FNPF how a full withdrawal before death interacts with active membership for the FNPF Special Death Benefit (Funeral Assistance Grant), and ensure the FNPF Memorandum of Nomination of beneficiaries is completely up to date while the member has capacity [3].
  • Disability Allowance and Social Protection programs: Under the Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, individuals living with severe permanent disability or chronic incapacitating illness may apply at the nearest Department of Social Welfare office for the monthly Disability Allowance, Care and Protection support, and subsidized transport passes [2] [4].
  • Statutory Family Care Leave under the Employment Relations Act: Under Fiji's Employment Relations Act, employees who have completed more than three months of continuous service are entitled to paid Family Care Leave (in addition to annual and sick leave) to provide care or support to a member of their immediate family or household who is ill [4]. Caregivers should request a medical certificate from the treating Ministry of Health doctor to submit to their employer [1] [4].

steps.title: Review the Will, FNPF Nomination, Civil Status Records, and Property Titles
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Will under the Wills Act: Under Fiji's Wills Act (and the Succession, Probate and Administration Act administered through the High Court of Fiji and the Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) Registry framework under the Ministry of Justice), a valid will must be in writing and signed at the foot or end by the testator in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent adult witnesses, who must also sign in the presence of the testator and each other [2]. A beneficiary or the spouse of a beneficiary must never act as a witness to the will, as doing so voids the gift to that beneficiary [2]. The ill person may draft a will through a licensed Fijian legal practitioner or through the Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited [2].
  • Updating the FNPF Nomination of Beneficiaries: In Fiji, FNPF superannuation funds do not automatically pass under a personal will if a valid FNPF nomination is registered [3]. Instead, FNPF pays directly to the nominees listed on the official FNPF Nomination Form [3]. Verify and, if needed, update the FNPF nomination directly with FNPF (note that marriage under Fijian law automatically revokes a prior FNPF nomination and a prior will unless made in contemplation of that marriage) [2] [3].
  • Civil status, tax, and cross-border property records: Gather original Birth and Marriage Certificates from the Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) Registry, Vola ni Kawa Bula (VKB) registration records for iTaukei family members, land titles, and Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) records with the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) [2] [5]. Fiji levies no inheritance tax, and Capital Gains Tax is deferred on transmission at death [5]. Because Fiji is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, powers of attorney or property documents involving family members abroad can be authenticated via an Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Suva [2].

3. Execute & register Power of Attorney and bank mandatesBefore any loss of mental or legal capacityOffice of the Registrar of Titles (Ministry of Justice) / Commercial Banks
4. Apply for FNPF Medical Incapacity & Family Care LeaveUpon medical board certification of incapacityFiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) / Department of Social Welfare
5. Execute a valid Will & update FNPF Beneficiary NominationWhile retaining full testamentary capacityFiji Public Trustee / Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM) Registry / FNPF

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Georgia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Georgia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Georgia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Georgia, we can guide you through the official medical certification, civil registration, funeral or repatriation, social security, and notarial succession procedures in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a licensed hospital or medical clinic supervised by the Ministry of Internally Displaced Persons from the Occupied Territories, Labour, Health and Social Affairs of Georgia, the attending physician records the cause of death and transmits an electronic medical certificate of death directly to the civil registration system while providing a printed copy to the family [1] [5].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home from a documented natural illness, call the national emergency service (112) so an emergency medical crew and local police unit can attend the address, verify that there are no signs of external trauma, and issue the medical confirmation required for the local clinic or hospital to generate the official medical death notice [1] [5].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, or unexplained, the Ministry of Internal Affairs patrol police secure the scene and transfer the deceased to the Levan Samkharauli National Forensics Bureau for a medico-legal autopsy [5] [6]. The forensic medical examiner issues the official medical certificate of cause of death once the examination is complete [5] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Law of Georgia on Civil Status Acts, all deaths in Georgia are registered by the Public Service Development Agency through any local branch of the Public Service Hall or Community Centre [1] [6]. Once the medical facility or forensic bureau uploads the electronic medical death notice (typically within one working day of death), a family member or authorised representative should complete civil registration within 5 working days [1].
  • Required documents for registration: Present (a) the medical certificate of death (if not already matched electronically in the civil registry database), (b) the deceased's Georgian Identity Card (ID) or passport, and (c) the valid identity document of the applicant (plus a power of attorney if submitted by a non-relative representative) [1] [6].
  • Issuance of the Death Certificate: The Public Service Hall registers the civil act of death, cancels the deceased's national identity document, and issues the official Death Certificate free of charge within 1 working day [1]. If documents will be needed by foreign authorities, you can request bilingual or multilingual extracts and an Apostille at the same counter [1] [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial arrangements: Engage a licensed municipal or private funeral service provider in Georgia to coordinate mortuary preparation and cemetery allocation (for example, through municipal cemetery administration services in Tbilisi, Batumi, or Kutaisi) using the official Death Certificate issued by the Public Service Hall [1]. Because Georgia does not currently operate domestic crematoria, families seeking cremation typically arrange cross-border transport to a neighbouring jurisdiction with a licensed crematorium.
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be repatriated abroad, the funeral provider must obtain: (a) the official Death Certificate from the Public Service Hall [1], (b) a sanitary and non-infectious disease certificate plus an embalming certificate from a licensed medical or forensic institution supervised by the Ministry of Internally Displaced Persons from the Occupied Territories, Labour, Health and Social Affairs of Georgia [5], (c) a coffin-sealing certificate confirming hermetically sealed zinc-lined containment for air cargo, and (d) consular clearance or a mortuary laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy.
  • Apostille and document legalisation: Georgia is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [4]. The Public Service Development Agency (accessible via any Public Service Hall) affixes Apostilles to Georgian Death Certificates and civil status extracts for use in other Apostille convention states [1] [4].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• Stopping state pensions and claiming social benefits: When the Public Service Hall registers a death, the electronic civil registry notifies the Social Service Agency (operating under the Ministry of Internally Displaced Persons from the Occupied Territories, Labour, Health and Social Affairs of Georgia) to halt old-age pension payments [1] [2]. Eligible surviving dependents (such as children under age 18 or disabled dependents) may apply to the Social Service Agency for a statutory survivor social package or targeted municipal funeral assistance where applicable [2].
  • Accumulated Pillar II pension funds: If your family member contributed to Georgia's mandatory funded pension scheme administered by the Pension Agency of Georgia, legal heirs may claim the deceased participant's accumulated retirement savings by presenting the Death Certificate and notarial Certificate of Inheritance [2] [3].
  • Commercial banks and tax obligations: Present the Death Certificate to Georgian commercial banks to freeze sole accounts and suspend automatic debits pending notarial probate [3]. Under the Tax Code of Georgia, notify the Revenue Service if the deceased operated an individual enterprise or held taxable property subject to final tax settlement [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession
steps.html:
• Competent succession authority and 6-month deadline: Under Book Six (Law of Succession) of the Civil Code of Georgia, estate administration and probate are handled by licensed notaries affiliated with the Notary Chamber of Georgia [3] [6]. Heirs (whether inheriting under a will or by intestate statutory order) must formally accept the succession within 6 months from the date of death by filing an application for a Certificate of Inheritance (samemkvidreo mowmoba) with a Georgian notary, or by taking actual possession and management of the estate assets within that 6-month window [3] [6].
  • Issuance of the Certificate of Inheritance: After verifying the Death Certificate, family relationship certificates (birth and marriage records from the Public Service Hall), any registered will, and asset ownership extracts, the notary from the Notary Chamber of Georgia issues the formal Certificate of Inheritance once the 6-month statutory period expires [1] [3]. Heirs then register inherited real estate and company shares with the National Agency of Public Registry at the Public Service Hall [1] [3].
  • Inheritance tax rules: Under the Tax Code of Georgia, inheritance received by first- and second-degree heirs (spouses, children, parents, grandchildren, and siblings) is 100% exempt from Georgian personal income/inheritance tax [6]. Third- and fourth-degree heirs enjoy a statutory tax-free threshold (up to GEL 150,000 of inherited value) and pay income tax only on the excess [6].
  • Cross-border heirs: An heir living outside Georgia does not need to travel in person to accept the estate; they may execute a Power of Attorney before a foreign notary (authenticated with a Hague Apostille or consular legalisation, or signed before a Georgian consulate abroad) authorising a local representative in Georgia to file the succession application with the Notary Chamber of Georgia before the 6-month deadline expires [3] [4].
StepDeadlineAuthority

2. Civil death registrationWithin 5 working days of medical noticePublic Service Hall
3. Funeral or repatriation permitsPrior to burial or cross-border transportPublic Service Development Agency
4. Pension and benefit notificationsPromptly after Death Certificate issuanceSocial Service Agency
5. Notarial succession acceptanceWithin 6 months of the date of deathNotary Chamber of Georgia

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Georgia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Georgia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Georgia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Georgia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and prevents administrative delays for the family. Below, we set out the five key steps to take in chronological order under the laws of Georgia.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Universal Healthcare Programme coverage: Under Georgia's state-funded Universal Healthcare Programme overseen by the Ministry of Internally Displaced Persons from the Occupied Territories, Labour, Health and Social Affairs of Georgia and administered through the National Health Agency, Georgian citizens and eligible residents with chronic, oncological, or terminal conditions are entitled to subsidised inpatient and outpatient palliative care, pain management, and oncology treatment [2] [5].
  • Inpatient hospice and home-based palliative teams: Ask the treating specialist or oncologist for a formal clinical summary (Forma IV-100/a) documenting the diagnosis, symptom-control plan, and palliative care needs [5] [6]. This medical certificate is required to enrol your family member in licensed inpatient palliative care units, specialized hospices, or mobile home-nursing and analgesic prescription programmes in Tbilisi and regional centres [5].
  • Private insurance coordination: If the ill person holds supplementary private medical insurance in Georgia, submit the Forma IV-100/a medical report early to pre-authorise home nursing visits, specialist consultations, and medical equipment [5].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Statutory right to advance directives and informed consent: Under the Law of Georgia on Patient Rights and the Law on Health Care (published via the Legislative Herald of Georgia), every patient with decision-making capacity has the right to give or refuse informed consent to medical interventions and to express advance written wishes regarding life-sustaining treatment, resuscitation, and palliative pain relief during a terminal stage of illness [5] [6].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative: Under Georgian patient rights legislation, a capable citizen may execute a written advance directive naming a trusted person (healthcare proxy or medical representative) who will make medical and care decisions if the patient later becomes unconscious or unable to communicate [3] [6].
  • Notarial certification and medical chart filing: To ensure hospital staff and emergency clinicians honour the directive without delay, it is advisable to have the advance medical statement and healthcare proxy appointment notarised by a notary of the Notary Chamber of Georgia and to place certified copies directly in the patient's hospital file alongside a physician's note confirming full mental capacity at the time of signing [3] [6].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarial Power of Attorney (mindobiloba): While your family member retains full legal and mental capacity, they should execute a comprehensive notarial Power of Attorney before a licensed notary of the Notary Chamber of Georgia [3] [6]. A Georgian notary can visit the patient at home or in a hospital ward if mobility is limited, or witness the mandate via official video-notarisation where permitted, verifying identity and mental capacity before registering the instrument [3].
  • Scope of financial and property authority: To prevent bank freezes or administrative blocks if the illness progresses, the notarial Power of Attorney should explicitly authorise the representative to manage commercial bank accounts, collect pensions or social transfers, represent the person before the Public Service Hall and tax authorities, and administer or lease real estate [1] [3].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates: Because Georgian commercial banks verify powers of attorney strictly, we suggest presenting the notarised Power of Attorney (and completing each bank's internal authorised-signatory mandate) while the account holder is still able to confirm instructions directly [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Critical-Illness Support, and Caregiver Allowances
steps.html:
• Medical-Social Expertise and disability status: If the illness causes severe functional impairment, the treating clinic issues Forma IV-100/a and refers your family member for a Medical-Social Expertise assessment to establish formal disability status (Category I - severe disability, or Category II - significant disability) under the standards of the Ministry of Internally Displaced Persons from the Occupied Territories, Labour, Health and Social Affairs of Georgia [2] [5].
  • State disability social package: Once disability status is certified, submit an application to the Social Service Agency to activate the monthly state social package for persons with severe disabilities, as well as municipal utility or medication subsidies available in cities such as Tbilisi and Batumi [2].
  • Workplace sick leave and caregiver flexibility: Under the Labour Code of Georgia, an employed person facing serious illness is entitled to temporary incapacity (sick) leave supported by an official medical certificate (biuletini), and family caregivers may request flexible working arrangements or unpaid family care leave from their employer [2] [6].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Designations, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a notarial Will (anderdzi): Under Book Six of the Civil Code of Georgia, the most secure testamentary instrument is a notarial will drafted or deposited with a notary of the Notary Chamber of Georgia (either signed in the notary's presence or lodged as a closed will in the presence of witnesses) and recorded in the electronic registry of wills [3] [6].
  • Accounting for statutory forced-share (savaldebulo wili) rules: When planning an estate in Georgia, note that the Civil Code of Georgia grants the testator's spouse, children, and parents a mandatory reserved share equal to one-half of the share each would have received under intestate succession, regardless of the terms of a will [6].
  • Verifying civil status and property records: Obtain updated civil status certificates (birth and marriage records) and real estate title extracts (amonaweri) from the Public Service Hall and the Public Service Development Agency so that family links and asset ownership are free of spelling or registration discrepancies [1] [4].
  • Cross-border powers of attorney and Apostilles: If a designated representative or heir resides outside Georgia, any Power of Attorney executed abroad for use in Georgia must be authenticated with a 1961 Hague Apostille (or consular legalisation) and translated into Georgian, while Georgian documents sent abroad can be Apostilled through the Public Service Development Agency at any Public Service Hall [1] [4].

cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Japan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are very sorry for your loss. When a family member dies in Japan, we can guide you through the official medical certification, municipal civil registration, cremation or repatriation permits, social security and tax filings, and estate succession procedures in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a hospital or clinic in Japan under natural medical care, the attending physician issues the official Medical Death Certificate (Shibou Shindansho), which forms the right-hand side of the statutory A3 Death Notification form (Shibou Todoke) regulated by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare and the Ministry of Justice [1] [6].
  • Deaths at home under ongoing medical supervision: If your family member died at home while receiving regular home visits from a physician for a known condition, call the visiting doctor immediately; if the physician confirms natural death within 24 hours of the last examination, they issue the Shibou Shindansho directly [6].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unattended deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, or occurred without recent medical attendance, do not move the body and call the police (110) rather than an ambulance [6]. Police forensic officers and a medical examiner (kansatsu-i) or police physician conduct an external inspection (kenshi) or forensic autopsy and issue a Post-Mortem Examination Certificate (Shitai Ken'ansho) on the right side of the Shibou Todoke form [1] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Municipal Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and 7-day statutory deadline: Under the Family Register Act (Koseki-ho) overseen by the Ministry of Justice, a cohabiting relative or legal informant must submit the completed Death Notification (Shibou Todoke paired with the Shibou Shindansho or Shitai Ken'ansho) within 7 days of learning of the death (or within 3 months if the death occurred abroad) to the municipal ward, city, or town office (Shiyakusho / Kuyakusho) of the place of death, the deceased's registered domicile (honseki-chi), or the informant's address [1].
  • Issuance of the Cremation or Burial Permit: At the exact time you submit the Shibou Todoke, submit the application for a Permit for Cremation or Burial (Kasou / Maisou Kyokasho). The municipal office stamps and issues this permit immediately, as no cremation or burial may take place in Japan without it [1] [6].
  • Obtaining official death records: Because the original Shibou Shindansho is retained by the municipal office and forwarded to the Legal Affairs Bureau under the Ministry of Justice, obtain several certified copies of the Shibou Shindansho from the hospital before filing, and request certified extracts of the updated Family Register (Koseki Tohon for Japanese citizens, typically updated within 7 to 10 days) or the Residence Record Deletion Certificate (Juminhyo no Johyo, which applies to both Japanese nationals and foreign residents) or a Certificate of Acceptance of Death Notification (Shibou Todoke Juri Shomeisho) [1].

steps.title: Arrange Cremation, Burial, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local cremation and interment: Under Japan's Graveyards, Burials, etc. Act, cremation cannot legally occur within the first 24 hours after death (except for specified infectious diseases) [6]. Engage a licensed funeral director (sougisha) to transport the deceased, hold the wake (tsuya) and funeral service (kokubetsushiki), present the municipal Kasou Kyokasho at the crematorium, and receive the cremated remains paired with the stamped Cremation Certificate needed for interment in a cemetery or columbarium (noukotsudou) [1] [6].
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains or cremated ashes must be transported abroad, the funeral provider coordinates: (a) a Certificate of Acceptance of Death Notification (Shibou Todoke Juri Shomeisho) and certified Shibou Shindansho [1], (b) an official embalming certificate (ibo shochi shomeisho) and non-infectious disease clearance from an accredited medical institution, plus hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin certification (for uncremated remains) [6], and (c) notification to the deceased's embassy or consulate in Japan and customs/quarantine clearance at the departure airport.
  • Apostille and document legalisation: Japan is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Official Japanese municipal death certificates (Shibou Todoke Juri Shomeisho) and Koseki Tohon extracts destined for use abroad can receive an Apostille free of charge from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tokyo or Osaka.

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Health Insurance, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• Japan Pension Service notifications and survivor pensions: Report the death to the Japan Pension Service within 10 days (for Employees' Pension Insurance / Kosei Nenkin) or 14 days (for National Pension / Kokumin Nenkin) to stop ongoing retirement payments and claim unpaid pension accrued up to the month of death (Mishikyu Nenkin), Survivor's Basic Pension (Izoku Kiso Nenkin), Survivor's Employees' Pension (Izoku Kosei Nenkin), or the Lump-Sum Death Payment (Shibou Ichijikin) [2] [5].
  • Health insurance and funeral expense grants: Return the deceased's health insurance card or My Number health insurance credential and Long-Term Care Insurance (Kaigo Hoken) card to the municipal office within 14 days (for National Health Insurance / Late-Stage Medical Care System for the Elderly) or to the employer's health insurance society [5] [6]. Apply for the statutory funeral grant (Sozai-hi under municipal National Health Insurance, typically JPY 30,000 to JPY 70,000, or Maiso-ryo of JPY 50,000 under Employees' Health Insurance) within 2 years [5].
  • Commercial banks and quasi-final income tax return: Once a Japanese bank is notified of an account holder's death, all sole bank accounts are immediately frozen until succession documentation is presented [1]. Under the rules of the National Tax Agency, if the deceased had self-employment, rental, or reportable income requiring a tax return, the heirs must file a quasi-final income tax return (Jun-Kakutei Shinkoku) and pay any income tax owed within 4 months from the day after learning of the death [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Inheritance Tax
steps.html:
• 3-month deadline for renunciation or qualified acceptance: Under the Civil Code of Japan, heirs automatically inherit both assets and debts unless they file a petition for Renunciation of Inheritance (Sozoku Hoki) or Qualified Acceptance (Gentei Shonin) with the Family Court (Katei Saibansho) within 3 months of learning of the death and their status as heir [4].
  • Probate of wills (Kennin) and estate division (Isan Bunkatsu Kyogisho): If the deceased left a handwritten will (Jihitsu Shosho Yuigon) that was not stored in the Legal Affairs Bureau's registry, do not open a sealed envelope yourself; submit it to the Family Court for formal verification (Kennin) [1] [4]. A Notarial Deed Will (Kosei Shosho Yuigon) or a handwritten will deposited under the Ministry of Justice storage system does not require Family Court Kennin [1] [4]. If there is no will, all statutory heirs must sign and seal (with registered Jitsuin seals and Inkan Shomeisho certificates) a formal Estate Division Agreement (Isan Bunkatsu Kyogisho) to unfreeze bank accounts and transfer assets [1].
  • Mandatory real estate inheritance registration and 10-month Inheritance Tax return: Under the revised Real Property Registration Act enforced by the Legal Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Justice, heirs must register inherited real estate (Sozoku Toki) within 3 years of learning of the inheritance (or face an administrative fine up to JPY 100,000) [1]. If the net taxable estate exceeds the basic exemption of JPY 30 million + (JPY 6 million × number of statutory heirs), heirs must file an Inheritance Tax (Sozokuzei) return and pay the tax in cash to the National Tax Agency within 10 months from the day after death [3].
  • Cross-border heirs: If a statutory heir resides outside Japan or is a foreign citizen without a Japanese registered seal (Inkan), they execute a Signature Certificate (Shomei Shomeisho) at a Japanese embassy/consulate abroad or before a foreign notary (with Apostille) to validate the Estate Division Agreement [1].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical Death Certificate (Shibou Shindansho)Immediately upon deathAttending physician or police medical examiner
2. Death Notification (Shibou Todoke) & Cremation PermitWithin 7 days of learning of the deathMunicipal Ward or City Office (under Ministry of Justice oversight)
3. Pension & Health Insurance notificationsWithin 10 to 14 days of deathJapan Pension Service and Municipal Health Insurance Division
4. Renunciation of Inheritance / Quasi-Final Income TaxWithin 3 months (Family Court) / 4 months (Income Tax)Family Court and National Tax Agency
5. Inheritance Tax return & Real Estate RegistrationWithin 10 months (Tax) / 3 years (Real Estate)National Tax Agency and Ministry of Justice Legal Affairs Bureau

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Japan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Japan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Japan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Japan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their autonomy and prevents account freezes or administrative delays for the family. Below, we set out the five key steps in chronological order under the laws of Japan.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Long-Term Care Insurance, and Medical Cost Ceilings
steps.html:
• Palliative care and home visiting medicine: Through the treating hospital's Medical Support and Patient Consultation Center (Chiiki Iryo Renkei Shitsu), coordinate referral to an inpatient palliative care ward (kanwa kea byoutou) or a 24-hour home-visit medical clinic (zaitaku Ryouyou Shien Shinryousho) and visiting nursing station (houmon kango) regulated under the national framework described by the World Health Organization [5] [6].
  • High-Cost Medical Expense Benefit (Kougaku Ryouyouhi Seido): Apply to the ill person's public health insurer (municipal National Health Insurance or employer health insurance association) for an Eligibility Certificate for Ceiling-Amount Application (Gendogaku Tekiyou Ninteisho), or verify automatic linkage via their My Number health insurance card, so monthly out-of-pocket hospital and pharmacy bills are capped at the statutory income-based limit at the counter [5] [6].
  • Long-Term Care Insurance (Kaigo Hoken) certification: For patients aged 65 or older - or aged 40 to 64 with a specified condition including terminal cancer - submit an application for Long-Term Care Need Certification (You-Kaigo Nintei) at the municipal ward or city office (Shiyakusho / Kuyakusho) [5] [6]. Once certified, a care manager (kea maneejaa) coordinates subsidised home-visit nursing, welfare equipment rental (such as electric hospital beds), and home-care aides at a 10% to 30% co-payment [5].

steps.title: Record Advance Care Planning (*Jinsei Kaigi*) and Designate a Healthcare Spokesperson
steps.html:
• Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare ACP guidelines: Japan does not have a single binding statutory living-will statute that overrides clinical consensus; instead, hospitals and home-care physicians follow the official Decision-Making Process Guidelines for Medical and Long-Term Care in the Final Stage of Life (promoted nationwide as Jinsei Kaigi or Advance Care Planning) [6].
  • Written statement of treatment preferences (Songenshi Sengensho): While your family member has full mental capacity, they should document their preferences in writing regarding artificial hydration and nutrition, mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (DNAR), and preferred place of care (home versus hospital palliative ward), and share copies with the attending physician and family [1] [6].
  • Designating a trusted healthcare representative: Under the Jinsei Kaigi framework, when a patient can no longer express their wishes, the multidisciplinary medical team consults the person appointed by the patient (or the family) to determine the patient's presumed wishes [6]. Naming this primary medical spokesperson explicitly inside a Notarial Voluntary Guardianship Contract or Notarial Mandate executed before a notary under the Ministry of Justice gives hospitals clear proof of whom to consult [1] [4].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Mandates, Voluntary Guardianship, and Bank Proxy Access While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Why private powers of attorney are often rejected by Japanese banks: In Japan, standard private powers of attorney (Ininjo) frequently cease to be accepted by commercial banks once the account holder's cognitive or physical capacity declines, and banks strictly freeze accounts if dementia or incapacity becomes apparent without a registered court or notarial mechanism [1] [4].
  • Voluntary Guardianship Contract (Nin'i Koken Keiyaku) and Notarial Mandate (Inin Keiyaku): While the ill person retains full decision-making capacity, arrange an appointment at a Notary Public Office (Koshonin Yakuba, supervised by the Legal Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Justice) - or request a hospital/home bedside visit by the notary - to execute a combined Property Management Mandate Contract (Zaisan Kanri Inin Keiyaku) (effective immediately while capacity is intact) and a Voluntary Guardianship Contract (Nin'i Koken Keiyaku) (which takes effect once the Family Court appoints a Voluntary Guardianship Supervisor if capacity later declines) [1] [4]. The notary registers the voluntary guardianship directly in the Legal Affairs Bureau registry [1].
  • Registered bank agent cards (Dairi Card) and Civil Trust (Kazoku Shintaku): While your family member can still communicate with their bank, complete each bank's formal Registered Agent (Dairinin Touroku) procedure to issue a second agent ATM/counter card, or consult a judicial scrivener/attorney regarding a Civil Family Trust (Kazoku Shintaku) so designated funds for medical and care expenses remain accessible without freezing [1] [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Sickness Allowances, and Caregiver Leave Benefits
steps.html:
• Injury and Sickness Allowance (Shoubyou Teatekin): If the ill person is an employee enrolled in Employees' Health Insurance (Kenkou Hoken) and cannot work due to treatment, they can claim the statutory Injury and Sickness Allowance paying approximately two-thirds of standard remuneration for up to 1 year and 6 months [5].
  • Disability Pension (Shougai Nenkin): If the illness causes severe functional impairment meeting statutory disability grade criteria (typically 1 year and 6 months after the first clinical consultation date shoshin-bi, or earlier for specific permanent impairments), file a claim with the Japan Pension Service for Disability Basic Pension (Shougai Kiso Nenkin) and Disability Employees' Pension (Shougai Kosei Nenkin) [2] [5].
  • Statutory Caregiver Leave (Kaigo Kyugyo) and Employment Insurance benefits: Under the Child Care and Family Care Leave Act, an employed family member caring for a relative requiring constant care may take up to 93 days of statutory Caregiver Leave (which can be split into up to 3 periods) plus up to 5 days per year of short-term nursing care leave, and claim the Caregiver Leave Benefit (Kaigo Kyugyo Kyufukin) covering 67% of pre-leave wages through Hello Work [5].

steps.title: Review the Will, Family Register Records, and Inheritance Tax Preparation
steps.html:
• Executing a Notarial Deed Will (Kosei Shosho Yuigon) or Legal Affairs Bureau Stored Will: Under the Civil Code of Japan, the safest way to avoid post-death Family Court probate (Kennin) and bank release delays is to execute a Notarial Deed Will (Kosei Shosho Yuigon) before a notary (under the Ministry of Justice) in the presence of two witnesses, or to deposit a compliant handwritten will (Jihitsu Shosho Yuigon) in person under the Legal Affairs Bureau Self-Handwritten Will Storage System [1] [4].
  • Statutory reserved share (Iryubun) and Civil Status records: When drafting a will, account for the statutory reserved share (Iryubun) granted to a surviving spouse, children, and lineal ascendants (generally one-half of the statutory intestate share) [1] [4]. Obtain current copies of the Family Register (Koseki Tohon), Registered Seal Certificate (Inkan Shomeisho), and real estate registry transcripts (Touki Jikou Shomeisho) from the municipal office and Legal Affairs Bureau [1].
  • Advance Inheritance Tax (Sozokuzei) review and Post-Death Bank Withdrawal Mandate: Review whether the net estate exceeds the National Tax Agency basic exemption of JPY 30 million + (JPY 6 million × number of statutory heirs), clarify life insurance death-benefit tax exemptions (JPY 5 million × number of statutory heirs), and consider adding a Notarial Post-Death Affairs Mandate (Shigo Jimu Inin Keiyaku) so the appointed representative can pay final hospital and funeral bills promptly [1] [3].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. High-Cost Medical Expense cap & Care InsuranceImmediately upon diagnosis / hospitalizationMunicipal Health Insurance & Long-Term Care Insurance Division
2. Advance Care Planning (Jinsei Kaigi)While the patient can express treatment wishesAttending clinical team & healthcare representative
3. Notarial Mandate & Voluntary GuardianshipWhile full legal decision-making capacity is intactNotary Public Office (under the Ministry of Justice) & Family Court
4. Sickness Allowance, Disability Pension & Care LeaveDuring treatment / upon meeting eligibility rulesJapan Pension Service, Health Insurer & Hello Work
5. Notarial Deed Will & Inheritance Tax reviewBefore any decline in testamentary capacityNotary Public Office, Ministry of Justice & National Tax Agency
