title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malaysia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malaysia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Malaysia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
When a family member in Malaysia is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, organizing palliative medical care, advance care planning, powers of attorney, provident fund and social security disability benefits, and succession documents while the ill person retains full mental and legal capacity significantly eases the burden on the family. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps to follow under the laws of Malaysia.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Coordinate Palliative Care and Health CoverageImmediately upon clinical diagnosisMinistry of Health Malaysia (Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia - KKM)
2. Record Advance Care Plan and Medical PreferencesWhile full mental capacity is intactMinistry of Health Malaysia (Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia - KKM) / Treating Hospital
3. Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank MandatesBefore any loss of mental capacity (High Court registration)Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia / LHDN
4. Activate EPF (KWSP), PERKESO, and JKM BenefitsUpon medical board or physician certificationEPF (KWSP) / PERKESO (SOCSO) / Department of Social Welfare (JKM)
5. Review the Will, Nominations, and Civil RecordsWhile full testamentary capacity remains intactNational Registration Department of Malaysia (Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara - JPN)

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public Hospital Palliative Care Units and Domiciliary Care: The Ministry of Health Malaysia (Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia - KKM) operates specialized Palliative Medicine Units and pain clinics at major state and specialist hospitals across Malaysia (including Hospital Selayang, Hospital Kuala Lumpur, National Cancer Institute / Institut Kanser Negara in Putrajaya, Hospital Pulau Pinang, Hospital Queen Elizabeth in Kota Kinabalu, and Sarawak General Hospital) [4] [6]. Public health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan) also coordinate domiciliary palliative care (Perkhidmatan Perawatan Domisiliari) for homebound patients [4].
  • Community Hospice Organizations: Alongside public hospital services, registered non-profit community hospice providers (such as Hospis Malaysia, Kasih Hospice Foundation, and state hospice societies) provide free community palliative home nursing, medical equipment loans, and symptom management upon referral from the treating physician [4] [6].
  • Public Healthcare Subsidies and Private Medical Takaful/Insurance: Malaysian citizens treated at public facilities under the Ministry of Health Malaysia (Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia - KKM) receive heavily subsidized inpatient care, oncology treatment, and controlled analgesic medications, while low-income households under the PeKa B40 and Skim Perubatan MADANI frameworks qualify for additional support [4] [6]. If the ill person holds private medical insurance or Takaful, the family should request a Guarantee Letter (GL) and verify outpatient oncology and palliative coverage limits early [4].

steps.title: Record Advance Care Planning (ACP) and Healthcare Preferences
steps.html:
• Advance Care Planning (Perancangan Awal Penjagaan - ACP) in Malaysia: While Malaysia does not yet have a standalone statute creating a binding statutory registry for living wills or healthcare proxies, the Ministry of Health Malaysia (Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia - KKM) and the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC) recognize Advance Care Planning (ACP) as an established clinical framework [4] [6].
  • Documenting Resuscitation and Life-Sustaining Treatment Preferences: While the ill person retains full decision-making capacity, they should conduct a structured ACP consultation with their attending specialist to document preferences regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation (Do Not Attempt Resuscitation / DNAR orders), mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, and preferred place of care [4]. These written instructions are signed and placed prominently in the hospital medical record.
  • Naming a Spokesperson for Clinical Consultations: Although a third party cannot legally override a competent patient's wishes, naming a primary family spokesperson in the medical chart helps the clinical team under the Ministry of Health Malaysia (Kementerian Kesihatan Malaysia - KKM) communicate consistently with the family if the patient loses consciousness or capacity [4].

steps.title: Execute Valid Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Powers of Attorney Act 1949 (Act 400) Requirements: In Peninsular Malaysia, a formal Power of Attorney (Surat Kuasa Wakil) authorizing an attorney-in-fact to manage property, legal affairs, and financial transactions is governed by the Powers of Attorney Act 1949 (in Sabah and Sarawak, governed by respective state stamping and registration ordinances) [2]. To be legally valid in Peninsular Malaysia, the Power of Attorney must be executed while the donor has full mental capacity, authenticated using the statutory verification certificate by an Advocate and Solicitor, Commissioner for Oaths, Notary Public, or Magistrate, stamped through the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (Lembaga Hasil Dalam Negeri Malaysia - LHDN), and deposited for registration at the Registry of the High Court overseen by the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia [2] [3].
  • Important Mental Capacity Limitation in Malaysia: Unlike jurisdictions that have enacted Lasting Power of Attorney legislation, a standard Power of Attorney in Malaysia (unless granted as an irrevocable power for valuable consideration) is generally revoked by operation of law if the donor becomes mentally incapacitated under the Mental Health Act 2001, at which point family members would have to apply to the High Court for a committee of the estate [2].
  • Bank Signatory Mandates and Joint Account Planning: Because Malaysian commercial banks apply strict internal compliance rules to third-party Powers of Attorney, the ill person should contact their banks directly while mobile and lucid to set up bank-approved third-party mandates, standing instructions for medical and household bills, or appropriate account arrangements [2].

steps.title: Activate EPF (KWSP), PERKESO (SOCSO), and Social Welfare Benefits
steps.html:
• EPF (KWSP) Health and Incapacitation Withdrawals: Under the Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, an insured member diagnosed with a critical illness or requiring costly medical equipment may apply for a Health Withdrawal (Pengeluaran Kesihatan) from Account Sejahtera (Account 2) to fund approved medical expenses [5]. Furthermore, if the member becomes permanently physically or mentally incapacitated from engaging in any employment, they may apply for a full Incapacitation Withdrawal (Pengeluaran Hilang Upaya) plus a compassionate RM 5,000 Incapacitation Benefit (Bantuan Hilang Upaya) [5].
  • PERKESO (SOCSO) Invalidity Pension and Constant Attendance Allowance: Private-sector employees insured under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 who suffer from a permanent incurable condition rendering them incapable of earning at least one-third of a normal worker's customary earnings can apply to PERKESO for an Invalidity Pension (Pencen Ilat) or Invalidity Grant, certified by a Medical Board [5]. If the recipient is so severely incapacitated as to constantly require the personal attendance of another person, PERKESO also pays a statutory Constant Attendance Allowance (Elaun Layanan Sentiasa equal to 40% of the invalidity pension rate, up to RM 500 per month) [5].
  • Department of Social Welfare (JKM) OKU Registration and Caregiver Allowance: Registering the ill person as a Person with Disabilities (Orang Kurang Upaya - OKU) with the Department of Social Welfare (Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat - JKM) unlocks public hospital fee exemptions and eligibility for the Financial Assistance for Caregivers of Bedridden Disabled and Chronically Ill Persons (Bantuan Pesakit Kronik Terlantar - BPT) for qualifying households [4] [5].

steps.title: Review the Will, Beneficiary Nominations, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Non-Muslim Wills vs. Muslim Wasiat and Hibah:
    • Non-Muslim Citizens: Under the Wills Act 1959 (applicable in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak; Wills Ordinance Cap. 158 in Sabah), a non-Muslim testator aged 18 or older (21 in Sabah) with sound testamentary capacity may execute a written Will signed in the presence of two independent witnesses (neither of whom is a beneficiary or the spouse of a beneficiary) naming an executor to streamline a future Grant of Probate at the High Court overseen by the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court of Malaysia [2].
    • Muslim Citizens: For Muslims in Malaysia, testamentary disposition by Wasiat is generally limited to one-third (1/3) of the net estate in favor of non-Faraid heirs (unless all Faraid heirs consent after death), while the remaining two-thirds pass according to Islamic inheritance law (Hukum Faraid) [2]. Muslim property owners may also execute inter vivos Islamic estate planning instruments such as Hibah (lifetime gift) or Deklarasi Harta Sepencarian (matrimonial property declaration) through state Islamic councils (Majlis Agama Islam Negeri), Amanah Raya, or Syariah legal practitioners [2].
  • Updating EPF (KWSP) and Insurance Nominations: Verify that KWSP (EPF), Tabung Haji (for Muslims), and life insurance / Takaful nominations are updated. Note that for non-Muslims, an EPF nominee receives the funds as a direct beneficiary, whereas for Muslims, an EPF nominee acts as an administrator (wasi) obligated to distribute the funds in accordance with Faraid unless supported by an eligible Hibah structure [5].
  • Verifying JPN Civil Records and Cross-Border Documents: Confirm that MyKad identity cards, marriage certificates, and children's birth certificates registered with the National Registration Department of Malaysia (Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara - JPN) contain no spelling or identity-number discrepancies [1]. Any property transfer deeds or powers of attorney should be properly stamped with the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (Lembaga Hasil Dalam Negeri Malaysia - LHDN), and cross-border documents for assets or relatives abroad must undergo consular legalization through Wisma Putra [1] [3].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Maldives: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Maldives: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Maldives: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in the Maldives. When a death occurs in the Republic of Maldives, the family or legal representative must complete a structured sequence of medical, civil registration, municipal burial or repatriation, social security, and Family Court inheritance procedures. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps to follow in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or health center deaths: When your family member dies in a tertiary hospital in Male' (such as Indira Gandhi Memorial Hospital, ADK Hospital, or Tree Top Hospital), a regional or atoll hospital, or an island health center regulated by the Ministry of Health, the attending physician examines the body and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (commonly referred to in Dhivehi as the Maru Form) [1, 2]. You should present the deceased's Maldivian National Identity Card (or passport for a foreign national) so that personal particulars match civil registry records [2, 3].
  • Deaths at home or on outer islands: If the death occurs at a private residence, aboard a vessel, or on an island or resort outside a hospital setting, you must immediately notify the nearest health facility or island health center and the local Island Council or City Council so a licensed medical officer can attend, verify the death, and issue the medical certification [1, 2].
  • Sudden, unexplained, or unnatural deaths: If the death is sudden, accidental, suspicious, or occurs without recent medical attendance, the Maldives Police Service must be notified immediately before the body is moved [2]. Police officers and medical examiners regulated under the Ministry of Health conduct an investigation and forensic or medico-legal assessment before releasing the body and issuing the medical death form required for burial and civil registration [1, 2].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Local council notification and statutory registration window: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act of the Maldives, every death must be reported to the relevant local council - the Male' City Council (or other City Council) or the respective Island Council where the death occurred - using the hospital-issued Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and the deceased's National Identity Card [1, 3]. While immediate reporting is required prior to burial clearance, formal civil registration and certificate applications are typically lodged within seven days of the death [1].
  • Digital application via oneGov and the Department of National Registration: Official Death Certificates are requested online through the central government service portal oneGov (using an eFaas digital identity login) or through the local council and the Department of National Registration [1, 3] [3]. The application requires the completed Death Registration Form, the medical death notification form stamped by the hospital or health center, and the identity details of both the deceased and the applicant [1].
  • Verification of civil status and national identity records: Once the local council verifies the death record, the central civil database maintained by the Department of National Registration is updated to cancel the deceased's National Identity Card, and certified copies of the Death Certificate (in Dhivehi and English where required for legal or cross-border use) are issued within approximately three working days [1, 3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Mortuary Services, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Islamic burial and municipal cemetery coordination: For Maldivian citizens and Muslim residents, funeral rites (Janaaza), ritual washing (Ghusl), shrouding (Kafan), funeral prayer, and burial at designated municipal cemeteries (such as the Aasaharaa cemetery complex in Male' or the local island cemetery) are coordinated directly through the City Council or Island Council Funeral Services unit immediately upon presentation of the stamped medical death form [1, 2]. Cremation facilities are not operated domestically in the Maldives.
  • Resort, foreign national, or international repatriation procedures: When a foreign national dies in the Maldives or when a family wishes to repatriate remains abroad for burial or cremation, the hospital mortuary, the Ministry of Health, the Maldives Police Service, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs coordinate the mortuary preservation, embalming or zinc-lined coffin sealing, infection-free certificate, and no-objection clearance for air cargo export [2].
  • Consular legalization and authentication of documents: Because the Maldives is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, Maldivian Death Certificates, medical cause-of-death reports, and court documents intended for use in a foreign jurisdiction must be issued or translated in English and authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Male', followed by consular legalization at the relevant foreign embassy or high commission [1, 3].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Social Protection, Tax, and Banking Institutions
steps.html:
• Maldives Pension Administration Office notification and RSA distribution: You should notify the Maldives Pension Administration Office promptly if the deceased contributed to the Maldives Retirement Pension Scheme (MRPS) or received the Basic Pension [4]. When an MRPS member dies before or during retirement, the accumulated balance in their Retirement Savings Account (RSA) is payable to their legal heirs; claimants submit the Death Certificate, the Family Court inheritance judgment, and heir identity documents via the pension portal or client services counter [4].
  • National Social Protection Agency and Aasandha health coverage: Contact the National Social Protection Agency to cease any ongoing disability allowance, single-parent support, or medical welfare benefits and to check whether surviving dependents qualify for statutory social protection allowances [5]. The deceased's public health insurance enrollment with Aasandha Company is terminated automatically once the Department of National Registration updates the civil death database [3, 5].
  • Banks, employers, and the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority: Present certified copies of the Death Certificate to Maldivian commercial banks (such as Bank of Maldives or Maldives Islamic Bank) to freeze individual accounts and obtain date-of-death balance statements for the court estate inventory. If the deceased owned a registered business, rental property, or held tax obligations, the legal representative should also notify the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority (MIRA) and settle any final employer wages or civil service benefits.

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Complete Family Court Succession (*Varoosaa*)
steps.html:
• Filing an inheritance (Tharika / Varoosaa) case at the Family Court: In the Maldives, succession and estate distribution are governed by Islamic Sharia principles and administered by the Family Court of the Maldives in Male' or the respective Island Magistrate Court [6]. The family or an heir must file a formal petition to confirm legal heirs (Varoosaa Sabithukurun) and administer the estate (Tharika), attaching the official Death Certificate, National Identity Cards of all potential heirs, marriage or birth certificates, and a schedule of known assets and liabilities [1, 6].
  • Settlement of debts, wills (Wasiyyath), and statutory shares: Under Maldivian succession rules, funeral expenses and verified debts of the deceased (including housing loans, unpaid taxes, or personal liabilities) are settled first from the gross estate, followed by any valid bequest (Wasiyyath, which may not exceed one-third of the net estate to non-heirs without the consent of legal heirs), before the Family Court of the Maldives calculates and orders the distribution of the remaining estate and Maldives Pension Administration Office balances among the Quranic heirs [4, 6].
  • Property transfers and cross-border heirs: Once the court issues the final inheritance decree, heirs present the judgment to banks, the Maldives Pension Administration Office, the Ministry of Housing/Land Registry, or transport authorities to transfer land plots, vessels, and bank funds into the heirs' names [4, 6]. If an heir resides outside the Maldives or if assets are held abroad, the heir may appoint a representative via a power of attorney recognized by the court, and foreign-used decrees must undergo consular legalization [6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance, did the death occur in Male' or on an outer island or resort, and did your family member hold Maldivian citizenship or assets in multiple jurisdictions?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Maldives: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Maldives: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Maldives: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in the Maldives is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, financial, and family welfare arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and decision-making capacity reduces administrative burdens and protects the person's wishes. Below, we outline the five key official and practical steps to take in order in the Republic of Maldives.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Medical Support, and Aasandha Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist clinical management and palliative care: Coordinate an integrated care plan through the treating oncology, internal medicine, or palliative care team at a tertiary facility in Male' (such as Indira Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Hulhumale' Hospital, ADK Hospital, or Tree Top Hospital) or the designated regional/atoll hospital overseen by the Ministry of Health [1]. Ask the lead specialist to issue a comprehensive medical summary detailing the diagnosis, symptom-management protocol, pain-relief prescriptions, and home-nursing requirements [1].
  • Public health insurance under the Aasandha scheme: For Maldivian citizens, verify coverage with Aasandha Company, which administers the national social health insurance scheme (Husnuvaa Aasandha) covering inpatient treatment, outpatient specialist consultations, prescription medications, and approved medical referrals abroad when specialized care is unavailable locally [2].
  • Emergency medical welfare and therapeutic equipment: When a patient requires specialized home-care consumables, oxygen concentrators, hospital beds, or financial assistance beyond standard insurance limits, submit the specialist's clinical report and cost estimates to the National Social Protection Agency under its Medical Welfare and assistive-device support programs [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Documenting clinical treatment preferences: The Maldives does not currently have a standalone statutory Living Will Registry, and active euthanasia or physician-assisted dying is prohibited under Maldivian law and Islamic medical ethics. However, while your family member has full mental capacity, they can discuss and record clear written care preferences with their treating physician at the facility regulated by the Ministry of Health - covering pain management, palliative sedation, artificial nutrition, and whether to withhold non-beneficial cardiopulmonary resuscitation in end-stage illness [1].
  • Designating a primary family medical representative: Hospitals in the Maldives rely on the patient's designated next-of-kin or legally authorized family representative when the patient can no longer communicate [1]. Ensure the hospital medical file explicitly names the primary family contact and records their Maldivian National Identity Card details and telephone number so there is no ambiguity among relatives during urgent clinical consultations [1, 4].
  • Maintaining accessible medical records via eFaas and Vinavi: Keep certified copies of the diagnostic summary, medication list, and Aasandha Company referral authorizations accessible both in print and through the family's authorized digital health portals so island health centers or emergency responders can verify the care plan immediately [1, 2].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Executing a formal Power of Attorney (Wakeelukamuge Liyun): While your family member retains full legal and mental capacity, they should execute a written Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage administrative filings, property matters, court appearances, or government transactions on their behalf. To ensure legal validity in the Maldives, the Power of Attorney should be drafted clearly in Dhivehi (or English where required for corporate or international use), signed before two witnesses, and registered or notarized through a licensed Maldivian legal practitioner or the relevant court registry [5].
  • Setting up commercial bank mandates: Maldivian commercial banks (such as Bank of Maldives and Maldives Islamic Bank) frequently require customers to complete the bank's own account-operation mandate or third-party authorization form in person (or via a verified bedside bank visit if the account holder is hospitalized) rather than relying solely on a general power of attorney. Arrange this while your family member can clearly confirm their instructions using their National Identity Card issued by the Department of National Registration [4].
  • Digital government access (eFaas and oneGov): Because civil, land, and pension services in the Maldives rely heavily on the eFaas digital identity and the oneGov portal, review how essential bills, tax filings, and public service applications will be managed lawfully without sharing personal biometric credentials [4, 6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Allowances, Critical-Illness Support, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• National Disability Registration and monthly allowance: If the progressive illness results in a long-term physical, sensory, or functional impairment, apply to the National Social Protection Agency to register the person on the National Register of Persons with Disabilities under the Disability Act (Law No. 8/2010), which provides a monthly financial disability allowance and grants for therapeutic care and assistive equipment [3].
  • Maldives Retirement Pension Scheme (MRPS) review: If the ill person is a contributor to the Maldives Retirement Pension Scheme, contact the Maldives Pension Administration Office to review their Retirement Savings Account (RSA) statement, confirm employment contribution status, and check eligibility for early pension access or medical withdrawal provisions under current pension regulations [6].
  • Statutory family caregiver leave under the Employment Act: Family members employed in the Maldives should notify their employer's human resources department and present a medical certificate from a practitioner registered with the Ministry of Health to claim paid family care leave (up to ten days per year under the Maldivian Employment Act to care for an immediately ill family member) or negotiate extended flexible or unpaid caregiving leave [1].

steps.title: Organize the Will (*Wasiyyath*), Civil Status Documents, and Estate Records
steps.html:
• Preparing a valid Wasiyyath (will) and reviewing succession rules: Under Maldivian law, succession is governed by Islamic Sharia principles administered by the Family Court of the Maldives [5]. While capacity is intact, your family member may execute a written Wasiyyath before witnesses or apply to verify it through the Family Court of the Maldives; under Sharia rules, bequests to non-heirs are valid up to one-third of the net estate after funeral costs and debts, whereas statutory shares for legal heirs (Varoosaa) are fixed by law unless all adult heirs consent after the testator's passing [5].
  • Consolidating civil identity and family records: Gather the ill person's National Identity Card (verified with the Department of National Registration), birth certificate, marriage certificates, divorce decrees, and the National Identity Cards of all children, spouse(s), and parents so that the family register is complete and unambiguous [4, 5].
  • Documenting debts, property titles, and cross-border assets: Prepare a clear written inventory of all real estate and land registry certificates, vessels, business shares, bank accounts, Maldives Pension Administration Office RSA balances, and outstanding liabilities or personal debts (which must be settled before estate distribution) [5, 6]. If the ill person owns assets abroad or has foreign-resident family members, coordinate separate powers of attorney and estate instruments legalized through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant foreign embassy.

closingQuestion: To help us provide more specific guidance, is your family member currently receiving care in Male' or on an outer atoll, and are there specific banking, pension, or property arrangements you need to prioritize?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Marshall Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Marshall Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Marshall Islands: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Following a death in the Marshall Islands, the family or legal representative must complete medical death certification, civil registration under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social security notifications, and High Court estate probate. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps to follow in order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital deaths in Majuro or Ebeye: When a death occurs at Leroij Atama Zedkaia Memorial Hospital (Majuro Public Hospital) in Majuro or Leroij Kitlang Memorial Health Center in Ebeye (Kwajalein Atoll), the attending physician under the Ministry of Health and Human Services examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1]. You should provide the deceased's Marshall Islands passport, birth certificate, or national identification card so personal details are recorded accurately [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home or on outer atolls: If your family member dies at a private residence or on an outer island or atoll served by a local health dispensary, the local health assistant and local government council notify the Ministry of Health and Human Services so a certifying medical officer can verify the circumstances of death and complete the medical death report [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: When a death is unexpected, unattended by a physician, or involves suspected trauma or unnatural causes, the Marshall Islands Police Department (under the Ministry of Justice) must be notified immediately before the body is moved [1]. Police investigators and the medical examiner conduct a medico-legal inquiry and, where ordered by the Attorney General's Office or High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, a post-mortem examination at the hospital mortuary before releasing the remains [1] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Filing with the Registrar General / Office of Vital Statistics: Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Title 26 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code), the medical certificate of death must be submitted to the Office of the Registrar General (Vital Statistics) in Majuro or the local government registrar in the municipality where the death occurred [1] [3]. Standard registration should be completed promptly following the death and prior to final disposition or export of remains [1].
  • Delayed registration of death through the court: If a death occurred on a remote outer atoll or was not recorded within the statutory period, the family must file a formal Petition for Delayed Registration of Death with the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands using the judiciary's official self-represented litigant forms and pay the prescribed court filing fee [3] [4].
  • Requesting certified copies of the Death Certificate: Once the death is entered in the civil register, obtain multiple certified copies of the official Republic of the Marshall Islands Death Certificate, as original sealed certificates are required for Marshall Islands Social Security Administration claims, bank closures, High Court probate petitions, and cross-border legal filings [1, 3, 5].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Mortuary Services, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Hospital mortuary storage, local burial, and customary rites: Mortuary refrigeration and embalming services in the Marshall Islands are handled primarily through the public hospital morgues operated by the Ministry of Health and Human Services in Majuro and Ebeye [1]. Local burial takes place at designated community or family land plots with permission from the relevant municipal government and traditional landowners, accompanied by the medical certificate of death and burial permit [1]. Domestic cremation facilities are not available in the Marshall Islands [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased is to be repatriated abroad (for example, to the United States or another Pacific or Asian jurisdiction), the Ministry of Health and Human Services prepares the body, performs arterial embalming, seals the casket in an airline-compliant hermetically sealed shipping container, and issues the Certificate of Embalming, Non-Contagious Disease Certificate, and export transit permit [1]. For deceased U.S. citizens, the U.S. Embassy in the Republic of the Marshall Islands issues the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad and disposition documentation [1].
  • Hague Apostille and consular coordination: The Republic of the Marshall Islands is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. When an official Marshall Islands Death Certificate or court order must be used in another Apostille member state (such as the United States), obtain an Apostille certificate through the designated competent authority (Office of the Attorney General / Registrar); Marshallese families residing in the United States under the Compact of Free Association may also coordinate document verification guidance through the Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands [1] [2].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Marshall Islands Social Security Administration survivor and lump-sum benefits: Notify the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA) in Majuro or Ebeye as soon as the Death Certificate is issued [5]. Under the Social Security Act, surviving spouses, dependent children, and eligible dependent parents of an insured worker may claim monthly survivor pensions as well as a statutory lump-sum burial/death benefit by submitting the official Death Certificate, marriage and birth certificates, and the deceased's MISSA number [5].
  • Workers' compensation and U.S. Social Security coordination: If the death was work-related, file a claim with the Workers' Compensation Division administered alongside the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration [5]. If the deceased also worked in the United States or received U.S. federal benefits, notify the U.S. Social Security Administration or the Consular Section at the U.S. Embassy in the Republic of the Marshall Islands [1] [5].
  • Bank accounts, employers, and passport cancellation: Present certified Death Certificates to local banks (such as Bank of Marshall Islands or Bank of Guam in Majuro) to freeze individual accounts and request date-of-death balance letters for probate [3]. Notify the deceased's employer (or the Public Service Commission for civil servants) to process final accrued wages and life insurance, and surrender the deceased's passport for cancellation [2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and File for Probate at the High Court
steps.html:
• Filing a Probate Petition with the High Court: Estate administration in the Marshall Islands is governed by the Probate Code (Title 25 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code) and the Marshall Islands Rules of Civil Procedure before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands [3] [6]. The executor or next-of-kin files a formal Probate Petition, Probate Notice Order, and Probate Announcement with the Clerk of Courts, attaching the original will (if any), the certified Death Certificate, an inventory of estate assets and debts, and the scheduled court filing fee [3, 4, 6].
  • Customary wills (Kalimur) and traditional land tenure: In the Marshall Islands, personal property, bank funds, and statutory death benefits are administered through High Court probate, whereas rights to customary land (bwidrej) are governed by Marshallese matrilineal custom and customary testamentary dispositions (kalimur) [3] [6]. When a probate dispute involves customary land titles or Iroij, Alap, and Senior Dri Jerbal interests, the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands may certify customary questions to the Traditional Rights Court for determination [6].
  • Court notice period, creditor claims, and cross-border assets: After the Probate Notice Order is published and the statutory notice period for creditors and interested heirs expires, the High Court issues Letters Testamentary or Letters of Administration authorizing distribution of the net estate [3] [6]. There is no separate national inheritance tax in the Marshall Islands, though outstanding debts and court fees must be paid before final distribution [4] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Marshall Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Marshall Islands: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Marshall Islands: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in the Republic of the Marshall Islands is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical care coordination, healthcare directives, financial powers of attorney, disability benefits, and estate arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and legal capacity protects their autonomy and supports the family. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to take in order in the Marshall Islands.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Public Health Services, and Off-Island Referral Coverage
steps.html:
• Hospital and home-based palliative care in Majuro and Ebeye: Coordinate a comprehensive symptom-management and palliative care plan through the treating medical team at Leroij Atama Zedkaia Memorial Hospital (Majuro Public Hospital) or Leroij Kitlang Memorial Health Center in Ebeye under the Ministry of Health and Human Services [1]. For patients returning to a family residence or outer atoll, obtain a detailed clinical summary, pain-management prescription schedule, and outer-island dispensary nursing instructions from the attending physician [1].
  • Marshall Islands Health Fund and off-island medical referral: Verify the ill person's enrollment and benefit coverage under the Basic Health Fund and Supplemental Health Fund administered alongside the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration and the Ministry of Health and Human Services [1] [2]. When specialized oncology or palliative procedures require off-island referral (for example, to Honolulu, Guam, or Manila), the National Medical Referral Committee reviews clinical documentation prior to authorizing travel [1] [2].
  • Travel and consular readiness for cross-border treatment: If off-island medical care or family caregiving in the United States under the Compact of Free Association is anticipated, ensure the ill person and accompanying caregiver hold valid Marshall Islands passports and certified civil status documents through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands [3].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance medical directives and treatment preferences: While your family member retains full decision-making capacity, they should execute a written Advance Healthcare Directive (living will) stating their preferences regarding life-sustaining interventions, mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (DNR orders), artificial nutrition, and palliative pain relief, and file a signed copy in their medical chart at Majuro Public Hospital or Ebeye Health Center [1].
  • Appointing a healthcare proxy or medical representative: In the same written instrument, the ill person should designate a trusted adult family member as their primary healthcare representative (and name an alternate proxy) authorized to make clinical decisions if the patient loses capacity to communicate [1] [4]. Having the directive signed before two adult witnesses and notarized ensures hospital clinicians and the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands can rely on the patient's clear intent [4] [5].
  • Cross-border recognition for off-island hospitals: If the patient may be referred to a hospital in Hawaii, Guam, or the Philippines, prepare the advance directive and durable power of attorney for healthcare in English using standard dual-witness and notarial execution so receiving hospitals recognize the proxy without delay [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• General or Durable Power of Attorney: While your family member has full mental and legal capacity, they should execute a written Power of Attorney authorizing a chosen representative to manage property, administrative filings, social security correspondence, and legal affairs in the Marshall Islands [4] [5]. The document should be signed before a licensed Notary Public or Clerk of the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands [4] [6].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates (Bank of Marshall Islands / Bank of Guam): Local banking institutions operating in Majuro and Ebeye (including Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam) generally require account holders to sign the bank's own power-of-attorney or authorized-signatory forms directly with bank compliance officers while the customer is mentally competent. Arrange an in-branch or verified bedside signing early so household and medical expenses can be paid uninterrupted.
  • Preventing contested guardianship proceedings: Executing valid financial and medical powers of attorney while capacity is intact avoids the need for relatives to file an urgent guardianship or conservatorship petition before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the Marshall Islands Rules of Civil Procedure if the illness later impairs cognition [4, 5, 6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Workers' Compensation, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Marshall Islands Social Security Administration disability benefits: If the illness prevents your family member from engaging in substantial gainful employment and is expected to last at least twelve months or result in end-stage progression, file an application for Disability Insurance Benefits with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MISSA) [2]. The application requires clinical evidence and physician certification on Form MISSA-200 confirming the severity of the impairment, alongside proof of required coverage quarters [2].
  • Work-related illness and U.S. Social Security coordination: If the condition is linked to occupational exposure, check eligibility under the RMI Workers' Compensation program administered with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration [2]. If the ill person previously accrued insured work quarters in the United States, contact the U.S. Social Security Administration or the Consular Section at the U.S. Embassy in the Republic of the Marshall Islands regarding federal disability benefits [1] [2].
  • Public service and employer medical/caregiver leave: If the ill person or a caregiving relative is employed in the Marshall Islands (including under the Public Service Commission), present the attending physician's medical certificate to claim accrued sick leave, compassionate family leave, or an approved leave of absence.

steps.title: Organize Wills, Customary Land Dispositions (*Kalimur*), and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Drafting a written will and addressing customary land (Kalimur): Under the Marshall Islands Probate Code, an adult of sound mind may execute a written will attested by two competent witnesses to govern personal property, bank accounts, and business assets [4] [5]. Where the ill person holds customary land rights (bwidrej) as Iroij, Alap, or Senior Dri Jerbal, any testamentary disposition (kalimur) must comply with Marshallese customary law and lineage consultation rules, which are reviewed by the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the Traditional Rights Court [4] [5].
  • Updating beneficiary designations and civil status records: Review beneficiary designations on life insurance policies, bank accounts, and Marshall Islands Social Security Administration records, and verify that birth certificates, marriage certificates, and passports are accurate and up to date with the Office of the Registrar General and the Embassy of the Republic of the Marshall Islands [2, 3, 4].
  • Cross-border estate and Apostille preparation: Compile a clear inventory of all local and foreign bank accounts, debts, and property titles, and store it with the original will so the designated executor has immediate access to the documents required by the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands [4, 5, 6]. Where powers of attorney or civil documents must be used in another Hague Apostille country, obtain an Apostille certificate through the RMI Registrar / Attorney General's Office [3] [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Micronesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Micronesia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Micronesia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in the Federated States of Micronesia. Because civil registration, public health services, and probate courts operate across both the national framework and the four constituent states (Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, and Kosrae), the family or legal representative must coordinate state hospital certification, court-based vital statistics registration, mortuary or repatriation permits, social security claims, and state court estate proceedings. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps to follow in order.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical certificate of cause of deathImmediately after deathState Hospital / Department of Health and Social Affairs
2. Civil death registration & certificatesPromptly before disposition or exportState Court Vital Statistics Division & Department of Health and Social Affairs
3. Burial, mortuary, or repatriation permitsPrior to burial or international shipmentState Department of Health Services & Embassy of the Federated States of Micronesia
4. Survivor pension & lump-sum death benefitFollowing issuance of Death CertificateFederated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration
5. Estate probate & customary land successionAfter death registrationState Court Probate Division & Supreme Court of the Federated States of Micronesia

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths at state hospitals in Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, or Kosrae: When a death occurs at a state hospital (such as Pohnpei State Hospital in Kolonia, Chuuk State Hospital in Weno, Yap State Hospital in Colonia, or Kosrae State Hospital in Tofol), the attending physician under the state Department of Health Services and the national Department of Health and Social Affairs examines the deceased and completes the official Certificate of Death [1] [2]. You should present the deceased's Federated States of Micronesia passport, birth certificate, or voter identification card so personal particulars are entered accurately [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home or on outer islands and atolls: If your family member died at a private residence or on a remote outer island served by a local health dispensary, the local health assistant and municipal chief or mayor notify the state hospital medical officer so the cause of death can be verified and certified [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unattended deaths: When a death is sudden, unnatural, or occurs without recent medical attendance, the State Police or FSM National Police must be notified immediately before the body is moved [1] [5]. Police officers and the state medical examiner conduct an investigation and, where directed by the State Attorney General or court, a medico-legal autopsy at the state hospital morgue before releasing the remains [1] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death and Obtain Official Death Certificates
steps.html:
• Filing with the State Court and Vital Statistics office: In the Federated States of Micronesia, civil registration of deaths is carried out collaboratively between the state Department of Health Services (which compiles medical vital statistics) and the Clerk of the State Court in Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, or Kosrae, which maintains the legal civil register and issues certified certificates [1]. The physician-signed Certificate of Death must be filed with the state vital statistics registrar and registered with the State Court prior to burial or off-island shipment [1] [2].
  • Late or outer-island death registration: If a death occurs on a distant outer atoll where immediate transport to the state capital is delayed, the municipal magistrate or dispensary officer records the declaration and transmits it to the State Court Clerk for formal entry; if the statutory registration window has elapsed, a petition for delayed registration of death must be approved by the State Court [1] [6].
  • Obtaining certified copies of the Death Certificate: Once the death record is sealed by the State Court registrar, it is advisable to request several certified copies of the official Certificate of Death, as original stamped certificates are required for claims with the Federated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration, bank account settlements, and probate filings [1] [3] [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Mortuary Services, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Hospital mortuary facilities and local burial: Mortuary refrigeration and preparation in the Federated States of Micronesia are provided primarily through the four state hospital morgues in Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, and Kosrae [1] [2]. Local burial takes place on family, clan, or municipal cemetery land in accordance with state public health sanitation permits and municipal customs once the Certificate of Death and burial permit are issued [1] [2]. Domestic cremation facilities are generally not available across the four states [2].
  • International repatriation and shipping of human remains: When remains are transported internationally into or out of the country, strict public health and entry documentation enforced by the Department of Health and Social Affairs and the Embassy of the Federated States of Micronesia applies [2]. Required documents accompanying human remains include a Certified Death Certificate, a Certified Burial-Transit Permit, a Certified Letter of Non-Contagious Disease from the public health authority, an Embalmer's Affidavit confirming arterial embalming and placement in a hermetically sealed casket container, a copy of the deceased's passport or birth certificate, and the airline airwaybill and itinerary [2].
  • Consular legalization and U.S. citizen procedures: The Federated States of Micronesia is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; therefore, official civil and court documents destined for foreign jurisdictions require formal authentication through the Department of Justice / Department of Foreign Affairs in Palikir and consular legalization [2] [5]. If the deceased held U.S. citizenship, the U.S. Embassy in the Federated States of Micronesia in Kolonia assists next-of-kin with local disposition clearance and issues the Consular Report of Death of a U.S. Citizen Abroad [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Survivor pensions and lump-sum death benefits: Under Title 53 of the FSM Code, the Federated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration administers retirement, disability, and survivor insurance from its national headquarters in Palikir (Pohnpei) and branch offices in Chuuk, Yap, and Kosrae [3] [4]. Surviving spouses (aged 60 or older, or caring for eligible dependent children) and unmarried dependent children (under age 18, or up to age 22 if full-time students) may apply for monthly survivor pensions equal to 60% (spouse) and 15% (each child, up to family maximums) of the deceased insured worker's benefit, alongside a statutory lump-sum death benefit where applicable [3] [4].
  • Required claim documentation and U.S. federal benefits: To file a survivor claim with the Federated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration, submit the certified Certificate of Death, the deceased's social security number, certified marriage and birth certificates, and recent tax or wage statements [3]. If the deceased also accrued work credits in the United States or received U.S. federal benefits, notify the U.S. Embassy in the Federated States of Micronesia, which coordinates with the U.S. Social Security Administration Federal Benefits Unit in Manila [4] [5].
  • Banks, employers, and passport cancellation: Present certified Death Certificates to local commercial banks (such as Bank of the Federated States of Micronesia or Bank of Guam) to freeze sole-name accounts, stop automatic deductions, and obtain date-of-death balance confirmations [3] [6]. Notify the deceased's employer or the National/State Office of Personnel to claim final unpaid wages and group life insurance, and surrender the deceased's FSM passport to the Department of Justice Division of Immigration and Labor [5] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession Before the State and National Courts
steps.html:
• Filing for probate in the relevant State Court: Probate of wills, appointment of estate administrators, and succession to personal property and real estate are governed primarily by the laws and Probate Divisions of the respective State Courts (Pohnpei State Supreme Court, Chuuk State Supreme Court, Yap State Court, and Kosrae State Court), while the Supreme Court of the Federated States of Micronesia exercises national appellate and constitutional jurisdiction as well as jurisdiction over diversity disputes between citizens of different states or foreign citizens [6].
  • Customary inheritance and constitutional land restrictions: Under the FSM Constitution and state constitutions, ownership of land in the Federated States of Micronesia is restricted strictly to FSM citizens, and succession to family or clan land in Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, and Kosrae is heavily governed by state statutes and traditional customary law [6]. Even where a deceased person leaves a written will for bank accounts and personal assets, transfers of customary land titles must comply with state lineage, clan, or traditional leadership rules enforced by the state land courts [6].
  • Creditor notices, taxes, and cross-border heirs: The court-appointed executor or administrator inventories the estate, publishes notice to creditors as required by state probate rules, settles valid debts, and distributes the net estate under court supervision [6]. There is no separate national inheritance or estate tax in the Federated States of Micronesia, though foreign heirs who are non-citizens cannot hold title to FSM land directly and must address lease or proceeds arrangements under state law [4] [6].

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative care & MiCare health coverageImmediately upon diagnosisDepartment of Health and Social Affairs & State Hospital
2. Advance healthcare directives & medical proxyWhile decision-making capacity is intactTreating State Hospital & State Court Notary
3. Financial powers of attorney & bank mandatesBefore any loss of legal capacityState Court Clerk / Notary & Local Banks

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Public Health Services, and Off-Island Medical Referral
steps.html:
• State hospital and home-based palliative care: Coordinate a comprehensive symptom-management and palliative care plan through the treating clinical team at the relevant state hospital (Pohnpei State Hospital in Kolonia, Chuuk State Hospital in Weno, Yap State Hospital in Colonia, or Kosrae State Hospital in Tofol) operating under the state Department of Health Services and the national Department of Health and Social Affairs [1]. If the ill person prefers to receive care at home or on an outer island, ask the attending physician for a written pain-management protocol, medication supply plan, and instructions for the local municipal dispensary nurse [1].
  • MiCare Plan coverage and off-island medical referral: Verify the ill person's enrollment and benefit limits under the National Government Employees' Health Insurance Plan (MiCare Plan) or state medical referral programs [1]. When specialized oncology, surgical, or palliative interventions require off-island referral (commonly to Guam, Honolulu, or Manila), the State Medical Referral Committee and MiCare review board must approve the attending physician's referral package before travel [1].
  • Passport and civil document readiness for off-island treatment: Because patients referred abroad or traveling to the United States under the Compact of Free Association require valid travel documents, verify early that the ill person and accompanying family caregiver hold current FSM passports and certified civil status certificates [5] [6].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Written advance medical directive (living will): While your family member retains full mental capacity, they should sign a written Advance Healthcare Directive stating their explicit wishes regarding life-sustaining treatment, mechanical ventilation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (do-not-resuscitate orders), artificial nutrition and hydration, and comfort-focused palliative care, and place a signed copy in their medical record with the state hospital and the Department of Health and Social Affairs [1] [6].
  • Designating a healthcare proxy or medical representative: In the same document, the ill person should appoint a trusted adult relative as their primary healthcare representative (and name an alternate proxy) authorized to make medical decisions if the patient becomes unable to communicate [1] [6]. Executing the directive before two adult witnesses and a Notary Public or Clerk of the State Court provides clear legal proof of the patient's wishes for hospital physicians and the courts [6].
  • Portability for off-island referral hospitals: If the ill person may be referred to a medical facility in Guam, Hawaii, or the Philippines, preparing the advance healthcare directive and durable medical power of attorney in English with formal witness and notarial attestation ensures receiving hospital ethics and admission teams can honor the proxy without delay [1] [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Durable or General Power of Attorney: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they should execute a written Power of Attorney authorizing a reliable representative to manage property, administrative filings, social security correspondence, and legal affairs across the Federated States of Micronesia [6]. The instrument should be executed before a commissioned Notary Public or Clerk of the State Court in Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, or Kosrae [6].
  • Direct commercial bank mandates: Local banking institutions operating in the Federated States of Micronesia (including Bank of the Federated States of Micronesia and Bank of Guam) typically require account holders to complete the bank's own power-of-attorney or joint/authorized signatory mandate forms in person or via verified bedside execution while the customer is mentally competent. Arrange this directly with the branch compliance officer early so household bills and medical travel expenses can be paid smoothly.
  • Avoiding contested court guardianship proceedings: Putting valid financial and healthcare powers of attorney in place while capacity is intact avoids the need for the family to petition the State Court for formal guardianship or conservatorship if the illness later impairs the person's ability to manage their affairs [6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits and Caregiver Leave Support
steps.html:
• FSM Social Security disability insurance benefits: Under Title 53 of the FSM Code, the Federated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration administers Disability Insurance Benefits from its national headquarters in Palikir (Pohnpei) and branch offices in Chuuk, Yap, and Kosrae [2] [3] [4]. An insured worker who is unable to engage in substantial gainful employment due to a severe physical or mental impairment expected to last at least one year or result in terminal progression may claim a monthly disability pension, provided they meet the statutory coverage and recent-contribution requirements [2] [4].
  • Submitting medical certification and U.S. Social Security coordination: To apply, submit the disability application and attending physician's clinical certification to the Federated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration headquarters or state branch office alongside the worker's social security number and birth record [2] [3]. If the ill person also accrued insured work quarters in the United States, contact the U.S. Embassy in the Federated States of Micronesia in Kolonia, which coordinates federal disability inquiries with the U.S. Social Security Administration Federal Benefits Unit in Manila [4] [5].
  • Public service and employer sick or compassionate leave: If the ill person or a caregiving family member works for the national or state government or a private employer, submit the physician's medical certificate to the relevant Office of Personnel or human resources department to activate accrued sick leave, annual leave, or approved family medical leave.

steps.title: Organize Wills, Customary Land Dispositions, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Executing a written will and respecting state customary land law: While of sound mind, the ill person should execute a formal written will before competent witnesses to govern bank accounts, personal property, and business interests under state probate law [6]. In Pohnpei, Chuuk, Yap, and Kosrae, constitutional provisions restrict land ownership strictly to FSM citizens, and succession to family or clan land is governed by state statutes and traditional customary law overseen by the State Courts and the Supreme Court of the Federated States of Micronesia [6]. Any intended transfer of customary land must follow the applicable state land tenure and lineage consultation rules [6].
  • Updating beneficiary designations and civil registration records: Review beneficiary designations on life insurance policies, retirement accounts, and records held by the Federated States of Micronesia Social Security Administration [2] [3]. Verify that the ill person's birth certificate, marriage certificate, and children's birth certificates are accurately registered with the State Court Vital Statistics Division so future survivor claims are not delayed [3] [6].
  • Cross-border document authentication: Compile an organized inventory of local and foreign bank accounts, property titles, and insurance policies. Because the Federated States of Micronesia is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, powers of attorney or civil records that must be used abroad should be authenticated through the FSM Department of Justice / Department of Foreign Affairs and legalized through the relevant embassy or the U.S. Embassy in the Federated States of Micronesia [5] [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Mongolia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Mongolia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Mongolia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Mongolia. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - from initial medical certification and civil death registration to funeral or repatriation arrangements, social insurance notifications, and notarial estate succession.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or clinical facility: When a person dies in a public or private hospital in Ulaanbaatar or a provincial (aimag) center, the attending physician under the oversight of the Ministry of Health of Mongolia issues the official medical certificate of cause of death (Маягт АМ-7 / Medical Death Certificate) [1] [5]. You will need to present the deceased's citizen identity card (иргэний үнэмлэх) or passport so the hospital administration can record accurate civil identification details [1] [6].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home from a documented medical condition, contact the local family health center (Өрхийн эрүүл мэндийн төв), emergency medical services (103), or the soum hospital immediately [5] [6]. A physician must examine the remains and review the medical history before issuing the medical death certificate [5] [6].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, outside medical supervision, or under suspicious or accidental circumstances, you must notify the National Police Agency (102) immediately [6]. Police officers and forensic specialists from the National Institute of Forensic Science will examine the scene and transfer the remains for a mandatory forensic autopsy before releasing the forensic medical conclusion required for civil registration [2] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory registration deadlines: Under Article 19 of the Law on Civil State Registration of Mongolia, a death must be registered within 3 working days in Ulaanbaatar or provincial (aimag) centers, and within 7 working days in rural districts (soums) from the date the death occurred or the medical or forensic conclusion was issued [1] [2]. If a court has declared a missing person deceased, the registration must be completed within 5 working days after the court decision takes legal effect [2].
  • Where and how to register: A family member, adult relative, or authorized representative may register the death at any local civil registration office of the General Authority for State Registration (regardless of residential address), at a One-Stop Service Center (Нэг цэгийн үйлчилгээ), or digitally through the E-Mongolia Unified Digital Service Portal [1] [2] [3].
  • Required documents and Death Certificate issuance: Submit the official medical certificate of cause of death (or forensic examination report), the deceased's citizen ID card, and the informant's ID card [1] [2]. The state registrar records the entry in the civil registry, invalidates the deceased's ID record, and issues the official Death Certificate (Нас барсны гэрчилгээ) free of stamp duty, along with a reference slip for social insurance and burial administration [1] [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Domestic burial and cremation procedures: Funeral arrangements in Mongolia require the official Death Certificate and the medical cause-of-death record [1] [6]. In Ulaanbaatar and provincial capitals, licensed funeral service providers coordinate mortuary preparation, transport, and plot allocation at designated municipal cemeteries (such as Sambalkhundev or Narangiin Enger) or cremation at licensed crematoria in compliance with municipal sanitary and environmental regulations [5] [6].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported abroad, the family or an international funeral director must obtain an official Death Certificate from the General Authority for State Registration, a forensic or medical certificate confirming the absence of communicable diseases, an embalming and hermetic coffin sealing certificate, and customs export clearance [1] [5] [6].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Mongolia is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. For official Mongolian Death Certificates and civil registry extracts to be recognized abroad in another Apostille member state, they must be translated by a certified translation bureau, notarized through a public notary registered with the Chamber of Notaries of Mongolia, and affixed with an Apostille by the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [2] [4] [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Insurance, Tax, and Banking Institutions
steps.html:
• Statutory funeral grant (Оршуулгын тэтгэмж): Under the social insurance framework overseen by the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Protection, if the deceased contributed to the Social Insurance Fund for at least 36 months (or died due to an industrial accident or occupational disease, or was receiving a state social insurance pension), the person who organized the funeral is entitled to claim a lump-sum funeral grant [3]. Applications can be submitted within 28 weeks of the death through the local social insurance office or digitally via the E-Mongolia Unified Digital Service Portal using the civil registry death reference [3].
  • Survivor's pension (Тэжээгчээ алдсаны тэтгэвэр): Dependent family members who were financially supported by the deceased - including minor children under age 18 (or up to age 19 if enrolled in secondary school), disabled dependents, and surviving spouses or parents who have reached statutory retirement age - may apply for a monthly survivor's pension through the General Authority for Social Insurance under the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Protection [3].
  • Banks, tax offices, and utilities: Present the Death Certificate to Mongolian commercial banks (such as Khan Bank, Golomt Bank, or Trade and Development Bank) to freeze individual accounts, halt recurring debits, and request account balance statements as of the date of death for the estate inventory [4]. You should also check with the General Department of Taxation via E-Mongolia to settle any pending personal income, property, or vehicle tax liabilities [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession
steps.html:
• Mandatory 1-year succession acceptance period: Under the Civil Code of Mongolia (Articles 515 to 538), succession opens on the date of death at the deceased's last place of permanent residence [4]. Statutory heirs and testamentary beneficiaries who did not reside jointly with the deceased at the time of death must submit a formal statement accepting the inheritance (or requesting a Certificate of Right to Inheritance) to a public notary within 1 year from the date the succession opened [4].
  • Notarial succession procedure: Estate settlement in Mongolia is conducted primarily through public notaries belonging to the Chamber of Notaries of Mongolia in the district (duureg) or soum where the deceased last resided [4]. The notary verifies the Death Certificate, family kinship references from the General Authority for State Registration, any registered will, and property ownership certificates (immovable property titles, vehicle records, and bank balances) [1] [2] [4]. Once the statutory six-month waiting period from the opening of succession has elapsed and all heirs are verified, the notary issues the official Certificate of Right to Inheritance (Өвлөх эрхийн гэрчилгээ) [4].
  • Property re-registration and cross-border coordination: With the notarial Certificate of Right to Inheritance, heirs register the transfer of real estate ownership with the property rights registry of the General Authority for State Registration [1] [4]. Mongolia does not levy a separate general estate tax on standard family inheritances, though small administrative registration fees and notarial tariffs apply [1] [4]. If an heir resides outside Mongolia, they may participate in the succession within the 1-year deadline by executing a notarized and Apostilled (or consular-legalized) Power of Attorney authorizing a representative in Mongolia to file the acceptance before the Chamber of Notaries of Mongolia [4] [6].
