title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Mongolia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Mongolia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Mongolia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Mongolia is facing an advanced or life-limiting illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place early while the person retains full decision-making capacity helps protect their autonomy and reduces administrative burdens on the household. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to follow in Mongolia.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Hospice Services, and Health Insurance Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialized palliative and oncology care: In Mongolia, clinical palliative care guidelines and pain-management standards are regulated by the Ministry of Health of Mongolia [1]. Inpatient and outpatient palliative care for advanced illnesses is provided through the Palliative Care Department at the National Cancer Center (Хавдар судлалын үндэсний төв) in Ulaanbaatar, tertiary state hospitals, provincial (aimag) general hospitals, and accredited hospice units (such as Hope Hospice, Grace Hospice, and Green Home Hospice) [1].
  • Home nursing and primary symptom control: For patients remaining at home, the local family health center (Өрхийн эрүүл мэндийн төв) in Ulaanbaatar or the soum hospital in rural areas coordinates home visits, ongoing nursing supervision, and prescriptions for controlled analgesics under national palliative care protocols [1].
  • Health Insurance Fund coverage: Ensure your family member's mandatory social health insurance contributions are active with the Health Insurance General Agency (Эрүүл мэндийн даатгалын ерөнхий газар) [2]. Under the Law on Health Insurance, inpatient palliative care, oncology treatment, diagnostics, and designated essential pain-relief medications at contracted medical facilities are subsidized by the Health Insurance Fund, and contribution status can be verified or paid online via the E-Mongolia Unified Digital Service Portal [2, 3].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Patient autonomy and informed consent under Mongolian health law: Under the Law on Health of Mongolia and clinical regulations of the Ministry of Health of Mongolia, a patient with full mental capacity has the statutory right to receive complete medical information, consent to proposed procedures, or refuse aggressive or invasive medical interventions in writing [1].
  • Documenting clinical treatment wishes: Although Mongolian statute does not establish a standalone statutory registry solely for living wills, the ill person can submit a signed written declaration of treatment preferences - specifying pain management priorities, resuscitation wishes, and transition to comfort-focused care - directly to their attending physician and hospital medical team so it is incorporated into their inpatient and family health center medical chart [1].
  • Appointing a healthcare representative: While decision-making capacity is intact, your family member should formally name a trusted adult family member or legal representative in their hospital admission records and execute a notarized representation mandate under the Civil Code of Mongolia so medical staff know exactly whom to consult if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [1, 4, 5].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Итгэмжлэл): Under Articles 62 to 68 of the Civil Code of Mongolia, a person who retains full legal capacity (эрх зүйн бүрэн чадамжтай) may grant a written Power of Attorney authorizing a representative to manage financial, administrative, and property affairs [4, 5]. Powers of Attorney involving real estate, banking transactions, social benefits, or official state filings must be certified by a licensed public notary registered with the Chamber of Notaries of Mongolia [5].
  • Statutory duration and validity rules: Under Article 64.2 of the Civil Code of Mongolia, a Power of Attorney may be issued for a specified term of up to 3 years; if no validity period is stated in the document, it remains valid for 1 year from the date of notarization [4, 5]. An unnotarized or undated Power of Attorney is legally void, and if the patient loses mental capacity before signing, a notary cannot execute the mandate (requiring a court guardianship proceeding instead) [4, 5].
  • Bank account and digital e-notary coordination: Present the notarized Power of Attorney directly to your family member's commercial banks in Mongolia (such as Khan Bank, Golomt Bank, or State Bank) to register the authorized agent on their accounts while the account holder can still verify the mandate [5]. Public notaries under the Chamber of Notaries of Mongolia also record all certified mandates in the national electronic notary system (e.notary.mn), and home or hospital bedside visits can be requested if the ill person cannot travel to a notary office [5].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Caregiver Allowances, and Employment Leave
steps.html:
• Medical and Labor Accreditation Commission assessment: When an advanced illness causes a lasting loss of working capacity, the treating physician prepares a clinical referral to the Medical and Labor Accreditation Commission (Эмнэлэг хөдөлмөрийн магадлах комисс), operating under the framework of the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Protection [3]. The commission evaluates the medical documentation to certify the percentage and duration of disability [3].
  • Disability pension and social welfare allowances: Depending on contribution history, the ill person can apply through the E-Mongolia Unified Digital Service Portal or local social insurance and welfare offices under the Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Protection for a social insurance disability pension (Тахир дутуугийн тэтгэвэр) or, if uninsured, a social welfare disability pension and permanent care allowance [3].
  • Caregiver cash support and Labor Law leave: Under the Law on Social Welfare, a family caregiver providing full-time home care to a severely ill or bedridden person certified as requiring constant assistance may apply for a monthly caregiver cash allowance (Асаргааны тэтгэмж) [3]. Furthermore, under the Labor Law of Mongolia, an employed family member is entitled to request temporary medical care leave or flexible working arrangements from their employer to care for a seriously ill relative [3, 4].

steps.title: Review Wills, Civil Records, and Property Titles
steps.html:
• Executing a notarized will (Гэрээслэл): Under Articles 522 to 526 of the Civil Code of Mongolia, a citizen with full legal capacity may execute a written will specifying how their movable and immovable assets are to be distributed and appointing an executor [4, 5]. To be legally valid, the will must state the place and date of execution and be signed by the testator and certified in person by a public notary of the Chamber of Notaries of Mongolia (or, in exceptional clinical emergencies where a notary is unavailable, certified by the chief physician of the hospital where the patient is hospitalized) [4, 5].
  • Awareness of statutory forced-heirship shares: When drafting a will under Article 522.3 of the Civil Code of Mongolia, the testator should note that minor children and dependents who are unable to work (including disabled or elderly spouses and parents) are legally protected and entitled to receive at least two-thirds of the share they would have inherited under intestate succession [4].
  • Organizing civil and property records: Verify that your family member's citizen identity card, family kinship records, and real estate ownership certificates (Үл хөдлөх эд хөрөнгийн улсын бүртгэлийн гэрчилгээ) are accurate and up to date with the General Authority for State Registration [6]. If family members or assets are located outside Mongolia, ensure any foreign powers of attorney or civil documents are properly notarized and carry an Apostille (or consular legalization) for seamless recognition [5, 6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Myanmar: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Myanmar: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Myanmar: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Myanmar. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - from medical certification of cause of death and municipal or township civil registration to funeral or repatriation arrangements, social security notifications, and estate administration under the Myanmar Succession Act.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a public or private hospital: When a death occurs in a hospital in Yangon, Mandalay, Nay Pyi Taw, or a regional township facility overseen by the Ministry of Health of Myanmar, the attending medical officer issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 103 / vital statistics medical notification) before the hospital mortuary releases the remains [1] [2]. The family must present the deceased's Citizenship Scrutiny Card (National Registration Card, or NRC), household registration list (Form 66/6), or foreign passport so clinical staff can record accurate identity details [1] [2].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home in an urban ward or rural village tract, notify the Ward or Village Tract Administration Office immediately and contact the local Township Health Department under the Ministry of Health of Myanmar [1] [2]. A township medical officer, public health supervisor, or basic health staff member verifies the circumstances and issues the death notification slip required for civil registration and burial clearance [1] [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was unexpected, occurred outside medical care, or involved an accident or suspected unnatural cause, report it immediately to the nearest Myanmar Police Force station (emergency number 199) and the Ward or Village Tract Administrator [2] [6]. The police open an inquest file and transfer the body to a public general hospital for a forensic post-mortem examination (Police Surgeon report), which is mandatory before burial, cremation, or repatriation permits can be granted [1] [2] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory registration authorities and deadlines: Under Myanmar's vital registration framework administered jointly by the Department of Public Health (under the Ministry of Health of Myanmar), the Central Statistical Organization, and municipal committees (such as the Yangon City Development Committee and Mandalay City Development Committee), deaths in urban wards must be reported within 3 to 7 days of occurrence, while rural deaths reported through the village tract administrator are compiled within 30 days [1] [3]. Early registration is essential because municipal cemetery and crematorium authorities require the registration receipt before burial or cremation takes place [1].
  • Where and how to register: A close relative, household head, or authorized funeral representative submits the medical cause-of-death certificate, the Ward or Village Tract Administrator's verification letter, the deceased's Citizenship Scrutiny Card (NRC), the household registration list (Form 66/6), and the informant's NRC to the local Township Health Department or Municipal Health Department vital registration office [1] [2].
  • Issuance of the official Death Certificate: Once the death entry is recorded in the vital statistics register, the Township Medical Officer or Municipal Health Officer issues the certified Death Certificate extract [1] [2]. Afterward, the family must also report the death to the Township Immigration and Population Office so the deceased's name is officially struck from the household registration list (Form 66/6) and their NRC is canceled [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Domestic burial and cremation permits: In Yangon, Mandalay, and other municipalities, burial or cremation may take place only at designated municipal cemeteries and crematoria (such as Yayway or Hteinpin in Yangon) after presenting the medical death notification and obtaining a burial or cremation pass from the municipal environmental sanitation or health department [1] [2]. Licensed funeral welfare associations (such as the Free Funeral Service Society) and municipal mortuary services assist families with cold storage, hearse transport, and scheduling [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported abroad, the family or an appointed international funeral director must obtain an official Death Certificate from the Ministry of Health of Myanmar (Township or Municipal Health Department), a clinical embalming certificate and non-infectious disease clearance from a public general hospital, a police no-objection certificate (if applicable), customs export clearance, and a consular mortuary laissez-passer from the destination country's embassy in Yangon [1] [2] [6].
  • Document authentication and consular legalization: Myanmar is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [3] [5]. Consequently, for a Myanmar Death Certificate or court succession document to be legally valid abroad, it must first be translated into English by a commissioned Notary Public registered with the Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar, authenticated by the Notarial and Legal Affairs division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Yangon or Nay Pyi Taw, and finally legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country [5] [6].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Social Security Board (SSB) funeral grant and survivor benefits: Under the 2012 Social Security Law overseen in cooperation with labour authorities documented by the International Labour Organization, if the deceased was an insured private-sector or public-enterprise employee registered with the Social Security Board, the surviving family or person who paid for the funeral may claim a statutory funeral expense grant (calculated up to five times the insured person's average monthly wage depending on contribution duration) as well as survivor benefits for eligible spouses, minor children, or dependent parents [4]. Claims should be filed promptly at the relevant Township Social Security Office with the certified Death Certificate, updated household registration list (Form 66/6), and SSB insurance card [1] [4].
  • Civil service pensions and tax notifications: If your family member was a retired or active civil servant, notify the Pension Department under the Ministry of Planning and Finance to transition a state service pension into a family survivor pension [3] [4]. You should also notify the Internal Revenue Department if the deceased operated a registered business or held pending income or commercial tax obligations [3].
  • Commercial banks and financial institutions: Present the certified Death Certificate and updated household list (Form 66/6) to the deceased's Myanmar banks (such as KBZ Bank, CB Bank, AYA Bank, or Myanma Economic Bank) to freeze individual accounts, stop automatic debits, and determine whether the bank requires a court Succession Certificate or Letters of Administration before releasing funds [3] [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Probate
steps.html:
• Governing succession framework: In Myanmar, inheritance and estate administration are governed both by the Succession Act (for general probate, Letters of Administration, and Succession Certificates) and by the deceased's personal customary or religious law - specifically Myanmar Customary Law for Buddhists, alongside specific statutory rules for Christians, Muslims, and Hindus - administered through the civil courts under the Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar [5].
  • Succession Certificate, Probate, or Letters of Administration: To collect bank deposits, securities, and debts owed to the deceased, or to transfer titled immovable property when banks or land registries require judicial authority, the surviving spouse or legal heir petitions the relevant District or Township Court under the Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar for a Succession Certificate (for debts and securities), Probate (where a valid written will exists and is permitted under the deceased's personal law, noting that Myanmar Buddhist Customary Law restricts testamentary wills and follows statutory family devolution), or Letters of Administration [5].
  • Property mutation and cross-border coordination: Once court succession documents or family partition deeds (Amwe-pyat စာချုပ်) are executed and stamped, heirs apply to the Office of the Registration of Deeds and the municipal or land records department to update land titles (Form 105 / Form 106) [3] [5]. Myanmar does not levy a separate standalone inheritance tax on estates, though court-fee stamp duties apply to probate and succession certificates based on asset value [3] [5]. If an heir lives outside Myanmar, they may authorize a representative in Myanmar through a Power of Attorney notarized abroad and legalized by a Myanmar embassy or consulate [5] [6].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Myanmar: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Myanmar: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Myanmar: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Myanmar is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place early while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their personal wishes and prevents urgent administrative delays. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to take in order in Myanmar.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Oncology and palliative care services: In Myanmar, tertiary clinical care and symptom management for serious illnesses are provided through specialist departments at Yangon General Hospital, Mandalay General Hospital, Nay Pyi Taw General Hospital, and regional general hospitals overseen by the Ministry of Health of Myanmar, alongside private specialist hospitals and charitable community clinics (such as U Hla Tun Hospice Cancer Foundation in Yangon and Mandalay) [1] [2].
  • Home nursing and controlled pain management: Because specialist inpatient palliative beds are concentrated in major cities and medical resources can be constrained outside urban centers, families caring for an ill person at home should coordinate early with their attending specialist and the local Township Health Department under the Ministry of Health of Myanmar to establish a written symptom-control plan and maintain uninterrupted prescriptions for essential analgesics and supportive medications [1] [2] [6].
  • Social Security Board and private health coverage: If the ill person is an active insured worker registered with the Social Security Board under the 2012 Social Security Law (documented by the International Labour Organization), verify their eligibility for free medical care, specialist referrals, and pharmaceutical reimbursement at SSB hospitals, clinics, or contracted public facilities [4]. If the patient holds private domestic or international health insurance, confirm coverage limits for inpatient palliative admissions or medical evacuation early [6].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Informed consent and patient autonomy: Under the clinical governance standards of the Ministry of Health of Myanmar and Myanmar Medical Council practice guidelines, a patient with intact decision-making capacity has the right to be informed of their diagnosis and treatment options, to consent to medical interventions, or to refuse invasive life-prolonging procedures [1] [2].
  • Documenting written treatment wishes: While Myanmar does not maintain a centralized statutory registry for living wills, the ill person should sign a clear written statement of their medical preferences - covering pain relief priorities, hospital admission versus home care, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation or mechanical ventilation choices - and provide signed copies to their treating physician so the document is placed directly in their hospital medical record [1] [2] [6].
  • Naming a primary family medical representative: In Myanmar clinical practice, physicians routinely consult the patient's immediate next of kin when the patient can no longer communicate [1] [2]. To avoid uncertainty among relatives, the ill person should formally record the name, National Registration Card (NRC) number, and telephone contact of their chosen primary healthcare spokesperson in their hospital admission file and execute a notarized representation instrument while capacity is intact [2] [5].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Special and General Powers of Attorney: Under the Powers of Attorney Act of Myanmar and the Contract Act administered through the legal framework of the Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar, an adult who is of sound mind (mental capacity intact) may execute a Special Power of Attorney (for a specific transaction) or a General Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted agent to manage property, administrative filings, and legal affairs [5].
  • Stamping, notarization, and Deeds Registration: To be legally enforceable in Myanmar, a Power of Attorney must be drafted on prescribed Myanmar judicial stamp paper (under the Myanmar Stamp Act), signed by the principal in the presence of two witnesses, and authenticated before a commissioned Notary Public or magistrate under the Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar [5]. Crucially, if the Power of Attorney authorizes the agent to sell, mortgage, or transfer immovable property in Myanmar, it must be compulsorily registered with the Office of the Registration of Deeds (such as the Yangon City Development Committee or Township Deeds Registration Office) while the principal is still able to confirm execution [3] [5].
  • Commercial bank mandates: Myanmar commercial banks (including KBZ Bank, CB Bank, AYA Bank, and Myanma Economic Bank) apply strict in-person verification rules to third-party withdrawals [3]. While your family member retains full capacity and mobility, contact each bank directly to add a joint signatory or register an official bank mandate on the account rather than relying solely on a general Power of Attorney [3] [5].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Invalidity, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Social Security Board sickness and invalidity benefits: Under the 2012 Social Security Law monitored in partnership with the International Labour Organization, an insured employee who has contributed to the Social Security Board for at least four months in the preceding six months is entitled to sickness cash benefits (60% of average wages for up to 26 weeks) when certified by an SSB medical officer as unable to work [4]. If the illness results in permanent total or partial incapacity for work, the insured person may apply for a permanent invalidity benefit (disability pension or lump-sum payment) plus a constant-attendance supplement if full-time personal care is medically certified [4].
  • Statutory medical and casual leave for family caregivers: Under the Leave and Holidays Act of Myanmar, employed family members in the formal sector may draw upon their statutory earned leave, casual leave (up to 6 days per year), or negotiated unpaid family-care leave with their employer to support a seriously ill household member [4].
  • Social welfare disability registration: For non-insured citizens experiencing severe physical dependency, the Department of Social Welfare (under the Ministry of Social Welfare, Relief and Resettlement) and partner community organizations outlined by the World Bank provide targeted disability certification and social assistance programs in participating townships [3] [4].

steps.title: Review Wills, Customary Succession Rules, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Crucial distinction between Buddhist Customary Law and the Succession Act: Before drafting a will in Myanmar, you must verify which personal law governs the ill person under the judicial framework of the Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar [5]. Under Myanmar Customary Law (Buddhist Law), a Myanmar Buddhist cannot execute a valid testamentary will disposing of their estate after death; instead, any lifetime distribution must be structured as a valid inter vivos family partition deed (Amwe-pyat စာချုပ်), lifetime gift deed (Meitta-za), or joint ownership arrangement while the person is alive and of sound mind [5]. By contrast, non-Buddhist citizens (including Christians, Hindus, and foreign nationals) and Muslims (typically up to one-third of net estate without heir consent) may execute a written testamentary will attested by at least two witnesses under the Succession Act [5].
  • Verifying civil identity and household registration (Form 66/6): Ensure that your family member's Citizenship Scrutiny Card (NRC), the official household registration list (Form 66/6), marriage certificates, and children's birth certificates are complete and accurately spelled across all records maintained with the civil registration and vital statistics authorities [1] [3]. Discrepancies in names or NRC numbers on Form 66/6 frequently delay bank releases and court succession filings later [1] [5].
  • Property titles and cross-border authentication: Gather original land grant leases, registered deeds, and tax receipts (Form 105 / Form 106) in a secure file [3] [5]. Because Myanmar is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, any foreign Power of Attorney or civil status document executed by family members living abroad must be notarized and legalized at a Myanmar embassy or consulate, and any Myanmar document destined for use abroad must be notarized and authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [5] [6].

1. Coordinate palliative care and SSB health coverageImmediately upon diagnosisMinistry of Health of Myanmar / Public Hospital & Social Security Board
2. Record written medical preferences and care spokespersonWhile decision-making capacity is intactTreating Hospital Medical Team & Ministry of Health of Myanmar
3. Execute stamped Power of Attorney and bank mandatesBefore any loss of mental capacityNotary Public (Supreme Court of the Union of Myanmar) & Office of Registration of Deeds
4. Claim SSB sickness or invalidity cash benefitsDuring certified medical incapacityTownship Social Security Board Office (under ILO-documented framework)
5. Prepare succession deeds or Succession Act will & verify Form 66/6While capacity is intactSupreme Court of the Union of Myanmar (Notary / Advocates) & Township Immigration Office

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Nauru: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Nauru. Below, we set out the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order - from medical certification of cause of death and civil registration in Yaren District to funeral or repatriation arrangements, social welfare and superannuation notifications, and estate administration before the Supreme Court of Nauru and the Nauru Lands Committee.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths at the Republic of Nauru Hospital: When a person dies at the Republic of Nauru Hospital (RONH) under the Ministry of Health and Medical Services of the Government of the Republic of Nauru, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [2] [4]. Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2017, the certifying doctor provides the medical certificate and notifies the civil registrar within 24 to 48 hours of the death [1] [3].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home in one of Nauru's districts from a known medical condition, contact the Republic of Nauru Hospital emergency medical team immediately so a registered medical officer can verify the death, transport the remains to the hospital mortuary, and issue the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [4] [6].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, outside medical supervision, or under accidental or unexplained circumstances, you must notify the Nauru Police Force (emergency number 110) immediately [2] [6]. Under the Coroners Act, the police report the death to the Coroner (the Resident Magistrate of the District Court), who conducts a coronial inquiry and orders a post-mortem examination if necessary before issuing the Coroner's certificate authorizing burial and civil death registration [1] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Statutory registration deadline: Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2017, a death occurring in Nauru must be officially registered with the Office of the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages (within the Department of Justice and Border Control at the Government Offices in Yaren District) within 14 days of the date of death (and in practice alongside funeral notifications within 7 days of burial) [1] [2] [3].
  • Who must register and required documents: The next of kin, a close adult relative present at the death, or the person organizing the funeral submits the official Death Registration Form together with the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's Certificate), the deceased's passport or Nauruan birth certificate, and the informant's identification [1] [2].
  • Obtaining official Death Certificates: Once the entry is recorded in the National Register of Deaths, the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages issues certified copies of the official Death Certificate [1] [2]. We suggest requesting several certified extracts at the time of registration, as original certificates are required by banks, the Nauru Superannuation Board, the Supreme Court of Nauru, and the Nauru Lands Committee [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Domestic burial procedures in Nauru: Burials in Nauru are predominantly conducted at designated district or community cemeteries after the Republic of Nauru Hospital issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or the Coroner issues a release order) and the death notification is lodged with the Office of the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages [1] [2] [4]. Hospital mortuary services and community funeral organizers assist families with mortuary storage, coffin preparation, and transport [2] [4].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national whose remains must be repatriated abroad - or if a Nauruan citizen died overseas while on an Overseas Medical Referral (OMR) in Australia, Fiji, or another country - repatriation requires an official Death Certificate, a public health non-infectious disease and embalming certificate from the Ministry of Health and Medical Services, customs and border clearance from the Department of Justice and Border Control, and air cargo coordination with Nauru Airlines [2] [4] [5] [6].
  • Document authentication and consular legalization: Nauru is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [3] [5]. Consequently, for a Nauruan Death Certificate or court grant to be recognized in a foreign jurisdiction, it must be certified by a Notary Public or Commissioner for Oaths under the Supreme Court of Nauru, authenticated by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade of the Government of the Republic of Nauru, and legalized by the relevant foreign diplomatic mission (such as the Australian High Commission in Nauru) [2] [3] [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Welfare, Superannuation, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Government bereavement assistance and social welfare: The Government of the Republic of Nauru (through the Ministry of Finance and community welfare administration) operates a statutory funeral and bereavement assistance scheme to help eligible Nauruan families meet burial and wake costs, and also administers elderly and survivor welfare adjustments [2] [5]. Notify the Ministry of Finance social payments office with the certified Death Certificate so any ongoing individual elderly or disability stipends are updated and funeral assistance can be processed [2].
  • Nauru Superannuation Board and overseas funds: If the deceased was an employee contributing to the Nauru Superannuation Board (or held an Australian or regional superannuation account), the surviving spouse, nominated beneficiary, or estate administrator should submit a death-benefit claim supported by the certified Death Certificate and proof of identity [2] [5].
  • Banking and financial notifications: Present the certified Death Certificate to the Bendigo Bank Agency in Nauru (and any overseas bank in Australia or elsewhere where the deceased held accounts) to freeze sole-name accounts, stop automatic debits, and confirm the balance as of the date of death for estate administration [2] [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Customary Land Succession
steps.html:
• Dual succession framework in Nauru: As documented by the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute (PacLII), estate administration in Nauru is divided between personal property (governed by statutory probate and administration rules before the Supreme Court of Nauru) and Nauruan customary land (governed by Nauruan custom before the Nauru Lands Committee) [3].
  • Probate, Letters of Administration, and the Curator of Intestate Estates: For bank accounts, personal chattels, superannuation payouts paid to the estate, and non-customary assets, succession is administered under the Administration of Estates Act and the Custom and Adopted Laws Act 1971 [3]. If the deceased left a valid written will covering personal estate, the named executor petitions the Supreme Court of Nauru (Probate Jurisdiction) in Yaren District for a Grant of Probate; if there is no will, the next of kin or the Curator of Intestate Estates (within the Department of Justice and Border Control) applies for Letters of Administration to collect debts and distribute personal property according to statutory intestacy rules [2] [3].
  • Nauru Lands Committee for customary land and royalties: Under the Nauru Lands Committee Act, ownership of Nauruan land, housing allotments on customary land, and associated phosphate royalty or landowner trust entitlements cannot be disposed of outside Nauruan custom [3]. Surviving family members must notify the Nauru Lands Committee, which investigates family lineage, holds a determination meeting, and publishes the succession determination in the Republic of Nauru Government Gazette (subject to a statutory 21-day appeal window to the Supreme Court of Nauru) [2] [3]. Nauru does not levy an inheritance tax or estate duty, and heirs residing abroad may participate via a notarized and authenticated Power of Attorney [2] [3] [5].
StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Obtain Medical Certificate of Cause of DeathWithin 24 to 48 hours of deathRepublic of Nauru Hospital (Ministry of Health and Medical Services) or Coroner
2. Register the death and obtain Death CertificatesWithin 14 days of deathOffice of the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages (Department of Justice and Border Control)
3. Arrange burial or international repatriation clearanceBefore burial or air transitMinistry of Health and Medical Services & Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade
4. Claim bereavement assistance and superannuationPromptly after death registrationGovernment of the Republic of Nauru (Ministry of Finance) & Nauru Superannuation Board
5. Complete probate and customary land determinationAfter Death Certificate issuance (21-day land appeal window)Supreme Court of Nauru (or Curator of Intestate Estates) & Nauru Lands Committee

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Nauru: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Nauru has been diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place early while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity protects their personal wishes and reduces administrative pressure on the family. Below, we set out the five key official and practical steps to follow in order in Nauru.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Overseas Medical Referral Options
steps.html:
• Inpatient and community care at the Republic of Nauru Hospital: In Nauru, public healthcare, inpatient symptom management, and community nursing support are provided free of charge to Nauruan citizens through the Republic of Nauru Hospital (RONH) and the Naoero Public Health Centre under the Ministry of Health and Medical Services of the Government of the Republic of Nauru [2] [4]. Families caring for a seriously ill person at home should coordinate with the medical and public health outreach teams at RONH to establish an ongoing pain-management, medication, and home-visit schedule [4] [6].
  • Overseas Medical Referral (OMR) vs. local comfort care: Because Nauru is a single-island nation where highly specialized tertiary oncology or palliative facilities are limited, patients with complex life-limiting illnesses are frequently evaluated by the Overseas Medical Referral Committee under the Ministry of Health and Medical Services for treatment in contracted hospitals in Australia, Fiji, or Southeast Asia [4] [5] [6]. While the ill person retains full capacity, discuss clearly with their treating doctors at RONH whether they wish to pursue an Overseas Medical Referral or remain in Nauru close to family with community palliative support [2] [4] [6].
  • Private health insurance and medical evacuation: If your family member is an expatriate resident or holds private international medical insurance, contact the insurer immediately to confirm coverage for inpatient stabilization at RONH and air ambulance evacuation from Nauru International Airport [5] [6].

steps.title: Record Advance Medical Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Proxy
steps.html:
• Informed consent and treatment refusal under Nauruan law: Under the clinical governance standards of the Ministry of Health and Medical Services, the Health Practitioners Act, and common-law principles applied in Nauru via the Custom and Adopted Laws Act 1971 (documented by the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute), an adult patient with intact mental capacity has the legal right to give informed consent to medical treatment and to refuse invasive or life-prolonging interventions [3] [4].
  • Placing a written treatment directive on the hospital chart: Although Nauru does not maintain a separate statutory registry for living wills, the ill person can sign a clear written statement of their medical preferences - covering pain relief priorities, cardiopulmonary resuscitation wishes, and whether they consent to or decline emergency overseas medical transfer - and ask their attending physician at the Republic of Nauru Hospital to file it directly in their medical record [2] [3] [4].
  • Naming a primary family medical representative: While capacity is intact, your family member should formally record the name and telephone details of their chosen primary family spokesperson in their hospital admission records at RONH and execute a witnessed written authorization so doctors know whom to consult if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [2] [3] [4].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Executing a valid Power of Attorney in Nauru: Under the common-law and statutory rules recognized by the Supreme Court of Nauru through the Custom and Adopted Laws Act 1971, an adult who retains full mental capacity (sound mind) may execute a written Power of Attorney appointing a trusted relative or representative to manage financial, administrative, and legal affairs [3]. To ensure formal validity, the Power of Attorney should be signed in the presence of independent witnesses and certified before a Commissioner for Oaths, Notary Public, or legal practitioner admitted before the Supreme Court of Nauru (families may also request procedural guidance from the Office of the Public Legal Defender within the Department of Justice and Border Control) [2] [3].
  • Bank account and superannuation mandates: Because Nauru's banking services are operated primarily through the Bendigo Bank Agency in Nauru (in partnership with the Ministry of Finance) and standard common-law powers of attorney require strict verification if mental capacity later declines, it is advisable for the ill person to visit or contact the bank while still able to act in person to register an authorized third-party signatory or joint mandate on their account [2] [5].
  • Cross-border powers of attorney: If the ill person holds bank accounts or property in Australia or another country, or if their chosen attorney-in-fact resides abroad, note that Nauru is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; documents executed in Nauru for use abroad must be notarized and authenticated through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade of the Government of the Republic of Nauru [2] [3] [5].

steps.title: Activate Disability Welfare Allowances, Superannuation Access, and Caregiver Leave
steps.html:
• Government Disability Allowance: Under the social protection programs administered by the Government of the Republic of Nauru (through the Ministry of Finance and Social Welfare services), Nauruan citizens living with a medically certified severe physical impairment or advanced debilitating illness may apply for a regular Disability Allowance following clinical certification by a medical officer at the Republic of Nauru Hospital [2] [4] [5].
  • Early medical access to Nauru Superannuation Board funds: If the ill person has accumulated retirement savings with the Nauru Superannuation Board (or an Australian superannuation fund), they can inquire about early lump-sum release on grounds of a certified terminal medical condition or permanent medical incapacity, submitting two medical practitioner reports from the Ministry of Health and Medical Services [2] [4] [5].
  • Caregiver leave for employed relatives: Family members employed in the Nauruan public sector may apply to their head of department and the Chief Secretary's office under the Public Service Act for compassionate leave, family carer's leave, or official escort leave if accompanying the patient on an approved Overseas Medical Referral [2] [3].

steps.title: Review Wills, Nauru Lands Committee Customary Rules, and Civil Records
steps.html:
• Distinguishing personal estate Wills from Nauruan customary land: As published by the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute, Nauru maintains a strict legal distinction between personal assets and customary land [3]. For personal property, bank balances, and overseas assets, an adult of sound mind may execute a written Will under the Wills / Succession rules recognized by the Supreme Court of Nauru, signed by the testator in the presence of two independent adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries [3]. The ill person should also verify that their binding beneficiary nomination with the Nauru Superannuation Board is up to date [2] [5].
  • Nauru Lands Committee rules for customary land and royalties: Under the Nauru Lands Committee Act, Nauruan customary land and associated phosphate royalty or landowner trust interests are governed by Nauruan custom and the Nauru Lands Committee [2] [3]. If the ill person wishes to express intentions or apply for an inter vivos family transfer regarding Nauruan land, they must communicate directly with the Nauru Lands Committee while they retain full capacity, as customary land determinations require committee approval and gazettal [2] [3].
  • Verifying civil status records: Ensure that the ill person's birth certificate, marriage certificate, and children's birth certificates are accurate and registered with the Office of the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages within the Department of Justice and Border Control under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2017 [1] [2]. Having certified civil status extracts ready prevents kinship disputes before the Nauru Lands Committee and the Supreme Court of Nauru [1] [3].

3. Execute witnessed Power of Attorney and bank mandateBefore any loss of mental capacityCommissioner for Oaths / Supreme Court of Nauru & Bendigo Bank Agency
4. Apply for Disability Allowance and medical super releaseUpon medical certification of incapacityGovernment of the Republic of Nauru (Ministry of Finance) & Nauru Superannuation Board
5. Execute Will for personal estate & review land recordsWhile capacity is intactSupreme Court of Nauru, Nauru Lands Committee & Department of Justice and Border Control

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nepal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nepal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Nepal: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Nepal. Navigating medical certification, municipal ward registration, funeral or international repatriation formalities, survivor benefit claims, and succession under Nepali law involves several distinct public authorities. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs in a public or private hospital in Nepal overseen by the Ministry of Health and Population, the attending physician issues a formal medical certificate of cause of death (Mrityu Pramanit Patra / hospital death discharge report) recording the deceased's full identity, date and time of death, and clinical cause [6]. Keep the original signed and stamped hospital report and make several certified photocopies, as the local Ward Office and funeral authorities require it.
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home without a physician in attendance, notify the local municipal or rural municipal Ward Office (Wada Karyalaya) immediately [1, 2]. Where no medical certificate is available, the local registrar accepts a community verification memo (Sarjamin Muchulka) witnessed by local residents or a recommendation from a local health post alongside the family informant's declaration [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, or occurred outside medical supervision under unclear circumstances, notify the Nepal Police (100) immediately before moving the body [1]. Police officers conduct an on-scene inquiry (Muchulka) and transfer the remains to an authorized government hospital forensic unit (such as Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu or a provincial hospital) for a medico-legal post-mortem examination (Autopsy Report) before releasing the body to the family [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Local Ward Office (Civil Registry)
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authority: Vital events in Nepal are governed by the National ID and Civil Registration Act, 2076 (2020) and administered nationally by the Department of National ID and Civil Registration under the Ministry of Home Affairs, with day-to-day registration handled by the Local Registrar (Panjikadhikari / Ward Secretary) at the Ward Office of the municipality or rural municipality where the deceased resided [1, 2].
  • Statutory deadline and informant duty: The head of the household or the closest adult family member must file the Death Notification Form (Schedule-3) within 35 days of the date of death [1, 2]. Registration completed within the 35-day statutory window is free of charge; late registration after 35 days remains possible upon payment of a small statutory fine prescribed by the municipality [2].
  • Required documentation and digital pre-filling: Families can pre-fill the application online via the Department of National ID and Civil Registration public portal and bring the token number to the Ward Office along with the hospital death report (or police post-mortem clearance), the deceased's Nepali Citizenship Certificate (Nagarikता Pramanpatra) or National Identity Card (Rastriya Parichayapatra), and the informant's Citizenship Certificate [1, 2].
  • Bilingual Death Registration Certificate: Request the official Death Registration Certificate (Mrityu Darta Pramanpatra) in both Nepali and English on the standard bilingual government template, as banks, foreign embassies, and international insurers require the English version [2].

steps.title: Arrange Funeral Rites, Cremation, Burial, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local cremation or burial permits: In Nepal, funeral rites are typically conducted rapidly in accordance with religious and cultural traditions (such as Hindu cremation at Pashupatinath Aryaghat managed by the Pashupati Area Development Trust, Buddhist rites, or designated cemetery burial) [1]. Before cremation or burial can proceed at an managed facility, you must present the hospital medical death certificate or police post-mortem release letter together with the deceased's and informant's identity documents [6].
  • Licensed mortuary and international repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or a Nepali citizen whose remains must be repatriated abroad, engage an international funeral assistance agency and a hospital mortuary equipped for embalming (such as Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital Forensic Department) [3, 6]. International air transport requires an official Medical Death Certificate, a Post-Mortem or Police No-Objection Certificate (NOC), an Embalming Certificate, a Coffin Sealing and Non-Infectious Certificate, a consular No-Objection Certificate from the relevant foreign embassy in Kathmandu, and customs clearance at Tribhuvan International Airport [3].
  • Consular attestation and legalization: Because Nepal is not currently a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Nepali Death Registration Certificates and court documents intended for official use abroad must be attested by the Department of Consular Services under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tripureshwor, Kathmandu, and subsequently legalized by the embassy or consulate of the destination country [3].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Provident Funds, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• Social Security Fund (SSF) survivor and funeral benefits: If the deceased was employed in the formal private or institutional sector and enrolled in the contribution-based Social Security Fund, notify the fund through the employer or directly via the Social Security Fund portal [4]. Under the Dependent Family Protection Scheme (Ashrit Pariwar Suraksha Yojana), eligible survivors may claim a statutory lump-sum funeral grant (Kriya Kharcha of NPR 25,000), a lifetime survivor spouse pension equal to 60 percent of the contributor's basic remuneration, educational allowances for dependent children up to age 21, or dependent parent benefits [4].
  • Employees Provident Fund, Citizen Investment Trust, and civil service pensions: If the deceased was a civil servant, teacher, security personnel, or corporate contributor, file a death and nominee claim with the Employees Provident Fund (Karmachari Sanchaya Kosh), the Citizen Investment Trust (Nagarik Lagani Kosh), and the Pension Management Office (Nivrittibharan Byawasthapan Karyalaya) to release accumulated provident fund balances, gratuity, welfare grants, and family pensions [4].
  • Municipal social security allowances and Health Insurance Board: Notify the Ward Office to cancel any municipal social security allowance (Samajik Suraksha Bhatta, such as senior citizen allowance) or transition a qualifying surviving spouse to the single women / widow social security allowance [1, 2], and update family household enrollment with the Health Insurance Board (Swasthya Bima Board) [6].
  • Banking and tax closure: Present the Death Registration Certificate to all commercial banks to freeze individual accounts and verify registered account nominees (Ichchhayeko Byakti), and notify the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) if the deceased held a business Permanent Account Number (PAN) so final tax returns can be settled [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession (Apatali), and Property Partition (Angsabanda)
steps.html:
• Succession and coparcenary rules under the Muluki Civil Code: Inheritance and property succession in Nepal are governed by the National Civil (Code) Act, 2017 (Muluki Devani Samhita, 2074), published by the Nepal Law Commission, specifically the chapters on Partition (Angsabanda, Sections 205-236) and Succession (Apatali, Sections 237-265) [5]. Nepali law combines joint family coparcenary rights (Angsa - where spouses, sons, and daughters hold equal birthright/marital shares in ancestral and joint family property) with succession to self-acquired or separate property (Apatali) in strict statutory order of priority [5].
  • Administrative relationship verification (Nata Pramanit): Before transferring land, vehicles, shares, or bank balances without a named nominee, heirs must obtain an official Relationship Verification Certificate (Nata Pramanit Pramanpatra) from the municipal Ward Office confirming all lawful coparceners (Angsiyar) and heirs (Hakwala), supported by citizenship certificates, marriage registration, and a local inquiry memo [1, 2].
  • Real property mutation (Namsari) and District Court jurisdiction: Applications for mutation of real estate (Jagga Namsari) into the names of surviving heirs must be filed with the Ward Office and the relevant Land Revenue Office (Malpot Karyalaya) within 35 days (extendable with a statutory late fee) [5]. If there is a testamentary instrument (Bakaspatra or Shesh Pachhiko Bakaspatra), a contested partition suit (Angsa Mudda), or a dispute among heirs, proceedings are heard by the competent District Court (Jilla Adalat) under the judicial oversight of the Supreme Court of Nepal [5].
  • No formal inheritance tax and cross-border heirs: Nepal does not levy a separate estate or inheritance tax on property transmitted by succession (Namsari), though nominal registration and administrative transfer fees apply at the Land Revenue Office and company registrar [5]. Heirs residing outside Nepal may execute a Special Power of Attorney (Waresnama) attested by a Nepali Embassy or Consulate abroad to authorize a representative in Nepal to complete Ward Office relationship verification and Land Revenue mutation on their behalf [3, 5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nepal: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Nepal: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Nepal: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that managing a serious or life-limiting illness for your family member in Nepal requires careful medical, legal, and administrative preparation. Taking structured steps while your family member retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity ensures that palliative care, healthcare consent preferences, financial powers of attorney (Waresnama), social security benefits, and family property documentation are properly established. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist hospital and palliative care units: Coordinate ongoing oncology, organ-failure, or supportive care through tertiary public hospitals overseen by the Ministry of Health and Population (such as Bir Hospital, Bhaktapur Cancer Hospital, B.P. Koirala Memorial Cancer Hospital in Bharatpur, or Patan Hospital) as well as dedicated palliative and hospice centers (including Hospice Nepal, Karuna Foundation, and Nepalese Association of Palliative Care partner units) [1]. Ask the treating specialist for a comprehensive written clinical summary (Diagnosis and Treatment Summary) and an outpatient symptom-management and pain-relief plan.
  • National Health Insurance Board (Swasthya Bima Board) coverage: If your family member is enrolled in the national health insurance scheme administered by the Health Insurance Board, verify active household coverage and designate the primary first-service point hospital (Pratham Bindu Aspatal) so referrals to tertiary care centers and covered prescription medications are billed directly [2].
  • Bishoweshwar Prasad Koirala / Impoverished Citizens Medical Treatment Fund (Bipanna Nagarik Aushadhi Upachar Kosh): Under the Ministry of Health and Population impoverished citizens' severe-disease relief program, Nepali citizens diagnosed with one of the eight listed critical illnesses (including cancer, renal failure, heart disease, Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, sickle cell anemia, spinal injury, and head injury) can apply for a recommendation letter from their municipal Ward Office to receive up to NPR 100,000 in subsidized hospital treatment at empanelled facilities [1, 3].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences, Informed Consent, and Medical Decision-Makers
steps.html:
• Statutory framework under the Public Health Service Act, 2075 (2018): Nepal does not currently have a standalone living-will statute, but patients' rights to informed consent, refusal of treatment, and dignified care are governed by the Public Health Service Act, 2075 (Janaswasthya Sewa Ain, 2075) and the National Penal and Civil Codes published by the Nepal Law Commission [1, 5]. While your family member has full capacity, they have the legal right to accept or decline invasive medical interventions and to request transition to comfort-focused palliative care.
  • Designating a primary family medical representative: Under Nepali hospital regulations and the Public Health Service Act, when a patient becomes unable to provide informed consent directly, physicians rely on the written consent of the closest adult family member (Natedar / next of kin) [1]. To prevent uncertainty among relatives, your family member should sign a written statement naming their primary and alternate family decision-makers for medical consultations, hospital admissions, and intensive-care decisions, and have this placed in their medical chart at the treating hospital [1].
  • Clinical capacity verification: Before signing legal powers of attorney or property dispositions, obtain a dated clinical note from the attending physician confirming that your family member is conscious, oriented, and retains full mental capacity (Hosh Hawaas / sound mind) at the time of execution [1, 5].

steps.title: Execute Valid Financial and Legal Powers of Attorney (Waresnama) and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Authorized Power of Attorney (Adhikrit Waresnama) for property and legal affairs: Under the National Civil Procedure (Code) Act, 2017 (Muluki Dewani Karyabidhi Samhita, 2074) published by the Nepal Law Commission, a person with full legal capacity may execute a general or specific Authorized Power of Attorney (Adhikrit Waresnama) appointing a trusted adult representative to manage movable and immovable property, sign official filings, or appear before administrative and land revenue offices [5].
  • Court verification and consular execution: An Adhikrit Waresnama authorizing the sale, transfer, or formal management of immovable property (Jagga Jamin) must be drafted in legal form, accompanied by passport-size photographs, citizenship certificates, and property ownership certificates (Lalpurja), and authenticated before a Judge of the District Court (Jilla Adalat) in Nepal (or before a Nepali Ambassador or Consul General if executed abroad and attested via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs) [5, 6].
  • Bank account mandates and nominee updates: Nepali commercial banks generally require either their own internal account operation mandate or a registered nominee (Ichchhayeko Byakti) on individual deposit accounts [5]. While your family member is able to sign in person (or via bank home/hospital verification visit), update the account nominee form and establish joint signatory access for household and medical expenses.

steps.title: Activate Critical-Illness, Disability, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Social Security Fund (SSF) medical and disability protection: If your family member is an active contributor to the Social Security Fund, file claims under the Medical Treatment, Health and Maternity Protection Scheme and the Accident and Disability Protection Scheme via the Social Security Fund portal [4]. Contributors who suffer permanent total disability due to illness or injury may qualify for a monthly disability pension (Ashaktata Pensan) or medical expense reimbursement up to the statutory ceilings [4].
  • Municipal disability identity card and monthly allowance: If the illness causes severe or profound physical functional impairment, apply at the local municipal office and Ward Office under the Department of National ID and Civil Registration framework for a Disability Identity Card (Apangata Parichayapatra - Category 'Ka' Red Card for complete disability or Category 'Kha' Blue Card for severe disability), which entitles the holder to a monthly federal social security disability allowance and municipal chronic-illness support grants (up to NPR 5,000 per month for designated catastrophic illnesses) [3].
  • Statutory sick leave and family caregiver leave: Under the Labour Act, 2074 (2017), formal-sector employees in Nepal are entitled to paid sick leave (Birami Bida, 12 days per year at full pay) and accumulated annual home leave (Ghar Bida), while family caregivers may request paid or unpaid special leave from their employer supported by a hospital medical certificate [4, 5].

steps.title: Organize Civil Status Records, Property Partition (Angsabanda), and Testamentary Deeds
steps.html:
• Distinguishing joint family property (Angsa) from testamentary gifts (Shesh Pachhiko Bakaspatra): Under the National Civil (Code) Act, 2017 (Muluki Devani Samhita, 2074) maintained by the Nepal Law Commission, joint or ancestral family property (Sagawaas / Angsa Sampatti) is subject to mandatory equal coparcenary shares (Angsa) among spouses, sons, and daughters and cannot be unilaterally willed away without the consent of coparceners [5]. However, a person with full mental capacity may freely dispose of their self-acquired property (Niji Arjit Sampatti) or their demarcated personal share by executing a Deed of Gift Effective After Death (Shesh Pachhiko Bakaspatra - Nepal's statutory equivalent of a testamentary bequest) registered at the Land Revenue Office (Malpot Karyalaya) [5].
  • Nominations (Ichchhayeko Byakti) on financial and retirement accounts: Review and update named beneficiaries on bank accounts, life insurance policies, the Social Security Fund, the Employees Provident Fund (Karmachari Sanchaya Kosh), the Citizen Investment Trust (Nagarik Lagani Kosh), and demat securities accounts (Mero Share), as valid statutory nominations allow rapid disbursement without court litigation [4, 5].
  • Consolidating civil registration and property records: Gather and verify the accuracy of the Nepali Citizenship Certificate (Nagarikta), National Identity Card (Rastriya Parichayapatra), Marriage Registration Certificate (Bibaha Darta), children's Birth Registration Certificates, and Land Ownership Certificates (Lalpurja) at the local Ward Office under the Department of National ID and Civil Registration so that names and dates match across all registries [3].
  • Cross-border family coordination: If family members or assets are located outside Nepal, ensure any foreign powers of attorney or property documents are attested through the relevant Nepali Embassy and the Department of Consular Services of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Kathmandu [6].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Palau: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Palau: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Palau: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in the Republic of Palau. Navigating medical certification, civil death registration, funeral or international repatriation formalities, survivor benefit claims, and estate probate under Palauan statutory and customary law involves several public authorities in Koror and Ngerulmud. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps in chronological order.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical deaths: When a death occurs at Belau National Hospital in Koror or a community health center operated by the Ministry of Health and Human Services, the attending physician examines the deceased and completes the medical certification of cause of death on the official Certificate of Death form (34 PNC § 4005) [1] [2]. Keep the signed medical certification, as it is required both for mortuary disposition and for formal filing with the Clerk of Courts.
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home in Koror, Babeldaob, or an outer state from natural causes without a physician present, contact Belau National Hospital under the Ministry of Health and Human Services immediately so a public health physician or medical officer can verify the death and sign the medical portion of the Certificate of Death [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unattended deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, or occurred under unexplained circumstances, notify the Bureau of Public Safety under the Ministry of Justice (911 or +680 488 1422) immediately before moving the body [1] [6]. Police officers and the Office of the Attorney General coordinate medico-legal clearance and, where warranted, a forensic post-mortem examination at Belau National Hospital before issuing a formal release of the remains [1] [6].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Vital Statistics Office and Clerk of Courts
steps.html:
• Competent civil registry authorities: Civil registration of deaths in the Republic of Palau is governed by Title 34 of the Palau National Code (34 PNC, Division 5 on Vital Statistics) and administered jointly by the Medical Records and Vital Statistics Office of the Ministry of Health and Human Services (at Belau National Hospital) and the Office of the Clerk of Courts at the Palau Supreme Court [1] [2] [3].
  • Statutory 7-day registration deadline: Under 34 PNC § 4005, every death occurring in Palau must be reported and registered within one week (7 days) after the death and prior to burial, cremation, or removal of the body from the state or Republic [2]. Late registrations after the statutory window require supporting affidavits and verification before the Clerk of Courts [2] [3].
  • Required documents and certified copies: The family informant (closest adult relative, clan representative, or funeral coordinator) submits the physician-signed Certificate of Death together with the deceased's Palauan passport, birth certificate, or Social Security card, and the informant's government photo identification [1] [2]. Once filed with the Office of the Clerk of Courts at the Palau Supreme Court, request multiple certified copies of the official Certificate of Death for social security, banking, and probate filings [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Customary Funeral Rites, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Burial-transit permits and national mortuary services: Before interment at a family, state, or community cemetery in Palau, the family must obtain a burial-transit and disposition permit through the Division of Environmental Health and Sanitation of the Ministry of Health and Human Services upon filing the completed medical death certification [1] [2]. Belau National Hospital operates the primary public mortuary facility in Koror for preservation and embalming of remains [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: When a foreign national dies in Palau or a Palauan citizen's remains must be transported internationally by air (typically via Roman Tmetuchl International Airport in Airai), the family must obtain an official Certificate of Death, an Embalming Certificate and Non-Contagious Disease Certificate from the Ministry of Health and Human Services, a Hermetic Casket Sealing Certificate, and consular transit clearance coordinated with the Ministry of State and the relevant foreign embassy in Koror (such as the Embassy of the United States, the Embassy of Japan, or the Embassy of the Republic of China) [1] [5].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Because the Republic of Palau is a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, official Palauan Death Certificates and court records intended for use in another Apostille country can be authenticated with an Apostille through the Ministry of State (Bureau of Foreign Affairs and Trade) or the Office of the Clerk of Courts at the Palau Supreme Court; documents destined for non-Apostille jurisdictions follow diplomatic consular legalization through the Ministry of State [3] [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Healthcare Fund, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• Survivor pensions and lump-sum benefits: Report the death promptly to the Republic of Palau Social Security Administration in Koror, which administers both the national Social Security Retirement Fund (41 PNC) and the National Healthcare Financing Program [4]. Eligible survivors (a surviving spouse, unmarried dependent children under age 18 or up to age 22 if full-time students, or dependent parents) may apply for a monthly survivor pension (equal to 60 percent of the deceased contributor's primary monthly benefit for a surviving spouse, plus 15 percent per eligible child up to statutory family maximums) or a statutory lump-sum survivor benefit if the deceased had not yet completed the minimum contribution quarters for a monthly pension [4].
  • Medical Savings Account (MSA) and Civil Service Pension Plan: File a claim with the Republic of Palau Social Security Administration Healthcare Fund to settle final covered hospital expenses and close or disburse any remaining balance in the deceased's individual Medical Savings Account [4]. If the deceased was a current or retired government employee, notify the Civil Service Pension Plan in Koror to process survivor annuity or refund entitlements [4].
  • Tax, business licensing, and banking closure: Notify the Bureau of Revenue and Taxation under the Ministry of Finance in Koror to close any individual business license, employer tax identification account, or Gross Revenue Tax filing obligation [5]. Present a certified Certificate of Death to commercial banks operating in Palau to freeze sole accounts and verify payable-on-death beneficiaries or probate requirements [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Customary Succession (Cheldecheduch)
steps.html:
• Palau Supreme Court probate jurisdiction: Estate administration and succession in the Republic of Palau are governed by Title 25 of the Palau National Code (25 PNC, Decedents' Estates) together with recognized Palauan customary law (Siukang), and are adjudicated by the Trial Division of the Palau Supreme Court [3]. Small estates consisting solely of personal property or bank deposits below the statutory threshold may be settled through a simplified small-estate petition, whereas larger estates or formal wills require a Petition for Probate or Letters of Administration before the Palau Supreme Court [3].
  • Customary family settlement (Cheldecheduch) and land ownership rules: For Palauan citizens, customary funeral and post-burial clan meetings (Cheldecheduch) held by maternal and paternal lineage elders (Rubak) play an important legal role in determining the distribution of personal property, house rights, and lineage obligations (Eldecheduch), which the Palau Supreme Court recognizes unless superseded by a valid written will or statutory provision [3]. Under Article XIII, Section 8 of the Constitution of the Republic of Palau and Title 39 of the Palau National Code, only citizens of Palau may hold title to land in Palau; land succession claims and title determinations are heard by the Palau Supreme Court and the Land Court [3].
  • No separate inheritance tax and cross-border heirs: The Republic of Palau does not levy a separate estate or inheritance tax on property passing to heirs at death, though standard court filing fees and business revenue tax clearances at the Ministry of Finance apply where commercial assets are transferred [3] [5]. Heirs residing abroad (such as in Guam, Hawaii, or the mainland United States) may appoint a legal representative or attorney-in-fact in Palau using a notarized and Apostilled Power of Attorney filed with the Palau Supreme Court [3] [5].
