title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sri Lanka: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Sri Lanka: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Sri Lanka: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Sri Lanka. Below, we outline the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order, covering medical certification, civil registration, funeral or international repatriation formalities, social security and pension notifications, and estate administration under Sri Lankan law.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital deaths: When a death occurs in a government or private hospital regulated by the Ministry of Health, the attending medical officer issues the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form B 33) once clinical verification is complete [1] [5]. If the cause of death is natural and clearly established, the hospital releases the medical declaration so the family can proceed to civil registration and mortuary release [1].
  • Deaths at home (natural causes): If your family member died at home without suspicious circumstances, you must immediately notify the area Grama Niladhari (village administrative officer) and the local Registrar of Births and Deaths (or Medical Registrar in designated urban divisions) [1] [2]. A registered medical practitioner who attended the deceased during their final illness may issue a medical certificate of cause of death; otherwise, the Grama Niladhari and divisional registrar verify the circumstances on-site before issuing the registration declaration [1].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, unattended by a doctor, or clinically unexplained, it must be reported to the nearest police station and the hospital Judicial Medical Officer (JMO) [1]. Under the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, an Inquirer into Sudden Deaths (Coroner) or a Magistrate conducts an inquest, orders a forensic post-mortem examination by the JMO if required, and issues the inquirer's certificate authorizing burial or cremation and civil registration [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory deadline: Under the Births and Deaths Registration Act No. 17 of 1951, administered by the Registrar General's Department, every death occurring in Sri Lanka must be notified to the area Grama Niladhari or divisional Registrar of Births and Deaths within 5 days of the death [1]. Registration within 3 months of the death is processed free of charge [1].
  • Informant priority and required forms: The closest relative present at the death or in attendance during the final illness (or the occupier of the premises) acts as the statutory informant by submitting the Declaration of Death (Form CR02) together with the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's certificate) and the deceased's National Identity Card (NIC) or passport [1] [2].
  • Obtaining certified copies of the Death Certificate: Upon registration, the divisional registrar issues the initial official Death Certificate free of charge [1]. We suggest requesting multiple certified extracts at the Divisional Secretariat (using Form B63a) or through the Registrar General's Department online eBMD portal, as banks, pension authorities, and courts require original certified copies [1] [2]. If the death is registered after 3 months, a delayed registration inquiry at the Divisional Secretariat is required [1].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial or cremation permits: Under the Cemeteries and Burial Grounds Ordinance and Births and Deaths Registration Act, no burial or cremation may take place without the written certificate of registration from the divisional Registrar of Births and Deaths or a specific order from an Inquirer into Sudden Deaths or Magistrate [1]. Licensed funeral directors coordinate mortuary preservation, municipal cemetery booking, or crematorium scheduling with the local municipal council or Pradeshiya Sabha [1].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or if the remains must be transported abroad, a licensed funeral director with international repatriation capability coordinates embalming certification from a Judicial Medical Officer, a non-contagious disease and public health clearance certificate from the Ministry of Health port health authorities, a hermetically sealed casket certificate, and customs export clearance at Bandaranaike International Airport [1] [5].
  • Consular authentication and document legalization: Foreign embassies in Colombo require the Sri Lankan Death Certificate (with an official English translation issued or certified by the Registrar General's Department) and medical/embalming certificates to issue a consular mortuary passport or no-objection certificate [1] [2]. Document authentication for cross-border legal use is processed through the Consular Affairs Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Colombo after verification by the Registrar General's Department [1].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Institutions
steps.html:
• Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) lump-sum death benefit: If your family member worked in the private or semi-government sector, their accumulated retirement balance is managed by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and administered for claims by the Department of Labour [3]. Registered nominees or legal heirs claim the full EPF balance (employee and employer contributions plus accumulated interest) by submitting Form L along with the certified Death Certificate, the deceased's NIC and B-card, and civil status proofs proving nomination or legal heirship [3].
  • Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) benefits and funeral/death grants: In parallel with EPF claims, surviving nominees or legal heirs should file a death claim with the Employees' Trust Fund Board to recover the member's accumulated ETF balance and apply for the statutory member death welfare grant [4].
  • Public sector survivor pensions and identity/tax notifications: If the deceased was a civil servant or government pensioner, surviving spouses and eligible dependents should notify the deceased's last public ministry or Divisional Secretariat to activate the Widows'/Widowers' and Orphans' Pension (W&OP) scheme and any public service death gratuity [1] [3]. You should also present the Death Certificate to the Department for Registration of Persons (via the Grama Niladhari) to cancel the NIC, notify the Inland Revenue Department if the deceased held an active tax file, and inform commercial banks and insurers so individual accounts are frozen pending succession clearance [2] [3].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Testamentary Probate
steps.html:
• Testamentary jurisdiction in the District Court: Under the Civil Procedure Code of Sri Lanka, if the deceased left an estate meeting or exceeding the statutory threshold for mandatory administration (or involving contested real property or un-nominated financial accounts), testamentary proceedings must be filed in the District Court where the deceased resided or where estate property is situated [1] [3]. If the deceased left a valid Last Will and Testament, the named executor petitions the District Court for a Grant of Probate; if the deceased died intestate (without a will), the surviving spouse or next of kin petitions for Letters of Administration [1].
  • Bank nominations and small estate exemptions: Under Sri Lankan banking and provident fund statutes, valid statutory nominations registered on EPF/ETF accounts, life insurance policies, or designated commercial bank accounts allow funds to be released directly to the named nominee upon verification of identity and the Death Certificate, though nominees may hold proceeds subject to underlying succession law if disputed [3] [4].
  • Tax clearance and cross-border coordination: Sri Lanka does not currently levy a separate statutory inheritance or estate duty on transfers at death, though any outstanding personal income tax up to the date of death must be settled by the legal representative, and stamp duty or notarial transfer fees apply when registering immovable property deeds at the Land Registry [2] [3]. If an heir lives outside Sri Lanka, powers of attorney or testamentary affidavits executed abroad must be signed before a Sri Lankan diplomatic mission or notarized and authenticated for acceptance by Sri Lankan courts and land registries [1] [2].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sri Lanka: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Sri Lanka: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Sri Lanka: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Sri Lanka is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking structured medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their care preferences and prevents administrative delays. Below, we set out the five key steps in chronological order under Sri Lankan practice.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist palliative care network: Under the Ministry of Health and the National Cancer Control Programme, Palliative Care Consult Services (PCCS) operate across major tertiary and provincial teaching hospitals, including Apeksha Hospital (National Cancer Institute) in Maharagama, National Hospital of Sri Lanka in Colombo, Teaching Hospital Karapitiya, Teaching Hospital Kandy, and Teaching Hospital Ratnapura [1] [2]. Your family member's treating specialist can refer them to the hospital palliative care clinic for pain management, oral morphine prescriptions, and multidisciplinary symptom control [1].
  • Community and home-based care: The Ministry of Health integrates hospital palliative units with community follow-up delivered by Public Health Nursing Officers (PHNOs) attached to regional Medical Officer of Health (MOH) divisions, alongside charitable hospice facilities such as Shantha Sevana Hospice and Karunakaraga [1] [2]. Establishing a shared care plan early ensures continuity between inpatient wards and home nursing visits [1].
  • Public and private health coverage: Inpatient and outpatient care at state hospitals under the Ministry of Health is provided free of charge at the point of delivery, while critical-illness grants may be requested from the President's Fund for specific high-cost interventions [1] [2]. If the ill person holds private health insurance or public-sector Agrahara medical coverage, notify the insurer early to obtain pre-authorization for inpatient palliative admissions, home-oxygen equipment, and ongoing specialist consultations [1].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Contact
steps.html:
• Clinical documentation of advance care preferences: Sri Lanka does not currently have a standalone statutory Living Will Act, so advance medical preferences (such as goals of care, comfort-focused treatment, or limits on invasive cardiopulmonary resuscitation in end-stage illness) are recorded through clinical Advance Care Planning discussions with the treating consultant and hospital palliative team under Ministry of Health clinical guidelines [1] [2].
  • Written statement of wishes and next-of-kin designation: While your family member has full mental capacity, we suggest recording their treatment wishes in writing, signed in the presence of witnesses and shared with the treating physician so it is placed in the hospital medical file [1] [2]. You should also ensure the hospital admission registry clearly identifies the primary next of kin or designated family representative whom clinicians should consult if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [1].
  • Capacity confirmation by the treating clinician: Asking the attending consultant or psychiatrist to document in the clinical notes that the patient currently possesses sound mind and full decision-making capacity strengthens both medical consent records and concurrent legal instruments executed during the same period [1] [2].

steps.title: Execute Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarial Power of Attorney under the Powers of Attorney Ordinance: In Sri Lanka, a Power of Attorney must be executed while the principal has full mental capacity, signed before a licensed Notary Public and two attesting witnesses [5]. Under the Powers of Attorney Ordinance (as amended), powers of attorney intended for formal legal, property, or banking transactions should be duly stamped and registered with the Registrar General's Department within the statutory registration window so third parties and financial institutions can verify their validity [5].
  • Dedicated bank mandates and joint account review: Commercial banks in Sri Lanka enforce strict internal compliance on general powers of attorney. While your family member is able to visit the branch or meet a bank officer, we suggest completing each bank's specific third-party operating mandate form and reviewing whether everyday household expense accounts should have an authorized signatory so medical and living bills can be paid without interruption [3] [5].
  • Safeguards if capacity is already declining: Standard Sri Lankan powers of attorney generally cease to operate if the principal loses mental capacity. Establishing bank mandates, standing orders for recurring medical bills, and registered powers of attorney early avoids the need for lengthy District Court curatorship or guardianship proceedings under the Civil Procedure Code [5].

steps.title: Activate Critical-Illness, Disability, and Provident Fund Benefits
steps.html:
• Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) medical and incapacity claims: If your family member contributed to the Employees' Provident Fund administered by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and the Department of Labour, a member who is permanently and totally incapacitated for work due to serious illness may apply to withdraw their accumulated EPF balance early upon certification by a qualified government medical board (using Form K and medical incapacity certificates) [3].
  • Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) critical-illness and medical welfare schemes: The Employees' Trust Fund Board provides specific welfare grants for active or eligible members diagnosed with qualifying critical illnesses (including advanced cancer, end-stage renal failure, or severe cardiac conditions), alongside permanent disability withdrawal entitlements [4]. Submit clinical diagnosis reports and hospital records directly to the Employees' Trust Fund Board regional or head office [4].
  • Public assistance and workplace leave: Low-income households facing severe illness or disability can apply through the Grama Niladhari and Divisional Secretariat (National Secretariat for Persons with Disabilities / Department of Social Services) for monthly chronic-illness (such as kidney or cancer) financial assistance allowances [2] [5]. Family caregivers employed in the public or private sector should coordinate accrued medical, casual, or unpaid family care leave with their employer's human resources department [3].

steps.title: Organize the Will, Statutory Nominations, and Civil Status Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a Last Will under the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance: Under Section 4 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, a valid Last Will and Testament in Sri Lanka must either be executed in writing before a licensed Notary Public and two witnesses present at the same time, or signed by the testator in the simultaneous presence of five witnesses if no notary is present [5]. Executing a notarial will while capacity is medically documented is the most reliable way to appoint an executor and avoid intestate court disputes [5].
  • Updating EPF, ETF, and bank statutory nominations: Because EPF and ETF balances pass according to registered statutory nominations rather than automatically under a general will, verify with the employer, Department of Labour, Central Bank of Sri Lanka, and Employees' Trust Fund Board that the member's nomination forms are current and accurately reflect surviving family members [3] [4]. Likewise, check beneficiary nominations on commercial bank accounts and life insurance policies [3].
  • Consolidating civil registry and property records: Gather originals and certified copies of the ill person's National Identity Card (NIC), Birth Certificate, Marriage Certificate, and Land Registry property deeds, requesting replacements if needed via the Registrar General's Department (using Form B63a or the eBMD portal) [5] [6]. If assets or family members are located abroad, ensure foreign powers of attorney or estate documents are notarized and authenticated through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Affairs Division [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Taiwan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Taiwan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Taiwan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Taiwan. Below, we outline the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order under Taiwanese law, covering medical certification, household death registration, funeral or international repatriation formalities, social insurance and tax notifications, and estate succession.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical or Judicial Death CertificateImmediately upon deathAttending Hospital, Public Health Center, or District Prosecutors Office
2. Household Death RegistrationWithin 30 days of deathHousehold Registration Office (Department of Household Registration)
3. Burial, Cremation, or RepatriationAfter death certificate issuanceMunicipal Mortuary Services Office and Bureau of Consular Affairs
4. Social Insurance and Pension ClaimsWithin 5 years of deathBureau of Labor Insurance
5. Estate Tax Return and SuccessionWaiver within 3 months; Estate tax within 6 monthsDistrict Court and National Taxation Bureau of Taipei

steps.title: Obtain Medical or Judicial Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital deaths: When a family member dies in a public or private hospital in Taiwan, the attending physician verifies the cause of death and issues the official Death Certificate (Siwang Zhengmingshu) [1] [2]. We suggest requesting at least 10 to 15 original signed and stamped copies from the hospital records counter, as multiple agencies, banks, and registries require original certificates [1].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home from a known natural illness, do not move the body before medical verification. Notify the local district Public Health Center (Weishengsuo) or a licensed physician who treated the deceased so a doctor can inspect the remains at home and issue the medical Death Certificate [1] [2].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, by accident, or without a clear clinical cause, report it immediately to the local police station (by dialing 110) [2]. The police refer the case to the District Prosecutors Office (Difang Jianchashu), where a prosecutor and forensic coroner conduct a judicial inquest (Xiangyan) and issue an Autopsy or Judicial Death Certificate before the remains may be released [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Household Registration Office
steps.html:
• Statutory 30-day deadline and competent authority: Under the Household Registration Act overseen by the Department of Household Registration (Ministry of the Interior), a death occurring in Taiwan must be registered within 30 days of the date of death [1] [2]. Registration can be completed at any local Household Registration Office (Huzheng Shiwusuo) nationwide [1] [2].
  • Required documents and informant eligibility: A spouse, relative, household head, or legally authorized representative submits the original Medical or Judicial Death Certificate, the deceased's National ID Card (Shenfenzheng, which is surrendered and canceled), the household's Household Certificate Booklet (Hukou Mingbu), and the informant's ID and personal chop (seal) or signature [1] [2].
  • Death registration transcripts and one-stop notifications: Once the death is recorded, obtain multiple certified copies of the Household Registration Transcript showing the death annotation (Chuhu Tengben) [1]. Local Household Registration Offices also offer a one-stop government notification service that forwards the death record to the National Health Insurance system, the Bureau of Labor Insurance, and tax authorities [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Domestic funeral, cremation, and burial permits: Funeral arrangements in Taiwan are coordinated through a municipal Mortuary Services Office (Binyiguan) and a licensed funeral service provider [1] [2]. Present the official Death Certificate to obtain the municipal cremation permit (Huohua Xukezheng) or burial permit (Maizang Xukezheng) and book public mortuary refrigeration, farewell hall services, and columbarium placement [1].
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: If your family member was a foreign national or if their body or cremated ashes will be transported abroad, the licensed funeral director coordinates an English Death Certificate from the hospital, an embalming certificate (Fangfu Zhengming) and non-contagious disease clearance for uncremated remains, a hermetically sealed casket certificate, and customs clearance at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport [1] [2].
  • Notarization and consular authentication: Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Consequently, Taiwanese death certificates and household transcripts intended for official use abroad must first be notarized by a Taiwanese District Court notary public (or licensed private notary) supervised by the Ministry of Justice, authenticated by the Bureau of Consular Affairs (Ministry of Foreign Affairs), and then legalized by the relevant foreign representative office in Taipei [1] [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Insurance, Pension, Tax, and Financial Institutions
steps.html:
• Labor Insurance funeral grant and survivor benefits: If the deceased was covered by Labor Insurance, Occupational Accident Insurance, or the National Pension Program, eligible survivors may claim funeral grants (Sangzang Jintie) and survivor allowances or pensions (Yishu Nianjin) through the Bureau of Labor Insurance [3]. Claims under the Labor Insurance Act may be filed within 5 years from the date of death using the official application form, the Death Certificate, Household Registration Transcripts showing family relationships, and a copy of the claimant's bank passbook [3].
  • Consolidated financial asset and debt inquiry: While completing death registration at the Household Registration Office (or afterward at any national tax office), legal heirs can submit a one-stop inquiry request to check the deceased's bank deposits, securities, real estate, and outstanding loans across Taiwanese financial institutions through the clearinghouse network coordinated with the National Taxation Bureau of Taipei and regional tax bureaus [1] [4].
  • National Health Insurance and bank account administration: Confirm that National Health Insurance coverage has been terminated effective from the date of death, and notify commercial banks and life insurers directly once you have gathered the estate tax clearance certificate required to transfer balances [1] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Succession, and Estate Tax Filing
steps.html:
• Statutory limited succession and 3-month court deadlines: Under Part V (Succession) of the Civil Code administered under the legal framework of the Ministry of Justice, Taiwan applies statutory limited succession (Fading Xianding Jicheng) by default: heirs are liable for the deceased's debts only up to the value of the inherited estate assets [5]. However, if an heir wishes to renounce the inheritance entirely (Paoqi Jicheng), they must file a written petition with the District Court of the deceased's domicile within 3 months of learning of their right to inherit [5]. To preserve full protection against unknown creditors, heirs should also file an estate inventory (Yichan Qingce) with the District Court within 3 months [5].
  • Mandatory Estate Tax return within 6 months: Under the Estate and Gift Tax Act, even if no tax is ultimately payable due to statutory exemptions and deductions, the executor or legal heirs must file an Estate Tax Return within 6 months of the date of death (a 3-month extension may be requested in writing before the deadline expires) [4]. For residents of Taipei or foreign nationals leaving property in Taiwan, filings are handled by the National Taxation Bureau of Taipei (or the relevant regional National Taxation Bureau where the deceased was domiciled) [4].
  • Transferring assets and cross-border heir coordination: Banks, securities brokers, and Land Registration Offices (Dizheng Shiwusuo) cannot transfer the deceased's accounts or real property until the tax authority issues either an Estate Tax Payment Certificate or an Estate Tax Exemption Certificate (Wanshui or Mianshui Zhengmingshu) [4] [5]. If an heir resides outside Taiwan, any power of attorney or succession agreement signed abroad must be authenticated by the local Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO) before submission in Taiwan [4] [5].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Taiwan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Taiwan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Taiwan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
When a family member in Taiwan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, putting medical, legal, and financial arrangements in place while the ill person still retains full mental and decision-making capacity ensures their treatment preferences are respected and prevents administrative disruption. Below, we set out the five main official steps in chronological order under Taiwanese law.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative Care and Catastrophic Illness CardUpon clinical diagnosisNational Health Insurance Administration
2. Advance Decision and Healthcare AgentWhile full capacity is intactMinistry of Health and Welfare (NHI IC Card Annotation)
3. Financial Mandates and Adult GuardianshipPrior to loss of capacityDistrict Court Notary Public and Ministry of Justice
4. Disability Benefits and Long-Term Care 2.0During active treatment or incapacityBureau of Labor Insurance and Local Long-Term Care Center
5. Civil Code Will and Estate PreparationWhile capacity is medically documentedDistrict Court Notary Public and Department of Household Registration

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Catastrophic Illness Coverage
steps.html:
• National Health Insurance palliative care benefits: Under the National Health Insurance system administered by the National Health Insurance Administration (Ministry of Health and Welfare), eligible patients have access to inpatient hospice wards (Anning Bingfang), hospital-based shared palliative care teams (Anning Gongzhao), and home-based palliative nursing and physician visits (Anning Jujia Liaohu) across accredited medical centers and regional hospitals [1] [3].
  • Catastrophic Illness Card (Zhongda Shangbing Ka): When a physician confirms a qualifying life-limiting diagnosis (such as advanced malignancy, end-stage organ failure, or motor neuron disease), the treating hospital can submit an electronic application to the National Health Insurance Administration for a Catastrophic Illness status annotation on the patient's NHI IC Card [1]. This exempts the ill person from statutory copayments for outpatient, inpatient, and home palliative care related to the certified condition [1].
  • Long-Term Care 2.0 (Changzhao 2.0) community services: Families caring for an ill person at home can call the national Long-Term Care hotline (1966) overseen by the Ministry of Health and Welfare and municipal health departments to arrange an in-home functional assessment for subsidized home care aides, assistive medical equipment rental, respite care, and medical transport [1] [2].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Directives and Appoint a Healthcare Agent
steps.html:
• Patient Right to Autonomy Act (Bingren Zizhu Quanli Fa): Under the Patient Right to Autonomy Act overseen by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, any person with full legal capacity may complete a statutory Advance Care Planning (ACP, Yuli Yiliao Zhaohu Zishang) consultation at an accredited hospital together with at least one relative of the first or second degree of kinship [2]. Following consultation, the ill person signs an Advance Decision (AD, Yuli Yiliao Jueding) specifying whether to accept or refuse life-sustaining treatment and artificial nutrition and hydration under five statutory clinical conditions (including terminal illness), which is then notarized or witnessed by two persons and registered onto their NHI IC Card [1] [2].
  • Hospice Palliative Care Act (Anning Huanhe Yiliao Tiaoli): Specifically for terminal illness certified by two specialist physicians, the Hospice Palliative Care Act allows a mentally competent patient to sign a Letter of Intent for Hospice Palliative Care and Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR, Bu Shixing Xinfei Fusu Shu) directly with the medical team (with two witnesses), without requiring a formal ACP clinic fee, and have that directive recorded on their NHI IC Card [1] [3].
  • Designating a Healthcare Agent (Yiliao Weiren Dailiren): Under both statutes, while capacity is intact, your family member may execute a written medical proxy appointing one or more trusted adults as their Healthcare Agent to express treatment wishes and give medical consent if the patient later becomes unconscious or unable to communicate [2] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial Mandates, Trusts, and Adult Guardianship Agreements
steps.html:
• Mandate contracts and bank powers of attorney: Under the Civil Code (Part II, Mandate), a mentally competent person may authorize a trusted relative to manage financial affairs and property [5]. However, Taiwanese commercial banks and Land Registration Offices require explicit, notarized special powers of attorney (Shouquan Shu) or branch-verified third-party mandates executed in person while the account holder has full capacity [5].
  • Adult Guardianship by Agreement (Yiding Jianhu): Because ordinary powers of attorney face practical banking restrictions if the principal later loses mental capacity, the Civil Code (Articles 1113-2 to 1113-10) overseen by the Ministry of Justice allows an adult with full capacity to enter into a notarized Adult Guardianship by Agreement contract appointing one or more chosen guardians [5]. The notary public notifies the District Court within 7 days, and the chosen guardianship takes legal effect automatically if a court later declares the person subject to guardianship due to incapacity, avoiding court-appointed guardianship disputes [5].
  • Preventive property and medical care trusts: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they may also establish a self-settled health and living care trust (Anlaoxintuo) with a Taiwanese commercial bank so deposited funds are automatically disbursed to hospitals, nursing facilities, and caregivers even if cognitive capacity later declines [5].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Insurance Claims, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Labor Insurance and National Pension disability benefits: If the ill person is insured under Labor Insurance or the National Pension Program and their illness results in permanent clinical impairment after treatment stabilizes, they may apply to the Bureau of Labor Insurance for a statutory Disability Pension (Shinen Nianjin) or lump-sum disability benefit using an official Disability Diagnosis Certificate completed by an NHI-contracted hospital [4].
  • Disability Identification (Shenxin Zhangai Zhengming) and municipal allowances: Through the local district office and hospital assessment teams supervised by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, the ill person can apply for an official Disability Identification card, which unlocks municipal disability living allowances, assistive device subsidies, and tax deductions [1] [2].
  • Family caregiver leave and support: Under the Gender Equality in Employment Act and Labor Standards Act, employed family members in Taiwan may request statutory family care leave (Jiating Zhaogu Jia) and unpaid parental or family care leave adjustments through their employer, alongside caregiver respite services funded under Long-Term Care 2.0 [2] [4].

steps.title: Review Wills, Beneficiary Designations, and Civil Status Records
steps.html:
• Five statutory forms of wills under the Civil Code: Under Article 1189 of the Civil Code administered under the legal framework of the Ministry of Justice, a will in Taiwan is legally valid only if it strictly follows one of five statutory forms: a Holographic Will (Zishou Yizhu, handwritten in full by the testator with the exact year, month, day, and personal signature), a Notarial Will (Gongzheng Yizhu, dictated before a notary public and two witnesses), a Sealed Will (Mifeng Yizhu), a Dictated Will (Daibi Yizhu, before three or more witnesses, one of whom writes it down), or an Oral Will (Koushou Yizhu, restricted to imminent crisis) [5]. We suggest executing a Notarial Will before a District Court or private notary public while capacity is medically documented to minimize future probate challenges [5].
  • Respecting statutory Compulsory Portions (Teliufen): When drafting a will under Civil Code Article 1223, keep in mind that Taiwanese law guarantees a statutory compulsory share (typically one-half of the intestate share for lineal descendants, parents, and the surviving spouse) that cannot be eliminated by will unless statutory disinheritance grounds apply [5].
  • Beneficiary designations and household registry records: Review designated beneficiaries on private life insurance policies and check Labor Pension accounts with the Bureau of Labor Insurance [4]. Ensure the family member's National ID Card, Household Certificate Booklet, and property title deeds (Quanli Zhuangshu) are organized, and note that any power of attorney or estate document involving assets or relatives abroad must be authenticated through Taiwan's Bureau of Consular Affairs or a Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO) [5].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tajikistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tajikistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tajikistan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We extend our sincere condolences on the death of your family member in Tajikistan. Below, we outline the five official administrative and legal steps in chronological order under the laws of the Republic of Tajikistan, covering medical certification, civil registration, burial or international repatriation formalities, pension and tax notifications, and notarial estate succession.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical Certificate of DeathImmediately upon deathMinistry of Health and Social Protection of the Population
2. Civil Death Registration (SAHSh / ZAGS)Within 3 days of deathMinistry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan
3. Burial or International RepatriationAfter death certificate issuanceLocal Hukumat Cemetery Administration and Consular Authorities
4. Funeral Grant and Survivor PensionFuneral grant within 6 monthsAgency of Social Insurance and Pensions
5. Notarial Inheritance AcceptanceWithin 6 months of deathState Notary Office (Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan)

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital deaths: When a family member dies in a public or private hospital overseen by the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population, the attending physician or hospital pathology unit verifies the cause of death and issues the official Medical Certificate of Death (Tibbi Guvohnomai Vafot / Form No. 106/u) [2] [3].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home from a documented illness, notify the local primary healthcare polyclinic (Markazi Salomatii Shahri or Nohiyavi) and the district police officer so a physician can inspect the body at the residence, confirm the absence of external trauma, and issue the Medical Certificate of Death [2].
  • Sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, unattended by a doctor, or clinically unexplained, report it immediately to the local police department (Ministry of Internal Affairs) [2] [4]. Police investigators and the prosecutor's office refer the remains to the Republican Center of Forensic Medical Examination (Markazi Jumhuriyavii Ekspertizai Tibbiyu Sudii), which performs a forensic examination and issues the medical death certificate required for burial and civil registration [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry Office (SAHSh / ZAGS)
steps.html:
• Competent authority and statutory 3-day deadline: Under the Law on State Registration of Acts of Civil Status administered by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan, every death must be declared to the local Civil Registry Office (Sabti Asari Holathoi Shahrvandi, or SAHSh / ZAGS) or, in rural sub-districts, the local Jamoat administration within 3 days of the date of death or discovery of the body [3] [4].
  • Informant eligibility and required documents: A spouse, close relative, household member, or authorized representative submits the original Medical Certificate of Death, the deceased's national passport (Shinosnoma, which is surrendered for official cancellation), and the informant's identity card [3] [4].
  • State Death Certificate and benefit extract: Upon registration, the SAHSh (ZAGS) office issues the official State Death Certificate (Guvohnomai Vafot) together with a statutory death registration extract (Ma'lumotnoma dar borai vafot) required to claim the state burial allowance [1] [4]. We suggest obtaining notarized copies of the State Death Certificate for banks, tax offices, and succession files [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Domestic burial arrangements: Using the Medical Certificate of Death and State Death Certificate, the family coordinates burial with the municipal cemetery administration under the local executive authority (Hukumat) or rural Jamoat, alongside community or religious funeral services [2] [3]. Because Tajikistan does not operate public crematoria, domestic disposition is carried out by traditional earth burial in designated municipal cemeteries [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or if the remains must be transported abroad (including for cremation outside Tajikistan), a licensed funeral repatriation provider coordinates forensic embalming certification, a Sanitary-Epidemiological Service non-contagious disease clearance from the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population, a hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin soldered in the presence of customs and sanitary officials, and air cargo clearance at Dushanbe International Airport [2] [3].
  • Apostille and consular legalization: Tajikistan is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. When the Tajik State Death Certificate and notarial translations must be used in another Apostille country, apply for an official Apostille through the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan (or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for diplomatic documents), and obtain the consular mortuary transit permit from the destination country's embassy in Dushanbe [3] [4].

steps.title: Notify Social Insurance, Pension, Tax, and Financial Authorities
steps.html:
• State funeral grant and survivor pensions: Under the Law on Insurance and State Pensions administered by the Agency of Social Insurance and Pensions under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan, the family member who paid for the funeral may claim a lump-sum statutory burial grant (Kumakpuli baroi dafn) within 6 months of the death by presenting the civil registry death extract and official Death Certificate [1]. Eligible dependents (including minor children, full-time students up to the statutory age limit, disabled family members, or a surviving spouse of retirement age or caring for young children) can apply to the Agency of Social Insurance and Pensions for a monthly survivor pension and any accumulated individual pension savings [1] [5].
  • Taxpayer Identification Number (RMA / INN) and tax obligations: Present the State Death Certificate to the Tax Committee under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan so the deceased's Taxpayer Identification Number (RMA) is deactivated and any outstanding land, property, or individual business tax balances up to the date of death are reconciled [3] [5].
  • Commercial bank notifications: Notify the State Savings Bank (Amonatbonk) and any commercial banks where the deceased held accounts or loans so individual accounts are frozen pending notarial succession certificates [3] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession Within 6 Months
steps.html:
• Mandatory 6-month filing before a State Notary: Under Part III of the Civil Code of the Republic of Tajikistan overseen by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan, inheritance opens on the date of death at the deceased's last permanent residence [3] [4]. Whether inheriting under a notarized will or under statutory intestate rules (where children, the surviving spouse, and parents inherit equally in the First Order), heirs must submit a written declaration accepting (or renouncing) the estate to the local State Notary Office (Idorai Davlatii Notariali) within 6 months from the date of death [4].
  • Issuance of the Certificate of Right to Inheritance: Once the 6-month statutory period concludes and the state notary verifies the State Death Certificate, civil status proofs of kinship, the surviving spouse's community property share, and cadastral property extracts, the notary issues the official Certificate of Right to Inheritance (Guvohnoma dar borai huquqi meros) [3] [4].
  • Property registration, state duty, and cross-border heirs: Tajikistan does not levy a separate progressive inheritance tax on statutory heirs, though heirs pay the scheduled state notarial duty (Boji davlati) and registration fees managed in coordination with the Tax Committee under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan and the State Unitary Enterprise for Registration of Immovable Property when transferring real estate titles [4] [5]. If an heir resides abroad, they may file their acceptance within the 6-month deadline through a representative holding a notarized Power of Attorney (Vokolatnoma) authenticated by Apostille (or recognized under CIS legal assistance treaties) and accompanied by a certified Tajik or Russian translation [3] [4].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tajikistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tajikistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Tajikistan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
When a family member in Tajikistan is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking structured medical, legal, and administrative steps while the ill person still retains full mental and decision-making capacity helps protect their treatment preferences and prevents legal or banking delays. Below, we set out the five key official steps in chronological order under Tajik law.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative Care and Co-Payment ExemptionsUpon clinical diagnosisMinistry of Health and Social Protection of the Population
2. Informed Consent and Medical RepresentativeWhile full capacity is intactTreating Hospital Consilium and Primary Health Center
3. Notarial Power of Attorney and Bank MandatesPrior to loss of capacityState Notary Office (Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan)
4. MSEK Disability Group and Pension ClaimsUpon persistent impairmentAgency of Social Insurance and Pensions
5. Notarized Will and Property OrganizationWhile capacity is medically documentedState Notary Office and Tax Committee under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Medical Supervision, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Oncology, palliative, and symptom control network: Under the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population, specialized palliative care and pain management are delivered through the Republican Scientific Center of Oncology in Dushanbe, regional oncology dispensaries in Sughd, Khatlon, and GBAO, and primary healthcare family medicine teams at city and district health centers (Markazi Salomatii Shahri or Nohiyavi) [2].
  • Analgesic therapy and home nursing visits: For patients receiving care at home, the treating specialist and polyclinic medical commission establish an ongoing symptom-control plan so prescribed opioid or non-opioid analgesics and home patronage visits by family physicians and community nurses continue without interruption [2].
  • State Basic Benefit Package exemptions (Decree No. 600): Under Tajikistan's Government Decree No. 600 on healthcare co-payments, citizens diagnosed with qualifying severe illnesses (including registered oncology patients and persons assigned Disability Group I or II) are entitled to exemptions or reductions on statutory hospital co-payments at public medical institutions upon presenting their clinical certificate and national passport [2] [3].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Patient Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and written refusal of invasive interventions: Under the Health Code of the Republic of Tajikistan overseen by the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population, a mentally competent patient has the statutory right to receive full diagnostic information, grant informed consent, or sign a written refusal of specific invasive medical interventions (Rad kardani mudokhilai tibbi), which the attending physician must record in the official medical chart [2].
  • Naming a trusted medical representative: Because Tajikistan does not operate a separate standalone living will registry, while your family member retains full legal capacity we suggest submitting a signed written authorization into their hospital and polyclinic medical record naming the family member or representative authorized to access confidential medical records, attend medical consiliums (Mashvarati tibbi), and communicate care preferences if the patient later becomes unable to speak [2] [4].
  • Clinical confirmation of decision-making capacity: Before signing notarial powers of attorney or a will while undergoing intensive medical therapy, ask the attending physician to document in the clinical chart that the patient is lucid, oriented, and possesses full mental capacity on the date of signing [2].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates While Capacity Is Intact
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Vokolatnoma): Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Tajikistan and the Law on State Notaries administered by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan, a general or special Power of Attorney (Vokolatnoma / Doverennost) authorizing a trusted relative to manage property, deal with government agencies, and operate bank accounts must be signed and certified before a State Notary while the principal has full legal capacity [4].
  • Bedside notarization at home or in the hospital: If the ill person is unable to visit the State Notary Office in person, the family can request an official bedside visit by a state notary to the hospital ward or home residence to verify capacity and attest the Power of Attorney [4]. In addition, under the Civil Code, a Power of Attorney specifically for receiving pensions and social allowances may be certified directly by the chief physician of the inpatient hospital where the patient is being treated [1] [4].
  • Registering bank mandates early: Under Tajik civil law, an ordinary Power of Attorney ceases to have legal effect if the principal is later declared legally incapacitated by a court, which would require lengthy court guardianship (Vasiyat va parastori) proceedings [4]. Registering the notarized Power of Attorney promptly with the State Savings Bank (Amonatbonk) and any commercial banks where the patient holds accounts ensures uninterrupted access to funds for medical and household care [3] [4].

steps.title: Activate Disability Group Certification, Pensions, and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Medical and Social Expert Commission (MSEK) assessment: When a serious or progressive illness causes lasting functional impairment, the local polyclinic prepares a clinical referral (Form 088/u) to the State Service for Medical and Social Expertise (Khizmati Davlatii Ekspertizai Tibbiyu Ijtimoi) under the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population [1] [2]. For severely ill or bedridden patients, the MSEK board conducts a home or hospital bedside examination and assigns Disability Group I (requiring constant third-party care) or Group II [1] [2].
  • Disability pensions and constant-care supplements: Using the MSEK disability certificate, the patient (or their authorized proxy) applies to the Agency of Social Insurance and Pensions for a monthly insurance or social disability pension (Nafaqai ma'yubi), which includes a statutory constant-care supplement for Group I disability [1] [5].
  • Workplace sick leave and caregiver leave: Employed patients receive paid temporary incapacity benefits based on medical sick-leave certificates prior to permanent disability assignment, and employed family caregivers may request flexible work hours or unpaid family care leave under the Labor Code of the Republic of Tajikistan [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute a Notarized Will and Organize Civil Status and Property Records
steps.html:
• Mandatory notarized Will (Vasiyatnoma): Under Part III of the Civil Code of the Republic of Tajikistan overseen by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan, informal un-notarized handwritten wills are not legally valid; a Will (Vasiyatnoma) must be signed in writing and certified by a State Notary [4]. If the testator is hospitalized in an inpatient medical institution and cannot wait for a notary, the Civil Code permits the Will to be certified by the hospital's chief physician or deputy for medical affairs in the testator's presence [4].
  • Statutory Compulsory Share rules: When drafting a Will in Tajikistan, keep in mind that the Civil Code guarantees a statutory compulsory share (Sahmi hatmii meros) to the testator's minor or disabled children and disabled surviving spouse or parents, regardless of testamentary dispositions [4].
  • Verifying civil registry, tax, and property documents: Check that the ill person's national passport (Shinosnoma), Taxpayer Identification Number (RMA / INN) issued by the Tax Committee under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan, civil status records (birth and marriage certificates from the SAHSh / ZAGS registry), and real estate registration certificates from the State Unitary Enterprise for Registration of Immovable Property are accurate and stored together [3] [4] [5]. If assets or family members are located outside Tajikistan, ensure cross-border powers of attorney carry an Apostille from the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan or comply with CIS legal assistance conventions [4].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tonga: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tonga: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tonga: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We are sorry to hear that your family member has died in the Kingdom of Tonga. Below, we outline the five official and practical steps to complete in order under Tongan law, covering medical certification, civil registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social security and financial notifications, and estate probate before the Supreme Court of Tonga.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or public health facility: When a death occurs at Vaiola Hospital in Nuku'alofa or at a provincial hospital on Vava'u (Prince Wellington Ngu Hospital), Ha'apai (Niu'ui Hospital), or 'Eua (Niu'eiki Hospital), an attending medical officer from the Ministry of Health of Tonga examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1] [5]. This medical certificate states the clinical cause, date, and place of death and is required before civil registration or burial can proceed [1] [5].
  • Deaths at home or in an outer-island village: If your family member died at home or in a rural district without a physician present, notify the nearest district health center operated by the Ministry of Health of Tonga and the local town officer (ofisa kolo) immediately [1] [5]. A medical officer or authorized health officer must verify the death and issue the medical notification of death, corroborated by the town officer's report where required [1].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or suspicious deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, unexplained, or occurred without recent medical attendance, notify the Tonga Police immediately so the case can be referred to a magistrate acting as Coroner under the Inquests Act [2]. No burial, cremation, or embalming may take place until any required post-mortem examination at Vaiola Hospital is completed and the Coroner issues written clearance and a coroner's certificate for registration [1] [2].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Where to register: Civil registration of deaths in Tonga is administered by the Registrar General's Office within the Ministry of Justice in Nuku'alofa (and through Sub-Registrars at the Supreme Court and Magistrate's Court registries in Vava'u, Ha'apai, 'Eua, and the Niuas), which coordinates national mortality records with the Tonga Statistics Department [1] [2].
  • Statutory deadline and informant duty: Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Cap. 42), the nearest relative present at the death or in attendance during the last illness (or the occupier of the premises or the town officer) must register the death with the Registrar or Sub-Registrar within the statutory registration period following the event [1] [2]. Late registrations require a formal statutory declaration and payment of a late registration fee.
  • Required documents and official certificates: Bring the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's order), the deceased's Tongan passport, national identity card, or birth certificate, and the informant's valid photo identification [1]. Once the entry is recorded in the civil register, request multiple certified extracts of the official Death Certificate, as originals are required by banks, pension schemes, and the probate registry [1, 3, 4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial and mortuary coordination: Traditional burial in community or church cemeteries (fa'itoka) is the standard practice across Tonga. Prior to release of the body from the Vaiola Hospital mortuary, the family must present the medical certificate of death, settle any applicable hospital mortuary fees with the Ministry of Health of Tonga, and coordinate grave allocation with the relevant town officer (ofisa kolo) or church authority [1] [5].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member's remains must be repatriated abroad (or brought to Tonga from overseas), a licensed funeral director or hospital mortuary team must prepare the body in accordance with public health regulations. International air transport requires an official Death Certificate, a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death confirming the absence of quarantinable infectious disease, an embalming certificate, a sanitary and coffin-sealing permit issued by the Public Health Division of the Ministry of Health of Tonga, and customs/import clearance from the destination country's embassy or high commission [1] [5].
  • Apostille and document authentication: Tonga is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. If Tongan death certificates or probate orders must be used in another Apostille member state, obtain an official Apostille certificate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Attorney General's Office in Nuku'alofa [2]. For countries outside the Apostille Convention, documents must undergo diplomatic or consular legalization.

steps.title: Notify Retirement Funds, Banks, and Public Authorities
steps.html:
• Public service and national retirement benefits: If the deceased was a civil servant or contributed to a statutory superannuation scheme, notify the Retirement Fund Board (or the National Retirement Benefits Fund for private and non-civil-service contributors) [3] [6]. Under the Retirement Fund (Administration) Regulations, surviving beneficiaries or estate representatives must submit an official Death Certificate, proof of identity, marriage or birth certificates establishing kinship, and the member's benefit claim form to claim lump-sum death benefits or survivor entitlements [3] [6].
  • Social protection and elderly or disability allowances: If your family member received the Social Welfare Scheme for the Elderly allowance or a disability transfer administered through the National Retirement Benefits Fund or the Ministry of Internal Affairs, report the death promptly so monthly disbursements cease and no overpayment debt accrues against the estate [6].
  • Banks, tax, and identity cancellation: Present certified copies of the Death Certificate to all commercial banks in Tonga (such as the Bank of South Pacific Tonga, MBF Bank, or Tonga Development Bank) to freeze individual accounts and identify any funeral-expense release policies. Notify the Ministry of Revenue and Customs to settle any final income tax or business tax liabilities, and surrender the deceased's passport to the Tonga Immigration Division.

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Land Succession
steps.html:
• Supreme Court jurisdiction over probate and administration: Under the Probate Act (Cap. 16), published by the Attorney General's Office, the Supreme Court of Tonga holds exclusive jurisdiction over the personal estate of deceased persons in Tonga [4]. It is unlawful for any person to intermeddle with or distribute estate assets without first obtaining a formal grant from the Supreme Court [4].
  • Grant of Probate vs. Letters of Administration: If your family member left a valid written will, the named executor must petition the Supreme Court for a Grant of Probate, submitting the original will, the official Death Certificate, and a sworn inventory and valuation of the estate [4]. If the deceased died intestate (without a will), the surviving spouse or next of kin must petition the Supreme Court for Letters of Administration and execute any required administration bond [4].
  • Hereditary land vs. personal estate and cross-border assets: In Tonga, hereditary estates (tofi'a), tax allotments ('api 'tukuhau), and town allotments ('api kolo) are governed strictly by the Land Act (Cap. 132) rather than ordinary testamentary wills; a widow or eldest legitimate male heir must lodge any statutory claim to a land allotment or widow's life estate with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources within the strict statutory deadline (typically 12 months from the date of death) [2]. If heirs reside overseas or assets are held in New Zealand, Australia, or the United States, foreign powers of attorney or resealed grants of probate must be authenticated with an Apostille and filed with the Supreme Court registry [2] [4].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your exact situation, on which island in Tonga did the death occur, and did your family member leave a written will, hold a registered land allotment, or have assets or heirs outside Tonga?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tonga: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tonga: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Tonga: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: We understand that your family member has been diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness in the Kingdom of Tonga. Below, we set out the five key medical, legal, financial, and administrative steps to complete in order while your family member still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public hospital and community palliative services: In Tonga, clinical care for serious and life-limiting illnesses is delivered primarily through the public healthcare network managed by the Ministry of Health of Tonga, centered at Vaiola Hospital in Nuku'alofa and provincial hospitals in Vava'u, Ha'apai, 'Eua, and the Niuas [1] [5]. Ask the attending specialist at Vaiola Hospital to establish a written symptom-management and pain-relief plan and to connect your family with the community public health nursing team and the Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) outreach unit for home visits [5].
  • Public health coverage and overseas medical referrals: Public inpatient consultations and essential medicines on the national formulary are heavily subsidized for Tongan citizens through the Ministry of Health of Tonga, though families may face out-of-pocket charges for private ward rooms or specialized medical supplies [5]. If complex palliative or oncology treatment is being coordinated through the Tonga Medical Treatment Scheme in New Zealand or Australia, confirm with the Medical Referral Committee whether ongoing care will transition back to Vaiola Hospital [5].
  • Home care equipment and community support: Coordinate early with district health nurses and local community organizations (such as the Tonga Red Cross Society or Mango Tree Centre for rehabilitation and mobility equipment) to arrange hospital beds, oxygen concentrators, pressure-relief mattresses, and home nursing supplies.

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment wishes while capacity is intact: Tonga does not have a standalone statutory Living Will Act under the consolidated statutes published by the Attorney General's Office, so medical decision-making relies on common-law principles of informed consent and the Health Services Act framework [2] [5]. While your family member has full mental capacity, they should sign a written statement of medical treatment preferences specifying their wishes regarding cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, pain management, and preferred place of care (hospital vs. home) [2] [5].
  • Appointing a trusted family healthcare spokesperson: In Tongan clinical practice, physicians consult closely with the patient and their designated immediate family representative (fakafofonga fāmili). Have your family member formally name a primary and alternate medical spokesperson in writing, have the document witnessed by the treating physician at the Ministry of Health of Tonga or a licensed legal practitioner, and place a signed copy directly into the patient's hospital file at Vaiola Hospital [2] [5].
  • Mental capacity documentation: If your family member's condition could later impair cognition, request a contemporaneous clinical note from the attending physician confirming that your family member was fully lucid and understood the nature and effect of their medical and legal instructions at the time of signing [2] [5].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• General Power of Attorney under Tongan law: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they should instruct a licensed Tongan legal practitioner (fakafofonga lao) to draft a formal Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted representative to manage property, sign legal instruments, pay bills, and deal with government ministries [2]. To ensure the instrument is accepted by registries and courts, execute it in the presence of a Commissioner for Oaths, Notary Public, or Supreme Court registrar [2].
  • Direct bank mandates and account access: Commercial banks in Tonga (including Bank of South Pacific Tonga, MBF Bank, and Tonga Development Bank) often require their own internal third-party signing mandate or authority form in addition to a general power of attorney. Accompany your family member to the bank branch - or arrange a home or hospital visit by a bank officer with a medical certificate confirming capacity - to register an authorized signatory on current and savings accounts.
  • Cross-border powers of attorney: Because ordinary powers of attorney under English and Tongan common-law rules may cease to operate if the donor loses mental capacity unless specifically structured or recognized under the target jurisdiction's enduring power of attorney statutes, any family member who holds bank accounts or real estate in New Zealand, Australia, or the United States should execute a separate Enduring Power of Attorney compliant with that foreign jurisdiction's law and have it notarized and Apostilled in Tonga [2].

steps.title: Activate Medical Incapacity, Retirement, and Caregiver Support Benefits
steps.html:
• Early medical retirement from public service or national funds: If your family member is a civil servant or active contributor who can no longer work due to permanent medical incapacity, contact the Retirement Fund Board (or the National Retirement Benefits Fund for non-civil-service workers) [3] [6]. Under the Retirement Fund (Administration) Regulations, a member certified by a medical board approved by the Ministry of Health of Tonga as permanently incapable of continuing employment on medical grounds may apply for an early medical invalidity or incapacity payout [3, 5, 6].
  • Updating beneficiary nominations: While your family member has full capacity, verify and update their official beneficiary nomination form on file with the Retirement Fund Board and the National Retirement Benefits Fund so that any future lump-sum entitlements reflect their current wishes and avoid contested distributions [3] [6].
  • Disability welfare transfers and employment leave: If the illness causes severe functional impairment, inquire with the Ministry of Internal Affairs Social Protection Division regarding eligibility for the Tonga Disability Welfare Scheme cash allowance. Family caregivers employed in the Tongan public service may apply for compassionate or special family care leave under the Public Service Policy Manual.

steps.title: Organize the Will, Land Records, and Civil Status Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a valid written will under the Probate Act: Under the Probate Act (Cap. 16), published by the Attorney General's Office, the Supreme Court of Tonga oversees the probate of wills and administration of personal estates [4]. To avoid intestacy disputes, your family member should execute a formal written will naming an executor, specifying the distribution of personal property, bank deposits, business interests, and leases, and signing the will in the simultaneous presence of two independent adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries (nor spouses of beneficiaries) [4].
  • Distinguishing hereditary land allotments from personal property: Under Tonga's Land Act (Cap. 132), registered tax allotments ('api 'tukuhau) and town allotments ('api kolo) cannot be devised freely by an ordinary will, as they pass strictly according to statutory rules of hereditary succession and widow's life estates administered by the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources [2]. Review all land registration deeds, lease agreements, and mortgage records now so the family understands which assets pass under the will through the Supreme Court and which require land registry filings [2] [4].
  • Consolidating civil registration records: Verify that your family member's birth certificate, marriage certificate, and children's birth records are accurate and accessible through the Registrar General's Office and the Tonga Statistics Department civil registration system, and obtain Apostille certificates for any vital records that will be needed by heirs or financial institutions abroad [1] [2].

closingQuestion: To help us provide more specific guidance, is your family member receiving care on Tongatapu or an outer island, and are they a member of the Retirement Fund Board or the National Retirement Benefits Fund?
