title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Turkmenistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Turkmenistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Turkmenistan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We are sorry to hear that your family member has died in Turkmenistan. Below, we set out the five official and practical steps to complete in order under Turkmen law, covering medical certification, civil registration at the civil registry (ZAGS / RYYÝ), burial or international repatriation formalities, social security and financial notifications, and succession before a state notary.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical certification of deathImmediately upon deathAttending polyclinic (Saglyk öýi), hospital, or forensic examination bureau
2. Civil death registrationWithin 3 days of death or discovery of the bodyCivil Status Registration Office (ZAGS) under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan
3. Burial, cremation, or repatriationAfter obtaining the medical and civil death certificatesMunicipal cemetery administration and Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan
4. Pension, tax, and bank notificationsPromptly after receiving the official Death CertificatePension Fund of Turkmenistan, tax authority, and commercial banks
5. Estate succession and notarial probateWithin 6 months of the date of deathState Notary Office (Döwlet notarial edarasy) under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths in a hospital or clinical center: When a death occurs in a state hospital or specialized medical center supervised by the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry, the attending physician or hospital pathology unit examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Death (lukmançylyk ölüm şahadatnamasy) [1] [5]. This certificate establishes the clinical cause, date, and place of death required for civil registration [1] [5].
  • Deaths at home: If your family member died at home, immediately notify the local territorial polyclinic (Saglyk öýi) and the emergency medical service (Tiz kömek) as well as the district police officer (uçastok polisiýa işgäri) [5]. If the deceased was under regular medical observation for a documented illness and there are no signs of external violence, the polyclinic physician issues the medical certificate of death after the police officer completes an inspection protocol confirming the absence of foul play [1] [5].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death occurred suddenly outside a medical facility, without recent clinical observation, or under suspicious or traumatic circumstances, the police and prosecutor's office refer the body to the Bureau of Forensic Medical Examination (Sud-lukmançylyk ekspertiza edarasy) [1] [5]. The burial or transport of remains cannot proceed until the forensic examination is finished and the forensic medical death certificate and prosecutorial clearance are issued [1] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry (ZAGS / RYYÝ)
steps.html:
• Where to register: Civil registration of deaths in Turkmenistan is administered by the district or municipal Civil Status Registration Offices (RYYÝ bölümi, commonly known as ZAGS), which operate under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan and transmit national mortality data to the State Committee of Turkmenistan on Statistics [1] [3]. Registration may be filed at the ZAGS office covering the deceased's place of permanent residence (ýazgy), the place where death occurred, or the location of the medical institution that certified the death [1].
  • Statutory deadline: Under the Family Code and civil registration regulations administered by the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan, an oral or written declaration of death must be submitted to the ZAGS office no later than three days from the moment of death or the discovery of the body [1].
  • Required documents and official certificates: Present the original Medical Certificate of Death, the deceased's internal citizen passport of Turkmenistan (which is surrendered to the registry for cancellation with the migration and internal affairs authorities), and the informant's valid passport [1] [3]. The ZAGS officer records the entry in the civil register and issues the official stamped Death Certificate (Ölüm hakynda şahadatnama) along with a certificate for social benefit purposes [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial procedures: Burial in local municipal or community cemeteries is the standard practice in Turkmenistan, typically arranged promptly in accordance with family and religious traditions once the medical certificate and ZAGS registration are secured [1] [5]. Present the Death Certificate to the municipal cemetery administration or local district governance body (häkimlik) to obtain the grave plot assignment and burial authorization [1] [6].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign national or if the family wishes to repatriate remains abroad, air transport requires a sealed zinc-lined coffin, an official Death Certificate from ZAGS, a medical and sanitary-epidemiological certificate confirming the absence of infectious disease and proper embalming, a non-objection certificate showing no extraneous items are enclosed inside the coffin, and customs clearance [1] [4] [5].
  • Consular legalization and CIS recognition: Turkmenistan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [4]. Consequently, if a Turkmen Death Certificate or notarial document must be used in Western Europe, North America, or another non-CIS state, it must undergo full consular legalization: first certification by the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan, second authentication by the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan, and final legalization at the embassy or consulate of the destination country [1] [4]. For several Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) countries covered by the Minsk Convention on Legal Assistance, notarized translations are recognized without consular legalization [1] [4].

steps.title: Notify Pension, Social Protection, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Survivor pensions and burial allowances: Notify the local district branch of the Pension Fund of Turkmenistan (operating under the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Population) to stop the deceased's old-age or disability pension and to inquire about statutory funeral grants and survivor pension entitlements [2] [6]. Under Turkmen social security rules, eligible dependents (including surviving minor children, full-time students up to age 23, and surviving spouses or parents who have reached retirement age (62 for men, 57 for women) or who have a recognized disability) may apply for a survivor pension (ekleýjisini ýitirendigi boýunça pensiýa) calculated from the deceased's pension rights or notional social insurance record [2].
  • Documents for benefit claims: Submit the official Death Certificate, documents proving kinship and dependency, the deceased's employment record book (zähmet depderçesi), and identity documents to the local social protection office of the Pension Fund of Turkmenistan [2].
  • Banks, housing registry, and tax notifications: Provide certified copies of the Death Certificate to Turkmen commercial banks (such as Dayhanbank, Turkmenistan Bank, Senagat Bank, or Halkbank) so individual accounts are frozen pending notarial succession [6]. Notify the local housing management office (ýaşaýyş jaý ulanyş edarasy) to remove the deceased from the household registration book (öý kitaby) and inform the state tax office if the deceased was registered as an individual entrepreneur [1] [6].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Succession Before a State Notary
steps.html:
• Six-month statutory deadline to accept the inheritance: Under the Civil Code of Turkmenistan, succession proceedings are conducted by the State Notary Office (Döwlet notarial edarasy) supervised by the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan at the place where the deceased last held permanent residence [1]. Both testamentary heirs (named in a notarized will) and statutory heirs must formally accept the inheritance within six months from the date of death by filing a written application with the state notary or by taking actual possession and management of estate property [1].
  • Opening the inheritance file (miras işi): To open the succession file and obtain the Certificate of Right to Inheritance (Miras hukugy hakynda şahadatnama) after the six-month period expires, heirs must submit the official Death Certificate, civil status records proving kinship (birth or marriage certificates issued by ZAGS), a certificate of the deceased's last place of residence, Any notarized will (wesýetnama), and title documents for real estate, vehicles, or bank deposits [1] [3].
  • Forced heirship and cross-border heirs: Turkmen succession law protects compulsory shares (hökmany paý) for minor or disabled children, as well as a disabled surviving spouse or parents, regardless of the terms of a will [1]. If an heir lives outside Turkmenistan, they may participate without traveling in person by executing a special power of attorney or statement of inheritance acceptance before a Turkmen consulate abroad or a foreign notary (duly legalized through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan or under an applicable bilateral treaty) and sending it to a representative in Turkmenistan before the six-month deadline expires [1] [4].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this guidance to your situation, in which city or province (welaýat) of Turkmenistan did the death occur, and did your family member leave a notarized will or have heirs or property located outside Turkmenistan?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Turkmenistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Turkmenistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Turkmenistan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
We understand that your family member has been diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or terminal illness in Turkmenistan. Below, we set out the five key medical, legal, financial, and administrative steps to complete in order while your family member still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative care and health coverageAs early as possible after diagnosisTerritorial polyclinic (Saglyk öýi) and oncology/specialty centers
2. Medical consent and healthcare representationWhile decision-making capacity is intactTreating medical institution and State Notary Office (Döwlet notarial edarasy)
3. Financial and legal powers of attorneyBefore any loss of legal capacityState Notary Office under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan
4. Disability assessment and social benefitsUpon clinical certification of impairmentMedical-Social Expert Commission (HÄK) and Pension Fund of Turkmenistan
5. Notarized will and civil status recordsWhile mental capacity is intactState Notary Office and ZAGS under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Medical Support, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Primary and specialized clinical care: In Turkmenistan, medical care for severe and life-limiting conditions is coordinated through the territorial polyclinic (Saglyk öýi) at the patient's registered place of residence and specialized national centers supervised by the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry (such as the Scientific and Clinical Center of Oncology in Ashgabat or provincial welaýat multi-profile hospitals) [5] [6]. Ask the attending specialist and the family physician (maşgala lukmany) to establish a written symptom-management and pain-relief protocol and to register the patient for home patronage visits by the district medical team [5].
  • State voluntary medical insurance (DMS): Verify that your family member's state voluntary medical insurance booklet (Meýletin lukmançylyk ätiýaçlandyryş şahadatnamasy) and disability or pensioner exemption status are current so that inpatient treatments, diagnostic imaging, and subsidized prescription analgesic medications are covered at the statutory state tariff rates [2] [5].
  • Home nursing and inpatient palliative relief: For patients remaining at home, the territorial polyclinic physician coordinates prescription analgesic dispensing and outpatient nursing visits [5]. Keep all clinical extracts (lukmançylyk göçürmesi) and hospital discharge summaries organized in a single folder at home for emergency medical crews (Tiz kömek) [5].

steps.title: Record Medical Treatment Preferences and Designate a Healthcare Representative
steps.html:
• Informed consent and patient representation under Turkmen health law: Under the Law of Turkmenistan on Protection of Citizens' Health, every patient with mental capacity has the right to give or refuse informed consent to medical intervention and to designate trusted family members who may receive confidential clinical information and consult with physicians [1] [5].
  • Notarized healthcare representation: Because Turkmenistan does not operate a separate standalone living-will registry, it is advisable for your family member, while fully lucid, to execute a notarized power of attorney (ynanç haty) before a state notary under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan explicitly authorizing a trusted family representative to access medical records, request medical commissions, sign hospital administrative forms, and communicate treatment preferences to the attending medical team [1] [5].
  • Confirming mental capacity at the time of signing: Request a current medical statement from the territorial polyclinic confirming that your family member is oriented and retains full capacity when executing medical and legal authorizations, and place a certified copy of the notarized authorization in the patient's hospital and polyclinic charts [1] [5].

steps.title: Execute Notarial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• State notarial power of attorney (Ynanç haty): Under the Civil Code of Turkmenistan, legal and financial representation requires a formal notarized power of attorney certified by a State Notary Office (Döwlet notarial edarasy) operating under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan [1]. While your family member has full legal capacity, they should execute a comprehensive notarized power of attorney empowering a trusted relative to manage bank accounts, receive pensions or social payments, pay utilities, deal with housing authorities, and represent them before state agencies [1].
  • Home or hospital visit by a state notary: If your family member is bedbound or hospitalized and cannot travel to the notary office in person, a family member may request an off-site visit by a state notary from the local district branch of the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan to verify identity and legal capacity and witness the signature at the bedside [1].
  • Commercial bank account and card mandates: Take the notarized power of attorney (or accompany the ill person directly) to their Turkmen commercial bank (such as Dayhanbank, Turkmenistan Bank, Senagat Bank, or Halkbank) to register an authorized representative on current accounts, deposit books, and pension bank cards (Altyn Asyr card accounts) before any incapacity arises [1] [6].

steps.title: Activate Disability Pensions, Caregiver Allowances, and Social Protection
steps.html:
• Referral to the Medical-Social Expert Commission (HÄK / MSEK): When an advanced illness causes persistent functional limitation, ask the attending physician at the territorial polyclinic (Saglyk öýi) to prepare a clinical referral to the Medical-Social Expert Commission (Hemaýata mätäçligi anyklaýjy lukmançylyk-durmuş ekspertiza topary) [2] [5]. Recognition of Category I disability (I topar maýyplyk, which applies to severely ill persons requiring constant external care) entitles the patient to a state disability pension or social allowance regardless of age [2].
  • Filing with the Pension Fund of Turkmenistan: Once the disability certificate is issued, the patient or their notarized representative submits the claim to the local district office of the Pension Fund of Turkmenistan (under the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Population) along with the passport, employment record book (zähmet depderçesi), and medical commission decision [2]. Under the Social Protection Code, individuals assessed with Category I disability requiring constant care and eligible family caregivers may also qualify for targeted care supplements and state social benefits [2] [6].
  • Temporary incapacity and workplace leave: If the ill person is still formally employed, ensure all medical incapacity certificates (işe ukypsyzlyk haty) are submitted to the employer to preserve paid sick-leave benefits prior to transitioning to a disability pension through the Pension Fund of Turkmenistan [2].

steps.title: Organize the Notarized Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a notarized will (Wesýetnama): Under the Civil Code of Turkmenistan, a valid will must be executed in writing and certified by a state notary at a State Notary Office under the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan (or, if the patient is in a hospital without access to a notary, certified by the chief physician or duty physician in accordance with statutory rules for wills equivalent to notarized instruments) [1]. When drafting the will, take into account Turkmenistan's compulsory heirship rules (hökmany paý), which guarantee a mandatory statutory share to minor children and disabled children, spouses, or parents [1].
  • Verifying civil status and property registration records: Gather and check the accuracy of the family's vital records (birth certificates, marriage certificates, and any name-change certificates) issued by the Civil Status Registration Offices (ZAGS) and coordinated with the State Committee of Turkmenistan on Statistics so that no spelling discrepancies delay future notarial proceedings [1] [3]. Consolidate original real estate title deeds (hususylaşdyryş or ownership certificates), technical passports, and the household registration book (öý kitaby) [1].
  • Cross-border documents and consular legalization: Because Turkmenistan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, any powers of attorney or civil status documents that must be used outside the CIS (or that arrive from relatives living abroad) must undergo full consular legalization through the Ministry of Justice of Turkmenistan and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Turkmenistan [1] [4].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your family's needs, in which city or province (welaýat) of Turkmenistan is your family member receiving care, and do they need a bedside visit from a state notary or cross-border powers of attorney for relatives living abroad?

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tuvalu: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tuvalu: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tuvalu: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We are sorry to hear that your family member has died in Tuvalu. Below, we outline the five official and practical steps to complete in order under Tuvaluan law, covering medical certification, civil registration, burial or international repatriation arrangements, provident fund and financial notifications, and estate administration.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical certification of deathImmediately upon deathPrincess Margaret Hospital (Funafuti) or outer-island clinic under the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu
2. Civil death registrationWithin 10 days of deathOffice of the Registrar General (Funafuti) or Island Council (Kaupule) Registrar
3. Burial or international repatriationAfter medical and civil certificationMinistry of Health of Tuvalu, local Kaupule, and diplomatic authorities
4. Provident fund, bank, and benefit noticesPromptly after obtaining the Death CertificateTuvalu National Provident Fund and National Bank of Tuvalu
5. Estate probate and customary land successionAfter death registrationHigh Court of Tuvalu, Island Lands Court, and Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of the Cause of Death
steps.html:
• Deaths at Princess Margaret Hospital or an outer-island health clinic: When a death occurs at Princess Margaret Hospital in Funafuti or at an outer-island medical center operated by the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu, the attending medical officer or registered nurse practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [2] [4]. This medical certificate records the clinical cause, date, and place of death required for civil registration [2] [4].
  • Deaths at home or in a village community: If your family member died at home in Funafuti or on an outer island (such as Vaitupu, Nanumea, Nukufetau, or Niutao), notify the nearest health clinic of the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu and the local Island Council (Kaupule) immediately [2] [4]. A medical officer or island health nurse must verify the death and issue the medical notification of death before registration and burial take place [2] [4].
  • Unexpected, accidental, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, unnatural, or occurred without recent medical attendance, report the matter immediately to the Tuvalu Police Service so that an inquiry can be referred to the Magistrate acting as Coroner under the Death and Fire Inquiries Act [2] [5]. No burial or removal of remains may proceed until any required post-mortem examination at Princess Margaret Hospital is completed and the Coroner issues written clearance [4] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry
steps.html:
• Where to register: Under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act (Cap. 24.08), civil registration of deaths is administered centrally by the Office of the Registrar General in Funafuti (under the Office of the Prime Minister and the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu) and locally on each island through the appointed Island Registrar at the Island Council (Kaupule), which shares vital statistics with the Central Statistics Division of Tuvalu [1] [2] [3].
  • Statutory deadline and informant obligation: The nearest relative present at the death or in attendance during the last illness (or, if none is available, the occupier of the house or person arranging the burial) must report and register the death with the Registrar within 10 days of the date of death [2] [3].
  • Required documents and official certificates: Present the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (or Coroner's certificate), the deceased's passport, birth certificate, or national identification documents, and the informant's valid identification [2]. Once the entry is recorded in the register of deaths, request several certified extracts of the official Death Certificate from the Office of the Registrar General or the Island Registrar, as originals are required for provident fund claims, banking, and succession [1] [2] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial in Funafuti or on outer islands: Community burial in family or village graves is the universal custom across Tuvalu, as there are no commercial crematoria on the islands [2] [4]. Coordinate release of the body from the Princess Margaret Hospital mortuary with the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu and obtain any required burial site clearance from the local Kaupule (Island Council) and church leadership [2] [4].
  • International repatriation of remains: If the deceased was a foreign citizen or if the family wishes to repatriate remains to Fiji, New Zealand, Australia, or another country (or return a Tuvaluan citizen's remains home from abroad), international air transport requires an official Death Certificate, a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death confirming the absence of communicable disease, an embalming and hermetically sealed coffin certificate, a public health export/import permit from the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu, and customs clearance [4] [5].
  • Document authentication and legalization: Tuvalu is not a contracting party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [5]. Consequently, when a Tuvaluan Death Certificate or court order must be used overseas, it must be certified by the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Labour and Trade, followed by consular legalization through the relevant foreign high commission or embassy (often accredited via Suva, Fiji, or Wellington, New Zealand) [5] [6].

steps.title: Notify the Provident Fund, Senior Citizen Scheme, and Banks
steps.html:
• Tuvalu National Provident Fund survivor payout: If the deceased was an employee, civil servant, or voluntary contributor, notify the Tuvalu National Provident Fund in Funafuti promptly [6]. Under the Tuvalu National Provident Fund Act (Cap. 32.08), upon the death of a member, the credit standing in their provident fund account (together with any applicable special death benefit) is payable to the nominated beneficiaries recorded on the member's official nomination form, or, if no valid nomination exists, in accordance with statutory distribution rules [6].
  • Senior Citizen Scheme and disability allowances: If your family member received the Tuvalu Senior Citizens Scheme monthly pension or a disability support allowance administered through the Department of Community Affairs and the Ministry of Finance, report the death with a certified copy of the Death Certificate so payments are closed without creating an estate overpayment [1] [6].
  • National Bank of Tuvalu and identity documents: Present the official Death Certificate to the National Bank of Tuvalu (and the Development Bank of Tuvalu if the deceased held loans or business accounts) to freeze individual accounts and inquire about procedures for releasing balances to executors or lawful next of kin [6]. Surrender the deceased's Tuvaluan passport to the Immigration Office in Funafuti [2].

steps.title: Administer the Estate, Probate, and Customary Land Succession
steps.html:
• Personal estate administration and probate: Under the Probate and Administration law overseen by the High Court and the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu, if the deceased left a valid written will covering personal property and bank balances, the named executor applies for a Grant of Probate [5] [6]. If the deceased died intestate (without a will), the surviving spouse or next of kin applies for Letters of Administration to collect and distribute personal estate assets after settling any debts [5] [6].
  • Customary land succession (Kaitasi and individual tenure): Under the Native Lands Act (Cap. 46.20), native land in Tuvalu cannot be alienated to non-natives, and succession to customary family land (kaitasi joint family estates or individual holdings) and wills of native land are governed strictly by the island's customary land code (Tuvalu Lands Code) and adjudicated by the local Lands Court on the island where the land is situated [2] [6]. Heirs must register land succession transfers before the Island Lands Court rather than relying on ordinary commercial probate [2] [6].
  • Cross-border heirs and overseas assets: Many Tuvaluan families have heirs or seamen's earnings and bank accounts in Fiji, New Zealand, or Australia [1] [6]. If an heir resides abroad, they may execute a notarized and legalized power of attorney authorizing a representative in Funafuti to act in estate or Lands Court proceedings, and any foreign grant of probate for overseas assets must be coordinated through the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu and the High Court registry [5] [6].

closingQuestion: To help us tailor this checklist to your exact situation, did the death occur on Funafuti or on an outer island, and did your family member hold an account with the Tuvalu National Provident Fund or leave customary land or overseas assets?

2. Advance healthcare preferences and medical proxyWhile decision-making capacity is intactTreating physicians at the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu and family representative
3. Financial powers of attorney and bank mandatesBefore any loss of legal capacityOffice of the Attorney General of Tuvalu / People's Lawyer and National Bank of Tuvalu
4. Medical incapacity, provident fund, and care supportUpon medical board certificationTuvalu National Provident Fund and Department of Community Affairs
5. Written will, customary land, and vital recordsWhile mental capacity is intactIsland Lands Court, Office of the Registrar General, and Central Statistics Division of Tuvalu

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Public clinical and home-based care: In Tuvalu, healthcare for serious and life-limiting illnesses is delivered through the public health system administered by the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu, centered at Princess Margaret Hospital in Funafuti and supported by outer-island medical clinics [4]. Ask the attending medical officer at Princess Margaret Hospital to establish a written symptom-management and pain-relief plan and to schedule regular community nursing visits if your family member wishes to be cared for at home [4].
  • Tuvalu Medical Treatment Scheme (overseas referrals): Public healthcare in Tuvalu is government-funded for Tuvaluan citizens, and complex oncology, cardiac, or tertiary palliative consultations are frequently referred overseas (most commonly to Fiji or New Zealand) through the Tuvalu Medical Treatment Scheme overseen by the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu [4] [6]. If your family member is returning to Funafuti from an overseas hospital, ensure that full clinical discharge summaries and analgesic prescriptions are transferred to Princess Margaret Hospital before travel [4].
  • Community and civil society support: Connect with public health nurses, the Tuvalu Red Cross Society, and local church or Falekaupule community networks to arrange home-care equipment, mobility aids, and practical caregiver assistance [4] [6].

steps.title: Record Advance Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Documenting treatment wishes while capacity is intact: Tuvalu does not have a standalone statutory Living Will Act, so clinical decision-making is governed by common-law principles of informed consent and public health legislation overseen by the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu and the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu [4] [5]. While your family member has full mental capacity, it is advisable for them to sign a clear written statement of treatment preferences covering cardiopulmonary resuscitation, mechanical ventilation, artificial nutrition, pain management, and whether they prefer to receive end-of-life care at home or at Princess Margaret Hospital [4] [5].
  • Designating a family healthcare spokesperson: In Tuvaluan clinical practice, physicians consult closely with the patient and their designated immediate family representative. Have your family member name a primary and alternate family medical spokesperson in writing, signed in the presence of the treating physician at the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu or a legal practitioner, and place a copy directly into the patient's chart at Princess Margaret Hospital [4] [5].
  • Contemporaneous capacity note: Ask the attending medical officer at Princess Margaret Hospital to record a dated clinical entry confirming that your family member was fully lucid and understood their medical and legal choices when signing their advance care instructions and legal mandates [4].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Formal Power of Attorney under Tuvaluan law: While your family member retains full legal capacity, they should execute a written Power of Attorney authorizing a trusted relative in Funafuti to manage financial affairs, sign administrative documents, and deal with public authorities [5]. Legal drafting assistance can be obtained through the Office of the People's Lawyer (which provides public legal aid in Tuvalu) or reviewed under the legal framework of the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu, and witnessed before a Commissioner for Oaths or Magistrate [5] [6].
  • National Bank of Tuvalu signing mandates: Because banking services in Tuvalu are concentrated at the National Bank of Tuvalu (and the Development Bank of Tuvalu), accompany your family member to the bank branch in Funafuti (or request a home or hospital verification if they are immobile) to register a third-party signatory mandate on their savings or current accounts while capacity is intact [6].
  • Cross-border powers of attorney: Because Tuvalu is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, any power of attorney executed in Tuvalu for use in Fiji, New Zealand, Australia, or regarding overseas seafarer accounts must be authenticated through the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Labour and Trade for consular legalization [5]. Conversely, if an enduring power of attorney is needed for assets held in New Zealand or Australia, execute a form compliant with that foreign jurisdiction's enduring power of attorney statute while capacity remains intact [5].

steps.title: Activate Medical Incapacity, Provident Fund, and Caregiver Benefits
steps.html:
• Tuvalu National Provident Fund medical incapacity withdrawal: If your family member is a member of the Tuvalu National Provident Fund and can no longer work due to permanent physical or mental incapacity caused by their illness, contact the Tuvalu National Provident Fund office in Funafuti [6]. Under the Tuvalu National Provident Fund Act (Cap. 32.08), a member who is certified by a medical board approved by the Ministry of Health of Tuvalu as permanently incapable of employment may apply to withdraw their accumulated provident fund balance early on medical grounds [4] [6].
  • Reviewing provident fund beneficiary nominations: If the member leaves funds in their account, verify and update their official beneficiary nomination form on file with the Tuvalu National Provident Fund while they have full mental capacity, ensuring that the named beneficiaries and share percentages accurately reflect their current wishes [6].
  • Disability support, Senior Citizen Scheme, and caregiver leave: Inquire with the Department of Community Affairs (under the Ministry of Home Affairs) regarding the Tuvalu Disability Support Scheme allowance or, if the patient is aged 70 or older, the Senior Citizens Scheme pension [1] [6]. Family caregivers employed in the Tuvalu Public Service may apply for compassionate leave or special family leave under the General Administrative Orders.

steps.title: Organize the Will, Customary Land Records, and Civil Status Documents
steps.html:
• Executing a valid written will for personal property: For bank deposits, personal effects, business interests, and non-customary assets, your family member should execute a formal written will in the simultaneous presence of two independent adult witnesses who are not beneficiaries (nor spouses of beneficiaries), naming an executor to administer the estate under the jurisdiction of the High Court and the Office of the Attorney General of Tuvalu [5] [6].
  • Customary land (kaitasi) and Lands Court rules: Under the Native Lands Act (Cap. 46.20) and the Tuvalu Lands Code, succession to customary native land on Funafuti and the outer islands is governed by island-specific customary tenure rules and the local Island Lands Court rather than ordinary commercial wills [2] [6]. If your family member wishes to make dispositions or clarify family arrangements regarding native land (kaitasi or individual holdings), consult the local Lands Court registrar on the relevant island while your family member has full capacity [2] [6].
  • Verifying civil registration documents: Check that your family member's birth certificate, marriage certificate, and children's birth certificates are properly recorded with the Office of the Registrar General in Funafuti and the Island Council (Kaupule) civil registry, which coordinate vital records with the Central Statistics Division of Tuvalu [1] [2] [3]. Obtain certified extracts now so that future benefit claims and estate filings proceed without delay [1] [2] [3].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Uzbekistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Uzbekistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Uzbekistan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We offer our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Uzbekistan. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to manage medical certification, civil death registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social security and financial notifications, and notarial estate administration under the laws of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinic deaths: When a person dies in a hospital or licensed healthcare facility overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Uzbekistan, the attending physician confirms the death and generates an electronic medical certificate of death (tibbiy o'lim haqidagi ma'lumotnoma) through the national automated health information system [1] [5]. The medical certificate is assigned a unique identification number and QR code and is transmitted electronically to the civil registry system [1].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home from a documented natural illness, contact the local family polyclinic or emergency medical service (103) immediately so an authorized physician can examine the body, verify prior clinical records, and issue the electronic medical certificate of death via the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Uzbekistan system [5].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or non-natural deaths: If the death occurred unexpectedly, outside medical supervision, or under accidental or unexplained circumstances, you must notify the territorial Internal Affairs department (police, 102) [1] [5]. The police and forensic medical examination bureau conduct an inquiry and, where required, an autopsy before issuing the forensic medical death certificate clearing the remains for release [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry (FHDYO / ZAGS)
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and automated filing: Under the Family Code of the Republic of Uzbekistan and civil status regulations administered by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan, a death declaration must be submitted within three days of the death or the discovery of the body [1] [4]. Through Uzbekistan's composite electronic system, the medical institution transmits the electronic death record directly to the Civil Status Acts Registration Department (FHDYO / ZAGS) [1] [4].
  • Issuance of the official death certificate: Once the FHDYO office registers the death act record, it issues an official extract and QR-coded certificate confirming registration, which can also be accessed through the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz) [1]. Family members or authorized representatives may request stamped paper death certificates in person at any Public Services Center or FHDYO branch on an extraterritorial basis [1] [4].
  • Required identification documents: When collecting physical certificates or completing manual registration, bring the deceased's national ID card or biometric passport (including the 14-digit personal identification number, JShShIR / PINFL), the informant's passport or ID card, and the medical or forensic certificate number [1] [4].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial and cemetery permits: Burials in Uzbekistan are coordinated with municipal cemetery administrations or local self-governing community bodies (mahalla committees) upon presentation of the medical death certificate or QR-coded FHDYO death registration extract [1] [5]. Traditional burials normally take place promptly once medical and civil clearances are issued.
  • Licensed mortuary preparation for international repatriation: If your family member's remains must be transported out of Uzbekistan, engage a licensed funeral and repatriation director to coordinate embalming, zinc-lined hermetically sealed coffin preparation, and a sanitary-epidemiological clearance certificate from the Committee for Sanitary and Epidemiological Welfare and Public Health under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Uzbekistan [5].
  • Apostille and consular documentation: Uzbekistan is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. For foreign nationals or cross-border estate use, obtain an official FHDYO death certificate, have it affixed with an Apostille through the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan or the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz), and notify the relevant foreign embassy in Tashkent to issue a consular mortuary laissez-passer [1] [4].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, and Banking Authorities
steps.html:
• Statutory funeral grant (Dafn nafaqasi): Under Uzbekistan's social protection legislation, the spouse, close relative, or person who bore the funeral expenses is entitled to a one-time statutory funeral allowance funded through the Extrabudgetary Pension Fund under the Ministry of Economy and Finance [1] [2]. When the electronic death certificate is generated, the claim is routed automatically and paid through designated commercial banks (such as Xalq Banki) upon presentation of the applicant's ID and QR-coded death record within 60 days [1] [2].
  • Unpaid pension arrears and survivor's pension: Under the Law on State Pension Provision of Citizens, any accrued pension unpaid before death is payable to eligible family members, and dependent relatives (such as minor children, full-time students under age 23, disabled dependents, or qualifying surviving spouses/parents) may apply for a survivor's pension (boquvchisini yo'qotganlik pensiyasi) through the Extrabudgetary Pension Fund under the Ministry of Economy and Finance or via the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz) [2] [3].
  • Banks, tax offices, and identity cancellation: The FHDYO electronic registration automatically updates the population registry to cancel the deceased's ID card and passport [1]. You should still present the death certificate to commercial banks in Uzbekistan to freeze individual bank accounts, stop recurring debits, and obtain date-of-death balance statements for notarial succession [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession (Meros)
steps.html:
• Six-month statutory deadline to open succession: Under Book Five of the Civil Code of the Republic of Uzbekistan, succession opens on the date of death at the deceased's last permanent place of residence [4]. Both testamentary heirs (under a notarized will) and statutory heirs must file a formal declaration accepting the inheritance with a notary within six months of the date of death [4].
  • Certificate of Right to Inheritance: Public and private notaries in Uzbekistan operate through the automated e-notarius system overseen by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Chamber of Notaries [4]. The notary verifies whether a will exists, confirms the statutory ranks of heirs, checks cadastral and vehicle registries, and issues the Certificate of Right to Inheritance (Meros huquqi to'g'risidagi guvohnoma) after the six-month period expires [4].
  • Tax treatment and cross-border heirs: Uzbekistan does not levy a separate inheritance tax on property inherited by natural persons, though statutory notary duties and cadastral re-registration fees apply [4]. Heirs residing outside Uzbekistan may participate in the succession by granting a notarized power of attorney (legalized or bearing an Apostille and translated into Uzbek or Russian) so a local representative can accept the inheritance and register title transfers on their behalf [1] [4].

closingQuestion: Which city or region in Uzbekistan did your family member pass away in, and did your family member hold Uzbek citizenship or foreign nationality so we can tailor the civil registration and notarial succession steps?

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Uzbekistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Uzbekistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Uzbekistan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Uzbekistan is diagnosed with an advanced or life-limiting illness, taking early, structured steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their healthcare preferences, financial affairs, and family security. Below, we set out the five main medical, legal, and administrative steps to complete under the laws of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Nursing, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Specialist oncology and palliative services: Under the Law on Protection of Citizens' Health and programs overseen by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Uzbekistan, patients with advanced or life-limiting illnesses are entitled to palliative medical care, pain management, and symptomatic support through regional multidisciplinary medical centers, specialized oncology centers, and local family polyclinics [1] [5].
  • Home patronage and pain relief prescriptions: Register the patient with the territorial family polyclinic (oilaviy poliklinika) at their place of residence so a patronage physician and visiting nurse can establish an ongoing home care plan, monitor symptoms, and issue regulated prescriptions for strong analgesics in accordance with clinical protocols [5].
  • State guaranteed health coverage and social registries: Verify the patient's registration in the electronic healthcare system using their 14-digit personal identification number (JShShIR / PINFL) via the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz) to access state-funded inpatient referrals, preferential medication supply lists, and inpatient palliative care beds [1] [5].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Medical Representation
steps.html:
• Informed consent and patient rights: Under Uzbekistan's Law on Protection of Citizens' Health, every capable patient has the right to receive clinical information in an accessible form, to give informed voluntary consent to medical intervention, or to refuse specific medical procedures or hospitalization in writing at the healthcare facility [5].
  • Designating a trusted representative in clinical records: While Uzbekistan does not have a standalone statutory living will registry separate from hospital records, the patient can submit a written statement to the treating facility under the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Uzbekistan naming trusted family members authorized to receive confidential medical updates, access medical extracts, and be consulted by physicians if the patient's condition deteriorates [4] [5].
  • Notarized authorization for medical administration: While the ill person retains full legal capacity, they may also execute a notarized power of attorney (ishonchnoma) through a notary supervised by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan authorizing a representative to request medical records, submit referrals, and handle administrative interactions with healthcare institutions and insurers [2] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Notarial powers of attorney while capacity is intact: Under the Civil Code of the Republic of Uzbekistan, a power of attorney (ishonchnoma) can only be executed while the principal has full legal capacity, and it ceases to have legal effect if the principal is subsequently declared legally incapacitated or dies [2] [3]. Act promptly to have a public or private notary record the power of attorney in the national electronic registry (e-notarius) overseen by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan [2] [3].
  • Mobile home or hospital notary visits: If your family member cannot travel due to serious illness, notaries and Public Services Centers under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan provide off-site (sayyor) visits to the patient's home or hospital ward to verify identity and mental capacity and certify powers of attorney in person [2] [4].
  • Bank mandates and pension collection rules: Specify explicit banking powers (operating accounts, paying bills, managing deposits) in the notarized power of attorney, and note that under Cabinet of Ministers pension regulations, powers of attorney used to collect state pensions or allowances are exempt from state notary duty but require periodic re-confirmation under the rules of the Extrabudgetary Pension Fund under the Ministry of Economy and Finance [2] [3].

steps.title: Activate Disability Benefits, Caregiver Support, and Sick Leave
steps.html:
• Medical and Social Expert Commission (TIEK) assessment: Ask the treating family polyclinic to refer the patient's clinical dossier electronically to the Medical and Social Expert Commission (Tibbiy-ijtimoiy ekspert komissiyasi, TIEK) to establish a formal disability group (Group I, II, or III) and determine the need for constant outside nursing care [1] [4].
  • Disability pension and social allowances: Once Group I or Group II disability is certified, submit an application through the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz) or the Extrabudgetary Pension Fund under the Ministry of Economy and Finance to activate a state disability pension or social disability allowance, which is often assigned proactively once TIEK data is logged [1] [3] [4].
  • Caregiver leave and social protection support: Employed family members caring for a seriously ill relative may obtain a temporary incapacity/care certificate (mehnatga layoqatsizlik varaqasi) through the healthcare facility, and caregivers of persons with Group I disability may qualify for social service support and pension service credit recognition [1] [4] [5].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing a notarized will (Vasiyatnoma): Under Book Five of the Civil Code of the Republic of Uzbekistan, a will must be made in writing and certified by a notary (or, in exceptional clinical circumstances, by the chief physician or duty doctor of the hospital where the testator is receiving inpatient treatment) while the testator possesses full mental capacity [2]. Note that minor or disabled children, spouses, and parents remain entitled to a statutory compulsory share (majburiy ulush) regardless of testamentary terms [2].
  • Auditing civil status and cadastral records: Verify that the ill person's national ID card, marriage certificate, children's birth certificates, and real estate cadastral records match the exact spelling and JShShIR (PINFL) in the state registries accessible via the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (my.gov.uz) so future heirs do not face name-discrepancy delays [1] [2].
  • Cross-border assets and foreign family members: If the ill person owns property outside Uzbekistan or if designated representatives or heirs live abroad, arrange for powers of attorney and civil status extracts to be affixed with an Apostille through the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Uzbekistan so they are legally recognized across jurisdictions [1] [2].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Vanuatu: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Vanuatu: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Vanuatu: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: We offer our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Vanuatu. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to manage medical certification, civil death registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, provident fund and financial notifications, and court probate or estate administration in the Republic of Vanuatu.

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death
steps.html:
• Hospital or health center deaths: When a death occurs at Vila Central Hospital in Port Vila, Northern Provincial Hospital in Luganville, or a provincial health facility overseen by the Ministry of Health, the attending medical practitioner examines the deceased and issues the official Medical Certificate of Cause of Death [1]. This clinical certificate is required to release the body from the hospital mortuary and register the death [1].
  • Deaths at home or in rural island communities: If your family member died at home or in a village from natural causes, contact the nearest hospital, provincial health center, or registered nurse practitioner immediately so an authorized health officer can verify the death and complete the medical death notification form required by the Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management [1].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or unexplained deaths: If the death was sudden, accidental, unattended by a medical practitioner, or occurred under unexplained circumstances, you must report it immediately to the Vanuatu Police Force [1] [3]. Under Vanuatu's inquest and coronial procedures, the police and a designated magistrate/coroner must investigate the circumstances and authorize any required post-mortem examination before issuing clearance for burial or repatriation [1] [3].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry (CRIM)
steps.html:
• Responsible national and municipal authorities: Civil registration of deaths in Vanuatu is governed by the Civil Registration and Identity Management Act and administered by the Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management, alongside municipal civil status offices such as the Port Vila City Council Civil Status Unit [1] [2].
  • Statutory deadline and informant obligations: A close relative, household head, or person present at the death must report and register the death with the Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management or provincial civil registrar as soon as practicable (standard statutory practice requires notification within 21 days of the death) [1].
  • Issuance of official death certificates: Present the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death, the deceased's national ID card, birth certificate, or passport, and the informant's identification [1]. Once recorded in the National Civil Register, the registrar issues the official Death Certificate, which is mandatory for burial permits, provident fund claims, banking closures, and court probate filings [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Municipal burial and cemetery permits: For burials within urban municipalities such as Port Vila or Luganville, present the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death and civil registration paperwork to the local municipal authority - such as the Port Vila City Council Civil Status Unit - to obtain a burial permit and allocate a plot at the municipal cemetery [2]. For customary burials on home islands, coordinate transport clearance with hospital mortuary authorities and local community chiefs [1] [2].
  • International repatriation of remains: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains must be repatriated abroad, coordinate with the hospital mortuary at Vila Central Hospital and an international funeral/cargo agent to arrange embalming, hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin preparation, a Ministry of Health public health export clearance certificate, and customs export documentation through Bauerfield International Airport [1].
  • Apostille and consular notification: Vanuatu is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. If Vanuatu death certificates or court documents must be used overseas, request an Apostille certification through the competent Vanuatu government authority (Department of Foreign Affairs / State Law Office) and notify the deceased's embassy or high commission so consular authorities can issue any required mortuary transit permit [1] [3].

steps.title: Notify Provident Fund, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• Vanuatu National Provident Fund (VNPF) death benefits: If the deceased was a contributor or member of the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, notify the fund promptly [4]. Under the VNPF Act, accumulated member credit balances and any applicable Special Death Benefit are paid out to the valid nominated beneficiaries on file with the Vanuatu National Provident Fund (or distributed in accordance with statutory rules if no nomination is active) upon submission of the official Death Certificate, medical certificate, and beneficiary identification [4].
  • Commercial banks and insurer notifications: Provide certified copies of the Death Certificate to all commercial banks operating in Vanuatu (such as National Bank of Vanuatu, ANZ, BSP, or Bred Bank) and any private insurers [3]. Banks will freeze sole accounts in the deceased's name and issue date-of-death balance statements needed for Supreme Court probate or small-estate release [3].
  • Identity card, passport, and employer settlements: The Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management updates the national identity register upon death registration [1]. You should also notify the deceased's employer to settle final wages, accrued annual leave, and any statutory severance entitlements under Vanuatu employment law [3] [4].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Supreme Court Probate
steps.html:
• Grant of Probate (where a valid Will exists): Formal administration of estates in Vanuatu is governed by the Wills Act [Cap 55], the Administration of Estates rules, and the Probate and Administration Rules overseen by the Supreme Court of Vanuatu [3]. If the deceased left a valid written will, the named executor must file an Application for Probate (Form 1), supported by a sworn executor's affidavit, the original will, the official Death Certificate, and an inventory of estate assets and liabilities with the Probate Registry of the Supreme Court of Vanuatu [3].
  • Letters of Administration (intestate estates) and customary land: If the deceased died without a will, the surviving spouse or next of kin must apply to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu for Letters of Administration [3]. Note that under the Constitution of Vanuatu, indigenous customary land rights follow custom (kastom) and customary dispute mechanisms rather than ordinary freehold estate distribution, whereas registered leases, bank accounts, and personal property are administered through the court grant [3].
  • Taxation and cross-border estate coordination: Vanuatu does not levy personal income tax, capital gains tax, estate duty, or inheritance tax, though court probate filing fees and lease transfer registration fees apply [3]. If an executor or heir resides outside Vanuatu, they may instruct a legal practitioner admitted to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu using a notarized and Apostilled power of attorney to apply for probate or reseal a foreign grant of probate in Vanuatu [1] [3].

title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Vanuatu: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Vanuatu: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Vanuatu: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member in Vanuatu is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking timely medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity ensures their care preferences and assets are properly protected. Below, we set out the five main steps to complete in order under the laws and administrative procedures of the Republic of Vanuatu.

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Hospital Services, and Health Coverage
steps.html:
• Referral hospitals and clinical symptom management: In Vanuatu, specialist medical management, inpatient care, and pain relief for serious or life-limiting conditions are coordinated primarily through Vila Central Hospital in Port Vila and Northern Provincial Hospital in Luganville, alongside provincial hospitals and health centers [1] [2]. Ask the treating physician for a written clinical care summary and symptom management plan [1].
  • Community nursing and home support: Because standalone hospice facilities are limited in Vanuatu, families caring for an ill person at home should coordinate directly with hospital outpatient clinics, provincial community health nurses, and municipal bodies such as the Port Vila City Council Civil Status Unit and community welfare teams to arrange home visits, wound care, and ongoing analgesic prescriptions [1] [2].
  • Overseas medical referral or private medical evacuation insurance: If the ill person holds private health or medical evacuation insurance, or is being assessed for a government-sponsored overseas medical referral scheme, ensure the patient's civil identity records with the Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management and passport validity are up to date for urgent travel [1].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Medical Consultation Instructions
steps.html:
• Absence of a standalone statutory living will act: Vanuatu's codified legislation does not currently establish a separate statutory advance healthcare directive registry or dedicated medical power of attorney statute [3]. Instead, clinical consent and end-of-life treatment decisions are governed by common-law principles of informed patient consent and hospital clinical protocols [3].
  • Written statement of treatment preferences: While your family member has full mental capacity, they should sign and date a clear written statement of their medical preferences (such as goals for comfort care, pain relief, hospitalization, or refusal of invasive life-prolonging interventions) and ask the attending doctor at Vila Central Hospital or the treating clinic to place a signed copy directly in the patient's medical file [1] [3].
  • Designating next-of-kin medical contacts: Have the ill person formally record in their hospital chart the names and phone numbers of the primary next-of-kin or family spokesperson whom clinicians should consult if the ill person becomes unable to communicate treatment decisions [1] [3].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Executing a Power of Attorney while capacity is intact: Under the legal principles applied by the Supreme Court of Vanuatu, a Power of Attorney deed authorizing a trusted representative (attorney-in-fact) to manage property, sign legal documents, and administer financial affairs is valid only if executed while the donor possesses full mental and legal capacity [3]. Consult a legal practitioner admitted to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu or a Commissioner for Oaths to draft and witness the deed properly [3].
  • Direct commercial bank account mandates: Commercial banks in Vanuatu (including National Bank of Vanuatu, ANZ, BSP, and Bred Bank) often require their own internal third-party authority forms or joint-signatory mandates in addition to a general power of attorney [3]. Arrange for your family member to sign the bank's specific mandate forms in person or via a verified home/hospital visit while they are able to do so [3].
  • Land lease and property management authority: If the ill person holds registered urban or agricultural land leases in Vanuatu, ensure the Power of Attorney meets formal execution and witnessing standards so the representative can deal with leasehold administration if needed [3].

steps.title: Activate Provident Fund Medical Withdrawals and Caregiver Support
steps.html:
• Vanuatu National Provident Fund (VNPF) medical and incapacity entitlements: If the ill person is a member of the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, contact VNPF to review eligibility for early withdrawal on grounds of permanent physical or mental incapacity (certified by approved medical practitioners) or eligible medical assistance schemes under the VNPF Act [4].
  • Updating VNPF Nominated Beneficiaries: While the member has full capacity, verify and update their official Nominated Beneficiaries form on file with the Vanuatu National Provident Fund [4]. Having an accurate, up-to-date beneficiary nomination ensures that accumulated VNPF savings and any Special Death Benefit are paid directly to designated family members without delay [4].
  • Employment sick leave and caregiver arrangements: Under Vanuatu's Employment Act, employees are entitled to statutory paid sick leave upon presentation of a medical certificate, and family caregivers should request formal medical documentation from the treating physician to arrange workplace leave or flexible care schedules [3] [4].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Estate Documents
steps.html:
• Drafting or updating a valid Will: Under the Wills Act [Cap 55] and probate procedures of the Supreme Court of Vanuatu, a valid written will must be signed by the testator while of sound mind in the presence of two independent witnesses who are present at the same time and who are not beneficiaries (nor spouses of beneficiaries) under the will [3]. Appoint a reliable executor who will later submit Form 1 (Application for Probate) to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu [3].
  • Verifying civil identity and family records: Check that the ill person's birth record, marriage certificate, and national identity card held by the Department of Civil Registration and Identity Management (and any municipal records at the Port Vila City Council Civil Status Unit) are accurate and consistent with the names on bank accounts and property leases [1] [2].
  • Cross-border assets and foreign representatives: Because Vanuatu has no inheritance or estate tax, clear documentation is the main priority for smooth estate administration [3]. If the ill person owns assets abroad or if family members live overseas, ensure powers of attorney and civil status documents are notarized and certified with an Apostille so they are recognized across jurisdictions [1] [3].

title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Vietnam: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Vietnam: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Vietnam: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml:
We offer our sincere condolences on the passing of your family member in Vietnam. Below, we set out the five main official and practical steps to manage medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral or international repatriation arrangements, social security and financial notifications, and estate succession under the laws of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Medical Death NoticeImmediately upon deathTreating hospital, commune health station, or Public Security authority
2. Civil Death RegistrationWithin 15 days of deathCommune-level or District-level People's Committee (Ministry of Justice of Vietnam)
3. Funeral or RepatriationAfter burial permit issuedLicensed funeral service provider, border health quarantine, and consular mission
4. Social Insurance & BanksWithin 90 days for survivor benefitsVietnam Social Security (BHXH Viet Nam), tax offices, and commercial banks
5. Estate SuccessionWithin 10-30 years depending on asset classNotary Office under the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam or People's Court

steps.title: Obtain Medical Certification of Death (Giay Bao Tu)
steps.html:
• Hospital or clinical facility deaths: When a person dies in a public or private hospital or healthcare center overseen by the Ministry of Health of Vietnam, the head of the medical facility issues the official Death Notice (Giay bao tu) confirming the time and medical cause of death [3] [4]. This document is required before the hospital mortuary releases the body and before civil registration can take place [3] [4].
  • Deaths at home from natural causes: If your family member died at home outside a medical facility, notify the local commune, ward, or township health station under the Ministry of Health of Vietnam and the local residential group leader so an authorized health official or Commune-level People's Committee officer can confirm the death and issue the document replacing a hospital Death Notice [3] [4].
  • Unexpected, sudden, or non-natural deaths: If the death occurred suddenly, in an accident, or under unexplained circumstances, you must report it immediately to the local Public Security (police) agency [3] [5]. Forensic medical examiners and the investigating authority conduct an inquiry and, where necessary, a forensic autopsy before issuing written confirmation clearing the remains for release and civil registration [3] [5].

steps.title: Register the Death with the Civil Registry (Dang Ky Khai Tu)
steps.html:
• Statutory deadline and competent authority: Under the Law on Civil Status administered by the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam, a close relative or household member must register the death within 15 days from the date of death [3] [5]. For Vietnamese citizens residing domestically, registration is completed at the Commune-level People's Committee (Uy ban nhan dan cap xa) of the deceased's last place of residence; for foreign citizens or Vietnamese citizens residing abroad who die in Vietnam, registration falls under the District-level People's Committee (Uy ban nhan dan cap huyen) [3] [5].
  • Issuance of the Death Certificate Extract: Submit the civil death declaration form together with the original Death Notice (Giay bao tu), the deceased's citizen identity card (Can cuoc cong dan) or passport, and the informant's identification via the Government Portal of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam or in person at the one-stop civil registry counter [3] [5]. Upon recording the entry in the civil status book, the registrar issues the official Death Certificate Extract (Trich luc khai tu) [3].
  • Ordering certified copies: Request multiple certified copies (ban sao trich luc khai tu) at the time of registration, as separate originals or certified extracts are required by Vietnam Social Security, commercial banks, insurers, and notary offices [1] [3].

steps.title: Arrange Burial, Cremation, or International Repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial and cremation permits: When registering the death, the Commune-level or District-level People's Committee notes the death registration clearance required by municipal cemetery boards or crematoria [3] [5]. Licensed funeral service providers coordinate mortuary storage, coffin preparation, burial plot allocation, or cremation in compliance with sanitation regulations issued by the Ministry of Health of Vietnam [4] [5].
  • International repatriation of remains or ashes: If your family member was a foreign national or if the remains or cremated ashes must be transported out of Vietnam, engage an authorized international funeral director to obtain a border health quarantine certificate from the Center for Disease Control under the Ministry of Health of Vietnam, an embalming and hermetically sealed zinc-lined coffin certificate (for bodily remains), and customs export clearance [4] [5].
  • Consular legalization of documents: Because Vietnam is not currently a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, Vietnamese Death Certificate Extracts intended for official use abroad must be certified by the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (or the Ho Chi Minh City Department of External Relations) and then legalized by the relevant foreign embassy or consulate in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City [3] [5].

steps.title: Notify Social Security, Pension, Tax, Banking, and Identity Authorities
steps.html:
• Funeral allowance and survivor benefits: Under the Law on Social Insurance administered by Vietnam Social Security, the family or person organizing the funeral of an insured worker or pensioner is entitled to a lump-sum funeral allowance (tro cap mai tang) equal to 10 times the statutory reference level, alongside either a monthly survivor pension (tro cap tuat hang thang) for eligible dependents or a lump-sum survivor benefit (tro cap tuat mot lan) [1] [2]. Submit the claim dossier, including the Death Certificate Extract and social insurance records, to the provincial or district office of Vietnam Social Security within 90 days of the death [1].
  • Commercial banks, insurers, and tax clearance: Present the Death Certificate Extract to all commercial banks in Vietnam where the deceased held accounts [2] [5]. Banks will freeze sole accounts in the deceased's name and issue date-of-death balance certificates required for notarial succession, while tax authorities and employers settle final personal income tax obligations and unpaid wages [2] [5].
  • Cancellation of Citizen Identity Card and residence registration: Through electronic data linkage between the civil status database of the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam and the National Population Database tracked via the Government Portal of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, the deceased's permanent residence record and Citizen Identity Card (CCCD) are updated and canceled upon death registration [3] [5].

steps.title: Administer the Estate and Notarial Succession
steps.html:
• Notarial agreement or declaration of inheritance: Under Part Four of the 2015 Civil Code of Vietnam, succession opens at the time of death at the deceased's last place of residence [2] [5]. Where there is no dispute among heirs, the executor and heirs appear before a public Notary Office (Phong cong chung) or private Notary Office supervised by the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam to execute a notarized Written Agreement on Division of Estate (Van ban phan chia di san thua ke) or Written Declaration of Acceptance of Estate [3] [5]. The notary posts a mandatory 15-day public notice at the Commune-level People's Committee where the deceased last resided and where any real estate is located to verify that no omitted heirs or creditors object before certifying the succession instrument [3] [5].
  • Compulsory heirs and court resolution of disputes: Even when a valid written will exists, Article 644 of the Civil Code protects compulsory heirs (minor children, parents, spouse, and adult children incapable of working), guaranteeing them at least two-thirds of the share they would have received under statutory intestate succession [5]. If heirs cannot reach an agreement or a will is contested, succession is adjudicated by the competent People's Court [5].
  • Tax treatment and cross-border heirs: In Vietnam, inheritance of real estate and registrable assets between spouses, biological or adoptive parents and children, parents-in-law and children-in-law, grandparents and grandchildren, and biological siblings is exempt from Personal Income Tax, whereas other heirs pay a 10% tax on inherited asset value exceeding VND 10 million upon registration [2] [5]. Foreign nationals and overseas heirs who are not permitted to hold direct land-use right titles in Vietnam are legally entitled to receive the monetary value from the sale of inherited real property, and heirs residing abroad may execute a consular-legalized power of attorney so a representative in Vietnam can complete notarial and land-registry formalities [2] [5].
