title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Vietnam: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Vietnam: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Vietnam: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml:
When a family member in Vietnam is diagnosed with an advanced, life-limiting, or serious illness, taking structured medical, legal, and financial steps while the ill person still retains full mental and legal decision-making capacity helps protect their care preferences, assets, and family security. Below, we set out the five main steps to complete in order under the laws and administrative procedures of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

StepDeadlineAuthority
1. Palliative Care & Health CoverageUpon specialist diagnosisTreating hospital, oncology center, and Vietnam Social Security (BHYT)
2. Medical Preferences & SpokespersonWhile capacity is intactTreating hospital department under the Ministry of Health of Vietnam
3. Financial Powers of AttorneyBefore any loss of legal capacityPublic or private Notary Office under the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam
4. Sickness & Disability BenefitsUpon Medical Assessment Council ratingMedical Assessment Council (Hoi dong Giam dinh Y khoa) and Vietnam Social Security
5. Will & Property Records AuditWhile testator has sound mindNotary Office, Commune-level People's Committee, and Land Registration Office

steps.title: Coordinate Palliative Care, Home Support, and Health Insurance (BHYT)
steps.html:
• Oncology and palliative care departments: Under national clinical guidelines issued by the Ministry of Health of Vietnam, specialist palliative care, symptom control, and regulated opioid pain management are provided through central and provincial oncology hospitals, general hospital palliative units, and district health centers [4]. Request a formal clinical summary and symptom management plan from the attending specialist [4].
  • Outpatient pain relief and community care: If the ill person is cared for at home, register their specialist treatment dossier with the local health facility overseen by the Ministry of Health of Vietnam so the treating physician can issue outpatient prescriptions for controlled analgesics in compliance with Ministry of Health regulations and coordinate community nursing support [4] [5].
  • Social Health Insurance (Bao hiem y te - BHYT) referral rules: Verify the patient's Social Health Insurance (BHYT) card status with Vietnam Social Security and obtain proper clinical referral certificates (Giay chuyen tuyen) when moving between district, provincial, and central hospitals so that inpatient treatment and listed catastrophic-illness medications receive maximum statutory reimbursement [1] [2] [4].

steps.title: Record Healthcare Preferences and Designate a Medical Representative
steps.html:
• Patient consent rights under the Law on Medical Examination and Treatment: Under Vietnamese healthcare law overseen by the Ministry of Health of Vietnam, an adult patient with full civil act capacity has the right to be informed of their medical condition, to consent to or refuse specific diagnostic or treatment interventions, and to designate a family representative to interact with clinicians [4].
  • Written statement of care preferences in the hospital chart: Because Vietnam does not operate a standalone national living-will registry outside clinical records, it is advisable for the ill person to sign a written statement setting out their treatment and comfort-care preferences and ask the treating hospital department to place a copy directly inside the inpatient medical record [4] [5].
  • Designating a primary family spokesperson: Have the ill person formally record the name, Citizen Identity Card (Can cuoc cong dan) number, and telephone number of their chosen family representative in the hospital admission file so doctors know whom to consult if the patient later becomes unable to communicate [3] [4].

steps.title: Execute Financial Powers of Attorney and Bank Mandates
steps.html:
• Notarized Power of Attorney (Hop dong uy quyen / Giay uy quyen): Under the 2015 Civil Code of Vietnam, an authorization contract or power of attorney is valid only if executed while the principal retains full civil act capacity, and it terminates automatically if either party loses civil capacity or dies [2] [5]. Arrange promptly for the ill person to execute a notarized Power of Attorney before a public or private Notary Office supervised by the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam [3] [5].
  • Off-site notary visits to the home or hospital: Under the Law on Notarization administered by the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam, if the principal cannot travel to a notary office due to serious illness or hospitalization, a notary is explicitly permitted to conduct notarization outside the office at the patient's hospital bedside or home after verifying mental clarity and identity [3] [5].
  • Commercial bank account and pension collection mandates: In addition to a notarized power of attorney, ask each commercial bank in Vietnam where the ill person holds accounts to register their internal account mandate form while the account holder can sign in person, and complete the standard authorization form required by Vietnam Social Security if a family member will collect monthly pension or social insurance disbursements on the patient's behalf [1] [5].

steps.title: Activate Sickness, Disability, and Caregiver Benefits
steps.html:
• Extended sickness benefits for long-term illnesses: Under the Law on Social Insurance administered by Vietnam Social Security, employees diagnosed with a condition on the Ministry of Health's official list of diseases requiring long-term treatment (such as advanced cancer or severe chronic organ failure) qualify for extended paid sickness leave (up to 180 days per year, followed by continued statutory benefit rates if treatment continues) [1] [4].
  • Lump-sum social insurance withdrawal or invalidity pension: If a person is diagnosed with an immediately life-threatening illness (such as terminal cancer, paralysis, decompensated cirrhosis, or severe chronic renal failure certified under Ministry of Health of Vietnam criteria) or is assessed by the Medical Assessment Council (Hoi dong Giam dinh Y khoa) with a working capacity loss of 81% or more, they may choose either to withdraw a lump-sum social insurance payout immediately or to claim an early monthly invalidity/retirement pension through Vietnam Social Security [1] [4].
  • Social assistance and caregiver allowances: Individuals classified as having an exceptionally severe disability who lack a pension may also apply through the Commune-level People's Committee and the Government Portal of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam for a monthly social protection disability allowance and a statutory monthly caregiving support allowance for the household caregiver [1] [2] [5].

steps.title: Review the Will, Civil Status Records, and Property Documentation
steps.html:
• Executing a valid notarized Will (Di chuc): Under Chapter XXII of the 2015 Civil Code of Vietnam, a written will is most secure when notarized by a Notary Office under the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam or certified by the Commune-level People's Committee while the testator is of sound mind (or, in urgent hospital situations, witnessed and confirmed by the head of the hospital where the patient is treated) [3] [5]. Keep in mind that Article 644 of the Civil Code grants compulsory heirs (minor children, spouse, parents, and adult children unable to work) at least two-thirds of a statutory intestate share regardless of the will's wording [5].
  • Reconciling identity and land-use right certificates: Check that the ill person's Citizen Identity Card (CCCD), birth and marriage extracts held under the civil registry system of the Ministry of Justice of Vietnam, bank records, and Land Use Right Certificates (Giay chung nhan quyen su dung dat, commonly called the Pink Book or Red Book) show consistent personal names and ID numbers [2] [3] [5].
  • Cross-border assets and foreign family members: Because Vietnam is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, any powers of attorney or civil status documents executed abroad for use in Vietnam (or executed in Vietnam for use abroad) must undergo consular legalization through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant diplomatic mission tracked via the Government Portal of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam [3] [5].
